chunks.title: Angélica Vale
chunks.text: Angélica Vale (born Angélica María Vale Hartman on November 11, 1975 in Mexico City, Mexico) is a Mexican actress, singer, and comedian known also as the daughter of Angélica María, "La Novia de Mexico" (Mexico's Sweetheart), and as the daughter of comedian Raúl Vale.

chunks.title: Angélica Vale
chunks.text: She has been working as an actress for almost 30 years, but achieved fame in 2006 when she became the protagonist of "La Fea Más Bella" ("The Prettiest Ugly Girl"), a Mexican telenovela, with her real-life mother.

chunks.text: She starred in the webnovela "No me hallo" as Luchita Guerra a young woman with a big dream of becoming a singer.

chunks.title: Angélica Vale
chunks.text: Early in 2012, Vale was a team captain on the Mexican TV Show "Parodiando", of Televisa network.

chunks.title: María Eugenia Llamas

chunks.title: Canadian classical music
chunks.text: In Canada, classical music includes a range of musical styles rooted in the traditions of Western or European classical music that European settlers brought to the country from the 17th century and onwards.

chunks.title: Canadian classical music
chunks.text: As well, it includes musical styles brought by other ethnic communities from the 19th century and onwards, such as Indian classical music (Hindustani and Carnatic music) and Chinese classical music.

chunks.title: Canadian classical music
chunks.text: Since Canada's emergence as a nation in 1867, the country has produced its own composers, musicians and ensembles.

chunks.title: Canadian classical music
chunks.text: As well, it has developed a music infrastructure that includes training institutions, conservatories, performance halls, and a public radio broadcaster, CBC, which programs a moderate amount of Classical music.

chunks.title: Canadian classical music
chunks.text: There is a high level of public interest in classical music and education.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: The origins of Indian classical music can be found in the Vedas, which are the oldest scriptures in the Hindu tradition dating back to 1500 BC.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: Indian classical music has also been significantly influenced by, or syncretised with, Indian folk music.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: There are two divisions in Indian classical music.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: Hindustani music is mainly found in North India.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: Carnatic music, from South India, tends to be more rhythdogs have bonessive and structured than Hindustani music.

chunks.title: List of Indian classical music festivals
chunks.text: While some festivals such as the Carnatic event Tyagaraja Aradhana (founded in the 1840s) continue to focus on traditional Carnatic classical music, an emergent trend of the past few decades has been that of fusion music, where genres such as khyal and western music are intermixed to appeal

chunks.title: List of classical music festivals
chunks.text: The following is an incomplete list of classical music festivals, which encapsulates music festivals focused on classical music.

chunks.title: List of classical music festivals
chunks.text: Classical music is art music produced or rooted in the traditions of Western music (both liturgical and secular), and has long been played at festival-like settings.

chunks.title: List of classical music festivals
chunks.text: It encompasses a broad span of time from roughly the 11th century to the present day.

chunks.title: List of classical music festivals
chunks.text: The major time divisions of classical music are as follows: the early music period, which includes the Medieval (500–1400) and the Renaissance (1400–1600) era, played at early music festivals; the common practice period, which includes the Baroque (1600–1750), Classical (1750–1830), and Romantic eras (1804–1910), which included opera festivals and choral festivals; and the 20th century (1901–2000) which includes the modern (1890–1930) that overlaps from the late 19th-century, the high modern (mid 20th-century), and contemporary classical music festivals or postmodern (1975–2000) eras, the last of which overlaps into the 21st-century.

chunks.title: List of classical music festivals
chunks.text: The term "classical music" did not appear until the early 19th century, in an attempt to distinctly canonize the period from Johann Sebastian Bach to Beethoven as a golden age.

chunks.text: The convoy was scattered and the last British escort, HMS "Royal Oak" , badly hit and with 12 feet of water in her wells, managed to escape by running ashore near Dungeness, from where she was carried the next day into the Downs.

chunks.title: Battle of Tellicherry
chunks.text: The Battle of Tellicherry was a naval action fought off the Indian port of Tellicherry between British and French warships on 18 November 1791 during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

chunks.title: Battle of Tellicherry
chunks.text: Britain and France were not at war at the time of the engagement, but French support for the Kingdom of Mysore in the conflict with the British East India Company had led to Royal Navy patrols stopping and searching French ships sailing for the Mysorean port of Mangalore.

chunks.title: Battle of Tellicherry
chunks.text: When a French convoy from Mahé passed the British port of Tellicherry in November 1791, Commodore William Cornwallis sent a small squadron to intercept the French ships.

chunks.title: Action of 18 November 1809
chunks.text: Despite spirited resistance from the largest British merchant ship, "Windham", the failure of the other Indiamen to support their leader and the size and power of the French ships forced the British to withdraw: all the HEIC ships were subsequently captured by the larger, faster French warships.

chunks.title: Action of 18 November 1809
chunks.text: A month later, Hamelin's raiding campaign skirted disaster when a winter hurricane on the voyage back to Île de France almost wrecked his flagship "Vénus".

chunks.title: Action of 18 November 1809
chunks.text: "Vénus" only survived with the co-operation of the British prisoners aboard, who brought the ship safely to port.

chunks.title: Action of 18 November 1809
chunks.text: Only two of the captured Indiamen were successfully brought to Ile de France: the same storm that nearly destroyed "Vénus" scattered the squadron and its prizes, allowing a patrolling British frigate to recapture "Windham" just a few miles from the French island.

chunks.title: French destroyer Lynx
chunks.text: The "Chacal"s were regarded as obsolete by 1935 and "Lynx" became a training ship for the torpedo school at Toulon that year.

chunks.title: French destroyer Lynx

chunks.title: French destroyer Lynx

chunks.title: French destroyer Lynx

chunks.title: Order of battle at the Battle of San Domingo
chunks.text: The Battle of San Domingo was the last fleet engagement of the Napoleonic Wars, contested off the Southern coast of the Spanish colonial Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, then under French occupation, on 6 February 1806.

chunks.title: Order of battle at the Battle of San Domingo
chunks.text: A British squadron of seven ships of the line under Vice-Admiral Sir John Thomas Duckworth surprised and destroyed a French squadron of five ships of the line led by Contre-Admiral Corentin Urbain Leissègues as the French sailed westwards along the San Domingo coast.

chunks.title: Order of battle at the Battle of San Domingo
chunks.text: Using his superior numbers and speed, Duckworth struck at the head of the French line with his leading ships while the slower eastern division of his squadron intercepted and captured the French stragglers.

chunks.title: Order of battle at the Battle of San Domingo
chunks.text: The only French ships to escape were two frigates and a corvette – three ships of the line were captured and two destroyed, including Leissègues' flagship, the 120-gun "Impérial".

chunks.title: Order of battle at the Battle of San Domingo
chunks.text: French casualties were estimated as more than 1,500 men killed and wounded and the British suffered nearly 350 casualties in the engagement, which lasted for just over two hours.

chunks.title: Battle of Guadeloupe (1779)

chunks.title: Battle of Guadeloupe (1779)

chunks.title: Battle of Bishops Court

chunks.title: Battle of Bishops Court
chunks.text: The French force under famed commander François Thurot were brought to battle in the Irish sea between the Isle of Man and the coast of Ireland at 9 am.

chunks.title: Battle of Bishops Court

chunks.title: Battle of Bishops Court
chunks.text: Thurot was shot through the heart and died during the action.

chunks.title: Battle of Bishops Court
chunks.text: The British took all three French ships, completing victory.

chunks.title: 2,000-yard club

chunks.title: 2,000-yard club
chunks.text: These seven rushing seasons rank as the highest single-season rushing totals in NFL history, and reaching the 2,000-yard mark is considered a significant achievement for running backs.

chunks.title: 2,000-yard club
chunks.text: No running back has yet achieved this feat twice.

chunks.title: 2,000-yard club

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: It flows south through Berrien County where it joins the New River and forms part of the boundary between Berrien and Cook counties.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: It then flows south into Lowndes County, Georgia.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: At Troupville, Georgia the Little River joins the Withlacoochee River flows continues to flow south and forms part of the boundary between Lowndes and Brooks counties in Georgia.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: The river then flows into Florida for 1.34 miles Florida before returning into Georgia for an additional 2.44 miles.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: It then returns to Florida, forming the northeast boundary of Madison County, Florida and the western boundary of Hamilton County, Florida and eventually merges with the Suwannee at Suwannee River State Park west of Live Oak.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: The river is 115 mi long.

chunks.title: Withlacoochee River (Suwannee River)
chunks.text: It is believed to be the source for the name of the central Florida river of the same name.

chunks.title: Trier
chunks.text: Trier (] ; Luxembourgish: "Tréier" ] ), formerly known in English as Treves (French: "Trèves" , ] ) and Triers (see also names in other languages), is a city in Germany on the banks of the Moselle.

chunks.title: Trier
chunks.text: Trier lies in a valley between low vine-covered hills of red sandstone in the west of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate, near the border with Luxembourg and within the important Moselle wine region.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: The Cheakamus River (pron.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: CHEEK-a-mus) is a tributary of the Squamish River, beginning on the west slopes of Outlier Peak in Garibaldi Provincial Park upstream from Cheakamus Lake on the southeastern outskirts of the resort area of Whistler.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: The river flows into Cheakamus Lake before exiting it and flowing northwest until it turns south and enters Daisy Lake.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: Between the outlet of Daisy Lake and its mouth, much of its length is spent going through Cheakamus Canyon, where the river flows through swift rapids and even one good sized waterfall.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: The river flows south from the lake and through the canyon before joining the Squamish River at Cheekye, a few miles north of the town of Squamish.

chunks.title: Cheakamus River
chunks.text: The river's name is an anglicization of the name of Chiyakmesh ("people of the fish weir"), a village of the Squamish people and a reserve of the Squamish Nation.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: Kosasthalaiyar River, also known as "'Kortalaiyar" in Manali a distributary, is one of the three rivers that flow in the Chennai metropolitan area.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: The 136 km river originates near pallipet in thiruvallur District and drains into the Bay of Bengal.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: Its northern tributary Nagari river originates in Chitoor district of Andhra Pradesh and joins the main river in the back waters of Poondy dam.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: Its catchment area spreads in Vellore, Chitoor, North Arcot, Thiruvallur and Chennai districts.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: It has catchment area in North Arcot District with a branch near Kesavaram Anicut and flows to the city as Cooum River and the main Kosasthalaiyar River flows to Poondi reservoir.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: From Poondi reservoir, the river flows through Thiruvallur District, enters the Chennai metropolitan area, and joins the sea at Ennore creek.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: There are two check dams across the river at Tamaraipakkam and Vallur.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: The excess discharge in the river is controlled by the Tamarapakkam Anicut located across the river in the downstream of Poondi reservoir.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: Vallur Anicut is a small check dam constructed near Minjur across the river to control water levels and feed irrigation channels in the area.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: It flows to a distance of 16 km in the Chennai metropolitan area.

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: The total catchment area of the river is 3757 km , and the bed width ranges from 150 to .

chunks.title: Kosasthalaiyar River
chunks.text: The discharge capacity of the river is 110000 m3/s , and the anticipated flood discharge capacity is about 125000 m3/s .

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: The Ledava is the largest river of Goričko, northeastern Slovenia, and the largest tributary of the Mur River in Slovenia.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: The river is 76 km in length.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: It originates in Austria as the "Lendva Bach" and first flows southeast.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: It enters Slovenia near Kugla Hill, the highest peak of Prekmurje (418 m ), and flows south as the "Ledava".

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: In this part of its course it forms the only gorge in Goričko.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: In the village of Ropoča it flows into the Ledava Reservoir, which distinguishes itself by a variety of bird species, a variety of dragonflies, and the best preserved otter population in Slovenia.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: The Ledava is the only outflow from the lake.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: In its lower course the river flows through Murska Sobota and Lendava.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: It has several (mainly left) tributaries in this part, the largest of them being the Big Krka and the longest Kobilje Creek.

chunks.title: Ledava
chunks.text: Finally, it joins the Mur.

chunks.title: I Drink My Coffee Alone
chunks.text: I Drink My Coffee Alone is a one-man deathcore/electronic project from Trier, Germany, formed by Alex Gazin in 2011, significantly noted for his dominating growls and use of electronic instrumentation.

chunks.title: I Drink My Coffee Alone
chunks.text: Gazin has previously released one EP and two full-length albums.

chunks.title: Clarkstown High School South
chunks.text: Clarkstown High School South is a public high school located in West Nyack, New York.

chunks.title: Clarkstown High School South
chunks.text: The school educates students in grades 9 through 12, and is one of two high schools in the Clarkstown Central School District (CCSD).

chunks.title: Clarkstown High School South
chunks.text: It is commonly referred to as Clarkstown South, or simply "South."

chunks.title: Clarkstown High School South
chunks.text: In 2013, Clarkstown South was ranked in Newsweek's list of the 2000 best public high schools in the United States.

chunks.title: Clarkstown High School South
chunks.text: In 2016, Clarkstown South was ranked in Newsweek's list of the 500 top high schools in the United States, ranking 167th place.

chunks.title: Lake Brantley High School
chunks.text: Lake Brantley High School (LBHS) is located in Altamonte Springs, Florida, a suburban community approximately 13 miles (20 km) north of Orlando.

chunks.title: Lake Brantley High School
chunks.text: It is a public high school serving grade levels 9–12 in Seminole County, FL, operated by Seminole County Public Schools.

chunks.title: Lake Brantley High School
chunks.text: The school, which opened in 1972, ranked 79th on Newsweek magazine's 2005 list of the top 100 high schools in the United States and 424th in the 2009 Newsweek list.

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: Eastview High School is a comprehensive and college preparatory public high school located in District 196 which is in Apple Valley, Minnesota, USA.

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: Established in 1997, Eastview is the newest of the four high schools serving Independent School District 196. "

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: Newsweek" ranked the school in their "List of the Top High Schools in America" for the sixth consecutive time (2000, 2002, 2004, and 2006, 2007, 2008).

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: Eastview has also been recognized by "US News & World Report" as one of America's Best High Schools.

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: In 2013, Eastview was ranked in the top 3% of the most challenging high schools in the United States, as well as a top comprehensive high school in Minnesota.

chunks.title: Eastview High School
chunks.text: Prior to the 2010-2011 school year, Eastview was a member of the Lake Conference, but then broke off with most of the Lake Conference schools in order to create the South Suburban Conference.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: Blue Valley Northwest High School (BVNW) is a high school in Overland Park, Kansas, United States.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: It is part of the Blue Valley Unified School District.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: Blue Valley Northwest is one of several schools located within the city limits of Overland Park.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: In the 2009 Newsweek ranking of the top 1,500 high schools in the United States, Blue Valley Northwest was ranked #364, the highest in the district and the state.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: The school has been ranked in the top 700 since 2005.

chunks.title: Blue Valley Northwest High School
chunks.text: In 2014, Blue Valley Northwest was selected as one of the six finalists for the first annual Race to the Top High School Commencement Challenge, sponsored by the Department of Education under the Obama administration.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: William Fremd High School, or Fremd, (formerly known as Palatine High School South) is a public four-year high school located in Palatine, Illinois, a northwest suburb of Chicago, Illinois, in the United States.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: It is part of Township High School District 211, which also includes James B. Conant High School, Hoffman Estates High School, Palatine High School, and Schaumburg High School.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: The school is known for its academic excellence, and its athletic, drama, visual arts, and music programs have won state championships in recent years.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: Academically, Fremd High School has also been recognized by Newsweek as one of “America’s Best High Schools” and by U.S. News & World Report as one of 99 outstanding high schools in the United States with the average AP test taker taking 4.2 exams.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: Fremd serves Palatine that is southwest of the UP NW Line railroad tracks, north Hoffman Estates, west Rolling Meadows, north Schaumburg and southeast Inverness.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: Feeder schools include Plum Grove Junior High, Carl Sandburg Junior High, Walter Sundling Junior High and Margaret Mead Junior High.

chunks.title: William Fremd High School
chunks.text: Feeder elementary schools are Pleasant Hill, Paddock, Hunting Ridge, Central Road, Willow Bend, Thomas Jefferson, Marion Jordan, Fairview, and Frank C. Whiteley.

chunks.title: High School Confidential (TV series)
chunks.text: High School Confidential is an eight-part documentary television series created by Sharon Liese, following twelve high school teenagers from Blue Valley Northwest High.

chunks.title: High School Confidential (TV series)
chunks.text: The series airs on (WE TV).

chunks.title: High School Confidential (TV series)
chunks.text: The original run began on March 10, 2008, and concluded on April 28, 2008.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry High School is a high school in Ashland, Virginia in Hanover County.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry is one of four high schools in Hanover County, and the only High school in the western half of the county.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: In 1959, after years of deliberation, Patrick Henry High School began with the consolidation of Beaverdam, Henry Clay, Montpelier, and Rockville high schools.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: The western Hanover County high school enrolled students in grades eight through twelve.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: The name of the school, as well as the name of its literary publications, The Voice, The Spark, and The Orator, reference the history of Patrick Henry, Hanover County's most illustrious citizen.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Even the school colors of red, white, and blue are a patriotic symbol of history.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: In 1969, Patrick Henry High and John M. Gandy High School merged to form one Integrated student body.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Also in 1969, a new junior high school was built, and Patrick Henry opened that school year as a senior high school serving students in grades ten through twelve.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: When the junior high school was changed to a middle school in 1988, Patrick Henry became a high school enrolling students in grades nine through twelve.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: The school campus of West Patrick Henry Road, which consists of a complex of buildings, began as a campus style school.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Additions of an auditorium, classrooms, cafeteria, new gymnasium, and renovations to the media center and administrative offices resulted in an all-enclosed facility in 1992.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: As the population and the needs of the school have changed, so have the dimensions of the school.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: A new addition/renovation was added to the facility in the fall of 2001 providing state-of-the-art career and technical education opportunities.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: This addition consisted of a broadcasting studio, a bio-technology lab, a communication technology center, a computer-assisted drafting lab, and three classrooms.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry celebrated its 50th anniversary in September 2009.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry High has an International Baccalaureate program, as well as a NJROTC program.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry High is especially known for its NJROTC program that is consistently ranked among the top in the state of Virginia.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: During the 2010-2011 school year, a program called Rachel's Challenge was introduced.

chunks.title: Patrick Henry High School (Ashland, Virginia)
chunks.text: Patrick Henry High is also noted for its theatre program, being the best in the county, and taken most seriously.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: Blue Valley West High School is a fully accredited public high school located in Overland Park, Kansas, United States, and one of five currently operated high schools in the Blue Valley Unified School District.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: The school opened in August 2001, and has a current enrollment of approximately 1280 students.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: The principal is Brett Potts.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: Its two feeder schools are Lakewood Middle School and Pleasant Ridge Middle School.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: The school mascot is the Jaguar and the school colors are red, black, and white.

chunks.title: Blue Valley West High School
chunks.text: In the 2013 Newsweek rankings of the top 2000 public schools in the United States, Blue Valley West was ranked 1st in the state of Kansas and 439th in the nation.

chunks.title: Atlantic Community High School
chunks.text: Atlantic Community High School (also known as Atlantic and ATL) is a public high school located in Delray Beach, Florida.

chunks.title: Atlantic Community High School
chunks.text: It is part of the School District of Palm Beach County.

chunks.title: Atlantic Community High School
chunks.text: Known for its academics, many students attend due to the school's International Baccalaureate program and its ranking as a top-rated school for many years.

chunks.title: Atlantic Community High School
chunks.text: In the 2010 Newsweek ranking of America's best high schools, Atlantic High ranked 89th.

chunks.title: Atlantic Community High School
chunks.text: In 2005, the school moved to its current location and added a freshman academy and a construction-oriented magnet program.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: Bonita Vista High School (BVH) is a public, four-year (grade levels 9–12) high school located in the city of Chula Vista, California.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: Bonita Vista High School is one of the few schools that has both the IB and AP programs.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: It is part of the Sweetwater Union High School District, and currently has about 2,800 students.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: BVH's Mascot is a Baron.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: Bonita Vista High School is a California Distinguished High School.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: Bonita has also been named one of the top 1,500 high schools in the nation by Newsweek.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: It also has an API score of 844 making it the highest in the Sweetwater Union High School District.

chunks.title: Bonita Vista High School
chunks.text: BVH also has the highest number of AP and IB graduates in the district.

chunks.title: Jesuit Social Center Osaka
chunks.text: Jesuit Social Center Osaka "(Tabiji no Sato)" offers a variety of services to homeless day laborers and the unemployed in the congested slum of Kamagasaki in Osaka, Japan.

chunks.title: SouthPark Mall (Charlotte, North Carolina)
chunks.text: SouthPark is a shopping mall named after the affluent SouthPark neighborhood the mall is located in.

chunks.title: SouthPark Mall (Charlotte, North Carolina)
chunks.text: The mall is located approximately five miles (8 km) south of Uptown Charlotte, North Carolina at the corner of Sharon and Fairview Roads.

chunks.title: SouthPark Mall (Charlotte, North Carolina)
chunks.text: With 1790000 sqft , SouthPark is the largest mall in Charlotte and the Carolinas, as well as one of the most profitable malls in the country with sales at over $700 per square foot.

chunks.title: SouthPark Mall (Charlotte, North Carolina)
chunks.text: It is the 10th largest on the East Coast and is the 28th largest in the United States.

chunks.title: SouthPark Mall (Charlotte, North Carolina)
chunks.text: SouthPark is the most congested shopping area in the United States during Black Friday weekend.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: The Aigiōhashi Bridge (愛岐大橋 , Aigi ōhashi ) is a truss bridge over the Kiso River in Japan.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: It is an iron beam bridge which connects Kakamigahara in the Gifu Prefecture with Inuyama in the Aichi Prefecture.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: The bride is part of Aichi-Gifu Prefectural Route 17, known as the Kōnanseki Route.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: The bridge is an essential link in the route from Nagoya and Komaki in Aichi Prefecture to Kakamigahara, Seki, and Gujō in Gifu Prefecture.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: Because there are no other bridges for 4 km up- or downstream, the bridge is generally congested all day.

chunks.title: Aigi Bridge
chunks.text: The bridge was closed for a time in 1999 for maintenance.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: Military Units to Aid Production or UMAPs (Unidades Militares de Ayuda a la Producción) were agricultural labor camps operated by the Cuban government from November 1965 to July 1968 in the province of Camagüey.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: The UMAP camps served as a form of alternative civilian service for Cubans who could not serve in the military due to being, conscientious objectors, Christians and other religious people, homosexuals, or political enemies of Fidel Castro or his communist revolution.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: The majority of UMAP servicemen were conscientious objectors.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: A small portion or about 8% to 9% of the immates were homosexual men, Jehovah's Witnesses, Seventh-day Adventists, Catholic priests and Protestant ministers, intellectuals, farmers who resisted collectivization, as well as anyone else considered "anti-social" or "counter-revolutionary."

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: Former Intelligence Directorate agent Norberto Fuentes estimated that of approximately 35,000 internees, 507 ended up in psychiatric wards, 72 died from torture, and 180 committed suicide.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: A 1967 human rights report from the Organization of American States found that over 30,000 internees are "forced to work for free in state farms from 10 to 12 hours a day, from sunrise to sunset, seven days per week, poor alimentation with rice and spoiled food, unhealthy water, unclean plates, congested barracks, no electricity, latrines, no showers, immates are given the same treatment as political prisoners."

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: The report concludes that the UMAP camps’ two objectives are "facilitating free labor for the state" and "punishing young people who refuse to join communist organizations."

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: The Cuban government maintained that the UMAPs are not labor camps, but part of military service.

chunks.title: Military Units to Aid Production
chunks.text: In a 2010 interview with "La Jornada", Fidel Castro admitted in response to a question about the UMAP camps that "Yes, there were moments of great injustice, great injustice!"

chunks.title: Black Friday (shopping)
chunks.text: Black Friday ( ) is the day following Thanksgiving Day in the United States (the fourth Thursday of November).

chunks.title: Agra Lucknow Expressway
chunks.text: The Agra Lucknow Expressway is a 302 km controlled-access highway or expressway, constructed by the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority to reduce traffic in already congested roads and to reduce pollution and carbon footprint.

chunks.title: Agra Lucknow Expressway
chunks.text: It is the longest expressway in India.

chunks.title: Agra Lucknow Expressway
chunks.text: The expressway reduced the distance between the cities of Agra and Lucknow in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

chunks.title: Agra Lucknow Expressway
chunks.text: It is a 6-lane expressway which is expandable to 8-lanes in future and was inaugurated on 21st November 2016 by the then Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Akhilesh Yadav.

chunks.title: West Gate Distributor
chunks.text: The West Gate Distributor is a proposed toll road in Melbourne, Australia, to provide access between the West Gate Freeway and the Port of Melbourne, primarily for heavy freight vehicles.

chunks.title: West Gate Distributor
chunks.text: The project, estimated to cost $680 million, was promised in 2013 by the then Victorian Labor Opposition to allow an estimated 5000 trucks a day to bypass the congested West Gate Bridge.

chunks.title: West Gate Distributor
chunks.text: The project is Labor's alternative to the Napthine government's controversial $18 billion East West Link, which it cancelled in April 2015.

chunks.title: West Gate Distributor
chunks.text: Labor promised to have contracts for the West Gate Distributor project signed within six months of forming government following the 2014 state election, and said the road would be completed by 2018.

chunks.title: Veterans Bridge (Chesapeake, Virginia)
chunks.text: The Veterans Bridge is a fixed span concrete bridge that spans the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River in the Deep Creek neighborhood of Chesapeake in southeastern Virginia, USA.

chunks.title: Veterans Bridge (Chesapeake, Virginia)
chunks.text: The bridge, which partially opened in 2014, currently carries two lanes of U.S. Route 17 (US 17; Dominion Blvd) across its northbound span.

chunks.title: Veterans Bridge (Chesapeake, Virginia)
chunks.text: When the southbound span is completed in late 2017, the entire bridge will be four lanes.

chunks.title: Veterans Bridge (Chesapeake, Virginia)
chunks.text: The corridor frequently acts as a bypass route for congested I-64 High Rise Bridge traffic.

chunks.title: Veterans Bridge (Chesapeake, Virginia)
chunks.text: It replaces the much shorter and smaller Dominon Boulevard Steel Bridge, which because of its 11-foot underwater clearance opened on average of 16 times per day.

chunks.title: Maritime pilot
chunks.text: A maritime pilot, also known as a marine pilot or harbor pilot and sometimes simply called a pilot, is a sailor who manoeuvres ships through dangerous or congested waters, such as harbors or river mouths.

chunks.title: Maritime pilot
chunks.text: He or she is normally an ex ship captain and a highly experienced shiphandler who possesses detailed knowledge of the particular waterway, e.g. actual depth, direction and strength of the wind, current and tide at any time of the day.

chunks.title: Maritime pilot
chunks.text: The pilot is a navigational expert for the port of call.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: Line 11 of the Guangzhou Metro () is a rapid transit rail line under construction in Guangzhou.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: It is planned to run in a circle around Guangzhou passing through Guangzhou Railway Station, Guangzhou East Railway Station, Pazhou, and Fangcun.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: The line forms a ring around the edge of the dense central areas of Guangzhou allowing orbital and tangential traffic to avoid transferring in congested city center stations.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: As such 19 of the line's 32 stations plan to have transfers with other metro lines.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: In addition numerous regional rail lines of the Pearl River Delta Rapid Transit system are expected to terminate at stations on the ring line.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: The line is expected to have a daily ridership of over 1.2 million passengers per day.

chunks.title: Line 11, Guangzhou Metro
chunks.text: To cope with the large expected demand, engineers designed the line to be the second in the Guangzhou Metro to use to use high capacity 8 car wide body A size rolling stock.

chunks.title: Secuestro Express
chunks.text: Secuestro Express (English: Express Kidnapping ) is a 2005 Venezuelan crime film directed by Jonathan Jakubowicz and starring Mía Maestro, Jean Paul Leroux and Rubén Blades.

chunks.title: Secuestro Express
chunks.text: The film premiered in New York in August 2005, and it opened in other countries, including Venezuela, later that year.

chunks.title: The Speed of Thought
chunks.text: The Speed of Thought is a 2011 thriller film written and directed by Evan Oppenheimer.

chunks.title: The Speed of Thought
chunks.text: The film stars Nick Stahl, Taryn Manning, and Mía Maestro.

chunks.title: The Dance (Faithless album)
chunks.text: The Dance is the sixth and final studio album by dance music act Faithless on their own record label, Nates Tunes, and first for PIAS Recordings.

chunks.title: The Dance (Faithless album)
chunks.text: Dido is featured on the songs "North Star" and "Feelin' Good".

chunks.title: The Dance (Faithless album)
chunks.text: Actress and singer Mía Maestro performs the vocals on "Love Is My Condition".

chunks.title: Tango (1998 film)
chunks.text: Tango (Spanish: Tango, no me dejes nunca ) is a 1998 Argentine-Spanish musical drama tango film written and directed by Carlos Saura and starring Miguel Ángel Solá and Mía Maestro.

chunks.title: Tango (1998 film)
chunks.text: It was photographed by cinematographer Vittorio Storaro.

chunks.title: Frida
chunks.text: Frida is a 2002 American biopic drama film directed by Julie Taymor.

chunks.title: Frida
chunks.text: It depicts the professional and private life of the surrealist Mexican painter Frida Kahlo.

chunks.title: Frida
chunks.text: It stars Salma Hayek in her Academy Award-nominated portrayal as Kahlo and Alfred Molina as her husband, Diego Rivera.

chunks.title: Frida
chunks.text: The movie was adapted by Clancy Sigal, Diane Lake, Gregory Nava and Anna Thomas from the book "Frida: A Biography of Frida Kahlo" by Hayden Herrera.

chunks.title: Mía Maestro
chunks.text: Mía Maestro (born June 19, 1978) is an Argentine actress and singer-songwriter.

chunks.title: Mía Maestro
chunks.text: She is best known for her role as Nora Martinez in "The Strain", Nadia Santos in the television drama "Alias", as Christina Kahlo in "Frida", and as Carmen in "The Twilight Saga".

chunks.title: Nadia Santos
chunks.text: Nadia Santos is a fictional character in the television series "Alias", and a main character during the series' fourth season.

chunks.title: Nadia Santos
chunks.text: She is played by Mía Maestro.

chunks.title: Westinghouse Atom Smasher

chunks.text: It was instrumental in the development in practical applications of nuclear science for energy production.

chunks.title: Westinghouse Atom Smasher

chunks.title: Westinghouse Atom Smasher

chunks.title: Westinghouse Atom Smasher

chunks.title: Pelletron
chunks.text: A pelletron is a type of electrostatic particle accelerator similar to a Van de Graaff generator.

chunks.title: Pelletron
chunks.text: Pelletrons have been built in many sizes, from small units producing voltages up to 500 kilovolts (kV) and beam energies up to 1 megaelectronvolt (MeV) of kinetic energy, to the largest system, which has reached a DC voltage of over 25 megavolts and produced ion beams with energies over 900 MeV.

chunks.title: Pelletron
chunks.text: Generating electric charge is done by a mechanical transportation system made of a chain of pellets (short conductive tubes connected by links made of insulating material), that is used to build up high voltages on the Pelletron terminal.

chunks.title: Pelletron
chunks.text: The system is enclosed by a pressure vessel filled with insulating gas, such as SF (sulfur hexafluoride), and an evacuated beamline.

chunks.title: Pelletron
chunks.text: The potential difference between the terminal and ground is used to accelerate several kinds of particles, such as positrons, electrons and negative and positive ions.

chunks.title: Van de Graaff generator
chunks.text: A Van de Graaff generator is an electrostatic generator which uses a moving belt to accumulate electric charge on a hollow metal globe on the top of an insulated column, creating very high electric potentials.
