chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: Ælfwine Haroldsson or Ælfwine was most probably an illegitimate son of King Harold Harefoot of England.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: He was probably born during the early 1030s, either in Scandinavia or after 1035 in England.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: He appears in an early twelfth-century cartulary from the monastery of Sainte Foi at Conques in Aquitaine as "Alboynus" (a cognate of Ælfwine), alongside the records that he was born in London and was the son of a King "Heroldus" (a Latinised version of Harold) and one "Alveva" ("Ælfgifu" Latinised).

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: It is also noted that he arrived in Conques in 1060 on pilgrimage and persuaded the local authorities to rebuild the church and make him prior.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: W. H. Stevenson showed the only chronologically plausible candidate for his father is King Harold Harefoot.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: With Harold Harefoot's sudden death on 17 March 1040 Ælfwine was most likely left in his otherwise unknown mother's care, or even that of his powerful and influential grandmother Ælfgifu of Northampton, who may be the Ælfgifu of the record mistakenly named as his mother, rather than grandmother.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: He did not lay any claim to the throne of England.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: Little is known about him, but he is thought to have died in the 1070s or 1080s.

chunks.title: Ælfwine Haroldsson
chunks.text: He was a grandson of Cnut the Great.

chunks.title: Grand Shaftesbury Run
chunks.text: The Grand Shaftesbury Run, previously known as the Great Shaftesbury Run, is an off-road, rural half marathon and 10k course that takes place on the 2,200 ha historic Shaftesbury Estate in Wimborne St Giles, Dorset, England.

chunks.title: Grand Shaftesbury Run
chunks.text: Both courses start and finish in the park at St Giles House, the historic home of the Earls of Shaftesbury.

chunks.title: Grand Shaftesbury Run
chunks.text: The inaugural event, held on 12 June 2011, opened the family estate to the public for the first time in 60 years.

chunks.title: Exeter Book
chunks.text: The Exeter Book, Exeter Cathedral Library MS 3501, also known as the Codex Exoniensis, is a tenth-century book or codex which is an anthology of Anglo-Saxon poetry.

chunks.title: Exeter Book
chunks.text: It is one of the four major Anglo-Saxon literature codices, along with the Vercelli Book, Nowell Codex and the Cædmon manuscript or MS Junius 11.

chunks.title: Exeter Book
chunks.text: The book was donated to the library of Exeter Cathedral by Leofric, the first bishop of Exeter, in 1072.

chunks.title: Exeter Book
chunks.text: It is believed originally to have contained 131 leaves, of which the first 8 have been replaced with other leaves; the original first 8 pages are lost.

chunks.title: Exeter Book
chunks.text: The Exeter Book is the largest known collection of Old English literature still in existence.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: Exeter Quay, also known as Exeter Quayside, is a part of the city of Exeter next to the River Exe and the Exeter Ship Canal.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: It was first used as a port in prehistoric times when a sandstone ledge was used to unload the ships of overseas traders.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: However, by 1381 the Countess Weir had blocked the river to shipping.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: A canal was completed in 1566 to provide access for ships.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: Over time the number of ships using the quayside increased and so the quay was expanded in the late 17th century.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: Further expansion occurred in 1830 when a new canal basin was dug.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: However, in 1840 the railways reached Exeter and the shipping began to decline.

chunks.title: Exeter Quay
chunks.text: The quayside no longer has any shipping but is now mostly used for leisure.

chunks.title: Nicholas Ashley-Cooper, 12th Earl of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: Nicholas Edmund Anthony Ashley-Cooper, 12th Earl of Shaftesbury Bt, (born 3 June 1979) also known as Nick Ashley-Cooper, is an English peer, landowner and philanthropist.

chunks.title: Nicholas Ashley-Cooper, 12th Earl of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: He succeeded his brother as Earl of Shaftesbury in 2005.

chunks.title: Nicholas Ashley-Cooper, 12th Earl of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: The 12th Earl of Shaftesbury is the godson of Gerald Grosvenor, 6th Duke of Westminster, and Simon Elliot, brother-in-law of Charles, Prince of Wales.

chunks.title: Edmund Ironside
chunks.text: Edmund II (died 30 November 1016), usually known as Edmund Ironside, was King of England from 23 April to 30 November 1016.

chunks.title: Edmund Ironside
chunks.text: He was the son of King Æthelred the Unready and his first wife, Ælfgifu of York.

chunks.title: Edmund Ironside
chunks.text: Edmund's reign was marred by a war he had inherited from his father, his cognomen "Ironside" was given to him "because of his valour" in resisting the Danish invasion led by Cnut the Great.

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: Saint Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury, also known as Saint Elgiva (died 944) was the first wife of Edmund I (r. 939–946), by whom she bore two future kings, Eadwig (r. 955–959) and Edgar (r. 959–975).

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: Like her mother Wynflaed, she had a close and special if unknown connection with the royal nunnery of Shaftesbury (Dorset), founded by King Alfred, where she was buried and soon revered as a saint.

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury
chunks.text: According to a pre-Conquest tradition from Winchester, her feast day is 18 May.

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Exeter
chunks.text: Ælfgifu of Exeter was an Anglo-Saxon saint, of unknown date or origin, whose relics were held by Exeter Cathedral.

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Exeter
chunks.text: She is mentioned in the Old English Exeter relic-list as "the holy servant of Christ ... who would daily perform her confession before she went into church".

chunks.title: Ælfgifu of Exeter
chunks.text: It is possible that she is the 10th-century royal abbess, Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury wife of Edmund I (as one 12th-century writer believed), but it is "more likely" according to historian John Blair that she was not.

chunks.title: Exeter Inn
chunks.text: The Exeter Inn (also known as The Inn at Exeter) is an inn in Exeter, New Hampshire, United States.

chunks.title: Exeter Inn
chunks.text: Located on Front Street on the campus of Phillips Exeter Academy, the Georgian style complex was built in 1932 and mirrors the school's architectural motif.

chunks.title: Exeter Inn
chunks.text: Guests, which include many parents of Academy students, enjoy its walking distance proximity to historic downtown Exeter.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: Edgar I (Old English: "Ēadgār" ;  943 8 July 975), known as the Peaceful or the Peaceable, was King of England from 959 until his death.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: He was the younger son of Edmund I and Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury, and came to the throne as a teenager, following the death of his older brother Eadwig.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: As king, Edgar further consolidated the political unity achieved by his predecessors, with his reign being noted for its relative stability.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: His most trusted advisor was Dunstan, who he recalled from exile and made Archbishop of Canterbury.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: The pinnacle of Edgar's reign was his coronation at Bath in 973, which was organised by Dunstan and forms the basis for the current coronation ceremony.

chunks.title: Edgar the Peaceful
chunks.text: After his death he was succeeded by his son Edward, although the succession was disputed.

chunks.title: Teatro Verdi (Florence)
chunks.text: Teatro Verdi is a theatre in Florence, Italy.

chunks.title: Teatro Verdi (Florence)
chunks.text: Established in 1854, it is located on Via Giuseppe Verdi on the block between Via Ghibellina and Via dei Lavatoi.

chunks.title: Teatro Verdi (Florence)
chunks.text: The Teatro Verdi was originally called Teatro Pagliano, but was renamed in 1901 to honour Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Teatro Verdi (Florence)
chunks.text: The theatre is located on the spot where there once stood the 14th-century Stinche Prison.

chunks.title: Rigoletto
chunks.text: Rigoletto (] ) is an opera in three acts by Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Rigoletto
chunks.text: The Italian libretto was written by Francesco Maria Piave based on the play "Le roi s'amuse" by Victor Hugo.

chunks.title: Rigoletto
chunks.text: Despite serious initial problems with the Austrian censors who had control over northern Italian theatres at the time, the opera had a triumphant premiere at La Fenice in Venice on 11 March 1851.

chunks.title: Parma Airport
chunks.text: Parma Airport (Italian: "Aeroporto di Parma" , IATA: PMF, ICAO: LIMP ) is located 1.3 NM northwest of Parma, a city in the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy.

chunks.title: Parma Airport
chunks.text: The airport was opened on 5 May 1991.

chunks.title: Parma Airport
chunks.text: It is also known as Giuseppe Verdi Airport or Parma "Giuseppe Verdi" Airport, named after Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi Monument
chunks.text: The Giuseppe Verdi Monument is a sculpture in honor of composer Giuseppe Verdi located in Verdi Square Park (between West 72nd and West 73rd streets, between Amsterdam Avenue and Broadway) in Manhattan, New York City.

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi Monument
chunks.text: The statue, by Pasquale Civiletti (1858–1952), depicts Verdi flanked by four of his most popular characters: Falstaff (on the west side of the statue of Verdi), Leonora of "La forza del destino" (south side), Aida (north side), and Otello (east side).

chunks.title: Orchestra Sinfonica di Milano Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: The Orchestra Sinfonica di Milano Giuseppe Verdi (Symphony Orchestra of Milan Giuseppe Verdi) is an Italian orchestra based in Milan.

chunks.title: Orchestra Sinfonica di Milano Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: The orchestra refers to itself as "La Verdi" colloquially.

chunks.title: Orchestra Sinfonica di Milano Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: The orchestra's primary residence is the "Auditorium di Milano Fondazione Cariplo".

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi (film)
chunks.text: Giuseppe Verdi is a 1938 Italian biographical film directed by Carmine Gallone and starring Fosco Giachetti, Gaby Morlay and Germana Paolieri.

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi (film)
chunks.text: The film portrays the life of the composer Giuseppe Verdi (1813-1901).

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi (film)
chunks.text: The casting of Giachetti as Verdi was intended to emphasise the composer's patriotism, as he had recently played patriotic roles in films such as "The White Squadron".

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi (film)
chunks.text: The film was made at the Cinecittà Studios in Rome.

chunks.title: Giuseppe Verdi (film)
chunks.text: The film is also known by the alternative title The Life of Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Ara Berberian
chunks.text: Ara Berberian (Armenian: Արա Բերբերյան , May 14, 1930 in Detroit, Michigan - February 21, 2005 in Boynton Beach, Florida, ) was an American bass and actor who had an active international career in operas, concerts, and musicals from the early 1960s until his retirement from the stage in 1997.

chunks.title: Ara Berberian
chunks.text: He notably had an 18-year association with the Metropolitan Opera in New York City, where he gave a total of 334 performances between 1979-1997.

chunks.title: Ara Berberian
chunks.text: He sang over 100 roles during his career, including those of Osmin in Mozart's "Abduction from the Seraglio" and Sparafucile in Verdi's "Rigoletto".

chunks.title: Verdi, the King of Melody
chunks.text: Giuseppe Verdi, released theatrically in the USA as The Life and Music of Giuseppe Verdi and on video as Verdi, the King of Melody, is a 1953 Italian biographical film starring Pierre Cressoy and directed by Raffaello Matarazzo.

chunks.title: Verdi, the King of Melody
chunks.text: It is based on adult life events of the composer Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Verdi, the King of Melody
chunks.text: The film was a commercial success, grossing over 957 million lire at the Italian box office.

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: Mark Delavan is an American operatic bass-baritone.

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: He made his professional debut in 1986 at the San Francisco Opera in a small role in Giuseppe Verdi's "Don Carlos".

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: He spent the next three years performing in numerous comprimario roles with the company.

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: He has since returned to that opera house to sing Scarpia in Giacomo Puccini's "Tosca" (2004, with Carol Vaness in the title role) and Wotan in Richard Wagner's "The Ring Cycle" (2008, 2010, and 2011).

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: In 2001 he made his debut at the Metropolitan Opera as Amonasro in Verdi's "Aida" with Deborah Voigt in the title role, Luciano Pavarotti as Radamès, Olga Borodina as Amneris, and James Levine conducting.

chunks.title: Mark Delavan
chunks.text: He has since been heard at the Met as Alfio in Pietro Mascagni's "Cavalleria rusticana", Carlo Gérard in "Andrea Chénier", Count Tomsky in "The Queen of Spades", Don Carlo in Verdi's "La Forza del Destino", the Messenger in Richard Strauss' "Die Frau ohne Schatten", Scarpia, and the title roles in Verdi's "Nabucco", Verdi's "Rigoletto", and Verdi's "Simon Boccanegra".

chunks.title: Teatro Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: Teatro Giuseppe Verdi (the Giuseppe Verdi Theatre) is a small opera house located in a wing of the Rocca dei Marchesi Pallavicino on the Piazza Giuseppe Verdi in Busseto, Italy, a town closely associated with the life of the opera composer, Giuseppe Verdi.

chunks.title: Teatro Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: From the 13th century, the “rocca” or “fortress” was the family’s palace; it is now the city hall after being acquired by the municipality in 1856.

chunks.title: Teatro Giuseppe Verdi
chunks.text: The theatre opened on 15 August 1868 and seats 300.

chunks.title: Jim Beatty
chunks.text: James Tully Beatty (born October 28, 1934 in New York, New York) is a former American track and field athlete who is best remembered as the first person to break the four-minute mile barrier on an indoor track when he ran 3:58.9 on February 10, 1962 at the Los Angeles Invitational in the Los Angeles Sports Arena in Los Angeles, California.

chunks.title: Division of Barton
chunks.text: The Division of Barton is an Australian electoral division in the state of New South Wales.

chunks.title: Division of Barton
chunks.text: The division was created in 1922 and is named for Sir Edmund Barton, the first Prime Minister of Australia.

chunks.title: Market towns of Østfold and Akershus counties
chunks.text: The Market towns of Østfold and Akershus counties (Norwegian: "Kjøpstedene i Østfold og Akershus fylker" ) was an electoral district for parliamentary elections in Norway.

chunks.title: Market towns of Østfold and Akershus counties
chunks.text: It comprised the market towns (Norwegian: "kjøpsteder" ) of Fredrikstad, Halden (until 1928 named Fredrikshald), Moss and Sarpsborg in Østfold county and Drøbak in Akershus county.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: James Thomas Tully (1877 – 15 October 1962) was an Australian politician.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: Born in Grafton, New South Wales, he was educated at state schools before becoming a farmer and teacher in Tullamore.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: In 1919, he unsuccessfully contested the federal seat of New England for the Australian Labor Party.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: He moved to Sydney in 1922, where he continued to teach.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: In 1928, he was elected to the Australian House of Representatives as the Labor member for Barton, defeating incumbent Nationalist Thomas Ley.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: He retained the seat until 1931, when he was challenged by both the United Australia Party's Albert Lane and Lang Labor's John Eldridge, the member for Martin.

chunks.title: James Tully (Australian politician)
chunks.text: Lane won the seat, making it the only time in Australian history that two sitting members have been simultaneously defeated for the same seat.

chunks.title: Bradgate Electoral Division
chunks.text: Bradgate Electoral Division is a County Council electoral division in Leicestershire, England, taking its name from Bradgate Park which is at the centre of the division.

chunks.title: Bradgate Electoral Division
chunks.text: It includes the villages of Anstey, Cropston, Thurcaston, Newtown Linford, Ulverscroft, Swithland, Woodhouse and Woodhouse Eaves, and is currently represented by David Snartt.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: Albert Lane (1873 – 29 December 1950) was an Australian politician.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: He was born in Windsor, New South Wales, and studied at public schools.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: He became an accountant and business manager.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: In 1917 he contested the federal election as the unsuccessful Nationalist candidate for the safe Labor seat of Dalley.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: In 1922 he was elected to the New South Wales Legislative Assembly as one of four members for the seat of Balmain, representing the Nationalist Party of Australia.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: The seat was abolished in 1927.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: Lane contested the 1931 federal election as the United Australia Party candidate for Barton, creating history by defeating both the incumbent member for Barton, James Tully, and the member for Martin, John Eldridge, who, as a member of the Lang Labor breakaway party, was attempting to transfer to Barton.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: Lane held the seat until 1940, when he was defeated by future Labor leader H. V. Evatt.

chunks.title: Albert Lane (politician)
chunks.text: He died in 1950.

chunks.title: Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974
chunks.text: The Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974 (No. 7/1974) was a law in Ireland which provided for parliamentary constituencies for the 21st Dáil Éireann.

chunks.title: Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974
chunks.text: It was a review of parliamentary constituencies passed in Ireland by the governing Fine Gael–Labour Party National Coalition.

chunks.title: Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974
chunks.text: It was intended to secure their re-election, but instead backfired disastrously resulting in a landslide victory for their main opponents in Fianna Fáil.

chunks.title: Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974
chunks.text: Consequently, the word "Tullymander" – combining the name of the minister James Tully with the word "gerrymander" – was coined.

chunks.title: Penparcau
chunks.text: Penparcau is a village and an electoral division in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, Wales, constituting the south side of Aberystwyth.

chunks.title: Penparcau
chunks.text: Aberystwyth-Penparcau is the largest electoral division in Ceredigion and elects two county councillors.

chunks.title: Penparcau
chunks.text: It is also the 3rd most populated division in Ceredigion (3,122 Census 2011) after Aberystwyth and Cardigan.

chunks.title: Penparcau
chunks.text: Penparcau is also the name of the village which covers a portion of the electoral division alongside Southgate and Caeffynnon.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: A district electoral division (DED; Irish: "Toghroinn ceantair" ) is a former name given to a low-level territorial division in Ireland.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: In 1994, both district electoral divisions and wards (the equivalent of district electoral divisions within the five county boroughs) were renamed as electoral divisions (the boundaries and names of the DEDs and wards themselves remained unchanged).

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: In the Republic of Ireland, DEDs are the smallest legally defined administrative areas in the state for which small area population statistics (SAPS) are published from the Census.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: In the European Union, Local administrative units (LAUs) are basic components of Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics (NUTS) regions.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: For each EU member country, two levels of Local Administrative Units (LAU) are defined: LAU-1 and LAU-2, which were previously called NUTS-4 and NUTS-5 respectively, until the NUTS regulation went into force in July 2003.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: The District electoral division is at the level of LAU-2.

chunks.title: District electoral division
chunks.text: There are a total of 3,440 electoral divisions within the Republic of Ireland.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: The Division of Maribyrnong is an Australian Electoral Division in the state of Victoria.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: It is located in the inner north-western suburbs of Melbourne.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: It covers the suburbs of Aberfeldie, Airport West, Avondale Heights, Braybrook, Essendon, Kealba, Keilor East, Maribyrnong, Moonee Ponds, Niddrie, St. Albans and Sunshine North.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: Due to redistributions, the division has been slowly moving west.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: It originally covered the suburbs of Footscray and North Melbourne.

chunks.title: Division of Maribyrnong
chunks.text: According to the 2011 census, Maribyrnong has the highest proportion of Catholics in any Commonwealth Electoral Division in Australia with 41.6% of the population.

chunks.title: Nik Stauskas
chunks.text: Nikolas Tomas Stauskas (born October 7, 1993) is a Canadian professional basketball player for the Philadelphia 76ers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Nik Stauskas
chunks.text: A native of Mississauga, Ontario, Stauskas played two seasons of National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) competition for the Michigan Wolverines ending with the 2013–14 team before declaring for the NBA draft.

chunks.title: Nik Stauskas
chunks.text: Stauskas was drafted eighth overall in the 2014 NBA draft by the Sacramento Kings, for which he began his NBA career.

chunks.title: Nik Stauskas
chunks.text: Towards the end of his rookie season, Stauskas was tagged with the nickname Sauce Castillo after a closed captioning error resulted in a social media meme.

chunks.title: Nik Stauskas
chunks.text: Stauskas, whose family is of Lithuanian heritage, is a member of the Canadian national basketball team.

chunks.title: Jordan Hill (basketball)
chunks.text: Jordan Craig Hill (born July 27, 1987) is an American professional basketball player who last played for the Minnesota Timberwolves of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Jordan Hill (basketball)
chunks.text: Hill played college basketball for the Arizona Wildcats before he was drafted eighth overall in the 2009 NBA draft by the New York Knicks.

chunks.title: Jordan Hill (basketball)
chunks.text: He was traded in the middle of his rookie season to the Houston Rockets, and was again involved in a midseason trade to the Los Angeles Lakers in 2011–12.

chunks.title: Jordan Hill (basketball)
chunks.text: In 2015, he signed with the Indiana Pacers, but departed after just one season, signing with the Timberwolves in 2016.

chunks.title: Ally Malott
chunks.text: Ally Malott (born October 31, 1992) is an American basketball player who last played for the Washington Mystics of the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA).

chunks.title: Ally Malott
chunks.text: She was drafted eighth overall in the 2015 WNBA draft.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: Lars Niklas Sundström (born June 6, 1975) is a former professional ice hockey player who started his professional career in Modo Hockey.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He was drafted eighth overall in the 1993 NHL Entry Draft by the New York Rangers.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He was also on Wayne Gretzky's line.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He was not known for his goal scoring ability, but for his defensive play.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He was traded to the San Jose Sharks in 1999, and to the Montreal Canadiens in 2003.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: Sundström plays forward and specializes in defensive roles.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: When he was a junior player he formed a line in Modo with future NHL stars Peter Forsberg and Markus Näslund.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He wore the number 24 for the San Jose Sharks and the New York Rangers but wore the number 37 for the Montreal Canadiens.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: After 11 NHL seasons, he returned to play in Sweden at the start of the 2006–07 season, leading Modo to a surprise title during his first season, scoring several vital goals in the playoffs.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: He formed an effective partnership with Norwegian Per-Åge Skrøder, leading to Skrøder winning the top scorer rankings in 2009.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: Modo still missed the playoffs that year, despite Sundström having the best plus-minus rating in the entire series.

chunks.title: Niklas Sundström
chunks.text: On December 3, 2013, Sundström officially announced his retirement.

chunks.title: Rudy Gay
chunks.text: Rudy Carlton Gay Jr. (born August 17, 1986) is an American professional basketball player for the San Antonio Spurs of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Rudy Gay
chunks.text: The 6'8" small forward played college basketball for the University of Connecticut before being drafted eighth overall in the 2006 NBA draft by the Houston Rockets; he was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies days later.

chunks.title: Channing Frye
chunks.text: Channing Thomas Frye (born May 17, 1983) is an American professional basketball player for the Cleveland Cavaliers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Channing Frye
chunks.text: The 6'11" power forward–center played college basketball for the University of Arizona.

chunks.title: Channing Frye
chunks.text: He was drafted eighth overall by the New York Knicks in the 2005 NBA draft, and was the first college senior to be selected in that draft.

chunks.title: Channing Frye
chunks.text: He has previously played for the Knicks, Portland Trail Blazers, Phoenix Suns, and Orlando Magic.

chunks.title: Terrence Ross
chunks.text: Terrence James Elijah Ross (born February 5, 1991) is an American professional basketball player for the Orlando Magic of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Terrence Ross
chunks.text: He played college basketball for the University of Washington, where he was a first-team All-Pac-12 selection before being drafted eighth overall in the 2012 NBA draft by the Toronto Raptors.

chunks.title: Terrence Ross
chunks.text: As a rookie, he was crowned champion of the 2013 Sprite Slam Dunk Contest.

chunks.title: Terrence Ross
chunks.text: In January 2014, he became the first player in NBA history to score 50 or more points in a game while averaging fewer than 10 points per game.

chunks.title: Joey Galloway
chunks.text: Joseph Scott Galloway (born November 20, 1971) is a former American football wide receiver in the National Football League and current college football analyst with ESPN.

chunks.title: Joey Galloway
chunks.text: He was drafted by the Seattle Seahawks eighth overall in the 1995 NFL Draft and also played for the Dallas Cowboys, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers and Washington Redskins.

chunks.title: Joey Galloway
chunks.text: He played college football at Ohio State.

chunks.title: Mark Andaya
chunks.text: Mark Anthony Gozar Andaya (born March 22, 1981 in Manila, Philippines) is a Filipino former professional basketball player.

chunks.title: Mark Andaya
chunks.text: He was drafted eighth overall by Talk 'N Text in the 2006 PBA draft.

chunks.title: Mark Andaya
chunks.text: After playing for the Philippine Patriots in the ASEAN Basketball League, he was acquired by the Barako Bull Energy Boosters.

chunks.title: Mark Andaya
chunks.text: He also had a brief stint with the Misamis Oriental Meteors in the Liga Pilipinas.

chunks.title: ESPN College Football Friday Primetime
chunks.text: ESPN College Football Friday Primetime is a live game presentation of Division 1-A college football on ESPN or sometimes ESPN2.

chunks.title: ESPN College Football Friday Primetime
chunks.text: There is no main sponsor.

chunks.title: ESPN College Football Friday Primetime
chunks.text: The game telecast airs every Friday night at 7:45pm ET during the college football regular season.

chunks.title: ESPN College Football Friday Primetime
chunks.text: In 2017, the games will be announced by Adam Amin and Dusty Dvoracek.

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: Indian actress Tabu, also credited as Tabbu, has appeared in Hindi, Telugu, English, Tamil, Malayalam and Bengali films.

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: Tabu's first credited role came as a teenager in Dev Anand's "Hum Naujawan" (1985), and her first major role was in the Telugu film "Coolie No. 1" (1991).

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: In 1994, she starred in two Hindi filmsthe romance "Pehla Pehla Pyar" and the action drama "Vijaypath"and received the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut for the latter.

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: After appearing in a series of poorly received films, including "Prem" and "Saajan Ki Baahon Mein" (both 1995), the year 1996 was key for Tabu.

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: Her performance as a young woman affected by the Punjab insurgency in Gulzar's "Maachis" (1996) proved to be a breakthrough for her, and won her the National Film Award for Best Actress.

chunks.title: Tabu filmography
chunks.text: Also that year, Tabu won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress – Telugu for the romance "Ninne Pelladata", and featured alongside Govinda and Karisma Kapoor in the commercially successful comedy film "Saajan Chale Sasural".

chunks.title: My Boyfriend Is Type B
chunks.text: My Boyfriend is Type B () is a 2005 South Korean romantic comedy film.

chunks.title: My Boyfriend Is Type B
chunks.text: The basic premise of the film comes from the blood type personality theory, which claims that a person's blood type can determine their personality traits.

chunks.title: My Boyfriend Is Type B
chunks.text: The heroine is type A (conservative and introverted) while her love interest is type B (passionate and irresponsible).

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: Richa Chadda is an Indian actress who works in Hindi films.

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: After debuting with a bit role in the comedy film "Oye Lucky!

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: Lucky Oye!

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: " (2008), she worked as a supporting actress in several films.

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: Her major breakthrough was a supporting role in the film noir gangster saga "Gangs of Wasseypur" (2012), where her role as the bellicose and extremely foul-tongued wife of a gangster earned her a Filmfare award.

chunks.title: Richa Chadda
chunks.text: Her sole foray into mainstream cinema has been as a supporting character in "Goliyon Ki Rasleela Ram-Leela" (2013).

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: Priyanka Chopra is an Indian actress who has established herself as a leading actress of Indian cinema.

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: She made her Bollywood debut in 2003 spy thriller "".

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: The same year, Chopra's role in the box-office hit musical "Andaaz" won her the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut.

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: In 2004, she starred in the highly successful comedy "Mujhse Shaadi Karogi" and garnered critical acclaim for her breakthrough role in the thriller "Aitraaz" which earned her the Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role and a second Best Supporting Actress nomination.

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: Chopra starred in six films in 2005, including "" and "Bluffmaster!

chunks.title: Priyanka Chopra filmography
chunks.text: In 2006, she starred in two of the highest-grossing films of the yearthe superhero film "Krrish" and the action thriller "Don".

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: Shari Headley (born July 15, 1964) is an American actress and former model.

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: Headley is best known for her role as Lisa McDowell in the 1988 box-office hit romantic comedy film, "Coming to America".

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: Headley also has appeared in films "The Preacher's Wife" (1996) and "Johnson Family Vacation" (2004).

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: On television, Headley starred as Det. Mimi Reed in the ABC daytime soap opera, "All My Children" on regular basic from 1991 to 1994.

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: As lead actress, she starred in the Fox short-lived drama series, "413 Hope St." (1997-1998), for which she received NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actress in a Drama Series nomination.

chunks.title: Shari Headley
chunks.text: In 2014, Headley began starring as villainous Jennifer Sallison in the Oprah Winfrey Network primetime soap opera, "The Haves and the Have Nots".

chunks.title: Brian Backer
chunks.text: Brian Backer (born December 5, 1956) is an American actor who has starred in film and on television.

chunks.title: Brian Backer
chunks.text: He is best known for his role in the 1982 hit comedy film "Fast Times at Ridgemont High" as shy teenager Mark "Rat" Ratner.

chunks.title: Brian Backer
chunks.text: His other films include the 1985 comedy film "Moving Violations" (playing the role of Scott Greeber) and the 1987 comedy film "".

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: Meryl Streep throughout the 2000s appeared in many cinematic and theatrical productions.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2001, Streep’s voice appeared in the animated film A.I. Artificial Intelligence.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: Streep that same year cohosted the annual Nobel Peace Prize concert as well as appeared in the popular play The Seagull.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2002, Streep appeared in the films Adaptation and The Hours.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2003, Streep appeared unaccredited in the comedy Stuck on You and starred in the HBO play adaptation Angels in America.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2004, Streep was awarded the AFI Life Achievement Award and in that same year starred in the films The Manchurian Candidate and Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2005, Streep starred in the film Prime.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: Streep began 2006 with the film A Prairie Home Companion and that same year starred in The Devil Wears Prada and the stage production Mother Courage and Her Children.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2007, Streep appeared in the films Dark Matter, Rendition, Evening, and Lions for Lambs.

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s

chunks.title: Meryl Streep in the 2000s
chunks.text: In 2009, Streep starred in Julie & Julia and It’s Complicated as well as loaning her voice to the animated film Fantastic Mr. Fox.

chunks.title: Tamanchey
chunks.text: Tamanchey (English: Gun ) is an Indian romantic crime comedy film released on 10 October 2014.

chunks.title: Tamanchey
chunks.text: The film is directed by Navneet Behal and stars Nikhil Dwivedi and Richa Chadda in leads.

chunks.title: Rajasree
chunks.text: Rajasree (Telugu: మెజెస్టి, born 1945), also known as Rajasri or Rajashri, is a noted South Indian film actress from 1956 to 1979.

chunks.title: Rajasree
chunks.text: She is particularly famous for her portrayal as princess in several folklore Telugu movies opposite N. T. Rama Rao and Tadepalli Lakshmi Kanta Rao and for acting alongside Ravichandran in the Tamil comedy films – Neeyum Nannum, Kadhalikka Neram Illai and Delhi Mappilai.

chunks.title: Rajasree
chunks.text: Notable among Rajasri's roles in non-folklore social films in Tamil are as Nimmi in Tamil hit comedy film "Kaadhalikka Neramillai", remade as "Preminchi Choodu" in Telugu, as movie star Bhama in Tamil film "Bama Vijayam".

chunks.title: Rajasree
chunks.text: She was credited as Gracy in the Malayalam movies she starred in her career since her debut film "Bharya" (1962) directed by Kunchakko.

chunks.title: Rajasree
chunks.text: Rajasree went on to do 200 films spread across the languages – Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam (as Gracy) and Hindi from beginning of 1956 to 1979.

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: Sandra Bullock is an American actress who made her film debut with a minor role in the 1987 thriller "Hangmen".

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: She made her television debut in the television film "Bionic Showdown: The Six Million Dollar Man and the Bionic Woman" (1989) and played the lead role in the short-lived sitcom "Working Girl" (1990) before making her breakthrough starring in the action film "Speed" (1994).

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: She starred with Sylvester Stallone in "Demolition Man" (1994).

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: Bullock founded her own production company, Fortis Films, and starred in the romantic comedy "While You Were Sleeping" in 1995.

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: Her performance in the film earned her first nomination for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical.

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: The following year, Bullock starred with Matthew McConaughey in the film adaptation of John Grisham's novel "A Time to Kill" (1996).

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: In 1997, she reprised her "Speed" role in the sequel, "".

chunks.title: Sandra Bullock filmography
chunks.text: The following year, Bullock starred in the romantic comedy "Practical Magic", voiced Miriam in the animated biblical film "The Prince of Egypt" and also executive produced her first film, the romantic drama "Hope Floats".

chunks.title: Western Airlines
chunks.text: Western Airlines (IATA: WA, ICAO: WAL, Call sign: Western) was a large airline based in California, with operations throughout the western United States including Alaska and Hawaii, and western Canada, as well as to New York City, Boston, Washington D.C. and Miami on the U.S. east coast and also into Mexico.

chunks.title: Western Airlines
chunks.text: The airline also served other international destinations such as London, England and Nassau, Bahamas during its existence.

chunks.title: Western Airlines
chunks.text: Western had hubs at Los Angeles International Airport, Salt Lake City International Airport, and the former Stapleton International Airport in Denver.

chunks.title: Western Airlines
chunks.text: Before it merged with Delta Air Lines in 1987 it was headquartered at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

chunks.title: Western Airlines
chunks.text: The company's slogan for many years was ""Western Airlines...The Only Way To Fly!""

chunks.title: Air Vanuatu
chunks.text: Air Vanuatu is an airline with its head office in the Air Vanuatu House, Port Vila, Vanuatu.

chunks.title: Air Vanuatu
chunks.text: It is Vanuatu's national flag carrier, operating to Australia, New Zealand and points in the South Pacific.

chunks.title: Air Vanuatu
chunks.text: Its main base is Bauerfield International Airport, Port Vila.

chunks.title: Bauerfield International Airport
chunks.text: Bauerfield International Airport (IATA: VLI, ICAO: NVVV) is an airport located in Port Vila, Vanuatu.

chunks.title: Bauerfield International Airport
chunks.text: The airport is relatively small in size, but its runway has the capability and length to accept jets up to the Airbus A330.

chunks.title: Bauerfield International Airport
chunks.text: It serves as the hub for Vanuatu's flag carrier airline, Air Vanuatu.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Lenelle Moïse (born 1980) is a poet, actress and playwright born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Currently based in the United States, she performs at colleges throughout the country, presenting work about race, gender, class, immigration and sexuality.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Her spoken word CD "Madivinez" won the 2007 Patchwork Majority Radio Album Award for Best Solo Album.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Moïse was a member of the permanent ensemble cast in the Culture Project's premiere production of "Rebel Voices", a play by Rob Urbinati based on Howard Zinn and Anthony Arnove's book "Voices of a People's History of the United States."

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: In 2008, she developed a two-person vocal musical about art, infamy and race called "EXPATRIATE", also at the Culture Project, in which she co-starred with Karla Cheatham-Mosley.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: When she was a junior at Ithaca College, Lenelle co-wrote "Sexual Dependency", a feature film by Bolivian filmmaker Rodrigo Bellot who was a schoolmate at the time.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: The film went on to win the International Film Critics' Award at the Locarno International Film Festival in Switzerland.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Moïse also wrote and starred in Mara Alper's short experimental video "To Erzulie" which premiered at the Berlin Sommerfest der Literaturen in July 2002.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: She has completed her own experimental shorts "Blue Passersby Eyes" and "Atlantic Soul."

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Her homemade music video "Pied Piper" was an official selection of the International Museum of Women 2007 Online Film Festival.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Her essays and poems are published in a number of anthologies, most recently "Word Warriors: 35 Women Leaders of the Spoken Word Revolution" (Seal Press).

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: Her debut book "Haiti Glass" (City Lights Publishers, April 2014), part of the Sister Spit series, is a collection of verse and prose.

chunks.title: Lenelle Moïse
chunks.text: She experiments with collage as a form of meditative practice and nonlinear storytelling.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: Champion Air was an airline based in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: It operated general charter services to sports teams, vacation wholesalers and government agencies.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: It also offered limited scheduled service.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: Its main base was Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport, with hubs at Denver International Airport, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport, McCarran International Airport in Las Vegas, Lambert-St.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: Louis International Airport, and Will Rogers World Airport in Oklahoma City.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: The airline ceased all operations on May 31, 2008.

chunks.title: Champion Air
chunks.text: Until its shutdown, the airline was a prime contractor for the Justice Prisoner and Alien Transportation System.

chunks.title: Líneas Aéreas Azteca
chunks.text: Líneas Aéreas Azteca ] was an airline based in Mexico City, Mexico.

chunks.title: Líneas Aéreas Azteca
chunks.text: It operated domestic scheduled services and international services to the USA.

chunks.title: Líneas Aéreas Azteca
chunks.text: Its main base was Mexico City International Airport, with a hub at General Abelardo L. Rodríguez International Airport, Tijuana.

chunks.title: Indochina Airlines
chunks.text: Indochina Airlines (Vietnamese: "Hãng Hàng không Đông Dương" ) was a Vietnamese airline based in Ho Chi Minh City.

chunks.title: Indochina Airlines
chunks.text: It was the first operational private airline based in Vietnam, originally licensed in May 2008 as Air Speed Up (Vietnamese: "Hãng hàng không Tăng Tốc" ).

chunks.title: Indochina Airlines
chunks.text: The founder and chairman of the board was Vietnamese musician Hà Hùng Dũng.

chunks.title: Indochina Airlines
chunks.text: Indochina Airlines began selling tickets on 12 November 2008 and launched its first commercial flight from Tân Sơn Nhất International Airport in Ho Chi Minh City to Nội Bài International Airport in Hanoi and Đà Nẵng International Airport in Đà Nẵng on 25 November 2008.

chunks.title: Indochina Airlines
chunks.text: After a series of difficulties, including unresolved debts and a drop in customers, Indochina Airlines ceased flying on November 25, 2009; its schedule was revoked two days later.

chunks.title: Cebu Pacific
chunks.text: Cebu Air, Inc., operating as Cebu Pacific (), is a Philippine low-cost airline based on the grounds of Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA Terminal 3), Pasay City, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.

chunks.title: Cebu Pacific
chunks.text: It offers scheduled flights to both domestic and international destinations.

chunks.title: Cebu Pacific
chunks.text: Its main base is Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila, with other hubs at Mactan-Cebu International Airport, Clark International Airport, Kalibo International Airport Francisco Bangoy International Airport, and Iloilo International Airport.

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: The International Islamic Relief Organization (IIRO; Arabic: هيئة الإغاثة الإسلامية العالمية‎ ‎ ), also known as the International Islamic Relief Organization of Saudi Arabia (IIROSA), is a charity based in Saudi Arabia founded by the Muslim World League in 1978.

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: It is a full member of The Conference of NGOs, where it serves on the board.

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: The IIRO is included in a list of some of the UNHCR's major NGO partners and has been involved in many joint programmes with UN Agencies and intergovernmental (such as the World Health Organization) and non-governmental organisations.

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: It has enjoyed consultative status on the United Nations Economic and Social Council since 1995.

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: It was the first Islamic NGO to gain observer status with the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

chunks.title: International Islamic Relief Organization
chunks.text: It is also a member of the International Humanitarian City based in Dubai, UAE.

chunks.title: Aeromar
chunks.text: Transportes Aeromar, S.A. de C.V, doing business as Aeromar, is an airline based in Hangar 7 of Zone D of the General Aviation Terminal at Mexico City International Airport in Venustiano Carranza, Mexico City, Mexico.

chunks.title: Aeromar
chunks.text: Aeromar operates scheduled domestic services in Mexico and international services to the United States.

chunks.title: Aeromar
chunks.text: Its main base is Mexico City International Airport.

chunks.title: Danielle Renfrew
chunks.text: Danielle Renfrew Behrens is an accomplished independent producer with credits ranging from grassroots documentaries to major motion pictures.

chunks.title: Danielle Renfrew
chunks.text: She has worked with top-notch talent including Quentin Tarantino, Elizabeth Banks, Courteney Cox, Nick Cannon, and Lily Tomlin.

chunks.title: Danielle Renfrew
chunks.text: She has premiered seven films at the Sundance Film Festival, including GRANDMA starring Lily Tomlin and KURT COBAIN: MONTAGE OF HECK, which received a jaw-dropping seven primetime Emmy Award Nominations.

chunks.title: Danielle Renfrew
chunks.text: Other credits include: Lauren Greenfield’s THE QUEEN OF VERSAILLES, which was the opening night film of Sundance 2012 and received the Grand Jury Prize for Directing, Fox Searchlight’s WAITRESS, and Sony Classics’ NOVEMBER and GROOVE.

chunks.title: Danielle Renfrew
chunks.text: Danielle is a Sundance Women’s Initiative Fellow and has served as an Advisor to Sundance’s Creative Producing Program and Film Independent’s Filmmaker Labs.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck
chunks.text: Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck (also billed as Cobain: Montage of Heck) is a 2015 documentary film about Nirvana lead singer Kurt Cobain.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck
chunks.text: The film was directed by Brett Morgen and premiered at the 2015 Sundance Film Festival.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck
chunks.text: It received a limited theatrical release worldwide and premiered on television in the United States on HBO on April 24, 2015.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck
chunks.text: The documentary chronicles the life of Kurt Cobain from his birth in Aberdeen, Washington in 1967, through his troubled early family life and teenage years and rise to fame as front man of Nirvana, up to his death in April 1994 in Seattle at the age of 27.

chunks.title: Suicide of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: On April 8, 1994, Kurt Cobain, the lead singer of the grunge band Nirvana, was found dead at his home, located at 171 Lake Washington Boulevard East in Seattle, Washington.

chunks.title: Suicide of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: Forensic analysis at the time determined he had killed himself on April 5.

chunks.title: Suicide of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: The Seattle Police Department incident report states: "Kurt Cobain was found with a shotgun across his body, had a visible head wound and there was a suicide note discovered nearby."

chunks.title: Suicide of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: The King County Medical Examiner noted puncture wounds on the inside of both the right and left elbow.

chunks.title: Suicide of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: Prior to his death, Cobain had checked out of a drug rehabilitation facility and had been reported as suicidal by his wife Courtney Love.

chunks.title: Montage of Heck: The Home Recordings
chunks.text: Montage of Heck: The Home Recordings is a compilation of home recordings by Kurt Cobain that were used as the soundtrack to the film "", released posthumously on November 13, 2015 by Universal Music.

chunks.title: Montage of Heck: The Home Recordings
chunks.text: The album was released as a standard 13-track CD, a 31-track deluxe album, and an audio cassette.

chunks.title: Montage of Heck: The Home Recordings
chunks.text: The 13-track standard version focuses on the music found on Cobain's personal cassettes and the 31-track deluxe version showcases tracks from the documentary including spoken word, demos and full songs.

chunks.title: Love and Death: The Murder of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: Love and Death: The Murder of Kurt Cobain, published by Simon & Schuster, is a collaborative investigative journalism book written by Ian Halperin and Max Wallace purporting to show that rock star Kurt Cobain, believed to have committed suicide, was in fact murdered, possibly at the behest of his wife Courtney Love.

chunks.title: Love and Death: The Murder of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: It is a follow-up to the authors' 1998 bestseller on the same subject, "Who Killed Kurt Cobain?"

chunks.title: Love and Death: The Murder of Kurt Cobain
Love and Death: The Murder of Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: The book is based on 30 hours of revealing audiotaped conversations, exclusively obtained by the authors, between Courtney Love's private investigator, Tom Grant, and her and Cobain's entertainment attorney, Rosemary Carroll, who both dispute the official finding of suicide and believe Cobain was in fact murdered.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: Last Days is a 2005 American drama film directed, produced and written by Gus Van Sant.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: It is a fictionalized account of the last days of a musician, loosely based on Kurt Cobain.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: It was released to theaters in the United States on July 22, 2005 and was produced by HBO.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Michael Pitt as the character Blake, based on Kurt Cobain.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: Lukas Haas, Asia Argento, Scott Patrick Green and Thadeus A. Thomas also star in the film.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: This is the first film from Picturehouse, a joint venture between Time Warner's New Line Cinema and HBO Films subsidiaries to release art house, independent, foreign, and documentary films.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: The film received mixed reviews from critics.

chunks.title: Last Days (2005 film)
chunks.text: Though meant to be based on Kurt Cobain, it contradicts the factual evidence of Cobain's final days.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: Kurt Cobain About a Son is a documentary about Kurt Cobain that debuted at the 2006 Toronto International Film Festival.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: It is directed by AJ Schnack.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: It was produced by Sidetrack Films.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: It features audio of interviews between Cobain and journalist Michael Azerrad done for the book "", set over ambient cinematography of the places which Kurt Cobain called his home, mainly Aberdeen, Olympia, and Seattle.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: The film played at numerous film festivals, and was nominated for the 2007 Independent Spirit's Truer than Fiction Award.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: The DVD, which was released by Shout!

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: Factory in February 2008, includes bonus interviews and commentary by Michael Azerrad and A.J. Schnack.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: Shout!

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain: About a Son
chunks.text: Factory also put out the documentary's first Blu-ray edition on October 6, 2009.

chunks.title: Soaked in Bleach
chunks.text: Soaked in Bleach is an American docudrama directed by Benjamin Statler, who co-wrote and produced it with Richard Middelton and Donnie Eichar.

chunks.title: Soaked in Bleach
chunks.text: The film details the events leading up to the death of Kurt Cobain, as seen through the perspective of Tom Grant, the private detective who was hired by Courtney Love to find Cobain, her husband, shortly before his death in 1994.

chunks.title: Soaked in Bleach
chunks.text: It also explores the premise that Cobain's death was not a suicide.

chunks.title: Soaked in Bleach
chunks.text: The film stars Tyler Bryan as Cobain and Daniel Roebuck as Grant, with Sarah Scott portraying Courtney Love and August Emerson as Dylan Carlson.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park
chunks.text: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park, also called Kurt Cobain Landing, is the first official, full-scale memorial to Kurt Cobain in his hometown of Aberdeen, Washington.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park
chunks.text: A welcome sign to the city, placed in 2005, more than ten years after Cobain's death, obliquely says "come as you are" but does not mention him by name and was the first official recognition of Cobain.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park
chunks.text: The park, initially built in Felony Flats on city-owned land near his Aberdeen home in 2011, and maintained by local volunteers as Kurt Cobain Landing, was adopted by the city of Aberdeen in 2015, 20 years after his death.

chunks.title: Kurt Cobain Memorial Park
chunks.text: As recently as 2011, a motion not to rename the adjacent Young Street Bridge after Cobain was applauded at a city council meeting.

chunks.title: Teen Spirit: The Tribute to Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: Teen Spirit: The Tribute to Kurt Cobain is a documentary about Nirvana band leader Kurt Cobain.

chunks.title: Teen Spirit: The Tribute to Kurt Cobain
chunks.text: Released in September 1996 it is significant as the first unofficial Kurt Cobain or Nirvana documentary to be available as a home video.

chunks.title: Virginia State Route 160
chunks.text: State Route 160 (SR 160) is a primary state highway in the U.S. state of Virginia.

chunks.title: Virginia State Route 160
chunks.text: Known as the Trail of the Lonesome Pine, the state highway runs 8.02 mi from the Kentucky state line on top of Black Mountain, where the highway continues north as Kentucky Route 160 (KY 160), east to SR 68 in Appalachia.

chunks.title: Alabama State Route 160
chunks.text: State Route 160 (SR 160) is an 18.415 mi state highway in Blount County, in the north-central part of the U.S. state of Alabama.

chunks.title: Alabama State Route 160
chunks.text: The western terminus of the highway is at an intersection with U.S. Route 31 (US 31) on the southern edge of Smoke Rise.

chunks.title: Alabama State Route 160
chunks.text: This intersection is just east of US 31's interchange with Interstate 65 (I-65 exit 284).

chunks.title: Alabama State Route 160
chunks.text: The eastern terminus of the highway is at an intersection with US 231 and Blount County Route 1 (CR 1) in Cleveland.

chunks.title: Alabama State Route 160

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry
chunks.text: Stress in the aviation industry is a common phenomenon composed of three sources, which are physiological stressors, psychological stressors, and environmental stressors.

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry
chunks.text: Chronic levels of stress can negatively impact one's health, job performance and cognitive functioning.

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry
chunks.text: Being exposed to stress does not always negatively influence humans because it can motivate people to improve and help them adapt to a new environment.

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry
chunks.text: Unfortunate accidents start to occur when a pilot is under excessive stress, as it dramatically affects his or her physical, emotional, and mental conditions.

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry
chunks.text: Stress "jeopardizes decision-making relevance and cognitive functioning" and it is a prominent cause of pilot error.

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry

chunks.title: Stress in the aviation industry

chunks.title: Strafing

chunks.text: This means that, although ground attack using automatic weapons fire is very often accompanied with bombing or rocket fire, the term "strafing" does not specifically include the last two.

chunks.text: The term "strafing" can cover either fixed guns, or aimable (flexible) guns.

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: Fixed guns firing directly ahead tend to be more predominant on fixed wing aircraft, while helicopters tend to use aimable weapons which can be fired in many different directions independent of the direction the aircraft is pointing in (in most cases, flexible guns on a fixed wing aircraft are for defense purposes only, although they can sometimes be used to fire on ground targets to limited effect).

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: Some fixed wing aircraft, like fighter-bombers, are capable of flying either air-combat missions or ground attack missions (P-47 Thunderbolt), while others are dedicated ground-attack types (Il-2 Shturmovik).

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: In cases where an aircraft is capable of both types of combat, when it is assigned to a ground attack role, and thus expected to be using the guns mostly for strafing, the fixed weapons are often mounted so that the convergence point is lower and at a greater range than would be used for air combat.

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: This is helpful because it allows the pilot to aim at a target without having to dive towards the ground as steeply, decreasing the risk of collision with the ground and increasing the amount of firing time available before having to pull up, and it also increases the range from the target, helping avoid anti-aircraft fire and potential damage from exploding targets.

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: Because of the low altitude and relatively low airspeed required for accurate strafing, it is very risky for the pilot, who is exposed not only to the risk of flight-into-terrain and obstacles such as power lines, but also to anti-aircraft weapons, including surface-to-air missiles (both vehicle mounted and hand-held), anti-aircraft artillery and small caliber weapons fire (such as machine guns and small arms).

chunks.title: Strafing
chunks.text: Planes purposely designed for ground attack may include additional armour around and underneath the cockpit and other vulnerable areas such as engines to protect the pilot and key flight components, while aircraft designed mostly for air combat tend to have most of their armor placed to protect directly ahead or to the rear, where fire from other aircraft is most likely, leaving them more vulnerable to fire from directly below or to the sides, where much ground fire often comes from.

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: Flextime (also spelled flexitime [British English], flex-time) is a flexible hours schedule that allows workers to alter workday start and finish times.

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: In contrast to traditional work arrangements that require employees to work a standard 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. day, flextime typically involves a "core" period of the day during which employees are required to be at work (e.g., between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.), and a "bandwidth" period within which all required hours must be worked (e.g., between 5:30 a.m. and 7:30 p.m.).

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: The working day outside of the "core" period is "flexible time", in which employees can choose when they work, subject to achieving total daily, weekly or monthly hours within the "bandwidth" period set by employers, and subject to the necessary work being done .

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: The total working time required of employees on flextime schedules is the same as that required under traditional work schedules.

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: A flextime policy allows staff to determine when they will work, while a flexplace policy allows staff to determine where they will work.

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: Advantages include allowing employees to coordinate their work hours with public transport schedules, with the schedules of their children, and with daily traffic patterns to avoid high congestion times such as rush hour.

chunks.title: Flextime
chunks.text: Some claim that flexible working will change the nature of the way we work.

chunks.title: L'Oiseau bleu (Metzinger)
