chunks.text: He was voted PSL Referee of the Season in 2000–01 and 2010–11 and has been an international referee since 2003.

chunks.title: South Australian Brewing Company
chunks.text: The South Australian Brewing Company, Limited, was established in 1888 by the amalgamation of Sir Edwin Smith's Kent Town Brewery and W. K. Simms's West End Brewery.

chunks.title: South Australian Brewing Company
chunks.text: T. A. Nation was the first brewer and G. B. Bryant the general manager.

chunks.title: South Australian Brewing Company
chunks.text: His board of directors comprised S. J. Jacobs (later Managing Director), Sir Lancelot Stirling, K.C.M.G., Edward Fitzgerald, LL.D., and H. W. Morphett.

chunks.title: W. H. Clark (brewer)
chunks.text: William Henry Clark ( – between 1862 and 1873) was a brewer in South Australia, the founder of the Halifax Street brewery, an antecedent of the West End brewery.

chunks.title: Matthew Vandrau
chunks.text: Matthew James Vandrau (born 22 July 1969) is a retired English-born South African-raised cricketer.

chunks.title: Matthew Vandrau
chunks.text: Having moved to South Africa at an early age, he first appeared in first-class cricket playing for Transvaal in 1990.

chunks.title: Matthew Vandrau
chunks.text: He moved to England in 1993 to play for Derbyshire in two stints between 1993 and 1997.

chunks.title: Emu (beer)
chunks.text: Emu is a beer brand name now owned by Lion.

chunks.title: Emu (beer)
chunks.text: It was originally brewed by the Emu Brewery in 1908 until the brewery's sale to the Swan Brewery in 1927.

chunks.title: Emu (beer)
chunks.text: The production of the Emu branded beer continued from a separate autonomous brewery in Perth until 1978, and then was relocated to a combined brewery in Canning Vale.

chunks.title: Emu (beer)
chunks.text: In 2014 Lion Nathan moved production of both the Emu and Swan beer brands to the company's West End Brewery in South Australia.

chunks.title: West End Draught
chunks.text: West End Draught is a South Australian lager brewed by the South Australian Brewing Company, which was later acquired by Lion Nathan in 1993 .

chunks.title: West End Draught
chunks.text: West End Draught is a full strength beer with an alcohol percentage of 4.5%.

chunks.title: Copper Coast Wines
chunks.text: Copper Coast Wines is a South Australian brewer founded in 2005 to supply beer for the biennial Kernewek Lowender Festival held in the Copper Coast region of South Australia.

chunks.title: Tim Swiel
chunks.text: Timothy Gregory Swiel (born 4 June 1993 in Taunton) is an English-born South African rugby union player, currently playing for Harlequins in the Aviva Premiership.

chunks.title: Tim Swiel
chunks.text: His regular position is fly-half.

chunks.title: Vacuum Diagrams
chunks.text: Vacuum Diagrams is a collection of science fiction short stories by British writer Stephen Baxter.

chunks.title: Vacuum Diagrams
chunks.text: The collection connects the novels of the Xeelee Sequence and also shows the history of mankind in the Xeelee universe, and ultimately the universe.

chunks.title: Vacuum Diagrams
chunks.text: While each short story in the collection is self-contained, the stories are presented as being contained in the context of the first story, "Eve", about a man (seemingly Jack Raoul from the portion of the timeline concerned with the silver ghosts) who is forced to witness the events in the short stories by a god-like being.

chunks.title: Vacuum Diagrams
chunks.text: "Eve" acts as a structure for the short stories, with an introduction at the beginning of "Vacuum Diagrams", short scenes occurring between each "era" (with "Eve" character explaining and introducing the next section), and an ending that wraps up the plot for the "Eve" story itself.

chunks.title: Vacuum Diagrams
chunks.text: "Vacuum Diagrams" won the Philip K. Dick Award in 1999.

chunks.title: Mai Al-Nakib
chunks.text: Mai Al-Nakib is author of "The Hidden Light of Objects", a collection of linked short stories published by Bloomsbury in 2014.

chunks.title: Mai Al-Nakib
chunks.text: The collection won the Edinburgh International Book Festival's 2014 First Book Award, the first collection of short stories to win.

chunks.title: Mai Al-Nakib
chunks.text: Her short stories have appeared in "Ninth Letter""," "The First Line", and the anthology "Novel of the World""."

chunks.title: Mai Al-Nakib
chunks.text: Two of her stories received honorable mention in "Glimmer Train" competitions.

chunks.title: Mai Al-Nakib
chunks.text: "The Hidden Light of Objects" is her first collection of short stories.

chunks.title: The Rest of the Robots
chunks.text: The Rest of the Robots is a collection of eight short stories and two full-length novels by American writer Isaac Asimov, published in 1964.

chunks.title: The Rest of the Robots
chunks.text: The stories, centred on positronic robots, are all part of the "Robot" series, most of which take place in the "Foundation" universe.

chunks.title: The Rest of the Robots
chunks.text: Another collection of short stories about robots, "I, Robot", was re-published in the previous year, which is why Asimov chose to title the collection as "The Rest of the Robots".

chunks.title: The Rest of the Robots
chunks.text: None of the short stories in this collection were in "I, Robot", however all of them were later included in "The Complete Robot", and both novels about Elijah Baley were also published separately.

chunks.title: Richard Ford
chunks.text: Richard Ford (born February 16, 1944) is an American novelist and short story writer.

chunks.title: Richard Ford
chunks.text: His best-known works are the novel "The Sportswriter" and its sequels, "Independence Day", "The Lay of the Land" and "Let Me Be Frank With You", and the short story collection "Rock Springs", which contains several widely anthologized stories.

chunks.title: Rock Springs (short story collection)
chunks.text: Rock Springs is a collection of short stories by author Richard Ford, published in 1987 and largely dealing with dysfunctional mothers and fathers and their effects on young male narrators.

chunks.title: Ambulanse
chunks.text: Ambulance (Original title: "Ambulanse") is a collection of short stories by the Norwegian author Johan Harstad, published in 2002.

chunks.title: Ambulanse
chunks.text: The collection contains eleven short stories, all connected to each other.

chunks.title: Ambulanse
chunks.text: The main character in one of the stories shows up as an 'extra' in the next, and several stories are told from different angles.

chunks.title: Ambulanse
chunks.text: The overall link between the short stories is an ambulance driving through an unnamed city.

chunks.title: J. J. Syvrud
chunks.text: J. J. Syvrud (born May 10, 1977) is a former American football linebacker who played one season with the New York Jets of the National Football League.

chunks.title: J. J. Syvrud
chunks.text: He was drafted by the New York Jets in the seventh round of the 1999 NFL Draft.

chunks.title: J. J. Syvrud
chunks.text: He played college football at Jamestown College and attended Rock Springs High School in Rock Springs, Wyoming.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: Richard Marsh (12 October 1857 – 9 August 1915) was the pseudonym of the English author born Richard Bernard Heldmann.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: A best-selling and prolific author of the late 19th century and the Edwardian period, Marsh is best known now for his supernatural thriller novel "The Beetle", which was published the same year as Bram Stoker's "Dracula" (1897), and was initially even more popular.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: "The Beetle" remained in print until 1960.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: Marsh produced nearly 80 volumes of fiction and numerous short stories, in genres including horror, crime, romance and humour.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: Many of these have been republished recently, beginning with "The Beetle" in 2004.

chunks.title: Richard Marsh (author)
chunks.text: Marsh's grandson Robert Aickman was a notable writer of short "strange stories".

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Richard Henderson Honaker (born March 10, 1951) is a lawyer in Rock Springs, Wyoming who was nominated on March 19, 2007, by U.S. President George W. Bush to serve as one of three U.S. District Judges for the District of Wyoming.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: The nomination was given the highest "well qualified" rating by the judicial evaluation committee of the American Bar Association.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Honaker was initially recommended to Bush by U.S. Senator Craig L. Thomas of Wyoming, who died some three months later.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Honaker had co-chaired Thomas' reelection campaign in 2006 in Rock Springs.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Honaker never obtained a Senate vote on his confirmation.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: The succession of Barack Obama to the presidency ended his candidacy.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Had he been confirmed, Honaker would have succeeded Judge Clarence A. Brimmer in Cheyenne.

chunks.title: Richard Honaker
chunks.text: Nancy D. Freudenthal was subsequently nominated and confirmed to the seat.

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories (published in England as The Artificial Nigger and Other Tales) is a collection of short stories by American author Flannery O'Connor.

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: The collection was first published in 1955.

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: The subjects of the short stories range from baptism ("The River") to serial killers ("A Good Man Is Hard to Find") to human greed and exploitation ("The Life You Save May Be Your Own").

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: The majority of the stories include jarring violent scenes that make the characters undergo a spiritual change.

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: The short stories commonly have tones of Catholicism related to life and death scenarios.

chunks.title: A Good Man Is Hard to Find and Other Stories
chunks.text: For instance, in the story "A Good Man Is Hard To Find" the villain states, "She would have been a good woman if it had been somebody there to shoot her every minute of her life."

chunks.title: Mehrdad Raissi Ardali
chunks.text: Mehrdad Raissi Ardali (Persian: مهرداد رئیسی اردلی‎ ‎ ), born (1978--)20 1978 in Iran, is a prolific Iranian voice actor, dubbing director, founder, director, CEO and Quality Control Manager of Glory Entertainment (The Association of Tehran Young Voice Actors).

chunks.title: Mehrdad Raissi Ardali
chunks.text: He has also provided Persian voices for several animation characters, including famous characters such as Donkey in "Shrek", Marty in "Madagascar", "" and "", Buck in "", Bolt in "Bolt", Carl Fredricksen in "Up", Flynn Rider in "Tangled", The Once-ler in "The Lorax", RJ in "Over the Hedge", Francesco Bernoulli in "Cars 2", Mr. Ping in "Kung fu Panda", Ramon in "Happy Feet 2", The Man in the Yellow Hat in "Curious George", Raoul in "A Monster in Paris", Kevin in "", Barry in "Bee Movie", Bunnymund in "Rise of the Guardians", Guy in "The Croods" and Kristoff in "Frozen (2013 film)".

chunks.title: Kanako Takatsuki
chunks.text: Kanako Takatsuki (高槻 かなこ , Takatsuki Kanako , born September 25, 1993) is a Japanese voice actress and singer born in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan.

chunks.title: Kanako Takatsuki
chunks.text: She is currently affiliated with Amuse and her single is released under label Victor Entertainment.

chunks.title: Scott Irby-Ranniar
chunks.text: Scott Irby-Ranniar (born September 15, 1984) is an American actor and singer born in Harlem, New York.

chunks.title: Scott Irby-Ranniar
chunks.text: He is well known for originating the role of Young Simba in the Broadway production of The Lion King in 1997.

chunks.title: Scott Irby-Ranniar
chunks.text: He is a former member of the band Steel Train.

chunks.title: I See the Light
chunks.text: "I See the Light" is a song written by composer Alan Menken and lyricist Glenn Slater for Walt Disney Animation Studios' 50th animated feature film "Tangled" (2010).

chunks.title: I See the Light
chunks.text: A duet originally recorded by American recording artist and actress Mandy Moore and American actor Zachary Levi in their respective film roles as main characters Rapunzel and Flynn Rider, the folk-inspired pop ballad serves as both the film's love and theme song.

chunks.title: I See the Light
chunks.text: Lyrically, "I See the Light" describes the developing romantic relationship between Rapunzel and Flynn, and is featured as the seventh track on the film's soundtrack album.

chunks.title: Zachary Levi
chunks.text: Zachary Levi Pugh ( ; born September 29, 1980) is an American actor and singer.

chunks.title: Zachary Levi
chunks.text: He is best known for playing Chuck Bartowski in the series "Chuck".

chunks.title: Zachary Levi
chunks.text: He also appeared in the films "", "Tangled", and "".

chunks.title: Pascal and Maximus
chunks.text: Pascal and Maximus are a pair of fictional characters who first appear in Walt Disney Pictures' 50th animated feature film "Tangled" (2010) as supporting characters, and subsequently star in its short "Tangled Ever After "(2012), television film "" and television series "".

chunks.title: Pascal and Maximus
chunks.text: Created by directors Nathan Greno and Byron Howard, both characters are voiced by American actor Frank Welker in "Tangled"; in "Tangled Ever After", Welker reprises his role as Pascal while Greno replaces the actor as Maximus.

chunks.title: Pascal and Maximus
chunks.text: A comedic chameleon and horse duo, Pascal and Maximus serve as sidekicks to main characters Rapunzel and Flynn Rider, respectively.

chunks.title: Milira
chunks.text: Milira Jones (born September 27, 1969), better known as Milira, is an American R&B/soul singer born in Hollis, New York.

chunks.title: Milira
chunks.text: She released two albums in the 1990s and scored four charting singles on Billboard's R&B singles chart, with two peaking top 40.

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: Stuart Charno (born September 29, 1956) is an American actor.

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: He has been a stand-up comic and has starred in film and on television.

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: His first role was in the 1981 horror film "Friday the 13th Part 2".

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: Other notable appearances of his include the 1985 comedy film "Just One of the Guys" (as Harold "Reptile" Sherpico) and the 1986 film "Modern Girls", in which he appeared with "Just One of the Guys" co-star Clayton Rohner.

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: Charno has made guest appearances on various television shows including "M*A*S*H", "The X-Files", "Chicago Hope", "Team Knight Rider", and "Profiler".

chunks.title: Stuart Charno
chunks.text: He also received story credits on three episodes of "" ("", "" and "").

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: Kenji Matsuda (松田 賢二 , Matsuda Kenji , born September 23, 1971 in Osaka) is a Japanese actor.

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: Matsuda began acting in high school when a girl he had a crush on convinced him to join the theatre club.

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: He later joined the sho-gekijo theatrical troupe Haiyu-Za.

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: Nowadays known for roles such as Kagero in the low-budget films "Shinobi: The Law of Shinobi", 2002, and its sequels "Shinobi: Runaway", 2005 (not related to the 2005 film ""), "Shinobi: Hidden Techniques", and "Shinobi: A Way Out".

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: He is probably best known in Japan for numerous roles he has played in the tokusatsu genre: starting with "Kamen Rider Hibiki" as Zaoumaru Zaitsuhara/Kamen Rider Zanki (as well as related characters: Buddhist monk Kamen Rider Touki in the movie special - a Sengoku-era version of Zanki - and an alternate Zanki from the Hibiki World as depicted in "Kamen Rider Decade"), and in "Kamen Rider Kiva" as Jiro/Garulu (who made a cameo appearance in "").

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: He has also appeared in a cameo in the "Kamen Rider G" special and has a recurring role in the series .

chunks.title: Kenji Matsuda
chunks.text: He played the role of Raizo Gabi in "Shuriken Sentai Ninninger".

chunks.title: Flynn Rider
chunks.text: Flynn Rider (born Eugene Fitzherbert) is a fictional character who appears in Walt Disney Animation Studios' 50th animated feature film "Tangled", its short film "Tangled Ever After", and the 2017 television series "".

chunks.title: Flynn Rider
chunks.text: The character is voiced by American actor Zachary Levi, who decided to audition for the role upon learning that he would also be providing the character's singing voice.

chunks.title: Flynn Rider
chunks.text: Levi's duet with singer and co-star Mandy Moore, "I See the Light", would go on to become the actor's first professionally recorded song and musical debut.

chunks.title: Alexis Knapp
chunks.text: Alexis Merizalde Knapp (born July 31, 1989) is an American actress and singer.

chunks.title: Alexis Knapp
chunks.text: She is known for her role as Stacie Conrad in the musical films "Pitch Perfect" (2012) , "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015) and the upcoming "Pitch Perfect 3".

chunks.title: Alexis Knapp
chunks.text: She is also known for her role of Alexis in the party film "Project X" (2012), and her role on the first season of the TBS comedy "Ground Floor".

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 3
chunks.text: Pitch Perfect 3 is an upcoming American musical comedy film directed by Trish Sie and written by Kay Cannon.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 3
chunks.text: A sequel to "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015) and the third and final installment in the "Pitch Perfect" trilogy, the film will star Anna Kendrick, Anna Camp, Rebel Wilson, Brittany Snow, Hailee Steinfeld, Alexis Knapp, Ester Dean, Hana Mae Lee, Chrissie Fit, Kelley Jakle and Shelley Regner, with Elizabeth Banks and John Michael Higgins.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 3
chunks.text: The film is scheduled to be released on December 22, 2017.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 2
chunks.text: Pitch Perfect 2 is a 2015 American musical comedy film directed and co-produced by Elizabeth Banks and written by Kay Cannon.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 2
chunks.text: It is a sequel to the 2012 film "Pitch Perfect" and the second installment in the "Pitch Perfect" series.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 2
chunks.text: The film centers on the fictional Barden University and The Bellas, an all-female a cappella singing group.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 2
chunks.text: The film features an ensemble cast, including Anna Kendrick, Rebel Wilson, Hailee Steinfeld, Brittany Snow, Alexis Knapp, Hana Mae Lee, Ester Dean, Chrissie Fit, Kelley Jakle and Shelley Regner as The Bellas.

chunks.title: Pitch Perfect 2
chunks.text: It was released on May 15, 2015 by Universal Pictures.

chunks.title: Kelley Jakle
chunks.text: Kelley Alice Jakle (born June 27, 1989) is an American actress and singer-songwriter.

chunks.title: Kelley Jakle
chunks.text: She is best known for her role as Jessica in "Pitch Perfect" (2012) and its sequel "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015).

chunks.title: Kelley Jakle
chunks.text: She is also known for her appearances on the first and second seasons of "The Sing-Off" in 2009 and 2010.

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: Anna Ragsdale Camp (born September 27, 1982) is an American actress and singer.

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: She is known for her role as Sarah Newlin in "True Blood", and her recurring roles in "Mad Men", "The Good Wife", and "The Mindy Project".

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: She is also known for her role as Aubrey Posen in "Pitch Perfect" (2012), "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015), and the upcoming "Pitch Perfect 3" (2017).

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: She made her Broadway debut in the 2008 production of "A Country House" and played Jill Mason in the 2008 Broadway revival of "Equus".

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: In 2012, she was nominated for a Drama Desk Award for her performance in the Off-Broadway play "All New People".

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: Camp played Jane Hollander, a researcher for the fictitious "News of the Week" magazine in the Amazon series "Good Girls Revolt."

chunks.title: Anna Camp
chunks.text: She also had a role in the 2011 film "The Help".

chunks.title: Shelley Regner
chunks.text: Shelley Anne Regner (born December 21, 1988) is an American actress and singer known for her role as Ashley in the musical films "Pitch Perfect" (2012) and its sequel "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015).

chunks.title: Shelley Regner
chunks.text: She will be returning for the third installment, "Pitch Perfect 3" (2017).

chunks.title: Hana Mae Lee
chunks.text: Hana Mae Lee (born September 28, 1988) is an American actress, model, comedian, and fashion designer.

chunks.title: Hana Mae Lee
chunks.text: She is best known for playing Lilly Okanakurama in the 2012 film "Pitch Perfect" and its sequel "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015).

chunks.title: Hana Mae Lee
chunks.text: She also owns her own fashion line titled "Hanamahn".

chunks.title: Flashlight (Jessie J song)
chunks.text: "Flashlight" is a song recorded by British singer and songwriter Jessie J for the soundtrack to the film "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015).

chunks.title: Flashlight (Jessie J song)
chunks.text: The song was written by Sia Furler, Christian Guzman, Jason Moore and Sam Smith.

chunks.title: Flashlight (Jessie J song)
chunks.text: The song was originally obtained when one pre-ordered the "Pitch Perfect 2" soundtrack in the United States, beginning on 23 April 2015; it later became available for download on its own.

chunks.title: Flashlight (Jessie J song)
chunks.text: "Flashlight" was released in the United Kingdom on 11 May 2015 both on the soundtrack and as a stand-alone single.

chunks.title: Flashlight (Jessie J song)
chunks.text: "Flashlight" was particularly successful in Australia, peaking at number two, and number seven in New Zealand.

chunks.title: Skylar Astin
chunks.text: Skylar Astin Lipstein (born September 23, 1987), known professionally as Skylar Astin, is an American actor and singer.

chunks.title: Skylar Astin
chunks.text: He became known for portraying Jesse Swanson in the musical films "Pitch Perfect" (2012) and "Pitch Perfect 2" (2015).

chunks.title: Skylar Astin
chunks.text: He was also in the original cast of the Broadway musical "Spring Awakening", and has since appeared in films such as "Hamlet 2" (2008), "Taking Woodstock" (2009), "Cavemen" (2013), and "21 & Over" (2013).

chunks.title: Brittany Snow
chunks.text: Brittany Anne Snow (born March 9, 1986) is an American actress, producer, and singer.

chunks.title: History of British Airways
chunks.text: British Airways (BA) is the flag carrier airline of the United Kingdom.

chunks.title: History of British Airways
chunks.text: It is the largest airline in the UK based on fleet size, international flights and international destinations.

chunks.title: History of British Airways
chunks.text: British Airways was considered the largest UK airline by passenger numbers from its creation in 1974 until 2008, when it was displaced by low-cost rival EasyJet.

chunks.title: History of British Airways
chunks.text: Since its inception, British Airways has been centred at its main hub at London Heathrow Airport, with a second major hub at London Gatwick Airport.

chunks.title: Hawaiian Airlines
chunks.text: Hawaiian Airlines (Hawaiian: "" ) is the largest airline in Hawaii.

chunks.title: Hawaiian Airlines
chunks.text: It is the 8th largest commercial airline in the US, and is based in Honolulu, Hawaii.

chunks.title: Hawaiian Airlines
chunks.text: The airline operates its main hub at Honolulu International Airport and a secondary hub out of Kahului Airport on the island of Maui.

chunks.title: Hawaiian Airlines
chunks.text: Hawaiian Airlines operates flights to Asia, Hawaii, New Zealand, Australia and the United States Mainland.

chunks.title: Hawaiian Airlines
chunks.text: Hawaiian Airlines is owned by Hawaiian Holdings, Inc. of which Mark Dunkerley is the current President and Chief Executive Officer.

chunks.title: Taichung County
chunks.text: Taichung County was a county in central Taiwan, the Republic of China, that surrounded but did not include the former Taichung City.

chunks.title: Taichung County
chunks.text: The county capital was Fengyuan.

chunks.title: Taichung County
chunks.text: The name "Taichung" means "central Taiwan".

chunks.title: Jet Airways
chunks.text: Jet Airways (Hindi: जेट एयरवेज , "Jet Eyaravej") is a major Indian international airline based in Mumbai.

chunks.title: Jet Airways
chunks.text: In July 2017, it was the second largest airline in India after IndiGo with an 18.2% passenger market share.

chunks.title: Jet Airways
chunks.text: It operates over 300 flights daily to 68 destinations worldwide from its main hub at Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport and secondary hubs at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Chennai International Airport, Indira Gandhi International Airport, Kempegowda International Airport and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport.

chunks.title: Taichung International Airport
chunks.text: Taichung International Airport () (IATA: RMQ, ICAO: RCMQ) , previously known as Ching Chuan Kang Airport (), is an international airport located in Taichung City, Taiwan (ROC) for both commercial and military purposes.

chunks.title: Taichung International Airport
chunks.text: It is also the third international airport in Taiwan, with scheduled services to Mainland China, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam.

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: China Airlines (CAL) () () is the flag carrier and largest airline of the Republic of China (Taiwan).

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: It is headquartered in Taoyuan International Airport and has 12,607 regular employees.

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: China Airlines operates over 1,400 flights weekly to 118 airports in 115 cities (including codeshare) across Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania.

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: The cargo division operates 91 pure freighter flights weekly.

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: The carrier was, in 2013, the 29th and 10th largest airline in the world in terms of passenger revenue per kilometer (RPK) and freight RPK, respectively.

chunks.title: China Airlines
chunks.text: China Airlines has three airline subsidiaries: Mandarin Airlines operates flights to domestic and low-demand regional destinations; China Airlines Cargo, a member of Skyteam Cargo, operates a fleet of freighter aircraft and manages its parent airline's cargo-hold capacity; Tigerair Taiwan is a low-cost carrier established by China Airlines and Singaporean airline group Tigerair Holdings and is wholly owned by China Airlines Group.

chunks.title: Blue Line (Taichung Metro)
chunks.text: The Taichung BRT Blue Line (Chinese: 臺中快捷巴士) was a Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system located in Taichung which stretched from Taichung Station to Providence University on the main road, Taiwan Boulevard.

chunks.title: Blue Line (Taichung Metro)
chunks.text: The line was 17.1 km in length with 21 stations.

chunks.title: Blue Line (Taichung Metro)
chunks.text: It was the first BRT line in Taiwan.

chunks.title: Blue Line (Taichung Metro)
chunks.text: The line was converted to dedicated bus lane for conventional buses on July 8, 2015 and the BRT is no longer in operation.

chunks.title: Mandarin Airlines
chunks.text: Mandarin Airlines () is an airline based in Taipei, Taiwan, whose parent company is China Airlines.

chunks.title: Mandarin Airlines
chunks.text: The Taiwanese carrier operates domestic and regional international flights, while its parent company focuses on international operations.

chunks.title: Mandarin Airlines
chunks.text: Charter services are also operated by the company.

chunks.title: Mandarin Airlines
chunks.text: Its other main hub is the Taichung Airport.

chunks.title: AirAsia
chunks.text: AirAsia Berhad () is a Malaysian low-cost airline headquartered near Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

chunks.title: AirAsia
chunks.text: It is the largest airline in Malaysia by fleet size and destinations.

chunks.title: AirAsia
chunks.text: AirAsia Group operates scheduled domestic and international flights to more than 165 destinations spanning 25 countries.

chunks.title: AirAsia
chunks.text: Its main hub is klia2, the low-cost carrier terminal at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Sepang, Selangor, Malaysia.

chunks.title: AirAsia

chunks.title: Red Dawson
chunks.text: Lowell Potter "Red" Dawson (December 20, 1906 – June 10, 1983) was an American football coach for the University of Pittsburgh Panthers and the Tulane Green Wave at the collegiate level and the AAFC's Buffalo Bills at the professional level.

chunks.title: Red Dawson
chunks.text: He learned the craft of football coaching at the University of Minnesota under Bernie Bierman, his former coach at Tulane.

chunks.title: Red Dawson
chunks.text: At Pitt he coached future Pro Football Hall of Famer Joe Schmidt and won Pittsburgh's "Dapper Dan" sports award in 1952.

chunks.title: Red Dawson

chunks.title: Red Dawson

chunks.title: Red Dawson

chunks.title: The Highwaymen (country supergroup)
chunks.text: The Highwaymen was a country music supergroup composed of four of the genre's biggest artists well known for their pioneering influence on the outlaw country subgenre: Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, and Kris Kristofferson.

chunks.title: The Highwaymen (country supergroup)
chunks.text: Active as a group between 1985 and 1995, these four artists recorded three major label albums as The Highwaymen: two on Columbia Records and one for Liberty Records.

chunks.title: The Highwaymen (country supergroup)
chunks.text: Their Columbia works produced three chart singles, including the number one "Highwayman" in 1985.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: "Highwayman" is a song written by American singer-songwriter Jimmy Webb, about a soul with incarnations in four different places in time and history: as a highwayman, a sailor, a construction worker on the Hoover Dam, and finally as a captain of a starship.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: The song was influenced by the real-life hanged highwayman Jonathan Wild.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: The dam builder verse alludes to the deaths of over one hundred men during the construction of Hoover Dam near Boulder City, Nevada.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: Webb first recorded the song on his album "El Mirage", released in May 1977.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: The following year, Glen Campbell recorded his version, which was released on his 1979 album "Highwayman".

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: In 1985, the song became the inspiration for the naming of the supergroup The Highwaymen, which featured Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, and Kris Kristofferson.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: Their first album, "Highwayman", became a number one platinum-selling album, and their version of the song went to number one on the Hot Country Songs "Billboard" chart in a twenty-week run.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: Their version earned Webb a Grammy Award for Best Country Song in 1986.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: The song has since been recorded by other artists.

chunks.title: Highwayman (song)
chunks.text: Webb himself included a different version on his 1996 album "Ten Easy Pieces", a live version on his 2007 album "Live and at Large", and a duet version with Mark Knopfler on 2010 album "Just Across the River".

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: Wildwood Flower is the last solo album from June Carter Cash.

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: It was released in 2003 on the Dualtone record label, four months after her death and only a few days before the death of Johnny Cash, who provides backing vocals, making this the final release of his lifetime.

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: It was produced by their son, John Carter Cash.

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: The album's opening track, "Keep on the Sunny Side" was a Carter Family anthem that June Carter Cash had previously recorded twice with Johnny Cash: for the 1964 Carter Family album of the same title, and for the 1974 Johnny Cash album "The Junkie and the Juicehead Minus Me".

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: "The Road to Kaintuck", written by June, had previously been recorded by her husband on several occasions for Columbia Records.

chunks.title: Wildwood Flower (album)
chunks.text: The medley of "Church in the Wildwood"/"Lonesome Valley" had been a regular part of Johnny Cash concerts in the 1970s.

chunks.title: El Mirage (album)
chunks.text: El Mirage is the sixth album by American singer-songwriter Jimmy Webb, released in May 1977 by Atlantic Records.

chunks.title: El Mirage (album)
chunks.text: This was the first album for which Webb handed production and arrangement duties on to another person, George Martin, producer of The Beatles.

chunks.title: El Mirage (album)
chunks.text: The album is notable for containing "The Highwayman", a song that later provided both the name and first hit for The Highwaymen, a country supergroup comprising Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, Kris Kristofferson, and Willie Nelson.

chunks.title: El Mirage (album)
chunks.text: Jennings also recorded the track "If You See Me Getting Smaller" for his album "Ol Waylon" (1977).

chunks.title: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas
chunks.text: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas is the 41st overall and second Christmas album by country singer Johnny Cash, released on Columbia Records in 1972).

chunks.title: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas
chunks.text: It is his second Christmas album, the first one being the 1963 release entitled "The Christmas Spirit".

chunks.title: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas
chunks.text: The album includes less original Cash material than its predecessor and contains narrations and dialogue featuring his family and friends, between tracks.

chunks.title: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas
chunks.text: In all, three songs were written or co-written by Cash, while two, "Christmas as I Knew It" and "Silent Night", had been featured on "The Christmas Spirit" ("Silent Night" would, in fact, be featured on all four Johnny Cash Christmas albums).

chunks.title: The Johnny Cash Family Christmas
chunks.text: June Carter Cash, Marshall Grant, Tommy Cash, Harold Reid, Larry Butler (who was both Cash's piano player and record producer at this time), Maybelle Carter, Anita Carter, Carl Perkins and Lew DeWitt are among those featured on the album.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: Kenneth Jones (1952–1969), was the son of Helen Myrl Carter (of country music's Carter Family) and of Glenn Jones.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: He is best remembered for a song he wrote called "Sing A Traveling Song" which appeared on Johnny Cash's albums "Hello, I'm Johnny Cash" and "Johnny Cash at Madison Square Garden".

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: Kenneth was Cash's nephew-in-law.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: Cash's second wife, June Carter Cash, was Helen's sister.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: Kenneth, or Kenny as he was also known, wrote many songs and was a talented musician.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: At the time of his death he was under contract with Monument Records and appeared destined for a highly successful career.

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: Following his death the Carter Family recorded one of his songs, "2001 Ballad to the Future".

chunks.title: Kenneth Jones (songwriter)
chunks.text: A few have noted the lyrics as being eerily prophetic of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on the United States which took place more than thirty years after the song was written.

chunks.title: Forty Shades of Green
chunks.text: "Forty Shades of Green" is a song about Ireland, written and first performed by American country singer Johnny Cash.

chunks.title: Forty Shades of Green
chunks.text: Cash wrote the song in 1959 while on a trip to Ireland; it was first released as a B-side of the song "The Rebel–Johnny Yuma" in 1961.

chunks.title: Forty Shades of Green
chunks.text: It is also included in two of Cash's albums: "Ring of Fire: The Best of Johnny Cash", released on Columbia Records in 1963, and "Johnny Cash: The Great Lost Performance – Live at the Paramount Theatre, Asbury Park, New Jersey", recorded live in 1990 and released in 2007.

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash is the 33rd album by American country singer Johnny Cash, released on Columbia Records in 1970 (see 1970 in music).

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: "If I Were a Carpenter", a famous duet with Cash's wife, June Carter Cash, earned the couple a Grammy Award for Best Country Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal in 1971 (see Grammy Awards of 1971); the song also reached No. 2 on the Country charts.

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: This album also includes "To Beat the Devil", the first Kris Kristofferson song covered by Cash; the two would later collaborate numerous times, most famously on "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down".

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: "See Ruby Fall" and "Blistered" were also released as singles, and the album itself reached No. 1 on the country charts and No. 6 on the pop charts.

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: It was certified Gold on 1/29/1970 by the R.I.A.A.

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: The album has been released on CD (Sony Music, Original Album Classics, along with "The Johnny Cash Show" and "Man In Black") and it has been made available on official download sites.

chunks.title: Hello, I'm Johnny Cash
chunks.text: This album is not to be confused with a best-of cd that has the same name.

chunks.text: Abraham Lincoln High School, usually referred to simply as Lincoln High School or Lincoln, is a secondary school located in Des Moines, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln High School (Des Moines, Iowa)
chunks.text: It is one of five secondary schools under the district of the Des Moines Public Schools, and was named after the 16th United States president Abraham Lincoln.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln High School (Des Moines, Iowa)
chunks.text: The school sports team is named after one of President Lincoln's nicknames, the "Rail Splitter" (the "Lincoln Railsplitters" or "Rails").

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln High School (Des Moines, Iowa)

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln High School (Des Moines, Iowa)

chunks.title: Richard Heffner
chunks.text: Richard Douglas Heffner (August 5, 1925 – December 17, 2013) was the creator and host of "The Open Mind," a public affairs television show first broadcast in 1956.

chunks.title: Richard Heffner
chunks.text: He was a University Professor of Communications and Public Policy at Rutgers University and also taught an honors seminar at New York University.

chunks.title: Richard Heffner
chunks.text: He was the author of "A Documentary History of the United States," a verbatim anthology of important public documents in American history, among them the Declaration of Independence, the Gettysburg Address and Martin Luther King's Letter from a Birmingham Jail.

chunks.title: Richard Heffner
chunks.text: Heffner collaborated with Nobel Peace Prize winner Elie Wiesel on the publication of "Conversations With Elie Wiesel", released by Schochen books in 2001.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: Lewis E. "Lew" Lehrman (born August 15, 1938 in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania) is an American investment banker, businessman, Republican politician, economist, and amateur historian who supports the ongoing study of American history based on original source documents.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He was presented the National Humanities Medal at the White House in 2005 for his contributions to American History, the study of President Abraham Lincoln and monetary policy.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He was a member of the Advisory Committee of the Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Commission and the Lincoln Forum.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: In addition to co-authoring "Money and the Coming World Order" and "The Case for Gold", Lehrman's has written "Lincoln at Peoria: The Turning Point," (2008), "The True Gold Standard, Newly Revised and Enlarged, Second Edition" (2012), "Money, Gold, and History" (2013) and "Lincoln "by littles"" (2013).

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He has written for major news publications such as the "Washington Post", the "New York Times" and the "Wall Street Journal", and has lectured widely on American history and economics.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: Lehrman also writes for the "Lincoln Institute" which has created award-winning websites on the 16th President.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: Lehrman achieved national political prominence in a 1982 campaign for Governor of New York, in which he ran against Democratic candidate Mario Cuomo, losing the election by only two percentage points.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He is a senior partner at L. E. Lehrman & Co., an investment firm he established in 1981.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He is also the chairman of the Lehrman Institute, a public policy research and grant making foundation founded in 1972.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He and Richard Gilder were awarded the National Humanities Medal in an Oval Office ceremony on Thursday, November 10, 2005.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: The Medal was presented by President George W. Bush.

chunks.title: Lewis Lehrman
chunks.text: He converted to Catholicism.

chunks.title: Gettysburg Address
chunks.text: The Gettysburg Address is a speech by U.S. President Abraham Lincoln, one of the best-known in American history.

chunks.title: Gettysburg Address
chunks.text: It was delivered by Lincoln during the American Civil War, on the afternoon of Thursday, November 19, 1863, at the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, four and a half months after the Union armies defeated those of the Confederacy at the Battle of Gettysburg.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: Abraham Lincoln: The Man (also called Standing Lincoln) is a larger-than-life size (12 ft ) bronze statue of Abraham Lincoln, the 16th president of the United States.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: The original statue is in Lincoln Park in Chicago, and several replicas have been installed in other places around the world.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: Completed by Augustus Saint-Gaudens in 1887, it has been described as the most important sculpture of Lincoln from the 19th century.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: At the time, the "New York Evening Post" called it "the most important achievement American sculpture has yet produced."

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: Abraham Lincoln II, Lincoln's only grandson, was present, among a crowd of 10,000, at the unveiling.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln: The Man
chunks.text: The artist later created the sculpture in Chicago's Grant Park.

chunks.title: Sexuality of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: The sexuality of Abraham Lincoln (1809–1865), the 16th President of the United States, has been a topic of debate among some scholars.

chunks.title: Sexuality of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: Lincoln was married to Mary Todd from November 4, 1842, until his death on April 15, 1865, and fathered four children with her.

chunks.title: Sexuality of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: The issue came to greater attention due to a 2005 book "The Intimate World of Abraham Lincoln" by psychologist C. A. Tripp, which described Lincoln as allegedly having a detached relationship with women, in contrast with a close male friend he allegedly shared a bed with.

chunks.title: Sexuality of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: According to the book "Lincoln the Unknown", Lincoln chose to spend several months of the year practicing law on a circuit that kept him living separately from his wife.

chunks.title: Sexuality of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: In 1928, a prominent writer had pointed to a close male friend of the young Lincoln as a possible lover that was denounced as absurd at the time.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: Harold Holzer (born February 5, 1949) is a scholar of Abraham Lincoln and the political culture of the American Civil War Era.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: He won the Gilder Lehrman Lincoln Prize and four other awards in 2015 for his book, "Lincoln and the Power of the Press".

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: Holzer served for nine years as co-chairman of the United States Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Commission (ALBC), appointed to the commission by President Bill Clinton in 2000 and elected co-chair by his fellow commissioners.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: In June 2010, he was elected chairman of the ALBC's successor organization, The Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Foundation, which he led through 2016.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: In his professional career, Holzer serves as the Jonathan F. Fanton Director of the Roosevelt House Public Policy Institute at Hunter College.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: He retired in 2015 as Senior Vice President for Public Affairs at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, where for 23 years he was chief spokesman and held responsibility for government relations, admissions, visitor services, and multicultural audience development at the nation's largest art institution.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: He is now a Trustee of The Metropolitan Museum, representing the New York City Comptroller.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: From 2012 to 2015, Holzer served as well as a Roger Hertog Fellow at the New-York Historical Society.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: In 2016-17 he served as Distinguished Visiting Scholar at The Zahava and Moshael Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University.

chunks.title: Harold Holzer
chunks.text: He was also a script consultant to the Steven Spielberg film, "Lincoln", and wrote the official young readers' companion book to the movie.

chunks.title: Lincoln High School (San Diego)
chunks.text: Abraham Lincoln High School (also known as Lincoln High Educational Complex, Lincoln High School, or simply Lincoln), is an urban public high school in San Diego, California, United States.

chunks.title: Lincoln High School (San Diego)
chunks.text: It is part of the San Diego Unified School District.

chunks.title: Lincoln High School (San Diego)
chunks.text: It serves approximately 2100-2700 students in grades 9-12 in the K-12 education system.

chunks.title: Lincoln High School (San Diego)
chunks.text: It is located in the Lincoln Park neighborhood of Southeast San Diego, part of the Encanto neighborhoods.

chunks.title: Lincoln High School (San Diego)
chunks.text: It was named after President Abraham Lincoln.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Foundation
chunks.text: The Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Foundation is the successor organization of the U.S. Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Commission (ALBC), which was created by Congress and the President of the United States to plan the commemoration of Abraham Lincoln’s 200th birthday in 2009.

chunks.title: Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Foundation
chunks.text: The Abraham Lincoln Bicentennial Commission sunset on April 30, 2010

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: This bibliography of Abraham Lincoln is a comprehensive list of written and published works about or by Abraham Lincoln, 16th President of the United States.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: In terms of primary sources containing Lincoln's letters and writings, scholars rely on "The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln", edited by Roy Basler, and others.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: It only includes writings by Lincoln, and omits incoming correspondence.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: In the six decades since Basler completed his work, some new documents written by Lincoln have been discovered.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: Currently, a project is underway at the Papers of Abraham Lincoln to provide "a freely accessible comprehensive electronic edition of documents written by and to Abraham Lincoln".

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: The Papers of Abraham Lincoln completed Series I of their project "The Law Practice of Abraham Lincoln" in 2000.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: They electronically launched "The Law Practice of Abraham Lincoln, Second Edition" in 2009, and published a selective print edition of this series.

chunks.title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
chunks.text: At present they are engaged in locating, digitizing, and transcribing documents for Series II (non-legal, pre-presidential materials) and Series III (presidential materials).

chunks.title: Ed Rasimus
chunks.text: Edward J. Rasimus (September 29, 1942–January 30, 2013) was a retired United States Air Force Major and a veteran fighter pilot of the Vietnam war.

chunks.title: Ed Rasimus
chunks.text: Rasimus flew more than 250 combat missions in F-105 Thunderchief and F-4 Phantom II fighters during the conflict and received the Silver Star, the Distinguished Flying Cross five times, and numerous Air Medals. Rasimus was an award-winning author residing in Northern Texas.

chunks.title: Hermann Kasack
chunks.text: Hermann Robert Richard Eugen Kasack (24 July 1896 – 10 January 1966) was a German writer.

chunks.title: Hermann Kasack
chunks.text: He is best known for his novel "Die Stadt hinter dem Strom" ("The city beyond the river").

chunks.title: Hermann Kasack
chunks.text: Kasack was a pioneer of using the medium broadcast for literature.

chunks.title: Hermann Kasack
chunks.text: He published radio plays also under the pen names Hermann Wilhelm and Hermann Merten.

chunks.title: Tadeusz Sawicz
chunks.text: Tadeusz Władysław Sawicz (13 February 1914 – 19 October 2011) was a Polish World War II fighter pilot.

chunks.title: Tadeusz Sawicz
chunks.text: He served in the Polish Air Force, and after the fall of Poland, he served in the Polish and allied units in France and United Kingdom.

chunks.title: Tadeusz Sawicz
chunks.text: He was the commander of several air units, including the No. 315 Polish Fighter Squadron, 1st Polish Fighter Wing, 3rd Polish Fighter Wing, 131st (Polish) Fighter Wing and 133rd Fighter Wing.

chunks.title: Tadeusz Sawicz
chunks.text: He participated in the Battle of Britain and was ranked as the 82nd highest scoring Polish fighter pilot of the war.

chunks.title: Cecil Chaudhry
chunks.text: Group Captain Cecil Chaudhry (27 August 1941 – 13 April 2012) was a Pakistani academic, human rights activist, and veteran fighter pilot.

chunks.title: Cecil Chaudhry
chunks.text: As a Flight Lieutenant, he fought in the Indo-Pakistani war of 1965 and later, as a Squadron Leader, in the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.

chunks.title: Cecil Chaudhry
chunks.text: During the 1965 war, Chaudhry and three other pilots, under the leadership of Wing Commander Anwar Shamim, attacked the Amritsar Radar Station in a difficult operation.

chunks.title: Cecil Chaudhry
chunks.text: He was awarded the Sitara-e-Jurat (Star of Courage) for his actions during that mission.

chunks.title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
chunks.text: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag is an IMAX film centered on the experiences of a USAF F-15 Eagle fighter pilot, then-Captain John Stratton, who wants to be professionally successful as a fighter pilot.

chunks.title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
chunks.text: It chronicles his experience during USAF Red Flag training at Nellis AFB, a simulated air war designed to train pilots for combat.

chunks.title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
chunks.text: Directed by Stephen Low and presented by Boeing, the film shows how airmen simulate a war without killing one another, as well as the training of military air base firemen, military ordnance crews, midair refueling operations, cockpit views, and other aspects of aerial combat.

chunks.title: Fighter Pilot: Operation Red Flag
chunks.text: The film was released in December 2004.

chunks.title: Lydia Litvyak
chunks.text: Lydia Vladimirovna Litvyak (Лидия Владимировна Литвяк, (August 18, 1921 in Moscow – August 1, 1943 in Krasnyi Luch), also known as Lilya, was a fighter pilot in the Soviet Air Force during World War II.

chunks.title: Lydia Litvyak
chunks.text: With twelve solo victories and four shared kills over a total of 66 combat missions, over about two years of missions, she was the first female fighter pilot to shoot down an enemy plane, the first of two female fighter pilots who have earned the title of fighter ace, and the holder of the record for the greatest number of kills by a female fighter pilot.

chunks.title: Lydia Litvyak
chunks.text: She was shot down near Orel during the Battle of Kursk as she attacked a formation of German planes.

chunks.title: Hermann Göring
chunks.text: Hermann Wilhelm Göring (or Goering; ] ; 12 January 1893 – 15 October 1946) was a German political and military leader as well as one of the most powerful figures in the Nazi Party (NSDAP) that ruled Germany from 1933 to 1945.

chunks.title: Hermann Göring
chunks.text: A veteran World War I fighter pilot ace, he was a recipient of the "Pour le Mérite".

chunks.title: Hermann Göring
chunks.text: He was the last commander of "Jagdgeschwader" 1, the fighter wing once led by Manfred von Richthofen.

chunks.title: World War I
chunks.text: World War I (WWI or WW1), also known as the First World War, the Great War, or the War to End All Wars, was a global war originating in Europe that lasted from 28 July 1914 to 11 November 1918.

chunks.title: World War I
chunks.text: More than 70 million military personnel, including 60 million Europeans, were mobilised in one of the largest wars in history.

chunks.title: World War I
chunks.text: Over nine million combatants and seven million civilians died as a result of the war (including the victims of a number of genocides), a casualty rate exacerbated by the belligerents' technological and industrial sophistication, and the tactical stalemate caused by gruelling trench warfare.

chunks.title: World War I
chunks.text: It was one of the deadliest conflicts in history, and paved the way for major political changes, including revolutions in many of the nations involved.

chunks.title: World War I
chunks.text: Unresolved rivalries still extant at the end of the conflict contributed to the start of the Second World War only twenty-one years later.

chunks.title: Quentin C. Aanenson
chunks.text: Quentin C. Aanenson (April 21, 1921 – December 28, 2008) was a World War II veteran fighter pilot and former captain of the 391st Fighter Squadron, 366th Fighter Group, 9th Air Force, U.S. Army Air Corps.

chunks.title: Quentin C. Aanenson
chunks.text: He flew the P-47 Thunderbolt in the Normandy D-Day invasion and subsequent European campaign.

chunks.title: Ashley Rolfe
chunks.text: Ashley Rolfe is one of the United States Air Force female fighter pilots who qualified to fly McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle.

chunks.title: Ashley Rolfe
chunks.text: As a member of the Massachusetts Air National Guard, she makes history at the 104th Fighter Wing as the first female fighter pilot in the wing’s 70-year history in Aug. 18, 2016.

chunks.title: Ashley Rolfe
chunks.text: She served in 67th Fighter Squadron at Kadena.

chunks.title: Ashley Rolfe
chunks.text: Kadena was Rolfe’s first duty assignment, where she also made history by serving in the 67th Fighter Squadron as the only female F-15 pilot.

chunks.title: Ashley Rolfe
chunks.text: In 2010 she was the only female fighter pilot participating in Exercise Commando Sling that appeared in Air Force TV News "One of a Kind".

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (novel)
chunks.text: Forrest Gump is a 1986 novel by Winston Groom.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (novel)
chunks.text: The title character retells adventures ranging from shrimp boating and ping pong championships, to thinking about his childhood love, as he bumbles his way through American history, with everything from the Vietnam War to college football becoming part of the story.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (character)
chunks.text: Forrest Gump is a fictional character who first appears in the 1986 novel by Winston Groom.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (character)
chunks.text: Forrest Gump also appeared on screen in the 1994 film of the same name directed by Robert Zemeckis.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (character)
chunks.text: Forrest was portrayed as a child by Michael Humphreys and portrayed as an adult by Tom Hanks, who won an Academy Award for the role.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (character)
chunks.text: The portrayal of Forrest in the novel is notably different from the portrayal in the film.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump (character)
chunks.text: He later reappears in the 1995 sequel novel "Gump and Co."

chunks.title: As Summers Die
chunks.text: As Summers Die is a 1986 American made-for-television drama film starring Scott Glenn, Jamie Lee Curtis, Bette Davis and Beah Richards, directed by Jean-Claude Tramont.

chunks.title: As Summers Die
chunks.text: The film is loosely based on Winston Groom's 1980 novel of the same name about greed, bigotry and justice in late 1950s segregationist southern Louisiana.

chunks.title: As Summers Die
chunks.text: It was filmed in Valdosta, Georgia and premiered on HBO on May 18, 1986.

chunks.title: As Summers Die
chunks.text: It was later released on VHS.

chunks.title: My Girl 2
chunks.text: My Girl 2 is a 1994 American comedy-drama film and a sequel to "My Girl" (1991) starring Anna Chlumsky, Dan Aykroyd, Christine Ebersole, Jamie Lee Curtis, Richard Masur, and Austin O'Brien.

chunks.title: My Girl 2
chunks.text: A book based on the script was written by Patricia Hermes in 1994.

chunks.title: A Simple Twist of Fate
chunks.text: A Simple Twist of Fate is a 1994 American comedy-drama film directed by Gillies MacKinnon.

chunks.title: A Simple Twist of Fate
chunks.text: The screenplay by Steve Martin is loosely based on the 1861 novel "Silas Marner" by George Eliot.

chunks.title: Nobody's Fool (1994 film)
chunks.text: Nobody's Fool is a 1994 American comedy-drama film based on the 1993 novel of the same name by Richard Russo.

chunks.title: Nobody's Fool (1994 film)
chunks.text: The film was written for the screen and directed by Robert Benton and stars Paul Newman, Jessica Tandy, Bruce Willis, Melanie Griffith, Dylan Walsh, Pruitt Taylor Vince, Gene Saks, Josef Sommer, Philip Seymour Hoffman, and Philip Bosco.

chunks.title: Nobody's Fool (1994 film)
chunks.text: It was Paramount's final production under its Paramount Communications ownership and Jessica Tandy's final produced film before her death on September 11, 1994.

chunks.title: Gump and Co.
chunks.text: Gump & Co. (or Forrest Gump and Co.) is a 1995 novel by Winston Groom.

chunks.title: Gump and Co.
chunks.text: It is the sequel to his novel "Forrest Gump" (1986), and the Academy Award-winning film of the same name released in 1994, with Tom Hanks.

chunks.title: Gump and Co.
chunks.text: It was written to chronicle Forrest's life throughout the 1980s.

chunks.title: List of accolades received by Forrest Gump
chunks.text: "Forrest Gump" is a 1994 epic romantic comedy-drama film based on the 1986 novel of the same name by Winston Groom.

chunks.title: List of accolades received by Forrest Gump
chunks.text: The film premiered in Los Angeles, California on June 23, 1994 and was released into the United States and Canada on July 6, 1994, opening into 1,595 domestic theaters and earning $24,450,602 on its first weekend.

chunks.title: List of accolades received by Forrest Gump
chunks.text: "Forrest Gump" grossed $677 million and was at its time the fourth highest grossing film of all time (behind only "E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial", "Star Wars IV: A New Hope", and "Jurassic Park").

chunks.title: List of accolades received by Forrest Gump
chunks.text: Despite its praise, it has only a 72% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

chunks.title: Stephan Lichtsteiner
chunks.text: Stephan Lichtsteiner (born 16 January 1984) is a Swiss professional footballer who plays for Italian club Juventus and the Switzerland national team.

chunks.title: Stephan Lichtsteiner
chunks.text: An attacking right-back or wing-back, he is known for his energetic runs down the right wing, as well as his stamina and athleticism, which earned him the nicknames "Forrest Gump" and "The Swiss Express".

chunks.title: Forrest Gump
chunks.text: Forrest Gump is a 1994 American comedy-drama film based on the 1986 novel of the same name by Winston Groom.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump
chunks.text: The film was directed by Robert Zemeckis and stars Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, Gary Sinise, Mykelti Williamson, and Sally Field.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump
chunks.text: The story depicts several decades in the life of Forrest Gump, a slow-witted but kind-hearted, good-natured and athletically prodigious man from Alabama, who witnesses, and in some cases influences, some of the defining events of the latter half of the 20th century in the United States; more specifically, the period between Forrest's birth in 1944 and 1982.

chunks.title: Forrest Gump
chunks.text: The film differs substantially from Winston Groom's novel, including Gump's personality and several events that were depicted.

chunks.title: John Lisle
chunks.text: Sir John Lisle (1610 – 11 August 1664) was an English lawyer and politician who sat in the House of Commons at various times between 1640 and 1659.

chunks.title: John Lisle
chunks.text: He supported the Parliamentarian cause in the English Civil War and was one of the Regicides of King Charles I of England.

chunks.title: John Lisle
chunks.text: He was assassinated by an agent of the crown while in exile in Switzerland.

chunks.title: Christopher Puller
chunks.text: Sir Christopher Puller (1774 – 26 May 1824) was an English lawyer who was briefly Chief Justice of Bengal.

chunks.title: William James (railway promoter)
chunks.text: William James (13 June 1771 – 10 March 1837) was an English lawyer, surveyor, land agent and pioneer promoter of rail transport.

chunks.title: William James (railway promoter)
chunks.text: According to his obituary "He was the original projector of the Liverpool & Manchester and other railways, and may with truth be considered as the father of the railway system, as he surveyed numerous lines at his own expense at a time when such an innovation was generally ridiculed."

chunks.title: Thomas Cromwell
chunks.text: Thomas Cromwell, 1st Earl of Essex ( or ; 1485 – 28 July 1540) was an English lawyer and statesman who served as chief minister to King Henry VIII of England from 1532 to 1540.

chunks.title: Chris Mort
chunks.text: Christopher "Chris" Mort is an English lawyer and former chairman of Newcastle United Football Club.

chunks.title: New Zealand Land Commission
chunks.text: The New Zealand Land Commission was a 19th-century government inquiry into the validity of claims to land purchases by European settlers from the New Zealand Māori people prior to 1840, when New Zealand was annexed to the Australian colony of New South Wales.

chunks.title: New Zealand Land Commission
chunks.text: The inquiry was designed to determine who owned what land, in order to formalise and regulate land ownership in the new colony.

chunks.title: New Zealand Land Commission
chunks.text: The commission carried out its work in two distinct sections—a three-man inquiry to examine purchases in general throughout New Zealand, and a one-man inquiry run by English lawyer William Spain to investigate just those purchases claimed by the New Zealand Company.

chunks.title: New Zealand Land Commission
chunks.text: The commissions were to advise the Governor of which claims were accepted, with the expectation that land owners would then be awarded a Crown grant to their property.

chunks.title: Christopher Mont
chunks.text: Dr. Christopher Mont (1496/7–1572) was a sixteenth-century diplomat, born in Koblenz but in 1531 awarded denization in England, where he became an agent of Thomas Cromwell.

chunks.title: Christopher Peyton
chunks.text: Sir Christopher Peyton was an English lawyer known for his service in Ireland where he oversaw the Peyton Survey, a preliminary investigation in preparation for the Plantation of Munster.

chunks.title: Christopher Peyton
chunks.text: He was made Auditor General of Ireland, and knighted by James I for his service.

chunks.title: Christopher Peyton
chunks.text: He was the younger son of Christopher Peyton of St Edmundsbury; his mother, Joanna (Mildmay) Peyton, was the sister of Sir Walter Mildmay, Chancellor of the Exchequer of England.

chunks.title: Christopher Erle
chunks.text: Christopher Erle (c. 1590 – 1634) was an English lawyer and politician who sat in the House of Commons at various times between 1621 and 1629.

chunks.title: Chris Grocock
chunks.text: Christopher Richard Grocock (born 30 October 1968) is an English lawyer and former professional footballer.

chunks.title: Dark•Matter
chunks.text: Dark•Matter is a science fiction/conspiracy theory campaign setting that was originally published in 1999 by Wizards of the Coast as the second campaign setting for the "Alternity" role-playing game.

chunks.title: Dark•Matter
chunks.text: It was written by Wolfgang Baur and Monte Cook.

chunks.title: Dark•Matter
chunks.text: It was later converted to "d20 Modern" rules and published as a stand-alone book in 2006.

chunks.title: Michael Dobson (author)
chunks.text: Michael S. Dobson (born September 9, 1952 in Charlotte, North Carolina) is an American author in the fields of business (particularly office politics and project management), alternate history novels (relating to WWII) and role-playing game adventures ("D&D", "Indiana Jones", and "Buck Rogers XXVC").

chunks.title: Buck Rogers XXVC
chunks.text: Buck Rogers XXVC (sometimes written as Buck Rogers in the 25th Century) is a game setting created by TSR, Inc. in the late 1980s.

chunks.title: Buck Rogers XXVC
chunks.text: Products based on this setting include novels, graphic novels, a role-playing game (RPG), board game, and video games.

chunks.title: Buck Rogers XXVC
chunks.text: The setting was active from 1988 until 1995.

chunks.title: Campaign setting
chunks.text: A campaign setting is usually a fictional world which serves as a setting for a role-playing game or wargame campaign.

chunks.title: Campaign setting
chunks.text: A "campaign" is a series of individual adventures, and a "campaign setting" is the world in which such adventures and campaigns take place.

chunks.title: Campaign setting
chunks.text: Usually a campaign setting is designed for a specific game (such as the "Forgotten Realms" setting for "Dungeons & Dragons") or a specific genre of game (such as Medieval fantasy, or outer space/science fiction adventure).

chunks.title: Campaign setting
chunks.text: There are numerous campaign settings available both in print and online.

chunks.title: Campaign setting
chunks.text: In addition to published campaign settings available for purchase, many game masters create their own settings, often referred to as "homebrew" settings or worlds.

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: Al-Qadim is an "Arabian Nights"-themed campaign setting for the "Dungeons & Dragons" role-playing game.

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: The setting was developed by Jeff Grubb for TSR, Inc., and was first released in 1992.

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: Al-Qadim is set in the land of Zakhara, called the "Land of Fate".

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: Thematically, the land of Zakhara is a blend of the historical Arabian Empire, the stories of legend, and a wealth of Hollywood cinematic history.

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: Zakhara is a peninsula on the continent of Faerûn in the world of Toril, the locale of the Forgotten Realms campaign setting, although Al-Qadim is designed to stand on its own or be added to any existing campaign setting.

chunks.title: Al-Qadim
chunks.text: The basic campaign setting was divided between two game products: "", a sourcebook describing character creation rules, equipment, and spells unique to the setting, and "Al-Qadim: Land of Fate", a boxed set describing the land of Zakhara, with separate sourcebooks for the players and the Dungeon Master.

chunks.title: Masque of the Red Death (Ravenloft)
chunks.text: Masque of the Red Death is a campaign setting for the "Dungeons & Dragons" role-playing game, named after the Edgar Allan Poe short story of the same name.

chunks.title: Masque of the Red Death (Ravenloft)
chunks.text: The setting was published after the release of the "Ravenloft" campaign setting in 1994 as "Masque of the Red Death and Other Tales", and is regarded as an add-on for that line.

chunks.title: Masque of the Red Death (Ravenloft)
chunks.text: "Masque of the Red Death" has many of the same qualities as "Ravenloft", such as "power checks" and restricted magic, including limited planar travel.

chunks.title: Masque of the Red Death (Ravenloft)
chunks.text: Unlike Ravenloft, the location of the adventures is "Gothic Earth", an 1890s version of Earth where fantasy creatures exist only in the shadows of civilization.

chunks.title: Masque of the Red Death (Ravenloft)
chunks.text: Many notable real-life figures or 19th century literary characters are included for the players to interact with, including Van Helsing, Jack the Ripper and Dorian Gray.

chunks.title: Star Drive
chunks.text: Star Drive (stylized as Star*Drive) is a science fiction campaign setting that was published in 1998 by TSR, Inc. for the "Alternity" role-playing game.

chunks.title: Star Drive
chunks.text: "Alternity"'s first setting was detailed in the "Star Drive Campaign Setting" (1998).

chunks.title: World of Greyhawk Fantasy Game Setting
chunks.text: The World of Greyhawk Fantasy Game Setting and the World of Greyhawk Fantasy World Setting are two closely related publications from TSR, Inc. that detail the fictional "World of Greyhawk" campaign setting for the "Dungeons & Dragons" ("D&D") fantasy roleplaying game.

chunks.title: World of Greyhawk Fantasy Game Setting
chunks.text: Both publications were authored by Gary Gygax, and they were the first stand-alone offerings to provide detailed, comprehensive information regarding a "D&D" campaign setting.

chunks.title: Buck Rogers: Countdown to Doomsday
chunks.text: Buck Rogers: Countdown to Doomsday is a role-playing video game released by Strategic Simulations in 1990 , set in the Buck Rogers XXVC game setting.

chunks.title: Faerûn
chunks.text: Faerûn is a fictional subcontinent, the primary setting of the "Dungeons & Dragons" world of "Forgotten Realms".

chunks.title: Faerûn
chunks.text: It is described in detail in the "Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting" (2001) from Wizards of the Coast, and various locales and aspects are described in more depth in separate campaign setting books.

chunks.title: Faerûn
chunks.text: Around a hundred novels and several computer and video games use the Faerûn setting.

chunks.title: KBXI
chunks.text: KBXI airs an adult hits music format.

chunks.title: KBXI
chunks.text: Licensed to Park City, Montana, United States, the station serves the Billings area.

chunks.title: KBXI

chunks.title: KEWF
chunks.text: The station formerly went by the call letters KGHL- FM before former sister station KGHL- AM 790 was sold to new owner Northern Broadcasting System.

chunks.title: KEWF
chunks.text: Licensed to Billings, Montana, United States, the station serves the Billings area.

chunks.title: KRSQ
chunks.text: Licensed to Laurel, Montana, United States, the station serves the Billings area.

chunks.title: KKBR
chunks.text: KKBR (97.1 FM) - operating as 97.1 Kiss FM - is a commercial radio station in Billings, Montana.

chunks.title: KKBR
chunks.text: Licensed to Billings, Montana, United States, the station serves the Billings area.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: KUMV-TV, channel 8, is the NBC affiliate for Williston, North Dakota.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: The station operates as a semi-satellite of KMOT in Minot, North Dakota.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: This outlet broadcasts a high definition digital signal on VHF channel 8 (or virtual channel 8.1 via PSIP) from a transmitter west of Williston near the North Dakota/Montana border.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: KUMV identifies itself as a station in its own right, but simulcasts all programming from KMOT.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: However, KUMV airs local news inserts into KMOT's weeknight newscasts, airs separate commercials and station identifications.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: The station maintains its studios and advertising sales office at the intersection of Main Street (U.S. 2 Business) and 6th Street East in Williston.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: The Montana portion KUMV's viewing area is within the Mountain time zone, and the station airs 6 p.m. starts to primetime rather than the usual 7 p.m. for the time zone.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: The station can also be seen on Midcontinent cable channel 5 in Williston, and cable channel 8 in most other areas.

chunks.title: KUMV-TV
chunks.text: There is a high definition feed provided on Midcontinent digital channel 605.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: KXMD-TV, channel 11, is the CBS affiliate for Williston, North Dakota.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: The station operates as a semi-satellite of KXMC-TV in Minot, North Dakota.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: This outlet broadcasts a high definition digital signal on UHF channel 14 (or virtual channel 11.1 via PSIP) from a transmitter west of Williston near the North Dakota/Montana border.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: KXMD identifies itself as a station in its own right, but simulcasts all programming from KXMC.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: However, KXMD airs separate commercials and station identifications.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: The station maintains a news bureau and advertising sales office at the intersection of 13th Avenue West and 18th Street West (near U.S. Highway 2/85) in Williston.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: KXMD's viewing area includes most of the Montana portion of this vast market.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: As Montana is within the Mountain Time Zone, primetime programming on KXMD begins at 6 pm rather than at 7 pm for other stations licensed in the Central Time Zone.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: The station can also be seen on Midcontinent cable channel 6 in Williston, and cable channel 11 in most other areas.

chunks.title: KXMD-TV
chunks.text: There is a high definition feed provided on Midcontinent digital channel 606.

chunks.title: KQCD-TV

chunks.title: KQCD-TV
chunks.text: However, KQCD airs separate commercials and station identifications.

chunks.text: KCTR airs a country music format.
