chunks.title: SWX Right Now
chunks.text: SWX Right Now (Sports and Weather Right Now) is a digital subchannel broadcasting high school and college sports, and automated weather information of interest to viewers throughout Eastern Washington state.

chunks.title: SWX Right Now
chunks.text: The channel is operated by Cowles Company and airs over Cowles' three NBC affiliated channels in Eastern Washington, including Spokane's KHQ, KNDO in Yakima and Richland's KNDU, as well as Billings' KULR in Montana, and on most cable systems throughout the markets they serve.

chunks.title: Christmas in Dixie
chunks.text: "Christmas in Dixie" is a song by American country band Alabama.

chunks.title: Christmas in Dixie
chunks.text: It was released as a single in December 1982 from the RCA Records compilation album "A Country Christmas".

chunks.title: Christmas in Dixie
chunks.text: The Christmas song celebrates the holiday in the southern United States.

chunks.title: Christmas in Dixie
chunks.text: The song was included on Alabama's 1985 Christmas album (titled "Alabama Christmas"), and has since been included on many Christmas compilations in both the country and all-genre music fields.

chunks.title: Diamond Rio
chunks.text: Diamond Rio is an American country and Christian country music band.

chunks.title: Diamond Rio
chunks.text: The band was founded in 1982 as an attraction for the Opryland USA theme park in Nashville, Tennessee, and was originally known as the Grizzly River Boys, then the Tennessee River Boys.

chunks.title: Diamond Rio
chunks.text: It was founded by Matt Davenport, Danny Gregg, and Ty Herndon, the last of whom became a solo artist in the mid-1990s.

chunks.title: Diamond Rio
chunks.text: After undergoing several membership changes in its initial years, the band has consisted of the same six members since 1989: Marty Roe (lead vocals, rhythm guitar), Gene Johnson (mandolin, guitar, fiddle, tenor vocals), Jimmy Olander (lead guitar, Dobro, banjo), Brian Prout (drums), Dan Truman (keyboards, organ, synthesizer), and Dana Williams (bass guitar, baritone vocals).

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: Completely is the seventh studio album from American country artists Diamond Rio.

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: Two of the album's singles, "Beautiful Mess" and "I Believe", reached Number One on the "Billboard" U.S. Hot Country Singles & Tracks charts.

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: Also released from this album were "Wrinkles" and "We All Fall Down", which peaked at #18 and #45, respectively, on the country charts.

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: The album was certified gold by the RIAA.

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: "Make Sure You've Got It All" was originally recorded by Collin Raye on his 1998 album "The Walls Came Down".

chunks.title: Completely (Diamond Rio album)
chunks.text: "If You'd Like Some Lovin'" was written and originally recorded by David Ball for his album, "Starlite Lounge" in 1996.

chunks.title: Thy Will
chunks.text: "Thy Will" is a Christian country song recorded by American singer and songwriter Hillary Scott for her collaborative album with the Scott Family, "Love Remains" (2016).

chunks.title: Thy Will
chunks.text: Scott co-wrote the faith-affirming song with Bernie Herms and Emily Weisband.

chunks.title: Thy Will
chunks.text: It was released April 22, 2016 as the lead single from the record and impacted Christian and country radio formats.

chunks.title: Around the Bend (album)
chunks.text: Around the Bend is the nineteenth studio album released in 2008 by American country music artist Randy Travis.

chunks.title: Around the Bend (album)
chunks.text: The album is Travis' first mainstream country music album since 1999's "A Man Ain't Made of Stone", all his other albums in the 2000s were composed of Christian country music.

chunks.title: Around the Bend (album)
chunks.text: It sold 31,000 copies in its first week of release, the best opening week of Travis' career.

chunks.title: Around the Bend (album)
chunks.text: Three singles were released from the album: "Faith in You", "Dig Two Graves" and "Turn It Around", none of which charted.

chunks.title: Live at Oak Tree (Austins Bridge album)
chunks.text: Live at Oak Tree is a live album from the Christian country band Austins Bridge, and part of the "" series from Daywind Records.

chunks.title: Live at Oak Tree (Austins Bridge album)
chunks.text: The album features a behind-the-scenes look at the presentation of the band to record live at the Oak Tree studio in Tennessee.

chunks.title: Live at Oak Tree (Austins Bridge album)
chunks.text: It was released in 2009.

chunks.title: Real Life (I Never Was the Same Again)
chunks.text: "Real Life (I Never Was the Same Again)" is a song written by Neil Thrasher and Jim Janosky, and recorded by American country music artist Jeff Carson.

chunks.title: Real Life (I Never Was the Same Again)
chunks.text: It released in May 2001 as the third single from his third album, "Real Life".

chunks.title: Real Life (I Never Was the Same Again)
chunks.text: The song was written by Neil Thrasher and Jim Janosky.

chunks.title: Real Life (I Never Was the Same Again)
chunks.text: It was nominated for Song of the Year at the 2001 Christian Country Music Awards.

chunks.title: Austins Bridge
chunks.text: Austins Bridge is an American Christian country band originally formed in Austin, Texas.

chunks.title: Austins Bridge
chunks.text: The band consists of Justin Rivers and Jason Baird.

chunks.title: Wrinkles (song)
chunks.text: "Wrinkles" is a song written by Neil Thrasher and Ronny Scaife, and recorded by American country music group Diamond Rio.

chunks.title: Wrinkles (song)
chunks.text: It was released in July 2003 as the third single from the album "Completely".

chunks.title: Wrinkles (song)
chunks.text: The song reached number 16 on the "Billboard" Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart.

chunks.title: Wild One (Faith Hill song)
chunks.text: "Wild One", originally titled "She's a Wild One", is a country music song written by Pat Bunch, Jaime Kyle, and Will Rambeaux.

chunks.title: Wild One (Faith Hill song)
chunks.text: It was first recorded in 1992 by country band Zaca Creek on their album, "Broken Heartland", and country band Evangeline on their 1993 album, "French Quarter Moon".

chunks.title: Wild One (Faith Hill song)
chunks.text: Faith Hill later covered the song on her 1993 debut album, "Take Me as I Am", and released it in late 1993 as her debut single.

chunks.title: Wild One (Faith Hill song)
chunks.text: Hill's rendition was also her first Number One, spending the first four chart weeks of 1994 at the top of the "Billboard" Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart.

chunks.title: Marloes de Boer
chunks.text: Marloes de Boer is a former Dutch football defender.

chunks.title: Marloes de Boer
chunks.text: Throughout her career she played for Oranje Nassau, Be Quick '28 and FC Twente in the Dutch league.

chunks.title: Marloes de Boer
chunks.text: She retired in 2011, after winning the league with Twente.

chunks.title: Quick '20
chunks.text: K. Voetbal Vereniging Quick 1920, known as Quick '20 is a football club from Oldenzaal, the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Quick '20
chunks.text: The club was founded in 1920 and is currently playing in the Derde Divisie, formerly Topklasse, which is the second highest tier of amateur football in the Netherlands and the fourth tier in general.

chunks.title: Be Quick '28
chunks.text: Be Quick '28 is a football club from Zwolle, Netherlands, which was founded on 22 November 1928.

chunks.title: Be Quick '28
chunks.text: They currently play in the Eerste Klasse.

chunks.title: Wim de Bois
chunks.text: Cornelis Hendrik Willem de Bois (19 June 1896 – 1 August 1975) is a former Dutch football manager and player who played for AFC Ajax in the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Wim de Bois
chunks.text: During his managerial career he managed the Dutch Guyana national team ("now known as Suriname"), DFC, DOS, RBC, Go Ahead, SC Veendam, VV Oldenzaal, Quick '20 and Tubantia.

chunks.title: Marije Brummel
chunks.text: Marije Brummel is a Dutch football defensive midfielder currently playing for Sandviken in the Toppserien.

chunks.title: Marije Brummel
chunks.text: She previously played for Bristol Academy in the FA WSL; SC Klarenbeek, SV Saestum and Be Quick '21 in the old Hoofdklasse; for FC twente and Heerenveen, in the women Eredivisie and BeNe League.

chunks.title: Marije Brummel
chunks.text: She also played the European Cup with Saestum.

chunks.title: PEC Zwolle (women)
chunks.text: PEC Zwolle is a Dutch women's football from Zwolle.

chunks.title: PEC Zwolle (women)
chunks.text: The team is founded in 2010, starting in the Eredivisie season 2010–11.

chunks.title: PEC Zwolle (women)
chunks.text: The club was the first two seasons working together with Be Quick '28, currently they are working together with SV Zwolle who's playing in the Hoofdklasse.

chunks.title: Zwolle
chunks.text: Zwolle (] ) is the capital city and municipality of the province of Overijssel, Netherlands.

chunks.title: Zwolle
chunks.text: It has a population around 125,000.

chunks.title: 1927–28 Birmingham F.C. season
chunks.text: The 1927–28 Football League season was Birmingham Football Club's 32nd in the Football League and their 15th in the First Division.

chunks.title: 1927–28 Birmingham F.C. season
chunks.text: They finished in 11th position in the 22-team division.

chunks.title: 1927–28 Birmingham F.C. season
chunks.text: They also competed in the 1927–28 FA Cup, entering at the third round proper and losing to Manchester United in the fifth.

chunks.title: 1927–28 Birmingham F.C. season
chunks.text: Bill Harvey stood down as manager at the end of the season.

chunks.title: Sebastiaan Bökkerink
chunks.text: Sebastiaan "Bas" Bökkerink (born 23 October 1994) is a Dutch football player who plays for Quick '20.

chunks.title: Zwart-Wit '28
chunks.text: RCVV Zwart-Wit '28 (full name: "Rotterdamse Christelijke Voetbalvereniging Zwart-Wit 1928") was a Dutch Saturday football club from Rotterdam, dubbed the "Feyenoord of Saturday Football".

chunks.title: Zwart-Wit '28
chunks.text: Its women's team won the 2000 National Women's Cup then played in the professional Eredivisie.

chunks.title: Zwart-Wit '28
chunks.text: Its men's team won the National Amateur Championship in 1971, then played in the Hoofdklasse.

chunks.title: Bonnie Winterbottom
chunks.text: Bonnie Winterbottom is a fictional character created in 2014 by Peter Nowalk.

chunks.title: Bonnie Winterbottom
chunks.text: Portrayed by Liza Weil, she is a Philadelphia-based associate attorney who works for Annalise Keating's firm, and one of the main characters developed for the American Broadcasting Company (ABC) legal drama mystery television series "How to Get Away with Murder".

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder episodes
chunks.text: "How to Get Away with Murder" is an American legal drama television series that airs on ABC, and first premiered on September 25, 2014.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder episodes
chunks.text: The series follows Professor Annalise Keating, a law professor and criminal defense attorney at Middleton University, who selects five interns to work in her law firm: Wes Gibbins, Connor Walsh, Michaela Pratt, Asher Millstone, and Laurel Castillo – alongside Annalise's employees Frank Delfino and Bonnie Winterbottom, an associate lawyer.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder episodes
chunks.text: With the exception of the pilot, every episode's title is a phrase said by one of the characters in that episode.

chunks.title: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase (film)
chunks.text: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase is a 1989 dark fantasy film directed by Stuart Orme with a screenplay by William M. Akers.

chunks.title: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase (film)
chunks.text: The cast includes Stephanie Beacham as Letitia Slighcarp, Mel Smith as Mr. Grimshaw, Richard O'Brien as James, and Jane Horrocks as Pattern.

chunks.title: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase (film)
chunks.text: Newcomers Emily Hudson and Aleks Darowska played Bonnie Willoughby and her cousin Sylvia.

chunks.title: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase (film)
chunks.text: The film is an adaptation of the 1962 book of the same name written by Joan Aiken.

chunks.title: The Wolves of Willoughby Chase (film)
chunks.text: It is currently aired on British television and it is also available on both VHS and DVD.

chunks.title: How to Get Away with Murder
chunks.text: How to Get Away with Murder is an American drama television series that premiered on ABC on September 25, 2014.

chunks.title: How to Get Away with Murder
chunks.text: The series was created by Peter Nowalk, and produced by Shonda Rhimes and ABC Studios.

chunks.title: How to Get Away with Murder
chunks.text: The series airs on ABC as part of a night of programming all under Rhimes's ShondaLand production company.

chunks.title: Smiley (2012 film)
chunks.text: Smiley is a 2012 American psychological slasher horror film directed by Michael Gallagher and made by Level 10 Films.

chunks.title: Smiley (2012 film)
chunks.text: The film stars were Caitlin Gerard, Melanie Papalia, Keith David, Shane Dawson, Andrew James Allen, Toby Turner, and Liza Weil.

chunks.title: Smiley (2012 film)
chunks.text: The film was released on October 12, 2012.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: "How to Get Away with Murder" is an American drama television series that premiered on ABC on September 25, 2014.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: The series was created by Peter Nowalk, and produced by Shonda Rhimes and ABC Studios.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: Viola Davis stars as Annalise Keating, a law professor at a prestigious Philadelphia university who, with five of her students, becomes entwined in a murder plot.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: The show features an ensemble cast with Alfred Enoch, Jack Falahee, Aja Naomi King, Matt McGorry, and Karla Souza as Keating's students, Charlie Weber and Liza Weil as her employees and Billy Brown as a detective with the Philadelphia Police Department, and Annalise's lover.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: From season three onward, Conrad Ricamora was added to the main cast after recurring heavily in the previous two seasons.

chunks.title: List of How to Get Away with Murder characters
chunks.text: Following is a list of characters who have appeared over the various seasons since the drama's premiere.

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: Stacy Heather Tolkin is a former child actress who played the part of Irina in "The Concorde ... Airport '79", and voiced a number of 1983 television productions featuring Charles Schulz Peanuts characters.

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: Tolkin also voiced Sally Brown and Truffles in "The Charlie Brown and Snoopy Show".

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: She also played Herb Tarlek's daughter in a few episodes of "WKRP In Cincinnati".

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: As a child actress, Tolkin was in over a hundred commercials including McDonald's, Grandma's Cookies, and Kellogg's Corn Flakes.

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: She was also on the cover of the Kellogg's Corn Flakes box.

chunks.title: Stacy Heather Tolkin
chunks.text: Tolkin played Bonnie Franklin's daughter in the TV movie, "Portrait of a Rebel: Margaret Sanger".

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: Bonnie (originally titled The Bonnie Hunt Show) is an American CBS television comedy that aired from 1995 to 1996.

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: Bonnie Hunt played Bonnie Kelly, a television reporter who moves from Wisconsin to take a job in Chicago.

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: There she encounters an eclectic group of coworkers.

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: Each episode had parts where Bonnie would interview real people, asking ridiculous questions.

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: These scenes were improvised.

chunks.title: Bonnie (TV series)
chunks.text: The show bore similarities to another series produced by David Letterman, "Welcome to New York".

chunks.title: Liza Weil
chunks.text: Liza Rebecca Weil (born June 5, 1977) is an American actress, known for her role as Paris Geller in the WB/CW series "Gilmore Girls" and its Netflix revival "".

chunks.title: Liza Weil
chunks.text: She is also known for her roles as White House aide Amanda Tanner in the first season of ABC's "Scandal" and as attorney Bonnie Winterbottom in ABC's "How to Get Away with Murder".

chunks.title: Jack Weil (American football)
chunks.text: Jack Lee Weil (born March 16, 1962) is a former American college and professional football player who was a punter in the National Football League (NFL) for two seasons during the mid-1980s.

chunks.title: Jack Weil (American football)
chunks.text: Weil played college football for the University of Wyoming, and then played professionally for the Denver Broncos and the Washington Redskins of the NFL.

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: Just a Little Time is an album by Lynsey de Paul.

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: It was originally released in 30 September 1994 on the Music Deluxe (catalogue number MSCD9) label but has since been released on the Tring International PLC label (catalogue number JHD128) and on Arc Records/The Magic Collection (Catalogue number MEC 949080).

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: All of the songs on the album are written or co-written by de Paul.

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: The songs "Sugar Me", Getting a Drag", "Storm in a Teacup and "Dancing on a Saturday Night" are radical re-recordings of her earlier hits performed in an updated and uptempo fashion.

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: "Won't Somebody Dance with Me" is still performed as a ballad, but has been updated and extended with an extra refrain.

chunks.title: Just a Little Time
chunks.text: Never before released songs on the album include the ballads "Words Don't Mean A Thing" and title track "Just a Little Time" as well as the more uptempo "Instant Love" and "Now & Then".

chunks.title: The Beautiful South
chunks.text: The Beautiful South was an English pop/rock group formed in 1988 by two former members of the Hull group the Housemartins—Paul Heaton and Dave Hemingway—both of whom performed lead and backing vocals.

chunks.title: The Beautiful South
chunks.text: Other members throughout the band's tenure were former Housemartins roadie Sean Welch (bass), Dave Stead (drums) and Dave Rotheray (guitar).

chunks.title: The Beautiful South
chunks.text: After the band's first album (recorded as a quintet), they were joined by a succession of female vocalists, all of whom performed lead and backing vocals alongside Heaton and Hemingway – Briana Corrigan for albums two and three after appearing as a guest vocalist on one, followed by Jacqui Abbott for the fourth through seventh albums, and finally Alison Wheeler for the final three Beautiful South albums.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Total Contrast song)
chunks.text: "Takes a Little Time" is a 1985 dance hit by British, techno-soul, duo, Total Contrast.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Total Contrast song)
chunks.text: Their debut American release went to number one on the U.S. dance chart for one week.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Total Contrast song)
chunks.text: "Takes a Little Time" did not make the Hot 100 but, peaked at number eighty on the R&B singles chart.

chunks.title: Dave Hemingway
chunks.text: Dave Hemingway (born David Robert Hemingway, 20 September 1960) is an English musician and songwriter, and was a vocalist for the Hull-based band The Beautiful South until they disbanded in 2007.

chunks.title: Dave Hemingway
chunks.text: Previously he had been a member of The Housemartins.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Amy Grant song)
chunks.text: "Takes a Little Time" was a maxi-single released in 1997 (see 1997 in music) to promote Amy Grant's album "Behind the Eyes", which was also released that year.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Amy Grant song)
chunks.text: "Takes a Little Time" included two songs from "Behind the Eyes", as well as a new version of Grant's 1982 Christian radio hit, "El Shaddai".

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Amy Grant song)
chunks.text: The maxi-single was also an enhanced CD (ECD), meaning it had a video that consumers could watch when they put it in their home computer.

chunks.title: Takes a Little Time (Amy Grant song)
chunks.text: The ECD portion of the CD contained a live acoustic version of the song After the Fire, which Grant later released on her 2003 album "Simple Things"; Grant stated on Oprah that she had written the song for her mother.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets is the 60th and final studio album by American country music singer George Jones released on August 19, 2008 on the Bandit Records label.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: It features duets never before released, including some that were cut from his 1994 duets album "The Bradley Barn Sessions".

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: The only new recording in the collection is "You And Me And Time", a song Jones recorded with his daughter by Tammy Wynette, Georgette.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: A music video accompanied the song.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: The album features several duets with artist from outside the country music pantheon, including Mark Knopfler, Leon Russell, and Keith Richards.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: The album peaked at number 15 on the Billboard country albums chart.

chunks.title: Burn Your Playhouse Down – The Unreleased Duets
chunks.text: Of the album's title track, Andrew Meuller of "Uncut" opined in July 2013, "The segue from Richards trying to sing like Jones to Jones actually singing like Jones is hilarious."

chunks.title: So Little Time
chunks.text: So Little Time is an American sitcom starring Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen in their second television series since the short-lived "Two of a Kind" ended in 1999.

chunks.title: So Little Time
chunks.text: It aired on Fox Family: the first half of the series aired from June 2, 2001, to August 15, 2001, and the series then went on a four-month hiatus owing to network management changes.

chunks.title: So Little Time
chunks.text: By December 2001, Fox Family had become ABC Family, and the remaining episodes aired until May 4, 2002.

chunks.title: So Little Time
chunks.text: "So Little Time" reruns briefly aired on Nickelodeon in 2015.

chunks.title: A Little Time
chunks.text: "A Little Time" is a song by The Beautiful South, and is the band's only single to reach number 1 in the UK Singles Chart.

chunks.title: A Little Time
chunks.text: It consists of a duet featuring vocalists Dave Hemingway and Briana Corrigan.

chunks.title: Hugh Whitaker
chunks.text: Hugh Whitaker (born 18 May 1961) is an English musician and the former drummer for the British indie rock band The Housemartins.

chunks.title: Hugh Whitaker
chunks.text: He replaced original drummer Chris Lang and drummed for the band's first album, "London 0 Hull 4", and its attendant single releases.

chunks.title: Hugh Whitaker
chunks.text: He left the band before the recording of their second album, "The People Who Grinned Themselves to Death".

chunks.title: Hugh Whitaker
chunks.text: Whitaker left the band on amicable terms and even participated in the promotional video for the band's first single without him, "Five Get Over Excited", wherein he was kidnapped by his replacement, Dave Hemingway, and locked in a hessian sack.

chunks.title: Briana Corrigan
chunks.text: Briana Corrigan (born 30 May 1965) is a Northern Irish singer.

chunks.title: Briana Corrigan
chunks.text: She was the first female singer for The Beautiful South, from 1988 to 1992.

chunks.title: Inspectorate General of Military Training
chunks.text: The Inspectorate General of Military Training (教育総監部 , Kyoiku sokanbu ) was responsible for all non-military aviation training of the Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Inspectorate General of Military Training
chunks.text: It was headed by an Inspector general who was responsible for overseeing technical and tactical training, and who reported directly to the Emperor of Japan via the Imperial General Headquarters rather than to the Army Minister or the Chief of the Imperial Japanese Army General Staff Office.

chunks.title: Inspectorate General of Military Training
chunks.text: The position of Inspector-General of Military Training was thus the third most powerful position within the Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Port Arthur massacre (China)
chunks.text: The Port Arthur massacre occurred during the First Sino-Japanese War from 21 November 1894 for two or three days, when advanced elements of the First Division of the Japanese Second Army under command of General Yamaji Motoharu (1841–1897) killed somewhere between 1,000 and 20,000 Chinese servicemen and civilians in the Chinese coastal city of Port Arthur (now Lüshunkou).

chunks.title: Port Arthur massacre (China)
chunks.text: Contemporaneous reports, including some Japanese accounts, claim that as many as 60,000 were killed, although some contemporary accounts of the war estimated Port Arthur's total population at 13,000 (6,000 excluding garrison troops).

chunks.title: Ōsako Naoharu
chunks.text: Viscount Ōsako Naoharu (大迫尚敏 , 24 December 1844 – 20 September 1927, sometimes known as "'Ōsako Naotoshi) was a general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Ōsako Naoharu
chunks.text: He was the older brother of General Ōsako Naomichi.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army
chunks.text: The Imperial Japanese Army (IJA; 大日本帝國陸軍 "Dai-Nippon Teikoku Rikugun"; "Army of the Greater Japanese Empire") was the official ground-based armed force of the Empire of Japan from 1868 to 1945.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army
chunks.text: It was controlled by the Imperial Japanese Army General Staff Office and the Ministry of War, both of which were nominally subordinate to the Emperor of Japan as supreme commander of the army and the navy.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army
chunks.text: Later an Inspectorate General of Aviation became the third agency with oversight of the army.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army
chunks.text: During wartime or national emergencies, the nominal command functions of the emperor would be centralized in an Imperial General Headquarters (IGHQ), an ad-hoc body consisting of the chief and vice chief of the Army General Staff, the Minister of War, the chief and vice chief of the Naval General Staff, the Inspector General of Aviation, and the Inspector General of Military Training.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
chunks.text: The Imperial Japanese Army Air Service (often called the Imperial Japanese Army Air Force (大日本帝國陸軍航空部隊 , Dainippon Teikoku Rikugun Kōkūbutai ) (IJAAS or IJAAF), was the land-based aviation force of the Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
chunks.text: As with the IJA itself, the IJAAS was developed along the lines of Imperial German Army Aviation so its primary mission was to provide tactical close air support for ground troops while maintaining a limited air interdiction capability.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
chunks.text: The IJAAS also provided important reconnaissance support for the Army.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
chunks.text: However, the Army Air Service usually did not control the light aircraft or balloons deployed and operated by the IJA artillery battalions as spotters or observers.

chunks.title: Imperial Japanese Army Air Service
chunks.text: Although the Army Air Service engaged in strategic bombing of enemy cities such as Shanghai, Nanking, Canton, Chongqing, Rangoon, and Mandalay, this was not its primary mission, and it lacked the heavy strategic bombers as were later deployed by the United States Army Air Forces.

chunks.title: Ōshima Hisanao
chunks.text: Viscount Ōshima Hisanao (大島久直 , 1 October 1848 – 27 September 1928) was a general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Miura Gorō
chunks.text: Viscount Miura Gorō (三浦 梧楼 , 1 January 1847 – 28 January 1926) was a lieutenant general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Ogawa Mataji
chunks.text: Viscount Ogawa Mataji (小川又次 , 22 August 1848 – 20 October 1909) was a general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Ogawa Mataji
chunks.text: He was also the father-in-law of Field Marshal Gen Sugiyama.

chunks.title: Takashima Tomonosuke
chunks.text: Viscount Takashima Tomonosuke (高島 鞆之助 , 18 December 1844 – 11 January 1916) was a general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Yamaji Motoharu
chunks.text: Viscount Yamaji Motoharu (山地 元治 , 10 September 1841 – 3 October 1897) , was a Japanese general in the early Imperial Japanese Army.

chunks.title: Yamaji Motoharu
chunks.text: Soldiers under his command took part in the Port Arthur massacre.

chunks.title: Alice River (Far North Queensland)
chunks.text: The Alice River is a river located on the Cape York Peninsula of Far North Queensland, Australia.

chunks.title: Uw Oykangand
chunks.text: The Uw Oykangand are an Indigenous Australian people living on the southwestern part of the Cape York Peninsula, Queensland in Australia.

chunks.title: Uw Oykangand
chunks.text: Their neighbours to the northwest are the Yir-Yoront, Their traditional lands are around the Alice River and the Crosbie River, and further west around the Mitchell River and into Gulf Country.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: Luigi Maria D'Albertis (21 November 1841 – 2 September 1901) was a flamboyant Italian naturalist and explorer who, in 1876, became the first person to chart the Fly River in Papua New Guinea.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: He took eight weeks to steam some 580 miles up the Fly River in an Australian launch, the "Neva".

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: On board as engineer was young Lawrence Hargrave, later to become an aviation pioneer.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: D'Albertis kept a pet python on board to prevent his motley crew from pilfering the stores.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: He also fired off exploding rockets to keep any hostile natives at bay.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: His expedition collected specimens of birds, plants and insects.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: The "Neva" forced its way upstream until brought to a halt by the shallows.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: They then steamed downriver to a tributary d'Albertis had named the Alice River (today known as the Ok Tedi), and d'Albertis cajoled his crew up this river with promises of gold.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: Eventually stricken by malaria and crippled by rheumatism in both legs, he admitted defeat.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: He tried once again in the following year, but did not reach as far as before, and returned to Europe.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: A homosexual, Goode was accompanied on his expeditions by a succession of young male companions.

chunks.title: Luigi D'Albertis
chunks.text: An account of d'Albertis' expeditions up the Fly in the "Neva" and his various political and personal problems with his contemporaries and the inhabitants of Papua are told in Goode, J. 1977 "Rape of the Fly" (Nelson, Melbourne).

chunks.title: Rupertswood
chunks.text: Rupertswood is a mansion and country estate located in Sunbury on the outskirts of Melbourne in Victoria, Australia.

chunks.title: Rupertswood
chunks.text: It is well known as the birthplace of The Ashes urn which was humorously presented to English cricket captain Ivo Bligh to mark his team's victory in an 1882-83 Test match series between Australia and England.

chunks.title: Rupertswood
chunks.text: Rupertswood is one of the largest houses constructed in Victoria and, although now subdivided, has significant farm land.

chunks.title: Rupertswood
chunks.text: The estate also had its own private railway station (until closure in 2004), and artillery battery.

chunks.title: Rupertswood
chunks.text: It is listed on the Victorian Heritage Register.

chunks.title: Dixie, Queensland
chunks.text: Dixie is a locality in the Shire of Cook, Queensland, Australia.

chunks.title: Dixie, Queensland
chunks.text: The locality contains the source of both the Morehead River and Alice River.

chunks.title: Todd River
chunks.text: The Todd River is an ephemeral river in the southern Northern Territory, central Australia.

chunks.title: Todd River
chunks.text: The origins of the Todd River are in the MacDonnell Ranges, where it flows past the Telegraph Station, almost through the center of Alice Springs, through Heavitree Gap at the southern end of Alice Springs and continuing on for some distance, passing through the western part of the Simpson Desert, as it becomes a tributary of the Hale River, and eventually flowing into Lake Eyre in South Australia.

chunks.title: Olkola
chunks.text: The Olkolo or Koko-olkola' were an Indigenous Australian people of central and eastern Cape York Peninsula in northern Queensland.

chunks.title: Olkola
chunks.text: According Norman Tindale, they are to be distinguished from the Kokangol,higher up on the Alice River watershed.

chunks.title: Alice River, Queensland
chunks.text: Alice River is a suburb of the City of Townsville in North Queensland, Australia.

chunks.title: Alice River, Queensland
chunks.text: The estate is also known as Rupertswood, the estate was named by the developer who was Sir Rupert Clarke, 3rd Baronet of Rupertswood, after his ancestral home "Rupertswood" at Sunbury, Victoria, Australia.

chunks.title: Melaleuca clarksonii
chunks.text: Melaleuca clarksonii, commonly known as Alice River bottlebrush, is a plant in the myrtle family, Myrtaceae and is endemic to Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, Australia.

chunks.title: Melaleuca clarksonii
chunks.text: It is similar to "Melaleuca cajuputi" and "Melaleuca leucadendra" with its broad leaves and spikes of creamy-coloured flowers but is distinguished from them by its (usually) hard, fibrous bark.

chunks.title: Alice River (Barcoo River)
chunks.text: The Alice River in central Queensland, Australia rises on the western slopes of the Great Dividing Range.

chunks.title: Alice River (Barcoo River)
chunks.text: The river bisects the Shire of Barcaldine, flowing in a south-westerly direction towards Isisford and its confluence with the Barcoo River to form Cooper Creek.

chunks.title: Alice River (Barcoo River)
chunks.text: Barcaldine is located on Lagoon Creek, which flows into the Alice River approximately five kilometre s to the south.

chunks.title: Alice River (Barcoo River)
chunks.text: The Alice River is often dry, except after the annual summer rains.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: Twisted Fortune is a black comedy about a bumbling small-time crook (played by Charlie Murphy) who finds a bottle cap worth $1,000,000 while robbing a convenience store.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: The comedy also features Ike Barinholtz and Jordan Peele (both of "Mad TV"), supermodel Carol Alt, comedians Donnell Rawlings and Dave Attell, and actress Davida Williams.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: It was directed by comedian Victor Varnado ("End of Days"), who also acted in the movie.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: The screenplay was written by Jim Yoakum (who worked with Monty Python's Graham Chapman), and by Paul Sapiano.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: It was released in 2007 and is listed as having been filmed in New York City in the same year.

chunks.title: Twisted Fortune
chunks.text: It was distributed by Warner Bros.

chunks.title: Charlie Murphy
chunks.text: Charles Quinton Murphy (July 12, 1959 – April 12, 2017) was an American actor, comedian, and writer.

chunks.title: Charlie Murphy
chunks.text: Murphy was best known as a writer and cast member of the Comedy Central sketch-comedy series "Chappelle's Show".

chunks.title: Charlie Murphy
chunks.text: He was the older brother of comedian Eddie Murphy.

chunks.title: Nicole Mitchell Murphy
chunks.text: Nicole Mitchell Murphy (born Nicole Mitchell) is an American fashion model, television personality, designer, actress, and businesswoman.

chunks.title: Nicole Mitchell Murphy
chunks.text: She is best known for her international modelling career, 12 year marriage to comedian/actor Eddie Murphy, and participation on reality television show "Hollywood Exes".

chunks.title: Nicole Mitchell Murphy
chunks.text: She has also been credited as Nicole Mitchell, her maiden name, and Nicole Murphy (her ex-husband being Eddie Murphy).

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Delirious
chunks.text: Delirious (1983) is an American stand-up comedy television special directed by Bruce Gowers, written by and starring Eddie Murphy.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Delirious
chunks.text: The comedy became a TV Special for HBO released August 30, 1983.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Delirious
chunks.text: The 70-minute film became Eddie Murphy's first feature stand-up film, becoming the predecessor to the wide theatrical release in 1987, "Eddie Murphy Raw".

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Delirious
chunks.text: The stand-up was also released as an album on October 24, 1983 titled """", which won Grammy for Best Comedy Album at the 1984 Grammy Awards.

chunks.title: Greatest Comedy Hits
chunks.text: Greatest Comedy Hits is the first compilation album by American comedian Eddie Murphy.

chunks.title: Greatest Comedy Hits
chunks.text: The album was released on May 27, 1997 for Columbia Records, produced by Vernon 'Vas' Lynch Jr and Murphy himself.

chunks.title: Greatest Comedy Hits
chunks.text: "Greatest Comedy Hits" featured his greatest stand-up comedy sketches as well as recordings from his films, "Coming to America", "The Nutty Professor" and "Eddie Murphy Raw".

chunks.title: Coming to America
chunks.text: Coming to America is a 1988 American romantic comedy film directed by John Landis, and based on a story originally created by Eddie Murphy, who also starred in the lead role.

chunks.title: Coming to America
chunks.text: The film also co-stars Arsenio Hall, James Earl Jones, Shari Headley and John Amos.

chunks.title: Coming to America
chunks.text: The film was released in the United States on June 29, 1988.

chunks.title: Coming to America
chunks.text: Eddie Murphy plays Akeem Joffer, the crown prince of the fictional African nation of Zamunda, who comes to the United States in the hopes of finding a woman he can marry.

chunks.title: All I Fuckin' Know
chunks.text: All I Fuckin' Know (titled All I "$%*#@*#" Know on the cover) is the second compilation album and seventh album overall by comedian/singer, Eddie Murphy.

chunks.title: All I Fuckin' Know
chunks.text: The album was released on April 28, 1998 for Sony Records and was produced by Eddie Murphy.

chunks.title: All I Fuckin' Know
chunks.text: "All I Fuckin' Know" contained both Stand-Up comedy sketches and songs that Murphy recorded in the 1980s.

chunks.title: The PJs
chunks.text: The PJs is an American stop-motion animated sitcom, created by Eddie Murphy, Larry Wilmore, and Steve Tompkins.

chunks.title: The PJs
chunks.text: It portrayed life in an urban public housing project, modeled after the Cabrini–Green housing projects in Chicago.

chunks.title: The PJs
chunks.text: The series starred Eddie Murphy, and was produced by Imagine Entertainment by Ron Howard and Brian Grazer, The Murphy Company and Will Vinton Studios in association with Touchstone Television.

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: Life is a 1999 American comedy-drama film written by Robert Ramsey & Matthew Stone and directed by Ted Demme.

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Eddie Murphy and Martin Lawrence.

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: It is the second film that Eddie Murphy and Martin Lawrence have worked on, the first being "Boomerang".

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: The supporting cast includes Obba Babatundé, Bernie Mac, Anthony Anderson, Miguel A. Núñez Jr., Bokeem Woodbine, Guy Torry and Barry Shabaka Henley.

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film's format is a story being told by an elderly inmate about two of his friends, who are both wrongly convicted of murder and given a life sentence in prison.

chunks.title: Life (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film was the last R-rated role to date for Eddie Murphy, who has stuck mainly to family-friendly films since.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: Eddie Murphy Raw is a 1987 American stand-up comedy film starring Eddie Murphy and directed by Robert Townsend.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: It was Murphy's second feature stand-up comedy film, following "Eddie Murphy Delirious".

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: However, unlike "Delirious", "Raw" received a wide theatrical release film.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: The 90-minute show was filmed in Manhattan New York City's Felt Forum, a venue in the Madison Square Garden complex.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: To this day, "Raw" is the #1 stand-up film of all time box office, making $50.5 million worldwide.

chunks.title: Eddie Murphy Raw
chunks.text: The film was released in the United States on December 18, 1987.

chunks.title: Lake Winnipesaukee
chunks.text: Lake Winnipesaukee ( ) is the largest lake in the U.S. state of New Hampshire, located in the Lakes Region.

chunks.title: Lake Winnipesaukee
chunks.text: It is approximately 21 mi long (northwest-southeast) and from 1 to wide (northeast-southwest), covering 69 sqmi —71 sqmi when Paugus Bay is included—with a maximum depth of 212 ft .

chunks.title: Lake Winnipesaukee
chunks.text: The center area of the lake is called The Broads.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The hill rises about 250 feet above the level of the plateau, which itself constitutes the summit of the Mahadev range at this point.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The cone with the walls on it is seen from a great distance and appears very small indeed.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: But on near approach it is seen to be but the inner citadel of a place of considerable size and strength for the times in which it was built.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: On the south-west the outer wall or enceinte is entered by a rude gateway of a single pointed arch about eight feet high and five feet broad.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: As usual there is a curtain of solid masonry inside.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The gate lies about 150 yards east of the edge of the plateau, which there terminates in an almost unbroken vertical precipice of several hundred feet in height and receding in a north-easterly direction.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: No wall was built along about three hundred yards of this part which is absolutely unscalable, but for the rest of the way the walling is continued along the edge of the cliff in a north-east direction for about another three hundred yards.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Here it turns still following the cliff to the south-east for another seven hundred yards, and then gradually rounds to the westward covering four hundred and fifty yards more till it meets the gateway.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: But for the break of the inaccessible precipice this outer wall would form a nearly equilateral triangle with the corners rounded off, the side being of some six hundred and fifty yards.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Facing nearly north, about fifty yards from the north-east angle, is a gateway with a couple of curtains in solid masonry.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: This entrance is cut in the sides of the cliff about twenty feet below the top which is reached by some dozen steps.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: It consisted as usual of a pointed arch, the top fallen in, about ten feet high by five broad.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: It leads out to the path down to Girvi, a village in the plains below and it probably formed the communication with Phaltan.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: This road winds down the face of the range for some five hundred feet till it hits the shoulder of a spur which it then follows to the base.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The walling on the south side, from the edge of the cliff to some hundred yards east of the southern gate, is not more than a couple of feet in thickness and consists of all-fitting stones unmortared.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The rest is massive and well mortared and still fairly preserved.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The average height is from seven to ten feet.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: In the south-east angle is a rude temple of Bhairavnath and a few houses with the remains of Man y more.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: On the right side of the southern gate is a well preserved stone pond about thirty yards square with steps leading down to it.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Next to and on the north of Bhairavnath's temple is another pond.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The way up to the fort proper or upper and lower citadels is from the north side.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The path up the hill side, which is steep but with grass and soil left in Man y places, is almost destroyed.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: About 150 feet up is the outer citadel built on a sort of shoulder of the hill and facing almost due west.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: It contains two massive bastions of excellent masonry looking north-west and south-west so that guns planted on them could comMan d respectively the north and south gateways.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: This citadel was connected with the main wall by a cross wall running across the whole breadth of the fort from east to west.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Its entrance lies close below that to the upper citadel.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: A masonry curtain projects so as to hide the arch itself, which is not more than seven feet high by three broad, and has to be entered from due east.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: On the south side the walls are carried right up to the scarp of the upper citadel and are some ten feet high, so that to take the lower citadel in rear or flank must have been difficult.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The upper citadel is above a vertical scarp some thirty feet high.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The entrance to it lies some thirty feet above that to the lower citadel, and is cut in the rock about eight feet wide.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: There is a gateway of a pointed arch with the top fallen in and twenty odd steps leading up to it and ten more cut out of the rock, and winding up past the inside curtain on to the top.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The walls of this upper citadel are still in tolerable preservation.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: They were originally about ten feet high and built of fair masonry.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: There is a large turret on the south-west corner, evidently meant to comMan d the southern gate.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: About ten yards to the east of this turret is a new looking building which was the headquarters or sadar.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Immediately east of this and below it is a great pit about thirty feet square and equally deep roughly cut in the rock and said by the people to be a dungeon.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Next to it on the south is a small pond evenly cut and lined with mortar used for storing water.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: There are some remains of sepoys' houses, and, near the turret, a small stone wheel said to belong to a gun.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The outer walls east of the gates have bastions at every turn of the cliffs, and the masonry here is particularly strong and well preserved.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: It would appear that attacks were dreaded chiefly from the plain below.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The assailants could either come up the spur towards the north entrance or they might attempt the spurs on the other side of the eastern ravine and attack the southern gateway.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: Hence apparently the reason for strengthening the walls of the enceinte on this side.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: After passing the southern gateway the assailants would be commanded Maan, Maharashtra from the lower citadel.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: They Would then be encountered by the cross wall.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: If that obstacle was overcome the besieged would run round the east side and into the two citadels.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The appearance from the fort of the plain in the north is most formidable.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The Panvan plateau completely commands Maan, Maharashtra and almost overhangs it.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The fort is believed to have been built by Shivaji to resist the Moghals whose attacks he must have dreaded from the plain below.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The Karkhanis or Superintendent of the fort was a Prabhu.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: The fort garrison consisted of 200 Ramoshis, Mahars, and other hereditary Gadkaris besides sepoys.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: It was surrendered in 1818 to Vitthal Pant Phadnis of the Raja of Satara left in charge of the town.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: He detached 200 men to take possession, being part of a force then raised to protect the town from the enterprizes of Bajirav's garrisons then in the neighbourhood.

chunks.title: Varugad
chunks.text: [Elphinstone in Pendhari and Maratha War Papers, 245.]

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: Mount Fitch is the third-highest peak in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts at 3110 ft .

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: It is located on the ridge between Mount Greylock at 3,491 feet (1,064 m) to its south and Mount Williams at 2,956 feet (901 m) to its north.

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: The peak sits in the northwest corner of the Town of Adams (originally known as the Town of East Hoosac) in Berkshire County.

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: The forested summit is approximately 123 yd due west of a local high-point on the Appalachian Trail.

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: Mount Fitch does not meet the AMC’s prominence criterion of 200 vertical feet of separation from adjacent peaks as outlined in New England’s Four-thousand footers list.

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: Currently there is no side-spur trail or signage directing a hiker to the summit of Mt. Fitch from the Appalachian Trail; however, there is a wooden placard at the summit itself (pictured at right).

chunks.title: Mount Fitch (Massachusetts)
chunks.text: The top is infrequently visited by hikers due to its anonymity, the bushwhack necessary to reach the top and the viewless summit.

chunks.title: List of lakes of Pakistan
chunks.text: Pakistan is home to many natural and man made lakes and reservoirs.

chunks.title: List of lakes of Pakistan
chunks.text: The largest lake in Pakistan is the Manchar Lake, which is also the largest lake in South Asia.

chunks.title: List of lakes of Pakistan
chunks.text: The lake is spread over an area of over 100 square miles.

chunks.title: List of lakes of Pakistan
chunks.text: The highest lake in Pakistan is the Rush Lake, which is also the 25th highest lake is the world at an altitude of over 4,700 meters.

chunks.title: List of lakes of Pakistan
chunks.text: The second highest lake in Pakistan is the Karambar Lake, which at an altitude of 4,272 meters, is the 31st highest lake in the world.

chunks.title: Lake Kanasatka
chunks.text: Lake Kanasatka is a 371 acre lake located in Carroll County in the Lakes Region of central New Hampshire, United States, in the town of Moultonborough.

chunks.title: Lake Kanasatka
chunks.text: Early maps refer to this pristine lake as Long Pond, presumably because of its long and narrow shape.

chunks.title: Lake Kanasatka

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: The history of the Roman Empire covers the history of Ancient Rome from the fall of the Roman Republic in 27 BC until the abdication of the last Western emperor in 476 AD.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: Rome had begun expanding shortly after the founding of the Republic in the 6th century BC, though it did not expand outside of the Italian Peninsula until the 3rd century BC.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: Civil war engulfed the Roman state in the mid 1st century BC, first between Julius Caesar and Pompey, and finally between Octavian and Mark Antony.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: Antony was defeated at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: In 27 BC the Senate and People of Rome made Octavian "imperator" ("commander") thus beginning the Principate, the first epoch of Roman imperial history usually dated from 27 BC to 284 AD; they later awarded him the name Augustus, "the venerated".

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: The success of Augustus in establishing principles of dynastic succession was limited by his outliving a number of talented potential heirs: the Julio-Claudian dynasty lasted for four more emperors—Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, and Nero—before it yielded in 69 AD to the strife-torn Year of Four Emperors, from which Vespasian emerged as victor.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: Vespasian became the founder of the brief Flavian dynasty, to be followed by the Nerva–Antonine dynasty which produced the "Five Good Emperors": Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius and the philosophically inclined Marcus Aurelius.

chunks.title: History of the Roman Empire
chunks.text: In the view of the Greek historian Dio Cassius, a contemporary observer, the accession of the emperor Commodus in 180 AD marked the descent "from a kingdom of gold to one of rust and iron"—a famous comment which has led some historians, notably Edward Gibbon, to take Commodus' reign as the beginning of the decline of the Roman Empire.
