chunks.text: It is primarily associated with the Archdiocese of Milan, and named after St. Ambrose much as Gregorian chant is named after Gregory the Great.

chunks.title: Ambrosian chant
chunks.text: It is the only surviving plainchant tradition besides the Gregorian to maintain the official sanction of the Roman Catholic Church.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Plainsong is also called plainchant.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: More specific terms such as Gregorian chant, Ambrosian chant, Gallican chant are also found.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Generally speaking, they all refer to a style of monophonic, unaccompanied, early Christian singing performed by monks and developed in the Roman Catholic Church mainly during the period 800-1000 .

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: The differences may be marginal—or even great, in some cases.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: These differences reflect the great ethnic, cultural and linguistic diversity that existed after the fall of the Roman Empire on the Italian peninsula.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Different monastic traditions arose within the Roman Catholic Church throughout Italy, but at different places and at different times.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Even a musical non-specialist can hear the difference, for example, between the straightforward tone production in the Ambosian chants from Milan and the chants from Benevento, which display a distinct "eastern" ornamental quiver in the voice, reflecting the vocal traditions of the Greek Orthodox Church.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Yet, in spite of the differences, the similarities are great.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: In any event, the formal Gregorian chant was imposed throughout Italy by 1100, although the music of Greeks rites continued to be heard at various places on the peninsula, especially in those places which Byzantium had once held, such as Ravenna or in the southern peninsula, which had been a refuge for those Greeks fleeing the great Byzantine iconoclast controversies before the year 1000.

chunks.title: Italian classical music
chunks.text: Obviously, where Greek rites were practiced, the chants were sung in the Greek language and not in Latin, as they were in the Roman Catholic liturgy.

chunks.title: Tonary
chunks.text: A tonary is a liturgical book in the Western Christian Church which lists by incipit various items of Gregorian chant according to the Gregorian mode ("tonus") of their melodies within the eight-mode system.

chunks.title: Tonary
chunks.text: Tonaries often include Office antiphons, the mode of which determines the recitation formula for the accompanying text (the psalm tone if the antiphon is sung with a psalm, or canticle tone if the antiphon is sung with a canticle), but a tonary may also or instead list responsories or Mass chants not associated with formulaic recitation.

chunks.title: Tonary
chunks.text: Although some tonaries are stand-alone works, they were frequently used as an appendix to other liturgical books such as antiphonaries, graduals, tropers, and prosers, and are often included in collections of musical treatises.

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: Old Roman chant is the liturgical plainchant repertory of the Roman rite of the Early Christian Church .

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: It was formerly performed in Rome, and, although it is closely related to the Gregorian chant,the two are distinct.

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: The Gregorian Chant gradually supplanted the Old Roman Chant between the 11th century and the 13th century AD.

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: Unlike other chant traditions (such as Ambrosian chant, Mozarabic chant, and Gallican chant), Old Roman chant and Gregorian chant share essentially the same liturgy and the same texts.

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: Many of their melodies are also closely related.

chunks.title: Old Roman chant
chunks.text: Although primarily associated with the churches of Rome, the Old Roman chant was also performed in parts of central Italy, and it was possibly performed much more widely.

chunks.title: Magnificat (Pärt)
chunks.text: Arvo Pärt set the Latin text of the Magnificat canticle in 1989.

chunks.title: Magnificat (Pärt)
chunks.text: It is a composition for five-part choir (SSATB) a cappella, with several divided parts.

chunks.title: Magnificat (Pärt)
chunks.text: Its performance time is approximately seven minutes.

chunks.title: Magnificat (Pärt)
chunks.text: The composition is in tintinnabuli style, a style which Pärt had invented in the mid-1970s.

chunks.title: Meine Seele erhebt den Herren
chunks.text: Meine Seele erhebt den Herren (My soul magnifies the Lord) is Martin Luther's translation of the Magnificat canticle.

chunks.title: Meine Seele erhebt den Herren
chunks.text: It is traditionally sung to a German variant of the tonus peregrinus , a rather exceptional psalm tone in Gregorian chant.

chunks.title: Meine Seele erhebt den Herren
chunks.text: The tonus peregrinus (or ninth tone) is associated with the ninth mode or Aeolian mode.

chunks.title: Meine Seele erhebt den Herren
chunks.text: For the traditional setting of Luther's German Magnificat that is the minor mode for which the last note of the melodic formula is the tonic, a fifth below its opening note.

chunks.title: Gregorian chant
chunks.text: Gregorian chant is the central tradition of Western plainchant, a form of monophonic, unaccompanied sacred song of the Roman Catholic Church.

chunks.title: Gregorian chant
chunks.text: Gregorian chant developed mainly in western and central Europe during the 9th and 10th centuries, with later additions and redactions.

chunks.title: Gregorian chant
chunks.text: Although popular legend credits Pope St. Gregory the Great with inventing Gregorian chant, scholars believe that it arose from a later Carolingian synthesis of Roman chant and Gallican chant.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: Semiology (from Greek σημεῖον "sēmeion", "a sign, a mark") is a branch of Gregorian Chant research.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: Semiology refers specifically to the study of the neumes as found in the earliest fully notated manuscripts of Gregorian Chant, the oldest of which have been dated to the 9th century.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: The first application of the term 'semiology' (which first appeared in the 1960s) for the study of Latin chant was made by Dom Eugène Cardine (1905–1988), a monk of the Abbey of Solesmes.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: In this context, 'semiology' is understood as 'the study of musical signs'.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: Text and neumatic notation, together with significative letters adjoined to the neumes, presents an effective and integrated mnemonic for the rhythmical interpretation and the melody.

chunks.title: Semiology (Gregorian Chant)
chunks.text: While Gregorian palaeography offers a description of the various neumes and their rhythmical and melodic values, Gregorian semiology explains their meaning for practical interpretation.

chunks.title: 92d Operations Group
chunks.text: The 92d Operations Group (92 OG) is the flying component of the 92d Air Refueling Wing, assigned to the United States Air Force Air Mobility Command Eighteenth Air Force.

chunks.title: 92d Operations Group
chunks.text: The group is stationed at Fairchild Air Force Base, Washington.

chunks.title: 67th Cyberspace Wing
chunks.text: The 67th Cyberspace Wing is a United States Air Force wing stationed at Lackland Air Force Base, Texas.

chunks.title: 67th Cyberspace Wing
chunks.text: It was activated in October 1993 as a military intelligence unit and is assigned to Twenty-Fourth Air Force.

chunks.title: 67th Cyberspace Wing
chunks.text: The wing was first activated at March Field as the 67th Reconnaissance Wing as part of the wing base organization system.

chunks.title: 67th Cyberspace Wing
chunks.text: However, only its 67th Tactical Reconnaissance Group ever became operational and it relied on another wing for support.

chunks.title: 67th Cyberspace Wing
chunks.text: It was inactivated in the 1949 Truman reductions in the Department of Defense budget.

chunks.title: 432d Operations Group
chunks.text: The 432d Operations Group is the flying component of the United States Air Force 432d Wing, stationed at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada.

chunks.title: Creech Air Force Base
chunks.text: Creech Air Force Base ("Creech" colloq.

chunks.title: Creech Air Force Base
chunks.text: ) is a United States Air Force (USAF) command and control facility in Clark County, Nevada used "to engage in daily Overseas Contingency Operations …of remotely piloted aircraft systems which fly missions across the globe."

chunks.title: Creech Air Force Base
chunks.text: In addition to an airport, the military installation has the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Battlelab, associated , and unmanned aerial vehicles of the type used in Afghanistan and Iraq.

chunks.title: Creech Air Force Base
chunks.text: Creech is the aerial training site for the USAF Thunderbirds and "is one of two emergency divert airfields" for the Nevada Test and Training Range.

chunks.title: 1st Operations Group
chunks.text: The 1st Operations Group (1 OG) is the flying component of the 1st Fighter Wing, assigned to the USAF Air Combat Command.

chunks.title: 1st Operations Group
chunks.text: The group is stationed at Langley Air Force Base, Virginia.

chunks.title: 1st Operations Group
chunks.text: The 1st Operations Group is the oldest major air combat unit in the United States Air Force, being the successor organization of the 1st Pursuit Group.

chunks.title: 1st Operations Group
chunks.text: The 1st Pursuit Group was the first air combat group formed by the Air Service, American Expeditionary Force, on 5 May 1918.

chunks.title: 2d Operations Group
chunks.text: The 2d Operations Group (2 OG) is the flying component of the United States Air Force 2d Bomb Wing, assigned to the Air Force Global Strike Command Eighth Air Force.

chunks.title: 2d Operations Group
chunks.text: The group is stationed at Barksdale Air Force Base, Louisiana.

chunks.title: 22d Operations Group
chunks.text: The 22d Operations Group is the operational flying component of the United States Air Force 22d Air Refueling Wing.

chunks.title: 22d Operations Group
chunks.text: It is stationed at McConnell Air Force Base, Kansas, and is part of Air Mobility Command (AMC)'s Eighteenth Air Force.

chunks.title: 380th Expeditionary Operations Group
chunks.text: The 380th Expeditionary Operations Group (380 EOG) is the operational flying component of the United States Air Force 380th Air Expeditionary Wing.

chunks.title: 380th Expeditionary Operations Group
chunks.text: It is a provisional unit stationed at Al Dhafra Air Base, United Arab Emirates, and is assigned to the United States Air Forces Central component of Air Combat Command (ACC).

chunks.title: 3d Operations Group
chunks.text: The 3d Operations Group is the operational flying component of the United States Air Force 3d Wing.

chunks.title: 3d Operations Group
chunks.text: It is stationed at Elmendorf Air Force Base, Alaska, and is assigned to Pacific Air Forces' Eleventh Air Force.

chunks.title: 432d Wing
chunks.text: The 432d Wing is a United States Air Force unit assigned to Air Combat Command, stationed at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada.

chunks.title: 432d Wing
chunks.text: The group operates unmanned reconnaissance aircraft which provide real-time reconnaissance, surveillance, and precision attack against fixed and time-critical targets.

chunks.title: 432d Wing
chunks.text: The 432d Air Expeditionary Wing is a provisional unit assigned to Air Combat Command and is the designation for components of the 432d Wing when deployed into combat areas as part of the Global War on Terror.

chunks.title: Jones Beach Island
chunks.text: Jones Beach Island is one of the outer barrier islands off the southern coast of Long Island in the U.S. state of New York.

chunks.title: Jones Beach Island
chunks.text: It is named for Major Thomas Jones, who first came to Long Island in 1692, where he proceeded to build the island's first brick house near Massapequa.

chunks.title: Jones Beach Island
chunks.text: Jones built a whaling station on Jones Island near the present site of Jones Beach State Park in 1700.

chunks.title: Jones Beach Island
chunks.text: Jones Beach Island is sometimes referred to as Oak Beach Island and is the former home of the infamous Oak Beach Inn.

chunks.title: Oak Beach Inn
chunks.text: The Oak Beach Inn, commonly referred to by the abbreviation OBI, was a Long Island nightclub located in Oak Beach, on Jones Beach Island near Captree State Park in the Town of Babylon, Suffolk County, New York.

chunks.title: Great South Bay Bridge
chunks.text: The Great South Bay Bridge is a bridge on the southwest side of Suffolk County, New York, on Long Island.

chunks.title: Great South Bay Bridge
chunks.text: It connects the Robert Moses Causeway from Long Island's mainland over the Great South Bay, connecting to both Captree and Jones Beach Island.

chunks.title: Great South Bay Bridge
chunks.text: It serves as access via the Robert Moses Causeway to both of the downstream crossings, the State Boat Channel Bridge and the Fire Island Inlet Bridge, also leading visitors and on-lookers to either the Fire Island Lighthouse or the Robert Moses State Park.

chunks.title: Great South Bay Bridge
chunks.text: It is the second longest bridge in the New York State, behind only the Tappan Zee Bridge.

chunks.title: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York
chunks.text: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree is a former census-designated place (CDP) in Suffolk County, New York and the Town of Babylon.

chunks.title: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York
chunks.text: The population was 333 at the 2000 census.

chunks.title: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York
chunks.text: For the 2010 census the area was delineated as two CDPs: Gilgo and Oak Beach–Captree.

chunks.title: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York
chunks.text: The CDP contained several small beach communities on the barrier island along the southern edge of Long Island.

chunks.title: Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York
chunks.text: In order from west to east, these include West Gilgo Beach (on the Nassau/Suffolk county border), Gilgo Beach, Cedar Beach (no residences), Oak Beach (including the Oak Island Beach Association), Oak Island and Captree Island.

chunks.title: Oak Beach–Captree, New York
chunks.text: Oak Beach–Captree is a census-designated place (CDP) in the town of Babylon in Suffolk County, New York, United States.

chunks.title: Oak Beach–Captree, New York
chunks.text: The population was 286 at the 2010 census.

chunks.title: Oak Beach–Captree, New York
chunks.text: Prior to the 2010 census the area was part of a larger CDP called Gilgo-Oak Beach-Captree, New York.

chunks.title: Oak Beach–Captree, New York
chunks.text: The Oak Beach–Captree CDP consists of some small beach communities on the barrier island along the southern edge of Long Island, including Oak Beach, Oak Island, and Captree Island.

chunks.title: Oak Beach, New York
chunks.text: Oak Beach is a small community located on the eastern end of Jones Beach Island, a barrier island between the Atlantic Ocean and the Great South Bay of Long Island.

chunks.title: Oak Beach, New York
chunks.text: The community is part of the town of Babylon in Suffolk County, New York, United States.

chunks.title: Oak Beach, New York
chunks.text: The eastern part, the Oak Island Beach Association, is gated, whereas the western part is not.

chunks.title: Oak Beach, New York
chunks.text: It is part of the Oak Beach–Captree census-designated place.

chunks.title: South Oyster Bay
chunks.text: South Oyster Bay or East Bay is a natural harbor along the western portion of the south shore of Long Island in New York in the United States.

chunks.title: South Oyster Bay
chunks.text: The harbor is formed by Jones Beach Island, a barrier island on the southern side of Long Island.

chunks.title: South Oyster Bay
chunks.text: It is approximately 3 mi (5 km) wide between the two islands, and approximately 15 mi (24 km) long.

chunks.title: South Oyster Bay
chunks.text: It links to Great South Bay on its eastern end and opens to the Atlantic Ocean through inlets on either side of Jones Beach Island.

chunks.title: Great South Bay
chunks.text: Great South Bay, actually a lagoon, is situated between Long Island and Fire Island, in the State of New York.

chunks.title: Great South Bay
chunks.text: It is approximately 45 mi long and protected from the Atlantic Ocean by Fire Island, a barrier island, as well as the eastern end of Jones Beach Island and Captree Island.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: Short Beach is the beach on the northern shore of the western end of Jones Beach Island.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: The beach faces Great South Bay instead of the Atlantic Ocean, thereby providing some shelter from storm waves.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: Since 1851 it has been the home of a coastal lifesaving station operated (at first) by the United States Life-Saving Service and later by the United States Coast Guard.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: The current facility, Station Short Beach, typically does around 500 search and rescue missions each year —one of the busiest units in the Coast Guard's 1st District.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: The Jones Beach State Park's West End Boat Basin is also on Short Beach.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: The Jones Beach West End barracks of the New York State Park Police is around 200 feet south of the Short Beach shoreline.

chunks.title: Short Beach (New York)
chunks.text: An uninhabited islet, Short Beach Island, is usually just offshore, but occasionally connects to the beach when low tide exposes sandbars to the surface.

chunks.title: Lower South Bay, New York
chunks.text: Lower South Bay, commonly called South Bay, is a hamlet on the southwest corner of Oneida Lake, Onondaga County, New York State, United States.

chunks.title: Lower South Bay, New York
chunks.text: It is opposite North Bay, and is surrounded by many islands to the west, north and east, including Geersbeck Island, Hall Island, Glosky Island, Schroeppel Island, Denmans Island and Long Island (not to be confused with Long Island, New York City).

chunks.title: Lower South Bay, New York
chunks.text: Lower South Bay also lies near the town of Cicero, about 2 miles west.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: The Yaté Dam is an arch dam on the Yaté River in Yaté commune of New Caledonia, France.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: The primary purpose of the dam is hydroelectric power generation and it supports a 68 MW power station.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: Plans for the project began in the early 1950s and the dam was designed by Coyne et Bellier.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: The owner and operator of the project, New Caledonian Society Energy (ENERCAL), was established on 27 August 1955 to implement the project.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: Construction began that year and the power station was commissioned in 1958.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: The dam and entire scheme was inaugurated by Jacques Soustelle, then Minister of State in charge of Overseas Departments, on 21 September 1959.

chunks.title: Yaté Dam
chunks.text: It is the tallest dam and creates the largest reservoir in New Caledonia.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: Campo Verde Solar Project is a 139-megawatt (MW) solar photovoltaic power station in Imperial County, California.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: The project was approved in December 2012.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: Construction began in early 2013 and was completed the same year.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: Designed and constructed by U.S. thin-film manufacturer First Solar, the plant uses nearly 2.3 million CdTe-PV modules.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: Campo Verde Solar was acquired in April 2013 by Southern Power and Turner Renewable Energy.

chunks.title: Campo Verde Solar Project
chunks.text: First Solar acquired the project in 2012 from US Solar Holdings LLC, which had developed the project and negotiated the 139 MW PPA with SDG&E.

chunks.title: Jeder Rappen zählt
chunks.text: Jeder Rappen zählt (JRZ) "(literally Every rappen (nickel) counts)" is the Swiss version of the Serious Request that broadcasts on Dutch radio/television.

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: Sega Hard Girls (Japanese: セガ・ハード・ガールズ , Hepburn: Sega Hādo Gāruzu ) is a Japanese multimedia project produced as a collaboration between ASCII Media Works' Dengeki Bunko imprint and video game company Sega.

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: The project re-imagines various Sega video game consoles as anthropomorphized goddesses who appear all over modern Japan.

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: The project has inspired a light novel series written by Tōru Shiwasu with illustrations by Kei, which began serialization in ASCII Media Works' "Dengeki Bunko Magazine" in June 2013, and an anime television series adaptation titled "Hi-sCoool!

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: SeHa Girls" (Hi☆sCoool!

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: セハガール , Hai Sukūru SeHa Gāru ) by TMS Entertainment, which aired in Japan between October and December 2014.

chunks.title: Sega Hard Girls
chunks.text: A crossover video game with Idea Factory's "Hyperdimension Neptunia" franchise, "Superdimension Neptune VS Sega Hard Girls", was released for the PlayStation Vita in Japan in November 2015, and in North America and Europe in October 2016.

chunks.title: The Ogden
chunks.text: The Ogden (originally Streamline Tower) is a 21-story luxury condominium tower located at 150 North Las Vegas Boulevard in downtown Las Vegas, Nevada.

chunks.title: The Ogden
chunks.text: The Ogden was announced in 2004 as the Streamline Tower condominium project, to be built on the former 1 acre property of the Golden Inn motel, which was demolished at the end of the year.

chunks.title: The Ogden
chunks.text: Work on the property began in 2005, to prepare it for the new project, which began construction the following year.

chunks.title: The Ogden
chunks.text: The project was financed by Corus Bank, and was developed by a half-dozen investors, including Las Vegas Stars baseball player Dusty Allen.

chunks.title: Serious Request
chunks.text: Serious Request is a family of annual multi-day, multimedia fundraising events for International Red Cross initiatives, typically hosted by radio stations in the week before Christmas.

chunks.title: Serious Request
chunks.text: The project was begun in 2004 by Dutch public pop music radio station 3FM.

chunks.title: Serious Request
chunks.text: "Serious Request" projects have since been adopted in Belgium, Switzerland, Sweden, Kenya, South Korea, Austria, Latvia and Portugal.

chunks.title: The Greenhouse Project
chunks.text: The Greenhouse Project is a non-profit organization which began as an art project by college students to raise awareness about the growing need for aid for Uganda's orphans.

chunks.title: The Greenhouse Project
chunks.text: The organization's main goals are to provide impoverished, underfunded orphanages around the world with the means to become self-sustaining.

chunks.title: The Greenhouse Project
chunks.text: The original project was named after the Greenhouse Orphanage of Mengo, Uganda, the orphanage which inspired the project's beginning.

chunks.title: High Resolution Microwave Survey
chunks.text: The High Resolution Microwave Survey was a NASA project that was to scan ten million frequencies using radio telescopes.

chunks.title: High Resolution Microwave Survey
chunks.text: A decade in the making, the objective was to find transmissions from alien intelligences.

chunks.title: High Resolution Microwave Survey
chunks.text: The primary point of observation for the project was the Arecibo Ionospheric Observatory in Puerto Rico.

chunks.title: High Resolution Microwave Survey
chunks.text: The project began in October 1992 with SETI researcher Jill Tarter on board.

chunks.title: High Resolution Microwave Survey
chunks.text: However, a year later, first-term Nevada Senator Richard Bryan succeeded in shutting down the project.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: Wikisource is an online digital library of free content textual sources on a wiki, operated by the Wikimedia Foundation.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: Wikisource is the name of the project as a whole and the name for each instance of that project (each instance usually representing a different language); multiple Wikisources make up the overall project of Wikisource.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: The project's aims are to host all forms of free text, in many languages, and translations.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: Originally conceived as an archive to store useful or important historical texts (its first text was the "Déclaration universelle des Droits de l'Homme"), it has expanded to become a general-content library.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: The project officially began in November 24, 2003 under the name Project Sourceberg, a play on the famous Project Gutenberg.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: The name Wikisource was adopted later that year and it received its own domain name seven months later.

chunks.title: Wikisource
chunks.text: The project has come under criticism for lack of reliability but it is also cited by organisations such as the National Archives and Records Administration.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Project Dragonfly is an American educational project.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: It was initially designed to give children opportunities in inquiry based learning in the sciences.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: The project was started as a magazine and website produced by professors in the Western College Program at Miami University and the National Science Teachers Association with a grant from the National Science Foundation and assistance from the Center for Human Development, Learning, and Teaching at Miami University.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Project Dragonfly now reaches millions of people each year through inquiry-driven learning media, public exhibits and graduate programs worldwide.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Project Dragonfly's partnership programs have generated an Emmy-Award-winning PBS television series, teacher workshops, master's degrees, public science exhibits, and conservation and education programs worldwide.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Supported by the National Science Foundation, the project began in 1994 with the first national magazine to feature children's science investigations and discoveries.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Project Dragonfly's programs include Earth Expeditions global graduate courses for educators and other professionals, the Global Field Program (GFP) and Advanced Inquiry Program (AIP) master's degrees, and iSaveSpecies, which engages zoo visitors throughout the country in science and conservation action.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Project Dragonfly is based in the biology department at Miami University, a state university in Oxford, Ohio.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Miami was established in 1809 and is listed as one of the eight original Public Ivies.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Public Engagement Projects include: iSaveSpecies, Wild Research, DragonflyTV.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Graduate Credit Workshops include Earth Expeditions, Zoo Expeditions, and iDiscovery.

chunks.title: Dragonfly Project
chunks.text: Master's Degree Programs include Global Field Program (GFP) and Advanced Inquiry Program (AIP), and Earth Expeditions (EE).

chunks.title: The One and Only (1999 film)
chunks.text: The One and Only (Danish: "Den Eneste Ene" ) is a 1999 Danish romantic comedy film directed by Susanne Bier.

chunks.title: The One and Only (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film starred Sidse Babett Knudsen, Niels Olsen, Rafael Edholm, and Paprika Steen in story about two unfaithful married couples faced with becoming first-time parents.

chunks.title: The One and Only (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film was considered to mark a modern transition in Danish romantic comedies, and became the third biggest box-office success of the 1990s in Denmark.

chunks.title: The One and Only (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film earned both the Robert Award and Bodil Award as the Best Film of 1999.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: The Night Manager is a British television serial directed by Susanne Bier and starring Tom Hiddleston, Hugh Laurie, Olivia Colman, David Harewood, Tom Hollander, and Elizabeth Debicki.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: It is based on the 1993 novel of the same name by John le Carré and adapted by David Farr to the present day.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: The six-part series began broadcasting on BBC One on 21 February 2016.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: In the United States, it began on 19 April 2016 on AMC.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: IMG sold the series internationally to over 180 countries.

chunks.title: The Night Manager (miniseries)
chunks.text: A second series has been commissioned by the BBC and AMC.

chunks.title: A Boy and His Dog (1975 film)
chunks.text: A Boy and His Dog is a 1975 American science fiction comedy-drama thriller film produced, written (with Alvy Moore), and directed by L. Q. Jones, starring Don Johnson, Susanne Benton, Alvy Moore, and Jason Robards.

chunks.title: A Boy and His Dog (1975 film)
chunks.text: The film was distributed in the United States by LQ/JAF Productions and in the United Kingdom by Anglo-EMI Film Distributors.

chunks.title: A Boy and His Dog (1975 film)
chunks.text: The film's script is based on the 1969 cycle of narratives by fantasy author Harlan Ellison titled "A Boy and His Dog".

chunks.title: Chaste Susanne (film)
chunks.text: Chaste Susanne (German:Die keusche Susanne) is a 1926 German silent comedy film directed by Richard Eichberg and starring Lilian Harvey, Willy Fritsch and Ruth Weyher.

chunks.title: Chaste Susanne (film)
chunks.text: It is based on the 1910 operetta "Die keusche Susanne" composed by Jean Gilbert with a libretto by Georg Okonkowski.

chunks.title: Chaste Susanne (film)
chunks.text: In Britain it was released under the alternative title The Girl in the Taxi in reference to "The Girl in the Taxi" in the English version of the operetta.

chunks.title: Chaste Susanne (film)
chunks.text: The film's art direction is by Jacek Rotmil.

chunks.title: All Dogs Go to Heaven
chunks.text: All Dogs Go to Heaven is a 1989 animated musical comedy-drama film directed and produced by Don Bluth, and released by United Artists and Goldcrest Films.

chunks.title: All Dogs Go to Heaven
chunks.text: It tells the story of Charlie B. Barkin (voiced by Burt Reynolds), a German Shepherd that is murdered by his former friend, Carface (voiced by Vic Tayback, in his final film role), but withdraws from his place in Heaven to return to Earth, where his best friend, Itchy Itchiford (voiced by Dom DeLuise) still lives, and he teams up with a young orphan girl named Anne-Marie (voiced by Judith Barsi, in her final film role), who teaches them an important lesson about kindness, friendship and love.

chunks.title: The Great Mouse Detective
chunks.text: The Great Mouse Detective is a 1986 American animated mystery comedy film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: The Great Mouse Detective
chunks.text: The 26th Disney animated feature film, the film was directed by Burny Mattinson, David Michener, and the team of John Musker and Ron Clements, who later directed Disney's hit films "The Little Mermaid" and "Aladdin".

chunks.title: The Great Mouse Detective
chunks.text: The film was also known as The Adventures of the Great Mouse Detective for its 1992 theatrical re-release and Basil the Great Mouse Detective in some countries.

chunks.title: The Great Mouse Detective
chunks.text: The main characters are all mice and rats living in Victorian London.

chunks.title: Brothers (2009 film)
chunks.text: Brothers is a 2009 American psychological war drama film and a remake of Susanne Bier's Danish film "Brødre" (2004), which takes place in Afghanistan and Denmark.

chunks.title: Brothers (2009 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Tobey Maguire, Jake Gyllenhaal, and Natalie Portman, and is directed by Jim Sheridan.

chunks.title: Brothers (2009 film)
chunks.text: Both films take inspiration from Homer's epic poem, the "Odyssey".

chunks.title: Brothers (2009 film)
chunks.text: The film received a mixed to positive response and grossed $43 million.

chunks.title: Brothers (2009 film)
chunks.text: Tobey Maguire received particular praise for his performance and received a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actor in a Motion Picture Drama for his performance.

chunks.title: Shrek 2
chunks.text: Shrek 2 is a 2004 American computer-animated fantasy film produced by DreamWorks Animation and directed by Andrew Adamson, Kelly Asbury and Conrad Vernon.

chunks.title: Shrek 2
chunks.text: It is the sequel to 2001's "Shrek", with Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy and Cameron Diaz reprising their respective voice roles of Shrek, Donkey, and Fiona from the first film, joined by Antonio Banderas, Julie Andrews, John Cleese, Rupert Everett, and Jennifer Saunders.

chunks.title: Shrek 2
chunks.text: Sometime after the first film, Shrek, Donkey and Fiona go to visit Fiona's parents (voiced by Andrews and Cleese), while Shrek and Donkey discover that a greedy Fairy God Mother (voiced by Saunders) is plotting to destroy Shrek and Fiona's marriage so Fiona can marry her son, Prince Charming (voiced by Everett).

chunks.title: Shrek 2
chunks.text: Shrek and Donkey team up with a swashing cat named Puss in Boots (voiced by Banderas) to stop her.

chunks.title: Susanne Pollatschek
chunks.text: Susanne Pollatschek (born February 7, 1977) is a Scottish-born Glaswegian actress, who voiced Olivia Flaversham in the 1986 Disney animated film "The Great Mouse Detective" when she was eight years old.

chunks.title: My Niece Susanne
chunks.text: My Niece Susanne (German: Meine Nichte Susanne) is a 1950 West German musical comedy film directed by  Wolfgang Liebeneiner and starring  Hilde Krahl, Inge Meysel and Harald Paulsen.

chunks.title: My Niece Susanne
chunks.text: It is set in Paris at the beginning of the twentieth century.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: The Settlers IV (German: "Die Siedler IV" ), released as The Settlers: Fourth Edition in North America, is a 2001 real-time strategy video game developed by Blue Byte and published by Ubi Soft Entertainment for Microsoft Windows.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: It is the fourth game in "The Settlers" series, following "The Settlers" (1993), "The Settlers II" (1996) and "The Settlers III" (1998).

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In August 2001, Blue Byte released an expansion, "The Settlers IV Mission CD", featuring new single-player campaign missions, new maps for both single-player and online multiplayer modes, a random map generator, and a map editor.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In December, they released a second expansion, "The Settlers IV: The Trojans and the Elixir of Power" (German: "Die Siedler IV: Die Trojaner und das Elixier der Macht" ), containing new single-player campaigns, and additional single and multiplayer maps.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In 2002, "The Settlers IV: Gold Edition" was released, containing the original game and both expansions, plus fan-made maps for multiplayer mode, and two minigames.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In 2009, Gameloft ported the original game to iOS, under the title The Settlers.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: Although featuring updated graphics and utilising touch controls, the gameplay, game mechanics and storyline are identical to the original.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In 2010, "The Settlers" was released for webOS, specifically optimised for the Palm Pre.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: Gameloft later released HD versions for iPad, bada, Symbian and Android.

chunks.title: The Settlers IV
chunks.text: In 2013, the "Gold Edition" was released on GOG.com.

chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail
chunks.text: Jones Falls Trail (typically abbreviated JFT) is a hiking and bicycling trail in Baltimore, Maryland.

chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail
chunks.text: It mostly runs along the length of the namesake Jones Falls, a major north–south stream in and north of the city that has long acted as a major transportation corridor for the city.

chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail
chunks.text: It also incorporates the bike path encircling Druid Hill Reservoir and its namesake park.

chunks.title: Jones Falls Trail
chunks.text: The Jones Falls Trail forms a segment of the East Coast Greenway, a partially completed network of off-road bicycling routes that runs the length of the East Coast.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: M-1, commonly known as Woodward Avenue, is a north–south state trunkline highway in the Metro Detroit area of the US state of Michigan.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: The highway, called "Detroit's Main Street", runs from Detroit north-northwesterly to Pontiac.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: It is one of the five principal avenues of Detroit, along with Michigan, Grand River, Gratiot, and Jefferson avenues.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: These streets were platted in 1805 by Judge Augustus B. Woodward, namesake to Woodward Avenue.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) has listed the highway as the Automotive Heritage Trail, an All-American Road in the National Scenic Byways Program.

chunks.title: M-1 (Michigan highway)
chunks.text: It has also been designated a Pure Michigan Byway by the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT), and was also included in the MotorCities National Heritage Area designated by the US Congress in 1998.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: The Nathan F. Cobb was a three-masted schooner named after the shipbuilder and founder of Cobb’s Salvaging Company whose many rescues of stranded ships help lead to the formation of the United States Life-Saving Service.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: Despite its namesake's history of shipwreck rescues, the "Nathan F. Cobb" capsized in heavy seas on 1 December 1896 en route from Brunswick, Georgia to New York with a cargo of timber and cross ties.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: The cook and a shipmate drowned when they were swept overboard in violent seas.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: The crew righted the vessel by removing the three masts and they drifted for four days until they became grounded on a sandbar off Ormond Beach, Florida.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: Rescue attempts led to the drowning of volunteer Ferd Waterhouse, whose body was never recovered, but no other crew members were lost.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: A plaque commemorates Ferd Waterhouse’s rescue efforts.

chunks.title: Nathan F. Cobb
chunks.text: The Cobb Cottage, a structure built using materials salvaged from the ship, is part of Ormond Beach’s Historic Trail.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Gurnee School District 56 is a PK-8 school district located in the northern Lake County village of the school district's namesake: Gurnee, Illinois.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Gurnee School District 56 is composed of four schools; three schools run in succession to the other, while the other services all nine grades.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Education in this school district often begins in Spaulding Elementary School, which serves the first and second grades; it also has a prekindergarten program.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: The principal is Dr. Ellen Mauer and the assistant principal is Dr. Cheryl Caesar.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Spaulding feeds into Prairie Trail School, which educates third, fourth, and fifth graders.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Kevin Simmons is the school's principal.Sheryl Gray is the assistant principal at Prairie Trail.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: The last section that this branch of the district's education can provide is to sixth, seventh, and eighth graders at Viking Middle School, whose principal is Patrick Jones.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Viking is renowned for its wonderful drama and arts programs, along with its beautiful architecture.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: Viking Middle feeds into Warren Township High School in Gurnee, Illinois.

chunks.title: Gurnee School District 56
chunks.text: The current Viking School was completed in 1998 after a flood rendered the old building unusable.

chunks.title: Steve Prefontaine
chunks.text: Steve Roland "Pre" Prefontaine (January 25, 1951 – May 30, 1975) was an American middle and long-distance runner who competed in the 1972 Olympics.

chunks.title: Steve Prefontaine
chunks.text: Prefontaine once held the American record in seven different distance track events from the 2,000 meters to the 10,000 meters.

chunks.title: Steve Prefontaine
chunks.text: Prefontaine died in May 1975 at the age of 24 in an automobile accident in Eugene, Oregon.

chunks.title: 2003 SCCA ProRally season
chunks.text: The 2003 SCCA ProRally Season was the 31st season of the SCCA ProRally and won by Manxman David Higgins and co-driver Daniel Barritt.

chunks.title: 2003 SCCA ProRally season
chunks.text: Nine rounds were held but the season was overshadowed by a tragic accident at the Oregon Trail Rally in which the 2001 champion Mark Lovell and his co-driver Roger Freeman were killed.

chunks.title: 2003 SCCA ProRally season
chunks.text: They were the second and third drives to die in the series, after Jonel Broscanc, who was killed in an accident at the 1992 Susquehannock Trail Performance Rally.

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The United States Congress designated the Bell Mountain Wilderness in 1980.

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The wilderness area now has a total of 9027 acre .

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: Bell Mountain is located within the Potosi-Fredericktown Ranger District of the Mark Twain National Forest, south of Potosi, Missouri in the United States.

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The wilderness lies in the Saint Francois Mountains and it was named after its highest point, Bell Mountain (elevation: 1,702).

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The namesake Bell Mountain has the name of Henry Bell, a pioneer settler.

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The Bell Mountain Wilderness is one of eight wilderness areas protected and preserved in Missouri.

chunks.title: Bell Mountain Wilderness
chunks.text: The area is popular for hiking as there are 12 mi of trail, including a section of the Ozark Trail.

chunks.title: Pre's Trail
chunks.text: Pre's Trail, located on the north side of the Willamette River in Eugene, Oregon, United States, popularly referred to as "Track Town USA", is a four-mile-long running and walking trail named after heralded University of Oregon athlete Steve Prefontaine.

chunks.title: Pre's Trail
chunks.text: The woodchip-and-bark trail features riparian scenery, including grasslands, duck ponds, and woods, as well as guide signs with trail maps at each of three primary trailheads.

chunks.title: Pre's Trail
chunks.text: Near downtown Eugene, in Alton Baker Park, Pre's Trail is part of an extensive network of running trails in and around the university town and neighboring Springfield.

chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt
chunks.text: The Capital Area Greenbelt is a looping trail located in the area of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt
chunks.text: This 20-mile loop around Pennsylvania's capital city provides visitors and tourists with opportunities to hike, ride bicycles, skate, jog, fish, walk their dogs, enjoy native flora and fauna, and appreciate nature.

chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt
chunks.text: While parts of the trail are shared with roads, most of the loop is a dedicated path.

chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt
chunks.text: The Trail, as it is commonly referred to by locals, passes along the Susquehanna River through Reservoir Park, Riverfront Park, Five Senses Garden, and Wildwood Park and Nature Center.

chunks.title: Capital Area Greenbelt
chunks.text: In addition to beautiful parks, the Capital Area Greenbelt showcases some historical attractions including the grave site of John Harris Sr. (the namesake of the city of Harrisburg), the Governor's Mansion, and the National Civil War Museum.

chunks.title: Chevrolet Corvette
chunks.text: The Chevrolet Corvette, known colloquially as the Vette or Chevy Corvette, is a sports car manufactured by Chevrolet.

chunks.title: Chevrolet Corvette
chunks.text: The car has been produced through seven generations.

chunks.title: Chevrolet Corvette
chunks.text: The first model, a convertible, was introduced at the GM Motorama in 1953 as a concept show car.

chunks.title: Chevrolet Corvette
chunks.text: Myron Scott is credited for naming the car after the type of small, maneuverable warship called a corvette.

chunks.title: Chevrolet Corvette
chunks.text: Originally built in Flint, Michigan and St. Louis, Missouri, the Corvette is currently manufactured in Bowling Green, Kentucky and is the official sports car of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: Asmodeus ( ; Greek: Ασμοδαίος , "Asmodaios") or Ashmedai ( ; Hebrew: אַשְמְדּאָי‎ ‎ , "ʾAšmədʾāy"; see below for other variations) is a "king of demons" mostly known from the deuterocanonical Book of Tobit, in which he is the primary antagonist.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: The demon is also mentioned in some Talmudic legends; for instance, in the story of the construction of the Temple of Solomon.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: He was supposed by some Renaissance Christians to be the King of the Nine Hells.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: Asmodeus also is referred to as one of the seven princes of Hell.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: In Binsfeld's classification of demons, each one of these princes represents one of the seven deadly sins (Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Sloth, Wrath, Envy, and Pride).

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: Asmodeus is the demon of lust and is therefore responsible for twisting people's sexual desires, as seen in the book of Tobias especially.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: He is also said to be here on Earth after millions of years in hell.

chunks.title: Asmodeus
chunks.text: In Jewish and Islamic lore he is the king of the demons (Shedim/Jinn).

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: The Blessed and the Damned is a double CD best of compilation album by the American heavy metal band Iced Earth.

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: The CD-booklet can be reversed, to show either angels or demons on the cover.

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: The booklet also includes Jon Schaffer's comments on previous albums and his life.

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: Even though the CD was released after "The Glorious Burden", the biography in the booklet makes no mention of it.

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: This is probably because Iced Earth left their record label Century Media Records prior to "The Glorious Burden", and signed with SPV.

chunks.title: The Blessed and the Damned
chunks.text: In turn, Century Media released this compilation album.

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons is the third full-length studio album by the drone doom band Earth.

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: It has a more rock-oriented sound than their earlier drone doom work, although in a very minimalist style.

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: "Peace in Mississippi" is a cover of the Jimi Hendrix song.

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: The original vinyl release of this album has an alternative take of "Peace in Mississippi".

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: The car depicted on the cover is a "Sassy Grass Green" Plymouth Barracuda with the car's iconic hockey-stick decal saying "Earth."

chunks.title: Pentastar: In the Style of Demons
chunks.text: The "Pentastar" named in the album title is an apparent reference to the brand logo of Chrysler, parent company of Plymouth and also a reference to the fact that this is the fifth CD by Earth (its predecessor being 1995's Sunn Amps and Smashed Guitars).

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: Fial ("Fabbrica Italiana Automobili Legnano"), direct translation "Italian Automobile Factory Legnano", was a company that manufactured industrial and marine engines in Legnano.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: In 1906 it entered the automobile business and manufactured one car, Legnano Type A 6/8 HP.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: The car had a two-cylinder 1135 cc engine.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: Two years later in 1908, the company was placed in liquidation after filing for bankruptcy.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: In 1909 the company was taken over by Rosa & Ferrario and car production ended.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: The 6/8 model was the only model they ever produced.

chunks.title: Fial
chunks.text: The Legnano is at display on Museo Nazionale dell'Automobile in Turin.

chunks.title: Plymouth Barracuda
chunks.text: The Plymouth Barracuda is a two-door car that was manufactured by Plymouth from the 1964 to 1974 model years.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: The Friend was an automobile manufactured in Pontiac, Michigan by the Friend Motors Corporation in 1920.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: Otis Friend had taken over the Olympian Motor Company in 1920, and manufactured that car until the car named after himself was ready.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: The Friend was shown at the New York Automobile Show in January 1921, featured a four-cylinder engine, a 112-inch (2842mm) wheelbase, and had a five-seater, two-door roadster body.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: Wooden artillery and wire wheels were options.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: The Friend originally sold for $1585.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: With sales sluggish, the price was reduced further to $1185, but this had no effect, and production ended with fewer than fifty cars built.

chunks.title: Friend (automobile)
chunks.text: A six-cylinder model was planned, but the company went out of business before any were manufactured.

chunks.title: Demons and Wizards (band)
chunks.text: Demons and Wizards is a power metal band conceived as a side-project by vocalist for Blind Guardian, Hansi Kürsch, and the guitarist for Iced Earth, Jon Schaffer.

chunks.title: Demons and Wizards (band)
chunks.text: Schaffer writes the music and Kürsch writes the lyrics.

chunks.title: Demons and Wizards (band)
chunks.text: The band's line-up during the recording of their first album in 1999 also featured Mark Prator, who was the drummer on a few Iced Earth albums, and Jim Morris doing most of the guitar solos, Morris also having worked with Iced Earth in the past.

chunks.title: Late model
chunks.text: A "late model car" is a car which has been recently designed or manufactured, often the latest model.

chunks.title: Late model
chunks.text: (An "early model car" or "classic car" is a car old enough to be of historical interest; there is no usual intermediate term.)

chunks.title: Late model
chunks.text: The term is broadly used in car racing, and often appears in common use, as in: "The officer was driving an unmarked, late model sedan."

chunks.title: Demons (Get Scared album)
chunks.text: Demons is the third studio album by American post-hardcore band Get Scared, released on October 30, 2015 via Fearless Records.

chunks.title: Demons (Get Scared album)
chunks.text: The album marks a departure from previous releases, such as "Everyone's Out to Get Me" and "Built for Blame, Laced With Shame" in favor of a style reminiscent of the band's 2009 EP "Cheap Tricks and Theatrics" with metalcore elements mixed in.

chunks.title: Demons (Get Scared album)
chunks.text: "Demons" was produced with Erik Ron who also worked with the band on "Everyone's Out to Get Me" and "Built for Blame, Laced With Shame" and received positive reviews upon release.

chunks.title: Demons (Get Scared album)
chunks.text: The hands of the clock on the cover show time that does not exist.

chunks.title: Demons (Get Scared album)
chunks.text: Since, the hand that shows the hours is slightly past 1 o'clock, and the minute hand is located between eleven and twelve.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Super Cup
chunks.text: The 2011 UEFA Super Cup was the 36th UEFA Super Cup, between the reigning champions of the two club competitions organised by the European football governing body UEFA: the UEFA Champions League and the UEFA Europa League.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Super Cup
chunks.text: It took place at the Stade Louis II in Monaco on 26 August 2011.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Super Cup
chunks.text: It was contested by the 2010–11 UEFA Champions League winners Barcelona of Spain and the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League winners Porto of Portugal.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Super Cup
chunks.text: Barcelona won the title defeating Porto 2–0.

chunks.title: 2017–18 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The 2017–18 UEFA Champions League knockout phase will begin on 13 February and end on 26 May 2018 with the final at the NSC Olimpiyskiy Stadium in Kiev, Ukraine, to decide the champions of the 2017–18 UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2017–18 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: A total of 16 teams compete in the knockout phase.

chunks.title: 2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The knockout phase of the 2010–11 UEFA Champions League began on 15 February and concluded on 28 May 2011 with the final at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

chunks.title: 2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The knockout phase involved the 16 teams who finished in the top two in each of their groups in the group stage.

chunks.title: 2015–16 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The 2015–16 UEFA Champions League knockout phase began on 16 February and concluded on 28 May 2016 with the final at San Siro in Milan, Italy, to decide the champions of the 2015–16 UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2015–16 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: A total of 16 teams competed in the knockout phase.

chunks.title: 2000–01 UEFA Champions League
chunks.text: The 2000–01 UEFA Champions League was the 46th season of the UEFA Champions League, UEFA's premier European club football tournament, and the ninth since it was rebranded from the "European Champion Clubs' Cup" or "European Cup".

chunks.title: 2000–01 UEFA Champions League
chunks.text: The competition was won by Bayern Munich (first title since 1976), who beat Valencia 5–4 on penalties after a 1–1 draw after extra time.

chunks.title: 2000–01 UEFA Champions League
chunks.text: It was their first UEFA Champions League title, and their fourth European Cup title overall, it was Valencia's second consecutive final defeat, losing to Real Madrid in the previous season.

chunks.title: 2000–01 UEFA Champions League
chunks.text: The knockout phase saw Bayern eliminate the preceding two Champions League winners, Manchester United and Real Madrid, winning all four games in the process.

chunks.title: 2000–01 UEFA Champions League
chunks.text: Valencia, meanwhile, defeated English sides Arsenal and Leeds United in the knockout phase en route to the final.

chunks.title: 2010–11 UEFA Europa League knockout phase
chunks.text: The knockout phase of the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League began on 15 February and concluded on 18 May 2011 with the final at Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Republic of Ireland.

chunks.title: 2010–11 UEFA Europa League knockout phase
chunks.text: The knockout phase involved 32 teams: the 24 teams that finished in the top two in each group in the group stage and the eight teams that finished in third place in the UEFA Champions League group stage.

chunks.title: 2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The 2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase began on 17 February and concluded on 6 June 2015 with the final at Olympiastadion in Berlin, Germany to decide the champions of the 2014–15 UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: A total of 16 teams competed in the knockout phase.

chunks.title: 2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: The 2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase began on 14 February and ended on 3 June 2017 with the final at Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, to decide the champions of the 2016–17 UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
chunks.text: A total of 16 teams competed in the knockout phase.

chunks.title: 2017 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: The 2017 UEFA Champions League Final was the final match of the 2016–17 UEFA Champions League, the 62nd season of Europe's premier club football tournament organised by UEFA, and the 25th season since it was renamed from the European Champion Clubs' Cup to the UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2017 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: It was played at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, Wales on 3 June 2017, between Italian side Juventus and Spanish side and title holders Real Madrid, in a repeat of the 1998 final.

chunks.title: 2017 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: Real Madrid won the match 4–1 to secure their 12th title in this competition.

chunks.title: 2017 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: With this victory, as the defending champions, Real Madrid became the first ever team to successfully defend their title in the Champions League era, and the first to do so since Milan in 1990.

chunks.title: 2017 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: On the other hand, Juventus lost a fifth final in a row and a seventh in nine finals reached.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: The 2011 UEFA Champions League Final was a football match played on 28 May 2011 at Wembley Stadium in London that decided the winner of the 2010–11 season of the UEFA Champions League.

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: The winners received the European Champion Clubs' Cup (the European Cup).

chunks.title: 2011 UEFA Champions League Final
chunks.text: The 2011 final was the culmination of the 56th season of the tournament, and the 19th in the Champions League era.

chunks.title: Iryna Amshennikova
chunks.text: Iryna Vitaliïvna Amshennikova (Ukrainian: Ірина Віталіївна Амшеннікова , born 19 May 1986) is a Ukrainian backstroke swimmer.

chunks.title: Iryna Amshennikova
chunks.text: She had her best achievements in short course competitions, where she won bronze at the 2002 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) in the 200 m backstroke and six medals, including one gold, at the European Short Course Swimming Championships.

chunks.title: Iryna Amshennikova

chunks.title: Iryna Amshennikova
chunks.text: During her career she set 29 national records in the 50–200 m backstroke and various relay events.

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen
chunks.text: She competed for Team Finland at the 2012 Summer Olympics.

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen
chunks.text: Her final ranking in the 100m breaststroke was 34th and 32nd in the 200m breaststroke.

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen

chunks.title: Jenna Laukkanen

chunks.title: Swedish Short Course Swimming Championships
chunks.text: Swimmers representing Swedish swim teams may participate.

chunks.title: Swedish Short Course Swimming Championships
chunks.text: Non-Swedish swimmers who have participated include Anthony Ervin and Attila Czene.

chunks.title: Royal Arena

chunks.title: Esther Baron

chunks.title: Esther Baron
chunks.text: She had her best achievements in the 200 m backstroke event: gold medals in the European Championships of 2006, long course and short course, silver medal at the 2007 European Short Course Swimming Championships and fourth place at the 2007 World Aquatics Championships.

chunks.title: Esther Baron

chunks.title: Apollo 9
chunks.text: Apollo 9 was the third manned mission in the United States Apollo space program and the first flight of the Command/Service Module (CSM) with the Lunar Module (LM, pronounced "lem").

chunks.title: Apollo 9
chunks.text: Its three-person crew, consisting of Commander James McDivitt, Command Module Pilot David Scott, and Lunar Module Pilot Rusty Schweickart, spent ten days in low Earth orbit testing several aspects critical to landing on the Moon, including the LM engines, backpack life support systems, navigation systems, and docking maneuvers.

chunks.title: Apollo 9
chunks.text: The mission was the second manned launch of a Saturn V rocket.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 7
chunks.text: Shenzhou 7 () was the third human spaceflight mission of the Chinese space program.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 7
chunks.text: The mission, which included the first Chinese extra-vehicular activity (EVA) carried out by crew members Zhai Zhigang and Liu Boming, marked the commencement of the second phase of the Chinese government's Project 921.

chunks.title: Soyuz TMA-9
chunks.text: Soyuz TMA-9 was a Soyuz mission to the International Space Station (ISS) launched by a Soyuz FG launch vehicle.

chunks.title: Soyuz TMA-9
chunks.text: It was a human spaceflight mission transporting personnel to and from the ISS.

chunks.title: Soyuz TMA-9
chunks.text: It launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on 18 September 2006 at 08:09 MSD (04:09 UTC), docked with the ISS at 09:21 MSD (05:21 UTC) on 20 September, and returned to Earth on 21 April 2007.

chunks.title: Soyuz TMA-9
chunks.text: Soyuz TMA-9 transported two-thirds of ISS Expedition 14 to the space station along with one "spaceflight participant" who performed several experiments on behalf of the European Space Agency.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 5
chunks.text: Shenzhou 5 () — was the first human spaceflight mission of the Chinese space program, launched on 15 October 2003.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 5
chunks.text: The Shenzhou spacecraft was launched on a Long March 2F launch vehicle.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 5
chunks.text: There had been four previous flights of unmanned Shenzhou missions since 1999.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 5
chunks.text: China became the third country in the world to have independent human spaceflight capability after the Soviet Union (later, Russia) and the United States.

chunks.title: Apollo 10
chunks.text: Apollo 10 was the fourth manned mission in the United States Apollo space program, and the second (after Apollo 8) to orbit the Moon.

chunks.title: Apollo 10
chunks.text: Launched on May 18, 1969, it was the F mission: a "dress rehearsal" for the first Moon landing, testing all of the components and procedures, just short of actually landing.

chunks.title: Apollo 10
chunks.text: The Lunar Module (LM) followed a descent orbit to within 8.4 nmi of the lunar surface, at the point where powered descent for landing would normally begin.

chunks.title: Apollo 10
chunks.text: Its success enabled the first landing to be attempted on the Apollo 11 mission two months later.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: Apollo 7 was an October 1968 human spaceflight mission carried out by the United States.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: It was the first mission in the United States' Apollo program to carry a crew into space.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: It was also the first U.S. spaceflight to carry astronauts since the flight of Gemini XII in November 1966.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: The AS-204 mission, also known as "Apollo 1", was intended to be the first manned flight of the Apollo program.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: It was scheduled to launch in February 1967, but a fire in the cabin during a January 1967 test killed the crew.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: Manned flights were then suspended for 21 months, while the cause of the accident was investigated and improvements made to the spacecraft and safety procedures, and unmanned test flights of the Saturn V rocket and Apollo Lunar Module were made.

chunks.title: Apollo 7
chunks.text: Apollo 7 fulfilled Apollo 1's mission of testing the Apollo Command/Service Module (CSM) in low Earth orbit.

chunks.title: Apollo 16
chunks.text: Apollo 16 was the tenth manned mission in the United States Apollo space program, the fifth and penultimate to land on the Moon and the first to land in the lunar highlands.

chunks.title: Apollo 16
chunks.text: The second of the so-called "J missions," it was crewed by Commander John Young, Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke and Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly.

chunks.title: Apollo 16
chunks.text: Launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 12:54 PM EST on April 16, 1972, the mission lasted 11 days, 1 hour, and 51 minutes, and concluded at 2:45 PM EST on April 27.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 6
chunks.text: Shenzhou 6 ( "Shénzhōu lìuhào") was the second human spaceflight of the Chinese space program, launched on October 12, 2005 on a Long March 2F rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 6
chunks.text: The Shenzhou spacecraft carried a crew of Fèi Jùnlóng (费俊龙) and Niè Hǎishèng (聂海胜) for five days in low Earth orbit.

chunks.title: Shenzhou 6
chunks.text: It launched three days before the second anniversary of China's first human spaceflight, "Shenzhou 5".

chunks.title: Frank Borman
chunks.text: Frank Frederick Borman II (born March 14, 1928), (Col, USAF, Ret.)

chunks.title: Frank Borman
chunks.text: , is a retired United States Air Force pilot, aeronautical engineer, test pilot, and NASA astronaut, best remembered as the Commander of Apollo 8, the first mission to fly around the Moon, making him, along with crew mates Jim Lovell and Bill Anders, the first of only 24 humans to do so.

chunks.title: Frank Borman
chunks.text: Before flying on Apollo, he set a fourteen-day spaceflight endurance record on Gemini 7, and also served on the NASA review board which investigated the Apollo 1 fire.

chunks.title: Frank Borman
chunks.text: After leaving NASA, he was the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Eastern Air Lines from 1975 to 1986.

chunks.title: Frank Borman
chunks.text: Borman is a recipient of the Congressional Space Medal of Honor.

chunks.title: Apollo 8
chunks.text: Apollo 8, the second human spaceflight mission in the United States Apollo space program, was launched on December 21, 1968, and became the first crewed spacecraft to leave Earth orbit, reach the Earth's Moon, orbit it and return safely to Earth.

chunks.title: Apollo 8
chunks.text: The three-astronaut crew — Commander Frank Borman, Command Module Pilot James Lovell, and Lunar Module Pilot William Anders — became the first humans to: travel beyond low Earth orbit; escape Earth's gravity; see Earth as a whole planet; enter the gravity well of another celestial body (Earth's moon); orbit another celestial body (Earth's moon); directly see the far side of the Moon with their own eyes; witness an Earthrise; escape the gravity of another celestial body (Earth's moon); and re-enter the gravitational well of Earth.

chunks.title: Apollo 8
chunks.text: The 1968 mission, the third flight of the Saturn V rocket and that rocket's first crewed launch, was also the first human spaceflight launch from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida, located adjacent to Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.

chunks.title: Freeloaders (film)
chunks.text: Freeloaders is an American ensemble comedy film directed by Dan Rosen and written by Rosen and singer Dave Gibbs.

chunks.title: Freeloaders (film)
chunks.text: The film is produced by the Broken Lizard comedy troupe and is independently financed.

chunks.title: Freeloaders (film)
chunks.text: "Freeloaders" stars Clifton Collins Jr., Josh Lawson, Kevin Sussman, Zoe Boyle, Nat Faxon, Warren Hutcherson, Jane Seymour, Olivia Munn, Dave Foley and Counting Crows lead singer Adam Duritz.

chunks.title: Freeloaders (film)
chunks.text: It follows a group of friends who find their luxurious lifestyle threatened when the rock star they freeload off decides to sell his home.

chunks.title: Office Christmas Party

chunks.title: Office Christmas Party
chunks.text: The film stars an ensemble cast, including Jason Bateman, Olivia Munn, T. J. Miller, Jillian Bell, Vanessa Bayer, Courtney B. Vance, Rob Corddry, Kate McKinnon and Jennifer Aniston, and was released on December 9, 2016 by Paramount Pictures.

chunks.title: Office Christmas Party
chunks.text: It grossed $114 million worldwide.

chunks.title: Deliver Us from Evil (2014 film)

chunks.title: Deliver Us from Evil (2014 film)
chunks.text: The film is officially based on a 2001 non-fiction book entitled "Beware the Night" by Ralph Sarchie and Lisa Collier Cool, and its marketing campaign highlighted that it was "inspired by actual accounts".

chunks.title: Deliver Us from Evil (2014 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Eric Bana, Édgar Ramírez, Sean Harris, Olivia Munn, and Joel McHale in the main roles and was released on July 2, 2014.

chunks.title: The Lego Ninjago Movie
chunks.text: The Lego Ninjago Movie is a 2017 3D computer-animated action comedy martial arts film produced by Warner Animation Group.

chunks.title: The Lego Ninjago Movie

chunks.title: The Lego Ninjago Movie

chunks.title: The Lego Ninjago Movie

chunks.title: Olivia Munn
chunks.text: Lisa Olivia Munn (born July 3, 1980) is an American actress and model.

chunks.title: Olivia Munn
chunks.text: She was credited as Lisa Munn in her early career, but since 2006, she has used the name Olivia Munn.

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: Akira Fuse (布施 明 , Fuse Akira , born on December 18, 1947) is a Japanese singer, who was once married to Olivia Hussey.

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: He debuted in 1965 with the single "Kimi ni Namida to Hohoemi o" (君に涙とほほえみを , "Tears and Smiles to You") .

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: His greatest hits are "Cyclamen no Kahori" (シクラメンのかほり , Shikuramen no Kahori , "The Scent of Cyclamen") and "Kimi wa Bara Yori Utsukushii" (君は薔薇より美しい , "You are More Beautiful than a Rose") .

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: He currently makes consistent appearances on television, performs occasional seasonal tours, hosts a late night talk show, and is involved in a number of stage plays.

chunks.title: Akira Fuse

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: and later its second opening theme "Hajimari no Kimi e" (始まりの君へ , "To the Original You") .

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: He married the actress Olivia Hussey in 1980 and later divorced in 1989 after he was unable to attain work in the United States and Olivia was unable to relocate her first-born son to Japan.

chunks.title: Akira Fuse
chunks.text: They had one child, son Maximillian Fuse, who currently attends university in America.

chunks.title: The Babymakers

chunks.title: The Babymakers
chunks.text: Chandrasekhar and Heffernan are both members of Broken Lizard.

chunks.title: The Babymakers
chunks.text: The film received a limited release on August 3, 2012 in theaters and on video on demand services.

chunks.title: The Babymakers
chunks.text: It received a DVD and Blu-ray release September 18, 2012.

chunks.title: Desi Lydic

chunks.title: Desi Lydic
chunks.text: She also stars as guidance counselor Valerie Marks on the MTV comedy-drama series "Awkward".

chunks.title: Desi Lydic
chunks.text: She got her start in the 2001 parody film "Not Another Teen Movie".

chunks.title: Desi Lydic

chunks.title: Desi Lydic

chunks.title: Desi Lydic

chunks.title: Desi Lydic

chunks.title: Ride Along 2

chunks.title: Ride Along 2

chunks.title: Ride Along 2

chunks.title: Mortdecai (film)

chunks.title: Mortdecai (film)
