chunks.title: Mortdecai (film)
chunks.text: It stars Johnny Depp in the title role and also features Gwyneth Paltrow, Ewan McGregor, Olivia Munn, Paul Bettany and Jeff Goldblum.

chunks.title: Mortdecai (film)
chunks.text: Released by Lionsgate on January 23, 2015, "Mortdecai" was a box office bomb, grossing $47 million against its $60 million budget, and received overwhelmingly negative reviews.

chunks.title: Maurice Milliere
chunks.text: Maurice Milliere (1871–1946) was a French painter, printmaker and illustrator, born in Le Havre to upper working class parents; his father was a merchant's clerk.

chunks.title: Maurice Milliere
chunks.text: His early artistic interests are not known, but he completed his secondary education at the Ecole De Beaux Arts in Le Havre before travelling to Paris in 1889 to continue his studies at the l'Ecole des Arts Decoratifs and l'Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

chunks.title: René Margotton
chunks.text: He studied at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts of Paris and later with Fernand Léger friend of Maurice Utrillo and Bernard Buffet.

chunks.title: René Margotton
chunks.text: He has exhibited extensively in Paris at the Salon de l'Art Libre, Salon des Independants, Salon de Printemps, Salon de l'Ecole Francaise, Salon de la Nationale des Beaux-Arts, and Salon "Les Grands et les Jeunes d'Aujourd' hui."

chunks.title: René Margotton
chunks.text: He participated in a show of French Masters in Rome.

chunks.title: René Margotton
chunks.text: He also exhibited with the French Young Painters in Geneva, Brussels, Finland, Germany, Canada, London, and Denmark.

chunks.title: René Margotton
chunks.text: His first one-man show in America was held at Newman Galleries in 1965.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Phan Chánh
chunks.text: Nguyen Phan Chanh (July 21, 1892 - November 22, 1984) was born in a rural Vietnamese village, in Ha Tinh (now Nghe Tinh) province.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Phan Chánh
chunks.text: His early education was in Chinese (as was common in pre-colonial times), and he studied Chinese calligraphy so as to pass the qualifying exams for the title of Mandarin.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Phan Chánh
chunks.text: However, the exams were abolished before he was old enough to sit them.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Phan Chánh
chunks.text: With his first ambition thwarted, it was decided that he should continue studying painting at the l’Ecole des Beaux-arts d’Indochine ("the Indochinese College of Fine Arts") in Hanoi.

chunks.title: Peggy Adam
chunks.text: Peggy Adam (born 1974) is a French comic book artist and illustrator.

chunks.title: Peggy Adam
chunks.text: She studied at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts in Saint-Étienne, at the OCAD University in Toronto, and at the ESI (Ecole Supérieure de l'Image) in Angoulême.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: John Lonergan was an American artist, educator, and writer.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: He was born in Troy, NY.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: Sources variously list the year of his birth as 1895, 1896,1897.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: Lonergan died in New York City in 1969.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: His art often depicted the sea and the men who worked it, done in various mediums.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: These include gouache, drawing in charcoal and ink, lithography and screen printing.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: Lonergan studied art in Paris at Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: During his career he taught at Friends Seminary, Columbia Grammar School, and Greenwich House, all in New York City.

chunks.title: John Lonergan (artist)
chunks.text: In 1939 he published a handbook on gouache painting, "Materials and Techniques of Gouache Painting".

chunks.title: Beaux-Arts architecture
chunks.text: Beaux-Arts architecture ( ; ] ) expresses the academic neoclassical architectural style taught at the "École des Beaux-Arts" in Paris.

chunks.title: Beaux-Arts architecture
chunks.text: The "style" "Beaux Arts" is the cumulative product of two-and-a-half centuries of instruction under the authority, first, of the "Académie royale d'architecture" (1671–1793), then, following the French Revolution of the late 18th century, of the Architecture section of the "Académie des Beaux-Arts" (1795– ).

chunks.title: Beaux-Arts architecture
chunks.text: The organization under the "Ancien Régime" of the competition for the "Grand Prix de Rome" in architecture, offering a chance to study in Rome, imprinted its codes and aesthetic on the course of instruction, which culminated during the Second Empire (1852–1870) and the Third Republic that followed.

chunks.title: Beaux-Arts architecture
chunks.text: The style of instruction that produced Beaux-Arts architecture continued without major interruption until 1968.

chunks.title: Detlef Lienau
chunks.text: Detlef Lienau (February 17, 1818 Uetersen – August 29, 1887) was a German architect born in Holstein.

chunks.title: Detlef Lienau
chunks.text: He is credited with having introduced the French style to American building construction, notably the mansard roof and all its decorative flourishes.

chunks.title: Detlef Lienau
chunks.text: Trained at L’Ecole des Beaux-Arts in Paris, he designed virtually every type of Victorian structure—cottages, mansions, townhouses, apartment houses, hotels, tenements, banks, stores, churches, schools, libraries, offices, factories, railroad stations, and a museum.

chunks.title: Detlef Lienau
chunks.text: Lienau was recognized by clients and colleagues alike as one of the most creative and technically proficient architects of the period, and was one of the 29 founding members of the American Institute of Architects.

chunks.title: Dayton Memorial Hall
chunks.text: The Dayton Memorial Hall is a historic meeting venue on First Street in downtown Dayton, Ohio, United States.

chunks.title: Dayton Memorial Hall
chunks.text: Constructed shortly after the turn of the twentieth century, this Beaux-Arts structure is one of many memorial halls statewide from the same time period, and it has been named a historic site.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Claude Minière (born October 25, 1938, Paris) is an essayist and poet.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Initially, he took part in various avant-garde activities before turning towards a more solitary, more classical approach to writing, never forgetting, however, the conquests of Rimbaud, Ezra Pound and free-verse.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: For fifteen years he taught at l’Ecole des Beaux-Arts and is the author of a “panorama” of artistic creativity in France between 1965 and 1996: "L’art en France 1965-1995" (Nouvelles editions françaises, Paris, 1995).

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Together with Margaret Tunstill, he translated two works by Ezra Pound: "Henri Gaudier-Brzeska, A Memoir" ("Henri Gaudier-Brzeska", ed.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Tristram, 1992) and "Treatise on Harmony" ("Traité d’Harmonie", ed.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Julien Salvy, 1980).

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: In addition to the many collections of his poetry he has produced three remarkable essays : "Pound caractère chinois" (ed.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Gallimard); "Barnett Newman" (ed.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Tarabuste); and "Descartes" (ed.

chunks.title: Claude Minière
chunks.text: Le Cherche-Midi).

chunks.title: Nguyễn Sáng

chunks.title: Nguyễn Sáng
chunks.text: He was a graduate of the 1940-1945 class of the Ecole des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Sáng
chunks.text: His favorite medias were pumice lacquer and oil paint.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Sáng
chunks.text: Although not overtly political, Sáng was reluctant and unenthusiastic about the new communist society in his paintings.

chunks.title: Nguyễn Sáng
chunks.text: He was posthumously awarded the Ho Chi Minh Prize in 1996.

chunks.title: Sins of My Father (song)
chunks.text: "Sins of My Father" is a song recorded by American recording artist Usher for his seventh studio album "Looking 4 Myself" (2012).

chunks.title: National Recording Corporation

chunks.title: National Recording Corporation

chunks.title: National Recording Corporation
chunks.text: Griggers' group took over stock sales for the company, but by April 27, 1961, according to the US Bankruptcy archives, the company was in bankruptcy.

chunks.title: National Recording Corporation

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Company
chunks.text: The F. W. Woolworth Company (often referred to as Woolworth's, or Woolworth) was a retail company and one of the original pioneers of the five-and-dime store.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Company

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: The C.M. Sanborn Building is a historic building located in Maquoketa, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: Built in 1896, it is significant as an example of High Victorian Italianate architecture.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: The three-story, brick building features cast hoodmolds above the windows, twin oriel windows, and an elaborate cornice.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: C.M. Sanborn was a local grocer whose business operated out of a number of buildings in the central business district before he built this building.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: He acted as the general contractor for the construction of this building, and hired two local builders to construct it.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: William Hancock was a brick mason, and W.P. Thomas was a carpenter.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: Sanborn filed for bankruptcy around 1911, and was forced to sell the building.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: A variety of retail establishments have occupied the main floor, while the second floor was rented as office space.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: A Masonic lodge occupied the third floor shortly after the building was completed, and remained until 1968.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: The Masons owned the building by that time.

chunks.title: C.M. Sanborn Building
chunks.text: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1991.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: Maynard Town Hall and Jail is a historic building located in Maynard, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: Before this building was constructed the town had no building to enact its business.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: They used the mayor's house or place of business for his office and council meetings.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: After it was completed, this building served as a jail into the late 1930s and as the city hall until 1952, when a new community building was completed.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: For most of the time it served as a jail it was outfitted with bars and had bunks.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: It was a short-term lock-up for those who committed minor infractions.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: It was used for a public library beginning in the 1940s.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: After its use as a city hall, it was bought by a local merchant for use in his grocery store in 1957.

chunks.title: Maynard Town Hall and Jail
chunks.text: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1997.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: The Pioneer Implement Company, also known as the International Harvester Transfer House, is a historic building located in Council Bluffs, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: Eli Shugart, Ferdinand Weis and F.R. Davis formed Pioneer Implement Company in 1893, and they built the four-story Late Victorian section of the building the same year.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: This was during a period of growth in the city's "Implement District," which is located to the south of the central business district.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: What made this company standout from the others in the district is that it was locally owned and operated agricultural implement business, rather than one owned by a factory from the east.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: The company went out of business in 1915 and the building was taken over by International Harvester, which owned the building next door.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: They added the single story brick addition to the south in 1927.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: When IH closed their Council Bluffs operation in 1964 they were the only farm implement that was still in business in the Implement District.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: The building was occupied by various businesses after that, including United Parcel Service.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: Artspace, Inc. acquired the building and converted it into live/work spaces for artists.

chunks.title: Pioneer Implement Company
chunks.text: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2008.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: The Sioux City Linseed Oil Works is a historic building located in Sioux City, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: It is located in an area east of the central business district where warehouses and other industrial buildings are located.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: It housed the Sioux City Linseed Oil Works (initially known as Hubbard and Gere) from 1884, when it was built, until 1927 when its owner, the American Linseed Oil Company, ceased production here.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: The building was largely destroyed in a fire that began late in the night of May 20, 1891.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: Mankato, Minnesota architect William D. McLaughlin stepped in to complete the work begun by Sioux City architect E.W. Loft.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: Essentially, the building was rebuilt and was very similar in appearance to the original structure.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: Gone was the gable roof on the westernmost wing, which was replaced by a flat roof, and two floors were added to the rebuilt press room annex in the back.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: The building was acquired by Bekins Van and Storage Company in 1928.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: They began operations here two years later, and they remained the primary tenant in the building until 1972.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: There was a variety of other tenants who were housed here over the years.

chunks.title: Sioux City Linseed Oil Works
chunks.text: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2008.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: The Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building, also known as the Dwarfies/Breeders Supply Building, is a historic building located in Council Bluffs, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: This building was built by the Sandwich Manufacturing Company and the Marseilles Manufacturing Company in what is known as the Implement District, an industrial area south of the central business district that was home to farm implement manufacturers.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: The two-story section on the north side was completed in 1883, and the single-story addition on the south side was completed sometime between 1889 and 1891.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: Marseilles then occupied the addition while Sandwich remained in the original building.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: There was a shift from agricultural implements to food processing as the area's business interests began to diversify.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: Dwarfies Corporation, a cereal manufacturer, took over the building in 1929.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: It is the only remaining building left in the city to illustrate this shift.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: The building was damaged in a fire in 1947.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: Dwarfies rebuilt this building and then built a new factory in 1949 along U.S. Route 6.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: Breeders Supply Company, an international mail order business for breeding supplies, moved into this building the following year.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: They used it as a warehouse for ten years.

chunks.title: Sandwich–Marseilles Manufacturing Building
chunks.text: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2014.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: The First National Bank of Mason City, also known as Norwest Bank Building and City Center of Mason City, is a historic building located in Mason City, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: It was designed by the Des Moines architectural firm of Liebbe, Nourse & Rasmussen, and it was the only Mason City commission for this firm.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: Completed in 1911, it was constructed by C.E. Atkinson of Webster City, Iowa who had built several other H.F. Liebbe designs.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: The 6½-story building follows the Early Commercial style.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: It features modestly decorated main floor and attic level with five floors of rather plain brick construction in between.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: The bank occupied most of the first floor and some of the office space above, while the other office space was taken up by professional offices.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: By the 1960s the bank occupied the whole building.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: John Dillinger, Baby Face Nelson, John Hamilton and Tommy Carroll robbed the bank on March 13,1934 and stole about $50,000.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: Dillinger was wounded in an exchange of gunfire during the heist.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: The building to the north of the bank was torn down in 1982 and a two-story annex to the bank replaced it.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: The bank building was individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1997, and as a contributing property in the Mason City Downtown Historic District in 2005.

chunks.title: First National Bank of Mason City
chunks.text: City Center of Mason City Inc. bought the building in 1995, and remodeled it into apartments and offices.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: The Hamilton Brothers Building, also known as Warfield-Pratt & Howell Co.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: Wholesale Grocers, and the Hach Brothers Company, is a historic building located in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: This is the only extant building associated with local businessman and politician John Taylor Hamilton.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: He was a representative of Cyrus McCormick at the time his company was opening new markets for his mechanical reaper and other implements.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: Hamilton expanded his business to other implement manufactures and included product lines for urban dwellers as well.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: His business grew beyond the local area to include the entire state.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: Built as a warehouse in 1899, it is the only building of this type left near the central business district.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: It is also the largest building of this type in the city.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building
chunks.text: The four-story, brick, Romanesque Revival sturcture features large round arch openings on the main floor and smaller windows on the upper floors.

chunks.title: Hamilton Brothers Building

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: The Evans Block, also known as Northwestern National Bank Building, is a historic building located in Sioux City, Iowa, United States.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: The city experienced a building boom that began in the late 1880s and continued into the early 1890s.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: Fred T. Evans, an entrepreneur who had business interests in Iowa, Nebraska and South Dakota, had this building constructed to house Northwestern National Bank of which he was the president.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: The bank occupied the main level and other offices were housed on the upper floors.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: Local architect Charles Brown designed the four-story Romanesque Revival style building.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: The Black Hills sandstone for the public facades was from Evans' quarry.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: The Panic of 1893 brought Sioux City's building boom to an end, and the Evans block was sold in January 1895.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: Subsequently, the building has housed a hotel, a factory, a saloon, and a variety of stores.

chunks.title: Evans Block (Sioux City, Iowa)
chunks.text: It was individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1985, and as a contributing property in the Fourth Street Historic District in 1995.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: The Woolworth Building is an historic building in Watertown, New York.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: It is a contributing building in the Public Square Historic District.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: Plans for the Woolworth Building were begun in 1916 by Frank W. Woolworth, the founder of the Woolworth's chain of department stores.

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: Cesare Pugni (Russian: Цезарь Пуни ) (] ; 31 May 1802–26 January [O.S. 14 January] 1870 ) born in Genoa, was an Italian composer of ballet music, a pianist and a violinist.

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: In his early career he composed operas, symphonies, and various other forms of orchestral music.

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: Pugni is most noted for the ballets he composed for Her Majesty's Theatre in London (1843–1850), and for the Imperial Theatres in St. Petersburg, Russia (1850–1870).

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: The majority of his ballet music was composed for the works of the ballet master Jules Perrot, who mounted nearly every one of his ballets to scores by Pugni.

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: In 1850 Perrot departed London for Russia, having accepted the position of "Premier maître de ballet" of the St. Petersburg Imperial Theatres at the behest of Carlotta Grisi, who was engaged as "Prima ballerina".

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: Cesare Pugni followed Perrot and Grisi to Russia, and remained in the imperial capital even after Grisi's departure in 1853 and Perrot's departure in 1858.

chunks.title: Cesare Pugni
chunks.text: Pugni went on the compose for Perrot's successors Arthur Saint-Léon and Marius Petipa, serving as the Imperial Theatre's official composer of ballet music until his death in 1870.

chunks.title: The Seasons (ballet)
chunks.text: The Seasons (Russian: Времена года , "Vremena goda"; also French: "Les saisons" ) is an allegorical ballet in one act, four scenes, by the choreographer Marius Petipa, with music by Alexander Glazunov, his Op.

chunks.title: The Seasons (ballet)
chunks.text: The work was composed in 1899 and first performed by the Imperial Ballet in 1900 in St. Petersburg, Russia.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: Hans Brenaa (b Copenhagen, 9 October 1910, d Copenhagen, 14 April 1988) was a Danish dancer, teacher, and ballet director.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: He studied at the Royal Danish Ballet School from 1918 and joined the company in 1928; promoted to principal in 1945.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: He created roles in George Balanchine Legend of Joseph (1931) and in numerous ballets by Lander, including Études (1948).

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: He produced Aurora's Wedding for the Royal Danish Ballet in 1950.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: After retiring from the stage in 1955 he became a producer, staging the Bournonville repertoire in Denmark and elsewhere.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: He also taught at the Royal Danish Ballet School in Copenhagen from 1942 and was a tireless teacher of the Bournonville style throughout Europe and America.

chunks.title: Hans Brenaa
chunks.text: Among the Bournonville productions he staged for the Royal Danish Ballet are The Kermesse in Bruges (1957 and 1978), La Sylphide (1967), Konservatoriet (1968), The King's Volunteers on Amager (1970), Far from Denmark (1973), and La Ventana (1979).

chunks.title: Alexander Glazunov
chunks.text: Alexander Konstantinovich Glazunov (Russian: Алекса́ндр Константи́нович Глазуно́в , 10 August 1865 – 21 March 1936) was a Russian composer, music teacher, and conductor of the late Russian Romantic period.

chunks.title: Alexander Glazunov
chunks.text: He served as director of the Saint Petersburg Conservatory between 1905 and 1928 and was instrumental in the reorganization of the institute into the Petrograd Conservatory, then the Leningrad Conservatory, following the Bolshevik Revolution.

chunks.title: Alexander Glazunov
chunks.text: He continued heading the Conservatory until 1930, though he had left the Soviet Union in 1928 and did not return.

chunks.title: Alexander Glazunov
chunks.text: The best-known student under his tenure during the early Soviet years was Dmitri Shostakovich.

chunks.title: Le baiser de la fée
chunks.text: Le baiser de la fée ("The Fairy's Kiss") is a ballet in one act and four scenes composed by Igor Stravinsky in 1928 and revised in 1950 for George Balanchine and the New York City Ballet.

chunks.title: Le baiser de la fée
chunks.text: Based on Hans Christian Andersen's short story "Isjomfruen" (English: The Ice-Maiden), the work is an homage to Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, for the 35th anniversary of the composer's death.

chunks.title: Le baiser de la fée
chunks.text: Stravinsky elaborated several melodies from early piano pieces and songs by Tchaikovsky in his score.

chunks.title: Le baiser de la fée
chunks.text: A commission by Ida Rubinstein from 1927, the ballet was choreographed by Bronislava Nijinska and premiered in Paris on 27 November 1928.

chunks.title: John Lanchbery
chunks.text: John Arthur Lanchbery OBE (15 May 1923 - 27 February 2003) was an English, later Australian, composer and conductor, famous for his ballet arrangements.

chunks.title: John Lanchbery
chunks.text: He served as the Principal Conductor of the Royal Ballet from 1959 to 1972, Principal Conductor of the Australian Ballet from 1972 to 1977, and Director of the American Ballet Theatre from 1978 to 1980.

chunks.title: John Lanchbery
chunks.text: Although he resigned from the position of Director of the Royal Ballet in 1972, he continued to conduct regularly for the Company until 2001.

chunks.title: Apollo (ballet)
chunks.text: Apollo (originally Apollon musagète and variously known as "Apollo musagetes", "Apolo Musageta", and "Apollo, Leader of the Muses") is a ballet in two tableaux composed between 1927 and 1928 by Igor Stravinsky.

chunks.title: Apollo (ballet)
chunks.text: It was choreographed in 1928 by twenty-four-year-old George Balanchine, with the composer contributing the libretto.

chunks.title: Apollo (ballet)
chunks.text: The scenery and costumes were designed by André Bauchant, with new costumes by Coco Chanel in 1929.

chunks.title: Apollo (ballet)
chunks.text: The scenery was executed by Alexander Shervashidze, with costumes under the direction of Mme. A. Youkine.

chunks.title: Apollo (ballet)
chunks.text: The American patron of the arts Elizabeth Sprague Coolidge had commissioned the ballet in 1927 for a festival of contemporary music to be held the following year at the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C.

chunks.title: New York City Ballet
chunks.text: New York City Ballet (NYCB) is a ballet company founded in 1948 by choreographer George Balanchine and Lincoln Kirstein.

chunks.title: New York City Ballet
chunks.text: Léon Barzin was the company's first music director.

chunks.title: New York City Ballet
chunks.text: Balanchine and Jerome Robbins are considered the founding choreographers of the company.

chunks.title: New York City Ballet
chunks.text: City Ballet grew out of earlier troupes: the Producing Company of the School of American Ballet, 1934; the American Ballet, 1935, and Ballet Caravan, 1936, which merged into American Ballet Caravan, 1941; and directly from the Ballet Society, 1946.

chunks.title: In G Major

chunks.title: In G Major

chunks.title: In G Major

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: Ballet is a formalized form of dance with its origins in the Italian Renaissance courts of the 15th and 16th centuries.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: Ballet spread from Italy to France with the help of Catherine de' Medici, where ballet developed even further under her aristocratic influence.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: An early example of Catherine's development of ballet is through 'Le Paradis d' Amour', a piece of work presented at her daughter's wedding, Marguerite de Valois to Henry of Navarre.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: Aristocratic money was responsible for the initial stages of development in 'court ballet', as it was royal money that dictated the ideas, literature and music used in ballets that were created to primarily entertain the aristocrats of the time.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: The first formal 'court ballet' ever recognized was staged in 1573, 'Ballet des Polonais'.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: In true form of royal entertainment, 'Ballet des Polonais' was commissioned by Catherine de' Medici to honor the Polish ambassadors who were visiting Paris upon the accession of Henry of Anjou to the throne of Poland.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: In 1581, Catherine de' Medici commissioned another court ballet, "Ballet Comique de la Reine", however it was her compatriot, Balthasar de Beaujoyeulx, who organized the ballet.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: Catherine de' Medici and Balthasar de Beaujoyeulx were responsible for presenting the first court ballet ever to apply the principles of Baif's Academie, by integrating poetry, dance, music and set design to convey a unified dramatic storyline.

chunks.title: History of ballet
chunks.text: Moreover, the early organization and development of 'court ballet' was funded by, influenced by and produced by the aristocrats of the time, fulfilling both their personal entertainment and political propaganda needs.

chunks.title: 1962 Utah state route renumbering

chunks.title: François Hollande presidential campaign, 2012
chunks.text: President of the General Council of Corrèze and former First Secretary of the French Socialist Party François Hollande launched his campaign in March 2011 to become the Socialist and Radical Left Party candidate for the 2012 French presidential election and announced that he would be contesting the presidential primary.

chunks.title: François Hollande presidential campaign, 2012
chunks.text: Hollande made the announcement that he was running for President following his re-election as a department executive.

chunks.title: François Hollande presidential campaign, 2012
chunks.text: On 16 October 2011, he won the Socialist and Radical Left Party nomination with more than 56% of the votes over First Secretary Martine Aubry, following a long campaign.

chunks.title: François Hollande presidential campaign, 2012

chunks.text: ; Greek: ΣΥΡΙΖΑ , ] ), is a left-wing political party in Greece, founded in 2004 as a coalition of left-wing and radical left parties.

chunks.title: Cabinet of Deuntzer
chunks.text: After the 1901 Danish Folketing election, the Council President Johan Henrik Deuntzer of the Venstre Reform Party became the leader of Denmark's first liberal government.

chunks.title: Cabinet of Deuntzer
chunks.text: The resulting cabinet, which replaced the Cabinet of Sehested consisting of member of the conservative party Højre, was formed on 24 July 1901 and was called the Cabinet of Deuntzer.

chunks.title: Cabinet of Deuntzer
chunks.text: The formation of the new cabinet is referred to in Danish as "systemskiftet", the shift of government.

chunks.title: Johan Henrik Deuntzer
chunks.text: Johan Henrik Deuntzer (20 May 1845 – 16 November 1918) was a Danish politician, member of the Liberal "Venstre" party until 1905 where he joined the Danish Social Liberal Party.

chunks.title: Johan Henrik Deuntzer

chunks.title: Political radicalism
chunks.text: The term political radicalism (or simply, in political science, radicalism) denotes political principles focused on altering social structures through revolutionary or other means and changing value systems in fundamental ways.

chunks.title: Political radicalism
chunks.text: Derived from the Latin "radix" (root), the denotation of radical has changed since its eighteenth-century coinage to comprehend the entire political spectrum—yet it retains the "change at the root" connotation fundamental to revolutionary societal change.

chunks.title: Political radicalism
chunks.text: Historically, radicalism has referred exclusively to the radical left (under the single category of far-left politics) and rarely incorporating far-right politics - though these may have revolutionary elements; the prominent exception is in the United States where some consider radicalism to include both political extremes of the radical left and the radical right.

chunks.title: Political radicalism
chunks.text: In traditional labels of the spectrum of political thought, the opposite of radical on the "right" of the political spectrum is termed "reactionary".

chunks.title: Abna' al-dawla
chunks.text: The abnāʾ al-dawla (meaning "sons of the regime/dynasty"), often simply " the "Abnāʾ"", is a term for the Khurasani Arabs who had participated in the Abbasid Revolution of 749–750 and their descendants, who settled in Baghdad and Iraq.

chunks.title: Abna' al-dawla
chunks.text: They became the ruling elite of the Abbasid Caliphate and formed the mainstay of the caliphal army.

chunks.title: Abna' al-dawla
chunks.text: However, the term appears rarely in the sources until the time of the Fourth Fitna civil war in the 810s, when it is applied to the Khurasanis of Baghdad, who overwhelmingly supported Caliph al-Amin against his brother al-Ma'mun.

chunks.title: Abna' al-dawla
chunks.text: The terms "ahl Khurāsān" ("people of Khurasan") and "abnāʾ ahl Khurāsān" ("sons of the people of Khurasan") are more frequently used for the Khurasanis who formed the mainstay of the Abbasid regime in general.

chunks.title: Abna' al-dawla
chunks.text: Following al-Ma'mun's victory in the civil war, the "abnāʾ al-dawla" were largely replaced by the latter's Persian followers, and under his successor al-Mu'tasim, the rise of the Turkish slave-soldiers to power began.

chunks.title: The Last Voyage of Somebody the Sailor
chunks.text: The Last Voyage of Somebody the Sailor is a novel by American writer John Barth, published in 1991.

chunks.title: The Last Voyage of Somebody the Sailor
chunks.text: It is a postmodern metafictional story of a man who jumps overboard a modern replica of a medieval Arab ship and is rescued by sailors from the world of Sinbad the Sailor.

chunks.title: The Last Voyage of Somebody the Sailor
chunks.text: Eventually he makes his way to "Baghdad, the City of Peace", and finds himself in the stories of Sindbad and Scheherazade.

chunks.title: The Last Voyage of Somebody the Sailor
chunks.text: The novel makes use of a challenging double-stranded narrative and a rich prose style.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: Abū al-Husayn Bajkam al-Mākānī (Arabic: أبو الحسين بجكم المكاني‎ ‎ ), referred to as Bajkam, Badjkam or Bachkam (from "Bäčkäm", a Persian and Turkish word meaning a horse- or yak-tail), was a Turkish military commander and official of the Abbasid Caliphate.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: A former "ghulam" of the Ziyarid dynasty, Bajkam entered Abbasid service following the assassination of the Ziyarid ruler Mardavij in 935.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: During his five-year tenure at the Caliphate's court at Baghdad, he was granted the title of "amir al-umara", consolidating his dominance over the Caliphs ar-Radi and al-Muttaqi and giving him absolute power over their domains.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: Bajkam was challenged throughout his rule by various opponents, including his predecessor as "amir al-umara", Muhammad ibn Ra'iq, the Basra-based Baridis, and the Buyid dynasty of Iran, but he succeeded in retaining control until his death.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: He was murdered by a party of Kurds during a hunting excursion in 941, shortly after the accession of al-Muttaqi as Caliph.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: Bajkam was known both for his firm rule and for his patronage of Baghdad intellectuals, who respected and in some cases befriended him.

chunks.title: Bajkam
chunks.text: His death led to a void in central power, resulting in a brief period of instability and fighting in Baghdad.

chunks.title: Battle of Hama
chunks.text: The Battle of Hama was fought some 24 km from the city of Hama in Syria on 29–30 November 903 between the forces of the Abbasid Caliphate and the Qarmatians.

chunks.title: Battle of Hama
chunks.text: The Abbasids were victorious, resulting in the capture and execution of the Qarmatian leadership.

chunks.title: Battle of Hama
chunks.text: This weakened the Qarmatian presence in northern Syria, which was finally eradicated after the suppression of another revolt in 906.

chunks.title: Battle of Hama
chunks.text: More importantly, it paved the way for the Abbasid attack on the autonomous Tulunid dynasty and the reincorporation of the Tulunid domains in southern Syria and Egypt into the Abbasid Caliphate.

chunks.title: Nahrawan Canal
chunks.text: The Nahrawan Canal (Arabic: قناة النهروان‎ ‎ ) was a major irrigation system of the Sassanid and early Islamic periods in central Iraq, along the eastern banks of the Tigris and the lower course of the Diyala River.

chunks.title: Nahrawan Canal
chunks.text: Created in the 6th century, it reached its peak under the Abbasid Caliphate, when it served the main water supply for the Abbasid capital of Baghdad, while the regions irrigated by it served as the city's main breadbasket.

chunks.title: Nahrawan Canal
chunks.text: Its destruction and progressive abandonment from the mid-10th century onwards mirror the Abbasid Caliphate's decline.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: Sa'id ibn Makhlad (died 889) was a senior official of the Abbasid Caliphate.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: Born a Nestorian Christian, he converted to Islam and served as a secretary in the Abbasid capital, Baghdad.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: He rose to prominence during the regency of al-Muwaffaq over his brother, the Caliph al-Mu'tamid (r. 870–892): between 878 and 885, he served as "de facto" vizier of the Caliphate, although he did not bear the title.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: His valuable assistance to al-Muwaffaq was recognized in 882 by the award of the unique honorific title Dhu'l-Wizaratayn ("possessor of the two vizierates"), with which he appears even on coins.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: However, the activities of his brother, Abdun, who had remained a Christian and tried to obtain concessions for the Christian subjects of the Caliphate, brought about his sudden fall from power in 885.

chunks.title: Sa'id ibn Makhlad
chunks.text: He died in 889.

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: The Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor in 806 was the largest operation ever launched by the Abbasid Caliphate against the Byzantine Empire.

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: The expedition was commanded in person by the Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid (reigned 786–809), who wished to retaliate for the Byzantine successes in the Caliphate's frontier region in the previous year and impress Abbasid might upon the Byzantine emperor, Nikephoros I (r. 802–811).

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: The huge Abbasid army, according to Arab sources numbering more than 135,000 men, raided across Cappadocia unopposed, capturing several towns and fortresses, most notably Herakleia, and forcing Nikephoros to seek peace in exchange for tribute.

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: Following Harun's departure, however, Nikephoros violated the terms of the treaty and reoccupied the frontier forts he had been forced to abandon.

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: Harun's preoccupation with a rebellion in Khurasan, and his death three years later, prohibited a reprisal on a similar scale.

chunks.title: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor (806)
chunks.text: Moreover, the Abbasid civil war that began after 809 and the Byzantine preoccupation with the Bulgars contributed to a cessation of large-scale Arab–Byzantine conflict for two decades.

chunks.title: Tuzun (amir al-umara)
chunks.text: Abu'l-Wafa Tuzun was a Turkish soldier who served first the Iranian ruler Mardavij ibn Ziyar and subsequently the Abbasid Caliphate.

chunks.title: Tuzun (amir al-umara)
chunks.text: Rising to a position of leadership in the Abbasid army, he evicted the Hamdanid Nasir al-Dawla from Baghdad and assumed the position of "amir al-umara" on 31 May 943, becoming the Caliphate's "de facto" ruler.

chunks.title: Tuzun (amir al-umara)
chunks.text: He held this position until his death in August 945, a few months before Baghdad, and the Abbasid Caliphate with it, came under the control of the Buyids.

chunks.title: Sinbad the Sailor
chunks.text: Sinbad the Sailor (Arabic: ٱلسِّنْدِبَادُ ٱلْبَحرِيّ‎ ‎ "as-Sindibādu al-Baḥriyy") also spelled Sindbad, is a fictional sailor and the hero of a story-cycle of Middle Eastern origin; he is described as living in Baghdad, during the Abbasid Caliphate.

chunks.title: Sinbad the Sailor
chunks.text: During his voyages throughout the seas east of Africa and south of Asia, he has fantastic adventures going to magical places, meeting monsters, and encountering supernatural phenomena.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: The term "Anarchy at Samarra" refers to the period 861–870 in the history of the Abbasid Caliphate, which was marked by extreme internal instability and the violent succession of four caliphs, who became puppets in the hands of powerful rival military groups.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: The term derives from the then capital and seat of the caliphal court, Samarra.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: The "anarchy" began in 861, with the murder of Caliph al-Mutawakkil by his Turkish guards.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: His successor, al-Muntasir, ruled for six months before his death, possibly poisoned by the Turkish military chiefs.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: He was succeeded by al-Musta'in.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: Divisions within the Turkish military leadership enabled Musta'in to flee to Baghdad in 865 with the support of some Turkish chiefs (Bugha the Younger and Wasif) and the Tahirids, but the rest of the Turkish army chose a new caliph in the person of al-Mu'tazz and besieged Baghdad, forcing the city's capitulation in 866.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: Musta'in was exiled and executed.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: Mu'tazz was able and energetic, and tried to control the military chiefs and exclude the military from civil administration.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: His policies were resisted, and in July 869 he too was deposed and killed.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: His successor, al-Muhtadi, also tried to reaffirm the Caliph's authority, but he too was killed in June 870.

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: With Muhtadi's death and the ascension of al-Mu'tamid, the Turkish faction around Musa ibn Bugha, closely associated with Mu'tamid's brother and regent al-Muwaffaq, became dominant in the caliphal court, ending the "anarchy".

chunks.title: Anarchy at Samarra
chunks.text: Although the Abbasid Caliphate was able to stage a modest recovery in the following decades, the troubles of the "Anarchy at Samarra" inflicted great and lasting damage on the structures and prestige of the Abbasid central government, encouraging and facilitating secessionist and rebellious tendencies in the Caliphate's provinces.

chunks.text: He served as chairman and chief executive officer of Toro Company from 1977 to 1981, after serving in various management positions at Toro Company since 1970.

chunks.title: David T. McLaughlin
chunks.text: McLaughlin served as a director of CBS Corporation from 1979, becoming chairman of the board in January 1999 until the CBS merger.

chunks.title: David T. McLaughlin
chunks.text: He also served as a director of Infininity Broadcasting Corporation until the Infinity merger.

chunks.title: Jonathan G. Ornstein
chunks.text: Jonathan Ornstein is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Mesa Air Group, Inc., and was appointed effective May 1, 1998.

chunks.title: Jonathan G. Ornstein
chunks.text: From April 1996 to his joining the company as Chief Executive Officer, Ornstein served as President and Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Virgin Express, a European airline.

chunks.title: Jonathan G. Ornstein
chunks.text: From 1995 to April 1996, Ornstein served as Chief Executive Officer of Virgin Express Holdings, Inc.

chunks.title: Jonathan G. Ornstein
chunks.text: Ornstein joined Continental Express as President and Chief Executive Officer in July 1994 and, in November 1994, was named Senior Vice President, Airport Services at Continental Airlines.

chunks.title: Jonathan G. Ornstein
chunks.text: Ornstein was previously employed by the company from 1988 to 1994, as Executive Vice President and as President of the company’s WestAir Holding, Inc., subsidiary.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: Glen F. Post III (born October 4, 1952) is the chief executive officer and president of CenturyLink, an S&P 500 integrated communications service provider based out of Monroe, Louisiana.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: He earned a bachelor's degree in accounting in 1974 at Louisiana Tech University and an MBA in 1976 at Louisiana Tech.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: Post joined CenturyTel in 1976.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: He was named vice president in 1982 and was promoted to senior vice president and treasurer in 1984.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: He was appointed to the CenturyTel board of directors in 1985, and the following year he was promoted to senior vice president and chief financial officer.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: In 1988 Post was named executive vice president and chief operating officer.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: He became the president and chief operating officer of CenturyTel in 1990.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: In 1992 Post was named vice chairman of the board, president, and chief executive officer.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: In 2002 he was appointed chairman of the board and chief executive officer.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: Since 2009 Post has served as chief executive officer and president of CenturyLink.

chunks.title: Glen Post
chunks.text: His honors include: Louisiana Tech College of Administration and Business Distinguished Alumni in 1991, Louisiana Tech University Tower Medallion Award in 1997 and DeGree Enterprises Lifetime Achievement Award in Business 2003.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: Bradley Wayne Hughes (born September 28, 1933) is the founder and chairman of Public Storage, the largest self-storage company in America doing business as a REIT or real estate investment trust.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: As of 2014, Hughes is worth $2.2 billion.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: Known all his life by his middle name, B. Wayne Hughes was the company's President and Co-Chief Executive Officer from 1980 until November 1991 when he became Chairman of the Board and sole Chief Executive Officer.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: He retired as Chief Executive Officer in November 2002 and remains Chairman of the Board.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: He was Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer from 1990 until March 1998 of Public Storage Properties XI, Inc., which was renamed PS Business Parks, Inc. ("PSB"), an affiliated REIT.

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: From 1989-90 until the respective dates of merger, he was Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of 18 affiliated REITs that were merged into the Company between September 1994 and May 1998 (collectively, the "Merged Public Storage REITs").

chunks.title: B. Wayne Hughes
chunks.text: has been active in the real estate investment field for over 30 years.

chunks.title: Sierra Nevada Corporation
chunks.text: Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) is an American privately held electronic systems provider and systems integrator specializing in microsatellites, telemedicine, and commercial orbital transportation services.

chunks.title: Sierra Nevada Corporation
chunks.text: Sierra Nevada Corporation operates under the leadership of Chief Executive Officer, Fatih Ozmen and President, Eren Ozmen.

chunks.title: Sierra Nevada Corporation
chunks.text: The company contracts with the United States Armed Forces, NASA and private spaceflight companies.

chunks.title: Sierra Nevada Corporation
chunks.text: It is headquartered in Sparks, Nevada.

chunks.title: Lulu Belle Madison White
chunks.text: Lulu (or Lula) Belle Madison White (1900-1957) was a teacher and civil rights activist in Texas during the 1940s and 1950s.

chunks.title: Lulu Belle Madison White
chunks.text: In 1939, White was named as the president of the Houston chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) before becoming executive secretary of the branch in 1943.

chunks.title: Lulu Belle Madison White
chunks.text: Under her leadership, the Houston chapter of the NAACP more than doubled in size from 1943 to 1948.

chunks.title: Daisy Elizabeth Adams Lampkin
chunks.text: Daisy Elizabeth Adams Lampkin (August 9, 1883 – March 10, 1965) was an American [[suffragist[[Civil rights movement|civil rights]] activist, organization executive, and community practitioner whose career spanned over half a century.

chunks.title: Daisy Elizabeth Adams Lampkin
chunks.text: Lampkin’s effective skills as an orator, fundraiser, organizer, and political activist guided the work being conducted by the [[National Association of Colored Women]] (NACW); [[National Association for the Advancement of Colored People]] (NAACP); [[National Council of Negro Women]] and other leading civil rights organizations of the [[Progressive Era]].

chunks.title: James Weldon Johnson
chunks.text: James Weldon Johnson (June 17, 1871June 26, 1938) was an American author, educator, lawyer, diplomat, songwriter, and civil rights activist.

chunks.title: James Weldon Johnson
chunks.text: Johnson is best remembered for his leadership of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), where he started working in 1917.

chunks.title: James Weldon Johnson
chunks.text: In 1920 he was the first African American to be chosen as executive secretary of the organization, effectively the operating officer.

chunks.title: James Weldon Johnson
chunks.text: He served in that position from 1920 to 1930.

chunks.title: James Weldon Johnson
chunks.text: Johnson established his reputation as a writer, and was known during the Harlem Renaissance for his poems, novels, and anthologies collecting both poems and spirituals of black culture.

chunks.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
chunks.text: William Edward Burghardt "W. E. B." Du Bois ( ; February 23, 1868 – August 27, 1963) was an American sociologist, historian, civil rights activist, Pan-Africanist, author, writer and editor.

chunks.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
chunks.text: Born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, Du Bois grew up in a relatively tolerant and integrated community.

chunks.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
chunks.text: After completing graduate work at the University of Berlin and Harvard, where he was the first African American to earn a doctorate, he became a professor of history, sociology and economics at Atlanta University.

chunks.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
chunks.text: Du Bois was one of the co-founders of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: Ernest Samuel McBride, Sr (November 20, 1909 – May 5, 2007) was an African American civil rights activist and community leader based in Long Beach, California.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: He fought to improve the working prospects and conditions of African Americans in the shipyards, grocery stores, housing, police and fire departments in Long Beach.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: He was a co-founder of the Long Beach chapter of National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP).

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: Like Martin Luther King, Jr., McBride employed Mahatma Gandhi's model of peaceful protest to achieve civil rights gains.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: He became a target of the FBI's CONINTELPRO, which targeted many of the country's civil rights organizations and leaders, including Martin Luther King, Jr. - most famously resulting in the FBI - King Suicide Letter.

chunks.title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
chunks.text: McBride's legacy is memorialized in numerous awards, historic land marking of his home, and the naming of a high school and park.

chunks.title: Hubert Thomas Delany
chunks.text: Hubert Thomas Delany ( ; May 11, 1901 - December 28, 1990) was an American civil rights pioneer, a lawyer, politician, Assistant U.S. Attorney, the first African American Tax Commissioner of New York and one of the first appointed African American judges in New York City.

chunks.title: Hubert Thomas Delany
chunks.text: Judge Delany was on the board of Directors for the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), the Harlem YMCA and became an active leader in the Harlem Renaissance.

chunks.title: Hubert Thomas Delany
chunks.text: He also served as a Vice President of the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund.

chunks.title: Charles Evers
chunks.text: James Charles Evers (born September 11, 1922) is an American civil rights activist and former politician.

chunks.title: Charles Evers
chunks.text: A Republican, Evers was known for his role in the Civil Rights Movement along with his younger brother Medgar Evers.

chunks.title: Charles Evers
chunks.text: He was made the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) State Voter Registration Chairman in 1954.

chunks.title: Charles Evers
chunks.text: After his brother's assassination in 1963, Evers took over his position as field director of the NAACP in Mississippi.

chunks.title: Charles Evers
chunks.text: As field director, Evers organized and led many demonstrations for the rights of African Americans.

chunks.title: Terry Francois
chunks.text: Terry A. Francois ( 1922 – June 9, 1989) was an African American attorney, civil rights activist, and politician.

chunks.title: Terry Francois
chunks.text: He served as San Francisco chapter president of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People and became the first African American to serve on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.

chunks.title: Grace Nail Johnson
chunks.text: Grace Nail Johnson (February 27, 1885 – November 1, 1976) was a civil rights activist and patron of the arts, and wife of writer James Weldon Johnson.

chunks.title: Clement G. Morgan
chunks.text: Clement Garnett Morgan (1859-1929) was an American attorney, civil rights activist, and city official of Cambridge, Massachusetts.

chunks.title: Clement G. Morgan
chunks.text: Born into slavery in Virginia and freed by the Emancipation Proclamation, he trained as a barber before moving to Massachusetts to pursue his education.

chunks.title: Clement G. Morgan
chunks.text: He was the first African American to earn degrees from both Harvard University and its law school; the first African American to deliver Harvard's senior class oration; and the first black alderman in New England.

chunks.title: Clement G. Morgan
chunks.text: As an attorney he handled many civil rights cases, in one instance closing down a segregated school.

chunks.title: Clement G. Morgan
chunks.text: He was a founding member of the Niagara Movement and of the Boston branch of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People.

chunks.title: Live at Austin City Limits Festival
chunks.text: Live at Austin City Limits Festival by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison is a limited edition live album recorded from the Austin City Limits Festival concert at which he was the first night headliner on September 15, 2006.

chunks.title: Live at Austin City Limits Festival
chunks.text: It has only been made available at live Van Morrison concerts and at the Van Morrison Official website.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3 is a compilation album by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison, that was released on 11 June 2007 in the UK with a digital version released in the U.S. on iTunes Store, on 12 June 2007.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: Manhattan/EMI Music Catalog Marketing released the CD version of the album on 19 June 2007 in the United States.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: This new two-disc collection of 31 tracks has been compiled by Morrison himself.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: It offers an overview of his large volume of material since the release of "The Best of Van Morrison Volume Two" in 1993.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: The album's thirty-one tracks include previously unreleased collaborations with Tom Jones ("Cry For Home") and Bobby Bland ("Tupelo Honey") as well as duets with John Lee Hooker, B.B. King and Ray Charles.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: The 2003 duet with Ray Charles is "Crazy Love" a song originally recorded on Morrison's 1970 album "Moondance".

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: "Blue and Green" was previously donated to be used on the charity album "", which raised money for relief efforts intended for Gulf Coast victims devastated by hurricane Katrina.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: The duet with Tom Jones, "Cry For Home" was taken from the same recording sessions that produced the "Sometimes We Cry" duet between the two artists, which featured on Jones' successful album "Reload".

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison Volume 3
chunks.text: "Cry for Home" was released as a single on 4 June 2007 in the UK, and was followed by "Blue and Green" on 27 August.

chunks.title: The Story of Them Featuring Van Morrison
chunks.text: The Story of Them Featuring Van Morrison is a compilation album that includes almost every song recorded by the Northern Irish band Them during the two-year history of the band when it featured Van Morrison as the vocalist for the group.

chunks.title: The Skiffle Sessions – Live in Belfast 1998
chunks.text: The Skiffle Sessions – Live In Belfast 1998 is a live album by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison, with Lonnie Donegan and Chris Barber, released in 2000 (see 2000 in music).

chunks.title: The Skiffle Sessions – Live in Belfast 1998
chunks.text: Lonnie Donegan had played with the Chris Barber jazz band when he had his first hit with "Rock Island Line"/"John Henry" in 1955.

chunks.title: The Skiffle Sessions – Live in Belfast 1998
chunks.text: He had been a childhood influence on Van Morrison, who had first performed in his own skiffle band with schoolmates when he was twelve years old in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

chunks.title: The Skiffle Sessions – Live in Belfast 1998
chunks.text: This would be Donegan's first studio album in twenty years; reviving his career until his death in 2002.

chunks.title: Live at the Grand Opera House Belfast
chunks.text: Live at the Grand Opera House Belfast is a live album by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison, released in 1984 (see 1984 in music).

chunks.title: Live at the Grand Opera House Belfast
chunks.text: It was recorded from four live shows in March 1983 at the Grand Opera House, Belfast, Northern Ireland (Morrison's birthplace).

chunks.title: Live at the Grand Opera House Belfast
chunks.text: The album was composed of songs from Morrison's last four recordings.

chunks.title: Live at the Grand Opera House Belfast
chunks.text: It is the second live album Morrison released, following 10 years after "It's Too Late to Stop Now".

chunks.title: Them (band)
chunks.text: Them were a Northern Irish band formed in Belfast in April 1964, most prominently known for the garage rock standard "Gloria" and launching singer Van Morrison's musical career.

chunks.title: Them (band)
chunks.text: The original five member band consisted of Morrison, Alan Henderson, Ronnie Milling, Billy Harrison and Eric Wrixon.

chunks.title: Them (band)
chunks.text: The group was marketed in the United States as part of the British Invasion.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison
chunks.text: The Best of Van Morrison is a compilation album by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison
chunks.text: It compiles songs spanning 25 years of his recording career.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison
chunks.text: Released in 1990 by Polydor Records, the album was a critical and commercial success, becoming one of the best-selling records of the 1990s and helping revive Morrison's mainstream popularity.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison
chunks.text: Its success encouraged him to release a second and third greatest hits volume in 1993 and 2007, respectively.

chunks.title: The Best of Van Morrison
chunks.text: The album remains Morrison's best-seller.

chunks.title: Van Morrison in Ireland
chunks.text: Van Morrison in Ireland is the first official video by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison, released in 1981 of a concert Morrison recorded in Northern Ireland two years earlier.

chunks.title: Van Morrison in Ireland
chunks.text: The video also shows footage of the band whilst touring in Ireland and images of Belfast, including Hyndford Street and Cyprus Avenue.

chunks.title: Van Morrison in Ireland
chunks.text: Tony Stewart of the NME states "The band display a range of textures reminiscent of The Caledonia Soul Orchestra, first with the dark resonance of Toni Marcus' violin, then Pat Kyle's bright sharp tenor sax and finally Bobby Tench's prickly electric guitar".

chunks.title: Duets: Re-working the Catalogue
chunks.text: Duets: Re-working the Catalogue is the 35th studio album recorded by Northern Irish singer/songwriter Van Morrison.

chunks.title: Duets: Re-working the Catalogue
chunks.text: It was released on 13 March 2015 on RCA Records.

chunks.title: Duets: Re-working the Catalogue
chunks.text: Produced by Van Morrison along with Don Was and Bob Rock, it consists of songs previously recorded by Morrison this time recorded as duets.

chunks.title: Duets: Re-working the Catalogue
chunks.text: Performances include the artists Bobby Womack, Steve Winwood, Mark Knopfler, Taj Mahal, Mavis Staples, Michael Bublé, Natalie Cole, George Benson, Gregory Porter, Clare Teal, P.J. Proby, Joss Stone, Georgie Fame, Mick Hucknall, Chris Farlowe, and Morrison’s daughter Shana Morrison.

chunks.title: Van Morrison: The Concert
chunks.text: Van Morrison: The Concert is the second video released by Northern Irish singer-songwriter Van Morrison, first released in 1990.

chunks.title: Van Morrison: The Concert
chunks.text: Recorded in New York City the previous year, the concert featured two special guests and long-time friends Mose Allison and John Lee Hooker, each of whom performed some of their own songs.

chunks.title: Van Morrison: The Concert
chunks.text: This video mainly consisted of Morrison's work from his last two albums; including four songs from both "Avalon Sunset" and "Irish Heartbeat".

chunks.title: Van Morrison: The Concert
chunks.text: The video also features jazz singer Georgie Fame on Hammond organ.

chunks.title: Van Morrison: The Concert
chunks.text: Some reviewers have stated that Van Morrison was not in best shape during the concert, his voice was probably strained by a cold.

chunks.title: Rachel Specter
chunks.text: Rachel Sarah Specter (born April 9, 1980) is an American actress and writer, who is best known as the model for the RGX body spray commercials.

chunks.title: Rachel Specter
chunks.text: In addition to her work in commercials, Specter has guest-starred in episodes of "How I Met Your Mother", "Gilmore Girls", "What I Like About You", and "Entourage", as well as co-hosted the April 4, 2007 episode of "Attack of the Show!

chunks.title: Rachel Specter
chunks.text: " and a segment of "The Feed" on May 23.

chunks.title: Rachel Specter
chunks.text: In September 2008, Specter began co-starring in the web series "Long Distance Relationship" on Crackle.

chunks.title: Endurance running hypothesis
chunks.text: The endurance running hypothesis is the hypothesis that the evolution of certain human characteristics can be explained as adaptations to long distance running.

chunks.title: Endurance running hypothesis
chunks.text: The hypothesis suggests that endurance running played an important role for early hominins in obtaining food.

chunks.title: Endurance running hypothesis
chunks.text: Researchers have proposed that endurance running began as an adaptation for scavenging and later for persistence hunting.

chunks.title: The Infestation Hypothesis
chunks.text: "The Infestation Hypothesis" is the second episode of the fifth season of "The Big Bang Theory" that first aired on CBS on September 22, 2011.

chunks.title: The Infestation Hypothesis
chunks.text: It is the 89th episode overall.

chunks.title: The Infestation Hypothesis
chunks.text: In it, Sheldon (Jim Parsons) becomes worried when Penny acquires a new chair, while Leonard (Johnny Galecki) tries to make his long distance relationship with Priya work.

chunks.title: The Infestation Hypothesis
chunks.text: The episode was watched by nearly 12 million viewers in the U.S. and received mixed reviews.

chunks.title: Meredith Kessler
chunks.text: Meredith Brooke Kessler (born June 28, 1978) is an American professional triathlete from Columbus, Ohio who races in long distance, non-drafting triathlon events.

chunks.title: Meredith Kessler
chunks.text: She took third place at the 2011 ITU Long Distance Triathlon World Championships and has won numerous Ironman and half-Ironman distance races as both an amateur and a professional.

chunks.title: Meredith Kessler
chunks.text: She was named USA Triathlon's 2014 Non-Drafting Athlete of the Year.

chunks.title: Johnny Galecki
chunks.text: John Mark Galecki (born April 30, 1975) is an American actor.

chunks.title: Johnny Galecki
chunks.text: He is known for playing David Healy in the ABC sitcom "Roseanne" from 1992 to 1997 and Dr. Leonard Hofstadter in the CBS sitcom "The Big Bang Theory" since 2007.

chunks.title: Johnny Galecki
chunks.text: Galecki also appeared in the films "National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation" (1989), "Prancer" (1989), "Suicide Kings" (1997), "I Know What You Did Last Summer" (1997), "Bookies" (2003), and "In Time" (2011).

chunks.title: Communications in Guam
chunks.text: Though Guam is a United States territory, some U.S. long distance plans and courier services list Guam as an international location.

chunks.title: Communications in Guam
chunks.text: As a result of Guam's being added to the North American Numbering Plan (NANP) in 1997, calls made to the U.S., Canada, or other participating countries from Guam (or to Guam from other NANP locations) only require the caller to dial a 1 followed by the area code.

chunks.title: Communications in Guam
chunks.text: In this way, only domestic charges are incurred between the US and Guam on most carriers.

chunks.title: Communications in Guam
chunks.text: Before Guam's inclusion, calling the U.S. required dialing the international 011 first, thus resulting in higher long distance rates and less frequent calls to the U.S. by relatives in Guam.

chunks.title: Communications in Guam
chunks.text: Prices of long distance calls to these destinations have dropped significantly to the point where now calling the U.S. from Guam or calling Guam from the U.S. costs the same.

chunks.title: Permanent Roommates
chunks.text: Permanent Roommates is an Indian web series created by The Viral Fever(TVF) and Biswapati Sarkar.

chunks.title: Permanent Roommates
chunks.text: This series revolves around a young couple,Tanya and Mikesh, who after being in a long distance relationship for 3 years, face the prospect of marriage.

chunks.title: Permanent Roommates
chunks.text: Permanent Roommates has been renewed for a third season, which will premiere in 2018.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: The tenth series of Made in Chelsea, a British structured-reality television programme, began airing on 19 October 2015 on E4.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: The official trailer for the new series was released on 29 September 2015 confirming the start date.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: It concluded on 4 January 2016 following nine regular episodes, a Christmas special, a New Year special, and an End of Season party hosted by Rick Edwards.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: This series was the first to include new cast members Emma Walsh, Sam Harney, Tallulah Rufus Isaacs.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: Richard Dinan also returned to the series having last appeared during the fifth series, and Francis Boulle made a one-off return during the Christmas special.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: This was also the final series to include original cast member Spencer Matthews, long-running cast member Oliver Proudlock, as well as Millie Wilkinson and Emily Weller, who both made their debuts during the ninth series.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: The series focused heavily on Sam and Tiff's rocky relationship coming to an end when Tiff admits to cheating on him during the summer and rumours of Sam cheating surface, until the pair eventually reunite.

chunks.title: Made in Chelsea (series 10)
chunks.text: It also includes Louise and Alik attempting to make their long distance relationship work with obstacles in their way, Binky and JP finally making their relationship official despite commitment issues from his part, and Spencer causing further trouble by hooking up with Ollie's latest love interest Emma.

chunks.title: The Heart Machine
chunks.text: The Heart Machine is a 2014 romantic thriller film written and directed by Zachary Wigon based on his short film "Someone Else's Heart".

chunks.title: The Heart Machine
chunks.text: The film centers on Cody's John Gallagher, Jr. and Virginia's Kate Lyn Sheil long distance relationship that becomes strained when evidence appears to contradict Virginia's background.

chunks.title: The Heart Machine
chunks.text: The film was released in a limited release on October 24, 2014, by Filmbuff.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: Northwestern International University was one of the first colleges to offer self-directed online programs, which were based on review of prior-earned college credits, professional life-experiences, practical knowledge, research, portfolio work, and the passage of comprehensive examinations *Cite (Northwestern International University Registration Catalog).

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: N.I.U. was a member of the Long Distance Learning Council *Cite (Long Distance Learning Council Catalog).

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: Their admissions process consisted of the initial registration process, student selection, and the review of student work and experience.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: Students had to show proof of passing content specific exams before being considered for school admission.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: They were also required to pass comprehensive exams at the completion of their respective program.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: Furthermore, students were expected to complete a Practicum Learning Portfolio Log.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: The time-requirement for portfolio hours varied by subject matter.

chunks.title: Northwestern International University
chunks.text: Lastly, students had to successfully complete and present research, before N.I.U. would issue their degree *Cite(Northwestern International University Registration Catalog).

chunks.title: Paperon Intelligence Agency
chunks.text: Paperon Intelligence Agency (acronym: P.I.A.) is an ongoing storyline in the Italian Donald Duck pocket books.

chunks.title: Paperon Intelligence Agency
chunks.text: In the storyline, Scrooge McDuck ("Paperon de' Paperoni") is the chief of an intelligence agency named after him, whose intention is the protection of his money.

chunks.title: Paperon Intelligence Agency
chunks.text: Scrooge employs Donald Duck and Fethry Duck as secret agents to fight various enemies, such as the Beagle Boys and the mad scientist Zantaf.

chunks.title: Paperon Intelligence Agency
chunks.text: Donald's codename is Qu-Qu 7 ("quasi qualificato", Italian for "almost qualified"; also a pun on "cucù-settete" or "bubù-settete", the Italian word for "peekaboo"), and Fethry's codename is Me-Se 12 ("a mezzo servizio", "in half service"; also a pun on "mese", "month", and the number of months in a year).

chunks.title: Paperon Intelligence Agency
chunks.text: In contrast to the "DoubleDuck" storyline, "Paperon Intelligence Agency" is farcical, with Donald and Fethry bumbling up pretty much every mission Scrooge sends them on.

chunks.title: Igor Naming Agency
chunks.text: Igor Naming Agency is an American naming agency.

chunks.title: Igor Naming Agency
chunks.text: Based in Sausalito, California, Igor is known for its "almost militant embrace" of using real and natural-sounding words in naming.

chunks.title: Igor Naming Agency
chunks.text: Among others, the company has named Gogo Inflight, "Cutthroat Kitchen", TruTV, the Aria Resort, and consumer products for The North Face and Target, among others.

chunks.title: Disney's Contemporary Resort
chunks.text: Disney's Contemporary Resort, originally to be named Tempo Bay Hotel and previously the Contemporary Resort Hotel, is a AAA Four-Diamond Award–winning resort located at the Walt Disney World Resort in Bay Lake, Florida.

chunks.title: Disney's Contemporary Resort
chunks.text: Opened on October 1, 1971, the hotel is one of two original properties located at the complex alongside Disney's Polynesian Village Resort, and is currently listed as a deluxe-priced resort.

chunks.title: Disney's Contemporary Resort
chunks.text: It is adjacent to the Magic Kingdom theme park, and is identified by its A-frame main building.

chunks.title: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora
chunks.text: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora is a luxury resort located at Motu Tehotu on the island of Bora Bora, in the Society Islands of French Polynesia.

chunks.title: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora
chunks.text: The Resort is a part of Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts, a Toronto-based hotel management company.

chunks.title: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora
