chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: Vélo'v is a bicycle sharing system run by the city of Lyon, France, in conjunction with the advertising company JCDecaux.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: It has been the pioneer smart bicycle sharing system, previous systems being more ad hoc and run similar to a charity.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: The relationship with JCDecaux allows the city to provide the service on a cost neutral basis for the city, and at very low cost to users, in return for providing exclusive advertising access on bus shelters and the like.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: The primary aim is to reduce vehicle traffic within the city.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: The scheme also aims to reduce pollution, create a convivial atmosphere within the city, and encourage the health benefits of increased activity.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: Its name is a portmanteau of French "vélo" ("bike") and English "love".

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: The first bicycle sharing system to open in France, after the pioneering 1974 scheme in La Rochelle, its thundering success inspired similar systems in major French and European cities, including Paris' Velib' in 2007.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: With the success of these two high profile smart bicycle sharing systems a new paradigm of government supporting bike sharing as a part of a public transportation network emerged.

chunks.title: Vélo'v
chunks.text: It is still the bike share scheme with the second highest market penetration (1 bike per 121 residents) in the world, after the Velib'.

chunks.title: Beyond Blunderdome

chunks.title: Uhaul Car Share

chunks.title: Mascogos

chunks.title: Dhoolpet
chunks.text: Dhoolpet is one of the old suburbs in Hyderabad, India.

chunks.title: Dhoolpet

chunks.title: Dhoolpet

chunks.title: Seminole music
chunks.text: Seminole music is the music of the Seminole people, an indigenous people of the Americas who formed in Florida in the 18th century.

chunks.title: Seminole music
chunks.text: Today most live in Oklahoma, but a minority continue in Florida.

chunks.title: Seminole music
chunks.text: They have three federally recognized tribes, and some people belong to bands outside those groups.

chunks.title: Seminole music
chunks.text: Their traditional music includes extensive use of rattles, hand drums, water drums, and flutes.

chunks.title: Seminole
chunks.text: The Seminole are a Native American people originally from Florida.

chunks.title: Seminole
chunks.text: Today, they principally live in Oklahoma with a minority in Florida, and comprise three federally recognized tribes: the Seminole Tribe of Oklahoma, the Seminole Tribe of Florida, and Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida, as well as independent groups.

chunks.title: Seminole
chunks.text: The Seminole nation emerged in a process of ethnogenesis from various Native American groups who settled in Florida in the 18th century, most significantly northern Muscogee (Creeks) from what is now Georgia and Alabama.

chunks.title: Seminole
chunks.text: The word "Seminole" is derived from the Creek word "simanó-li", which may be itself be derived from the Spanish word "cimarrón", menaning "runaway" or "wild one".

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: The history of draining and development of the Everglades dates back to the 19th century.

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: During the Second Seminole War beginning in 1836, the United States military's mission was to seek out Seminole people in the Everglades and capture or kill them.

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: Those missions gave the military the opportunity to map land that seemed to frustrate and confound them at every turn.

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: A national push for expansion and progress toward the latter part of the 19th century stimulated interest in draining the Everglades for agricultural use.

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: According to historians, "From the middle of the nineteenth century to the middle of the twentieth century, the United States went through a period in which wetland removal was not questioned.

chunks.title: Draining and development of the Everglades
chunks.text: Indeed, it was considered the proper thing to do."

chunks.title: Muscogee language
chunks.text: The Muscogee language (Mvskoke in Muscogee), also known as Creek, Seminole, Maskókî or Muskogee, is a Muskogean language spoken by Muscogee (Creek) and Seminole people, primarily in the U.S. states of Oklahoma and Florida.

chunks.title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
chunks.text: Seminole County is a county located in the U.S. state of Oklahoma.

chunks.title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
chunks.text: As of the 2010 census, the population was 25,482.

chunks.title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
chunks.text: Its county seat is Wewoka.

chunks.title: Seminole County, Oklahoma
chunks.text: Before Oklahoma's admission as a state, the county was the entire small portion of Indian Territory allocated to the Seminole people, who were removed from Florida in the 1820s.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
chunks.text: The Battle of Jupiter Inlet occurred on January 15, 1838, between the Seminole Indians - Seminole Negro and the United States Navy.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
chunks.text: This was the first of a series of battles led by the US Navy in the area, also referred to as the First Battle of Loxahatchee.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
chunks.text: The battle started when Lt. Levin Powell led an expedition of 200 soldiers, sailors and marines, down the east coast of Florida.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
chunks.text: The Navy spotted a trail alongside the Jupiter Inlet, and seventy-five men were landed to find the Seminole camp nearby.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet
chunks.text: The camp was led by Sam Jones, Ar-pi-uck-i, the spiritual medicine and war chief of the Miccosukee and Seminole people during the war.

chunks.title: Battle of Jupiter Inlet

chunks.title: MMB-2201

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: Citrus greening disease (; or HLB), is a disease of citrus caused by a vector-transmitted pathogen.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: The causative agents are motile bacteria, "Candidatus" Liberibacter spp.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: The disease is vectored and transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid, "Diaphorina citri", and the African citrus psyllid, "Trioza erytreae", also known as the two-spotted citrus psyllid.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: It has also been shown to be graft-transmissible.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: Three different types of HLB are currently known: The heat-tolerant Asian form, and the heat-sensitive African and American forms.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: The disease was first described in 1929 and first reported in China in 1943.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: The African variation was first reported in 1947 in South Africa, where it is still widespread.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: Eventually, it affected the United states, reaching Florida in 2005.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: Within three years, it had spread to the majority of citrus farms.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: The rapid increase in this disease has threatened the citrus industry not only in Florida, but the entire US.

chunks.title: Citrus greening disease
chunks.text: As of 2009, 33 countries have reported HLB infection in their citrus crop.

chunks.title: Step over

chunks.title: Step over

chunks.title: Step over

chunks.title: Satoyoshi syndrome

chunks.title: Diarylpropionitrile
chunks.text: Diarylpropionitrile (DPN), also known as 2,3-bis(p-hydroxyphenyl)propionitrile (2,3-BHPPN), is a synthetic, nonsteroidal, and highly selective agonist of ERβ (IC = 15 nM) that is used widely in scientific research to study the function of this receptor.

chunks.title: Diarylpropionitrile
chunks.text: It is 70-fold more selective for ERβ over ERα, and has 100-fold lower affinity for GPER (GPR30) relative to estradiol.

chunks.title: Diarylpropionitrile
chunks.text: DPN produces antidepressant- and anxiolytic-like effects in animals via activation of the endogenous oxytocin system.

chunks.title: Diarylpropionitrile
chunks.text: First reported in 2001, DPN was the first selective ERβ agonist to be discovered, and was followed by prinaberel (ERB-041, WAY-202041), WAY-200070, and 8β-VE2 in 2004, ERB-196 (WAY-202196) in 2005, and certain phytoestrogens like liquiritigenin and nyasol ("cis"-hinokiresinol) since 2007.

chunks.title: EAM-2201

chunks.title: EAM-2201
chunks.text: Structurally, EAM-2201 is a hybrid of two known cannabinoid compounds JWH-210 and AM-2201, both of which had previously been used as active ingredients in synthetic cannabis blends before being banned in many countries.

chunks.title: Silicon boride

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: Several stoichiometric silicon boride compounds, SiB, have been reported: silicon triboride, SiB, silicon tetraboride, SiB, silicon hexaboride, SiB, as well as SiB ("n" = 14, 15, 40, etc.).

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: The "n" = 3 and "n" = 6 phases were reported as being co-produced together as a mixture for the first time by Henri Moissan and Alfred Stock in 1900 by briefly heating silicon and boron in a clay vessel.

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: The tetraboride was first reported as being synthesized directly from the elements in 1960 by three independent groups: Carl Cline and Donald Sands; Ervin Colton; and Cyrill Brosset and Bengt Magnusson.

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: It has been proposed that the triboride is a silicon-rich version of the tetraboride.

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: Hence, the stoichiometry of either compound could be expressed as SiB where "x" = 0 or 1.

chunks.title: Silicon boride

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, SiB and SiB are intermediate between diamond (10) and ruby (9).

chunks.title: Silicon boride
chunks.text: The silicon borides may be grown from boron-saturated silicon in either the solid or liquid state.

chunks.title: Fitzgerald Theater

chunks.title: Fitzgerald Theater

chunks.title: Fitzgerald Theater

chunks.title: Fitzgerald Theater

chunks.title: Fitzgerald Theater

chunks.title: Duke Jing of Qi
chunks.text: Duke Jing of Qi (; died 490 BC) was ruler of the State of Qi from 547 to 490 BC.

chunks.title: Duke Jing of Qi
chunks.text: Qi was a major power during the Spring and Autumn period of ancient China.

chunks.title: Duke Jing of Qi
chunks.text: His personal name was Lü Chujiu (呂杵臼), ancestral name Jiang (姜), and Duke Jing was his posthumous title.

chunks.title: Duke Jing of Qi

chunks.title: Aristodemus of Cumae

chunks.title: Aristodemus of Cumae
chunks.text: As a strategos, he twice defeated Etruscan armies.

chunks.title: Aristodemus of Cumae
chunks.text: He gained popularity amongst the people of Cumae due to his opposition to the city's aristocracy and his proposals to more fairly share land and to forgive debts.

chunks.title: Aristodemus of Cumae

chunks.title: Aristodemus of Cumae

chunks.title: Battle of Marathon
chunks.text: The Battle of Marathon (Greek: Μάχη τοῦ Μαραθῶνος , "Machē tou Marathōnos") took place in 490 BC, during the first Persian invasion of Greece.

chunks.title: Battle of Marathon
chunks.text: It was fought between the citizens of Athens, aided by Plataea, and a Persian force commanded by Datis and Artaphernes.

chunks.title: Battle of Marathon
chunks.text: The battle was the culmination of the first attempt by Persia, under King Darius I, to subjugate Greece.

chunks.title: Battle of Marathon
chunks.text: The Greek army decisively defeated the more numerous Persians, marking a turning point in the Greco-Persian Wars.

chunks.title: Cynaegirus
chunks.text: Cynegeirus, also spelled Cynaegeirus or Cynegirus (Greek: Κυνέγειρος or Κυναίγειρος "Kynegeiros" or "Kynaigeiros"; died 490 BC) was an ancient Greek hero of Athens and had three siblings.

chunks.title: Cynaegirus
chunks.text: His two brothers were the playwright Aeschylus and Ameinias, hero of the battle of Salamis, while his sister was Philopatho (Greek: Φιλοπαθώ ), the mother of the Athenian tragic poet Philokles.

chunks.title: Cynaegirus
chunks.text: He was the son of Euphorion (Greek: Ευφορίωνας ) from Eleusis and member of the Eupatridae, the ancient nobility of Attica.

chunks.title: Themistocles
chunks.text: Themistocles ( ; Greek: Θεμιστοκλῆς "Themistoklẽs"; "Glory of the Law"; c. 524–459 BC) was an Athenian politician and general.

chunks.title: Themistocles
chunks.text: He was one of a new breed of non-aristocratic politicians who rose to prominence in the early years of the Athenian democracy.

chunks.title: Themistocles
chunks.text: As a politician, Themistocles was a populist, having the support of lower-class Athenians, and generally being at odds with the Athenian nobility.

chunks.title: Themistocles
chunks.text: Elected archon in 493 BC, he convinced the polis to increase the naval power of Athens, a recurring theme in his political career.

chunks.title: Themistocles
chunks.text: During the first Persian invasion of Greece he fought at the Battle of Marathon (490 BC) and was possibly one of the ten Athenian "strategoi" (generals) in that battle.

chunks.title: Callimachus (polemarch)

chunks.title: Callimachus (polemarch)

chunks.title: Battle of Thermopylae
chunks.text: The Battle of Thermopylae ( ; Greek: Μάχη τῶν Θερμοπυλῶν , "Machē tōn Thermopylōn") was fought between an alliance of Greek city-states, led by King Leonidas of Sparta, and the Persian Empire of Xerxes I over the course of three days, during the second Persian invasion of Greece.

chunks.title: Battle of Thermopylae
chunks.text: It took place simultaneously with the naval battle at Artemisium, in August or September 480 BC, at the narrow coastal pass of Thermopylae ("The Hot Gates").

chunks.title: Battle of Thermopylae
chunks.text: The Persian invasion was a delayed response to the defeat of the first Persian invasion of Greece, which had been ended by the Athenian victory at the Battle of Marathon in 490 BC.

chunks.title: Battle of Thermopylae
chunks.text: Xerxes had amassed a huge army and navy, and set out to conquer all of Greece.

chunks.title: Battle of Thermopylae
chunks.text: The Athenian politician and general Themistocles had proposed that the allied Greeks block the advance of the Persian army at the pass of Thermopylae, and simultaneously block the Persian navy at the Straits of Artemisium.

chunks.title: 490 BC

chunks.title: 490 BC

chunks.title: 490 BC

chunks.title: Arthurdale, West Virginia
chunks.text: Arthurdale is an unincorporated community in Preston County, West Virginia, United States.

chunks.title: Arthurdale, West Virginia
chunks.text: Arthurdale was named for Richard Arthur, former owner of the land on which it was built, who had sold the land to the federal government under a tax default.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: Cedar Creek is an 11.2 mi tributary of the South Fork Eel River in Mendocino County in the U.S. state of California.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: The creek begins southeast of Red Mountain, at an elevation of 778 ft .

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: It makes an S-curve west-northwest then bends sharply south, dropping into the valley of the South Fork Eel.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: The confluence is south of the city of Leggett, on the river's right bank.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: The only named tributary of Cedar Creek is Little Cedar Creek, a headwaters tributary.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: Big Dann Creek joins the South Fork Eel on the same bank, just upstream of Cedar Creek, while the next major tributary downstream of Cedar is Rock Creek.

chunks.title: Cedar Creek (South Fork Eel River)
chunks.text: The Cedar Creek watershed is rugged and has few tributaries.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: West Hemlock Creek is a tributary of Hemlock Creek in Montour County and Columbia County, in Pennsylvania, in the United States.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: It is approximately 3.7 mi long and flows through West Hemlock Township, Montour County and Hemlock Township, Columbia County.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: The creek has at least one unnamed tributary.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: West Hemlock Creek and its unnamed tributary are considered by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection to be impaired.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: The watershed of the creek has an area of 2.80 sqmi .

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: The creek is designated as a coldwater fishery.

chunks.title: West Hemlock Creek
chunks.text: Rock formations in the watershed include the Catskill Formation and the Trimemrs Rock Formation.

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: West Branch Little Muncy Creek is a tributary of Little Muncy Creek in Sullivan County and Lycoming County, in Pennsylvania, in the United States.

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: It is approximately 3.5 mi long and flows through Davidson Township in Sullivan County and Franklin Township and Jordan Township in Lycoming County.

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: The watershed of the creek has an area of 4.33 sqmi .

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: The creek has one named tributary, which is known as West Creek.

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: The surficial geology in the vicinity of West Branch Little Muncy Creek includes alluvium, bedrock, fill, Wisconsinan and Reworked Illinoian Till, Wisconsinan Till, Wisconsinan Flow-Till, Wisconsinan Till Moraine, and Boulder Colluvium.

chunks.title: West Branch Little Muncy Creek
chunks.text: The creek designated as a Coldwater Fishery and a Migratory Fishery and is being considered for addition to the wild trout waters list of the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission.

chunks.title: Deckers Creek
chunks.text: Deckers Creek is a 24.6 mi tributary of the Monongahela River that runs through north-central West Virginia.

chunks.title: Deckers Creek
chunks.text: It begins west of Arthurdale and flows southeast, then north, then northwest towards Morgantown, where it empties into the Monongahela River.

chunks.title: Deckers Creek
chunks.text: The stream has been contaminated by various sources, though largely due to extractive resource mining and improper sewage disposal.

chunks.title: Deckers Creek
chunks.text: Recently, a conservation effort has been launched and conditions are improving, as the area continues to develop for recreational purposes.

chunks.title: Deckers Creek Trail
chunks.text: The Deckers Creek Trail is a rail trail located in West Virginia.

chunks.title: Turkey Creek (Econlockhatchee River)
chunks.text: Turkey Creek is a creek and tributary of the Econlockhatchee River located in the community of Narcoossee in Southeast Orlando, in the U.S. State of Florida.

chunks.title: Turkey Creek (Econlockhatchee River)
chunks.text: The source of the 3 mi river is Turkey Creek Bay, which is the northern beginning of the Econlockhatchee River Swamp that extends to Lake Conlin, the source of the Econlockhatchee River.

chunks.title: Turkey Creek (Econlockhatchee River)
chunks.text: From Turkey Creek Bay, the creek flows north and goes under Wewahootee Road and then State Road 528, commonly known as the "Beachline Expressway".

chunks.title: Turkey Creek (Econlockhatchee River)
chunks.text: A tributary of the creek itself, the Green Branch, joins Turkey Creek at about 1100 ft before Turkey Creek joins the Econlockhatchee at .

chunks.title: Cascade, West Virginia
chunks.text: Cascade is an unincorporated community in Preston County, West Virginia, United States.

chunks.title: Cascade, West Virginia
chunks.text: Cascade is located along West Virginia Route 7, Deckers Creek, and a CSX Railroad line 1.2 mi northwest of Morgantown.

chunks.title: Upper Deckers Creek Wildlife Management Area
chunks.text: Upper Deckers Creek Wildlife Management Area, is located about 1 mi north of Reedsville, West Virginia in Preston County.

chunks.title: Upper Deckers Creek Wildlife Management Area
chunks.text: Upper Deckers Creek WMA is located on 56 acre , consisting of two small fishing ponds and surrounding forested rolling hills.

chunks.title: Coles Creek (Pennsylvania)
chunks.text: Coles Creek (also known as Cole's Creek) is a tributary of Fishing Creek, in Columbia County, Pennsylvania and Sullivan County, Pennsylvania, in the United States.

chunks.title: Coles Creek (Pennsylvania)
chunks.text: It is 6.0 mi long and is the first named tributary of Fishing Creek downstream of where East Branch Fishing Creek and West Branch Fishing Creek meet to form Fishing Creek.

chunks.title: Coles Creek (Pennsylvania)
chunks.text: The creek is on the edge of Columbia County and parts of its watershed are in Luzerne County.

chunks.title: John Wesley
chunks.text: John Wesley ( or ; 28 June [O.S. 17 June] 1703 2 March 1791) was an English Anglican cleric and theologian who, with his brother Charles and fellow cleric George Whitefield, founded Methodism.

chunks.title: Kentucky Synod
chunks.text: Kentucky Synod was a synod of the Presbyterian Church in the United States of America established in the late 18th century.

chunks.title: Kentucky Synod
chunks.text: As a body, Kentucky Synod was a great deal more conservative than the Presbyterian Church as a whole — especially in its opposition to many aspects of the Second Great Awakening, a revival movement that thrived in Kentucky from about 1798 to about 1820.

chunks.title: Kentucky Synod
chunks.text: Synod suspended or deposed a number of revivalist Presbyterian ministers, but these men continued to preach to their former congregations.

chunks.title: Kentucky Synod
chunks.text: Eventually, Barton W. Stone, who abandoned Washington Presbytery in 1803, formed Springfield Presbytery, which eventually became the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ).

chunks.title: Kentucky Synod
chunks.text: In 1810, ministers from the former Cumberland Presbytery, which had been dissolved by Synod five years earlier, left the church and created an independent presbytery which became the Cumberland Presbyterian Church.

chunks.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
chunks.text: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (known as the LDS Church or, informally, the Mormon Church) is a Christian restorationist church that is considered by its members to be the restoration of the original church founded by Jesus Christ.

chunks.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
chunks.text: The church is headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, and has established congregations and built temples worldwide.

chunks.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
chunks.text: According to the church, it has over 70,000 missionaries and a membership of over 15 million.

chunks.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
chunks.text: It is ranked by the National Council of Churches as the fourth-largest Christian denomination in the United States.

chunks.title: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
chunks.text: It is the largest denomination in the Latter Day Saint movement founded by Joseph Smith during the period of religious revival known as the Second Great Awakening.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: Bishop was born on September 29, 1760 in Stamford, Connecticut, United States.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: In 1779, according to Shaker Elder Henry C. Blinn, Bishop became interested in a "religious revival", just around a decade before the beginning of the Second Great Awakening.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: He later recorded an account of his experiences and conversion to Shakerism, writing:"I entered fully into the spirit of the work and received great light.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: Although zealous prayers and religious exercises often had the effect to produce spiritual impressions, yet they were not permanent, and left me a subject to temptations.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: We passed the winter exhorting each other to faithfulness, while we anxiously waited for the accomplishment of the prophetic spirit of the revival.In the spring of 1780 we learned of a people near the city of Albany, NY, who were reported to have received a singular kind of religion, and that they possessed a large degree of divine light and spiritual power.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: Many went out to see them and returned fully persuaded that they were the true witnesses of God.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: The work increased and I felt a great desire to satisfy myself concerning these strangers and their religion.In June, in company with several others, I made them a visit.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: We arrived on Saturday evening and remained till Monday.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: We attended their meetings.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: The singing was inspiring, the speaking powerful and heart-searching.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: The wisdom of their instruction, the purity of their doctrine, and the Christ-like simplicity of their deportment all reminded me of the apostolic faith.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I saw that the work was of God, and my salvation depended upon it.The cross that was before me was an evidence of the spirit of the testimony.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: On the one hand, the prospects of the world were flattering to my mind.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I was in the prime of life and in the vigor of health.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: My reputation was fair, and my hopes not unpromising.On the other hand, religion had been my pursuit.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: The revival had raised my hopes and directed my faith to a greater and more glorious work.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I subsequently made another visit and was received with kindness.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I confessed my sins to God, and with a fixed resolution accepted the cross of Christ.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I was now taught to rectify every wrong that I had committed, to forsake all sin and to take up a daily cross. "

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I also became better acquainted with Mother Ann and the Elders who were with her, and am a witness of the purity of life which they constantly maintained.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: The doctrine they taught was strictly conformable to the precepts and example of Jesus Christ.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: By obeying their instruction I experienced the truth of their testimony.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: I was blessed with heavenly visions and felt my faith established on a sure foundation.I visited Mother Ann and the Elders many times at Watervliet, Harvard, Ashfield, Hancock, and New Lebanon, and freely associated with all the leading members of the Society.

chunks.title: Job Bishop
chunks.text: To my great satisfaction I have seen that the principles which were first taught by Mother Ann have been faithfully kept by her successors."

chunks.title: List of Methodist churches in the United States
chunks.text: This is a list of Methodist churches in the United States.

chunks.title: List of Methodist churches in the United States
chunks.text: It includes notable churches either where a church means a congregation (in the New Testament definition) or where a church means a building (in the colloquial sense).

chunks.title: List of Methodist churches in the United States
chunks.text: It also includes campgrounds and conference centers and retreats that are significant Methodist gathering places, including a number of historic sites of camp meetings. Methodism was founded with a large component being a rejection of past churches and was developed by John Wesley and others in large open-air gatherings in Great Britain.

chunks.title: List of Methodist churches in the United States
chunks.text: In the United States, Methodists (along with Baptists and other Protestants) were major participants in the Second Great Awakening wherein people would travel from a large area to a particular site to camp out, listen to itinerant preachers, and pray.

chunks.title: List of Methodist churches in the United States
chunks.text: The list also includes selected notable Methodist theological buildings.

chunks.title: James McGready
chunks.text: Rev. James McGready (1763–1817) was a Presbyterian minister and a revivalist during the Second Great Awakening in the United States of America.

chunks.title: James McGready
chunks.text: He was one of the most important figures of the Second Great Awakening in the American frontier.

chunks.title: Fourth Great Awakening
chunks.text: The Fourth Great Awakening was a Christian religious awakening that some scholars — most notably economic historian Robert Fogel — say took place in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s, while others look at the era following World War II.

chunks.title: Fourth Great Awakening
chunks.text: The terminology is controversial, with many historians believing the religious changes that took place in the US during these years were not equivalent to those of the first three great awakenings.

chunks.title: Fourth Great Awakening
chunks.text: Thus, the idea of a Fourth Great Awakening itself has not been generally accepted.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: The evangelical revival in Scotland was a series of religious movements in Scotland from the eighteenth century, with periodic revivals into the twentieth century.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: It began in the later 1730s as congregations experienced intense "awakenings" of enthusiasm, renewed commitment and rapid expansion.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: This was first seen at Easter Ross in the Highlands in 1739 and most famously in the Cambuslang Wark near Glasgow in 1742.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: Most of the new converts were relatively young and from the lower groups in society.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: Unlike awakenings elsewhere, the early revival in Scotland did not give rise to a major religious movement, but mainly benefited the secession churches, who had broken away from the Church of Scotland.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: In the late eighteenth century and early nineteenth century the revival entered a second wave, known in the US as the Second Great Awakening.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: In Scotland this was reflected in events like the Kilsyth Revival in 1839.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: The early revival mainly spread in the Central Belt, but it became active in the Highlands and Islands, peaking towards the middle of the nineteenth century.

chunks.title: Evangelical revival in Scotland
chunks.text: Scotland gained many of the organisations associated with the revival in England, including Sunday Schools, mission schools, ragged schools, Bible societies and improvement classes.

chunks.title: Second Great Awakening
chunks.text: The Second Great Awakening was a Protestant religious revival during the early 19th century in the United States.

chunks.title: Second Great Awakening
chunks.text: The movement began around 1790, gained momentum by 1800 and, after 1820, membership rose rapidly among Baptist and Methodist congregations whose preachers led the movement.

chunks.title: Second Great Awakening
chunks.text: It was past its peak by the late 1850s.

chunks.title: Second Great Awakening
chunks.text: The Second Great Awakening reflected Romanticism characterized by enthusiasm, emotion, and an appeal to the super-natural.

chunks.title: Second Great Awakening
chunks.text: It rejected the skeptical rationalism and deism of the Enlightenment.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: The United Methodist Church (UMC) is a mainline Protestant denomination, and a major part of Methodism.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: In the 19th century, its main predecessor—the Methodist Church—was a leader in Evangelicalism.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: It was founded in 1968 in Dallas, Texas, United States, by union of the Methodist Church and the Evangelical United Brethren Church.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: The UMC traces its roots back to the revival movement of John and Charles Wesley in England as well as the Great Awakening in the United States.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: As such, the church's theological orientation is decidedly Wesleyan.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: It embraces both liturgical and evangelical elements.

chunks.title: United Methodist Church
chunks.text: It has a connectional polity, a typical feature of a number of Methodist denominations.

chunks.title: Horrors of Spider Island
chunks.text: Horrors of Spider Island (German: "Ein Toter hing im Netz" , "A Dead One Hung in the Web") is a 1960 West German horror film directed by Fritz Böttger from his screenplay, and produced by Gaston Hakim and Wolf C. Hartwig for Rapid-Film/Intercontinental Filmgesellschaft.

chunks.title: Horrors of Spider Island
chunks.text: The film stars Alexander D'Arcy as a talent agent who invites several girls to a club in Singapore.

chunks.title: Horrors of Spider Island
chunks.text: Their plane ride ends abruptly when they crash-land into the ocean.

chunks.title: Horrors of Spider Island
chunks.text: D'Arcy and the women make their way to an island where they find a larger spider web.

chunks.title: Horrors of Spider Island
chunks.text: A giant spider sinks its teeth in D'Arcy which turns him into a mutant.

chunks.title: Bhool Bhulaiyaa
chunks.text: Bhool Bhulaiya (English: "The Maze") is a 2007 Indian comedy horror film directed by Priyadarshan.

chunks.title: Bhool Bhulaiyaa
chunks.text: It is the official remake of the 1993 Malayalam film, "Manichitrathazhu", starring Mohanlal and Shobana, which was already remade into several languages films.

chunks.title: Makdee
chunks.text: Makdee (English: Spider ), promoted as The Web Of The Witch, in English, is a 2002 Indian comedy horror film directed by Vishal Bhardwaj.

chunks.title: Makdee
chunks.text: It stars Shabana Azmi, Makrand Deshpande, Shweta Prasad, Vijay Raaz and Alaap Mazgaonkar.

chunks.title: Makdee
chunks.text: The film tells the story of a young girl in north India and an alleged witch in all mansion.

chunks.title: Makdee
chunks.text: It also explains the belief in witches and witchcraft across modern day India.

chunks.title: Makdee
chunks.text: The film was screened in the Critics' Week (Spotlight on India) section at the 2003 Cannes Film Festival.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Padosan (Hindi: "पड़ोसन", English: lady Neighbour ) is a 1968 Indian comedy film.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Directed by Jyoti Swaroop.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: It was produced by Mehmood, N. C. Sippy and written by Rajendra Krishan.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: It was a remake of the Bengali film "Pasher Bari" (1952) starring Bhanu Bandyopadhyay and Sabitri Chatterjee.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: The movie stars Sunil Dutt and Saira Banu in lead roles.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Kishore Kumar, Mukri, Raj Kishore and Keshto Mukherjee played the supporting roles.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Mehmood as the South Indian musician and rival to Sunil Dutt is among the highlights of the film.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: It was considered as one of the best comedy movies ever made in Hindi film history.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Mehmood's portrayal of a south Indian music teacher was one of his all time best and noted performances and a key highlight of the film.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Kishore Kumar's character of a comical theater director was also well received.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: "Indiatimes Movies" ranked the movie amongst the "Top 25 Must See Bollywood Films".

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Music was composed by R.D. Burman and was a huge hit.

chunks.title: Padosan
chunks.text: Kishore Kumar sang for himself while Manna Dey sang for Mehmood.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: Vampire in Brooklyn (also known as Wes Craven's Vampire in Brooklyn) is a 1995 American comedy horror film directed by Wes Craven.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: Eddie Murphy, who also produced and stars in the film, wrote the film's script, alongside Vernon Lynch and Murphy's older brother Charles Q. Murphy.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: "Vampire in Brooklyn" co-stars Angela Bassett, Allen Payne, Kadeem Hardison, John Witherspoon, Zakes Mokae, and Joanna Cassidy.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: Murphy also plays an alcoholic preacher and a foul-mouthed Italian gangster.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: The film was released in the United States on October 27, 1995.

chunks.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
chunks.text: Despite negative reviews, the film became a cult film among fans.

chunks.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
chunks.text: Awara Paagal Deewana (Hindi: आवारा पागल दीवाना , English: "Wayward, Crazy, Insane") is a 2002 Indian Hindi action comedy film directed by Vikram Bhatt.

chunks.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
chunks.text: The film's music was composed by Anu Malik, and the lyrics by Sameer.

chunks.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
chunks.text: It has a plot loosely inspired by "The Whole Nine Yards", and features action scenes choreographed by stunt director Dion Lam, who worked on "The Matrix" and Hong Kong action films.

chunks.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
chunks.text: "Awara Paagal Deewana" was one of the highest grossing Hindi films of the year 2002.

chunks.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
chunks.text: It was notable for lavish and exotic song picturisations, stunts/action scenes by Akshay Kumar, and Paresh Rawal's popular comical chemistry with Johnny Lever, who played a funny character called Chhota Chhatri.

chunks.title: Vishal Bhardwaj
chunks.text: Vishal Bhardwaj (born 4 August 1965) is an Indian film director, screenwriter, producer, music composer and playback singer.

chunks.title: Vishal Bhardwaj
chunks.text: He is known for his work in Hindi cinema, and is the recipient of a Filmfare Award and seven National Film Awards in four categories.

chunks.title: Hello Naan Pei Pesuren
chunks.text: Music composed by Siddharth Vipin, cinematography handled by Banu Murugan and editing done by N. B. Srikanth.

chunks.title: Ultra (Depeche Mode album)

chunks.title: Angels & Ghosts

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: Depeche Mode are an English electronic band that formed in Basildon, Essex in 1980.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: The group consists of founders Dave Gahan (lead vocals), Martin Gore (guitar, keyboards, vocals), and Andy Fletcher (keyboards, bass guitar).

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: Depeche Mode released their debut album "Speak & Spell" in 1981, bringing the band onto the British new wave scene.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: Original band member Vince Clarke (keyboards, guitar), left the band after the release of the album, leaving the band as a trio to record "A Broken Frame", released the following year.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: Gore took over the lead songwriting duties and, later in 1982, Alan Wilder (keyboards, drums, bass guitar) officially joined the band to fill Clarke's spot, establishing a line up that would continue for the next 13 years.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode
chunks.text: Depeche Mode have been a trio again since 1995, when Wilder left.

chunks.title: Tim Simenon
chunks.text: Tim Simenon (born 21 June 1967, Brixton, London) is an English musician, composer and record producer, known for his work as Bomb the Bass.

chunks.title: Tim Simenon
chunks.text: Simenon has produced, remixed and collaborated with a range of artists including Dave Gahan and Martin Gore of Depeche Mode.

chunks.title: Gareth Jones (music producer)
chunks.text: Gareth Jones (born 1954) is a British music producer and engineer notable for working with Depeche Mode, Einstürzende Neubauten, Wire and Erasure.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode discography
chunks.text: The discography of English electronic music group Depeche Mode consists of fourteen studio albums, six live albums, ten compilation albums, eight box sets, thirteen video albums, fifty-three singles and seventy music videos.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode discography
chunks.text: The band's music has been released on several labels, including Some Bizzare, Mute Records, Sire Records, Reprise Records, and Columbia Records.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode discography
chunks.text: Formed in Basildon, Essex, England in 1980, the group's original line-up was Dave Gahan (lead vocals), Martin Gore (keyboards, guitar, vocals, chief songwriter after 1981), Andy Fletcher (keyboards) and Vince Clarke (keyboards, chief songwriter 1980–81).

chunks.title: Depeche Mode discography
chunks.text: Vince Clarke left the band after the release of their 1981 debut album "Speak & Spell" and was replaced by Alan Wilder (production, keyboards, drums), who was a band member from 1982 to 1995.

chunks.title: Depeche Mode discography
chunks.text: Following Wilder's departure, Gahan, Gore, and Fletcher continued as a trio.

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)
chunks.text: "Heaven" is a song by English electronic music band Depeche Mode, released as the lead single from their thirteenth studio album, "Delta Machine" (2013).

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)
chunks.text: In the United Kingdom, "Heaven" was released digitally on 17 March 2013 and physically the following day.

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)

chunks.title: Heaven (Depeche Mode song)
chunks.text: An accompanying music video for "Heaven" was directed by Timothy Saccenti and premiered on VEVO on 1 February 2013.

chunks.title: Das Shadow

chunks.title: Das Shadow

chunks.title: Eastern Group of Painters
chunks.text: The Eastern Group of Painters was a Canadian artists collective founded in 1938 in Montreal, Quebec.

chunks.title: Eastern Group of Painters
chunks.text: The group included Montreal artists whose common interest was painting and an art for art's sake aesthetic, not the espousal of a nationalist theory as was the case with the Group of Seven or the Canadian Group of Painters.

chunks.title: Eastern Group of Painters
chunks.text: The group’s members included Alexander Bercovitch, Goodridge Roberts, Eric Goldberg, Jack Weldon Humphrey, John Goodwin Lyman, and Jori Smith.

chunks.title: Eastern Group of Painters
chunks.text: Goldberg and Lyman were both well represented by Max Stern's Dominion Gallery in Montreal.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Regina Seiden (4 July 1897- 11 January 1991) was a Jewish Canadian Woman painter who was an early member of the Beaver Hall Group.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Born in Rigaud, Quebec, Seiden moved with her family to Montreal in 1905.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Between 1905 and 1912 she attended the French Catholic school Académie Marie-Rose, located in the Plateau neighbourhood of Montreal, where she was encouraged to explore her talents as a painter.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Between 1913 and 1918 Seiden attended the Art Association of Montreal where she studied under William Brymner, Edmond Dyonnet and Maurice Cullen.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Along with other former students of William Brymner, Seiden joined the Beaver Hall Group and took part in their first exhibit in 1921.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: In 1921 Seiden moved to Paris where she studied for a year at the Académie Julien.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: In 1926 Seiden returned to Paris where she met her husband, fellow artist Eric Goldberg.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: They got married in 1928 at which point she stopped painting until after his death in 1969.

chunks.title: Regina Seiden
chunks.text: Seiden lived and painted in Montreal until her death in 1991.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (animator)
chunks.text: Eric Goldberg (born May 1, 1955) is an American animator, film director and voice actor.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (animator)
chunks.text: He is known for his work at both Walt Disney Animation Studios and Warner Bros.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (animator)
chunks.text: Animation.

chunks.title: You Were Never Duckier
chunks.text: You Were Never Duckier is an animated cartoon in the "Merrie Melodies" series from 1948.

chunks.title: You Were Never Duckier
chunks.text: Starring Daffy Duck and Henery Hawk, this cartoon marked the start of a direction change for Daffy Duck, from a "screwball" character, to a greedy, self-centered one (though, according to commentary by Eric Goldberg on the Looney Tunes Golden Collection DVD [fifth volume], this cartoon showed Daffy as being "both" a greedy, self-centered character "and" a screwball one).

chunks.title: You Were Never Duckier
chunks.text: This cartoon was also the next-to-last Henery Hawk cartoon to "not" be directed by Robert McKimson, and one of only four to be directed by creator Chuck Jones (after "The Squawkin' Hawk", "Flop Goes the Weasel", and followed by "The Scarlet Pumpernickel").

chunks.title: Pocahontas (1995 film)
chunks.text: Pocahontas is a 1995 American animated musical romantic-comedy-drama film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Pocahontas (1995 film)
chunks.text: The 33rd Disney animated feature film, the film is part of the era known as the Disney Renaissance which lasted from 1989 to 1999.

chunks.title: Pocahontas (1995 film)
chunks.text: Directed by Mike Gabriel and Eric Goldberg, the film is inspired by the known history and folklore surrounding the Native American woman Pocahontas and portrays a fictionalized account of her historical encounter with Englishman John Smith and the Jamestown settlers that arrived from the Virginia Company.

chunks.title: Pocahontas (1995 film)
chunks.text: The voice cast features Irene Bedard, Mel Gibson, David Ogden Stiers, Russell Means, Christian Bale, Billy Connolly, and Linda Hunt.

chunks.title: Pocahontas (1995 film)
chunks.text: The musical score was written by Alan Menken, with songs written by Menken and lyricist Stephen Schwartz.

chunks.title: MadMaze
chunks.text: MadMaze is an online video game designed by Eric Goldberg and developed by Greg Costikyan in 1989.

chunks.title: MadMaze
chunks.text: It was the first online game to draw over a million players., and was playable through the Prodigy service.

chunks.title: MadMaze
chunks.text: The game disappeared in 1999 with the death of the Prodigy service, but with the permission from the service and the creators, fans of the game have rehosted it.

chunks.title: Paranoia (role-playing game)
chunks.text: Paranoia is a dystopian science-fiction tabletop role-playing game originally designed and written by Greg Costikyan, Dan Gelber, and Eric Goldberg, and first published in 1984 by West End Games.

chunks.title: Paranoia (role-playing game)
chunks.text: Since 2004 the game has been published under license by Mongoose Publishing.

chunks.title: Paranoia (role-playing game)
chunks.text: The game won the Origins Award for Best Roleplaying Rules of 1984 and was inducted into the Origins Awards Hall of Fame in 2007.

chunks.title: Paranoia (role-playing game)
chunks.text: "Paranoia" is notable among tabletop games for being more competitive than co-operative, with players encouraged to betray one another for their own interests, as well as for keeping a light-hearted, tongue in cheek tone despite its dystopian setting.

chunks.title: Highway to the Reich
chunks.text: Highway to the Reich was a highly detailed simulation "monster" board wargame published by Simulations Publications, Inc. (SPI) in 1977, and reprinted by Decision Games in 2008.

chunks.title: Highway to the Reich
chunks.text: It was designed by Jay A. Nelson, Irad B. Hardy and Eric Goldberg, with a second edition of the rules published in July 1977.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (artist)
chunks.text: Eric Goldberg (1890–1969) was a Jewish-Canadian painter, born in 1890 in Berlin, Germany.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (artist)
chunks.text: Goldberg was influenced by the art of Pierre-Auguste Renoir at an early age.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (artist)
chunks.text: He studied at Paris, France's École des Beaux-Arts (1906–10) and Académie Julian under Tony Robert-Fleury, Jules Joseph Lefebvre and Jean-Paul Laurens, and taught at the Prussian Academy of Arts and, later, the Bezalel Academy of Art and Design, Jerusalem (1911–1915, returning to teach again in then British Mandate of Palestine from 1924–1926).

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (artist)
chunks.text: He began working in Montreal in 1928, and soon after began favouring the landscapes of Quebec's Gaspésie region as subjects.

chunks.title: Eric Goldberg (artist)
chunks.text: In 1939, Goldberg became a founding member of the Contemporary Arts Society (in French, "Société d'art contemporain"), a group of Canadian artists intent on sensitizing the public to modern art.

chunks.title: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn
chunks.text: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn was a professional wrestling show in the NXT TakeOver series that took place on August 22, 2015.

chunks.title: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn
chunks.text: The NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn event was produced by WWE, showcasing its NXT developmental brand, and streamed live on the WWE Network.

chunks.title: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn
chunks.text: The event took place at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York - the first night of what was billed as a WWE "triple-header" at the arena, with SummerSlam taking place the following evening, and "Raw" the night after that.

chunks.title: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn

chunks.title: NXT TakeOver: Brooklyn

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: Elimination Chamber is a professional wrestling pay-per-view (PPV) event, produced by WWE, a professional wrestling promotion based in Connecticut.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: The event was created in 2010, with its inaugural event taking place on February 21, 2010, replacing No Way Out.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: Elimination Chamber is a pay-per-view (PPV) event consisting of a main event and undercard that features championship matches and other various matches.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: The concept of the show was that the two main event matches were contested inside the Elimination Chamber; one of these matches typically featured the WWE Championship being defended, while the other was usually contested for the World Heavyweight Championship (the two titles were unified in December 2013).

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: The first Elimination Chamber event took place on February 21, 2010 and aired live on PPV.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: The event's name was selected after WWE allowed fans to provide input via a survey on their official website and was chosen over Heavy Metal, Battle Chamber, Chamber of Conflict, and the original No Way Out name.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: Since its origin, each event has been held in an indoor arena, with all five taking place in the United States.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: In 2015, the event was replaced by Fastlane in the February pay-per-view slot.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: However, the 2015 event was later announced to be streamed exclusively on the WWE Network in the United States on May 31 and was also available on PPV elsewhere.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: WWE also confirmed that the newly vacant WWE Intercontinental Championship was being decided inside the Elimination Chamber.

chunks.title: WWE Elimination Chamber
chunks.text: The event did not occur in 2016, but returned in 2017 as a SmackDown branded event.

chunks.title: Dumbo
chunks.text: Dumbo is a 1941 American animated film produced by Walt Disney Productions and released by RKO Radio Pictures.

chunks.title: Dumbo
chunks.text: The fourth Disney animated feature film, it is based upon the storyline written by Helen Aberson and illustrated by Harold Pearl for the prototype of a novelty toy ("Roll-a-Book").

chunks.title: Dumbo
chunks.text: The main character is Jumbo Jr., a semi-anthropomorphic elephant who is cruelly nicknamed "Dumbo".

chunks.title: Dumbo
chunks.text: He is ridiculed for his big ears, but in fact he is capable of flying by using his ears as wings. Throughout most of the film, his only true friend, aside from his mother, is the mouse, Timothy – a relationship parodying the stereotypical animosity between mice and elephants.

chunks.title: Dumbo (air-sea rescue)
chunks.text: Dumbo was the code name used by the United States Navy during the 1940s and 1950s to signify search and rescue missions, conducted in conjunction with military operations, by long-range aircraft flying over the ocean.

chunks.title: Dumbo (air-sea rescue)
chunks.text: The purpose of Dumbo missions was to rescue downed American aviators as well as seamen in distress.

chunks.title: Dumbo (air-sea rescue)
chunks.text: Dumbo aircraft were originally land-based heavy bomber aircraft converted to carry an airborne lifeboat to be dropped in the water near survivors.

chunks.title: Dumbo (air-sea rescue)
chunks.text: The name "Dumbo" came from Walt Disney's flying elephant, the main character of the animated film "Dumbo", appearing in October 1941.

chunks.title: Three Sons o' Guns
chunks.text: Three Sons o' Guns is a 1941 American comedy film directed by Benjamin Stoloff and written by Fred Niblo, Jr..

chunks.title: Three Sons o' Guns
chunks.text: The film stars Wayne Morris, Marjorie Rambeau, Irene Rich, Tom Brown, William T. Orr, Susan Peters and Moroni Olsen.

chunks.title: Three Sons o' Guns

chunks.title: Jan Novák (composer)
chunks.text: Jan Novák (8 April 1921, Nová Říše – 11 November 1984, Neu Ulm) was a popular Czech composer of classical music.

chunks.title: Jan Novák (composer)
chunks.text: Novák was primarily active in the 1960s and composed the music for several films of Karel Kachyňa.

chunks.title: Jan Novák (composer)
chunks.text: Novák also composed music for the films of animators Jiří Trnka and Karel Zeman, the leading figures of the Czech animated film, as well as for "Wir" (1982, TV film) (based on "We", the 1921 Russian novel by Yevgeny Zamyatin).

chunks.title: Merrill Jenson
chunks.text: Merrill Boyd Jenson (born January 20, 1947) is an American composer and arranger who has composed film scores for over thirty films including , , The Testaments of One Fold and One Shepherd, , Harry's War, and Windwalker.

chunks.title: Merrill Jenson
chunks.text: Many of the films Jenson composed music for were directed by Academy Award-winning director Kieth Merrill.

chunks.title: Merrill Jenson
chunks.text: Jenson has also composed several concert productions including a symphony that premiered at Carnegie Hall.

chunks.title: Merrill Jenson
chunks.text: Additionally, he has composed music for many television commercials including the acclaimed Homefront ads, music for three outdoor pageants, and several albums.

chunks.title: Merrill Jenson
chunks.text: Jenson lives in Provo, Utah with his wife Betsy Lee Jenson.

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: Naoki Satō (佐藤 直紀 , Satō Naoki , born May 2, 1970 in Chiba, Japan) is a Japanese composer who has provided the music for several popular anime series including the first five "Pretty Cure" series, "X", "Eureka Seven", "Sword of the Stranger", and "Blood-C".

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: He graduated from the Tokyo College of Music in 1993.

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: At the 29th Japan Academy Prize in 2006, he won the Best Music prize for his work on the film "Always Sanchōme no Yūhi (Always Sunset on Third Street)".

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: He also composed music for anime films such as "Pretty Cure All Stars DX" trilogy, "Stand By Me Doraemon".

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: In live-action dramas, he provided music and soundtracks for TV dramas "Good Luck!!

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: " "Water Boys", "H2: Kimi to Ita Hibi" and "Ryōmaden".

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: He provided the music for the "Space Battleship Yamato" film, as well as the "Rurouni Kenshin" and "" live-action film series.

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: For the 38th Japan Academy Prize in 2015, he was nominated in the Best Score category for his work in "The Eternal Zero".

chunks.title: Naoki Satō
chunks.text: While he did not win the award, "The Eternal Zero" won several awards including Best Picture, and "Stand By Me Doraemon" won for Best Animated Film.

chunks.title: Dan Crow (musician)
chunks.text: Dan Crow is a performer of children's songs.

chunks.title: Dan Crow (musician)
chunks.text: He is best known for performing the theme song ("Walk Outside") of the movie "The Adventures of Milo and Otis", but also composed many Disney songs, most significantly for Winnie the Pooh and Dumbo.

chunks.title: Dan Crow (musician)
chunks.text: He also performed on a Baby Songs spinoff video, and regular appearances on children's educational channels like Noggin and The Learning Channel, as well as his own commercial video and audio recordings.

chunks.title: The Reluctant Dragon (1941 film)
chunks.text: The Reluctant Dragon is a 1941 American live action and animated film produced by Walt Disney, directed by Alfred Werker, and released by RKO Radio Pictures on June 20, 1941.

chunks.title: The Reluctant Dragon (1941 film)
chunks.text: Essentially a tour of the then-new Walt Disney Studios facility in Burbank, California, the film stars radio comedian Robert Benchley and many Disney staffers such as Ward Kimball, Fred Moore, Norman Ferguson, Clarence Nash, and Walt Disney, all as themselves.

chunks.title: Down on the Farm (1941 film)
chunks.text: Down on the Farm is a 1941 American short animated film directed by Tex Avery.

chunks.title: Down on the Farm (1941 film)
chunks.text: It was nominated for an Academy Award at the 14th Academy Awards for Best Short Subject (One-Reel).

chunks.title: Music of Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
chunks.text: The music for the 2013 action role-playing game "", developed and published by Square Enix, was composed by Masashi Hamauzu, Naoshi Mizuta, and Mitsuto Suzuki.

chunks.title: Music of Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
chunks.text: Hamauzu was the leader composer for "XIII" and "XIII-2", and Mizuta and Suzuki previously composed music for "XIII-2".

chunks.title: Music of Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
chunks.text: Musicians who had previously worked with the composers on "XIII-2" and "The 3rd Birthday" worked on the project in Japan, while the main soundtrack was performed and recorded in Boston by the Video Game Orchestra, conducted by Shota Nakama.

chunks.title: Music of Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
chunks.text: Along with including more percussion and ethnic elements, the soundtrack used "Blinded by Light", the main theme for main character Lightning, as a leitmotif.

chunks.title: Music of Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
chunks.text: Unlike the previous "XIII" games, the soundtrack did not include a theme song, as the composers felt it would detract from the emotional impact of the ending.

chunks.title: Sukhoi S-54
chunks.text: The Sukhoi S-54 is a series of three closely related aircraft proposals; the S-54 trainer aircraft, S-55 light fighter designed for export, and the S-56 carrier-capable light fighter.

chunks.title: Sukhoi S-54
chunks.text: All members of the family resemble the Sukhoi Su-27 in general form, or the Sukhoi Su-33 more closely, but built around a single example of the Saturn AL-31 engine instead of two, and scaled down accordingly to a smaller layout.

chunks.title: Sukhoi S-54
chunks.text: The design was offered to several potential customers, including South Africa and India, but was turned down.

chunks.title: Sukhoi S-54
chunks.text: Development is apparently on hold, awaiting a launch customer.

chunks.title: Levasseur PL.8
chunks.text: The Levasseur PL.8 was a single engine, two-seat long-distance record-breaking biplane aircraft modified from an existing Levasseur PL.4 carrier-based reconnaissance aircraft produced in France in the 1920s.

chunks.title: Levasseur PL.8
chunks.text: Levasseur built the aircraft in 1927, specifically for pilots Charles Nungesser and François Coli for a transatlantic attempt to win the Orteig Prize.

chunks.title: Levasseur PL.8
chunks.text: Only two examples of the type were built, with the first PL.8-01 named "L'Oiseau Blanc" (The White Bird), that gained fame as Nungesser and Coli's aircraft.

chunks.title: Loehle Spad XIII
chunks.text: The Loehle SPAD XIII is a family of American single-seat, biplane, conventional landing gear, single engine, ultralight aircraft produced in kit form by Loehle Aircraft for amateur construction.

chunks.title: Loehle Spad XIII
chunks.text: The aircraft meets the requirements of the US FAR 103 Ultralight Vehicles regulations when equipped with a lightweight engine.

chunks.title: Piper PA-32R
chunks.text: The Piper PA-32R is a six-seat, high-performance, single engine, all-metal fixed-wing aircraft produced by Piper Aircraft of Vero Beach, Florida.

chunks.title: Piper PA-32R
chunks.text: The design began life as the "Piper Lance", a retractable gear version of the Piper Cherokee Six.

chunks.title: Piper PA-32R
chunks.text: Later models became known by the designation "Piper Saratoga".

chunks.title: Piper PA-32R
chunks.text: The primary difference between the Lance and early Saratoga is the development of a tapered wing on the Saratoga, replacing the "Hershey Bar" wing on the Lance that was a carryover from the Cherokee Six.

chunks.title: Piper PA-32R
chunks.text: Later Saratoga models provided updated/improved avionics, engine and interior touches but retained the same airframe design.

chunks.title: Hawker Hunter
chunks.text: The Hawker Hunter is a transonic British jet-powered fighter aircraft that was developed by Hawker Aircraft for the Royal Air Force (RAF) during the late 1940s and early 1950s.

chunks.title: Hawker Hunter
chunks.text: It was designed to take advantage of the newly developed Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet engine and the swept wing, and was the first jet-powered aircraft produced by Hawker to be procured by the RAF.

chunks.title: Hawker Hunter
chunks.text: On 7 September 1953, the modified first prototype broke the world air speed record for aircraft, achieving a speed of 727.63 mph .

chunks.title: Chengdu J-10
chunks.text: The Chengdu J-10 ([[Simplified Chinese characters|simplified Chinese]]: 歼-10; [[Traditional Chinese characters|traditional Chinese]]: 殲-10; [[NATO reporting name]] : Firebird) is a lightweight [[multirole combat aircraft|multirole]] [[fighter aircraft]] capable of all-weather operation, configured with a [[delta wing]] and [[Canard (aeronautics)|canard]] design, with [[fly-by-wire]] flight controls, and produced by the [[People's Republic of China]]'s [[Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group|Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC)]] for the [[People's Liberation Army Air Force]] (PLAAF).

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: The Gotha G.VII.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: a.k.a.GL.VII, was a bomber aircraft produced in Germany during the final months of World War I.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: With the strategic bombing campaign effectively over, it was intended to be a high-speed tactical bomber with a secondary reconnaissance capability.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: It was a conventional two-bay biplane design with tractor-mounted engines, and a conventional empennage with twin fins and rudders.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: The bombardier's position in the nose of the aircraft that had featured on earlier Gotha designs was removed, and the nose of the aircraft severely truncated and fitted with a streamlined nose-cone.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: This allowed the engines to be located further inboard than on previous designs, bringing them closer to the aircraft's centreline and therefore minimising the effects of asymmetric thrust in the event of an engine failure.

chunks.title: Gotha G.VII
chunks.text: The engine nacelles also featured careful streamlining.

chunks.title: Saturn AL-31
chunks.text: The Saturn AL-31 is a family of military turbofan engines.

chunks.title: Saturn AL-31
chunks.text: It was developed by Lyulka, now NPO Saturn, of Soviet Union, originally for the Sukhoi Su-27 air superiority fighter.

chunks.title: Saturn AL-31
chunks.text: It produces a thrust of 123 kN (27,600 lb) with afterburning in the AL-31F, 137 kN (30,800 lb) in the AL-31FM (AL-35F) and 145 kN (32,000 lb) in the AL-37FU variants.

chunks.title: Saturn AL-31
chunks.text: Currently it powers all Su-27 derivatives and the Chengdu J-10 multirole jet fighter which has been developed by China.

chunks.title: Ayres Thrush
chunks.text: The Ayres Thrush, formerly the Snow S-2, Aero Commander Ag Commander, and Rockwell Thrush Commander, is an American agricultural aircraft produced by Ayres Corporation and more recently by Thrush Aircraft.

chunks.title: Ayres Thrush
chunks.text: It is one of the most successful and long-lived agricultural application aircraft types in the world, with almost 2,000 sold since the first example flew 61 years ago.

chunks.title: Ayres Thrush
chunks.text: Typical of agricultural aircraft, it is a single-seat monoplane of conventional taildragger configuration.

chunks.title: Ayres Thrush
chunks.text: Originally powered by a radial piston engine, most examples produced since the 1980s have been turboprop-powered.

chunks.title: Lavochkin La-9
chunks.text: The Lavochkin La-9 (NATO reporting name Fritz) was a Soviet fighter aircraft produced shortly after World War II.

chunks.title: Lavochkin La-9
chunks.text: It was a piston engined aircraft produced at the start of the jet age.

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: The Silver Jubilee Bridge, "Widnes-Runcorn Bridge" or Runcorn Bridge crosses the River Mersey and the Manchester Ship Canal at Runcorn Gap between Runcorn and Widnes in Halton, England.

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: It is a through arch bridge with a main arch span of 361 yards (330 m).

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: It was opened in 1961 as a replacement for the Widnes-Runcorn Transporter Bridge, and was initially known simply as the Runcorn Bridge or Runcorn–Widnes Bridge.

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: In 1975–77 it was widened, after which it was given its official name in honour of the Queen's Silver Jubilee.

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: It carries the A533 road and a cantilevered footway.

chunks.title: Silver Jubilee Bridge
chunks.text: The bridge is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II listed building.

chunks.title: River Mersey
chunks.text: The River Mersey is a river in the North West of England.

chunks.title: River Mersey
chunks.text: Its name is derived from the Anglo-Saxon language and translates as "boundary river".

chunks.title: River Mersey
chunks.text: The river may have been the border between the ancient kingdoms of Mercia and Northumbria and for centuries it formed part of the boundary between the historic counties of Lancashire and Cheshire.

chunks.title: Deschutes River (Washington)
chunks.text: The Deschutes River is a 50 mi river in Washington, United States.

chunks.title: Deschutes River (Washington)
chunks.text: Its source is in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest in Lewis County, and it empties into Budd Inlet of Puget Sound at Olympia in Thurston County.

chunks.title: Deschutes River (Washington)
chunks.text: It was given its name by French fur traders, who called it Rivière des Chutes, or "River of the Falls", a translation of the First Nations name for the site.

chunks.title: Deschutes River (Washington)
chunks.text: (The city of Tumwater, founded in the same location, takes its name from another translation for "waterfall", this one in Chinook Jargon.)

chunks.title: Catalyst Science Discovery Centre
chunks.text: The Catalyst Science Discovery Centre (originally known as The Museum of the Chemical Industry) is a science centre and museum focusing on chemistry and the history of the chemical industry.

chunks.title: Catalyst Science Discovery Centre
chunks.text: It is located near Spike Island in Widnes, Cheshire, and next to the River Mersey.

chunks.title: Catalyst Science Discovery Centre
chunks.text: The museum is accredited by the Arts Council England.

chunks.title: Fiddlers Ferry power station
chunks.text: Fiddlers Ferry Power Station is a coal fired power station located in Warrington, Cheshire, in North West England, which is capable of co-firing biomass.

chunks.title: Fiddlers Ferry power station
chunks.text: It is situated on the north bank of the River Mersey between the towns of Widnes and Warrington.

chunks.title: Fiddlers Ferry power station
chunks.text: Opened in 1971, the station has a generating capacity of 1,989 megawatts (MW).

chunks.title: Fiddlers Ferry power station
chunks.text: In a bid to combine efforts at the design and construction stages the Boiler and Turbo-generator plant were replicated at West Burton power station located between Retford and Gainsborough in North Nottinghamshire.

chunks.title: Mersey Gateway
chunks.text: The Mersey Gateway is a multi-million pound transport scheme between Runcorn and Widnes in Cheshire, England.

chunks.title: Mersey Gateway
chunks.text: The main part of the project is the construction of the "Mersey Gateway" toll bridge that will span the River Mersey and the Manchester Ship Canal.

chunks.title: Mersey Gateway
chunks.text: The crossing, which will have three traffic lanes in each direction, will be located approximately 1.5 km to the east of the existing Silver Jubilee Bridge.

chunks.title: Mersey Gateway
chunks.text: Apart from the new bridge, the project also includes major civil engineering work realigning the existing road network, constructing new interchanges and landscaping 9 km of highway.

chunks.title: Runcorn
chunks.text: Runcorn is an industrial town and cargo port in Cheshire, England, located within the Borough of Halton.

chunks.title: Runcorn
chunks.text: In 2010, Runcorn's population was estimated to be 61,000.

chunks.title: Runcorn
chunks.text: The town is on the southern bank of the River Mersey, where the estuary narrows to form the Runcorn Gap.

chunks.title: Runcorn
chunks.text: Directly to the north across the River Mersey is the town of Widnes.

chunks.title: Runcorn
chunks.text: Upstream and 8 mi to the northeast is the town of Warrington, and downstream 16 mi to the west is the city of Liverpool.

chunks.title: Listed buildings in Widnes
chunks.text: Widnes is an industrial town in the Borough of Halton, Cheshire, England, on the north bank of the River Mersey where it narrows at Runcorn Gap.

chunks.title: Listed buildings in Widnes
chunks.text: The town contains 21 buildings that are recorded in the National Heritage List for England as designated listed buildings. Of these, 5 are classified at Grade II*, and 16 at Grade II; Widnes has no Grade I listed buildings.

chunks.title: Listed buildings in Widnes
chunks.text: In the United Kingdom, the term "listed building" refers to a building or other structure officially designated as being of special architectural, historical, or cultural significance.

chunks.title: Listed buildings in Widnes
chunks.text: Listed buildings are categorised in three grades: Grade I consists of buildings of outstanding architectural or historical interest; Grade II* includes particularly significant buildings of more than local interest; Grade II consists of buildings of special architectural or historical interest.

chunks.title: Listed buildings in Widnes
chunks.text: Buildings in England are listed by the Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport on recommendations provided by English Heritage, which also determines the grading.

chunks.title: Lac qui Parle River
chunks.text: The Lac qui Parle River is a tributary of the Minnesota River, 118 miles (190 km) long, in southwestern Minnesota in the United States.

chunks.title: Lac qui Parle River
chunks.text: A number of tributaries of the river, including its largest, the West Branch Lac qui Parle River, also flow in eastern South Dakota.

chunks.title: Lac qui Parle River
chunks.text: Via the Minnesota River, the Lac qui Parle River is part of the watershed of the Mississippi River, draining an area of 1,156 sqmi in an agricultural region.

chunks.title: Lac qui Parle River
chunks.text: Slightly more than two-thirds of the Lac qui Parle watershed is in Minnesota.

chunks.title: Lac qui Parle River
chunks.text: "Lac qui parle" means "the lake which speaks" in the French language, and was a translation of the Sioux name for Lac qui Parle, a lake on the Minnesota River upstream of the mouth of the Lac qui Parle River.

chunks.title: Cuerdley railway station
chunks.text: One source gives Cuerdley railway station as being on what is now the southeastern edge of Widnes, England, stating that it was located near the then bone works which the 1849 OS Map shows as at the convergence of Moss Lane, the railway, the Sankey Canal, a creek and the north bank of the tidal River Mersey.

chunks.title: Cuerdley railway station
chunks.text: Of these only Moss Lane is no longer readily identifiable on a modern OS Map.

chunks.title: Cuerdley railway station
chunks.text: The authoritative "Disused Stations" website does not include an article on Cuerdley station, however, it does repeatedly use a map which places Cuerdley station some distance nearer Warrington.

chunks.title: Cuerdley railway station
chunks.text: This is corroborated by the Engineer's Line Reference (ELR) database which gives Cuerdley station as 1 mile 10 chains from Fiddlers Ferry and Penketh station and 1 mile 31 chains from Carterhouse Junction.

chunks.title: Cuerdley railway station
chunks.text: Furthermore, the ELR data gives the station site as only 31 chains west of the modern-day junction for Fiddlers Ferry Power station.

chunks.title: Paul H. Brown
chunks.text: Paul Brown "PB" (March 6, 1934 – May 6, 2016), was an American jazz bassist.

chunks.title: Paul H. Brown
chunks.text: He was the founder of the Monday Night Jazz Series in Hartford, Connecticut, which was recognized by the Library of Congress as the oldest and longest-running free festival for jazz in the United States and featured jazz greats such as Herbie Hancock, Ron Carter, Thelonious Monk, Tito Puente, Woody Shaw, Sun Ra, Bobby Hutcherson, Freddie Hubbard, and the "MJQ" Modern Jazz Quartet just to name a few.

chunks.title: Paul H. Brown
chunks.text: Brown also founded The Greater Hartford Festival of Jazz in 1992 to commemorate 25 years of the Monday night jazz series which in 2016, the Hartford Jazz Society renamed "Paul Brown Monday Night Jazz".

chunks.title: Paul H. Brown
chunks.text: He was co-founder of Hartford's Artists Collective, Inc.

chunks.title: Chocolate Williams
chunks.text: Chocolate Williams "(aka" Billy, "aka" Bob, "né" Robert Williams, Jr.; February 1, 1916 Augusta, Georgia – June 22, 1984, Manhattan, New York) was an American jazz bassist and vocalist based in New York City.

chunks.title: Chocolate Williams
chunks.text: He was a prolific performer of jazz, and, notably, performed and recorded with Art Tatum in 1941 and Herbie Nichols in 1952.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: Chris Bates is an American jazz bassist.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: He started studying upright bass in the 4th grade, and he attended the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: He studied with James Clute of the Minnesota Orchestra and jazz bassist Anthony Cox.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: Beyond his work with jazz, Bates performs in reggae, funk, country, folk and classical styles.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: He has performed with several notable musicians including Mose Allison, Lee Konitz, Joe Lovano, Steven Bernstein, Howard Levy, Ira Sullivan, Eric Alexander, Tim Sparks and Dean Magraw.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: Bates was a member of the Motion Poets, formed in 1993, which "released three albums to wide critical acclaim."

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: He received a McKnight Composers Fellowship for his compositions in 1999 and has performed on over 30 albums.

chunks.title: Chris Bates (musician)
chunks.text: Bates' first album as leader was released in 2012.

chunks.title: Michael Formanek
chunks.text: Michael Formanek (born May 7, 1958) is an American jazz bassist born in San Francisco, California and associated with the jazz scene in New York City.

chunks.title: Junjo
chunks.text: Junjo is the debut album by American bassist and vocalist Esperanza Spalding.

chunks.title: Junjo
chunks.text: It was released on 18 April 2006 on the Spanish label Ayva Music.

chunks.title: Junjo
chunks.text: The piano trio features pianist Aruán Ortiz, Francisco Mela on drums and then 22-year-old Spalding on upright bass, and providing vocals –often wordless– on all but two tracks.

chunks.title: Junjo
chunks.text: Besides compositions by Jimmy Rowles, Egberto Gismonti and Chick Corea the trio plays originals.

chunks.title: The Art of Conversation
chunks.text: The Art of Conversation is a studio album by English jazz bassist Dave Holland and American jazz pianist Kenny Barron.

chunks.title: The Art of Conversation
chunks.text: The record was released via the Impulse!

chunks.title: The Art of Conversation
chunks.text: Records label on October 14, 2014.

chunks.title: The Art of Conversation
chunks.text: The album contains 10 compositions: a mix of jazz standards and original tunes.

chunks.title: The Art of Conversation
chunks.text: The Jazz Journalists Association (JJA) recognized the record as the Record of the Year 2014.

chunks.title: Francisco Mela
