chunks.text: Francisco Jose Mela is a Cuban drummer and percussionist who has performed with a wide array of prominent international Latin and jazz artists including Kenny Barron, Gary Bartz, JoAnne Brackeen, Jane Bunnett, Regina Carter, Anat Cohen, Paquito D'Rivera, George Garzone, Larry Grenadier, Stefon Harris, Lionel Loueke, Joe Lovano, Jason Moran, John Patitucci, John Scofield, Esperanza Spalding, Mark Turner, McCoy Tyner, Chucho Valdés, Kenny Werner, and many others.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: Brian Bromberg (born December 5, 1960) is an American jazz bassist and record producer who performs on both electric and acoustic instruments.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: Though he tends to gravitate towards the genre of smooth jazz, Bromberg has released some straight-ahead jazz records in which he performs with a trio, and has even ventured into more rock-oriented jazz fusion territory as of late.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: His innovative and technically demanding style of playing extends to both electric and upright bass.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: On his acoustic bass albums, Bromberg performs jazzy interpretations of various pop and rock staples from the 1960s and '70s completely solo.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: Regarding his work with electric bass, Bromberg, among other bassists, helped popularize the piccolo bass, or bass with each string tuned an octave up, by releasing several albums in which he plays both the bass line and melody.

chunks.title: Brian Bromberg
chunks.text: For instance, upon first listen many will be surprised to learn that, although soaring guitar can be heard throughout the album, Bromberg's 2005 release "Metal" contains only Bromberg on two overdubbed basses, one of which is heavily effects-laden to make it sound like an electric guitar.

chunks.title: Esperanza Spalding
chunks.text: Esperanza Emily Spalding (born October 18, 1984) is an American jazz bassist and singer.

chunks.title: Esperanza Spalding
chunks.text: Spalding was raised in Portland, Oregon and was a musical prodigy, playing violin in the Chamber Music Society of Oregon at five years old.

chunks.title: Esperanza Spalding
chunks.text: She was later both self-taught and -trained on a number of instruments, including guitar and bass.

chunks.title: Esperanza Spalding
chunks.text: Her proficiency earned her scholarships to Portland State University and the Berklee College of Music.

chunks.title: Esperanza Spalding
chunks.text: In 2017 she was appointed Professor of the Practice of Music at Harvard University.

chunks.title: Bird Songs (Joe Lovano album)
chunks.text: Bird Songs is the 22nd album by Joe Lovano released via the Blue Note label in 2011.

chunks.title: Bird Songs (Joe Lovano album)
chunks.text: The album features Esperanza Spalding, James Weidman, Otis Brown III, and Francisco Mela performing songs mostly written or performed by iconoc jazz musician Charlie "Bird" Parker.

chunks.title: Thomas Fane, 6th Earl of Westmorland
chunks.text: Thomas Fane, 6th Earl of Westmorland {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (3 October 1681 – 4 June 1736), styled The Honourable Thomas Fane from 1691 to 1699, was a British peer and member of the House of Lords.

chunks.title: Thomas Fane, 6th Earl of Westmorland
chunks.text: He was the third son (second surviving son) of Vere Fane, 4th Earl of Westmorland and his wife Rachel Bence; as well as the younger brother of Vere Fane, and the older brother of John Fane, 7th Earl of Westmorland.

chunks.title: Thomas Fane, 6th Earl of Westmorland
chunks.text: As his older brother Vere died without issue in 1699, Thomas Fane inherited the Earldom of Westmorland, as well as his brother's further titles Baron Burghersh and Lord le Despencer.

chunks.title: Lucien Lazaridès
chunks.text: Lucien Lazaridès (Athens, Greece, 30 December 1922 — Cannes, 19 July 2005) was a French professional road bicycle racer.

chunks.title: Lucien Lazaridès
chunks.text: Lazaridès was born with Greek nationality but became French in 1929.

chunks.title: Lucien Lazaridès
chunks.text: Lucien Lazaridès was an older brother of cyclist Apo Lazaridès.

chunks.title: Lucien Lazaridès
chunks.text: Lazaridès won the Dauphiné Libéré in 1949 and reached the podium of the Tour de France in 1951.

chunks.title: Lucien Lazaridès
chunks.text: Later in his career he won two Tour de France stages.

chunks.title: Józef Mackiewicz
chunks.text: Józef Mackiewicz (April 1, 1902 – January 31, 1985) was a Polish writer, novelist and political commentator; best known for his documentary novels "Nie trzeba głośno mówić" (One Is Not Supposed to Speak Aloud), and "Droga donikąd" (The Road to Nowhere).

chunks.title: Józef Mackiewicz
chunks.text: He staunchly opposed communism, referring to himself as an "anticommunist by nationality".

chunks.title: Józef Mackiewicz
chunks.text: Mackiewicz died in exile.

chunks.title: Józef Mackiewicz
chunks.text: His older brother Stanisław Mackiewicz was also a writer.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: Los Debutantes is a 2003 Chilean film directed by Andres Waissbluth and starring Antonella Rios and Alejandro Trejo.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: It tells the story of two brothers from a small town, played by Nestor Castillana and Juan Pablo Miranda, who move to Santiago and visit a nightclub to celebrate the younger brother's 17th birthday.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: The older brother is subsequently offered a job by the club owner Don Pascual (played by Alejandro Trejo), and both brothers become friendly with Gracia, a dancer at the club who has dreams of becoming a singer (played by Antonella Rios).

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: The story is told in Rashomon style from three different perspectives: firstly from the perspective of the younger brother, secondly from the perspective of the older brother, and finally from the perspective of Gracia.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: The film was the Chilean submission for the 76th Academy Awards in the category Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film which took place in 2004, but was not one of the five nominated films.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: It was also nominated for the Goya Awards.

chunks.title: Los Debutantes
chunks.text: The film was released on DVD in the UK in 2005, and received a mildly critical review in Time Out.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: Infante Carlos of Spain (29 March 178810 March 1855) was an Infante of Spain and the second surviving son of King Charles IV of Spain and of his wife, Maria Luisa of Parma.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: As Carlos V, he was the first of the Carlist claimants to the throne of Spain.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: He is often referred to simply as 'Don Carlos'.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: He was a reactionary who was angry with liberalism in Spain and the assaults on the Catholic Church.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: He claimed the throne of Spain after the death of his older brother King Ferdinand VII in 1833.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: His claim was contested by liberal forces loyal to the dead king's infant daughter.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: The result was the bloody First Carlist War (1833–40).

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: Don Carlos had support from Basque provinces and much of Catalonia, but it was not enough, and he lost the war and never became king.

chunks.title: Infante Carlos, Count of Molina
chunks.text: His heirs continued the arch-conservative cause, fought two more "Carlist" wars and were active into the mid-20th century, but never obtained the throne.

chunks.title: Carlos Hasselbaink
chunks.text: Carlos Hasselbaink (born December 13, 1968 in Paramaribo, Suriname) is a former Dutch football (soccer) player.

chunks.title: Carlos Hasselbaink
chunks.text: He played as a striker for several Dutch clubs, including AZ Alkmaar, Telstar, VVV-Venlo, FC Utrecht and HFC Haarlem, before retiring in 2005.

chunks.title: Carlos Hasselbaink
chunks.text: He is the older brother of former Chelsea and Middlesbrough striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink.

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: Cody Votolato (born May 20, 1982) is a musician from Redmond, Washington, best known for being the guitarist in the post-hardcore band The Blood Brothers.

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: He grew up in the eastside suburbs of Seattle.

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: Cody attended Redmond High School with his bandmates in the late 1990s when the band originally formed, graduating Spring of 2000.

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: His accomplished thrashy and discordant style, exhibited in early Blood Brothers albums and in Head Wound City, has evolved into a more melodic and experimental sound in recent years .

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: Votolato's older brother Rocky Votolato is a folk musician and solo artist who played in the band Waxwing with his brother, as well as with Rudy Gajadhar, the older brother of The Blood Brothers' drummer Mark Gajadhar.

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: Votolato also contributed artwork to The Blood Brothers' album "...Burn, Piano Island, Burn".

chunks.title: Cody Votolato
chunks.text: On September 4, 2012, it was announced that Cody has joined Cold Cave as touring guitarist.

chunks.title: Emil Leeb
chunks.text: Emil Leeb (17 June 1881 – 8 September 1969) was a Bavarian-German general who saw active service during both World Wars.

chunks.title: Emil Leeb
chunks.text: His older brother, who became Field Marshal Wilhelm Ritter von Leeb, had the knightly rank of "Ritter" and the nobiliary particle of "von", not by birth, but thanks to the conferment of the Bavarian Military Order of Max Joseph and a patent of nobility.

chunks.title: Emil Leeb
chunks.text: Hence, the older brother had “von” between his names, but the younger brother did not.

chunks.title: Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink
chunks.text: Jerrel "Jimmy" Floyd Hasselbaink (born 27 March 1972) is a Dutch former professional footballer and current manager of EFL League One club Northampton Town.

chunks.title: John Michael McDonagh
chunks.text: John Michael McDonagh is a screenwriter and film director with British and Irish nationality.

chunks.title: John Michael McDonagh
chunks.text: He wrote and directed "The Guard" (2011) and "Calvary" (2014), both films starring Brendan Gleeson, receiving a BAFTA Award nomination for the former.

chunks.title: John Michael McDonagh
chunks.text: He was born in London in 1967.

chunks.title: John Michael McDonagh
chunks.text: He is the older brother of playwright and filmmaker Martin McDonagh.

chunks.title: Młyniska, Myślibórz County
chunks.text: Młyniska (formerly German "Mühlenfünftel") is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Dębno, within Myślibórz County, West Pomeranian Voivodeship, in north-western Poland.

chunks.title: Młyniska, Myślibórz County
chunks.text: It lies approximately 11 km south of Dębno, 35 km south of Myślibórz, and 87 km south of the regional capital Szczecin.

chunks.title: Tymawa, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: Tymawa (German "Thymau") is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Gniew, within Tczew County, Pomeranian Voivodeship, in northern Poland.

chunks.title: Tymawa, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: It lies approximately 5 km south of Gniew, 35 km south of Tczew, and 65 km south of the regional capital Gdańsk.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: Poljčane (] ) is a settlement in northeastern Slovenia.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: It is the centre of the Municipality of Poljčane.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: It lies 35 km south of Maribor and 35 km northeast of Celje.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: Traditionally the area was part of the Styria region.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: The town lies in the Dravinja Valley north of Mount Boč.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: It is a crossing of two important regional roads, the route from Maribor to Rogaška Slatina and the route from Celje to Ptuj.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: The railway line from Ljubljana to Maribor runs through the settlement, and the town has a railway station.

chunks.title: Poljčane
chunks.text: There are also a primary school, a health centre, a post office, two supermarkets, several small inns and bars, and some restaurants.

chunks.title: Cradock, South Australia
chunks.text: Cradock is a settlement 320 kilometres north of Adelaide on the Hawker to Orroroo Road in South Australia.

chunks.title: Cradock, South Australia
chunks.text: The nearest town with a greater population is Hawker which is approximately 20 km away with a population of around 360.

chunks.title: Cradock, South Australia
chunks.text: Cradock is in the Flinders Ranges Council area, the state Electoral district of Stuart and the federal Division of Grey.

chunks.title: Cradock, South Australia
chunks.text: The southern part of the locality is in the electoral district of Stuart and District Council of Orroroo Carrieton.

chunks.title: Penor, Pahang
chunks.text: Penor is a small town 35 km south of Kuantan town.

chunks.title: Penor, Pahang
chunks.text: Located near the Kuantan-Pekan district border, it is accessible by the Tanjung Lumpur Highway ( ).

chunks.title: Penor, Pahang
chunks.text: Penor houses the jail of Pahang, Penor Jail, which is Penor's landmark.

chunks.title: Penor, Pahang
chunks.text: Apart from the jail, Penor is famous among locals for its calm beach and also as a fishing spot.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Mawson
chunks.text: Mawson is an electoral district of the House of Assembly in the Australian state of South Australia.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Mawson
chunks.text: It covers most of the outer southern suburbs of the City of Onkaparinga, including Hackham, Hackham West, Huntfield Heights, Noarlunga Downs, Old Noarlunga, Onkaparinga Hills and Seaford Heights, the regional shopping centre area at Noarlunga Centre, parts of Woodcroft, and the southern wine region around McLaren Vale and Willunga.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: McLaren Vale is a wine region approximately 35 km south of Adelaide in South Australia.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: It is internationally renowned for the wines it produces.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: The region was named after either David McLaren, the Colonial Manager of the South Australia Company or John McLaren (unrelated) who surveyed the area in 1839.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: Among the first settlers to the region in late 1839, were two English farmers from Devon, William Colton and Charles Thomas Hewett.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: William Colton established the Daringa Farm and Charles Thomas Hewett established Oxenberry Farm.

chunks.title: McLaren Vale
chunks.text: Both men would be prominent in the early days of McLaren Vale.

chunks.title: Lipia Góra, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: Lipia Góra is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Morzeszczyn, within Tczew County, Pomeranian Voivodeship, in northern Poland.

chunks.title: Lipia Góra, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: It lies approximately 6 km south of Morzeszczyn, 35 km south of Tczew, and 65 km south of the regional capital Gdańsk.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Port Adelaide
chunks.text: Port Adelaide is an electoral district of the House of Assembly in the Australian state of South Australia.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Port Adelaide
chunks.text: Named after Port Adelaide because of its geographical location, it is a 91.3 km² urban electorate on Adelaide's Lefevre Peninsula and stretches east toward Adelaide's northern suburbs.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Port Adelaide
chunks.text: It contains a mix of seaside residential areas, wasteland and industrial regions.

chunks.title: Electoral district of Port Adelaide
chunks.text: Besides the bulk of the suburb of Port Adelaide, which is shared with Cheltenham, it includes the suburbs of Cavan, Dry Creek, Gillman, Globe Derby Park, Green Fields, Largs North, Mawson Lakes, North Haven, Osborne, Ottoway, Outer Harbor, Taperoo and Wingfield as well as parts of Gepps Cross, Pooraka and Rosewater.

chunks.title: Bielsk, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: Bielsk is a village in the administrative district of Gmina Morzeszczyn, within Tczew County, Pomeranian Voivodeship, in northern Poland.

chunks.title: Bielsk, Pomeranian Voivodeship
chunks.text: It lies approximately 6 km south of Morzeszczyn, 35 km south of Tczew, and 65 km south of the regional capital Gdańsk.

chunks.title: Jayanta Bhatta
chunks.text: Jayanta Bhatta (c. 9th Century CE) was a Kashmir poet and a philosopher of Nyaya school of Hindu philosophy.

chunks.title: Jayanta Bhatta
chunks.text: In his philosophical treatise "Nyayamanjari" and drama "Agamadambara", Jayanta mentions the king Shankaravarman (883 – 902 CE) as his contemporary.

chunks.title: Jayanta Bhatta
chunks.text: Also, his son Abhinanda in his "Kadambari-kathasara", mentioned that the great grandfather of Jayanta was a minister of King Lalitaditya of 8th century CE.

chunks.title: Jayanta Bhatta
chunks.text: So most probably Jayanta belonged to the last quarter of 9th Century CE.

chunks.title: Buddhist logic
chunks.text: Buddhist logic is a term used in Western scholarship to refer to Buddhist traditions of 'Hetuvidya' (Sanskrit) and 'Pramanavada' (Sanskrit), which arose circa 500,which in turn were influenced by 'Indian Logic', from which they seceded.

chunks.title: Buddhist logic
chunks.text: Indian logic, and Buddhist Logic—in main heralded by Dignāga (c. 480 - 540 CE)—are both primarily studies of 'inference'-patterns, where ‘inference’ is a gloss of anumāna (Sanskrit).

chunks.title: Dharmakirti
chunks.text: Dharmakīrti (fl.

chunks.title: Dharmakirti
chunks.text: c. 6th or 7th century) was an influential Indian Buddhist philosopher who worked at Nālandā.

chunks.title: Dharmakirti
chunks.text: He was one of the key scholars of epistemology (pramana) in Buddhist philosophy, and is associated with the Yogācāra and Sautrāntika schools.

chunks.title: Dharmakirti
chunks.text: He was also one of the primary theorists of Buddhist atomism.

chunks.title: Dharmakirti
chunks.text: His works influenced the scholars of Mīmāṃsā, Nyaya and Shaivism schools of Hindu philosophy as well as scholars of Jainism.

chunks.title: Udyotakara
chunks.text: Udyotakara (or Uddyotakara) (c. 6th century CE) was a philosopher of the Nyaya school of Indian philosophy.

chunks.title: Udyotakara
chunks.text: "Subandhu"’s "Vāsavadattā" mentioned him as the rescuer of the "Nyaya".

chunks.title: Udyotakara
chunks.text: He was a brahmin of "Bharadvaja" gotra and he belonged to the Pashupata sect.

chunks.title: Udyotakara
chunks.text: His philosophical treatise, the "Nyāyavārttika " was written to defend Vatsyayana's "Nyāyavāṣya " against the criticisms made by Dignaga.

chunks.title: Nyāya Sūtras
chunks.text: The Nyāya Sūtras is an ancient Indian Sanskrit text composed by Akṣapāda Gautama , and the foundational text of the Nyaya school of Hindu philosophy.

chunks.title: Nyāya Sūtras
chunks.text: The date when the text was composed, and the biography of its author is unknown, but variously estimated between 6th-century BCE and 2nd-century CE.

chunks.title: Nyāya Sūtras
chunks.text: The text may have been composed by more than one author, over a period of time.

chunks.title: Nyāya Sūtras
chunks.text: The text consists of five books, with two chapters in each book, with a cumulative total of 528 aphoristic sutras, about rules of reason, logic, epistemology and metaphysics.

chunks.title: Indian logic
chunks.text: The development of Indian logic dates back to the "anviksiki" of Medhatithi Gautama (c. 7th century BCE) the Sanskrit grammar rules of Pāṇini (c. 5th century BCE); the Vaisheshika school's analysis of atomism (c. 2nd century BCE); the analysis of inference by Gotama (c. 2nd century), founder of the Nyaya school of Hindu philosophy; and the tetralemma of Nagarjuna (c. 2nd century CE).

chunks.title: Indian logic
chunks.text: Indian logic stands as one of the three original traditions of logic, alongside the Greek and the Chinese logic.

chunks.title: Indian logic
chunks.text: The Indian tradition continued to develop through to early modern times, in the form of the Navya-Nyāya school of logic.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: Nabadwip ( ) is a city under Municipal administration in the district of Nadia in West Bengal, (India).

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: It is seated on the western bank of the Bhagirathi river.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: The Bhagirathi river originally flowed down the west of Nabadwip in the past, forming a natural boundary between the districts of Bardhaman and Nadia.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: With time it has shifted its course to where it is at present, cutting the city off from the rest of the Nadia district.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: It is considered to have been founded in 1063 AD, which served as the old capital of the Sena dynasty.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: It was a center of learning and philosophy in medieval India and is still noted for its traditional Sanskrit schools.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: The Navya Nyaya school of logic reached its peak with the efforts of some well known contemporary philosophers of Nabadwip.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: The great Vaishnava saint, social reformer and an important figure of the Bhakti movement, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486–1533) was born here, for whose sake, this place has turned into an important center of pilgrimage for the Vaishnavs world wide as well as the Hindoos in general.

chunks.title: Nabadwip
chunks.text: Many devotees who adhere to the Gaudiya sect of Vaishnavism come to Nabadwip for pilgrimage on the auspicious occasion of the Birthday celebration of Shri Mahaprabhu on the Phalguni Purnima (i.e. on the Full moon day of the March every year), and for various festivals in relation to Leelas of Shri Mahaprabhu like Sri Nabadwip-mandala Parikrama and other festivities like Dol yatra, Ras purnima Gaura-purnima.

chunks.title: Dignāga
chunks.text: Dignāga (c. 480 – c. 540 CE) was an Indian Buddhist scholar and one of the Buddhist founders of Indian logic ("hetu vidyā").

chunks.title: Dignāga
chunks.text: Dignāga's work laid the groundwork for the development of deductive logic in India and created the first system of Buddhist logic and epistemology (Pramana).

chunks.title: Dignāga
chunks.text: According to Georges B Dreyfus, his philosophical school brought about an Indian "epistemological turn" and became the "standard formulation of Buddhist logic and epistemology in India and Tibet."

chunks.title: Dignāga
chunks.text: Dignāga's thought influenced later Buddhist philosophers like Dharmakirti and also Hindu thinkers of the Nyaya school.

chunks.title: Dignāga
chunks.text: Dignāga's epistemology accepted only "perception" (pratyaksa) and "inference" (anumāṇa) are valid instruments of knowledge.

chunks.title: List of Hindu texts
chunks.text: Hinduism is an ancient religion with diverse traditions such as Vaishnavism, Shaivism, Shaktism and others.

chunks.title: List of Hindu texts
chunks.text: Each tradition has a long list of Hindu texts, with subgenre based on syncretization of ideas from Samkhya, Nyaya, Yoga, Vedanta and other schools of Hindu philosophy.

chunks.title: List of Hindu texts
chunks.text: Of these some called "Sruti" are broadly considered as core scriptures of Hinduism, but beyond the "Sruti", the list of scriptures vary by the scholar.

chunks.title: Hindu philosophy
chunks.text: Hindu philosophy refers to a group of "darśanas" (philosophies, world views, teachings) that emerged in ancient India.

chunks.title: Hindu philosophy
chunks.text: The mainstream ancient Indian philosophy includes six systems ("ṣaḍdarśana") – Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa and Vedanta.

chunks.title: Hindu philosophy
chunks.text: These are also called the Astika (orthodox) philosophical traditions and are those that accept the Vedas as authoritative, important source of knowledge.

chunks.title: Hindu philosophy
chunks.text: Ancient and medieval India was also the source of philosophies that share philosophical concepts but rejected the Vedas, and these have been called "nāstika" (heterodox or non-orthodox) Indian philosophies.

chunks.title: Hindu philosophy
chunks.text: Nāstika Indian philosophies include Buddhism, Jainism, Cārvāka, Ājīvika, and others.

chunks.title: Mark Hunt (politician)
chunks.text: Mark Allen Hunt (born January 23, 1960 in Charleston, West Virginia) is an American politician and a Democratic member of the West Virginia House of Delegates representing District 36 since January 12, 2013.

chunks.title: Mark Hunt (politician)
chunks.text: Hunt served consecutively from January 2009 until January 2013, and non-consecutively from January 1995 until January 2001 and from January 2005 until January 2007 in District 30 and District 31 seats.

chunks.title: Mark Hunt (politician)
chunks.text: Hunt was a candidate for West Virginia Senate in 2000 and a candidate for the United States House of Representatives for West Virginia's 2nd congressional district in 2006.

chunks.title: Alexander Acosta
chunks.text: Rene Alexander Acosta (born January 16, 1969) is an American attorney, academic, and politician who is the 27th and current United States Secretary of Labor.

chunks.title: Alexander Acosta
chunks.text: A Republican, he was appointed by President George W. Bush to the National Labor Relations Board and later served as Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights and federal prosecutor for the Southern District of Florida.

chunks.title: Alexander Acosta
chunks.text: On , President Donald Trump nominated Acosta to be United States Secretary of Labor.

chunks.title: Alexander Acosta
chunks.text: Acosta is the first and only Hispanic member of Trump's cabinet so far.

chunks.title: Alexander Acosta
chunks.text: He is the former dean of Florida International University College of Law.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: Jennifer Hunt is a Professor of Economics at Rutgers University.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: She previously served as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Microeconomic Analysis at the U.S. Department of the Treasury after serving a term as Chief Economist to the U.S. Secretary of Labor, serving under Acting Secretary Seth Harris and Secretary Thomas Perez.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: She is a Research Associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: She has done research in the areas of employment and unemployment policy, immigration, wage inequality, transition economics, crime and corruption.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: Her current research focuses on immigration and innovation in the United States, the U.S. science and engineering workforce, and the 2008-2009 recession in Germany.

chunks.title: Jennifer Hunt
chunks.text: Her research on immigration has been cited by media in the context of immigration reform legislation, currently under consideration by the U.S. Congress.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: Vilma Rose Hunt (November 15, 1926 – December 29, 2012) was a scientist noted for research into radiation and workplace safety for women.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: After beginning a dentistry career in Australia and New Zealand, Hunt traveled to the United States where she earned her A.M. in Physical Anthropology at Radcliffe College and began researching public health and radiation biology.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: In 1964, Hunt discovered that polonium 210 is a natural contaminant of tobacco, providing additional evidence for the link between smoking and bronchial cancer.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: In 1974, she wrote a 121-page report on workplace hazards for pregnant women, which made the front page of the "New York Times".

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: She published a book, Work and the Health of Women, in 1979.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: From 1979 to 1981, Hunt served as an administrator for the United States Environmental Protection Agency, enacting public health solutions to environmental contamination at sites like Love Canal, New York, and Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station, Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Vilma Rose Hunt
chunks.text: Hunt retired in Gloucester in 1985, though she served as an environmental consultant and visiting lecturer until her death.

chunks.title: Dave Hunt (Oregon politician)
chunks.text: Dave Hunt (born November 10, 1967) is an American politician in the state of Oregon.

chunks.title: Dave Hunt (Oregon politician)
chunks.text: A Democrat, he was the Oregon House Speaker and served as State Representative for District 40 of the Oregon House of Representatives representing Clackamas County from 2003 to 2013.

chunks.title: Dave Hunt (Oregon politician)
chunks.text: He was elected House Majority Leader for the 2007–2009 session, succeeding Minority Leader Jeff Merkley, who was chosen as Speaker.

chunks.title: Dave Hunt (Oregon politician)
chunks.text: Hunt served as Speaker during the 2009–2011 session, again succeeding Merkley, who was elected to serve in the United States Senate.

chunks.title: Dave Hunt (Oregon politician)
chunks.text: After his service in the House, Hunt ran for Clackamas County Chair, but ultimately lost.

chunks.title: Edward C. Hugler
chunks.text: Edward Charles "Ed" Hugler (born February 7, 1950) is Deputy Assistant Secretary for Operations in the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration and Management.

chunks.title: Edward C. Hugler
chunks.text: That position has been his formal position at the United States Department of Labor since April 2000.

chunks.title: Edward C. Hugler
chunks.text: However, he served as Acting Secretary of Labor from February 2–24, 2009, when Hilda Solis's nomination by President Barack Obama became bogged down during Senate confirmation hearings.

chunks.title: Edward C. Hugler
chunks.text: He stepped down from the position when Solis was confirmed and sworn in as Secretary of Labor.

chunks.title: Edward C. Hugler
chunks.text: Ed Hugler served as Acting Secretary of Labor from January 20, 2017 to April 28, 2017 until when Alexander Acosta was confirmed and sworn into office.

chunks.title: Charles A. Hunt
chunks.text: Charles A. Hunt served in the California legislature and during World War I he served in the United States Army.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Seth D. Harris (born October 12, 1962) was the 11th United States Deputy Secretary of Labor, and served for six months as the Acting U.S. Secretary of Labor and a member of President Barack Obama's Cabinet.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Nominated by President Obama in February 2009, Harris was unanimously confirmed by the U.S. Senate in May 2009, and became acting Secretary of Labor following the resignation of Hilda Solis in January 2013.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Harris was also a member of the Overseas Private Investment Corporation's Board of Directors.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Harris stepped down from his post on January 16, 2014.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Since leaving the Obama Administration, Harris has been a Distinguished Scholar at Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations, and Counsel in the Public Policy & Regulation and Employment & Labor practices of Dentons, a global law firm, before establishing his own law office.

chunks.title: Seth Harris
chunks.text: Harris is also a member of the United Cerebral Palsy Association's Board of Directors.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: W.A "Walt" Barrows is the current Labor Member of the United States Railroad Retirement Board.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: He was nominated by President Barack Obama on February 28, 2011 and was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on September 26, 2011.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: He replaced outgoing board member V.M. "Butch" Speakman, who announced his retirement in 2010.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: The appointment of Barrows to the Board was supported by a number of labor organizations, including the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen, as well as the Transportation Trades Department.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: Barrows has had a long career in the railroad industry, beginning with Norfolk and Southern Railroad in 1974.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: He has held numerous positions with Locals 199 and 228, including Local Chairman, Local President, and Recording-Financial Secretary.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: Most recently, Barrows served as the International Secretary-Treasurer for the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: In addition, he has served as a labor member on the joint healthcare subcommittee, which oversees the Railroad Employee's National Health and Welfare Plan.

chunks.title: W.A. Barrows
chunks.text: In 2004, 2007, and 2010, Barrows served as labor trustee, responsible for oversight of the National Railroad Retirement Trust Fund.

chunks.title: United States Deputy Secretary of Labor
chunks.text: The United States Deputy Secretary of Labor is the second-highest-ranking official in the United States Department of Labor.

chunks.title: United States Deputy Secretary of Labor
chunks.text: In the United States federal government, the Deputy Secretary oversees the day-to-day operation of the Department of Labor, and may act as Secretary of Labor during the absence of the Secretary.

chunks.title: United States Deputy Secretary of Labor
chunks.text: The Deputy Secretary is appointed by the President of the United States with the advice and consent of the United States Senate and the United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: The discography of DNCE, an American band, consists of one studio album, one extended play, five singles (including one as a featured artist) and other album appearances.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: The group released their debut single, "Cake by the Ocean", on September 18, 2015.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: Though starting out slow, the song went on to become a success in numerous territories.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: The song has so far peaked at number 9 on the "Billboard" Hot 100, and at number 7 on the Canadian Hot 100.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: The group released their debut extended play, "Swaay", on October 23, 2015.

chunks.title: DNCE discography
chunks.text: The four-track album received a generally positive critical reception upon its release, with "Entertainment Weekly" writing that it "splits the difference between [Joe's] former band’s slick power pop and the electro-kissed pop stylings of his solo album."

chunks.title: Ænima
chunks.text: Ænima ("ON-ima") is the second studio album by American rock band Tool.

chunks.title: Ænima
chunks.text: It was released in vinyl format on September 17, 1996, and in compact disc format on October 1, 1996, through Zoo Entertainment.

chunks.title: Ænima
chunks.text: The album was recorded and cut at Ocean Way, Hollywood and The Hook, North Hollywood from 1995 to 1996.

chunks.title: Ænima
chunks.text: The album was produced by David Bottrill.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: This is a comprehensive list of the awards received by 2NE1, a girl group formed by YG Entertainment in South Korea.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: Their first extended play, "2NE1" (2009), was received well and spawned the hits "Fire" and "I Don't Care", one of the biggest singles of 2009.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: It earned 2NE1 many awards and nominations.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: After initial success in 2009, the group released their first full-length album in 2010, "To Anyone". "

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: Clap Your Hands", "Go Away", and "Can't Nobody" were used as promotional singles.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: In 2011, they came back with the second EP, "2NE1" (2011), which earned 2NE1 many awards and nominations, including Album of the Year, and Song of the Year for the lead single "I Am the Best".

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: They released four singles in 2012 to 2013, including the hits "I Love You" and "Missing You", and released their first full-album in Japan.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: They released their second full Korean album "Crush" in 2014 with the lead single "Come Back Home", and entered the Billboard 200 chart.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by 2NE1
chunks.text: In January 2017, they released a farewell song called "Goodbye" for their fans after the announce of their disbandment.

chunks.title: All I Really Want (Alanis Morissette song)
chunks.text: "All I Really Want" is a song written by Alanis Morissette and Glen Ballard, and produced by Ballard for Morissette's third album, "Jagged Little Pill" (1995).

chunks.title: All I Really Want (Alanis Morissette song)
chunks.text: In the United States it was released as the album's third single in 1995 (see 1995 in music), and outside the U.S. it was released as the album's sixth and final single in 1996 (see 1996 in music).

chunks.title: All I Really Want (Alanis Morissette song)
chunks.text: The song was one of the first written for "Jagged Little Pill" and originated from a song called "The Bottom Line", which was the first song Morissette wrote with Glen Ballard.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: Group Hepsi, commonly known as Hepsi, are a famous Turkish R&B band.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: They consist of "Eren Bakıcı", "Cemre Kemer" and "Yasemin Yürük", and formerly of "Gülçin Ergül", 2009, all the members of the group are from the city of Istanbul.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: The group rose to fame in the year 2005 with their debut album "Bir", which spawned the hit songs "Olmaz Oğlan", "Üç Kalp", and "Herşeye Rağmen", and the hugely successful song "Yalan".

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: They later went on to release their first official EP, "Tempo", in association with Pepsi, and worked with Turkish Pop legend Sezen Aksu, famous for working with Tarkan.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: In 2006 they also released their second studio album, "Hepsi 2", which spawned the huge hit "Kalpsizsin", and Aşk Sakızı.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: The group released their third studio album on 24 May 2008 called "Şaka" meaning "Joke" in English.

chunks.title: Hepsi
chunks.text: The group released their first single for this album on 23 May 2008, called "4 Peynirli Pizza" meaning "4 cheese pizza".

chunks.title: Stinkfist
chunks.text: "Stinkfist" is a song by the American rock band Tool.

chunks.title: Stinkfist
chunks.text: It is their first industry single and first music video release from their third major label album "Ænima".

chunks.title: Candles (song)
chunks.text: "Candles" is a song recorded by American pop punk band Hey Monday.

chunks.title: Candles (song)
chunks.text: The song was first included on the group's debut album, "Hold On Tight" (2008).

chunks.title: Candles (song)
chunks.text: While working on their scrapped second studio album, the band re-recorded the song; this new version was released on February 8, 2011 as the "Candles EP", along with an acoustic demo of the song and a previously-unreleased song called "The One That Got Away".

chunks.title: Candles (song)
chunks.text: A music video for the song debuted March 9, 2011 on Just Jared.

chunks.title: Candles (song)
chunks.text: "Candles" was the last single released by the group before they went on hiatus for Cassadee Pope to pursue her solo career.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: The Prize Fighter Inferno is an acoustic/electronica solo project of Claudio Sanchez, the lead singer and lead/rhythm guitarist for the band Coheed and Cambria.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: The first album, called "My Brother's Blood Machine" was released on October 31, 2006 through indie label Equal Vision Records.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: According to "My Brother's Blood Machine" liner notes, Claudio recorded the album over a period of seven years with "...random recording devices...".

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: As of August 2009, Sanchez has been reportedly working on a follow up album to 2006's "My Brother's Blood Machine" releasing updates of the album's status on his Twitter account every few months.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: On September 25, 2009, A new song called "Gears" was introduced in the trailer of Claudio's comic series Kill Audio.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: The song was released on 7" vinyl along with another song called "Erizo Schultz" in February 2010.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: The vinyl credits both Claudio Sanchez and his wife Chondra Echert as "The Prize Fighter Inferno".

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: An EP was release for New York Comic Con 2012 titled "Half Measures" with tracks, Elm Street Lover Boy, Simple Fix, Pistol Pete Matty, and Half Measures.

chunks.title: The Prize Fighter Inferno
chunks.text: On Record Store Day, the EP is set to release as a Glow in the Dark vinyl, along with Big Beige Demos in a coke-bottle clear vinyl, and Davenport Cabinet's EP in a blue vinyl.

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: 702 (pronounced ""Seven-Oh-Two""), named after the area code of their hometown of Las Vegas, Nevada, was an American platinum-selling trio, with the final and most known line up consisting of: Kameelah Williams, Irish and LeMisha Grinstead.

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: The group was originally a quartet with three sisters, twins Irish and Orish Grinstead (born June 2, 1980), LeMisha 'Misha' Grinstead (born June 10, 1978) and their cousin Amelia Childs whom featured on Subway's hit single "This Lil' Game We Play".

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: After the exit of Amelia, friend Kameelah Williams joint the group signing with Motown records recording songs such as "Steelo" and "Get It Together".

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: Orish Grinstead (twin sister of Irish) then left the group even though vocals on the first released album "No Doubt" in 1996 which sold 500,000 copies in the United States.

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: In 1999 the trio released the most associated 702 song called "Where My Girls At?

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: " on the album "702" which gained a high level of success for the group selling 1,000,000 copies in the United States.

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: Lead singer Kameelah then left the group in 2001 and was then replaced by Cree La'More.

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: Even though the new line-up released a single called "Pootie Tang" for the "Pootie Tang" soundtrack, Kameelah returned and replaced La'More, and released the album "Star" which is mostly remembered for the single "I Still Love You".

chunks.title: 702 (group)
chunks.text: The group then disbanded in 2006.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Secret
chunks.text: Secret is a four-member South Korean girl group formed by TS Entertainment in 2009.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Secret
chunks.text: Secret debuted with the song "I Want You Back" on October 13, 2009.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Secret
chunks.text: In 2010, the group released their hit single "Magic" which was nominated at the 12th Mnet Asian Music Awards for "Best Dance Performance by a Female Group".

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Secret
chunks.text: The same year, the group released their number one hit single "Madonna" which won them a "Bonsang" award at the 20th Seoul Music Awards.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Secret
chunks.text: With the success of "Magic" and "Madonna", the group received the "Newcomer award" at the 25th Golden Disk Awards.

chunks.title: Moment distribution method
chunks.text: The moment distribution method is a structural analysis method for statically indeterminate beams and frames developed by Hardy Cross.

chunks.title: Moment distribution method
chunks.text: It was published in 1930 in an ASCE journal.

chunks.title: Moment distribution method
chunks.text: The method only accounts for flexural effects and ignores axial and shear effects.

chunks.title: Moment distribution method
chunks.text: From the 1930s until computers began to be widely used in the design and analysis of structures, the moment distribution method was the most widely practiced method.

chunks.title: Fault tree analysis
chunks.text: Fault tree analysis (FTA) is a top down, deductive failure analysis in which an undesired state of a system is analyzed using Boolean logic to combine a series of lower-level events.

chunks.title: Fault tree analysis
chunks.text: This analysis method is mainly used in the fields of safety engineering and reliability engineering to understand how systems can fail, to identify the best ways to reduce risk or to determine (or get a feeling for) event rates of a safety accident or a particular system level (functional) failure.

chunks.title: Fault tree analysis
chunks.text: FTA is used in the aerospace, nuclear power, chemical and process, pharmaceutical, petrochemical and other high-hazard industries; but is also used in fields as diverse as risk factor identification relating to social service system failure.

chunks.title: Fault tree analysis
chunks.text: FTA is also used in software engineering for debugging purposes and is closely related to cause-elimination technique used to detect bugs.

chunks.title: Software architecture analysis method
chunks.text: Software architecture analysis method (SAAM) is a method used in software architecture to evaluate a system architecture.

chunks.title: Software architecture analysis method
chunks.text: It was the first documented software architecture analysis method, and was developed in the mid 1990s to analyze a system for modifiability, but it is useful for testing any non-functional aspect.

chunks.title: Optimal matching
chunks.text: Optimal matching is a sequence analysis method used in social science, to assess the dissimilarity of ordered arrays of tokens that usually represent a time-ordered sequence of socio-economic states two individuals have experienced.

chunks.title: Optimal matching
chunks.text: Once such distances have been calculated for a set of observations (e.g. individuals in a cohort) classical tools (such as cluster analysis) can be used.

chunks.title: Optimal matching
chunks.text: The method was tailored to social sciences from a technique originally introduced to study molecular biology (protein or genetic) sequences (see sequence alignment).

chunks.title: Optimal matching
chunks.text: Optimal matching uses the Needleman-Wunsch algorithm.

chunks.title: Homotopy analysis method
chunks.text: The homotopy analysis method (HAM) is a semi-analytical technique to solve nonlinear ordinary/partial differential equations.

chunks.title: Homotopy analysis method
chunks.text: The homotopy analysis method employs the concept of the homotopy from topology to generate a convergent series solution for nonlinear systems.

chunks.title: Homotopy analysis method
chunks.text: This is enabled by utilizing a homotopy-Maclaurin series to deal with the nonlinearities in the system.

chunks.title: Liao Shijun
chunks.text: Liao Shijun (; born September 15, 1963) is a fluid mechanics and applied mathematics expert working in homotopy analysis method (HAM), nonlinear waves, nonlinear dynamics, and applied mathematics.

chunks.title: Liao Shijun
chunks.text: He was born in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China.

chunks.title: Liao Shijun
chunks.text: Professor Liao works at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

chunks.title: Taylor series
chunks.text: In mathematics, a Taylor series is a representation of a function as an infinite sum of terms that are calculated from the values of the function's derivatives at a single point.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: Weighted correlation network analysis, also known as weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), is a widely used data mining method especially for studying biological networks based on pairwise correlations between variables.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: While it can be applied to most high-dimensional data sets, it has been most widely used in genomic applications.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: It allows one to define modules (clusters), intramodular hubs, and network nodes with regard to module membership, to study the relationships between co-expression modules, and to compare the network topology of different networks (differential network analysis).

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: WGCNA can be used as data reduction technique (related to oblique factor analysis ), as clustering method (fuzzy clustering), as feature selection method (e.g. as gene screening method), as framework for integrating complementary (genomic) data (based on weighted correlations between quantitative variables), and as data exploratory technique.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: Although WGCNA incorporates traditional data exploratory techniques, its intuitive network language and analysis framework transcend any standard analysis technique.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: Since it uses network methodology and is well suited for integrating complementary genomic data sets, it can be interpreted as systems biologic or systems genetic data analysis method.

chunks.title: Weighted correlation network analysis
chunks.text: By selecting intramodular hubs in consensus modules, WGCNA also gives rise to network based meta analysis techniques

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: In mathematics, specifically in homotopy theory, a classifying space "BG" of a topological group "G" is the quotient of a weakly contractible space "EG" (i.e. a topological space for which all its homotopy groups are trivial) by a proper free action of "G".

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: It has the property that any "G" principal bundle over a paracompact manifold is isomorphic to a pullback of the principal bundle "EG" → "BG".

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: As explained later, this means that classifying spaces represent a set-valued functor on the homotopy category of topological spaces.

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: The term classifying space can also be used for spaces that represent a set-valued functor on the category of topological spaces, such as Sierpiński space.

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: This notion is generalized by the notion of classifying topos.

chunks.title: Classifying space
chunks.text: However, the rest of this article discusses the more commonly used notion of classifying space up to homotopy.

chunks.title: Newmark's sliding block
chunks.text: The Newmark's sliding block analysis method is an engineering method used to calculate the permanent displacements of soil slopes (also embankments and dams) during seismic loading.

chunks.title: Newmark's sliding block
chunks.text: It is also simply called Newmark's analysis or Sliding block method of slope stability analysis.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: Green Lantern Coaster is a steel roller coaster at Warner Bros.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: Movie World on the Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: The ride is themed after DC Comics' Green Lantern and is located within the park's DC Comics superhero hub.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: The ride is an El Loco roller coaster manufactured by S&S Worldwide, characterised by a tight circuit featuring a beyond-vertical drop and an outward banked turn.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: It holds the record for the steepest drop of any roller coaster in the Southern Hemisphere, and the second steepest in the world.

chunks.title: Green Lantern Coaster
chunks.text: "Green Lantern Coaster" officially opened on 23 December 2011.

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: The Riddler's Revenge is a stand-up roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain.

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: Manufactured by Bolliger & Mabillard, the ride opened in 1998 as the park's eleventh roller coaster, setting world records among stand-up coasters for height, speed, drop length, track length and number of inversions.

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: The previous record holder was Chang at Six Flags Kentucky Kingdom which opened a year earlier.

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: Located in the Movie Town area of the park, The Riddler's Revenge was also the park's single biggest investment at a cost of $14 million.

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: It stands 156 ft tall and features a top speed of 65 mph .

chunks.title: The Riddler's Revenge
chunks.text: The 4370 ft coaster also features six inversions and a ride duration of approximately three minutes.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (Six Flags Great Adventure)
chunks.text: Green Lantern is a steel stand-up roller coaster located at Six Flags Great Adventure in Jackson Township, New Jersey.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (Six Flags Great Adventure)
chunks.text: "Green Lantern" stands 155 ft tall and features a top speed of 63 mph .

chunks.title: Green Lantern (Six Flags Great Adventure)
chunks.text: The 4155 ft ride features five inversions and a duration of approximately 2⁄ minutes.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (Six Flags Great Adventure)
chunks.text: The ride was manufactured by Swiss firm Bolliger & Mabillard.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (Six Flags Great Adventure)
chunks.text: Green Lantern is fairly similar to the former Mantis, stand-up coaster at Cedar Point, but is taller, faster, and features one more inversion.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: King Cobra (1984–2001) was a TOGO Stand-up roller coaster located at Kings Island in Mason, Ohio.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: It was the first in the world to be designed from the ground up as a stand-up roller coaster.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Other stand-up roller coasters that preceded King Cobra were sit-down models later modified to accommodate stand-up trains.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: After the ride's manufacturer, TOGO, went out of business in 2001, parts for the ride became more expensive and harder to find.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: In addition, the ride was losing popularity in recent years.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: So in April 2002, Paramount Parks decided to dismantle King Cobra and put it up for sale.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Trains were sent to Kings Island's "graveyard" located at the old Wild Animal Habitat feeding house area next to the Son of Beast.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: After the ride wouldn't sell, the decision was made in 2008 to transfer some of the ride including the trains to Kings Dominion to be used as spare parts for Shockwave.

chunks.title: King Cobra (roller coaster)
chunks.text: As of 2010, remnants of the King Cobra can still be spotted in some back areas of Kings Island near Flight of Fear

chunks.title: Green Lantern (comic book)
chunks.text: Green Lantern is an ongoing American comic book series featuring the DC Comics heroes of the same name.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (comic book)
chunks.text: The character's first incarnation, Alan Scott, appeared in "All-American Comics" #16 (July 1940), and was later spun off into the first volume of "Green Lantern" in 1941.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (comic book)
chunks.text: That series was canceled in 1949 after 38 issues.

chunks.title: Green Lantern (comic book)
chunks.text: When the Silver Age Green Lantern, Hal Jordan, was introduced, the character starred in a new volume of "Green Lantern" starting in 1960 and has been the lead protagonist of the Green Lantern mythos for the majority of the last fifty years.

chunks.title: Katun (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Katun is a steel inverted roller coaster at the Mirabilandia Amusement Park, Savio, outside Ravenna, Italy.

chunks.title: Katun (roller coaster)
chunks.text: It's the longest inverted roller coaster in Europe.

chunks.title: Katun (roller coaster)
chunks.text: The coaster stands 164 ft tall making it the world's fourth tallest complete circuit inverted coaster, has a track length of 3937 ft , a top speed of 65 mph and six inversions:

chunks.title: Freestyle (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Freestyle is a stand-up roller coaster operating at Cavallino Matto in Tuscany, Italy.

chunks.title: Freestyle (roller coaster)
chunks.text: It opened as the park's fifth roller coaster on 18 July 2015.

chunks.title: Freestyle (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Freestyle originally opened at Canada's Wonderland in 1985 as SkyRider and closed in 2014.

chunks.title: Freestyle (roller coaster)
chunks.text: Built by TOGO, it was the second stand-up roller coaster from the company following the now-defunct King Cobra, which opened the previous year at Kings Island.

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: Extremeroller was a steel stand-up roller coaster at Worlds of Fun in Kansas City, Missouri.

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: It was built by Arrow Dynamics and the first stand-up roller coaster in the United States.

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: It was built in 1976 under the name Screamroller.

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: In 1983, Arrow designed a stand-up train for the attraction, which was subsequently renamed Extremeroller (also known as EXT).

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: However, the original sit-down trains were reinstalled in 1984, remaining in place until the attraction was removed in 1988 and replaced by Timber Wolf that opened in 1989.

chunks.title: Extremeroller
chunks.text: In 1990 extremeroller was relocated to Formosa WonderWorld in Taipei Taiwan under as "spiral" which standing until end of 2006 the attraction have been removed and it is unknown if it its being scrapped or in storage somewhere.

chunks.title: Apocalypse (Six Flags America)
chunks.text: Apocalypse is a steel stand-up roller coaster located at Six Flags America in Prince George's County, Maryland.

chunks.title: Apocalypse (Six Flags America)
chunks.text: The ride made its debut in 1990 as Iron Wolf at Six Flags Great America before being relocated to Six Flags America and renamed to Apocalypse.

chunks.title: Apocalypse (Six Flags America)
chunks.text: The roller coaster was the first built by Swiss manufacturer Bolliger & Mabillard.

chunks.title: Apocalypse (Six Flags America)
chunks.text: When known as Iron Wolf, the roller coaster held the records of the highest (100 ft ) and fastest (55 mph ) stand-up looping roller coaster in the world before losing them to other roller coasters in 1992 and 1996.

chunks.title: White Cyclone
chunks.text: White Cyclone (ホワイトサイクロン , Howaito Saikuron ) is a wooden roller coaster at Nagashima Spa Land in Mie Prefecture, Japan.

chunks.title: White Cyclone
chunks.text: At 1700 m in length, White Cyclone is the third longest wooden roller coaster in the world, and is the longest wooden roller coaster outside of the United States.

chunks.title: White Cyclone
chunks.text: Despite its length, White Cyclone is still considerably shorter than the 2479 m Steel Dragon 2000, the world's longest steel roller coaster, which is also at Nagashima Spa Land.

chunks.title: White Cyclone
chunks.text: In addition to being the third longest wooden roller coaster, White Cyclone is the seventh tallest wooden roller coaster in the world and the fourth tallest wooden roller coaster outside the United States.

chunks.title: White Cyclone
chunks.text: A single ride on the White Cyclone costs ¥1,000 (approximately $9 USD), and the ride is restricted to those individuals above 1.3 m in height; and those individuals under 54 years of age.

chunks.title: Luis Lima
chunks.text: Luis Lima (born 12 September 1948 in Córdoba, Argentina) is an Argentine operatic tenor, who studied in Buenos Aires under Carlos Guichandut and in Sicily under Gina Cigna.

chunks.title: Luis Lima
chunks.text: He made his opera debut in 1974, in Lisbon, in "Cavalleria rusticana", and since then sang in seventy-seven performances at the Metropolitan Opera (from 1977 to 2001) in nine different roles, starting with Alfredo Germont in "La traviata".

chunks.title: Luis Lima
chunks.text: He has also sung with the New York City Opera (1978–79, debuting in "Madama Butterfly"), at the Teatro alla Scala (first appearing in "Lucia di Lammermoor", 1977) and the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden (from 1984).

chunks.title: Bertha May Crawford
chunks.text: Bertha May Crawford (June 20, 1886 - May 26, 1937) was a Canadian opera singer.

chunks.title: Bertha May Crawford
chunks.text: She built an international reputation as a lyric coloratura soprano in the early 20th century in eastern Europe, performing prima donna roles with opera companies in Russia and Poland between 1914 and 1934.

chunks.title: Bertha May Crawford
chunks.text: At her death in 1937, music critics considered her the most distinguished soprano produced in that century in Canada.

chunks.title: Bertha May Crawford
chunks.text: She is remembered as having "a high lyric soprano of great beauty and agility" and was most famous for her performances as Rosina in The Barber of Seville, Violetta in La traviata, and Gilda in Rigoletto.

chunks.title: History of Lisbon
chunks.text: The history of Lisbon, the capital city of Portugal, revolves around its strategic geographical position at the mouth of the Tagus, the longest river in the Iberian Peninsula.

chunks.title: History of Lisbon
chunks.text: Its spacious and sheltered natural harbour made the city historically an important seaport for trade between the Mediterranean Sea and northern Europe.

chunks.title: History of Lisbon
chunks.text: Lisbon has long enjoyed the commercial advantages of its proximity to southern and extreme western Europe, as well as sub-Saharan Africa and the Americas, and today its waterfront is lined with miles of docks, wharfs, and drydock facilities that accommodate the largest oil tankers.

chunks.title: Renée Fleming
chunks.text: Renée Fleming (born February 14, 1959) is an American opera singer and soprano whose repertoire encompasses Richard Strauss, Mozart, Handel, bel canto, lieder, French opera and chansons, jazz and indie rock.

chunks.title: Renée Fleming
chunks.text: Fleming has a full lyric soprano voice.

chunks.title: Renée Fleming
chunks.text: She has performed coloratura, lyric, and lighter spinto soprano operatic roles in Italian, German, French, Czech, and Russian, aside from her native English.

chunks.title: Renée Fleming
chunks.text: She also speaks fluent German and French, along with limited Italian.

chunks.title: Renée Fleming
chunks.text: Her signature roles include Countess Almaviva in Mozart's "Le nozze di Figaro", Desdemona in Verdi's "Otello", Violetta in Verdi's "La traviata", the title role in Dvořák's "Rusalka", the title role in Massenet's "Manon", the title role in Massenet's "Thaïs", the title role in Richard Strauss's "Arabella", the Marschallin in "Der Rosenkavalier", and the Countess in "Capriccio".

chunks.title: Maria Callas
chunks.text: Maria Callas, Commendatore OMRI (Greek: Μαρία Κάλλας ; December 2, 1923 – September 16, 1977), was a Greek-American soprano, and one of the most renowned and influential opera singers of the 20th century.

chunks.title: Maria Callas
chunks.text: Many critics praised her "bel canto" technique, wide-ranging voice and dramatic interpretations.

chunks.title: Maria Callas
chunks.text: Her repertoire ranged from classical "opera seria" to the "bel canto" operas of Donizetti, Bellini and Rossini and further, to the works of Verdi and Puccini; and, in her early career, to the music dramas of Wagner.

chunks.title: Maria Callas
chunks.text: Her musical and dramatic talents led to her being hailed as "La Divina".

chunks.title: The Lisbon Traviata
chunks.text: The Lisbon Traviata is a play by Terrence McNally.

chunks.title: The Lisbon Traviata
chunks.text: The play premiered Off-Broadway in 1989.

chunks.title: The Lisbon Traviata
chunks.text: It revolves around several opera fans, especially of the opera singer Maria Callas, and their gay relationships.

chunks.title: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
chunks.text: The 1755 Lisbon earthquake, also known as the Great Lisbon earthquake, occurred in the Kingdom of Portugal on Saturday, 1 November, the holy day of All Saints' Day, at around 09:40 local time.

chunks.title: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
chunks.text: In combination with subsequent fires and a tsunami, the earthquake almost totally destroyed Lisbon and adjoining areas.

chunks.title: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
chunks.text: Seismologists today estimate the Lisbon earthquake had a magnitude in the range 8.5–9.0 on the moment magnitude scale, with its epicentre in the Atlantic Ocean about 200 km (120 mi) west-southwest of Cape St. Vincent.

chunks.title: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
chunks.text: Estimates place the death toll in Lisbon alone between 10,000 and 100,000 people, making it one of the deadliest earthquakes in history.

chunks.title: The Night in Lisbon
chunks.text: The Night in Lisbon (German: "Die Nacht von Lissabon" ) is a novel by Erich Maria Remarque published in 1962.

chunks.title: The Night in Lisbon
chunks.text: It revolves around the plight of two German refugees in the opening months of World War II.

chunks.title: The Night in Lisbon
chunks.text: One of the refugees relates their story during the course of a single night in Lisbon in 1942.

chunks.title: The Night in Lisbon

chunks.title: Pirate decryption
chunks.text: The term "pirate" in this case is used in the sense of copyright infringement and has little or nothing to do with sea piracy, nor with pirate radio, which involved the operation of a small broadcast radio station without lawfully obtaining a license to transmit.

chunks.title: Pirate decryption
chunks.text: The MPAA and other groups which lobby in favour of intellectual property (specifically copyright and trademark) regulations have labelled such decryption as "signal theft" even though there is no direct tangible loss on the part of the original broadcaster, arguing that losing out on a potential chance to profit from a consumer's subscription fees counts as a loss of actual profit.

chunks.text: It is part of the Penn Center complex designed by Edmund Bacon.

chunks.title: Five Penn Center

chunks.title: Kahramanlar Business Center
chunks.text: Kahramanlar Business Center (Turkish: "Kahramanlar İş Merkezi"), originally known as Emek Business Center (Turkish: "Emek İşhanı"), is a 22 storey highrise building in Kızılay Square, Kızılay, Ankara, Turkey.

chunks.title: Kahramanlar Business Center
chunks.text: Inspired by the Lever House building in New York City, it was designed in 1959 as one of the first International Style highrise buildings in Turkey.

chunks.title: Kahramanlar Business Center
chunks.text: At the time of its completion in 1965, it was the tallest building in Ankara.

chunks.title: Wisma Nusantara
chunks.text: Wisma Nusantara is an office highrise building located in Jalan M.H. Thamrin, Jakarta, Indonesia.

chunks.title: Wisma Nusantara
chunks.text: Constructed in 1964, Wisma Nusantara is considered to be the first highrise in Indonesia and Southeast Asia to reach 100 metre height.

chunks.title: Wisma Nusantara
chunks.text: The building complex included the Pullman Hotel.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: Three Nationwide Plaza is a 408 ft(124m) postmodern highrise building located at the address 3 Nationwide Plaza in Downtown Columbus, Ohio.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: The building is part of the larger multi-building complex known as Nationwide Plaza.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: Nationwide Plaza is the headquarters of Nationwide Mutual Insurance Company.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: Three Nationwide Plaza is the 10th tallest building in Columbus.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: Construction on the building finished in December 1988.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: The architect responsible was the NBBJ Group and the building design follows a postmodern style.

chunks.title: Three Nationwide Plaza
chunks.text: The building was constructed for approximately $89 million and the main materials used were glass, steel, and concrete.

chunks.title: Rotunda (Birmingham)

chunks.title: Rotunda (Birmingham)
chunks.text: The Grade II listed building is 81 m tall and was completed in 1965.

chunks.title: Rotunda (Birmingham)
chunks.text: It was refurbished between 2004 and 2008 by Urban Splash with Glenn Howells who turned it into a residential building with serviced apartments on 19th and 20th floors.

chunks.title: Rotunda (Birmingham)
chunks.text: The building was officially reopened on 13 May 2008.

chunks.title: Huntin' Fool

chunks.title: Huntin' Fool
chunks.text: The magazine is part of Carter Hunter Services.

chunks.title: Huntin' Fool
chunks.text: "Huntin’ Fool" is a resource for non-resident hunters, as well as those interested in trophy hunting.

chunks.title: Huntin' Fool
chunks.text: The publication focuses on big game hunting in Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Kansas, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming.

chunks.title: Architectural photographers
chunks.text: Early architectural photographers include Roger Fenton, Francis Frith (Middle East and Britain), Samuel Bourne (India) and Albert Levy (United States and Europe).

chunks.title: Architectural photographers
chunks.text: They paved the way for the modern speciality of architectural photography.

chunks.title: Architectural photographers
chunks.text: Later architectural photography had practitioners such as Ezra Stoller and Julius Shulman.

chunks.title: Architectural photographers
chunks.text: Stoller worked mainly on the east coast of America, having graduated with a degree in architecture in the 1930s.

chunks.title: Architectural photographers
chunks.text: Shulman, who was based on the West Coast, became an architectural photographer after some images that he had taken of one of Richard Neutra's houses in California made their way onto the architect's desk.

chunks.title: Diana Lemieux
chunks.text: Diana Lemieux is a United States freelance photographer and has been the assistant to the President of the Lymphoma Research Foundation, a non-profit cancer organization in downtown Manhattan.

chunks.title: Diana Lemieux
chunks.text: She resides in Brooklyn, New York.

chunks.title: Diana Lemieux
chunks.text: Her photograph "Sometimes the Road Gets Rugged and It's Hard to Travel On" was first published in the December 2006/January 2007 issue of "JPG Magazine".

chunks.title: Diana Lemieux
chunks.text: Most recently, the same photograph appeared in the June 2007 issue of Smithsonian Magazine.

chunks.title: Diana Lemieux
chunks.text: The photograph earned her a place as a finalist of the 4th Annual Smithsonian Magazine Photo Contest in the travel category and will be featured in an exhibit called "Through Our Reader's Eyes" at the Smithsonian in Washington DC from July 1 – August 15, 2007.

chunks.title: Country Living

chunks.title: Country Living
chunks.text: The monthly magazine focuses on food, home renovation, home decor, DIY and lifestyle.

chunks.title: Country Living
chunks.text: The magazine hosts four Country Living Fairs a year in Rhinebeck, NY, Nashville, TN, Columbus, OH and Atlanta, GA.

chunks.title: WSJ.

chunks.title: WSJ.

chunks.title: WSJ.
chunks.text: Kristina O’Neill is Editor in Chief and Anthony Cenname is Publisher.

chunks.title: WSJ.
chunks.text: Launched as a quarterly in 2008, the magazine grew to 12 issues a year for 2014.

chunks.title: Pacific RailNews
chunks.text: Pacific RailNews "(PRN)", originally named Pacific News and later RailNews, was an American monthly magazine about railroads and rail transit, oriented for railfans.

chunks.title: Pacific RailNews
chunks.text: It was published from 1961 until 1999.

chunks.title: Pacific RailNews
chunks.text: Although its coverage primarily concerned the western United States and western Canada, the magazine included less-detailed news on railroads and rail-transit from non-western states, as well as Mexico.

chunks.title: Sunset (magazine)
chunks.text: Sunset is a lifestyle magazine in the United States.

chunks.title: Sunset (magazine)
chunks.text: "Sunset" focuses on homes, cooking, gardening, and travel, with a focus almost exclusively on the Western United States.

chunks.title: Sunset (magazine)
chunks.text: The magazine is published monthly by the Sunset Publishing Corporation, part of Southern Progress Corporation, itself a subsidiary of Time Warner.

chunks.title: Rodney Walker (architect)
chunks.text: Rodney Walker (1910–1986) was a midcentury American modern designer and builder who specialized in residential architecture in the Southern California area.

chunks.title: Rodney Walker (architect)
chunks.text: He contributed three designs to Arts & Architecture magazine's Case Study House program during the late 1940s (Case Study House #16, #17, and #18).

chunks.title: Rodney Walker (architect)
chunks.text: Many of his homes were photographed by Julius Shulman for "Arts & Architecture" magazine, "Better Homes and Gardens", "Architectural Record", "Sunset", and the "Los Angeles Times Home" magazine.

chunks.title: Portland Monthly
chunks.text: Portland Monthly (also referred to as Portland Monthly Magazine) is a monthly news and general interest magazine which covers events and culture in Portland, Oregon.

chunks.title: Portland Monthly
chunks.text: The magazine was co-founded in 2003 by siblings Nicole and Scott Vogel.

chunks.title: Portland Monthly
chunks.text: Nicole had previously worked for Cendant Corporation and Time Warner, and Scott had been a journalist at "The New York Times".

chunks.title: Portland Monthly
chunks.text: Though the magazine had some trouble with funding in its first year, it grew to a stable circulation of 56,000 and by 2006 was the seventh-largest city magazine in the United States.

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)
chunks.text: Georgia (ジョージア , Jōjia ) is the name of a popular brand of coffee drinks sold by The Coca-Cola Company.

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)
chunks.text: The brand is named after Coca-Cola's home state of Georgia.

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)
chunks.text: It was launched in 1975 by Coca-Cola (Japan) Company, a Japanese subsidiary of the company.

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)
chunks.text: It has since expanded to markets in Singapore, South Korea, India, Bahrain, and the United States of America.

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)

chunks.title: Georgia (coffee)
