chunks.title: Macbeth (opera)
chunks.text: Macbeth (] ) is an opera in four acts by Giuseppe Verdi, with an Italian libretto by Francesco Maria Piave and additions by Andrea Maffei, based on William Shakespeare's play of the same name.

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: De Mi Alma Latina (also known as From My Latin Soul) is a 1994 Latin music album by Spanish tenor Plácido Domingo.

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: It was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Latin Pop Album of the year.

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: Most of the tracks on the album are medleys of, in the words of one author, "some of the Latino world's most memorable melodies."

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: The only new composition on the album, "De México a Buenos Aires", was written by Domingo's son Plácido Domingo Jr. All the songs are in Spanish, except for "Manhã de Carnaval" and "Aquarela do Brasil", which are in Portuguese.

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: Domingo also used "De Mi Alma Latina" and "From My Latin Soul" as the names for some of his subsequent Latin music concerts.

chunks.title: De Mi Alma Latina
chunks.text: In 1997, he released a follow-up album entitled "De Mi Alma Latina 2".

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: Spanish tenor Plácido Domingo has officially sung 147 roles in Italian, French, German, English, Spanish and Russian.

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: His main repertoire however is Italian ("Otello", Cavaradossi in "Tosca", "Don Carlo", Des Grieux in "Manon Lescaut", Dick Johnson in "La fanciulla del West", Radames in "Aida"), French ("Faust", "Werther", Don José in "Carmen", Samson in "Samson et Dalila"), and German ("Lohengrin", "Parsifal", and Siegmund in "Die Walküre").

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: Domingo currently continues to add more operas to his repertoire.

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: Since 2009, he has moved substantially into the baritone repertoire, especially focusing on Verdi baritone roles.

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: In 2015, he made his most recent debuts as Macbeth at the Berliner Staatsoper, Don Carlo in "Ernani" at the Metropolitan Opera, and Gianni Schicchi at the Los Angeles Opera.

chunks.title: Repertoire of Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: Tim Page, a Pulitzer Prize-winner for music criticism, described Domingo in a 1996 "Washington Post" article as "the most versatile, intelligent and altogether accomplished operatic tenor now before the public."

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: José Plácido Domingo Embil, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (] ; born 21 January 1941), known as Plácido Domingo, is a Spanish tenor, conductor and arts administrator.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: He has recorded over a hundred complete operas and is well known for his versatility, regularly performing in Italian, French, German, Spanish, English and Russian in the most prestigious opera houses in the world.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: Although primarily a "lirico-spinto" tenor for most of his career, especially popular for his Cavaradossi, Hoffmann, Don José, and Canio, he quickly moved into more dramatic roles, becoming the most acclaimed Otello of his generation.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: In the early 2010s, he transitioned from the tenor repertory into almost exclusively baritone parts, most notably Simon Boccanegra.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo
chunks.text: He has performed 147 different roles.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: Josefa "Pepita" Embil Echániz (Basque: "Josefa Enbil Etxaniz"; February 28, 1918—August 28, 1994) was a Spanish Basque soprano who starred in zarzuela and operetta productions throughout Spain and Latin America.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: Known as the "Queen of Zarzuela," she is especially remembered for her son, the internationally famous operatic tenor Plácido Domingo, whose early career she helped to nurture.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: Embil began her professional career singing as a soloist in choirs, including the Basque national choir, Eresoinka, which based itself in France during the Spanish Civil War.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: While still in her twenties, she appeared in the world premieres of several new zarzuelas.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: She collaborated with some of the most prominent Spanish composers of the 1940s, including Federico Moreno Torroba, Jacinto Guerrero, and Pablo Sorozábal.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: In late 1948, she moved to Mexico with her baritone husband, Plácido Domingo Ferrer.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: In Mexico they ran a successful zarzuela company of their own, which toured throughout the Americas.

chunks.title: Pepita Embil
chunks.text: Over the course of her career, Embil made several recordings, primarily of zarzuela music.

chunks.title: The Private Lives of the Three Tenors
chunks.text: The Private Lives of the Three Tenors is a gossip biography of tenors Plácido Domingo, Luciano Pavarotti, and José Carreras by Marcia Lewis, the mother of Monica Lewinsky.

chunks.title: The Private Lives of the Three Tenors
chunks.text: The book received high-level publicity during the 1998 Lewinsky scandal, as journalists compared Lewis' "hints" of an affair with popular opera singer, Plácido Domingo, to Lewinsky’s then-unproven allegations against U.S. President Bill Clinton.

chunks.title: The Private Lives of the Three Tenors
chunks.text: Domingo insisted that he only knew Lewis socially.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo Ferrer
chunks.text: Plácido Domingo Ferrer (8 March 1907 – 22 November 1987) was a Spanish zarzuela baritone and father of popular operatic tenor Plácido Domingo.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo Ferrer
chunks.text: Half Catalan and half Aragonese, he grew up and made his early career in Zaragoza, the capital of Aragon.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo Ferrer
chunks.text: He frequently toured Spain with his soprano wife Pepita Embil.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo Ferrer
chunks.text: In late 1948, they permanently moved to Mexico, where they successfully ran their own zarzuela company.

chunks.title: Plácido Domingo Ferrer
chunks.text: He also appeared in recordings and on Mexican television.

chunks.title: Rick Potion No. 9
chunks.text: "Rick Potion #9" is the sixth episode of "Rick and Morty".

chunks.title: Rick Potion No. 9
chunks.text: It premiered on Adult Swim on January 27, 2014, was written by Justin Roiland, and directed by Stephen Sandoval.

chunks.title: Rick Potion No. 9
chunks.text: In the episode, a love potion goes wrong, creating a virus that begins to infect the entire world population, making everyone fall in love with Morty.

chunks.title: Rick Potion No. 9
chunks.text: The episode has been well received, and was seen by about 1.7 million viewers when airing.

chunks.title: Rick Potion No. 9
chunks.text: The title of the episode is in reference to the 1959 song "Love Potion No. 9" by the Clovers.

chunks.title: Rick and Morty (season 2)
chunks.text: The second season of the animated television series "Rick and Morty" originally aired in the United States on Cartoon Network's late night programming block, Adult Swim, which premiered on July 26, 2015 with "A Rickle in Time", and concluded on October 4 with "The Wedding Squanchers".

chunks.title: Rick and Morty (season 2)
chunks.text: This season aired a total of ten episodes.

chunks.title: Meeseeks and Destroy
chunks.text: "Meeseeks and Destroy" is the fifth episode of the first season of "Rick and Morty".

chunks.title: Meeseeks and Destroy
chunks.text: It premiered on Adult Swim on January 20, 2014.

chunks.title: Meeseeks and Destroy
chunks.text: The episode was written by Ryan Ridley and directed by Bryan Newton.

chunks.title: Meeseeks and Destroy
chunks.text: In the episode, Rick provides the family with a solution to their problems, freeing him up to go on an adventure led by Morty.

chunks.title: Meeseeks and Destroy
chunks.text: The episode has been well received, and was seen by about 1.6 million viewers when it was first aired on the Adult Swim channel.

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: Legends of Bikini Bottom is an anthology series of six episodes in the American animated television series "SpongeBob SquarePants", as part of its seventh season.

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: As the name suggests, the episodes have plots involving things like monsters, magic and mythical creatures.

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: The first episode called "Trenchbillies" first premiered on the online social networking service Facebook on January 27, 2011 before airing on Nickelodeon on January 29, 2011.

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: The four other episodes titled "Sponge-Cano!"

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: , "The Main Drain", "The Monster Who Came to Bikini Bottom" and "Welcome to the Bikini Bottom Triangle" premiered on Nickelodeon as part of an hour-long special on January 28, 2011.

chunks.title: Legends of Bikini Bottom
chunks.text: The decision to air the series online was aimed at attracting "the young and the restless hooked to the internet and the social media."

chunks.title: Faerie Tale Theatre
chunks.text: Faerie Tale Theatre (also known as Shelley Duvall's Faerie Tale Theatre) is an American award-winning live-action children's anthology television series, starring many famous and well known actors (particularly of the period) including Robin Williams, consisting of 27 episodes retelling 25 classic fairy tales, particularly of The Brothers Grimm, plus the poem The Pied Piper of Hamelin and a special episode called "The Grimm's Party", showcasing the series cast and crew, (including Duvall and Teri Garr), that originally aired on Showtime from September 11, 1982 until November 14, 1987.

chunks.title: Faerie Tale Theatre
chunks.text: Shelley Duvall, who created the series served as narrator, host and executive producer of the program alongside Fred Fuchs, and occasionally starred in episodes.

chunks.title: Faerie Tale Theatre
chunks.text: The series was followed by two other, albeit less successful shorter anthology series "Tall Tales & Legends" (episode 9) which followed the same format as "Faerie Tale Theatre" and focused on classic American folk tales and third series Nightmare Classics (4 episodes, originally planned as 6).

chunks.title: Faerie Tale Theatre
chunks.text: This was one of the first examples of cable original programming, alongside HBO's "Fraggle Rock".

chunks.title: Rixty Minutes
chunks.text: "Rixty Minutes" is the eighth episode of the first season of "Rick and Morty".

chunks.title: Rixty Minutes
chunks.text: It premiered on Adult Swim on March 17, 2014.

chunks.title: Rixty Minutes
chunks.text: The episode was written by Tom Kauffman and Justin Roiland, and directed by Bryan Newton.

chunks.title: Rixty Minutes
chunks.text: In the episode, Rick and Morty watch cable from other dimensions, while Jerry, Beth, and Summer watch alternate reality versions of themselves using a pair of interdimensional goggles.

chunks.title: Rixty Minutes
chunks.text: The episode was well received and watched by about 1.48 million viewers in the United States.

chunks.title: Pilot (Rick and Morty)
chunks.text: "Pilot" is the first episode of "Rick and Morty".

chunks.title: Pilot (Rick and Morty)
chunks.text: It premiered on Adult Swim on December 2, 2013.

chunks.title: Pilot (Rick and Morty)
chunks.text: It is written by series creators Dan Harmon and Justin Roiland, and directed by Roiland.

chunks.title: Pilot (Rick and Morty)
chunks.text: The series introduces protagonists, alcoholic scientist Rick Sanchez and his innocent teenage grandson Morty Smith, as they embark on a dangerous interdimensional adventure to fetch Mega tree seeds.

chunks.title: Pilot (Rick and Morty)
chunks.text: The pilot had a mixed to positive reception and was seen by about 1.1 million viewers when airing.

chunks.title: Lawnmower Dog
chunks.text: "Lawnmower Dog" is the second episode of "Rick and Morty".

chunks.title: Lawnmower Dog
chunks.text: It premiered on Adult Swim on December 9, 2013, was written by Ryan Ridley, and directed by John Rice.

chunks.title: Lawnmower Dog
chunks.text: In the episode, Rick gives Jerry a device to enhance the dog's intelligence, whilst Rick and Morty get lost in the dreams of Morty's math teacher.

chunks.title: Lawnmower Dog
chunks.text: The episode was well received, with approximately 1.5 million viewers when airing.

chunks.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (season 6)
chunks.text: The sixth season of the American comedy television series "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia" premiered on FX on September 16, 2010.

chunks.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (season 6)
chunks.text: The season contains 14 episodes and concluded airing on December 9, 2010 with the hour-long Christmas special (which was produced for season 5, however aired as part of season 6).

chunks.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (season 6)
chunks.text: An additional episode called "The Gang Gets Successful" (production code IP06004) was produced for this season, but was not aired, despite scenes from the episode being included in promotional material for season 6.

chunks.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia (season 6)
chunks.text: It was later re-edited with new scenes to create the season 7 episode "How Mac Got Fat".

chunks.title: The Ricks Must Be Crazy
chunks.text: "The Ricks Must Be Crazy" is the sixth episode in the second season of the American animated television sitcom "Rick and Morty", and the seventeenth overall episode in the series.

chunks.title: The Ricks Must Be Crazy
chunks.text: Written by Dan Guterman and directed by Dominic Polcino, the episode first aired on Adult Swim in the United States on August 30, 2015.

chunks.title: The Ricks Must Be Crazy
chunks.text: It is speculated that the title of the episode is a reference to the 1980 film "The Gods Must Be Crazy".

chunks.title: John Carter (film)
chunks.text: John Carter is a 2012 American science fiction action film directed by Andrew Stanton from a screenplay written by Stanton, Mark Andrews, and Michael Chabon.

chunks.title: John Carter (film)
chunks.text: The film was produced by Jim Morris, Colin Wilson, and Lindsey Collins, and is based on "A Princess of Mars", the first book in the "Barsoom" series of novels by Edgar Rice Burroughs.

chunks.title: John Carter (film)
chunks.text: "John Carter" stars Taylor Kitsch in the title role, Lynn Collins, Samantha Morton, Mark Strong, Ciarán Hinds, Dominic West, James Purefoy, and Willem Dafoe.

chunks.title: John Carter (film)
chunks.text: The film chronicles the first interplanetary adventure of John Carter and his attempts to mediate civil unrest amongst the warring kingdoms of Barsoom.

chunks.title: Finding Dory
chunks.text: Finding Dory is a 2016 American 3D computer-animated comedy adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Finding Dory
chunks.text: Directed by Andrew Stanton with co-direction by Angus MacLane, the screenplay was written by Stanton and Victoria Strouse.

chunks.title: Finding Dory
chunks.text: The film is a sequel/spinoff to 2003's "Finding Nemo" and features the returning voices of Ellen DeGeneres and Albert Brooks, with Hayden Rolence (replacing Alexander Gould), Ed O'Neill, Kaitlin Olson, Ty Burrell, Diane Keaton and Eugene Levy joining the cast.

chunks.title: Finding Dory
chunks.text: The film focuses on the amnesiac fish Dory, who journeys to be reunited with her parents.

chunks.title: Toy Story
chunks.text: Toy Story is a 1995 American computer-animated buddy comedy adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Toy Story
chunks.text: The directorial debut of John Lasseter, "Toy Story" was the first feature-length computer-animated film and the first feature film produced by Pixar.

chunks.title: Toy Story
chunks.text: Taking place in a world where anthropomorphic toys pretend to be lifeless whenever humans are present, the film's plot focuses on the relationship between Woody, an old-fashioned pullstring cowboy doll (voiced by Tom Hanks), and Buzz Lightyear, an astronaut action figure (voiced by Tim Allen), as they evolve from rivals competing for the affections of Andy, their owner, to friends who work together to be reunited with Andy as his family prepares to move to a new home.

chunks.title: Toy Story
chunks.text: The screenplay was written by Joss Whedon, Andrew Stanton, Joel Cohen and Alec Sokolow, based on a story by Lasseter, Pete Docter, Stanton and Joe Ranft.

chunks.title: Toy Story
chunks.text: The film features music by Randy Newman, and was executive-produced by Steve Jobs and Edwin Catmull.

chunks.title: Finding Nemo (franchise)
chunks.text: Finding Nemo is a CGI animated film series and Disney media franchise that began with the 2003 film, "Finding Nemo", produced by Pixar and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Finding Nemo (franchise)
chunks.text: The original film was followed by a sequel, "Finding Dory", released in 2016.

chunks.title: Finding Nemo (franchise)
chunks.text: Both films are directed by Andrew Stanton.

chunks.title: A Bug's Life
chunks.text: A Bug's Life is a 1998 American computer-animated adventure comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: A Bug's Life
chunks.text: Directed by John Lasseter, the film involves a misfit ant named Flik that is looking for "tough warriors" to save his colony from greedy grasshoppers, only to recruit a group of bugs that turn out to be an inept circus troupe.

chunks.title: A Bug's Life
chunks.text: The film stars the voices of Dave Foley, Kevin Spacey and Julia Louis-Dreyfus.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: Brave is a 2012 American 3D computer-animated fantasy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: It was directed by Mark Andrews and Brenda Chapman and co-directed by Steve Purcell.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: The story is by Chapman, with the screenplay by Andrews, Purcell, Chapman and Irene Mecchi.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: The film was produced by Katherine Sarafian, with John Lasseter, Andrew Stanton, and Pete Docter as executive producers.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: The film's voice cast features Kelly Macdonald, Billy Connolly, Emma Thompson, Julie Walters, Robbie Coltrane, Kevin McKidd, and Craig Ferguson.

chunks.title: Brave (2012 film)
chunks.text: Set in the Scottish Highlands, the film tells the story of a princess named Merida who defies an age-old custom, causing chaos in the kingdom by expressing the desire not to be betrothed.

chunks.title: Toy Story 3
chunks.text: Toy Story 3 is a 2010 American 3D computer-animated comedy-drama film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Toy Story 3
chunks.text: It is the third installment in Pixar's "Toy Story" series, and the sequel to 1999's "Toy Story 2".

chunks.title: Toy Story 3
chunks.text: It was directed by Lee Unkrich, the editor of the first two films and the co-director of "Toy Story 2", written by Michael Arndt, while Unkrich wrote the story along with John Lasseter and Andrew Stanton, respectively director and co-writer of the first two films.

chunks.title: Toy Story 3
chunks.text: The plot focuses on the toys Woody, Buzz Lightyear, and their friends dealing with an uncertain future as their owner, Andy, prepares to leave for college.

chunks.title: Toy Story 3
chunks.text: The film features an ensemble voice cast with Tom Hanks, Tim Allen, Joan Cusack, Don Rickles, Wallace Shawn, John Ratzenberger, Estelle Harris, Jodi Benson, and John Morris reprising their roles from the previous films, along with Blake Clark as the voice of Slinky Dog (because Jim Varney died ten years before the release of the film) and Ned Beatty, Michael Keaton, Whoopi Goldberg, Timothy Dalton, Kristen Schaal, Bonnie Hunt, and Jeff Garlin voicing the new characters introduced in this film.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: Monsters University is a 2013 American 3D computer-animated comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: It was directed by Dan Scanlon and produced by Kori Rae, with John Lasseter, Pete Docter, Andrew Stanton and Lee Unkrich as executive producers.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: The music for the film was composed by Randy Newman, marking his seventh collaboration with Pixar.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: It was the fourteenth feature film produced by Pixar, and is a prequel to 2001's "Monsters, Inc.", marking the first time Pixar has made a prequel film.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: "Monsters University" tells the story of two monsters, Mike and Sulley, and their time studying at college, where they start off as rivals, but slowly become best friends.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Steve Buscemi, Bob Peterson, and John Ratzenberger reprise their roles as James P. Sullivan, Mike Wazowski, Randall Boggs, Roz, and the Abominable Snowman, respectively.

chunks.title: Monsters University
chunks.text: Bonnie Hunt, who played Ms. Flint in the first film, voices Mike's grade school teacher Ms. Karen Graves.

chunks.title: Andrew Stanton
chunks.text: Andrew Stanton (born December 3, 1965) is an American film director, screenwriter, producer and voice actor based at Pixar.

chunks.title: Andrew Stanton
chunks.text: His film work includes writing and directing Pixar's "A Bug's Life" (1998) (as co-director), "Finding Nemo" (2003), and "WALL-E" (2008), and the live-action film, Disney's "John Carter" (2012).

chunks.title: Andrew Stanton
chunks.text: He also co-wrote all three "Toy Story" films and "Monsters, Inc." (2001)

chunks.title: Monsters, Inc.
chunks.text: Monsters, Inc. is a 2001 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Monsters, Inc.
chunks.text: Featuring the voices of John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Steve Buscemi, James Coburn, and Jennifer Tilly, the film was directed by Pete Docter in his directorial debut, and executive produced by John Lasseter and Andrew Stanton.

chunks.title: Monsters, Inc.
chunks.text: The film centers on two monsters employed at the titular energy-producing factory Monsters, Inc. — top scarer James P. "Sulley" Sullivan and his one-eyed partner and best friend Mike Wazowski.

chunks.title: Monsters, Inc.
chunks.text: In the film, employees at Monsters, Inc. generate their city's power by scaring children, but they themselves are afraid that the children are toxic to them, and when one child enters the factory, Sulley and Mike must return her home before it is too late.

chunks.title: David Sutton (writer)
chunks.text: David Sutton (born 1966) is the current editor of the "Fortean Times" magazine.

chunks.title: David Sutton (writer)
chunks.text: Sutton was born in Canterbury, Kent.

chunks.title: David Sutton (writer)
chunks.text: He was educated at the University of East Anglia, University College London, Birkbeck College and the British Film Institute.

chunks.title: David Sutton (writer)
chunks.text: He holds a doctorate, earned for his thesis on the origins and progress of British film comedy, and is the author of the book "A Chorus of Raspberries: British Film Comedy, 1929-1939".

chunks.title: John Gillett
chunks.text: John Gillett (1925–1995) was a British film critic and researcher whose career at the British Film Institute spanned over 44 years.

chunks.title: John Gillett
chunks.text: He was also a programmer for the National Film Theatre on the works of Buster Keaton, early Russian cinema and Japanese cinema, to name a few.

chunks.title: John Gillett
chunks.text: He wrote film reviews for "The Monthly Film Bulletin".

chunks.title: John Gillett
chunks.text: With Ian Christie, he edited "Futurism/Formalism/FEKS: 'Eccentrism' and Soviet Cinema 1918-1936."

chunks.title: John Gillett
chunks.text: He was also an editor of "Yasujiro Ozu: A Critical Anthology", with David Wilson.

chunks.title: East Is East (play)
chunks.text: East Is East is a 1996 play by Ayub Khan-Din, first produced by Tamasha Theatre Company in co-production with the Royal Court and Birmingham Repertory Theatre.

chunks.title: East Is East (play)
chunks.text: It is often cited as one of the key works to bring Asian culture to mainstream British audiences.

chunks.title: East Is East (play)
chunks.text: The play is published by Nick Hern Books.

chunks.title: All in Good Time (film)
chunks.text: All in Good Time is a British film directed by Nigel Cole.

chunks.title: All in Good Time (film)
chunks.text: It is based on Ayub Khan-Din's 2007 play "Rafta, Rafta," which itself was based on a 1963 play and 1966 film by Bill Naughton, "All in Good Time" and "The Family Way."

chunks.title: West Is West (2010 film)
chunks.text: West Is West is a 2010 British comedy-drama film, which is a sequel to the 1999 comedy "East Is East".

chunks.title: West Is West (2010 film)
chunks.text: It stars Om Puri, Linda Bassett, Aqib Khan, Ila Arun and Jimi Mistry, is written by Ayub Khan-Din, directed by Andy DeEmmony, and produced by Leslee Udwin for Assassin Films and BBC Films.

chunks.title: East Is East (1999 film)
chunks.text: East Is East is a 1999 British comedy-drama film written by Ayub Khan-Din and directed by Damien O'Donnell.

chunks.title: East Is East (1999 film)
chunks.text: It is set in Salford, Lancashire, in 1971, in a mixed-ethnicity British household headed by Pakistani father George (Om Puri) and an English mother, Ella (Linda Bassett).

chunks.title: Ben Keaton
chunks.text: Ben Keaton (born 1956) is an Irish actor who appeared as Jeff Brannigan in ITV soap opera "Emmerdale".

chunks.title: Ben Keaton
chunks.text: He appeared in BBC's "Casualty" playing the part of Spencer between 1999-2002.

chunks.title: Ben Keaton
chunks.text: He guest starred as Father Austin Purcell in "Think Fast, Father Ted", an episode of the Channel 4's sitcom "Father Ted".

chunks.title: Ben Keaton
chunks.text: He had a small part in the British film "East is East" as a priest.

chunks.title: Rafta, Rafta...
chunks.text: Rafta, Rafta... is a comedy by British Pakistani playwright Ayub Khan-Din adapted from the 1963 Bill Naughton play, "All in Good Time".

chunks.title: Rafta, Rafta...
chunks.text: The play is set in the working class English town of Bolton, and examines a story of marital difficulties within an immigrant Indian family.

chunks.title: Rafta, Rafta...
chunks.text: Eeshwar Dutt is a first-generation immigrant and patriarch of the family.

chunks.title: Rafta, Rafta...
chunks.text: He has a troubled relationship with his newlywed son Atul, whose married life with Vina Patel has got off to a rocky start.

chunks.title: Rafta, Rafta...
chunks.text: The play deals with setting out and resolving these various conflicts.

chunks.title: Ayub Khan-Din
chunks.text: Ayub Khan Din (born 1961) is a British Pakistani actor perhaps best known for his role of Sammy in Hanif Kureishi's film "Sammy and Rosie Get Laid" in (1987) and as the writer of the BAFTA, BIFA and London Film Critics Circle award-winning film "East Is East", based on the original 1996 play that was nominated for an Olivier Award in 1998.

chunks.title: Ayub Khan-Din
chunks.text: In 2008 his new comedy play "Rafta, Rafta..." won the Olivier Award that year.

chunks.title: Ayub Khan-Din
chunks.text: He also wrote the film sequel "West Is West" released in 2010.

chunks.title: Idiot (1992 film)
chunks.text: Idiot is a 1992 Hindi film based on Fyodor Dostoevsky's novel, "The Idiot".

chunks.title: Idiot (1992 film)
chunks.text: It was directed by Mani Kaul and starred Shah Rukh Khan and Ayub Khan-Din.

chunks.title: Idiot (1992 film)
chunks.text: The film debuted at the New York Film Festival in October 1992.

chunks.title: Idiot (1992 film)
chunks.text: In this version of the tale, placed in contemporary Mumbai, Prince Miskin (Khan-Din) is a man whose epilepsy is mistaken for idiocy.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show
chunks.text: The Super Bowl XLVII halftime show occurred on February 3, 2013 at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome in New Orleans as part of Super Bowl XLVII and featured American entertainer Beyoncé with special guests Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams from Destiny's Child.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show
chunks.text: It became the then second most watched show in Super Bowl history by garnering 110.8 million viewers.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show
chunks.text: The performance, and the stadium blackout that followed, generated more than 299,000 tweets per minute, making it the then second most tweeted moment in the history of Twitter.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVII halftime show
chunks.text: This would be the first Pepsi sponsored halftime show since Prince's performance in Super Bowl XLI.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime-show controversy
chunks.text: Super Bowl XXXVIII – which was broadcast live on February 1, 2004 from Houston, Texas on the CBS television network in the United States – was noted for a controversial halftime show in which Janet Jackson's breast, adorned with a nipple shield, was exposed by Justin Timberlake for about half a second, in what was later referred to as a "wardrobe malfunction".

chunks.title: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime-show controversy
chunks.text: The incident, sometimes referred to as Nipplegate, was widely discussed.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime-show controversy
chunks.text: Along with the rest of the halftime show, it led to an immediate crackdown and widespread debate on perceived indecency in broadcasting.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime-show controversy
chunks.text: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) fined CBS a record US$550,000 which was fought in the Supreme Court, but that fine was appealed and ultimately voided by the Third Circuit Court of Appeals in a 2011 ruling, and a case to reinstate the fine was refused in 2012.

chunks.title: Super Bowl 50 halftime show

chunks.title: Super Bowl 50 halftime show

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVIII halftime show

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVIII halftime show
chunks.text: The show was produced by Ricky Kirshner and directed by Hamish Hamilton.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVIII halftime show
chunks.text: At the time of airing the halftime show attracted the largest audience in the history of the Super Bowl, attracting 115.3 million viewers.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVIII halftime show
chunks.text: The show was later surpassed by the following year's Super Bowl XLIX halftime show in which American pop star Katy Perry was headliner.

chunks.title: Super Bowl XLVIII halftime show
chunks.text: The performance generated 2.2 million tweets, due to clamoring for tickets to Mars' Moonshine Jungle Tour.

chunks.title: Lady Gaga: Queen of Pop

chunks.title: List of Super Bowl halftime shows
chunks.text: As the Super Bowl itself is typically the most-watched event on television in the United States annually, the halftime show has been equally-viewed in recent years: the halftime show of Super Bowl XLIX featuring Katy Perry was viewed by 118.5 million, as part of an overall telecast that peaked at 120.3 million at its conclusion—the most-watched television broadcast in U.S. history.

chunks.title: List of Super Bowl halftime shows

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: A development director or director of development is the senior fundraising manager of a non-profit organization, company, or corporation.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: The position works closely with a chief financial officer (CFO) or treasurer.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: A Director of Development is chiefly responsible for bringing in revenue streams to a non-profit (grants, donations, special events), and a CFO is responsible for the fiscal management of the organization.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: A CFO is rarely assigned to write grant narratives, but may oversee the budget section of a grant application or a fiscal report for a grant.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: Some larger organizations (especially those that have large government grants) have a grants manager as well as a grant writer/Director of Development.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: A Grants Manager assists the CFO with grant reports and/or grant related accounting.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: A development director is usually remunerated for his or her work, and in best practices for nonprofit organizations, development directors earn salaries.

chunks.title: Development director
chunks.text: Commissions are still considered unethical by professional organizations such as the Grant Professionals Association (GPA) and the Association of Fundraising Professionals (AFP), but the practice of commission based remuneration is growing, particularly in the current economy.

chunks.text: German educated Greek stage director Fotos Politis (Greek: Φώτος Πολίτης), 1890-1934, was one of the most prominent figures in the revival of the ancient Greek tragedies in the 20th century.

chunks.title: Fotos Politis
chunks.text: A literary and theater reviewer and playwright, who was responsible for the creation of what came to be called “the theatrical tradition of the National Theater of Greece”, he developed original teaching methods for aspiring young actors in Athenian drama schools while the rehearsals for the plays that he staged were known for their long duration and exhaustive intensity.

chunks.title: Fotos Politis
chunks.text: Politis felt an obligation to educate not only the actors, corrupted by the French "Théâtre de boulevard" of the time, but also the general public by bringing it in contact with the masterpieces of ancient Greek tragedy, Shakespeare, classical European theater and avant-garde theater.

chunks.title: DMPO's on Broadway
chunks.text: Live at DMPO's on Broadway is a VHS/DVD of the Dead Kennedys' performance at the old San Francisco avant-garde theater, DMPO's on Broadway.

chunks.title: DMPO's on Broadway
chunks.text: It was filmed on June 16, 1984, the last night the theater was open before it was torn down.

chunks.title: DMPO's on Broadway
chunks.text: The show is about an hour long and includes 14 songs.

chunks.title: DMPO's on Broadway
chunks.text: Originally released on VHS in 1985 as "Live In San Francisco", it was released on DVD on August 29, 2000, under its current title.

chunks.title: Christoph Marthaler
chunks.text: Christoph Marthaler (born Oсtober 17, 1951, Erlenbach, Switzerland) is a Swiss director and musician, working in the style of avant-garde theater, such as Expressionism and Dada, a theater of the absurd elements.

chunks.title: Jean Erdman
chunks.text: Jean Erdman (born February 20, 1916) is an American dancer and choreographer of modern dance as well as an avant-garde theater director.

chunks.title: Richard Foreman
chunks.text: Richard Foreman (born June 10, 1937 in New York City) is an American playwright and avant-garde theater pioneer.

chunks.title: Richard Foreman
chunks.text: He is the founder of the Ontological-Hysteric Theater.

chunks.title: Lovisa Simson
chunks.text: Lovisa Concordia Simson, née "Kliecnik" or "Lindström" (1746 – 26 February 1808, Gothenburg), was a Swedish theater director.

chunks.title: Lovisa Simson
chunks.text: She was the managing director of the theater "Comediehuset" in Gothenburg between 1787 and 1792.

chunks.title: Lovisa Simson
chunks.text: She was the first female theater director over a permanent theater (rather than a travelling theater company) in her country.

chunks.title: Teatr Tworzenia
chunks.text: Teatr Tworzenia, or The Theater of Creation, Polish avant-garde theater, founded by Jarosław Pijarowski.

chunks.title: Teatr Tworzenia
chunks.text: According to the author's definition it is: "Uninstitutionalized form of realization of creative ideas, consisting on intuitive-improvisational thematic activities; Have on the goal of integration and promotion of creative thought (word, music, theater, paintings) in audio-visual forms.

chunks.title: Ethel Rojo
chunks.text: Ethel Rojo (née Ethel Inés Rojo Castro; December 23, 1937 in Santiago del Estero – June 24, 2012 in Buenos Aires) was an Argentine actress, vedette, dancer and theater director.

chunks.title: Ethel Rojo
chunks.text: She was the sister of Gogó Rojo.

chunks.title: Ahmad Kamyabi Mask
chunks.text: Ahmad Kamyabi Mask (Persian: احمد کامیابی مَسْک‎ ‎ ; born 1944) is a writer, translator, publisher, and current Professor Emeritus of Modern Drama and Theater of the Faculty of Fine Arts of the University of Tehran.

chunks.title: Ahmad Kamyabi Mask
chunks.text: He is a prominent scholar of French Avant-garde theater and influential in the study of Eugène Ionesco and Samuel Beckett.

chunks.title: Ethel Winter
chunks.text: Ethel Winter (June 18, 1924 – March 10, 2012) was an American ballet dancer and dance instructor.

chunks.title: Ethel Winter
chunks.text: Winter was an early ballet dancer with the Martha Graham Dance Company from the 1940s to the 1960s, working with other notable early members of the company, including Martha Graham, Yuriko, Yuriko, Ethel Butler, Jean Erdman, and Patricia Birch.

chunks.title: Ethel Winter
chunks.text: She later taught dance and ballet at the Juilliard School.

chunks.title: Rumer Willis
chunks.text: Rumer Glenn Willis (born August 16, 1988) is an American actress and singer.

chunks.title: Rumer Willis
chunks.text: She is the oldest daughter of actors Bruce Willis and Demi Moore.

chunks.title: Rumer Willis
chunks.text: Willis won season 20 of "Dancing with the Stars."

chunks.title: Rumer Willis
chunks.text: She went on to make her Broadway debut in "Chicago" as Roxie Hart on September 21, 2015.

chunks.title: Rumer Willis
chunks.text: She currently has a recurring role in season 3 of FOX musical-drama "Empire".

chunks.title: The Return of Bruno (album)
chunks.text: The Return of Bruno is the debut album by actor Bruce Willis.

chunks.title: The Return of Bruno (album)
chunks.text: Released by Motown in 1987, this album is an eclectic gathering of R&B music sung by Willis, with backing musicians including Booker T. Jones, The Pointer Sisters and The Temptations.

chunks.title: The Return of Bruno (album)
chunks.text: It is a companion piece to an HBO special of the same name which aired shortly after the album's release.

chunks.title: The Return of Bruno (album)
chunks.text: A re-issue was distributed by Razor & Tie in 1997.

chunks.title: David Dunn (character)
chunks.text: David Dunn is a fictional character and the main protagonist in the "Unbreakable" film series, portrayed by American actor Bruce Willis.

chunks.title: David Dunn (character)
chunks.text: Dunn is a former college football prodigy and presently a security guard who discovers he has superhuman abilities.

chunks.title: Mortal Thoughts
chunks.text: Mortal Thoughts is a 1991 American dramatic mystery thriller, about a woman who is interrogated by the police regarding the death of her friend's husband.

chunks.title: Mortal Thoughts
chunks.text: It was directed by Alan Rudolph and stars Demi Moore, Glenne Headly, Bruce Willis, and Harvey Keitel.

chunks.title: Mortal Thoughts
chunks.text: Willis plays James Urbanski, the violent, drug-addicted husband of Joyce (Headly), who is murdered one evening at a Feast of Saint Rocco festival.

chunks.title: Red (2010 film)
chunks.text: Red is a 2010 American action comedy film inspired by the limited comic book series of the same name created by Warren Ellis and Cully Hamner and published by the DC Comics imprint Homage.

chunks.title: Red (2010 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Bruce Willis, Morgan Freeman, John Malkovich, Mary-Louise Parker, Helen Mirren and Karl Urban, with German film director Robert Schwentke directing a screenplay by Jon Hoeber and Erich Hoeber.

chunks.title: Red (2010 film)
chunks.text: In the film version, the title is derived from the designation of former CIA Agent Frank Moses (Bruce Willis), meaning "Retired, Extremely Dangerous".

chunks.title: Billy Bathgate (film)
chunks.text: Billy Bathgate is a 1991 American gangster film directed by Robert Benton, starring Loren Dean as the title character and Dustin Hoffman as real-life gangster Dutch Schultz.

chunks.title: Billy Bathgate (film)
chunks.text: The film co-stars Nicole Kidman, Steven Hill, Steve Buscemi, and Bruce Willis.

chunks.title: Billy Bathgate (film)
chunks.text: Although Billy is a fictional character, at least four of the other characters in the film were real people from New York of the 1930s.

chunks.title: Billy Bathgate (film)
chunks.text: The screenplay was adapted by British writer Tom Stoppard from E.L. Doctorow's novel of the same name.

chunks.title: Billy Bathgate (film)
chunks.text: However, Doctorow distanced himself from the film for the extensive deviations from the book.

chunks.title: Cop Out (2010 film)
chunks.text: Cop Out is a 2010 American buddy cop action-comedy film directed and edited by Kevin Smith, written by Mark and Robb Cullen and starring Bruce Willis, Tracy Morgan, Kevin Pollak and Seann William Scott.

chunks.title: Cop Out (2010 film)
chunks.text: The plot revolves around two veteran NYPD partners (Willis and Morgan) on the trail of a stolen, rare, mint-condition baseball card who find themselves up against a relentless, memorabilia-obsessed bloodthirsty gangster.

chunks.title: Cop Out (2010 film)
chunks.text: This is the first film that Smith directed that he did not also write.

chunks.title: Cop Out (2010 film)
chunks.text: Upon its release, the film was met with negative reviews by critics and underperformed at the box office.

chunks.title: Cop Out (2010 film)
chunks.text: It is nevertheless Kevin Smith's highest grossing film.

chunks.title: Bruce Willis
chunks.text: Walter Bruce Willis (born March 19, 1955) is an American actor, producer, and singer.

chunks.title: Bruce Willis
chunks.text: His career began on the Off-Broadway stage and then in television in the 1980s, most notably as David Addison in "Moonlighting" (1985–1989).

chunks.title: Bruce Willis
chunks.text: He is known for his role of John McClane in the film "Die Hard" (1988) and its four sequels.

chunks.title: Bruce Willis
chunks.text: He has appeared in over 60 films, including "Death Becomes Her" (1992), "Color of Night" (1994), "Pulp Fiction" (1994), "Nobody's Fool" (1994), "12 Monkeys" (1995), "The Fifth Element" (1997), "Armageddon" (1998), "The Sixth Sense" (1999), "Unbreakable" (2000), "Sin City" (2005), "Lucky Number Slevin" (2006), "Red" (2010), "Moonrise Kingdom" (2012), "The Expendables 2" (2012), and "Looper" (2012).

chunks.title: Bruce Willis
chunks.text: The actor has also done voice overs for movies such as "Look Who's Talking" (1989), "Beavis and Butt-Head Do America" (1996), "Rugrats Go Wild" (2003) and "Over the Hedge" (2006).

chunks.title: In Country
chunks.text: In Country is a 1989 American drama film produced and directed by Norman Jewison, starring Bruce Willis and Emily Lloyd.

chunks.title: In Country
chunks.text: The screenplay by Frank Pierson and Cynthia Cidre was based on the novel by Bobbie Ann Mason.

chunks.title: In Country
chunks.text: The original music score was composed by James Horner.

chunks.title: In Country
chunks.text: Willis earned a best supporting actor Golden Globe nomination for his role.

chunks.title: Unbreakable (film)
chunks.text: Unbreakable is a 2000 American superhero thriller film written, produced, and directed by M. Night Shyamalan, and starring Bruce Willis and Samuel L. Jackson, alongside Robin Wright and Spencer Treat Clark.

chunks.title: Unbreakable (film)
chunks.text: The movie is the first installment in a trilogy.

chunks.title: Unbreakable (film)
chunks.text: In "Unbreakable", a security guard named David Dunn survives a horrific train crash.

chunks.title: Unbreakable (film)
chunks.text: After the incident, with the help of a manipulative disabled comic book shop owner named Elijah Price, he learns that he possesses superhuman powers.

chunks.title: Unbreakable (film)
chunks.text: As Dunn explores and reluctantly confronts his powers while trying to navigate a difficult family life, he begins to fight crime and learns the true nature of Elijah Price.

chunks.title: Street Music
chunks.text: Street Music is the third album by Defari, an American hip hop musician who is also part of the Likwit Crew.

chunks.title: Street Music
chunks.text: The album features regular collaborators Evidence, J-Ro, E-Swift, The Alchemist and DJ Babu, the latter Defari's partner in the Likwit Junkies.

chunks.title: Likwit Crew
chunks.text: The Likwit Crew is a West Coast hip hop collective.

chunks.title: Likwit Crew
chunks.text: It was founded by King T who recruited Tha Alkaholiks as his first acts.

chunks.title: Likwit Crew
chunks.text: Then, other artists such as Xzibit, Phil Da Agony, Lootpack, Defari, Styliztik Jones, Declaime, J. Wells and The Barbershop MC's joined.

chunks.title: Full Circle (Xzibit album)
chunks.text: Full Circle, released in 2006, is the sixth album from West Coast rapper Xzibit, his first release on Koch Records.

chunks.title: Full Circle (Xzibit album)
chunks.text: To assist in the making of "Full Circle", Xzibit enlisted Keith Shocklee of the Bomb Squad as co-executive producer.

chunks.title: Full Circle (Xzibit album)
chunks.text: The Game, DJ Quik, Too Short, T-Pain and Tha Dogg Pound make up the many high-profile guests, and the "Chappelle's Show"'s Donnell Rawlings makes a comedic appearance.

chunks.title: Full Circle (Xzibit album)
chunks.text: The presence of King Tee is particularly notable for being the first Likwit Crew rapper to appear on an Xzibit album since 2000's "Restless".

chunks.title: Colin Griffiths
chunks.text: Colin Griffiths (born 16 August 1983) is an English comedian, DJ, VJ and writer.

chunks.title: Colin Griffiths
chunks.text: He is most famous for his work as host of the MTV show "Up, Up, Down, Down...", the flagship program of MTV Flux which has also aired on TMF UK and MTV UK and Ireland.

chunks.title: Xzibit
chunks.text: Alvin Nathaniel Joiner (born September 18, 1974), better known by his stage name Xzibit (pronounced "exhibit"), is an American rapper, actor, television host, radio personality and record producer.

chunks.title: Xzibit
chunks.text: He is known as the host of the MTV show "Pimp My Ride", which brought him mainstream success.

chunks.title: Xzibit
chunks.text: Before hosting the show, he achieved fame in the West Coast hip-hop scene as a rapper, debuting with his acclaimed "At the Speed of Life" and gathering chart success with his follow-up albums "Restless", "Man vs. Machine" and "Weapons of Mass Destruction", working with high-profile artists such as Eminem, Cypress Hill, Snoop Dogg, Ice Cube, Dr. Dre, Knoc-turn'al, Timbaland, Limp Bizkit, Alice Cooper, Game, 50 Cent and Within Temptation, as well as being one of the first rappers to work internationally, collaborating with overseas acts such as Russian rapper Timati, Raptile from Germany and Bliss N Eso from Australia.

chunks.title: Traci Stumpf
chunks.text: Traci Stumpf is an American TV host, Stand-up Comedian and actress.

chunks.title: Traci Stumpf
chunks.text: She recently hosted the 2016 MTV MIAW Music awards in Mexico City with Fall Out Boy’s frontman Pete Wentz.

chunks.title: Traci Stumpf
chunks.text: She is the host of a new MTV show called GameChanger currently filming in New York, as well working on new shows currently in development with production company DiGa.

chunks.title: Traci Stumpf
chunks.text: Her unique brand of comedic hosting was one of the reasons she was named one of the "Four Comedians You Need to Check Out this Year" by The Sharpe.

chunks.title: J. Wells
chunks.text: J. Wells (born Jon Wells; 1983 in Chicago) is an American record producer, record executive, and rapper.

chunks.title: J. Wells
chunks.text: He is a member of the Likwit Crew.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: IV Life is the fourth album by West Coast hip hop artist King Tee.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: It is his first album released by MCA Records on March 28, 1995 after his split with Capitol Records.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: It stands as one of King Tee's most diverse albums production-wise as not only King Tee and DJ Pooh produced tracks, but DJ Broadway, Mark Sparks and plenty of other producers lacking previous relationships with King Tee also produce.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: The production on this album is sample reliant and artists sampled include A Tribe Called Quest (on "You Can't See Me"), The Four Tops (on "Dippin'"), Freddie Hubbard (on "3 Strikes Ya' Out") and Grover Washington, Jr. (on "Down Ass Loc").

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: Upon release, "IV Life" received an above average critical reception and reached #10 on the Top Heatseekers list.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: 'It contains King Tee's last charting single, "Dippin'," which has been described as a classic track to play in a car.

chunks.title: IV Life
chunks.text: It also contains two less popular singles, "Way Out There" and "Free Style Ghetto" featuring Breeze, Tha Alkaholiks and Likwit Crew newcomer, Xzibit.

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: 21 & Over is the debut album by West Coast hip hop group, Tha Alkaholiks.

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: It is highly praised, and has been described as "the quintessential West Coast party album."

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: It has ten tracks, timed at only about 35 minutes, but it contains three singles, "Make Room," "Likwit" and "Mary Jane."

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: None of these singles reached The Billboard Hot 100, but they all did well on the Hot Dance Music/Maxi-Singles Sales chart.

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: The only single that contains vocals from anybody other than Tash and J-Ro is "Likwit," which features King Tee.

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: King Tee is responsible for founding Tha Alkaholiks, and the track's title is a reference to the Likwit Crew that he created.

chunks.title: 21 & Over (album)
chunks.text: Lootpack and Threat are the only other guest vocalists on this album, but production is provided by Tha Alkaholiks, King Tee, Lootpack and Derick "D. Pimp" Williams.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: Tha Triflin' Album is the third album by West Coast hip hop artist King Tee.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: It was panned critically for being dated and containing a "lighter rap approach."

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: It contains two singles; "Got It Bad Y'all" featuring Tha Alkaholiks and "Black Togetha Again."

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: Neither of them charted, but "Tha Triflin' Album" performed better on the "Billboard" 200 chart than any other King Tee album.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: This relative commercial success can be attributed to guest appearances by Tha Alkaholiks and Ice Cube as well as hip hop newcomers Nefretitti, Coke and Dr. Soose of Mad Kap and Deadly Threat.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: The production, handled by producers including Tha Alkaholiks, DJ Pooh and Marley Marl may have also attributed to the album's reception.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: The success of this album is quite significant as it allowed King Tee's protégés, Tha Alkaholiks, to gain a following.

chunks.title: Tha Triflin' Album
chunks.text: It also provided a foundation for King Tee's Likwit Crew.

chunks.title: Revival meeting
chunks.text: A revival meeting is a series of Christian religious services held to inspire active members of a church body to gain new converts.

chunks.title: Revival meeting
chunks.text: Nineteenth-century Baptist preacher Charles Spurgeon said, "Many blessings may come to the unconverted in consequence of a revival among Christians, but the revival itself has to do only with those who already possess spiritual life."

chunks.title: Revival meeting
chunks.text: These meetings are usually conducted by churches or missionary organizations throughout the world.

chunks.title: Revival meeting
chunks.text: Notable historic revival meetings were conducted in the US by evangelist Billy Sunday and in Wales by evangelist Evan Roberts.

chunks.title: Evangelical Christian Church in Canada
chunks.text: The Evangelical Christian Church (Christian Disciples) as an evangelical Protestant Canadian church body in North America (2004) can be traced to the formal organization of the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) in 1804, in Bourbon County, Kentucky under the leadership of Barton Warren Stone (1772–1844).

chunks.title: Evangelical Christian Church in Canada
chunks.text: The Stone Movement later merged with the efforts of Thomas Campbell (1772–1854) and his son Alexander Campbell (1788–1866) to become the Restoration Movement that gave birth to the Churches of Christ (Non-Instrumental), the Christian churches and churches of Christ, the Churches of Christ (non-institutional), and the Disciples of Christ.

chunks.title: Evangelical Christian Church in Canada
chunks.text: The Evangelical Christian Church (Christian Disciples) as a separate group within the Restoration tradition was reorganized in 2001.

chunks.title: Evangelical Christian Church in Canada
chunks.text: The Evangelical Christian Church's national office in Canada is in Waterloo, Ontario.

chunks.title: Francis Asbury (Lukeman)
chunks.text: Francis Asbury, also known as the Francis Asbury Memorial, is a public equestrian statue, by American artist Augustus Lukeman, located at 16th Street and Mt. Pleasant Street, Northwest, Washington, D.C., in the Mount Pleasant neighborhood.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: A Christian music festival (also known as a Jesus music festival or simply a Jesus festival) is a music festival held by the Christian community, in support of performers of Christian music.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: The festivals are characterized by more than just music; many feature motivational speakers and evangelists, and include seminars on Christian spiritual and missions topics, service, and evangelism.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: They are often viewed as evangelical tools, and small festivals can draw 10 times the crowd of traditional revival meetings.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: While the central theme of a Christian festival is Jesus Christ, the core appeal of a Christian music festival remains the artists and their music.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: Critics point out that the dichotomy of business and religious interests can be problematic for Christian festivals.

chunks.title: Christian music festival
chunks.text: In similar ways as the Christian music industry in general, festivals can be drawn away from their central theme and gravitate toward commercialization and mainstream acts in an attempt to draw crowds.

chunks.title: Revival of 1800
chunks.text: The Revival of 1800 was a series of evangelical Christian meetings which began in Logan County, Kentucky, which ignited the subsequent events and influenced several of the leaders of the Second Great Awakening.

chunks.title: Revival of 1800
chunks.text: The events represented a transition from traditions carried over from Europe to innovations that responded to the unique needs and personality of Americans in the new century.

chunks.title: Revival of 1800
chunks.text: The startling manifestations of revival fervor that first occurred in June 1800 at the Red River Meeting House, a small Presbyterian congregation led by James McGready, began as a Scottish sacrament service, but brought about the important innovation of serial religious services later known as camp meetings.

chunks.title: Revival of 1800
chunks.text: These multi-day gatherings hosted people from great distances for outdoor services focused on the heart-felt conversion and religious enthusiasm that came to characterize especially rural evangelicalism throughout the nineteenth century.

chunks.title: Revival of 1800
chunks.text: The Logan County revival quickly spread into the larger Cumberland region of southwestern Kentucky and middle Tennessee and expanded outward in all directions attracting the attention of evangelical leaders such as Presbyterian-turned-Disciples of Christ leader, Barton Stone, and Methodists Francis Asbury and Peter Cartwright, as well as leaders in the Shaker and Cumberland Presbyterian movements, all of whom attended the revival meetings in their initial year-long period beginning in June 1800 and continuing through May 1801.

chunks.title: Brownsville Revival
chunks.text: The Brownsville Revival (also known as the Pensacola Outpouring) was a widely reported Christian revival within the Pentecostal Movement that began on Father's Day June 18, 1995, at Brownsville Assembly of God in Pensacola, Florida.

chunks.title: Brownsville Revival
chunks.text: Characteristics of the Brownsville Revival movement, as with other Christian religious revivals, included acts of repentance by parishioners and a call to holiness, said to be inspired by the manifestation of the Holy Spirit.

chunks.title: Brownsville Revival
chunks.text: Some of the occurrences in this revival fit the description of moments of religious ecstasy.

chunks.title: Brownsville Revival
chunks.text: More than four million people are reported to have attended the revival meetings from its beginnings in 1995 to around 2000.

chunks.title: Falcon Tabernacle
chunks.text: The Falcon Tabernacle, also known as the Octagon Tabernacle and the Little Tabernacle, is an historic octagon-shaped Pentecostal Holiness church building in Falcon, North Carolina.

chunks.title: Falcon Tabernacle
chunks.text: Built in 1898, it was designed by Julius A. Culbreth (1871-1950) for prayer meetings and was built using wood from trees that had been uprooted by a tornado.

chunks.title: Falcon Tabernacle
chunks.text: Culbreth, who was the founder of Falcon, chose the octagon shape because it reminded him of the tents used in revival meetings.

chunks.title: Falcon Tabernacle
chunks.text: In 1900 the building became the home of the Falcon Pentecostal Holiness Church, of which Culbreth was a leader.

chunks.title: Tent revival
chunks.text: A tent revival is a gathering of Christian worshipers in a tent erected specifically for revival meetings, healing crusades, and church rallies.

chunks.title: Tent revival
chunks.text: Tent revivals have had both local and national ministries.

chunks.title: Francis Asbury
chunks.text: Francis Asbury ( ; August 20 or 21, 1745 – March 31, 1816) was one of the first two bishops of the Methodist Episcopal Church in the United States.

chunks.title: Francis Asbury
chunks.text: As a young man in October 1771, the Englishman traveled to America and, during his 45 years there, he devoted his life to ministry, traveling on horseback and by carriage thousands of miles to those living on the frontier.

chunks.title: John S. Coffman
chunks.text: John S. Coffman (October 16, 1848 – July 22, 1899) was a leader in the Mennonite Church in the late 19th century.

chunks.title: John S. Coffman
chunks.text: He promoted evangelical and progressive reform through his positions in the Mennonite Publishing Company, revival meetings and chairmanship of the Elkhart Institute (a forerunner to Goshen College).

chunks.title: The Good Provider
chunks.text: The Good Provider is a 1922 American silent drama film directed by Frank Borzage and written by Fannie Hurst and John Lynch.

chunks.title: The Good Provider
chunks.text: The film stars Vera Gordon, Dore Davidson, Miriam Battista, Vivienne Osborne, William Collier, Jr., John Roche, and Ora Jones.

chunks.title: The Good Provider
chunks.text: The film was released on April 2, 1922, by Paramount Pictures.

chunks.title: The Good Provider
chunks.text: It is not known whether the film currently survives.

chunks.title: Bought and Paid For
chunks.text: Bought and Paid For is a lost 1922 American silent drama film produced by Famous Players-Lasky and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

chunks.title: Bought and Paid For
chunks.text: It was directed by William C. deMille and starred Agnes Ayres.

chunks.title: Bought and Paid For
chunks.text: It is based on a play by George Broadhurst performed on Broadway in 1911 with Julia Dean and revived 1921 respectively.

chunks.title: Bought and Paid For
chunks.text: The play was filmed before in 1916 by the World Film Company with Alice Brady in the lead role.

chunks.title: A Doll's House (1922 film)
chunks.text: A Doll's House is a 1922 American silent drama film produced by and starring Alla Nazimova and directed by her husband Charles Bryant.

chunks.title: A Doll's House (1922 film)
chunks.text: The couple released the film through United Artists.

chunks.title: A Doll's House (1922 film)
chunks.text: It is based on the play "A Doll's House" by Henrik Ibsen with the scenario written by Nazimova under the pseudonym Peter M. Winters.

chunks.title: A Doll's House (1922 film)
chunks.text: The film was the fourth silent version filmed of the play, being preceded by a 1918 Paramount film directed by Maurice Tourneur.

chunks.title: A Doll's House (1922 film)
chunks.text: The film is classified as being lost.

chunks.title: The Man Who Played God (1922 film)
chunks.text: The Man Who Played God is a 1922 American silent drama film directed by F. Harmon Weight and written by Forrest Halsey.

chunks.title: The Man Who Played God (1922 film)
chunks.text: The film stars George Arliss, Ann Forrest, Ivan Simpson, Edward Earle, and Effie Shannon.

chunks.title: The Man Who Played God (1922 film)
chunks.text: The film was released on October 1, 1922, by United Artists.

chunks.title: The Law and the Woman
chunks.text: The Law and the Woman is a lost 1922 American silent drama film directed by Penrhyn Stanlaws and starring Betty Compson.

chunks.title: The Law and the Woman
chunks.text: This film is a version of Clyde Fitch's play "The Woman in the Case" and a remake of a 1916 silent version "The Woman in the Case" starring Pauline Frederick.

chunks.title: The Law and the Woman
chunks.text: Jesse Lasky produced.

chunks.title: Outcast (1922 film)
chunks.text: Outcast is a 1922 American silent drama film directed by Chester Withey.

chunks.title: Outcast (1922 film)
chunks.text: The film starred Elsie Ferguson (in her next to last silent) and David Powell.

chunks.title: Outcast (1922 film)

chunks.title: Rock City, New York

chunks.title: Rock City, New York

chunks.title: WYPX-TV
chunks.text: WYPX-TV is a full-service television station, licensed to Amsterdam, New York, as the affiliate of the Ion Television (formerly Pax and i) network in the New York state's Capital District and Mohawk Valley.

chunks.title: WYPX-TV
chunks.text: The station's broadcast is digital-only on UHF channel 50 from a transmitter located near New York State Route 30 near the Montgomery/Fulton County line, and is carried on Time Warner Cable in much of the Albany market on channel 20.

chunks.title: WYPX-TV
chunks.text: WYPX can also be seen on the eastern fringes of the Utica market.

chunks.title: WYPX-TV

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: Yonkers Avenue is an east–west street in the city of Yonkers in Westchester County, New York, in the United States.

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: It is one of four major east–west through routes in the city.

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: The western terminus of the street is at Nepperhan Avenue, which connects to U.S. Route 9 (US 9) and New York State Route 9A (NY 9A).

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: Its eastern terminus is at Bronx River Road near the Bronx River Parkway.

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: The entirety of Yonkers Avenue is maintained by the New York State Department of Transportation as New York State Route 983C from Nepperhan Avenue to the Saw Mill River Parkway and New York State Route 984E from the Saw Mill Parkway to Bronx River Road.

chunks.title: Yonkers Avenue
chunks.text: Both are unsigned reference route designations.

chunks.title: New York State Route 308
chunks.text: New York State Route 308 (NY 308) is a short state highway, 6.19 mi in length, located entirely in northern Dutchess County, in the U.S. state of New York.

chunks.title: New York State Route 308
chunks.text: It is a major collector road through mostly rural areas that serves primarily as a shortcut for traffic from the two main north–south routes in the area, U.S. Route 9 (US 9) and NY 9G, to get to NY 199 and the Taconic State Parkway.

chunks.title: New York State Route 308
chunks.text: The western end of NY 308 is located within the Rhinebeck Village Historic District, a 2.6 sqmi historic district comprising 272 historical structures.

chunks.title: New York State Route 308
chunks.text: The highway passes near the Dutchess County Fairgrounds, several historical landmarks, and the Landsman Kill.

chunks.title: Washington State Route 308
chunks.text: State Route 308 (SR 308) is a 3.42 mi state highway in the U.S. state of Washington, serving the community of Keyport in Kitsap County.

chunks.title: Washington State Route 308
chunks.text: The highway travels generally east from an interchange with SR 3 east of Naval Base Kitsap at Bangor to the main entrance of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center in Keyport.

chunks.title: Washington State Route 308
chunks.text: SR 308 was codified as the Keyport branch of State Road 21 in 1929 and continued as the Keyport branch of Primary State Highway 21 (PSH 21) in 1937.

chunks.title: Washington State Route 308
chunks.text: During the 1964 highway renumbering, the branch became a section of SR 303, which ran from Bremerton to Bangor and had a spur route serving Keyport.

chunks.title: Washington State Route 308
chunks.text: SR 308 was established in 1971 along the old route of SR 303 Spur and was extended in 1991 to the SR 3 freeway after SR 303 was re-routed onto a new freeway in Silverdale.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 308
chunks.text: State Route 308 (SR 308) is a north–south state highway in the central portion of Ohio, a U.S. state.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 308
chunks.text: The southern terminus of SR 308 is at SR 229 in the western end of the village of Gambier, and its northern terminus is 3 mi to the north of that point at a T-intersection with U.S. Route 36 (US 36) that is located approximately 1+1/2 mi east of the city limits of Mount Vernon.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: State Route 29 (SR 29) is an east–west state highway in the west-central portion of the U.S. state of Ohio.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: Its western terminus is at the Indiana state line near Celina, where State Road 67 continues west.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: It continues east to St. Marys where it junctions with U.S. Route 33.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: In that town, it also crosses State Route 66, State Route 116, and State Route 703, which was its former alignment before a divided highway was built.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: After turning south it crosses State Route 219 in New Knoxville and then has an interchange with Interstate 75, continuing into Sidney where it meets State Route 47.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: Still going southeast, it briefly joins State Route 235 before turning east and then south again to enter Urbana.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: Here the route joins U.S. Route 36, and the concurrency intersects with U.S. Route 68 and State Route 54.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: From there, State Route 29 leaves U.S. Route 36 and continues to Mutual, intersecting with State Route 161, and State Route 56 shortly after; later, in Mechanicsburg, the route intersects with State Route 4.

chunks.title: Ohio State Route 29
chunks.text: The route then intersects with State Route 38, U.S. Route 42, and Interstate 70 before reaching its eastern terminus at U.S. Route 40 on the western edge of West Jefferson.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Route 44
chunks.text: Pennsylvania Route 44 (PA 44) is a 149.24 mi -long state highway in the U.S. state of Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Route 44
chunks.text: The route is designated from Interstate 80 and Pennsylvania Route 42 in Buckhorn to the New York state line near New York State Route 417 in Ceres Township.

chunks.title: Kill (body of water)
chunks.text: As a body of water, a kill is a creek.

chunks.title: Kill (body of water)

chunks.title: Georgia State Route 308
chunks.text: State Route 308 (SR 308) is a northwest-southeast state highway located in the southwest part of the U.S. state of Georgia.

chunks.title: Georgia State Route 308
