chunks.title: Karen Clark Sheard
chunks.text: Karen Clark-Sheard (born Karen Valencia Clark; November 15, 1960) also known as "The Maestris Of Gospel" is an American gospel four-time Grammy Award-winning singer, musician, and songwriter.

chunks.title: Karen Clark Sheard
chunks.text: The youngest daughter of pioneering gospel choral director Mattie Moss Clark, Sheard began her career as a member of the legendary Grammy Award-winning female gospel group The Clark Sisters.

chunks.title: Karen Clark Sheard
chunks.text: She is the mother of contemporary gospel singer and actress Kierra "Kiki" Sheard.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: David Huntsinger is a pianist, composer, songwriter, and arranger who moved from his native California to Nashville, TN, in 1976 and played for the Rambos.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He co-wrote the song, "Holy Spirit, Thou Art Welcome", with Dottie Rambo, as well as the children’s musical, "Down By The Creek Bank".

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: In 1979 he left the Rambos to pursue a career as a studio pianist.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He wrote and arranged music for the 1989 Grammy-winning album "A Child’s Gift of Lullabyes", and arranged for and co-produced Andy Griffith’s 1996 Grammy-winning album, "I Love To Tell The Story: 25 Timeless Hymns".

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He has worked with many artists, such as Sandi Patti, Steve Green, Kathy Troccoli, Michael Crawford, Glen Campbell, Carman, Larnelle Harris, Johnny Cash and Dolly Parton.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He toured with Vince Gill for a Christmas tour in 1999, and in 2001 for the Amy Grant/Vince Gill Christmas tour.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He has also written a number of children’s musicals, as well as produced many albums of his own original works and arrangements.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He played the piano for "An Unfinished Life", and contributed to two songs heard in "The Great Debaters".

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He arranged for and played piano in the 1997 Christmas album "Piano Winterlude" (Unison).

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: He has done several projects for Discovery House Music.

chunks.title: David Huntsinger
chunks.text: In 2010 he composed a number of pieces for a special 25th Anniversary concert for the international television network 3ABN called "Pillars of Our Faith".

chunks.title: Just as I Am (Yolanda Adams album)
chunks.text: Just as I Am is the debut album by gospel singer Yolanda Adams, released on September 22, 1987 on the Sound of Gospel label and produced by Thomas Whitfield, who also worked with singer Vanessa Bell Armstrong on early 1980s gospel releases.

chunks.title: Just as I Am (Yolanda Adams album)
chunks.text: Though original pressings of the vinyl and cassette release are difficult to find, the album has since been re-released on CD along with another catalog album from Sound of Gospel by Wanda Nero Butler entitled "New Born Soul".

chunks.title: Andraé Crouch
chunks.text: Andraé Edward Crouch (July 1, 1942 – January 8, 2015) was an American gospel singer, songwriter, arranger, record producer and pastor.

chunks.title: Andraé Crouch
chunks.text: Referred to as "the father of modern gospel music" by contemporary Christian and gospel music professionals, Crouch was known for his compositions "The Blood Will Never Lose Its Power", "My Tribute (To God Be the Glory)" and "Soon and Very Soon".

chunks.title: Andraé Crouch
chunks.text: In secular music, he was known for his collaborative work during the 1980s and 1990s with Stevie Wonder, Elton John and Quincy Jones as well as conducting choirs that sang on the Michael Jackson hit "Man in the Mirror" and Madonna's "Like a Prayer".

chunks.title: Andraé Crouch
chunks.text: Crouch was noted for his talent of incorporating contemporary secular music styles into the gospel music he grew up with.

chunks.title: Andraé Crouch
chunks.text: His efforts in this area helped pave the way for early American contemporary Christian music during the 1960s and 1970s.

chunks.title: J-Shin
chunks.text: Jonathan "J-Shin" Shinoster is a contemporary R&B/gospel singer born in Liberty City, Florida, who was signed to Slip-n-Slide Records/Atlantic Records and is best known for his hit single "One Night Stand" with LaTocha Scott of Xscape.

chunks.title: Larnelle Harris
chunks.text: Larnelle Steward Harris (born July 6, 1947) is an American gospel singer and songwriter.

chunks.title: Larnelle Harris
chunks.text: During his 30-plus years of ministry, Harris has recorded 18 albums, won five Grammy Awards and 11 Dove Awards, and has had several number one songs on the inspirational music charts.

chunks.title: Kierra Sheard
chunks.text: Kierra Valencia "Kiki" Sheard (born June 20, 1987 in Detroit, Michigan) is an American gospel singer, fashion designer, and radio host.

chunks.title: Kierra Sheard
chunks.text: She is the daughter of gospel singer Karen Clark Sheard (member of gospel singing group The Clark Sisters) and the granddaughter of gospel choral director Mattie Moss Clark.

chunks.title: Kierra Sheard
chunks.text: Sheard portrayed Litha in the 2010 Christian-drama film "Preacher's Kid".

chunks.title: Kierra Sheard
chunks.text: After appearing on her mother's albums, Sheard broke onto the music scene with the release of her debut album "I Owe You" in 2004.

chunks.title: Kierra Sheard
chunks.text: Her hit single "You Don't Know" was written about her mother's bout with an almost fatal blood clot.

chunks.title: Charles Charamba
chunks.text: Charles Charamba (born 27 April 1971) is a Zimbabwean gospel musician and a pastor in the Apostolic Faith Mission Church of Zimbabwe.

chunks.title: Charles Charamba
chunks.text: Charamba's albums have been the top selling gospel music in Zimbabwe since the early 2000s.

chunks.title: Charles Charamba
chunks.text: He has toured both Great Britain and the United States, and throughout southern Africa.

chunks.title: Charles Charamba
chunks.text: One of Charamba's most famous songs is “Machira Chete”.

chunks.title: Charles Charamba
chunks.text: His wife, Olivia (née Maseko), is also a gospel singer, and appears with him on stage and on his albums; they are often called the "First Family of Gospel".

chunks.title: Latice Crawford
chunks.text: Latice Crawford (born July 22, 1982 as Latice Tenae Crawford) is an American urban contemporary gospel singer and composer.

chunks.title: Latice Crawford
chunks.text: She is best known for using her three-octave, contralto vocal range of to finish third on the second season of the competitive gospel singing television show "Sunday Best" on Black Entertainment Television.

chunks.title: Latice Crawford
chunks.text: Her self-titled debut album reached two "Billboard" charts, the Top Gospel Albums and the Top Heatseekers.

chunks.title: Latice Crawford
chunks.text: Her second album, "Diary of a Church Girl", also appeared on the Top Gospel Albums chart.

chunks.title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
chunks.text: Muyiwa Olarewaju (born 26 November is a British Gospel singer and songwriter who mixes traditional gospel music with elements of world music (from Africa, the Caribbean and Asia), soul, R&B and pop.

chunks.title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
chunks.text: He is also an experienced performer, broadcaster and presenter.

chunks.title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
chunks.text: In 2009 he became the first-ever international act to perform on America's popular entertainment channel, BET, for the prestigious annual Celebration of Gospel show.

chunks.title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
chunks.text: He has presented the Turning Point programme to an estimated global audience of 70 million.

chunks.title: Muyiwa Olarewaju
chunks.text: With his group Riversongz, he sold out Indigo2 at the O2 in London, the first gospel act to do so, and he has played at the largest gospel music event in the world, The Experience, attracting a 500,000 strong audience.

chunks.title: Don Larsen's perfect game
chunks.text: On October 8, 1956, in Game 5 of the 1956 World Series, Don Larsen of the New York Yankees threw a perfect game against the Brooklyn Dodgers.

chunks.title: Don Larsen's perfect game
chunks.text: Larsen's perfect game is the only perfect game in the history of the World Series; it is one of only 23 perfect games in MLB history.

chunks.title: Don Larsen's perfect game
chunks.text: His perfect game remained the only no-hitter of any type ever pitched in postseason play until Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Roy Halladay threw a no-hitter against the Cincinnati Reds on October 6, 2010, in Game 1 of the National League Division Series, and the only postseason game in which any team faced the minimum 27 batters until Kyle Hendricks and Aroldis Chapman of the Chicago Cubs managed to combine for the feat in the decisive sixth game of the 2016 National League Championship Series.

chunks.title: 1998 Minnesota Twins season
chunks.text: Like many Twins teams of its half-decade, the 1998 Minnesota Twins neither impressed nor contended.

chunks.title: 1998 Minnesota Twins season
chunks.text: The team finished with a 70-92 record, with subpar batting and pitching.

chunks.title: 1998 Minnesota Twins season
chunks.text: The season was not without its bright spots, as individual players had solid seasons and Hall of Fame designated hitter Paul Molitor announced his retirement at the end of the season.

chunks.title: 1998 Minnesota Twins season
chunks.text: Tom Kelly's team had plenty of lowlights, most notably David Wells' perfect game against the team on May 17 at Yankee Stadium.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: The Oakland Athletics are a Major League Baseball franchise based in Oakland, California.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: They play in the American League West division.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: Also known in their early years as the “Philadelphia Athletics” (1901–54) and “Kansas City Athletics” (1954–67), pitchers for the Athletics have thrown eleven no-hitters in franchise history, five during the Philadelphia years and six after the move to Oakland but none during the Kansas City era.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: A no-hitter is officially recognized by Major League Baseball only “when a pitcher (or pitchers) retires each batter on the opposing team during the entire course of a game, which consists of at least nine innings.”

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: No-hitters of less than nine complete innings were previously recognized by the league as official; however, several rule alterations in 1991 changed the rule to its current form.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: A no-hitter is rare enough that one team in Major League Baseball has never had a pitcher accomplish the feat.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: Two perfect games, a special subcategory of no-hitter, have been pitched in Athletics history.

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: As defined by Major League Baseball, “in a perfect game, no batter reaches any base during the course of the game.”

chunks.title: List of Oakland Athletics no-hitters
chunks.text: These feats were achieved by Catfish Hunter in 1968, which was the first perfect game in American League history since 1922, and Dallas Braden in 2010, which was the second perfect game in the majors – both against the same team – in ten months.

chunks.title: Paul Molitor
chunks.text: Paul Leo Molitor (born August 22, 1956), nicknamed "Molly" and "The Ignitor", is an American former Major League Baseball (MLB) player and current manager of the Minnesota Twins, who is in the Baseball Hall of Fame.

chunks.title: Paul Molitor
chunks.text: During his 21-year baseball career, he played for the Milwaukee Brewers (1978–1992), Toronto Blue Jays (1993–1995), and Minnesota Twins (1996–1998).

chunks.title: Paul Molitor
chunks.text: He was known for his exceptional hitting and speed.

chunks.title: Paul Molitor
chunks.text: He made seven All-Star Game appearances and was the World Series MVP in 1993.

chunks.title: Dennis Martínez's perfect game
chunks.text: On July 28, 1991, Dennis Martínez of the Montreal Expos pitched the 13th perfect game in Major League Baseball history, blanking the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-0 at Dodger Stadium.

chunks.title: Dennis Martínez's perfect game
chunks.text: A native of Granada, Nicaragua, Martínez became the first pitcher born outside of the United States to pitch a perfect game.

chunks.title: Dennis Martínez's perfect game
chunks.text: (He has since been joined by Venezuela native Félix Hernández, who pitched a perfect game in 2012.)

chunks.title: Dennis Martínez's perfect game
chunks.text: The perfect game also made the Dodgers, the losing team in Tom Browning's perfect game in 1988, the first team to be on the losing end of consecutive perfect games; they have since been joined by the Tampa Bay Rays, who were the losing team in Mark Buehrle's perfect game in 2009 and Dallas Braden's perfect game the following year.

chunks.title: Dennis Martínez's perfect game
chunks.text: After completing the perfect game, Martínez slowly walked into the Dodger stadium dugout, sat down by himself and cried.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: The Detroit Tigers are a Major League Baseball franchise based in Detroit, Michigan.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: They play in the American League Central division.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: Pitchers for the Tigers have thrown seven no-hitters in franchise history.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: A no-hitter is officially recognized by Major League Baseball only "when a pitcher (or pitchers) allows no hits during the entire course of a game, which consists of at least nine innings.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: In a no-hit game, a batter may reach base via a walk, an error, a hit by pitch, a passed ball or wild pitch on strike three, or catcher's interference."

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: No-hitters of less than nine complete innings were previously recognized by the league as official; however, several rule alterations in 1991 changed the rule to its current form.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: A no-hitter is common enough that only one team in Major League Baseball has never had a pitcher accomplish the feat.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: A perfect game, a special subcategory of no-hitter, has yet to be thrown in Tigers history.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: As defined by Major League Baseball, "in a perfect game, no batter reaches any base during the course of the game."

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: This feat came closest on June 2, 2010 when Armando Galarraga lost his perfect game bid against the Cleveland Indians with two outs in the ninth due to the incorrect call made by a first base umpire Jim Joyce.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: But there are two other times when the Tigers perfect game bids were lost with two outs in the ninth, one in 1932 and the other in 1983.

chunks.title: List of Detroit Tigers no-hitters
chunks.text: The Tigers lead all franchises with three perfect game bids lost with two outs in the ninth.

chunks.title: Sandy Koufax's perfect game
chunks.text: Sandy Koufax of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitched a perfect game in the National League against the Chicago Cubs at Dodger Stadium on September 9, 1965.

chunks.title: Sandy Koufax's perfect game
chunks.text: Koufax, by retiring 27 consecutive batters without allowing any to reach base, became the sixth pitcher of the modern era, eighth overall, to throw a perfect game.

chunks.title: Sandy Koufax's perfect game
chunks.text: The game was Koufax's fourth no-hitter, breaking Bob Feller's Major League record of three (and later broken by Nolan Ryan, in 1981).

chunks.title: Sandy Koufax's perfect game
chunks.text: Koufax struck out 14 opposing batters, the most ever recorded in a perfect game, and matched only by San Francisco Giants pitcher, Matt Cain, on June 13, 2012.

chunks.title: Sandy Koufax's perfect game
chunks.text: He also struck out at least one batter in all nine innings (Cain did not strike out a batter in the ninth in his perfect game), the only perfect game pitcher to do so to date.

chunks.title: Matt Cain's perfect game
chunks.text: On June 13, 2012, Matt Cain of the San Francisco Giants pitched the 22nd perfect game (no opposing batters reach first base) in Major League Baseball (MLB) history and the first in Giants' franchise history.

chunks.title: Matt Cain's perfect game
chunks.text: Pitching against the Houston Astros at AT&T Park in San Francisco, California, Cain retired all 27 batters that he faced and tallied 14 strikeouts, tied for the most strikeouts in a perfect game with Sandy Koufax of the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965.

chunks.title: Matt Cain's perfect game
chunks.text: Following Philip Humber's perfect game earlier in 2012, Cain's performance marked just the third season in MLB history in which multiple perfect games were thrown.

chunks.title: Matt Cain's perfect game
chunks.text: In June 1880, Lee Richmond and John Montgomery Ward both threw perfect games; in May 2010 Dallas Braden and Roy Halladay both accomplished the feat.

chunks.title: Randy Johnson's perfect game
chunks.text: On May 18, 2004, Randy Johnson, who was a pitcher for the Major League Baseball (MLB) Arizona Diamondbacks, pitched a perfect game against the Atlanta Braves.

chunks.title: Randy Johnson's perfect game
chunks.text: The game took place at Turner Field in Atlanta in front of a crowd of 23,381 people.

chunks.title: Randy Johnson's perfect game
chunks.text: Johnson, who was 40 at the time, was the oldest pitcher in MLB history to throw a perfect game, surpassing Cy Young who was 37 when he threw his perfect game in 1904.

chunks.title: Randy Johnson's perfect game
chunks.text: The perfect game was the 17th in baseball history, the predecessor being David Cone in 1999 and the seventh in National League history, the predecessor being Dennis Martínez in 1991.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: Over the 140 years of Major League Baseball history, and over 210,000 games played, there have been 23 official perfect games by the current definition.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: No pitcher has ever thrown more than one.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: The perfect game thrown by Don Larsen in game 5 of the 1956 World Series is the only postseason perfect game in major league history and one of only two postseason no-hitters, the other being a no-hitter thrown by Roy Halladay in game 1 of the 2010 National League Division Series against the Cincinnati Reds.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: The first two major league perfect games, and the only two of the premodern era, were thrown in 1880, five days apart.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: The most recent perfect game was thrown on August 15, 2012 by Félix Hernández of the Seattle Mariners.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: There were three perfect games in 2012, with no other year ever having more than two thrown.

chunks.title: List of Major League Baseball perfect games
chunks.text: By contrast, there have been spans of 23 and 33 consecutive seasons in which not a single perfect game was thrown.

chunks.title: Hidden City (album)
chunks.text: Hidden City is the tenth studio album by the British rock band The Cult, released on 5 February 2016 through Cooking Vinyl and Dine Alone Records.

chunks.title: Hidden City (album)
chunks.text: It is the final part of a trilogy that began with "Born into This" (2007), and The Cult's first album since their 1994 self-titled album not to feature bassist Chris Wyse; the role was filled by producer Bob Rock and Jane's Addiction bassist Chris Chaney.

chunks.title: Hidden City (album)
chunks.text: It also marks the fifth time Rock had produced a Cult album.

chunks.title: Tripcombi
chunks.text: Tripcombi, founded in 2012, as Tripdelta, is an online startup.

chunks.title: Tripcombi
chunks.text: Free for users, it is a flight search engine that enables travelers to find airfares globally from different online travel agencies and airlines.

chunks.title: Tripcombi
chunks.text: It does this by using hidden flight routing and hidden city ticketing techniques.

chunks.title: Tripcombi
chunks.text: Tripdelta's tactics include combining two separate ticket bookings, searching airfares on low-cost carriers, and booking passengers in the airports close to their place of departure and their intended destination.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2015
chunks.text: The 2015 Best Footballer in Asia, given to the best football player in Asia as judged by a panel of 20 sports journalists, was awarded to Son Heung-min on the 28th December, 2015.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2015
chunks.text: Son Heung-min became the first footballer who won Best Footballer in Asia for more than one time, and the first footballer who won this trophy in succession.

chunks.title: Oleksandr Zavarov
chunks.text: Oleksandr Anatoliyovych Zavarov, also spelt Aleksandr Anatoljević Zavarov (Ukrainian: Олександр Анатолійович Заваров , Russian: Заваров, Александр Анатольевич ) – (born 26 April 1961 in Luhansk, Ukrainian SSR) is a former Ukrainian football midfielder and the former head coach at FC Arsenal Kyiv.

chunks.title: Oleksandr Zavarov
chunks.text: In 1986, he was named the best footballer in the USSR and Ukraine and the 6th best footballer in Europe according to France Football.

chunks.title: Oleksandr Zavarov
chunks.text: Zavarov is widely regarded to be among the greatest footballers in the history of the USSR and Ukraine, and in 2000 he was included in the Ukrainian Team of The Century according to a poll by the "Ukrainsky Futbol" weekly.

chunks.title: Shinji Okazaki
chunks.text: Shinji Okazaki (岡崎 慎司 , Okazaki Shinji , born 16 April 1986) is a Japanese footballer who plays for Leicester City and the Japan national team as a forward.

chunks.title: Hugo Sánchez
chunks.text: Hugo Sánchez Márquez (born 11 July 1958) is a retired Mexican professional footballer and manager, who played as a forward.

chunks.title: Hugo Sánchez
chunks.text: A prolific goalscorer known for his spectacular strikes and volleys, Sánchez is widely regarded as Mexico's greatest-ever footballer, and one of the greatest players of his generation.

chunks.title: Hugo Sánchez
chunks.text: In 1999, the International Federation of Football History and Statistics voted Sánchez the 26th best footballer of the 20th century, and the best footballer from the CONCACAF region.

chunks.title: Hugo Sánchez
chunks.text: In 2004 Sánchez was named in the FIFA 100 list of the world's greatest living players.

chunks.title: Hugo Sánchez
chunks.text: He is the fourth highest scorer in the history of Spain's top division, and is the sixth highest goalscorer in Real Madrid's history.

chunks.title: South American Footballer of the Year
chunks.text: The Rey del Fútbol de América ("King of Football of America"), often referred to as the South American Footballer of the Year, is an annual association football award presented to the best footballer in South America over the previous calendar year.

chunks.title: South American Footballer of the Year
chunks.text: The award was conceived by Venezuelan newspaper "El Mundo", which awarded it from 1971 to 1985.

chunks.title: South American Footballer of the Year
chunks.text: Uruguayan newspaper "El País" took over from 1986 onwards.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2013
chunks.text: The Best Footballer in Asia 2013 was the inaugural Best Footballer in Asia.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2013
chunks.text: Based upon the voting of a panel of 22 journalists the winner was Keisuke Honda.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2013
chunks.text: On March 16, 2014, the trophy was conferred to Keisuke Honda by Luo Ming, the deputy chief editor of Titan Sports in San Siro stadium.

chunks.title: Best Footballer in Asia 2016
chunks.text: The 2016 Best Footballer in Asia, given to the best football player in Asia as judged by a panel of 38 sports journalists, was awarded to Shinji Okazaki on Dec 26th, 2016.

chunks.title: Steven Gerrard
chunks.text: Steven George Gerrard {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (born 30 May 1980) is an English professional football coach and former professional footballer who serves as an academy coach at Liverpool.

chunks.title: Steven Gerrard
chunks.text: He spent the majority of his playing career as a central midfielder for Liverpool and the England national team, with most of that time spent as club captain.

chunks.title: Steven Gerrard
chunks.text: Regarded as one of the greatest midfielders of his generation, Gerrard was awarded the UEFA Club Footballer of the Year award in 2005, and the Ballon d'Or Bronze Award.

chunks.title: Steven Gerrard
chunks.text: In 2009, Zinedine Zidane and Pelé said that they considered Gerrard to be the best footballer in the world.

chunks.title: Steven Gerrard
chunks.text: A versatile and well-rounded player, highly regarded for his leadership, Gerrard is the only footballer in history to score in an FA Cup Final, a League Cup Final, a UEFA Cup Final and a UEFA Champions League Final, winning on each occasion.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: The Miracle at the New Meadowlands, also called "New Miracle at the New Meadowlands and "Miracle at the Meadowlands II" is the term used by sportscasters and Philadelphia Eagles fans to refer to an improbable come-from-behind win by the Philadelphia Eagles over rival team the New York Giants at New Meadowlands Stadium on December 19, 2010.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: The game was a crucial one in the context of the season, played between two divisional rivals in Week 15 of the 2010 NFL season.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: With just under eight minutes to play in the fourth quarter, the Eagles trailed the Giants by 21 points.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: They went on to score four unanswered touchdowns in the final seven minutes and 28 seconds of play, including a punt returned for a touchdown by DeSean Jackson as time expired.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: Jackson became the first player in NFL history to win a game by scoring on a punt return as time expired.

chunks.title: Miracle at the New Meadowlands
chunks.text: The win allowed the Eagles to progress to the 2010 NFL playoffs, where they lost to eventual Super Bowl champion Green Bay.

chunks.title: Chicago Tigers
chunks.text: The Chicago Tigers of the American Professional Football Association (APFA) played only in the first year of the league (1920) and, because of this, have the distinction of being the first NFL team to fold.

chunks.title: Chicago Tigers
chunks.text: They had a record of 2 wins, 5 losses and 1 tie.

chunks.title: Chicago Tigers
chunks.text: The team played its home games at Chicago's Wrigley Field (then called Cubs Park) and was the first NFL team to do so.

chunks.title: Chicago Tigers
chunks.text: The Tigers were never formally members of the APFA.

chunks.title: Chicago Tigers
chunks.text: However, since the team played seven games against APFA teams in 1920, resulting in a 1–5–1 league record, they are generally included in the league standings.

chunks.title: DeSean Jackson
chunks.text: DeSean William Jackson (born December 1, 1986) is an American football wide receiver for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers of the National Football League (NFL).

chunks.title: DeSean Jackson
chunks.text: He played college football for the University of California, Berkeley, where he was recognized as a consensus All-American.

chunks.title: DeSean Jackson
chunks.text: He was drafted by the Philadelphia Eagles in the second round of the 2008 NFL Draft, and played for the Washington Redskins for three seasons after his departure from the Eagles.

chunks.title: DeSean Jackson
chunks.text: Jackson has been selected to the Pro Bowl three times, and was the first player selected to the Pro Bowl at two different positions in the same year when he was named to the 2010 Pro Bowl as a wide receiver and return specialist.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: The 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season began with the team trying to improve on an 2–14 season.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: This was one of the worst seasons in franchise history.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: There is some sentiment that the 1986 team was even worse than the winless team of 1976, and the 473 points conceded was not beaten by any NFL team until the 2001 Indianapolis Colts gave up 486.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: The Buccaneers selected Bo Jackson with the top pick in the draft, but were unable to convince him to join the team.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: Three weeks after the draft, Jackson signed a three-year baseball contract with the Kansas City Royals.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: Despite holding four of the first forty selections in the draft, and the presence of a great influx of fresh talent from defunct USFL teams, the Buccaneers were unable to find any impact players in either the draft or free agency.

chunks.title: 1986 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season
chunks.text: They entered the season with a roster nearly identical to the previous season's 2–14 team.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: The Brooklyn Dodgers were an American football team that played in the National Football League from 1930 to 1943, and in 1944 as the Brooklyn Tigers.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: The team played its home games at Ebbets Field of the baseball National League's team, the Brooklyn Dodgers.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: In 1945, because of financial difficulties and the increasing scarcity of major league-level players because of the war-time defense requirements at the height of World War II, the team was merged with the Boston Yanks and were known as the Yanks for that season.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: This old NFL franchise was not related to the earlier (second incarnation) American Football League II with a franchise that played as the Brooklyn Tigers for the first half of the 1936 season before moving to Rochester, New York and playing as the Rochester Tigers.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: Another NFL team that played in the Brooklyn borough was the Brooklyn Lions (which became the Brooklyn Horsemen after merging with a team from an earlier first incarnation AFL of the same name) in 1926.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: Later co-owner and partner Dan Topping (1912–1974), pulled the Tigers team out of the old NFL in 1946 and placed it in the newly established rival professional league – the All-America Football Conference, which shortly lasted until 1949 until several stronger teams from the AAFC merged with and entered a reorganized NFL in 1950.

chunks.title: Brooklyn Dodgers (NFL)
chunks.text: It lasted until 1970 with the NFL-AFL (third) merger following the establishment of the first "Super Bowl" inter-league national championship game three years before with the old NFL champions playing the victors of the latest rival fourth incarnation of the American Football League IV, formed in 1960 (now the American Football Conference (AFC).

chunks.title: Kevin Warren
chunks.text: Kevin Fulbright Warren (born November 17, 1963) is an attorney and professional sports executive.

chunks.title: Kevin Warren
chunks.text: He is currently the Chief Operating Officer of the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League, and is the highest-ranking African-American executive working on the business side for an NFL team.

chunks.title: Kevin Warren
chunks.text: In 2015, Warren became the first black chief operating officer of an NFL team.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: The Dallas Texans played in the National Football League (NFL) for one season, 1952, with a record of 1–11.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: The team is considered one of the worst teams in NFL history, both on (lowest franchise winning percentage) and off the field.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: The team was based first in Dallas, then Hershey, Pennsylvania, and Akron, Ohio, during its only season.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: The Texans were the last NFL team to fold.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: Many players on the 1952 roster went to the new Baltimore Colts franchise in 1953.

chunks.title: Dallas Texans (NFL)
chunks.text: The American Football League (AFL) had a 1960 charter member named the Dallas Texans (who later became the Kansas City Chiefs), but the AFL Texans have no relationship with the earlier NFL team.

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: John Don Looney (September 2, 1916 – April 5, 2015) was a professional American football end in the National Football League.

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: He was born in Sulphur Springs, Texas.

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: He played three seasons for the Philadelphia Eagles (1940) and the Pittsburgh Steelers (1941–1942).

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: He was the first receiver in NFL history to have over 100 yards receiving in each of his first two games, a feat which was not equaled until the 2008 NFL season by another Eagles wide receiver, DeSean Jackson.

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: At the time of his death, Looney was the second oldest living former NFL player.

chunks.title: Don Looney
chunks.text: He was the father of NFL running back Joe Don Looney, who later died in a one-person motorcycle accident after his NFL career ended.

chunks.title: Tereza Vilišová
chunks.text: Tereza Vilišová (born 1981) is a Czech actress.

chunks.title: Tereza Vilišová
chunks.text: She won the Alfréd Radok Award for Best Actress in 2013 for her role of "Amy" in the D C Jackson play "My Romantic History" at the Divadlo Petra Bezruče in Ostrava.

chunks.title: Tereza Vilišová
chunks.text: At the 2013 Thalia Awards she won the category of Best Actress in a Play for the same work.

chunks.title: Tereza Vilišová
chunks.text: Vilišová joined Prague's National Theatre in 2015.

chunks.title: Fayez Sarofim
chunks.text: Fayez Sarofim (Arabic: فايز صاروفيم‎ ‎ ) (born 1929) is a Coptic American heir to the Sarofim family fortune, fund manager for a number of Dreyfus family stock funds, an original and second largest shareholder of Kinder Morgan (NYSE: KMI) and part owner of the NFL team Houston Texans; ranked 5th Most Valuable NFL team worth $1.85 billion.

chunks.title: Fayez Sarofim
chunks.text: He is divorced with five children, and lives in Houston, Texas.

chunks.title: Fayez Sarofim
chunks.text: With an estimated current net worth of $1.91 billion, Sarofim is ranked by "Forbes" as the 847-richest person in the world, in 2015.

chunks.title: Fayez Sarofim
chunks.text: His investment firms oversees over $30 billion in assets.

chunks.title: Arts Centre Melbourne
chunks.text: The Arts Centre Melbourne, originally known as the Victorian Arts Centre and briefly officially called the Arts Centre, is a performing arts centre consisting of a complex of theatres and concert halls in the Melbourne Arts Precinct, located in the central Melbourne suburb of Southbank in Victoria, Australia.

chunks.title: Bella Rose Arts Centre
chunks.text: The Bella Rose Arts Centre is a community-based proscenium theatre performing arts centre located inside of Halifax West High School in the Clayton Park neighbourhood of the Halifax.

chunks.title: Bella Rose Arts Centre
chunks.text: The 600 seat, professional grade, multi-purpose theatre has the capacity to handle almost any type of event from music and dance shows, to theatrical productions, and conferences.

chunks.title: Bella Rose Arts Centre
chunks.text: It currently functions primarily as a rental venue.

chunks.title: North Wall Arts Centre
chunks.text: The North Wall Arts Centre (often just referred to as the North Wall) is a performing arts centre in Oxford, owned by St Edward's School and shared with the city.

chunks.title: North Wall Arts Centre
chunks.text: It houses a 200-seat theatre, plus a rehearsal space, dance studio and a visual art gallery.

chunks.title: North Wall Arts Centre
chunks.text: The arts centre hosts touring theatre companies, musicians and other public events, as well as events by the school, with the aim to provide facilities and arts events both for St Edward's students and for the public at large.

chunks.title: Jose Thomas Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The Jose Thomas Performing Arts Centre (JT Pac), is a theatre of performing arts in Thrippunithura, Kochi, India.

chunks.title: Jose Thomas Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: It was founded on 26 February 2009 by Malayalam film actor Mohanlal and The Choice Group chairman Jose Thomas who respectively serves as the Chairman and President of the arts centre.

chunks.title: Jose Thomas Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The centre is situated in the Choice School complex and has a sitting-capacity of 700.

chunks.title: Jose Thomas Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The Rhyme by Soorya Krishnamoorthy was the first show played at the theatre and as of 2013 it has organised about 165 shows.

chunks.title: KLPac Sinfonietta
chunks.text: The Kuala Lumpur Performing Arts Centre Orchestra (klpac Orchestra) (formerly known as klpac Sinfonietta until 2008) was an amateur symphony orchestra located in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

chunks.title: KLPac Sinfonietta
chunks.text: It presented performances at the Kuala Lumpur Performing Arts Centre (klpac), which fostered creative excellence and develops and nurtures a performing arts culture in Malaysia.

chunks.title: KLPac Sinfonietta
chunks.text: At the time that the Centre was proposed a music conservatory was part of the proposal, but the cost proved to be too high at that time.

chunks.title: Canberra Theatre
chunks.text: The Canberra Theatre or officially the Canberra Theatre Centre, is the Australian Capital Territory’s central performing arts venue and Australia’s first performing arts centre, the first Australian Government initiated performing arts centre to be completed.

chunks.title: Canberra Theatre
chunks.text: It opened on 24 June 1965 with a gala performance by the Australian Ballet.

chunks.title: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
chunks.text: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay, also known as the Esplanade Theatre or simply The Esplanade, is a 60000 m2 performing arts centre located in Marina Bay near the mouth of the Singapore River.

chunks.title: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
chunks.text: Named after the nearby Esplanade Park, it consists of a concert hall which seats about 1,600 and a theatre with a capacity of about 2,000 for the performing arts.

chunks.title: Toronto Centre for the Arts
chunks.text: The Toronto Centre for the Arts, previously known as the "Ford Centre for the Performing Arts", is a performing arts centre in the former city of North York in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

chunks.title: Toronto Centre for the Arts
chunks.text: It opened in 1993 as the "North York Performing Arts Centre" designed by Canadian architect Eberhard Zeidler for musicals, theatre productions and other performing arts.

chunks.title: Toronto Centre for the Arts
chunks.text: At opening, North York awarded management of the centre to Livent who sold the naming rights in 1994 to Ford Motor.

chunks.title: Toronto Centre for the Arts
chunks.text: It originally housed three theatres: the Main Stage Theatre with 1,727 seats, the George Weston Recital Hall with 1,036 seats, and the multi-purpose, 200-seat Studio Theatre.

chunks.title: Toronto Centre for the Arts
chunks.text: When Livent declared bankruptcy in 1998, the City of Toronto assumed control of the facility.

chunks.title: Burlington Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The Burlington Performing Arts Centre (BPAC) is a multi-purpose venue located in the downtown core of Burlington, Ontario.

chunks.title: Burlington Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The venue is the only performing arts centre in Ontario and second in Canada to receive Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold certification.

chunks.title: Burlington Performing Arts Centre
chunks.text: The venue features three stages; the Main Theatre, a world-class performance stage featuring a six-story fly tower; Community Studio Theatre, a smaller scale of the Main Theatre with 2,500 square feet of floor space; the Family Lobby, features an open concept with a glass roof encircled by a balcony overlooking the floor.

chunks.title: State Theatre (Melbourne)
chunks.text: The State Theatre opened in 1984 and is part of the Arts Centre Melbourne located by the Yarra River and St Kilda Road.

chunks.title: State Theatre (Melbourne)
chunks.text: Like the other performance venues within the Arts Centre, the State Theatre is underground.

chunks.title: State Theatre (Melbourne)
chunks.text: The stage is one of the largest in the world.

chunks.title: Boeing 737 Classic
chunks.text: The Boeing 737 Classic refers to the -300/-400/-500 series of the Boeing 737.

chunks.title: Boeing 737 Classic
chunks.text: It is the second generation derivative of the 737, following the original -100/-200 models that began production in 1966.

chunks.title: Boeing 737 Classic
chunks.text: They are short- to medium-range, narrow-body jet airliners. Produced by Boeing Commercial Airplanes from 1984 to 2000, the 737 Classic includes three variants and can seat between 145 and 188 passengers.

chunks.title: Boeing 737 Classic
chunks.text: Improvements over the previous generation of 737 aircraft included CFM International CFM56 high bypass ratio turbofan engines, upgraded avionics, and increased passenger capacity (in the -300/-400 models).

chunks.title: Boeing Business Jet
chunks.text: The Boeing Business Jet series are variants of Boeing jet airliners for the corporate jet market.

chunks.title: Boeing Business Jet
chunks.text: The Boeing Business Jet is a 50/50 partnership between Boeing Commercial Airplanes and GE Aviation.

chunks.title: Boeing 747-8
chunks.text: The Boeing 747-8 is a wide-body jet airliner developed by Boeing Commercial Airplanes.

chunks.title: Boeing 747-8
chunks.text: Officially announced in 2005, the 747-8 is the third generation of the 747, with a lengthened fuselage, redesigned wings, and improved efficiency.

chunks.title: Boeing 747-8
chunks.text: The 747-8 is the largest 747 version, the largest commercial aircraft built in the United States, and the longest passenger aircraft in the world.

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: The Boeing 777 is a family of long-range wide-body twin-engine jet airliners developed and manufactured by Boeing Commercial Airplanes.

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: It is the world's largest twinjet and has a typical seating capacity of 314 to 396 passengers, with a range of 5240 to .

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: Commonly referred to as the "Triple Seven", its distinguishing features include the largest-diameter turbofan engines of any aircraft, six wheels on each main landing gear, fully circular fuselage cross-section, and a blade-shaped tail cone.

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: Developed in consultation with eight major airlines, the 777 was designed to replace older wide-body airliners and bridge the capacity difference between Boeing's 767 and 747.

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: As Boeing's first fly-by-wire airliner, it has computer-mediated controls.

chunks.title: Boeing 777
chunks.text: It was also the first commercial aircraft to be designed entirely with computer-aided design.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: Renton is a city in King County, Washington, United States.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: Situated 11 mi southeast of downtown Seattle, Washington, Renton straddles the southeast shore of Lake Washington, at the mouth of the Cedar River.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: While long an important salmon fishing area for Native Americans, Renton was first settled by people of European descent in the 1860s, and its early economy was based on coal mining, clay production, and timber export.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: Today, Renton is best known as the final assembly point for the Boeing 737 family of commercial airplanes, but it is also home to a growing number of well known manufacturing, technology, and healthcare organizations, including Boeing Commercial Airplanes Division, Paccar, Kaiser Permanente, IKEA, Providence Health & Services, UW Medicine Valley Medical Center, and Wizards of the Coast.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: As of 2016, the population in Renton is 101,300, up from 90,927 at the 2010 census.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: Renton currently is the 8th largest city in Washington State, and is the 4th largest in King County.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: The National Football League's Seattle Seahawks have a training facility in Renton.

chunks.title: Renton, Washington
chunks.text: It is the second-largest facility in the NFL at 200000 sqft .

chunks.title: Boeing 767
chunks.text: The Boeing 767 is a mid- to large-size, mid- to long-range, wide-body twin-engine jet airliner built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes.

chunks.title: Boeing 767
chunks.text: It was Boeing's first wide-body twinjet and its first airliner with a two-crew glass cockpit.

chunks.title: Boeing 767
chunks.text: The aircraft has two turbofan engines, a conventional tail, and, for reduced aerodynamic drag, a supercritical wing design.

chunks.title: Boeing 767
chunks.text: Designed as a smaller wide-body airliner than earlier aircraft such as the 747, the 767 has seating capacity for 181 to 375 people, and a design range of 3850 to , depending on variant.

chunks.title: Boeing 767
chunks.text: Development of the 767 occurred in tandem with a narrow-body twinjet, the 757, resulting in shared design features which allow pilots to obtain a common type rating to operate both aircraft.

chunks.title: Boeing 757
chunks.text: The Boeing 757 is a mid-size, narrow-body twin-engine jet airliner that was designed and built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes.

chunks.title: Boeing 757
chunks.text: It is the manufacturer's largest single-aisle passenger aircraft and was produced from 1981 to 2004.

chunks.title: Boeing 757
chunks.text: The twinjet has a two-crew member glass cockpit, turbofan engines of sufficient power to allow takeoffs from relatively short runways and higher altitudes, a conventional tail and, for reduced aerodynamic drag, a supercritical wing design.

chunks.title: Boeing 757
chunks.text: Intended to replace the smaller three-engine 727 on short and medium routes, the 757 can carry 200 to 295 passengers for a maximum of 3150 to , depending on variant.

chunks.title: Boeing 757
chunks.text: The 757 was designed concurrently with a wide-body twinjet, the 767, and owing to shared features pilots can obtain a common type rating that allows them to operate both aircraft.

chunks.title: Boeing South Carolina
chunks.text: Boeing South Carolina (previously "Boeing Charleston") is an assembly site for Boeing's Commercial Airplanes division, located in North Charleston, South Carolina.

chunks.title: Boeing South Carolina
chunks.text: The site is the major manufacturing, assembly and delivery site for Boeing commercial aircraft in the eastern United States and is one of the largest employment centers in the state.

chunks.title: Boeing South Carolina
chunks.text: The site currently serves as one of two final assembly and delivery points for the Boeing 787 Dreamliner.

chunks.title: Boeing South Carolina
chunks.text: The site has seen rapid investment and growth since Boeing made a number of purchases in 2008 and 2009 from its former suppliers Vought and Global Aeronautica who had factories there.

chunks.title: Boeing South Carolina
chunks.text: The Boeing South Carolina Delivery Center, a 57,920 sqft facility, opened on Nov. 12, 2011, and delivers South Carolina-built 787s to customers from around the world.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: James "Jim" F. Albaugh (born May 31, 1950) is the former Executive Vice President of The Boeing Company and Chief Executive Officer of the Boeing Commercial Airplanes business unit.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: He served in these capacities for Boeing Commercial Airplanes from September 1, 2009 until his retirement on June 26, 2012.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: He retired from the company on October 1, 2012.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: He previously served as President and Chief Executive Officer of Boeing Defense, Space & Security business unit.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: In that capacity, Albaugh was responsible for over 70,000 employees and supervised a $30.8 billion budget.

chunks.title: James Albaugh
chunks.text: Jim Albaugh is one of the defense industry's best paid managers ($1,499,923 in 2005).

chunks.title: Trump Force One
chunks.text: The aircraft called Trump Force One by the media is Donald J. Trump's private jet.

chunks.title: Trump Force One
chunks.text: The current incarnation of Trump Force One is a Boeing 757, which replaced the preceding Boeing 727.

chunks.title: Trump Force One
chunks.text: It is operated as part of "Trump Air", the air assets of The Trump Organization.

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: Spontaneous Combustion is an album by progressive metal group Liquid Trio Experiment, and is the result of the studio improvisations of Liquid Tension Experiment which occurred while John Petrucci was with his wife while she was giving birth.

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: The trio of Mike Portnoy, Tony Levin and Jordan Rudess continued to write music during this period.

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: It was released on October 23, 2007.

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: A few songs from "Liquid Tension Experiment 2" were spawned from these jam sessions including "914", "Chewbacca", and "Liquid Dreams".

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: The song "Chris & Kevin's Bogus Journey" is not a reference to Portnoy and Petrucci's former Dream Theater bandmates Chris Collins and Kevin Moore, but rather to the track on Liquid Tension Experiment's first album entitled "Chris & Kevin's Excellent Adventure", which is itself a reference to the band's photographer's habit of calling Mike Portnoy and Tony Levin "Chris and Kevin", even after being corrected several times.

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: It is also a reference to the 1991 film "Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey", the sequel to "Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure".

chunks.title: Spontaneous Combustion (album)
chunks.text: The song "Jazz Odyssey" is a reference to the movie "This Is Spinal Tap", in which Spinal Tap experiments with an improvisational song of the same name.

chunks.title: She Is Love (Parachute song)
