chunks.title: 2009 Oregon Ducks football team
chunks.text: Kelly was only the third Ducks head coach since 1977 and led the Ducks to a Pac-10 Championship and was named Pac-10 Coach of the Year.

chunks.title: 2009 Oregon Ducks football team
chunks.text: He took over for Mike Bellotti.

chunks.title: 1910 Detroit Titans football team
chunks.text: The 1910 Detroit Titans football team was an American football team that represented the University of Detroit in the 1910 college football season.

chunks.title: 1910 Detroit Titans football team
chunks.text: In its third season under head coach George A. Kelly, the team compiled a 3–2 record, but was outscored by its opponents by a combined total of 67 to 28.

chunks.title: 1910 Detroit Titans football team
chunks.text: The team opened the season with back-to-back losses Michigan Agricultural (35–0) and Olivet College (29–5), and ended the season with three victories over Hillsdale College, Adrian College, and Michigan Normal School.

chunks.title: Kevin Kelly (coach)
chunks.text: Kevin Kelly (born c. 1960) is an American football coach, currently the defensive coordinator of the Ball State Cardinals football team.

chunks.title: Kevin Kelly (coach)
chunks.text: He was previously the head coach of the Georgetown Hoyas football team, a special teams coordinator at the United States Naval Academy, and a defensive coordinator at Marshall University.

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: The Oregon Ducks football program is a college football team for the University of Oregon, located in the U.S. state of Oregon.

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: The team competes at the NCAA Division I level in the FBS and is a member of the Pac-12 Conference (Pac-12).

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: Known as the Ducks, the team was commonly called the Webfoots until the mid-1960s.

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: The first football team was fielded in 1894.

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: Oregon plays its home games at the 54,000 seat Autzen Stadium in Eugene; its main rivals are the Oregon State Beavers and the Washington Huskies.

chunks.title: Oregon Ducks football
chunks.text: The Ducks and Beavers historically end each regular season with the Civil War rivalry game in late November.

chunks.title: Civil War (college football game)
chunks.text: The Civil War is the colloquial name for an American college football rivalry game played annually in Oregon, between the Ducks of the University of Oregon in Eugene and the Beavers of Oregon State University in Corvallis.

chunks.title: Civil War (college football game)
chunks.text: First played in 1894, it is the fifth most played college football rivalry game in NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision.

chunks.title: Civil War (college football game)
chunks.text: Both universities are members of the North Division of the Pac-12 Conference.

chunks.title: Textile Bowl
chunks.text: The Textile Bowl is an American college football rivalry game played annually by the Clemson Tigers football team of Clemson University and the NC State Wolfpack football team of North Carolina State University.

chunks.title: Textile Bowl
chunks.text: The rivalry game has been known as the Textile Bowl since 1981.

chunks.title: Textile Bowl
chunks.text: The two universities are founding members of the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC), and both have competed in the ACC's Atlantic Division since the conference initiated divisional play.

chunks.title: Textile Bowl
chunks.text: The rivalry's name is derived from the fact that Clemson and North Carolina State have two of the largest university-level textile schools in the world, and from the textile industry's historic importance in the economic development of their respective states of South Carolina and North Carolina.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: The Rivalry is an American college football rivalry game played by the Lafayette Leopards football team of Lafayette College and the Lehigh Mountain Hawks football team of Lehigh University.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: It is the most-played football rivalry in the nation and the longest uninterrupted annual rivalry series.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: As of 2016, "The Rivalry" has been played 152 times since 1884 with only a single interruption in 1896.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: The college's football teams met twice annually (except 1891, when they played three games, and 1896, when they did not play at all) until 1901.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: The two institutions are located seventeen miles apart in the Lehigh Valley in eastern Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: The Rivalry (Lehigh–Lafayette)
chunks.text: Though primarily alluding to football, "The Rivalry" pertains to a meeting between the two schools in all sports and other endeavors.

chunks.title: 1983 Oregon State vs. Oregon football game
chunks.text: The 1983 Oregon State vs. Oregon football game was a college football game played on November 19, 1983, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon, the 87th playing of the annual Civil War rivalry game.

chunks.title: 1983 Oregon State vs. Oregon football game
chunks.text: The game ended in a scoreless tie.

chunks.title: 1983 Oregon State vs. Oregon football game
chunks.text: Since overtime was added to NCAA Division I games in 1996, this game is likely to be the last ever with that distinction.

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: The LSU–Ole Miss football rivalry, renamed the Magnolia Bowl in 2008, is an American college football rivalry game played annually by the LSU Tigers football team of Louisiana State University (LSU) and the Ole Miss Rebels football team of the University of Mississippi (Ole Miss).

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: The teams compete for the Magnolia Bowl Trophy.

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: The Tigers and the Rebels first met in 1894, and have been regular opponents in Southeastern Conference (SEC), meeting annually since 1945.

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: The rivalry was at its height during the 1950s and 1960s, when both teams were highly ranked and during which time both teams claimed a national championship.

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: The rivalry died down from the 1970s to the 1990s, owing to Ole Miss not returning to conference or national prominence since the 1970s and because LSU has seen new rivalries emerge when the SEC split into two divisions in 1992, most notably Alabama, Arkansas, Auburn, and Florida.

chunks.title: Magnolia Bowl
chunks.text: Even though the rivalry has not attracted the same national attention in recent years, it still stirs up passion in both Oxford and Baton Rouge.

chunks.title: Joe Walker (American football)
chunks.text: Joe Walker (born December 11, 1992) is an American football linebacker for the Philadelphia Eagles of the National Football League (NFL).

chunks.title: Joe Walker (American football)
chunks.text: He played college football at Oregon.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: The Battle of the Blue is an annual college football rivalry game between the University of Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens and Villanova University Wildcats.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: The first game was played between the two teams in 1895, was played annually from 1964 to 1980 when Villanova dropped football, and then resumed with the re-emergence of Villanova football having been played annually since 1988.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: Beginning in 2007, the annual Delaware–Villanova game became known as Battle of the Blue.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: As part of this concept, the winning team gets to keep the Battle of the Blue Trophy at its institution for the year and is responsible for bringing the trophy to the following installment of the rivalry game.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: The trophy consists of a football with a Villanova logo and the Wildcat shade of blue on one side and the Blue Hen logo and the Delaware shade of blue on the other side.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: The ball sits in a wooden platform and the scores of each game are engraved on the base of the trophy.

chunks.title: Battle of the Blue
chunks.text: Villanova had possession of the trophy for the first four years, until Delaware won in 2011.

chunks.title: Army–Navy Game
chunks.text: The Army–Navy Game is an American college rivalry game in college football between the Army Black Knights of the United States Military Academy (USMA) at West Point, New York, and the Navy Midshipmen of the United States Naval Academy (USNA) at Annapolis, Maryland.

chunks.title: Army–Navy Game
chunks.text: The Black Knights (formerly the "Army Cadets" and "Army Black Knights") and Midshipmen each represent their service's oldest officer commissioning sources.

chunks.title: Army–Navy Game
chunks.text: As such, the game has come to embody the spirit of the interservice rivalry of the United States Armed Forces.

chunks.title: Army–Navy Game
chunks.text: The game marks the end of the college football regular season and the third and final game of the season's Commander-in-Chief's Trophy series, which also includes the Air Force Falcons of the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) near Colorado Springs, Colorado.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: The Battle for the Bell is an American college football rivalry game played by the Marshall Thundering Herd football team of Marshall University and the Ohio Bobcats football team of Ohio University.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: It is a regional rivalry, with the universities' campuses located about 80 miles (130 km) from each other, with a bell awarded as the trophy for the winner of the game.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: With Marshall's move from the Mid-American Conference to Conference USA in 2005, this rivalry game was on hiatus for several years.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: The series unexpectedly resumed in 2009 when the Herd and Bobcats faced off in the 2009 Little Caesars Pizza Bowl, which Marshall won 21–17.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: A six-year contract between the schools began in 2010.

chunks.title: Battle for the Bell
chunks.text: Ohio leads the all-time series over Marshall 33–20–6.

chunks.title: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park
chunks.text: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park is located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

chunks.title: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park
chunks.text: It was founded in 1996, and covers 256.14 km².

chunks.title: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park
chunks.text: It commemorates Lakshmibai, the Rani of Jhansi (1828-58).

chunks.title: Malindi Marine National Park
chunks.text: Malindi Marine National Park is located in the Indian Ocean, off the coast of Kenya.

chunks.title: Malindi Marine National Park
chunks.text: It is claimed to be oldest marine park in Africa.

chunks.title: Malindi Marine National Park
chunks.text: The park lies at Malindi, about 118 km north of Mombasa and is protected and administered by the Kenya Wildlife Service.

chunks.title: Malindi Marine National Park
chunks.text: Along with Watamu Marine National Park, Malindi Marine Park is enclosed by the Malindi Marine National Reserve.

chunks.title: Jhansi State
chunks.text: Jhansi was an independent princely state ruled by the Maratha Newalkar dynasty under suzerainty of British India from 1804 till 1853, when the British authorities took over the State under the terms of the Doctrine of Lapse.

chunks.title: Jhansi State
chunks.text: The fortified town of Jhansi served as its capital.

chunks.title: Middle Button Island National Park
chunks.text: Middle Button Island National Park is an Indian national park located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

chunks.title: Middle Button Island National Park
chunks.text: The park was created in 1979 and is situated about 200 km northeast of Port Blair, capital of the island group.

chunks.title: Middle Button Island National Park
chunks.text: The total area that the national park covers is about 64 km2 .

chunks.title: Middle Button Island National Park
chunks.text: Along with the neighbouring islands of North Button and South Button, both also national parks, it forms part of the Rani Jhansi Marine National Park off the coast of South Andaman Island.

chunks.title: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
chunks.text: The Jammu & Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) is a state political party in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir.

chunks.title: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
chunks.text: Founded as the "All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference" by Sheikh Abdullah and Chaudhry Ghulam Abbas in 1932 in the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, the organisation renamed itself to "National Conference" in 1939 in order to represent all the people of the state.

chunks.title: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
chunks.text: It supported the accession of the princely state to India in 1947.

chunks.title: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
chunks.text: Prior to that, in 1941, a group led by Ghulam Abbas broke off from the National Conference and revived the old Muslim Conference.

chunks.title: Jammu & Kashmir National Conference
chunks.text: The revived Muslim Conference supported the accession of the princely state to Pakistan and led the movement for Azad Kashmir.

chunks.title: South Button Island National Park
chunks.text: South Button Island National Park is a national park located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands off the coast of India, the total area of this protected island is about 5 km2 .

chunks.title: South Button Island National Park
chunks.text: Along with the neighbouring islands of North Button and Middle Button, both also national parks, it forms part of the Rani Jhansi Marine National Park off the coast of South Andaman Island.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kutch is situated on the southern shore of the Gulf of Kachchh in the Devbhumi Dwarka District of Gujarat state, India.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: In 1980, an area of 270 km.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: from Okha to Jodiya was declared Marine Sanctuary.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: Later, in 1982, a core area of 110 km was declared Marine National Park under the provisions of the Wildlife (protection) Act, 1972 of India.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: There are 42 islands on the Jamnagar coast in the Marine National Park, most of them surrounded by reefs.

chunks.title: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch
chunks.text: The best known island is Pirotan.

chunks.title: Rani of Jhansi
chunks.text: Lakshmibai, the Rani of Jhansi (   ; 19 November 1828 – 18 June 1858), was the queen of the princely state of Jhansi in North India currently present in Jhansi district in Uttar Pradesh, India.

chunks.title: Rani of Jhansi
chunks.text: She was one of the leading figures of the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and became a symbol of resistance to the British Raj for Indian nationalists.

chunks.title: North Zone women's cricket team
chunks.text: The North Zone women's cricket team is a women's first-class cricket team that represents North India in the Inter Zone Women's One Day Competition and Inter Zone Women's Three Day Competition.

chunks.title: North Zone women's cricket team
chunks.text: Team also represented North India in the now defunct Rani Jhansi Trophy from 1974 to 1997.

chunks.title: Bunurong Marine National Park
chunks.text: The Bunurong Marine National Park ( ) is a protected marine national park located off the coast of Cape Paterson in the South Gippsland region of Victoria, Australia.

chunks.title: Bunurong Marine National Park
chunks.text: The 2100 ha marine national park is located about 6 km southwest of Inverloch and about 5 km off the coastline.

chunks.title: Bunurong Marine National Park
chunks.text: The coastal waters protect a range of habitats including intertidal reefs, subtidal rocky reefs, algal gardens and seagrass beds.

chunks.title: Bunurong Marine National Park
chunks.text: The waters are cool, akin to Victoria’s central and western coasts.

chunks.title: Bunurong Marine National Park
chunks.text: However, they are relatively protected from south-westerly swells due to the location of far away King Island, Tasmania.

chunks.title: Shouting fire in a crowded theater
chunks.text: "Shouting "fire" in a crowded theater" is a popular metaphor for speech or actions made for the principal purpose of creating unnecessary panic.

chunks.title: Shouting fire in a crowded theater
chunks.text: The phrase is a paraphrasing of Oliver Wendell Holmes, Jr.'s opinion in the United States Supreme Court case "Schenck v. United States" in 1919, which held that the defendant's speech in opposition to the draft during World War I was not protected free speech under the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.

chunks.title: R v Cheshire
chunks.text: R v Cheshire [1991] 1 WLR 844 is an English criminal law case establishing the role of the jury in finding liability for death, where subsequent medical negligence occurs following the original injury.

chunks.title: R v Cheshire
chunks.text: The Court of Appeal found that the jury did not have to weigh up different causes of death, and need only be satisfied that the defendant's actions made a "significant contribution" to the victim's death.

chunks.title: Kaikhosro II Jaqeli
chunks.text: Kaikhosro II Jaqeli (Georgian: ქაიხოსრო II ჯაყელი ; b. 1522 – d. 1573), of the House of Jaqeli, son of Qvarqvare III, was prince of Samtskhe (styled with the hereditary title of atabeg), ruling nominally in 1545–1573.

chunks.title: Kaikhosro II Jaqeli
chunks.text: Invested as a puppet ruler by the Ottomans in 1545, Kaikhosro II's further tenure over Samtskhe continued as a hard one, and it was marked by incessant Iranian–Ottoman rivalry, as well as uneasy relations with neighboring Georgian polities, and internecine feuds.

chunks.title: Kaikhosro II Jaqeli
chunks.text: He quickly ended up with the western part of his principality being assimilated by the Ottomans and formed into a "paşalık", while the eastern part came under Iranian suzerainty.

chunks.title: Kaikhosro II Jaqeli
chunks.text: Continued Ottoman actions made him eventually seek direct assistance in 1570 from his suzerain, king Tahmasp I (r. 1524–1576) at the Iranian royal court, where he died three years later as well.

chunks.title: God Is Not Great
chunks.text: God Is Not Great: How Religion Poisons Everything is a 2007 book by Anglo-American author and journalist Christopher Hitchens, in which he makes a case against organized religion.

chunks.title: God Is Not Great
chunks.text: It was published by Atlantic Books in the United Kingdom as God Is Not Great: The Case Against Religion.

chunks.title: Big Painting No. 6
chunks.text: Big Painting No. 6 (sometimes Big Painting or Big Painting VI) is a 1965 oil and Magna on canvas painting by Roy Lichtenstein.

chunks.title: Big Painting No. 6
chunks.text: Measuring 235 cm × 330 cm (92.5 in × 129 in), it is part of the "Brushstrokes" series of artworks that includes several paintings and sculptures whose subject is the actions made with a house-painter's brush.

chunks.title: Big Painting No. 6
chunks.text: It set a record auction price for a painting by a living American artist when it sold for $60,000 in 1970.

chunks.title: Big Painting No. 6
chunks.text: The painting is in the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen collection.

chunks.title: Christopher Hitchens
chunks.text: Christopher Eric Hitchens (13 April 1949 – 15 December 2011) was an Anglo-American author, columnist, essayist, orator, religious and literary critic, social critic, and journalist.

chunks.title: Christopher Hitchens
chunks.text: Hitchens was the author, co-author, editor or co-editor of over 30 books, including five collections of essays, on politics, literature and religion.

chunks.title: Christopher Hitchens
chunks.text: A staple of public discourse, his confrontational style of debate made him both a lauded intellectual and a controversial public figure.

chunks.title: Christopher Hitchens
chunks.text: He contributed to "New Statesman", "The Nation", "The Weekly Standard", "The Atlantic", "London Review of Books", "The Times Literary Supplement", "Slate", "Free Inquiry" and "Vanity Fair".

chunks.title: Injo coup
chunks.text: King Gwanghae (光海君, 광해군) was an outstanding administrator and great diplomat, he was largely unsupported by many politicians, scholars, and aristocrats because he was not the first-born and he was born of a concubine.

chunks.title: Injo coup
chunks.text: Greater Northerners tried to stomp out those opinions, suppressing Lesser Northerners and killing Prince Imhae (臨海君, 임해군), the oldest son of Seonjo, and Grand Prince Yeongchang (永昌大君, 영창대군), the queen's son.

chunks.title: Injo coup
chunks.text: It was not Gwanghae's plan to keep his throne; and in fact, he actually tried to bring minor factions into the government, but was blocked by opposition from members of the Greater Northerners, such as Jeong In-hong and Yi Icheom.

chunks.title: Injo coup
chunks.text: The actions made Gwanghae even more unpopular among wealthy aristocrats, and they finally began plotting against him.

chunks.title: Education for Liberation of Siam
chunks.text: Education for Liberation of Siam (Thai: กลุ่มการศึกษาเพื่อความเป็นไท ) is a group of high school students who demand to reform Thai education system which the core members are from "the Thailand Educational Revolution Alliance".

chunks.title: Education for Liberation of Siam
chunks.text: It was established on 2 December 2013 by Netiwit Chotiphatphisal, whom also is the first secretary of the group.

chunks.title: Education for Liberation of Siam
chunks.text: There has been a fan page on Facebook called “The Education for Liberation of Siam” to be the intermediate for disseminating any information concerning misconducts and questionable actions made by politicians or figures of authorities that have an effect on the Thai educational community.

chunks.title: Education for Liberation of Siam
chunks.text: before Coup d'état in Thailand, in January this group set the event anti-coup in front of army camp Recently there was a small event, coined “Presenting flowers to show appreciation towards the military officers for not commititting Coup d'état” .

chunks.title: Elisabeth Croll
chunks.text: Elisabeth Joan "Lisa" Croll, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (21 September 1944 – 3 October 2007) was a New Zealand anthropologist.

chunks.title: Elisabeth Croll
chunks.text: She is known as the first anthropologist to visit Chinese villages in a period when political actions made access into the country for foreigners difficult.

chunks.title: Elisabeth Croll
chunks.text: Croll published books on the subject and held several short-term fellowships at various educational institutions.

chunks.title: Elisabeth Croll
chunks.text: She also worked for United Nations agencies and international non-government organisations.

chunks.title: Brushstrokes in Flight
chunks.text: Brushstrokes in Flight is a 1984 sculpture by Roy Lichtenstein, installed at the John Glenn Columbus International Airport in Columbus, Ohio.

chunks.title: Brushstrokes in Flight
chunks.text: It is part of the "Brushstrokes" series of artworks that includes several paintings and sculptures whose subject is the actions made with a house-painter's brush.

chunks.title: Teddy Riley
chunks.text: Edward Theodore Riley (born October 8, 1967) is an American singer-songwriter, musician, keyboardist, and record producer credited with the creation of the new jack swing genre.

chunks.title: Teddy Riley
chunks.text: Through his production work with artists including Michael Jackson, Bobby Brown, Doug E. Fresh, Today, Keith Sweat, Heavy D., Usher, and Jane Child, and his membership of the groups Guy and Blackstreet, Riley is credited with having a major impact and seminal influence on the formation of contemporary R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop since the 1980s.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: New jack swing or swingbeat is a fusion genre spearheaded by Teddy Riley and Bernard Belle that became popular from the late 1980s into the early 1990s.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: Its influence, along with hip hop, seeped into pop culture and was the definitive sound of the inventive black New York club scene.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: It fuses the rhythms, samples, and production techniques of hip hop and dance-pop with the urban contemporary sound of R&B.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: The new jack swing style developed as many previous music styles did, by combining elements of older styles with newer sensibilities.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: It used R&B style vocals sung over hip hop and dance-pop style influenced instrumentation.

chunks.title: New jack swing
chunks.text: The sound of new jack swing comes from the hip hop "swing" beats created by drum machine, and hardware samplers, which were popular during the Golden Age of Hip Hop, with contemporary R&B style singing.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: "I Want Her" is a song by American R&B singer Keith Sweat.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: As the first single from his debut album, "Make It Last Forever", it reached number five on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and number one on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart for three weeks.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: and became the most successful number one single of 1988 on the Billboard Hot R&B chart.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: This was the first new jack swing song to reach #1 on the R&B charts.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: "I Want Her" also peaked at number 38 on the dance chart.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: The song topped the R&B Billboard Year-End chart for 1988.

chunks.title: I Want Her
chunks.text: It was ranked number 6 on complex.com's list of 25 best new jack swing songs of all time.

chunks.title: I Got the Feeling (Today song)
chunks.text: I Got the Feeling is a new jack swing song released as a single by the Motown artists Today.

chunks.title: I Got the Feeling (Today song)
chunks.text: The first track on Today's album titled "The New Formula", the single was released on August 17, 1990 on both vinyl and cassette.

chunks.title: I Got the Feeling (Today song)
chunks.text: The song peaked at #12 on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.

chunks.title: I Got the Feeling (Today song)
chunks.text: It was featured in the 2004 video game, Grand Theft Auto San Andreas on the new jack swing radio station, .

chunks.title: Damion Hall
chunks.text: Damion Hall, also known as Damion "Crazy Legs" Hall is an African-American R&B singer.

chunks.title: Damion Hall
chunks.text: He is a member of the new jack swing group Guy and is the brother of Guy member, Aaron Hall.

chunks.title: Damion Hall
chunks.text: He has released one solo album, Straight to the Point in 1994, which spawned one single, "Satisfy You", featuring Chanté Moore.

chunks.title: Damion Hall
chunks.text: That song managed to reach #48 on the Billboard R&B charts.

chunks.title: Damion Hall
chunks.text: He is currently unsigned.

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)
chunks.text: New Jack City is the original soundtrack to the 1991 film "New Jack City" released by Giant Records through Reprise Records and distributed by Warner Bros.

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)
chunks.text: Records.

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)
chunks.text: The soundtrack consists of eleven original songs, most of which were performed by chart-topping R&B and hip-hop artists of the time.

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)
chunks.text: The music is heavily influenced by the new jack swing genre of R&B.

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)
chunks.text: Prominent artists and producers of the new jack swing era contributed to the soundtrack, including Guy with Teddy Riley, Keith Sweat, Color Me Badd, and Johnny Gill; Al B. Sure!

chunks.title: New Jack City (soundtrack)

chunks.title: 1990s in music
chunks.text: Popular music in the 1990s saw the continuation of teen pop and dance-pop trends which had emerged in the 1970s and 1980s.

chunks.title: 1990s in music
chunks.text: Furthermore, hip hop grew and continued to be highly successful in the decade, with the continuation of the genre's golden age.

chunks.title: 1990s in music
chunks.text: Aside from rap, reggae, contemporary R&B and urban music in general remained extremely popular throughout the decade; urban music in the late-1980s and 1990s often blended with styles such as soul, funk and jazz, resulting in fusion genres such as new jack swing, neo-soul, hip hop soul and g-funk which were popular.

chunks.title: New Jack Reunion Tour
chunks.text: The New Jack Reunion Tour was a 2006 concert tour that featured members of the 1990s music genre "new jack swing," which was created by Teddy Riley.

chunks.title: List of new jack swing artists
