chunks.title: List of new jack swing artists
chunks.text: The sound of new jack swing comes from the hip hop "swing" beats created by drum machine, and hardware samplers, which was popular during the golden age of hip hop, with contemporary R&B style singing.

chunks.title: Aaron Hall (singer)
chunks.text: Aaron Hall (born August 10, 1964, The Bronx, New York City and growing up in Brooklyn and Roosevelt, Long Island), is an American soul singer and songwriter.

chunks.title: Aaron Hall (singer)
chunks.text: He is a current member of the group Guy, which he founded in the late 1980s, along with New jack swing producer Teddy Riley and songwriter Timmy Gatling, who was later replaced by Hall's brother Damion Hall.

chunks.title: Aaron Hall (singer)
chunks.text: In 1988, they released their debut album which went on to sell over a million copies being certified platinum.

chunks.title: Aaron Hall (singer)
chunks.text: Hall led the group in songs like "Groove Me", "I Like" and "Piece Of My Love".

chunks.title: Polytrimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Polytrimethylene terephthalate (PTT), is a polyester synthesized and patented in 1941.

chunks.title: Polytrimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: It is produced by a method called condensation polymerization or transesterification.

chunks.title: Polytrimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: The two monomer units used in producing this polymer are: 1,3-propanediol and terephthalic acid or dimethyl terephthalate.

chunks.title: Polytrimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Similar to polyethylene terephthalate, the PTT is used to make carpet fibers.

chunks.title: Polyethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate
chunks.text: Polyethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate, also named poly(ethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate), polyethylene furanoate and poly(ethylene furanoate) and generally abbreviated as PEF, is a polymer that can be produced by polycondensation of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and monoethylene glycol (MEG).

chunks.title: Polyethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate
chunks.text: As an aromatic polyester from ethylene glycol it is a chemical analogue of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyethylene naphthalate (PEN).

chunks.title: Polyethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate
chunks.text: PEF has been described in (patent) literature since 1951, but has gained renewed attention since the US department of energy proclaimed its building block, FDCA, as a potential bio-based replacement for purified terephthalic acid (PTA) in 2004.

chunks.title: Ecopack
chunks.text: Ecopack Ltd is a PET bottles blowing company in Pakistan.

chunks.title: Krones
chunks.text: Krones AG is a German packaging and bottling machine manufacturer.

chunks.title: Krones
chunks.text: It is the world's leading manufacturer of lines for filling beverages in plastic and glass bottles or beverage cans.

chunks.title: Krones
chunks.text: The company manufactures stretch blow-moulding machines for producing polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles, plus fillers, labellers, bottle washers, pasteurisers, inspectors, packers and palletisers.

chunks.title: Krones
chunks.text: This product portfolio is complemented by material flow systems and process technology for producing beverages, plus syrup kitchens, for clients like breweries, dairies and soft-drink companies.

chunks.title: Polyethylene naphthalate
chunks.text: Polyethylene naphthalate (poly(ethylene 2,6-naphthalate or PEN) is a polyester with good barrier properties (even better than Polyethylene terephthalate).

chunks.title: Polyethylene naphthalate
chunks.text: Because it provides a very good oxygen barrier, it is particularly well-suited for bottling beverages that are susceptible to oxidation, such as beer.

chunks.title: Polyethylene naphthalate
chunks.text: It is also used in making high performance sailcloth.

chunks.title: Polyethylene naphthalate
chunks.text: It also has been found to show supreme scintillation properties and is expected to replace classic plastic scintillators.

chunks.title: Two-liter bottle
chunks.text: The two-liter bottle is a common container for soft drinks.

chunks.title: Two-liter bottle
chunks.text: These bottles are produced from polyethylene terephthalate, also known as PET plastic, using the blow molding process.

chunks.title: Two-liter bottle
chunks.text: Bottle labels consist of a printed, tight-fitted plastic sleeve.

chunks.title: Two-liter bottle
chunks.text: A resealable screw-top allows the contents to be used at various times while retaining carbonation.

chunks.title: Polyethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Polyethylene terephthalate (sometimes written poly(ethylene terephthalate)), commonly abbreviated PET, PETE, or the obsolete PETP or PET-P, is the most common thermoplastic polymer resin of the polyester family and is used in fibers for clothing, containers for liquids and foods, thermoforming for manufacturing, and in combination with glass fiber for engineering resins.

chunks.title: BoPET
chunks.text: BoPET (Biaxially-oriented polyethylene terephthalate) is a polyester film made from stretched polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and is used for its high tensile strength, chemical and dimensional stability, transparency, reflectivity, gas and aroma barrier properties, and electrical insulation.

chunks.title: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate (PCT) is a thermoplastic polyester formed from the polycondensation of terephthalic acid and cyclohexanedimethanol.

chunks.title: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Its chemical structure is similar to that of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), with which it shares properties like dimensional stability and chemical resistance.

chunks.title: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: PCT is also particularly resistant to high temperatures and hydrolysis.

chunks.title: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: The melting point is 545 °F (285 °C).

chunks.title: Polycyclohexylenedimethylene terephthalate
chunks.text: Common brand names are "Thermx" (Ticona), "Eastar" (Eastman) and "SkyPURA" (SK Chemicals).

chunks.title: Xenoy
chunks.text: Xenoy is a blend of plastics with many industrially-useful properties.

chunks.title: Xenoy
chunks.text: It is typically polyester (polybutylene terephthalate, PBT, or polyethylene terephthalate, PET) and polycarbonate (PC): it is often labeled PBT+PC or PET+PC.

chunks.title: University of Zurich
chunks.text: The University of Zurich (UZH, German: "Universität Zürich" ), located in the city of Zürich, is the largest university in Switzerland, with over 26,000 students.

chunks.title: University of Zurich
chunks.text: It was founded in 1833 from the existing colleges of theology, law, medicine and a new faculty of philosophy.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: BMVA Summer School is an annual summer school on computer vision, organised by the British Machine Vision Association and Society for Pattern Recognition (BMVA).

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: The course is residential, usually held over five days, and consists of lectures and practicals in topics in image processing, computer vision, pattern recognition.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: It is intended that the course will complement and extend the material in existing technical courses that many students/researchers will encounter in their early stage of postgraduate training or caeeers.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: It aims to broaden awareness of knowledge and techniques in Vision, Image Computing and Pattern Recognition, and to develop appropriate research skills, and for students to interact with their peers, and to make contacts among those who will be the active researchers of their own generation.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: It is open to students from both UK and non-UK universities.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: The registration fees vary based on time of registration and are in general slightly higher for non-UK students.

chunks.title: BMVA Summer School
chunks.text: The summer school has been hosted locally by various universities in UK that carry out Computer Vision research, e.g., Kingston University, the University of Manchester and Swansea University.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: University Cooperative Housing Association (UCHA) is a student housing cooperative in Westwood, Los Angeles serving the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) campus.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: Approximately 400 students live there and in addition to housing UCLA students, UCHA offers housing to students of any college, including the UCLA Extension and Santa Monica College.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: UCHA operates three buildings, Hardman-Hansen Hall, Essene Hall, and Robison Hall, the latter being a renovated version of the Landfair Apartments and cultural landmark designed by Richard Neutra.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: Jim Morrison, of The Doors, purportedly lived at UCHA during his time at UCLA.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: Green Day and Margaret Cho performed at UCHA in the early 1990s.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: In addition to the UCLA campus, Hardman-Hansen and Robison Halls were used as filming locations for the 1982 horror film, The Dorm That Dripped Blood.

chunks.title: University Cooperative Housing Association
chunks.text: Many students of China's Lost Generation studying at UCLA reside at UCHA.

chunks.title: Eduard Schweizer
chunks.text: Eduard Schweizer (1913-2006) was a Swiss New Testament scholar who taught at the University of Zurich for an extended period.

chunks.title: Eduard Schweizer
chunks.text: He won the Burkitt Medal for Biblical Studies in 1996.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: The National High School Debate League of China, or simply NHSDLC, is an English-language high school debate league serving Mainland China.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: It uses the Public Forum debate format.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: Each year, the NHSDLC sees around 50,000 students participate in its debate workshops and around 12,000 students participate in its regional or national tournaments that it hosts in more than 33 cities in China.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: According to The Economist, many students believe participating will help their application to a Western university.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: It was founded in 2012, and it hosted one of China's first ever English-language high school national debate tournaments for local students at Peking University in May 2013.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: Each year, its national debate championship hosted in Beijing attracts 450 students from around China.

chunks.title: National High School Debate League of China
chunks.text: NHSDLC is partnered with Harvard College Mentors for Urban Debate, Penn for Youth Debate, the Chicago Debate Society, the Yale Debate Association, Sunrise International Education, and the Stanford Youth Debate Initiative.

chunks.title: Donald B. Fullerton
chunks.text: Donald B. Fullerton (July 6, 1892 – April 9, 1985) was a Christian missionary and teacher who founded the Princeton Evangelical Fellowship and served with it from 1931 until 1980.

chunks.title: Donald B. Fullerton
chunks.text: He was noted for convincing many students at Princeton University of the truth of the Christian faith.

chunks.title: Donald B. Fullerton
chunks.text: Arthur Glasser also credited his conversion to Dr. Fullerton, through hearing him speak at the Keswick Bible Conference.

chunks.title: Donald B. Fullerton
chunks.text: In addition to his evangelistic efforts, Dr. Fullerton was a major spiritual influence on many students including Paul Pressler, a major figure in the Conservative resurgence of the Southern Baptist Convention, and the noted Reformed theologian John Frame.

chunks.title: Donald B. Fullerton
chunks.text: He was a member of the Princeton University Class of 1913 and received an honorary Doctorate of Ministry from Grace Theological Seminary.

chunks.title: Matthias Eduard Schweizer
chunks.text: Matthias Eduard Schweizer (8 August 1818 – 23 October 1860) was a Swiss chemist.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: Port Moody Secondary School is a public coeducational high school located in Port Moody, British Columbia.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: The school is notable for offering the International Baccalaureate Program and the Career Preparation Program to its students, which many students travel from other districts to participate in.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: There are approximately 400 students in the pre-International Baccalaureate Diploma programme and the International Baccalaureate diploma programme tracks.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: Port Moody Secondary is widely known in the area for sending an impressive number of students to the world's most selectivities universities.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: In the past three years, students have matriculated to schools such as: Harvard University, Princeton University, University of Chicago, University of Pennsylvania, Cornell University, UC Berkeley and Dartmouth College.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: Port Moody serves grades nine through twelve and currently has an enrollment of 1,312 students.

chunks.title: Port Moody Secondary School
chunks.text: The school is respected for its academics, visual arts, musical arts and athletic programs.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences (PGSS) is one of the Pennsylvania Governor's Schools of Excellence, a group of five-week summer programs for gifted high school students in the state of Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh has hosted the program since its inception in 1982.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: Most recently, it has been directed by Physics Professor Dr. Barry Luokkala.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: Participants are required to be Pennsylvania high school students between their junior and senior years and are required to live in the dormitories for the full five weeks of the program.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: Admission is very competitive - approximately 500 of the most scientifically gifted students in the state compete for 56 to 60 slots in the program.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The aim of PGSS is to promote interest in science rather than to advance students' knowledge in a specific area.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The curriculum includes five "core" courses in Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics and Physics, and numerous electives.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: In addition to taking classes, students are required to participate in a lab course and a research-style team project.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The emphasis is on cooperation, rather than competition - students are encouraged to both collaborate with other students on academic work and to interact socially.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The Residence Life staff provides a number of structured social events to foster friendship and teamwork.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: There is at least one event per day and is advertised on the social calendar in the dorm lobby.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: For many students, the social development gained from the program rivals the scientific knowledge they acquire.

chunks.title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
chunks.text: The students leave the program with a strong bond; most attend an organized reunion the following year after the 4th week of the program.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Symphony, the annual cultural festival of K. J. Somaiya College of Engineering, has created its name and popularity among Engineering and Management institutes far and wide for the last decade.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Every year many students from various institutes be a part of this festival.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: The main aim is to promote, encourage and exhibit the talents of the students on a common platform and create interest in the classical, vocal and instrumental music.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Symphony hosts more than 9000 students every year.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Symphony has been graced by artists of the magnitude of Pt.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pt ShivKumar Sharma, Louis Banks, Hariharan, Indus Creed, Parikrama, KK, Bombay Vikings, Taufiq Qureshi, Dagar, Suraj Jagan, and Ustad Zakir Hussain.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: The event also has a social touch to propagate a message relevant to the times like AIDS awareness, etc.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: There have also been Auto Shows and an Army display at Symphony.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: The organization is done by students which is also a time for building strong camaraderie and teamwork.

chunks.title: KJSCE Symphony
chunks.text: Many students look back fondly at the memories gathered during this phase of their lives.

chunks.title: Eaten by Lions (film)
chunks.text: Eaten by Lions is a British comedy feature film written and directed by Jason Wingard.

chunks.title: Eaten by Lions (film)
chunks.text: The film stars Antonio Aakeel, Jack Carroll, Johnny Vegas, and Asim Chaudhry.

chunks.title: Eaten by Lions (film)
chunks.text: The Film is the feature-length adaptation of the director's 2013 short film 'Going to Mecca' which won best comedy at the Manchester International Film Festival.

chunks.title: Eaten by Lions (film)
chunks.text: The feature follows half-brothers Omar and Pete as they embark on a journey to find Omar's estranged father, confronting him on the day of his daughters engagement party.

chunks.title: Circus Days
chunks.text: Circus Days (1923) is a feature length silent film comedy starring child actor Jackie Coogan, directed by Eddie Cline, produced by Sol Lesser and Jackie Coogan's own production company, and distributed through Associated First National Pictures.

chunks.title: Trust (1990 film)
chunks.text: Trust is a 1990 American dark romantic comedy starring Adrienne Shelly and Martin Donovan.

chunks.title: Trust (1990 film)
chunks.text: It is the second feature film from writer-director Hal Hartley.

chunks.title: Something's Got to Give
chunks.text: Something's Got to Give is an unfinished 1962 American feature film, directed by George Cukor for Twentieth Century-Fox and starring Marilyn Monroe, Dean Martin and Cyd Charisse.

chunks.title: Something's Got to Give
chunks.text: A remake of "My Favorite Wife" (1940), a screwball comedy starring Cary Grant and Irene Dunne, it was Monroe's last work, but from the beginning its production was disrupted by her personal troubles, and after her death on August 5, 1962, the film was abandoned.

chunks.title: Something's Got to Give
chunks.text: Most of its completed footage remained unseen for many years.

chunks.title: Confessions of a Sexist Pig
chunks.text: Confessions of a Sexist Pig is a 1998 American independent romantic comedy starring Edward Kerr and Traylor Howard.

chunks.title: Confessions of a Sexist Pig
chunks.text: It was directed and written by Sandy Tung.

chunks.title: Confessions of a Sexist Pig
chunks.text: It won Best Feature Film at the New Orleans International Film Festival, and the Werner Fassbinder Award at the Mannheim-Heidelberg International Film Festival.

chunks.title: Dexter Fletcher
chunks.text: Dexter Fletcher (born 31 January 1966) is an English actor and director.

chunks.title: Dexter Fletcher
chunks.text: He has appeared in the Guy Ritchie film "Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels", Crime comedy "Smoking Guns" as well as television roles in such shows as the comedy-drama "Hotel Babylon", the HBO series "Band of Brothers", and earlier in his career, the children's show "Press Gang", and the film "Bugsy Malone".

chunks.title: Dexter Fletcher
chunks.text: He also had a short-lived stint at presenting the third series of Channel 4's "GamesMaster" that aired between 1993 and 1994.

chunks.title: Dexter Fletcher
chunks.text: In 2016, he directed the feature film "Eddie the Eagle".

chunks.title: Sweet Revenge (1998 film)
chunks.text: Sweet Revenge is a 1998 British comedy film written and directed by Malcolm Mowbray.

chunks.title: Sweet Revenge (1998 film)
chunks.text: The screenplay is based on the epic two-part play "The Revengers' Comedies" by Alan Ayckbourn.

chunks.title: Still Crazy
chunks.text: Still Crazy is a 1998 British comedy film about a fictional 1970s rock band named "Strange Fruit", who, after being split up for two decades, are persuaded to get back together to perform at a reunion of the same concert venue where they played their last gig.

chunks.title: Still Crazy
chunks.text: The film focuses on the personal lives of the band members and those closest to them, and their individual experiences with approaching middle-age and the success that eluded them.

chunks.title: Easy Come, Easy Go (1967 film)
chunks.text: Easy Come, Easy Go is a 1967 American musical film comedy starring Elvis Presley.

chunks.title: Easy Come, Easy Go (1967 film)
chunks.text: Hal Wallis produced the film for Paramount Pictures, and it was his final movie for Elvis Presley.

chunks.title: Easy Come, Easy Go (1967 film)
chunks.text: The film co-starred Dodie Marshall, Pat Harrington, Jr., Pat Priest, Elsa Lanchester and Frank McHugh.

chunks.title: Easy Come, Easy Go (1967 film)
chunks.text: (It was McHugh's last feature film.)

chunks.title: Easy Come, Easy Go (1967 film)
chunks.text: The movie reached #50 on the "Variety" magazine national box office list in 1967.

chunks.title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
chunks.text: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels is a 1998 British crime comedy film written and directed by Guy Ritchie, produced by Matthew Vaughn and starring an ensemble cast featuring Jason Flemyng, Dexter Fletcher, Nick Moran, Jason Statham, Steven Mackintosh, Vinnie Jones, and Sting.

chunks.title: Elena Krykanova
chunks.text: Elena Krykanova, also romanized as Krikanova, (Russian: Елена Крыканова ) is a former ice dancer who represented the Soviet Union.

chunks.title: Elena Krykanova
chunks.text: With former partner Evgeni Platov, she is a three-time World Junior champion (1984–1986).

chunks.title: Elena Krykanova
chunks.text: They began skating together around December 1976 in Odessa and were coached by Boris Rublev until 1982 when they moved to Moscow to train under Natalia Dubova.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: Adam Alavdinovich Batirov (Russian: Адам Алавдинович Бати́ров ; born 13 January 1985 in Dagestan) is an Avar Dagestani-born Russian Naturalized Bahraini freestyle wrestler.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: He is World Cadet Championships runner-up and Cadet European Champion (2002).

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: Three time Ivan Yarygin winner, National Russian Freestyle wrestling Champion (2007).

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: Senior European Champion.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: At the 2016 Asian Wrestling Championships he won gold medal, in final match he beat Kumar Vinod of India.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: Adam is the younger brother of two-time Olympic Champion Mavlet Batirov.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: After won 2016 World Wrestling Olympic Qualification Tournament 1 he qualified Bahrain for the 2016 Summer Olympics.

chunks.title: Adam Batirov
chunks.text: But he lost in round one to Ikhtiyor Navruzov from Uzbekistan.

chunks.title: Hrant Shahinyan
chunks.text: Hrant Shahinyan (Armenian: Հրանտ Շահինյան ) (July 30, 1923 – May 29, 1996) also known as Grant Shaginyan was a Soviet Armenian gymnast.

chunks.title: Hrant Shahinyan
chunks.text: Specializing in the still rings and pommel horse, he is a two-time Olympic Champion, two-time World Champion and seven-time USSR Champion.

chunks.title: Ludmila Belousova
chunks.text: Ludmila Yevgenyevna Belousova (Russian: Людмила Евгеньевна Белоусова ; 22 November 1935 – 29 September 2017) was a Russian pair skater who represented the Soviet Union.

chunks.title: Ludmila Belousova
chunks.text: With her partner and husband Oleg Protopopov she was a two-time Olympic champion (1964, 1968) and four-time World champion (1965–1968).

chunks.title: Ludmila Belousova
chunks.text: In 1979 the pair defected to Switzerland and became Swiss citizens in 1995.

chunks.title: Ludmila Belousova
chunks.text: They continued to skate at ice shows and exhibitions through their seventies.

chunks.title: Oksana Grishuk
chunks.text: Oksana (Pasha) Vladimirovna Grishuk (Russian: Оксана (Паша) Владимировна Грищук ; born March 17, 1972) is a Russian former competitive ice dancer.

chunks.title: Oksana Grishuk
chunks.text: She is best known for her partnership with Evgeni Platov from 1989–1998.

chunks.title: Oksana Grishuk
chunks.text: With Platov, she is a two-time Olympic champion (1994, 1998), four-time World champion (1994–1997), and three-time European champion (1996–1998).

chunks.title: Oksana Grishuk
chunks.text: With previous partner Alexandr Chichkov, she is the 1988 World Junior champion.

chunks.title: Gail Devers
chunks.text: Yolanda Gail Devers ( ; born November 19, 1966) is an American retired track and field athlete.

chunks.title: Gail Devers
chunks.text: A two-time Olympic champion in the 100 meters for the USA, her 1996 win made her only the second woman (after Wyomia Tyus) to successfully defend an Olympic 100m title.

chunks.title: Gail Devers
chunks.text: She won a third Olympic gold medal in the 4 x 100m relay in 1996.

chunks.title: Gail Devers
chunks.text: She is also the 1993 World champion in the 100m and a three-time World champion in the 100m hurdles.

chunks.title: Gail Devers
chunks.text: In 2011, she was inducted into the National Track and Field Hall of Fame.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: Randall Scott "Randy" Lewis (born June 7, 1959, in Rapid City, South Dakota) is an American wrestler and olympic champion.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: He competed at the 1984 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, where he received a gold medal in freestyle featherweight.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: After winning three high school state titles in South Dakota, he was a four-time All-American and two-time NCAA champion at the University of Iowa.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: A two-time Olympian, and 1984 Olympic champion in Los Angeles.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: At Iowa, he was a four-time All-American and two-time NCAA champion.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: Was member of 1980 Olympic team but President Jimmy Carter's boycott prevented the U.S. team from traveling to the Games in Moscow.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: Won gold medal at 136.5 pounds in freestyle wrestling at 1984 Olympics, outscoring his first four opponents 52-4 to advance to the final, where he crushed Japan's Kosei Akaishi 24-11 in 4:52.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: He was second in the 1988 Olympic trials to John Smith, who wound up winning a gold medal.

chunks.title: Randy Lewis (wrestler)
chunks.text: Lewis was also 1983 Pan American Games champion.

chunks.title: Dietmar Schauerhammer
chunks.text: Dietmar Schauerhammer (born 12 August 1955 in Neustadt an der Orla, Thuringia) is an East German two-time Winter Olympic champion, pentathlete, decathlete and bob pusher for six-time World champion, two-time Olympic champion, four-time European champion, two-time German champion and five-time GDR champion Wolfgang Hoppe who competed during the 1980s.

chunks.title: Dietmar Schauerhammer
chunks.text: Competing in two Winter Olympics, he won three medals with two golds (Two-man: 1984, Four-man: 1984) and one silver (Four-man: 1988).

chunks.title: Evgeni Platov
chunks.text: Evgeni Arkadievich Platov (Russian: Евгений Аркадьевич Платов , born August 7, 1967) is a Russian former competitive ice dancer.

chunks.title: Evgeni Platov
chunks.text: He is best known for his partnership with Oksana Grishuk from 1989–1998.

chunks.title: Evgeni Platov
chunks.text: With Grishuk, he is a two-time Olympic champion (1994, 1998), four-time World champion (1994–1997), and three-time European champion (1996–1998).

chunks.title: Roman Vlasov
chunks.text: Roman Andreyevich Vlasov (Russian: Роман Андреевич Власов ; born 6 October 1990) is a Russian Greco-Roman wrestler.

chunks.title: Roman Vlasov
chunks.text: He is a two-time Olympic Champion (2012, 2016), a two-time World Champion (2011, 2015), and a two-time European Champion (2012, 2013).

chunks.title: Roman Vlasov
chunks.text: He also won the gold medal at the 2013 Summer Universiade.

chunks.title: Roman Vlasov
chunks.text: Furthermore, he was runner-up at the 2013 World Championships and the 2014 and 2015 World Cup.

chunks.title: Roman Vlasov
chunks.text: Vlasov trains under Viktor Kuznetsov, the same coach who raised Aleksandr Karelin.

chunks.title: European Masters Games
chunks.text: The European Masters Games (EMG) is a multi-sport event, consisting of summer sports, that is held every four years.

chunks.title: European Masters Games
chunks.text: The age categories vary depending on the sport but the competition is generally for people 30–35 years or older.

chunks.title: European Masters Games
chunks.text: The first games were held in 2008 in Malmö, Sweden.

chunks.title: European Masters Games
chunks.text: The European Masters Games are held once every four year, while the last games were held in 2015 in Nice, France, the next games will be celebrated in Torino, Italy, in 2019.

chunks.title: European Masters Games
chunks.text: The International Masters Games Association (IMGA), which is based in Lausanne, Switzerland, is the body responsible for the bidding and placing of the games.

chunks.title: Antisemitism in the Olympic Games
chunks.text: The modern Olympic Games or Olympics (French: "Jeux olympiques" ), are leading international sporting events featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in a variety of competitions.

chunks.title: Antisemitism in the Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Olympic Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition with more than 200 nations participating.

chunks.title: Antisemitism in the Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.

chunks.title: Antisemitism in the Olympic Games
chunks.text: In the Olympic games during the years, although its approach of "peace through sport", there have been many anti-Semitic occasions which brought the politics into the sports field, and at least in 1972 – ended in the death of eleven Israeli athletes.

chunks.title: Olympic Games
chunks.text: The modern Olympic Games or Olympics (French: "Jeux olympiques" ) are leading international sporting events featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in a variety of competitions.

chunks.title: Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Olympic Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition with more than 200 nations participating.

chunks.title: Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.

chunks.title: Elections in Japan
chunks.text: The Japanese political system has three types of elections: general elections to the House of Representatives held every four years (unless the lower house is dissolved earlier), elections to the House of Councillors held every three years to choose one-half of its members, and local elections held every four years for offices in prefectures, cities, and villages.

chunks.title: Elections in Japan
chunks.text: Elections are supervised by election committees at each administrative level under the general direction of the Central Election Administration Committee, an attached organization to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC).

chunks.title: Elections in Japan
chunks.text: The minimum voting age in Japan's non-compulsory electoral system was reduced from twenty to eighteen years in June 2016.

chunks.title: Elections in Japan
chunks.text: Voters must satisfy a three-month residency requirement before being allowed to cast a ballot.

chunks.title: Winter Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Olympic Winter Games (official name) (French: "Jeux olympiques d'hiver" ) is a major international sporting event held once every four years, for sports practised on snow and ice.

chunks.title: Winter Olympic Games
chunks.text: The first Winter Olympics, the 1924 Winter Olympics, was held in Chamonix, France.

chunks.title: Winter Olympic Games
chunks.text: The original five sports (broken into nine disciplines) were bobsleigh, curling, ice hockey, Nordic skiing (consisting of the disciplines military patrol, cross-country skiing, Nordic combined, and ski jumping), and skating (consisting of the disciplines figure skating and speed skating).

chunks.title: Winter Olympic Games
chunks.text: The Games were held every four years from 1924 to 1936, interrupted in 1940 and 1944 by World War II, and resumed in 1948.

chunks.title: Winter Olympic Games
chunks.text: Until 1992 the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

chunks.title: Fatma Lanouar
chunks.text: Fatma Lanouar (Arabic: فاطمة لأنور; born March 14, 1978) is a former female middle distance runner from Tunisia.

chunks.title: Fatma Lanouar
chunks.text: She is best known for twice (2001 and 2005) winning the gold medal at the Mediterranean Games in the women's 1500 metres.

chunks.title: Fatma Lanouar
chunks.text: Lanouar set her personal best (4:06.91) in the 1,500 metres in 2000.

chunks.title: Fatma Lanouar
chunks.text: She was also the silver medallist at the 2001 Jeux de la Francophonie.

chunks.title: Women's Rugby World Cup
chunks.text: The Women's Rugby World Cup is the premier international competition in rugby union for women.

chunks.title: Women's Rugby World Cup
chunks.text: The tournament is organised by the sport's governing body, World Rugby.

chunks.title: Women's Rugby World Cup
chunks.text: The championships are currently held every four years; the event was most recently held in France in August 2014.

chunks.title: Women's Rugby World Cup
chunks.text: World Rugby has chosen to reset the tournament on a new four-year cycle to avoid conflict with the Olympics and Women's World Cup Sevens; the next World Cup will thus be held in Dublin, Ireland and Belfast, Northern Ireland in 2017 and then every four years thereafter.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: The number of elections in Iowa varies from year to year.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: Presidential elections are held every four years.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: Since 1972, Iowa has been the first state to vote in presidential primaries, with their caucuses.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: As with presidential elections, gubernatorial elections are held every four years - but are staggered such that they are held on general elections independently of the presidential election.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: Members of the Iowa Senate are elected every four years, with half of the Senate elected at each general election; all members of the Iowa House of Representatives are elected every two years.

chunks.title: Elections in Iowa
chunks.text: Additionally, elections for various government officials, judicial retention elections, and elections on referenda occur as part of various elections in Iowa.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: The national Scout jamboree is a gathering, or jamboree, of thousands of members of the Boy Scouts of America, usually held every four years and organized by the National Council of the Boy Scouts of America.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: Referred to as "the Jamboree", "Jambo", or NSJ, Scouts from all over the nation and world have the opportunity to attend.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: They are considered to be one of several unique experiences that the Boy Scouts of America offers.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: The first jamboree was scheduled to be held in 1935 in Washington, D.C. to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Scouting, but was delayed two years after being cancelled due to a polio outbreak.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: The 1937 jamboree in Washington attracted 25,000 Scouts, who camped around the Washington Monument and Tidal Basin.

chunks.title: National Scout jamboree (Boy Scouts of America)
chunks.text: The event was covered extensively by national media and attended by President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

chunks.title: Mediterranean Games
chunks.text: The Mediterranean Games are a multi-sport games held usually every four years, between nations around or very close to the Mediterranean Sea, where Europe, Africa, and Asia meet.

chunks.title: Mediterranean Games
chunks.text: The games are under the auspices of the International Committee of Mediterranean Games (CIJM).

chunks.title: Evidently... John Cooper Clarke
chunks.text: Evidently... John Cooper Clarke is a 2012 television documentary about the life of the Salford performance poet John Cooper Clarke.

chunks.title: Evidently... John Cooper Clarke
chunks.text: It was directed by John Ross and produced by Scotty Clark and was first aired on BBC Four in May 2012 as part of BBC Four and BBC 6 Music's "Punk Britannia" season.

chunks.title: Evidently... John Cooper Clarke
chunks.text: It features testimonies from Alex Turner, Bill Bailey, Pete Shelley, Paul Farley, Steve Coogan, Mark Radcliffe, Craig Charles, Plan B, Kate Nash, Miranda Sawyer and Paul Morley; and poems by Clarke including "Things Are Gonna Get Worse", "Evidently Chickentown", "Twat" and "Beasley Street".

chunks.title: Music for Miners
chunks.text: Music for Miners (MFM) was a collective of UK writers, artists and filmmakers (including several independent television producers associated with RPM Productions and Channel 4) who attempted to engage young people with politics during the UK Miner's Strike of 1984-1985.

chunks.title: Music for Miners
chunks.text: Members of the collective included the television producer Don Coutts and the writer and artist Ian McKay.

chunks.title: Music for Miners
chunks.text: Music for Miners organised several events to raise funds and support striking miners, the most notable of which was the MFM event held at the Royal Festival Hall in London on May 14, 1984.

chunks.title: Music for Miners
chunks.text: The English rock group New Order headlined the event with John Cooper Clarke supporting.

chunks.title: Music for Miners
chunks.text: Music for Miners was disbanded soon after the end of the strike in March 1985.

chunks.title: Splitting Image
chunks.text: Splitting Image is a 2 issue comic-book limited series created in 1993 by Don Simpson (though based on an idea from Image co-founder Rob Liefeld ) and published by Image Comics.

chunks.title: Splitting Image
chunks.text: It satirizes the founders of Image and their initial titles such as "Savage Dragon", "Spawn", "Youngblood", "WildC.A.T.s: Covert Action Teams", "Cyber Force", "Shadowhawk", "Wetworks", and "Pitt".

chunks.title: Splitting Image
chunks.text: Issue #2 ends with a cliffhanger ending featuring Megaton Man, Captain Everything from "normalman", and Mr. Spook from "Tales of the Beanworld" which was continued in the "Megaton Man/normalman Special".

chunks.title: Steve Coogan
chunks.text: Stephen John Coogan (born 14 October 1965) is an English actor, stand-up comedian, impressionist, screenwriter, and producer.

chunks.title: Steve Coogan
chunks.text: He began his career in the 1980s, working as a voice artist on the satirical puppet show "Spitting Image" and providing voiceovers for television advertisements.

chunks.title: Steve Coogan
chunks.text: In the early 1990s, he began creating original comic characters, leading him to win the Perrier Award at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

chunks.title: Steve Coogan
chunks.text: In 1999, he co-founded the production company Baby Cow Productions.

chunks.title: Walking Back to Happiness
chunks.text: Walking Back to Happiness is the third album by John Cooper Clarke, originally released on 10" clear vinyl in 1979, and long out of print.

chunks.title: Walking Back to Happiness
chunks.text: All tracks were recorded live, with the exception of the final track, "Gimmix", was re-recorded in studio and became a UK top 40 hit that year.

chunks.title: Walking Back to Happiness
chunks.text: The penultimate track refers to "The Marble Index" a 1969 album by Nico, with whom Clarke had a romance in the mid-1980s.

chunks.title: Evidently Chickentown
chunks.text: "Evidently Chickentown" is a poem by the English performance poet John Cooper Clarke.

chunks.title: Evidently Chickentown
chunks.text: The poem uses repeated profanity to convey a sense of futility and exasperation.

chunks.title: Evidently Chickentown
chunks.text: Featured on Clarke's 1980 album "Snap, Crackle & Bop", the realism of its lyrics is married with haunting, edgy arrangements.

chunks.title: Pauline Murray and The Invisible Girls (album)
chunks.text: Pauline Murray and the Invisible Girls (sometimes called Untitled) is the only album made by Penetration singer Pauline Murray and the Invisible Girls, John Cooper Clarke's backing band.

chunks.title: Pauline Murray and The Invisible Girls (album)
chunks.text: It was released in September 1980 on the RSO label.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: George F. Fitzpatrick (1875–1920) was a prominent barrister of East Indian descent and member of Trinidad & Tobago's Legislative Council.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: He played an early role in helping bring to light malpractices carried out under the system of Indian indentured labour.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: In 1909, George Fitzpatrick provided testimony before a British parliamentary investigation, led by Lord Sanderson, regarding alleged mistreatment of East Indian labourers living in Trinidad.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: The Sanderson Committee, however, failed to bring about the immediate abolition of the indentured system, only its postponement, which was further deferred by the onset of the First World War.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: It was not until January 2, 1920, that the system of indentured labour would come to an end.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: George F. Fitzpatrick's son, Hon. George Fitzpatrick, trained as a solicitor and served a three-year term as member of parliament, representing the district of San Fernando.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: Following the death of his first wife during childbirth, Hon. George Fitzpatrick married Phyllis Sinanan, sister of Mitra and Ashford Sinanan, uniting the Fitzpatrick family with another prominent political family of Trinidad (see Ashford Sinanan, Ambassador, Leader of the Opposition, Democratic Labour Party (DLP), West Indies Federation, Founder of the West Indian National Party (WINP) and High Commissioner to India.

chunks.title: George F. Fitzpatrick
chunks.text: See also M. Sinanan, "Constitution Commission of Trinidad and Tobago," presented to His Excellency Sir Ellis Clarke, Commander-in-Chief of Trinidad and Tobago, January 22, 1974.

chunks.title: Beasley Street
chunks.text: "Beasley Street" is one of the many notable works by punk poet John Cooper Clarke.

chunks.title: Beasley Street
chunks.text: Dealing with poverty in inner-city Salford in the Britain of Margaret Thatcher, Cooper Clarke has said that the poem was inspired by Camp Street in Lower Broughton.

chunks.title: Beasley Street
chunks.text: It has a relentless theme of squalor and despair:

chunks.title: Disguise in Love
chunks.text: Disguise in Love is the second studio album by John Cooper Clarke, first released in 1978.

chunks.title: Disguise in Love
chunks.text: (It followed "Ou est la maison de fromage?

chunks.title: Disguise in Love
chunks.text: Most of the tracks are spoken over musical accompaniment provided by Clarke's band The Invisible Girls, except "Psycle Sluts 1&2" and "Salome Maloney" — both live recordings from the Ritz Ballroom in Manchester on 8 May 1978, delivered in his trademark a cappella style.

chunks.title: Maxsta
chunks.text: Ian Koromah, better known by the stage name Maxsta, is an English grime MC from South East London.

chunks.title: Maxsta
chunks.text: Having been an active and high profile member of the London urban music scene for several years, he recently attracted attention for being signed to Just Jam, a subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment.

chunks.title: Maxsta
chunks.text: A fast-paced, choppy style of delivery has led him to be compared to fellow London rapper Dizzee Rascal.

chunks.title: Maxsta
chunks.text: He has worked with some of the most notable members in grime and UK hip hop, including Tinie Tempah, Chipmunk and Wiley.

chunks.title: Maxsta
chunks.text: He is known as not just one of the best MC's of his age group but one of the best in the whole of the Grime scene.

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: "Amazing" is a song by American hip hop artist Kanye West, released as the third single for his fourth studio album, "808s & Heartbreak".

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: Co-produced with Victor Alexander, the song features hip hop artist Young Jeezy and contains additional vocals provided by Mr Hudson and Tony Williams.

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: This song was used in the NBA during the 2009 Playoffs, and is featured on the "NBA 2K10" and "NBA 2K13" soundtracks.

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: UFC Fighter Frank Mir walks out to this song before his fights.

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: The song was nominated at the 52nd Grammy Awards in the Best Rap Performance By a Duo or Group category.

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: The song also marks the second collaboration with Kanye West and Young Jeezy, the first being Young Jeezy's 2008 single "Put On".

chunks.title: Amazing (Kanye West song)
chunks.text: The song also marks the two rappers' second time to do a song to be nominated for a Grammy award.

chunks.title: Big Dada
chunks.text: Big Dada is a British independent record label imprint distributed by Ninja Tune.

chunks.title: Big Dada
chunks.text: It was started by reputed hip hop journalist Will Ashon in 1997.

chunks.title: Big Dada
chunks.text: It is best known for being the home of prominent British hip hop artist Roots Manuva, poet and playwright Kate Tempest, grime pioneer Wiley, rapper and designer DELS and Mercury Prize winners Speech Debelle and Young Fathers.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: Anomaly is the seventh studio album by American Christian hip hop artist Lecrae, released on September 9, 2014, through Reach Records.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: The album features appearances from Crystal Nicole, Kari Jobe, and For King & Country, along with label-mate Andy Mineo.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: "Anomaly" met with a positive critical reception, and the song "Nuthin", released for streaming as a single on July 1, 2014, was nominated for the 2014 BET Hip Hop Awards in the best Impact Track category.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: The album also fared well commercially, debuting at No. 1 on the "Billboard" 200 with over 88,000 copies sold.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: It also debuted at No. 1 on the Top Gospel Albums chart, marking the first time that any artist has ever topped both the 200 and Gospel charts.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: "Anomaly" won Rap/Hip Hop Album of the Year at the 2015 GMA Dove Awards, and Rap, Hip Hop Gospel CD of the Year at the 2015 Stellar Awards.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: Two songs earned a nomination for the 2015 Grammy Awards; "All I Need is You" was nominated for Best Rap Performance, and "Messengers", featuring For King & Country, which won Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song.

chunks.title: Anomaly (Lecrae album)
chunks.text: Rolling Stone ranked it at No. 12 on their list "40 best rap albums of 2014".

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: Lecrae is an American Christian hip hop artist.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: His career began in 2004 when he and Ben Washer co-founded the record label Reach Records.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: In 2007 his first album, "Real Talk" (2005)"," received a nomination at the Stellar Awards and his second album, "After the Music Stops" (2007), was nominated at the GMA Dove Awards.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: The following year Lecrae's third album, "Rebel", became the first Christian hip hop album to chart at number one on the U.S. "Billboard" Gospel Albums Chart.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: In 2011 his fourth album, "Rehab" (2010), received a Grammy nomination for Best Rock Gospel Album.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: That year Lecrae began achieving mainstream success and recognition after he collaborated with DJ Statik Selektah on the song "Live & Let Live" and performed at the 2011 BET Hip Hop Awards Cypher.

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: The following year he garnered two GMA Dove awards: Rap/Hip Hop Album of the Year for "" (2011) and Rap/Hip Hop Recorded Song of the Year for "Hallelujah" (2011).

chunks.title: List of awards and nominations received by Lecrae
chunks.text: He also released the mixtape "Church Clothes" and the studio album "Gravity", the latter of which of has been called the most important album in Christian hip hop history by Rapzilla and "Atlanta Daily World".

chunks.title: Stormzy
chunks.text: Michael Ebenazer Kwadjo Omari Owuo, Jr. (born 26 July 1993), better known by his stage name Stormzy, is an English grime and hip hop artist.

chunks.title: Stormzy
chunks.text: He won Best Grime Act at the 2014 and 2015 MOBO Awards and was named as an artist to look out for in the BBC's influential Sound of 2015 list.

chunks.title: Stormzy
chunks.text: His most successful song to date is the BPI gold-selling "Shut Up", which was initially released as a freestyle on YouTube.

chunks.title: Stormzy
chunks.text: The track was then officially released and got to number eight on the UK Singles Chart after Stormzy launched a campaign to reach Christmas number one.

chunks.title: Oh My (DJ Drama song)
chunks.text: "Oh My" is a song by American hip hop artist DJ Drama, released on May 13, 2011, as the lead single from his third studio album "Third Power".

chunks.title: Oh My (DJ Drama song)
chunks.text: The song was produced by frequent collaborator Drumma Boy and features rappers Fabolous, Roscoe Dash and Wiz Khalifa.

chunks.title: Oh My (DJ Drama song)
chunks.text: The song peaked at #18 on the "Billboard" and #12 on the Top R&B/Hip-Hop Songs, making it the most successful song for DJ Drama to date.

chunks.title: Grime Wave
chunks.text: Grime Wave is the fourth album by English grime artist Wiley.

chunks.title: Grime Wave
chunks.text: The album was released on 26 May 2008 by Eskibeat Recordings.

chunks.title: Grime Wave
chunks.text: It is debated whether "Grime Wave" is an album or a mixtape.

chunks.title: Grime Wave
chunks.text: It is in fact his fourth album as stated in the track "Where You Gonna Run Too?"

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: "Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom" is a single by Australian hip hop group Hilltop Hoods.

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: The song is the fourth official single from their sixth album Drinking From the Sun.

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: The song was announced to be the fourth single on 14 September through their official website and Facebook by posting the artwork of the single.

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: They announced that the single will be released on 21 September.

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: They also said that there was something big happening with Australian hip hop and that there will be more announced on the same date as the single is released.

chunks.title: Rattling the Keys to the Kingdom
chunks.text: On the artwork there are Australian hip hop artist logos, tags and Australian hip hop labels logos which are put together to form a crown.

chunks.title: Big for Your Boots
chunks.text: "Big for Your Boots" is a song by English rapper Stormzy.

chunks.title: Big for Your Boots
chunks.text: It was released as the lead single from his debut studio album "Gang Signs & Prayer" on 3 February 2017, by <nowiki>#</nowiki>Merky Records.

chunks.title: Big for Your Boots
chunks.text: The song was written by Stormzy and produced by Sir Spyro and Fraser T Smith.

chunks.title: Big for Your Boots
chunks.text: It peaked at number six on the UK Singles Chart, becoming Stormzy's highest-charting single to date at the time of release.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: The song "See The U.S.A.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: In Your Chevrolet" (title as filed for 1950 copyright) is a commercial jingle from c. 1949, with lyrics and music by Leo Corday (ASCAP) and Leon Carr (ASCAP), written for the Chevrolet Division of General Motors.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: The song was the Chevrolet jingle sung on the show "Inside U.S.A. with Chevrolet" by Chevrolet's real-life husband-wife duo, Peter Lind Hayes and Mary Healy, years before it became associated with Dinah Shore through Chevrolet's decade-long sponsorship of her television shows.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: Dinah Shore sang the song after 1952, and it became something of a signature song for her.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: Later the song was also sung by male spokesman Pat Boone on his "Pat Boone-Chevy Showroom" (ABC) from 1957 through 1960.

chunks.title: See the USA in Your Chevrolet
chunks.text: When the games of the Los Angeles Dodgers were televised in the 1960s, commercials were aired with the song sung by John Roseboro and Don Drysdale, whose singing careers, announcer Vin Scully said, were "destined to go absolutely nowhere."

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: Linda Ellen November (born October 16, 1944) is an American singer who has sung tens of thousands of commercial jingles.

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: She was the voice of the singing cat in the Meow Mix commercials, sang the jingle "Galaxy Glue" in the 1981 film "The Incredible Shrinking Woman", the "Coke and a Smile" jingle in the classic Mean Joe Greene Super Bowl commercial, and has won many Clio Awards for her work on television and radio.

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: Her voice can also be heard on many pop songs, as she was a regular backup singer for artists such as Frankie Valli, Burt Bacharach, Engelbert Humperdinck, and Neil Diamond.

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: In the 1970s, she was one of the main singers in the disco group Wing and a Prayer Fife and Drum Corps, which charted with the Top 40 hit "Baby Face" in 1976.

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: In the 1980s and 1990s she was a regular performer in Atlantic City at The Grand and Harrah's, with her husband, composer and arranger Artie Schroeck.

chunks.title: Linda November
chunks.text: As of 2011, she works as a piano accompanist in Las Vegas, Nevada.

chunks.title: Bing Rodrigo
chunks.text: Bing Rodrigo (1954–2001) is a Filipino singer most famous for songs such as Bakit May Pag-ibig Pa and Gintong Araw.

chunks.title: Bing Rodrigo
chunks.text: He was also known to have sang the most memorable jingle in all of Philippine culture, the "Seiko Wallet" commercial.

chunks.title: Bing Rodrigo
chunks.text: He was contemporary to Jun Polistico and Nonoy Zuniga, and was crowned "King of Tagalog Songs" in 1982, and scored a number of gold records.

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: The Distrito Federal Trios Championship is a "Trios" (six-man) tag team Championship primarily promoted by the Mexican Lucha libre professional wrestling promotion International Wrestling Revolution Group (IWRG).

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: The title was created in 1986 and is controlled by the "Comisión de Box y Lucha Libre Mexico D.F." ("Mexico City Boxing and Wrestling Commission"), which regulates all matches where the title is defended, allowing it to only be defended in Mexico City and the State of Mexico.

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: It is considered a secondary, lower level championship than the Mexican National Trios Championship also sanctioned by the Commission but almost exclusively controlled by Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL).

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: IWRG has held the control of the Distrito Federal Trios Championship since IWRG was founded in 1996 and has at times been a secondary title for the promotion, below the IWRG Intercontinental Trios Championship.

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: The championship is not restricted by nationality, only by geographical location of where it can or cannot be defended.

chunks.title: Distrito Federal Trios Championship
chunks.text: Being a professional wrestling championship, it is not won legitimately: it is instead won via a scripted ending to a match or awarded to a wrestler because of a storyline.

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: Leslie Pearl is an American pop singer-songwriter born in Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: She wrote hits for Crystal Gayle, Karen Carpenter, Kenny Rogers, Johnny Mathis, and Dr. Hook, among others.

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: She recorded two albums, the first, "Pearl" with singer (sister) Deborah Pearl on London Records, scoring a chart hit on her second with the RCA Records single, "If the Love Fits Wear It".

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: The song peaked at number 28 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and number 7 on the Adult Contemporary chart in 1982.

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: She also wrote and sang jingles for Pepsi, Folgers Coffee, Ford, Gillette and others.

chunks.title: Leslie Pearl
chunks.text: Composed in 1984 Pearl's Folger Coffee jingle been transformed into country, gospel, jazz, R & B, folk, Celtic, and a cappella versions and Folgers runs an annual contest to find the best new interpretation.

chunks.title: Crucial FM

chunks.title: Evander Bradley McGilvary
chunks.text: Evander Bradley McGilvary Ph.D. (July 19, 1864–September 11, 1953) was an American philosophical scholar, born in Bangkok to American Presbyterian missionaries, the Rev. Daniel McGilvary and Mrs. Sophia McGilvary.

chunks.title: Evander Bradley McGilvary
chunks.text: He came to the United States to study, graduating from Davidson College (N.C.) in 1884 and from Princeton University (A.M.) in 1888.

chunks.title: Evander Bradley McGilvary

chunks.title: Evander Bradley McGilvary
chunks.text: In the wake of the 1893 heresy trial of Charles Augustus Briggs, whose views on Scripture he agreed with, McGilvary resigned from the Laos Mission in 1894 and returned to the United States.

chunks.title: Evander Bradley McGilvary

chunks.text: The school uses the Baptist Faith and Message (2000) as its confessional statement (see the "Southwestern Declaration on Academic and Theological Integrity") Its stand on inerrancy and gender is as stated in the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy, which states that science cannot override scriptural statements on creation and the flood, and the Danvers Statement on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood.

chunks.title: Francis Schaeffer

chunks.title: Francis Schaeffer

chunks.title: Biblical inerrancy
chunks.text: Biblical inerrancy, as formulated in the "Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy", is the doctrine that the Protestant Bible "is without error or fault in all its teaching"; or, at least, that "Scripture in the original manuscripts does not affirm anything that is contrary to fact".

chunks.title: Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy
chunks.text: At a conference sponsored by the International Council on Biblical Inerrancy (ICBI) and held in Chicago in October 1978, more than 200 evangelical leaders formulated the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy.

chunks.title: Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy
chunks.text: The statement was designed to defend the position of Biblical inerrancy against a perceived trend toward liberal conceptions of Scripture.

chunks.title: Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy
chunks.text: Those signing the statement came from a variety of evangelical Christian denominations, and included Robert Preus, James Montgomery Boice, Kenneth Kantzer, J. I. Packer, Francis Schaeffer, R. C. Sproul and John F. MacArthur.

chunks.title: Biblical authority
chunks.text: The term biblical authority refers to the extent to which commandments and doctrines within the Old and New Testament scriptures are authoritative over human belief and conduct, as well as the extent to which their propositions are accurate in matters of history and science.

chunks.title: Biblical authority
chunks.text: Biblical authority stems from the fact that God has revealed himself in written form through human authors and that the information contained in the canonical books is not of human origin.

chunks.title: Biblical authority
chunks.text: It entails, but is not exhausted by, questions raised by biblical inerrancy, biblical infallibility, biblical interpretation, biblical criticism, and Biblical law in Christianity.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: Tidal flooding, also known as sunny day flooding or nuisance flooding, is the temporary inundation of low-lying areas, especially streets, during exceptionally high tide events, such as at full and new moons.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: The highest tides of the year may be known as the king tide, with the month varying by location.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: In Florida, controversy was created when state-level government mandated that the term "nuisance flooding" and other terms be used in place of terms such as sea level rise, climate change and global warming, prompting allegations of climate change denial, specifically against Governor Rick Scott.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: This amid Florida, specifically South Florida and the Miami metropolitan area being one of the most at risk areas in the world for the potential effects of sea level rise, and where the frequency and severity of tidal flooding events increased in the 21st century.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: The issue is more bipartisan in South Florida, particularly in places like Miami Beach, where a several hundred million dollar project is underway to install more than 50 pumps and physically raise roads to combat the flooding, mainly along the west side of South Beach, formerly a mangrove wetland where the average elevation is less than one meter (3.3 feet).

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: In the Miami area, where the vast majority of the land is below 10 ft , even a one-foot increase over the average high tide can cause widespread flooding.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: The 2015 and 2016 king tide event levels reached about 4 ft MLLW, 3 ft above mean sea level, or about 2 ft NAVD88, and nearly the same above MHHW.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: While the tide range is very small in Miami, averaging about 2 ft , with the greatest range being less than 2 m , the area is very acute to minute differences down to single inches due to the vast area at low elevation.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: NOAA tide gauge data for most stations shows current water level graphs relative to a fixed datum, as well as mean sea level trends for some stations.

chunks.title: Tidal flooding
chunks.text: During the king tides, the local Miami area tide gauge at Virginia Key shows levels running at times 1 ft or more over datum.

chunks.title: Michel Thomas
chunks.text: Michel Thomas (born Moniek Kroskof, February 3, 1914 – January 8, 2005) was a polyglot linguist, and decorated war veteran.

chunks.title: Michel Thomas

chunks.title: Michel Thomas

chunks.title: French Resistance
chunks.text: The French Resistance (French: "La Résistance" ) was the collection of French movements that fought against the Nazi German occupation of France and against the collaborationist Vichy régime during the Second World War.

chunks.title: French Resistance
chunks.text: Résistance cells were small groups of armed men and women (called the Maquis in rural areas), who, in addition to their guerrilla warfare activities, were also publishers of underground newspapers, providers of first-hand intelligence information, and maintainers of escape networks that helped Allied soldiers and airmen trapped behind enemy lines.

chunks.title: French Resistance
chunks.text: The men and women of the Résistance came from all economic levels and political leanings of French society, including émigrés; academics, students, aristocrats, conservative Roman Catholics (including priests) and also citizens from the ranks of liberals, anarchists and communists.

chunks.title: Women in the French Resistance
chunks.text: Women in the French Resistance played an important role in the context of the resistance to occupying German forces during World War II.

chunks.title: Women in the French Resistance
chunks.text: Women represented 15 to 20% of the total number of French Resistance fighters within the country.

chunks.title: Women in the French Resistance
chunks.text: Women also represented 15% of political deportations to Nazi-run concentration camps.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel
chunks.text: Madeleine Truel (Lima, Peru, 28 August 1904 - Stolpe, Parchim, Germany, 1945), was a Peruvian woman of French parentage who fought in the French Resistance.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel
chunks.text: The exact date of Madeleine Truel's alliance with the French Resistance is unknown.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel
chunks.text: She worked as a document forger.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel
chunks.text: She was captured in 1944 and was tortured to extract information without success, following which she was sent to Sachsenhausen concentration camp in 1945.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel
chunks.text: She died in Stolpe (Germany) on 3 May 1945, after the so-called "death march", a few hours before the Russian troops arrived.

chunks.title: Madeleine Truel

chunks.title: Guy Môquet

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: René Carmille (born Trémolat, Dordogne, 1886; died Dachau, Bavaria, 25 January 1945) was a punched card computer expert and comptroller general of the French Army in the early 20th century.

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: In World War II he was a double agent for the French Resistance and part of the Marco Polo Network.

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: He ran the Demographics Department ("Service de la démographie") of Vichy which soon through a merger with the SGF (General Statistics of France) became the new National Statistics Service, which he continued to head up.

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: In this capacity, he sabotaged the Nazi census of France, saving untold numbers of Jewish people from death camps.

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: The IEEE newspaper, "The Institute", describes Carmille as being an early ethical hacker: "Over the course of two years, Carmille and his group purposely delayed the process by mishandling the punch cards.

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: He also hacked his own machines, reprogramming them so that they’d never punch information from Column 11 [which indicated religion] onto any census card."

chunks.title: René Carmille
chunks.text: He also used his department to help mobilize French resistance in Algeria.

chunks.title: A Man Escaped

chunks.title: A Man Escaped

chunks.title: A Man Escaped
chunks.text: Bresson himself was imprisoned by the Germans as a member of the French Resistance.

chunks.title: Nikolai Vasenin

chunks.title: Nikolai Vasenin

chunks.title: Nikolai Vasenin
chunks.text: The French gave him an opportunity to fight among them and so he took the offer.

chunks.title: Nikolai Vasenin

chunks.title: Launceston, Tasmania

chunks.title: New World (2013 film)
chunks.text: New World () is a 2013 South Korean crime drama film written and directed by Park Hoon-jung.

chunks.title: New World (2013 film)
chunks.text: Starring Choi Min-sik, Hwang Jung-min and Lee Jung-jae, the film shows the conflict between the police and the mob through the eyes of an undercover cop.

chunks.title: New World (2013 film)
chunks.text: "New World" is the first entry in a planned trilogy.

chunks.title: The Battleship Island
chunks.text: The Battleship Island () is a 2017 South Korean period action fiction film starring Hwang Jung-min, So Ji-sub, Song Joong-ki and Lee Jung-hyun.

chunks.title: The Battleship Island
chunks.text: It is a Japanese occupation-era film about an attempted prison break from a forced labor camp on Hashima Island.

chunks.title: Happiness (2007 film)
chunks.text: Happiness () is a 2007 South Korean film, directed by Hur Jin-ho and starring Hwang Jung-min and Im Soo-jung.

chunks.title: Happiness (2007 film)
chunks.text: It is a love story about two people who meet while battling serious illnesses.

chunks.title: Dancing Queen (2012 film)
chunks.text: Dancing Queen (Hangul: 댄싱퀸 ; RR: "Daensing Kwin " ) is 2012 South Korean romantic comedy film starring Uhm Jung-hwa and Hwang Jung-min.

chunks.title: Dancing Queen (2012 film)
chunks.text: The film tells a story of a married couple, who in the midst of their mundane lives decides to pursue their lost dreams.

chunks.title: Dancing Queen (2012 film)
chunks.text: The husband finds himself accidentally running for Mayor of Seoul and his wife decides to become a pop singer.

chunks.title: Dancing Queen (2012 film)
chunks.text: It was produced by JK Film and distributed by CJ Entertainment, and released on January 18, 2012.

chunks.title: The Himalayas (film)
chunks.text: The Himalayas () is a 2015 South Korean drama film directed by Lee Seok-hoon.

chunks.title: The Himalayas (film)
chunks.text: The film was released on December 16, 2015.

chunks.title: Hwang Jung-min
chunks.text: Hwang Jung-min (born September 1, 1970) is a South Korean actor.

chunks.title: Hwang Jung-min
chunks.text: He is one of the highest-grossing actors in South Korea, and has starred in several box office hits such as "Ode to My Father" (2014), "Veteran" (2015), "The Himalayas" (2015), "A Violent Prosecutor" (2015) and "The Wailing" (2016).

chunks.title: Hwang Jung-min
chunks.text: Hwang is the third actor in South Korea to be part of the "100 Million Viewer Club" in Chungmuro.

chunks.title: A Violent Prosecutor
chunks.text: A Violent Prosecutor is a 2016 South Korean crime film directed by Lee Il-hyung, produced by Guk Su Ran and starring Hwang Jung-min, Kang Dong-won, Lee Sung-min and Park Sung-woong.

chunks.title: A Violent Prosecutor
chunks.text: It was released in South Korea on February 3, 2016 by Showbox.

chunks.title: Korean Peninsula (TV series)
chunks.text: Korean Peninsula () is a 2012 South Korean television series starring Hwang Jung-min and Kim Jung-eun.

chunks.title: Korean Peninsula (TV series)
chunks.text: It aired on newly launched cable channel TV Chosun from February 6 to April 3, 2012 on Mondays and Tuesdays at 20:50 for 18 episodes.

chunks.title: The Accidental Couple
chunks.text: The Accidental Couple (; lit.

chunks.title: The Accidental Couple
chunks.text: "Just Looking"; shortened to That Fool () is a 2009 South Korean television series starring Hwang Jung-min and Kim Ah-joong.

chunks.title: The Accidental Couple
chunks.text: The show is a romantic comedy focusing on the relationship between a post office clerk and an actress after they agree to a six-month contract marriage.

chunks.title: The Accidental Couple
chunks.text: It aired on KBS2 from April 29 to June 18, 2009 on Wednesdays and Thursdays at 21:55 for 16 episodes.

chunks.title: Ode to My Father
chunks.text: Ode to My Father (; lit.

chunks.title: Ode to My Father
chunks.text: "Gukje (International) Market") is a 2014 South Korean drama film directed by Yoon Je-kyoon.

chunks.title: Ode to My Father
chunks.text: Starring Hwang Jung-min and Yunjin Kim, it depicts modern Korean history from the 1950s to the present day through the life of an ordinary man, as he experiences events such as the Hungnam Evacuation of 1950 during the Korean War, the government's decision to dispatch nurses and miners to West Germany in the 1960s, and the Vietnam War.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: Alice Upside Down is a 2007 comedy-drama film, based in the "Alice" series written by Phyllis Reynolds Naylor.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: The film was shot at Bishop DuBourg High School in St. Louis, Missouri, United States.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: Screened in limited cinema in 2007, it was released wide straight-to-DVD on July 29, 2008.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: In North America, it airs on Starz Kids & Family, but in the early years, it was on demand.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: The film's plot centers on Alice, an 11-year-old girl starting the sixth grade at a new school.

chunks.title: Alice Upside Down
chunks.text: It was starring Alyson Stoner, Lucas Grabeel, Bridgit Mendler, Luke Perry, Penny Marshall and Ashley Eckstein.

chunks.title: Switched at Birth (season 2)

chunks.title: Lea Thompson
chunks.text: Lea Katherine Thompson (born May 31, 1961) is an American actress, television director, and television producer.

chunks.title: Lea Thompson
chunks.text: She is known for her role as Lorraine Baines in the "Back to the Future" trilogy and as the title character in the 1990s NBC sitcom "Caroline in the City".

chunks.title: Lea Thompson
chunks.text: Other films for which she is known include "All the Right Moves" (1983), "Red Dawn" (1984), "Howard the Duck" (1986) "Some Kind of Wonderful" (1987), and "The Beverly Hillbillies" (1993).

chunks.title: Lea Thompson

chunks.title: Lucas Grabeel
chunks.text: Lucas Stephen Grabeel ( ; born November 23, 1984) is an American actor, director, producer, singer and songwriter.

chunks.title: Lucas Grabeel
chunks.text: He is best known for roles such as Ryan Evans in the "High School Musical" film series, as Ezra Chase in The Adventures of Food Boy (2008) and as Ethan Dalloway in the third and fourth installments of the Halloweentown series: "Halloweentown High" (2004) and "Return to Halloweentown" (2006).

chunks.title: Lucas Grabeel
chunks.text: He also appeared as a young Lex Luthor and Conner Kent in the television series "Smallville".

chunks.title: Lucas Grabeel
chunks.text: He played Toby Kennish in the ABC Family/Freeform drama "Switched at Birth".

chunks.title: Lucas Grabeel
chunks.text: He provides the voice of Deputy Peck in the Disney Junior TV series "Sheriff Callie's Wild West".

chunks.title: Switched at Birth (TV series)
chunks.text: Switched at Birth is an American teen/family drama television series that premiered on ABC Family on June 6, 2011, at 9:00 ET/PT.

chunks.title: Switched at Birth (TV series)
chunks.text: The one-hour scripted drama is set in the Kansas City metropolitan area, and revolves around two teenagers who were switched at birth and grew up in very different environments: one in an affluent suburb, and the other in working-class areas.

chunks.title: Switched at Birth (TV series)
chunks.text: According to ABC Family, it is "the first mainstream television series to have multiple deaf and hard-of-hearing series regulars and scenes shot entirely in American Sign Language (ASL)".

chunks.title: List of Switched at Birth episodes
chunks.text: "Switched at Birth" is an American television drama series which premiered on ABC Family on June 6, 2011.

chunks.text: Created by Lizzy Weiss, the series follows two teenage girls who learn that they were switched at birth.
