chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: "General Hospital" is the longest running American television serial drama, airing on ABC.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Created by Frank and Doris Hursley, the series premiered on April 1, 1963.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: The longest-running cast member is Leslie Charleson, who has portrayed Dr. Monica Quartermaine since August 17, 1977, also making her one of the longest-tenured actors in American soap operas.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Former cast member Rachel Ames was previously the series' longest-running cast member, portraying Audrey Hardy from 1964 to 2007, and making guest appearances in 2009 and 2013, the latter for the series' fiftieth anniversary.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Ames made a special appearance on October 30, 2015.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Actors Genie Francis and Kin Shriner, who portray Laura Spencer and Scott Baldwin, are the second and third longest-running cast members, having joined "General Hospital" in February and August 1977, respectively.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Actress Jacklyn Zeman — who portrays Bobbie Spencer — is the fourth longest-running cast member, joining the serial in December 1977.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Actress Jane Elliot, who joined the serial in June 1978 as Tracy Quartermaine, is the fifth longest-running cast member, joining "General Hospital" in June 1978 until her departure in May 2017.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: Former cast member Anthony Geary, who portrayed Luke Spencer, was the sixth longest-running cast member, having joined "General Hospital" in November 1978.

chunks.title: General Hospital cast members
chunks.text: The following list is of cast members who are currently on the show: the main and recurring cast members, or those who are debuting, departing or returning to the series.

chunks.title: Constance Marie
chunks.text: Constance Marie Lopez (born September 9, 1965) known professionally as Constance Marie, is an American actress.

chunks.title: Constance Marie
chunks.text: She is known for her role as Angie Lopez on "George Lopez" (2002–2007) and her role as Marcela Quintanilla (mother of Selena) in the 1997 film "Selena".

chunks.title: Constance Marie
chunks.text: She portrayed Regina Vasquez on the ABC Family/Freeform drama "Switched at Birth" (2011–2017).

chunks.title: Harald II of Denmark
chunks.text: Harald II of Denmark (died 1018) was King of Denmark from 1014 until his death in 1018.

chunks.title: Harald II of Denmark
chunks.text: He was the youngest son of Sweyn Forkbeard and Gunhild of Wenden, and was regent while his father was fighting Ethelred the Unready in England.

chunks.title: Harald II of Denmark
chunks.text: He inherited the Danish throne in 1014, and held it while his brother, the later king Cnut the Great conquered England.

chunks.title: Harald II of Denmark
chunks.text: After his death in 1018, he was succeeded by Cnut the Great.

chunks.title: Harald II of Denmark
chunks.text: Little detail is known about Harald II.

chunks.title: Christopher I of Denmark
chunks.text: Christopher I (Danish: "Christoffer I" ) (1219 – 29 May 1259) was King of Denmark between 1252 and 1259.

chunks.title: Christopher I of Denmark
chunks.text: He was the son of Valdemar II of Denmark by his wife, Infanta Berengária of Portugal.

chunks.title: Christopher I of Denmark
chunks.text: He succeeded his brothers Eric IV Plovpenning and Abel of Denmark on the throne.

chunks.title: Christopher I of Denmark
chunks.text: Christopher was elected King upon the death of his older brother Abel in the summer of 1252.

chunks.title: Christopher I of Denmark
chunks.text: He was crowned at Lund Cathedral on Christmas Day 1252.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: Ptolemy (Greek: ); 237 BC-died 234 ВС), king of Epirus, was the second son of Alexander II, king of Epirus, and Olympias, grandson of the great Pyrrhus and brother of Phthia of Macedon.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: He was named in honor of his late uncle Ptolemy, a late brother of his parents.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: He succeeded to the throne on the death of his elder brother, Pyrrhus II of Epirus, but reigned only a very short time, having set out on a military expedition, during the course of which he fell sick and died.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: Polyaenus, instead, tells us a different story and states that he was treasonably assassinated.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: The date of his reign cannot be fixed with certainty, but as he was contemporary with Demetrius II, king of Macedonia, it may be placed between 239 and 229 BC.

chunks.title: Ptolemy of Epirus
chunks.text: He was succeeded by his niece Deidamia.

chunks.title: King Kang of Chu
chunks.text: King Kang of Chu (, died 545 BC) was from 559 to 545 BC the king of Chu, a major power during the Spring and Autumn period of ancient China.

chunks.title: King Kang of Chu
chunks.text: Born Xiong Zhao (), he succeeded his father King Gong of Chu.

chunks.title: King Kang of Chu
chunks.text: His reign was marked by constant wars with Jin, Chu's traditional enemy, and Wu, its new enemy.

chunks.title: King Kang of Chu
chunks.text: He ruled for 15 years and was succeeded by his son, Jia'ao, who would four years later be murdered by King Kang's younger brother King Ling of Chu.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: Baron Plunket, of Newtown in the County of Cork, is a title in the Peerage of the United Kingdom.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: It was created in 1827 for the prominent Irish lawyer and Whig politician William Plunket.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He served as Lord Chancellor of Ireland from 1830 and 1834 and again from 1835 to 1841.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: His eldest son, the second Baron, was Bishop of Tuam, Killala and Achonry between 1839 and 1866.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He was succeeded by his younger brother, the third Baron.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He was a barrister.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: His eldest son, the fourth Baron, served as Archbishop of Dublin between 1884 and 1897.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He was succeeded by his eldest son, the fifth Baron.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He was a diplomat and held office as Governor of New Zealand between 1904 and 1910.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: His grandson, Patrick, the seventh Baron, was Equerry to both King George VI and Queen Elizabeth II.

chunks.title: Baron Plunket
chunks.text: He was succeeded by his younger brother, Robin who died in 2013 and was in turn succeeded by his nephew, Tyrone who was a Page of Honour to Queen Elizabeth II.

chunks.title: Eric IV of Denmark
chunks.text: Eric IV, also known as Eric Ploughpenny or Eric Plowpenny (Danish: "Erik Plovpenning" ), (  1216 – 10 August 1250) was king of Denmark from 1241 until his death in 1250.

chunks.title: Eric IV of Denmark
chunks.text: He was the son of King Valdemar II by his wife, Berengaria of Portugal, and brother of King Abel and King Christopher I.

chunks.title: Eric II of Denmark
chunks.text: Eric II the Memorable (Danish: "Erik II Emune" ) (  1090 – 18 September 1137) was king of Denmark between 1134 and 1137.

chunks.title: Eric II of Denmark
chunks.text: Eric was an illegitimate son of Eric I of Denmark, who ruled Denmark from 1095 to 1103.

chunks.title: Eric II of Denmark
chunks.text: Eric the Memorable rebelled against his uncle Niels of Denmark, and was declared king in 1134.

chunks.title: Eric II of Denmark
chunks.text: He punished his adversaries severely, and rewarded his supporters handsomely.

chunks.title: Eric II of Denmark
chunks.text: He was killed by a subject in 1137 and was promptly succeeded by his nephew Eric III of Denmark.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: Earl of Norbury, in the County of Tipperary, is a title in the Peerage of Ireland.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: It was created in 1827, along with the title Viscount Glandine, of Glandine in the King's County, for the Irish politician and judge John Toler, 1st Baron Norbury, upon his retirement as Chief Justice of the Common Pleas in Ireland.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: The titles were created with special remainder to his second son, Hector, as his eldest son, Daniel, was then considered mentally unwell.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: Lord Norbury had already been created Baron Norbury, of Ballycrenode in the County of Tipperary, in the Peerage of Ireland in 1800, with remainder to the heirs male of his body.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: Moreover, his wife, Grace Toler (née Graham), had been created Baroness Norwood, of Knockalton in the County of Tipperary, in the Peerage of Ireland in 1797, with remainder to the heirs male of her body.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: By the time Lord Norbury was raised to the Earldom, his wife had died and their eldest son had succeeded her as 2nd Baron Norwood.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: This son also succeeded Lord Norbury himself on his death in 1831 as 2nd Baron Norbury, whilst his younger brother Daniel succeeded to the viscountcy and earldom according to the special remainder.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: In 1832, the second Earl also succeeded his elder brother in the two baronies.

chunks.title: Earl of Norbury
chunks.text: He had already in 1825 assumed the additional surname of Graham by Royal licence.

chunks.title: Eric III of Denmark
chunks.text: Eric III Lamb (Danish: "Erik III Lam" ) (  1120 – 27 August 1146) was the King of Denmark from 1137 until 1146.

chunks.title: Eric III of Denmark
chunks.text: He was the grandson of Eric I of Denmark and the nephew of Eric II of Denmark, whom he succeeded on the throne.

chunks.title: Eric III of Denmark
chunks.text: He abdicated in 1146, as the first and only Danish monarch to do so.

chunks.title: Eric III of Denmark
chunks.text: His succession led to a period of civil war between Sweyn III, Canute V, and Valdemar I.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof (variation : Mbin Boureh Gnilane in Serer) was a royal house founded in the 14th century by Jaraff Boureh Gnilane Joof (var : "Bouré Gnilane Diouf" or "Buré Ñilaan").

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: He was a member the Serer tribe, from the pre-colonial Kingdom of Sine now part of independent Senegal.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: It was the first royal house founded by the Joof family during the Guelowar period (1350 - 1969).

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: Boureh Gnilane Joof was a royal prince and a Jaraff (var : "Diaraf"), a with the powers of a Prime Minister.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: He was neither a Maad a Sinig (king of Sine) nor a Maad Saloum (king of Saloum) but a royal prince who had the title "Jaraff" bestowed upon him by his cousin and brother-in-law - Maad a Sinig Diessanou Faye (king of Sine).

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: His father Maad Patar Kholleh Joof (the conqueror) was the king of Laa and Teigne of Baol (king of Baol).

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: Boureh's brothers were the first from this house to have succeeded to the throne of Sine during the Guelowar period.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: His name was adopted in his honour to refer to the first royal house founded by the Joof family during this dynastic period.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: The Joof family of Sine, from this royal house also ruled in the Kingdom of Saloum (the Joof paternal dynasty of Sine and Saloum) The Joof family also ruled in Baol (the Joof paternal dynasty of Baol).

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: From the date of its foundation up to the abolition of the Serer monarchies of Sine and Saloum in 1969, at least ten kings from this house had succeeded to the throne of Sine.

chunks.title: The Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof
chunks.text: As the first royal house of Sine founded by the Joof family in this dynastic period, the Royal House of Boureh Gnilane Joof holds great significance in Senegambian, Joof family and , because all the subsequent royal houses founded by the Joof family (who ruled in three Senegambian kingdoms) branched out from this royal house.

chunks.title: Tenacious D Live
chunks.text: Tenacious D Live is the first live album by American rock band Tenacious D.

chunks.title: Tenacious D Live
chunks.text: Produced by John Spiker, it was released as a worldwide vinyl on November 27, 2015 by Columbia Records and was released on digital platforms on January 15, 2016.

chunks.title: Tenacious D Live
chunks.text: The release features recordings from the band's 2012 Rize of the Fenix tour and their 2013 European tour.

chunks.title: Tenacious D Live
chunks.text: The album features five songs from the bands debut album, five songs from their "Rize of the Fenix" album and one song from their "The Pick of Destiny" album.

chunks.title: Neman (album)
chunks.text: Neman is an album by the Serbian noise-rock band Klopka Za Pionira, released in 2006 (see 2006 in music) on the Ne-ton independent label.

chunks.title: Neman (album)
chunks.text: The album's five songs contain no lyrics and are mostly experiments with various noise-making machines that the band was building.

chunks.title: Neman (album)
chunks.text: The outcome of these experiments can be heard on the following albums, so this was a kind of a showcase of their future work.

chunks.title: Neman (album)
chunks.text: The songs do not have names, merely numbers that position them on the disk.

chunks.title: Neman (album)
chunks.text: All of the songs were recorded at once and are first takes and complete improvisations on the spot.

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: Two Steps from the Blues is the debut album by Bobby Bland, in 1961.

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: It compiles five songs recorded between 1956 and 1960 and seven songs recorded in two sessions from August 3 to November 12, 1960.

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: The sessions took place in the Universal Studio in Chicago, where Bland and his backing band moved after a series of successful singles and albums.

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: The backing band was composed of Joe Scott and Melvin Jackson (trumpet), Pluma Davis (trombone), Robert Skinner and L. A. Hill (tenor saxophone), Rayfield Devers (baritone saxophone), Teddy Reynolds (piano), Clarence Holloman (guitar on some tracks, notably "I Don't Want No Woman," where Bobby Bland shouts, "Look out, Clarence!"

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: in the middle of the guitar solo), Wayne Bennett (guitar on other tracks), Hamp Simmons (bass), and John "Jabo" Starks (drums).

chunks.title: Two Steps from the Blues
chunks.text: Scott also served as an arranger.

chunks.title: Bluelove
chunks.text: Bluelove is the second Korean mini album of South Korean rock band CNBLUE.

chunks.title: Bluelove
chunks.text: It was released on May 19, 2010 by FNC Entertainment and distributed by Mnet Media.

chunks.title: Bluelove
chunks.text: Before the album was release "Love Light" (Korean: 사랑 빛 ) was released as the first digital single on May 10, 2010.

chunks.title: Bluelove
chunks.text: After it was released "Love" was promoted as the lead single.

chunks.title: Bluelove
chunks.text: The album contain five new tracks plus previously released English track, "Let's Go Crazy" from their debut Japanese EP, "Now or Never".

chunks.title: Fünf Gesänge, Op. 104 (Brahms)
chunks.text: Fünf Gesänge (Five songs), Op.

chunks.title: Fünf Gesänge, Op. 104 (Brahms)
chunks.text: 104, is a song cycle of five part songs for mixed choir a cappella by Johannes Brahms.

chunks.title: Fünf Gesänge, Op. 104 (Brahms)
chunks.text: Composed in 1888 when Brahms was a 55-year-old bachelor, the five songs reflect an intensely nostalgic and even tragic mood.

chunks.title: Fünf Gesänge, Op. 104 (Brahms)
chunks.text: Brahms has chosen texts which centre on lost youth, summer turning into fall and, ultimately, man's mortality.

chunks.title: Fünf Gesänge, Op. 104 (Brahms)
chunks.text: While the score and the parts themselves are not that difficult for the singers, the sombre nature of the texts coupled with intense soaring melodies and complex harmonies make it quite a demanding work for any choir.

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)
chunks.text: Stop the Bleeding is the seventh studio album by the alternative rock band Sponge.

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)
chunks.text: It was released in 2013 on Three One Three Records.

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)
chunks.text: This album features the five songs previously released on Sponge's 2010 EP "Destroy the Boy".

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)
chunks.text: These five songs are "Dare to Breathe", "Destroy the Boy", "Come In from the Rain", "Star", and "Before the End", however these songs appear in a different order than they did on "Destroy the Boy".

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)
chunks.text: Also on this album Sponge does their own rendition on a classic Jim Croce song "Time in a Bottle".

chunks.title: Stop the Bleeding (Sponge album)

chunks.title: Captain Beefheart
chunks.text: Don Van Vliet ( , born Don Glen Vliet; January 15, 1941 – December 17, 2010) was an American singer, songwriter, musician and artist best known by the stage name Captain Beefheart.

chunks.title: Captain Beefheart
chunks.text: His musical work was conducted with a rotating ensemble of musicians called the Magic Band (1964–1982), with whom he recorded 13 studio albums.

chunks.title: Captain Beefheart
chunks.text: Noted for his powerful singing voice and his wide vocal range, Van Vliet also played the harmonica, saxophone, and numerous other wind instruments.

chunks.title: Captain Beefheart
chunks.text: His music integrated blues, rock, psychedelia, and free jazz with contemporary experimental composition and the avant-garde.

chunks.title: Captain Beefheart
chunks.text: Beefheart was also known for often constructing myths about his life and for exercising an almost dictatorial control over his supporting musicians.

chunks.title: BBC Sessions and Other Polished Turds
chunks.text: BBC Sessions and Other Polished Turds is a compilation album by The Vandals, released August 12, 2008 by Kung Fu Records.

chunks.title: BBC Sessions and Other Polished Turds
chunks.text: It was released as a digital download through iTunes and the band's website, as well as on CD in Japan.

chunks.title: BBC Sessions and Other Polished Turds
chunks.text: The album collects rare songs by the band from compilations and out-of-print singles, as well as five songs recorded during various sessions at the BBC.

chunks.title: BBC Sessions and Other Polished Turds
chunks.text: It was promoted as "A collection of the band's most rare tracks all sharing one thing in common in that they were recorded when the band didn't give a crap, so they are fun, funny, and unpretentious".

chunks.title: The Legendary A&M Sessions
chunks.text: The Legendary A&M Sessions is an extended play featuring five songs by Captain Beefheart & His Magic Band, recorded early in their career for their original record label A&M Records.

chunks.title: The Legendary A&M Sessions
chunks.text: The EP was released by the company in 1984 after Captain Beefheart had gone into retirement.

chunks.title: Symphony No. 3 (Tchaikovsky)
chunks.text: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's Symphony No. 3 in D major, Op. 29, was written in 1875.

chunks.title: Symphony No. 3 (Tchaikovsky)
chunks.text: He began it at Vladimir Shilovsky's estate at Ussovo on 5 June and finished on 1 August at Verbovka.

chunks.title: Symphony No. 3 (Tchaikovsky)
chunks.text: Dedicated to Shilovsky, the work is unique in Tchaikovsky's symphonic output in two ways: it is the only one of his seven symphonies (including the unnumbered "Manfred Symphony") in a major key (discounting the unfinished Symphony in E♭ major); and it is the only one to contain five movements (an additional "Alla tedesca" movement occurs between the opening movement and the slow movement).

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: The Mazda RX-9 is a sports car produced by the Japanese automaker Mazda scheduled for release in 2020.

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: "Holiday Auto", a Japanese magazine, reported it will be previewed at the 2017 Tokyo Auto Show, and the final production model will be featured at the same event in 2019.

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: The car will be released in January 2020, to coincide with Mazda's 100th anniversary, and will be initially priced at eight million yen (US$(8000000/ 105.944781 )round0 in 2015).

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: It is believed it will showcase the return of the Wankel rotary engine, but CEO Masamichi Kogai said Mazda will not launch another rotary engine.

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: In the middle of the September 2017, Mazda has filed a patent application for an engine that uses two conventional turbochargers and an electric supercharger.

chunks.title: Mazda RX-9
chunks.text: The engine looks compact, can replace the rotary engine and possibly be included in RX-9 production.

chunks.title: Mazda 929
chunks.text: The Mazda 929 is a full-size car which was sold by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Mazda between 1973 and 1997.

chunks.title: Mazda 929
chunks.text: Mazda utilized the 929 nameplate for export markets only, badge engineering its Luce model until 1991 and then transferring the name to export specification Sentia models.

chunks.title: Mazda 929
chunks.text: Between 1982 and 1986, Mazda also used the 929 nameplate for its Cosmo coupe in certain export markets.

chunks.title: Mazda Takeri
chunks.text: The Mazda Takeri was a concept car made by Mazda.

chunks.title: Mazda Takeri
chunks.text: It was a preview to the next generation Mazda6.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: The Mazda GTP is an IMSA GTP car that was built by Pierre Honegger in 1981.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: Based on a Mazda RX-7, the car initially competed in the GTX category as the Mazda RX-7 GTP, before it was rebuilt for the IMSA GTP category in 1983.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: Throughout its career, the car used a Mazda 13B Wankel rotary engine, similar to that used in the production RX-7s.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: Although the rotary-engined sports prototypes generally had a reputation of being very reliable, the Mazda GTP frequently failed to finish races, and was never able to better the eighth place achieved at the 1983 24 Hours of Daytona.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: In 1986, one car was purchased by Erie Scientific Racing, and rebuilt to become the Badger BB.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: This car was no more successful or reliable than its predecessor, and was last used in 1989, by which point it was owned by Jack Engelhardt.

chunks.title: Mazda GTP
chunks.text: The other car, meanwhile, was rebuilt by Honegger into the Denali Speedcar, which was used with moderate success in 1986 and 1987.

chunks.title: Mazda Taiki
chunks.text: The Mazda Taiki is a one-off concept car produced by Mazda, and is the fourth car in Mazda's 'Nagare' design series.

chunks.title: Mazda Taiki
chunks.text: Mazda says the Taiki "reflects one possible direction for a future generation of Mazda sports cars aimed at helping to create a sustainable society".

chunks.title: Nissan Altima
chunks.text: The Nissan Altima (Japanese: 日産・アルティマ ) is a mid-size car which has been manufactured by Nissan since 1992.

chunks.title: Nissan Altima
chunks.text: It is a continuation of the Nissan Bluebird line, which began in 1957.

chunks.title: Nissan Altima
chunks.text: The Nissan Altima mainly competes against cars such as Chevrolet's Malibu, Ford's Fusion, Honda's Accord, Hyundai's Sonata, Mazda's Mazda6, Subaru's Legacy, Kia's Optima, Toyota's Camry and Volkswagen's Passat.

chunks.title: Mazda Hakaze Concept
chunks.text: The Mazda Hakaze Concept is a concept car that was revealed in early February 2007 by Japanese manufacturer Mazda.

chunks.title: Mazda Hakaze Concept
chunks.text: Its major design elements come from a new design language developed by Mazda called Nagare, developed by Laurens van den Acker, Mazda Global Design Director.

chunks.title: Mazda Hakaze Concept
chunks.text: It translates to "flow".

chunks.title: Mazda Hakaze Concept
chunks.text: This element has been used on past Mazda concept cars such as: Mazda Nagare; Mazda Ryuga; Mazda Kabura.

chunks.title: Mazda Kazamai
chunks.text: The Mazda Kazamai is a concept car made by the Japanese car manufacturer Mazda.

chunks.title: Mazda Kazamai
chunks.text: It was first introduced at the 2008 Moscow International Motor Show in August.

chunks.title: Mazda6
chunks.text: The Mazda 6 or Mazda6 (known as the Mazda Atenza in China and Japan, derived from the Italian "attenzione") is a Midsize family produced by the Japanese car manufacturer Mazda since 2002.

chunks.title: Mazda6
chunks.text: It replaced the long-produced Mazda Capella (616, 626) in 2002.

chunks.title: Mazda6
chunks.text: The Mazda6 sold more than one million units faster than all previous Mazdas.

chunks.title: Bahman Group
chunks.text: Bahman Group (Persian: ‎ ‎ ) is an Iran-based manufacturer of vehicles under license by Mazda.

chunks.title: Bahman Group
chunks.text: Bahman Group was founded in 1952 under the title of Iran Khalij Co by Mr. Amanollah Sarbaz and his son.

chunks.title: Bahman Group
chunks.text: They have since then manufactured, under license, versions of Mazda's trucks, including versions of the Mazda B-Series pickups and the previous generation Mazda 323 and Mazda 3.

chunks.title: Bahman Group
chunks.text: They also manufacture Isuzu buses and FAW trucks.

chunks.title: Bahman Group
chunks.text: Currently, the group is headed by Mohammad Reza Soroush.

chunks.title: Geographic information system
chunks.text: A geographic information system (GIS) is a system designed to capture, store, manipulate, analyze, manage, and present spatial or geographic data.

chunks.title: Geographic information system
chunks.text: The acronym GIS is sometimes used for geographic information science (GIScience) to refer to the academic discipline that studies geographic information systems and is a large domain within the broader academic discipline of geoinformatics.

chunks.title: Geographic information system
chunks.text: What goes beyond a GIS is a spatial data infrastructure, a concept that has no such restrictive boundaries.

chunks.title: Rashid Khan (Afghan cricketer)
chunks.text: Rashid Khan Arman (Pashto: ‎ ; born 20 September 1998), commonly known as Rashid Khan, is an Afghan cricketer who represents the national team.

chunks.title: Rashid Khan (Afghan cricketer)
chunks.text: Rashid played in the 2017 Indian Premier League for Sunrisers Hyderabad.

chunks.title: Rashid Khan (Afghan cricketer)
chunks.text: In June 2017, he took the best bowling figures for an associate nation in a One Day International (ODI) match.

chunks.title: Ghulam Rasool Gangi
chunks.text: Ghulam Rasool Gangi was a direct descendant of Genghis Khan and the son of Pir Bukhsh.

chunks.title: Ghulam Rasool Gangi
chunks.text: His family moved from Yarkand and Kashgar to India in 1598, where he lived in the Siakolt district of Langrewali.

chunks.title: Ghulam Rasool Gangi
chunks.text: For three generations Abdul Rashid Khan's descendants were rulers of Khotan and Yarkand, but were scattered geographically until 1707.

chunks.title: Ghulam Rasool Gangi
chunks.text: Quresh Sultan, one of Abdul Rashid Khan's sons, and other Chugtai royal family members were relocated to India during the time of Emperor Akbar.

chunks.title: Master of Research
chunks.text: In some anglophone countries, the degree Master of Research is an advanced postgraduate research degree in a specific academic discipline.

chunks.title: Master of Research
chunks.text: At some universities, the conferred degree is called the Master of Arts by Research or Master of Science by Research in a specific academic discipline of Science or Social Sciences.

chunks.title: Master of Research
chunks.text: The Master of Research degree is usually abbreviated as MRes whereas the Master of Arts by Research is often abbreviated as MARes or MA(Res), while the Master of Science by Research is sometimes abbreviated as MSc(Res) or MScRes.

chunks.title: Major (academic)
chunks.text: An academic major is the academic discipline to which an undergraduate student formally commits.

chunks.title: Major (academic)
chunks.text: A student who successfully completes all courses required for the major qualifies for an undergraduate degree.

chunks.title: Major (academic)
chunks.text: The word "major" is also sometimes used administratively to refer to the academic discipline pursued by a graduate student or postgraduate student in a master's or doctoral program.

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: The debate over whether the ancient Chinese masters can be counted as philosophy has been discussed since the introduction of this academic discipline into China about a hundred years ago.

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: Cultural immersion in the West by figures such as Hu Shi and Feng Youlan led to an increased interest in a Chinese philosophy and stimulated the creation of this field which had not yet been labeled nor discussed as such until this point.

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: Feng Youlan made sure to make the distinction between "Zhongguo de zhexue" [any philosophical activity pursued in China] and "Zhongguo di zhexue" [indigenous philosophy from Chinese soil].

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: The debates over the legitimacy of Chinese philosophy primarily concern the indigenous philosophy of China.

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: They range in their central focus: whether the discipline of “philosophy” existed in traditional Chinese thought; whether the subjects and issues involved in the discipline existed in Chinese thought; and whether the now established discipline of Chinese philosophy can be truly be considered Chinese.

chunks.title: Legitimacy of Chinese philosophy
chunks.text: These contentions have led to larger questions about the nature of philosophy and its discipline.

chunks.title: Postcolonialism
chunks.text: Postcolonialism or postcolonial studies is an academic discipline that analyzes, explains, and responds to the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.

chunks.title: Postcolonialism
chunks.text: Postcolonialism speaks about the human consequences of external control and economic exploitation of native people and their lands.

chunks.title: Postcolonialism
chunks.text: Drawing from postmodern schools of thought, postcolonial studies analyze the politics of knowledge (creation, control, and distribution) by examining the functional relations of social and political power that sustain colonialism and neocolonialism—the imperial regime's depictions (social, political, cultural) of the colonizer and of the colonized.

chunks.title: Hafiz Rashid Khan
chunks.text: Hafiz Rashid Khan (Bengali: হাফিজ রশিদ খান , born June 23, 1961<ref name="ISNI/"> </ref>) is a Bangladeshi postcolonialist poet, author, editor and journalist.

chunks.title: Hafiz Rashid Khan
chunks.text: He wrote more than twenty titles including poetry and criticism.

chunks.title: Hafiz Rashid Khan
chunks.text: He is known for his postcolonialism, anti-military voice and was reputed for working in tribal area at Chittagong Hill Tracts in Bangladesh.

chunks.title: Hafiz Rashid Khan
chunks.text: In his twenty one years old his first book of poems was published in 1982.

chunks.title: Rashid Khan Gaplanov
chunks.text: Rashid Khan Zavid oglu Gaplanov (Azerbaijani: "Rəşid xan Qaplanov Zavid oğlu" , Russian: Рашид хан Завитович Капланов ; 1883–1937), also known as Rashid Khan Kaplanov, was an Azerbaijani statesman of Kumyk ethnicity who served as the Minister of Finance and Minister of Education and Religious Affairs in the fifth and fourth cabinets of Azerbaijan Democratic Republic.

chunks.title: Practical theology
chunks.text: Practical theology is an academic discipline that examines and reflects on religious practices in order to understand the theology that is enacted in those practices and in order to consider how theological theory and theological practices can be more fully aligned, changed, or improved.

chunks.title: Practical theology
chunks.text: Practical theology has often sought to address a perceived disconnection between theology as an academic discipline or dogmatics on the one hand, and the life and practice of the Church on the other.

chunks.title: Price Chopper Supermarkets
chunks.text: Golub Corporation (the parent company of both Market 32 and Price Chopper Supermarkets), operates a chain of supermarkets and is headquartered in Schenectady, New York.

chunks.title: Price Chopper Supermarkets
chunks.text: The chain opened its first supermarkets in New York's Capital District in 1932, and changed its name from Central Market to Price Chopper in 1973.

chunks.title: Price Chopper Supermarkets
chunks.text: On June 2, 2010 Price Chopper dedicated its new headquarters, on Nott Street, in Downtown Schenectady.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: Purity Supreme, Inc. was a corporation involved in the operation of supermarkets and other stores.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: From 1984 it was a division of Supermarkets General Holdings Corporation.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: It operated from a headquarters located in North Billerica, Massachusetts.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: At its height, the company operated 64 supermarkets in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Maine, and Connecticut.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: They also operated 63 owned and franchised Li'l Peach convenience stores and 23 drugstores in Massachusetts.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: They also ran the successful Heartland Foods warehouse style supermarket chain.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: In 1984 at the time of the buyout by Supermarkets General, Purity, had an annual sales of $800 million with 28 supermarkets, 13 warehouse stores and 23 drugstores.

chunks.title: Purity Supreme
chunks.text: Purity Supreme and Li'l Peach had combined sales of about US$1.3 billion in 1990 before the company was bought out again by Freeman Spogli & Co., an investment firm for about US$300 million, including the acquisition of debt.

chunks.title: Inserra Supermarkets
chunks.text: Inserra Supermarkets Inc. is a supermarket chain operating in the northeastern United States.

chunks.title: Inserra Supermarkets
chunks.text: The company is a member of the Wakefern retailers' cooperative and does business as ShopRite and PriceRite.

chunks.title: Inserra Supermarkets
chunks.text: Inserra Supermarkets is headquartered in Mahwah, New Jersey, and operates approximately 22 stores.

chunks.title: Inserra Supermarkets
chunks.text: It is a family-owned business and is one of the 500 largest private companies in the United States, according to the 2008 Forbes.com list of America's Largest Private Companies.

chunks.title: Inserra Supermarkets
chunks.text: The Chairman and CEO of Inserra Supermarkets is Lawrence R. Inserra Jr.

chunks.title: Joseph E. Grosberg
chunks.text: Joseph E. Grosberg (December 27, 1883 – July 25, 1970) was a pioneer in the American supermarket and wholesale foods industries.

chunks.title: Joseph E. Grosberg
chunks.text: He was a founder and the president of Central Markets, a chain of grocery stores in upstate New York that established some of the first supermarkets in the United States, and is now known as Price Chopper.

chunks.title: Joseph E. Grosberg
chunks.text: He was also a noted philanthropist, especially known for his support of Jewish causes as well as charitable activities in Schenectady and the Capital District of New York.

chunks.title: Nott Memorial
chunks.text: The Nott Memorial is an elaborate 16-sided stone-masonry building which serves as both architectural and physical centerpiece of Union College in Schenectady, New York.

chunks.title: Nott Memorial
chunks.text: Dedicated to Eliphalet Nott, president of Union for a remarkable sixty-two years (1804–1866), the 110 ft high by 89 ft wide structure is a National Historic Landmark.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Galati Brothers Supermarkets was a family owned and run Italian grocery store chain in the Toronto area.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Founded in 1958 by Tony Galati & Frank Galati, the stores were smaller than traditional supermarkets and carried many Italian items.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Most of the stores were located in areas where there was a large number of Italian-Canadians.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Some stores have been branded separately as Galati Market Fresh.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Galati Brothers Supermarkets came to a close when then its final store (2592 Finch Avenue West) was sold upon the retirement of Tony Galati.

chunks.title: Galati Brothers
chunks.text: Galati Market Fresh is still running in North York, on Leslie Street by Frank Galati's two children Robert and Grace Galati.

chunks.title: Triveni Supermarkets
chunks.text: Triveni Supermarkets is a chain of retail supermarkets operating in the co-operative sector in the state of Kerala, India.

chunks.title: Triveni Supermarkets
chunks.text: This system is operated by the Kerala State Co-operative Consumers Federation Limited, which is at large controlled by the Government of Kerala.

chunks.title: Triveni Supermarkets
chunks.text: Hence this chain is in principle used as a form of governmental intervention in the retail market in the state to control and limit retail prices.

chunks.title: Triveni Supermarkets
chunks.text: As of 2017, there are a total of 229 outlets throughout the state, including some mobile, floating supermarkets, coffeehouses and a noon meal scheme.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets was a chain of supermarkets which operated in the Greater Cleveland, Ohio area.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: The company's origin can be traced to the year 1928 and the opening of a small dairy store in Cleveland Heights, Ohio by Edward Silverberg who then expanded his operation and created a chain of such stores which he called Farmview Creamery Stores.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: In 1938, Mr. Silverberg opened a supermarket on E. 185th Street which he called Pick-N-Pay.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: In 1940, he changed the name of all his stores to Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: He grew the chain to a total of 10 stores and in 1951 sold the company to Cook Coffee Company (later, as of 1969, Cook United, Inc.).

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: Under Cook Coffee's ownership, the chain continued to grow through expansion and through Pick-N-Pay's acquisition of the Foodtown supermarkets in 1959.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: In 1972, it was sold to a group of private investors led by Julius Kravitz (previously the head of Foodtown).

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: who continued the use of the brand for the newly independent company.

chunks.title: Pick-N-Pay Supermarkets
chunks.text: Principal competitors in the Greater Cleveland market were the Fisher-Fazio-Costa, Stop-N-Shop, and Heinen's grocery chains.

chunks.title: Edward Tuckerman Potter
chunks.text: Edward Tuckerman Potter (September 25, 1831 in Schenectady, New York – December 21, 1904 in New York, New York) was an American architect best known for designing the 1871 Mark Twain House in Hartford, Connecticut.

chunks.title: Edward Tuckerman Potter
chunks.text: With his half-brother William Appleton Potter, he also designed Nott Memorial Hall (1858–79) at his alma mater, Union College, Schenectady, New York.

chunks.title: Edward Tuckerman Potter
chunks.text: Both the Mark Twain House and Nott Memorial Hall are National Historic Landmarks.

chunks.title: Nott Street School
chunks.text: Nott Street School is a historic school building located at Schenectady, Schenectady County, New York.

chunks.title: Nott Street School
chunks.text: It was originally built in 1877 as a four room school, with an eight classroom addition completed in 1909.

chunks.title: Nott Street School
chunks.text: It is a two-story, red brick building above a stone and concrete raised basement.

chunks.title: Nott Street School
chunks.text: The exterior has been painted since at least 1952.

chunks.title: Nott Street School
chunks.text: The building was used as a school until 1942, and has since been used for offices.

chunks.title: 2013 Young Hollywood Awards

chunks.title: 2013 Young Hollywood Awards
chunks.text: Aisha Tyler was the host while there were no nominees this year, the recipients were "honored" with the awards.

chunks.title: 2013 Young Hollywood Awards
chunks.text: This was the first year that the awards were televised.

chunks.title: Jeremy Schoenberg
chunks.text: Jeremy Schoenberg (born May 8, 1972), born in Los Angeles County, California, United States.

chunks.text: Jeremy started out as a child star on both film and television.

chunks.title: Jeremy Schoenberg

chunks.title: Jeremy Schoenberg

chunks.text: The 12th Youth in Film Awards ceremony (now known as the Young Artist Awards), presented by the Youth in Film Association, honored outstanding youth performers under the age of 21 in the fields of film, television and music for the 1989-1990 season.

chunks.text: The exact date of the 12th annual ceremony is unknown, however, using the dates of the 11th and 13th annual awards, the 12th annual ceremony is believed to have taken place in late 1990 or early 1991 in Hollywood, California.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: The Nickelodeon Kids Choice Awards 2003 was held on April 12, 2003.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: It was the 16th annual Kids' Choice Awards ("KCA").

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: It was hosted by Rosie O'Donnell.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: The award show was held in the Barker Hangar at the Santa Monica Airport in Santa Monica, California.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: This was the last time O'Donnell would host the awards.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: By that time she has hosted the awards seven times in a row.

chunks.title: 2003 Kids' Choice Awards
chunks.text: The announcers were Daran Norris and Susanne Blakeslee from "The Fairly OddParents" who used their Cosmo and Wanda voices, respectively, for the event.

chunks.title: Maureen Dragone
chunks.text: Maureen Dragone (January 20, 1920 – February 8, 2013) was an American journalist and author.

chunks.title: Maureen Dragone
chunks.text: She was one of the longest-standing members of the Hollywood Foreign Press Association which presents the annual Golden Globe Awards.

chunks.title: Maureen Dragone
chunks.text: In 1978 she founded the Young Artist Association, which presents the annual Young Artist Awards.

chunks.title: Kelly Osbourne
chunks.text: Kelly Lee Osbourne (born 27 October 1984) is a British singer-songwriter, actress, television presenter and fashion designer.

chunks.title: Kelly Osbourne
chunks.text: The daughter of Ozzy and Sharon Osbourne, she is known for her appearances on "The Osbournes" with her family, for which they won a 2002 Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality Program, as well as on E!'s "Fashion Police", where she was a presenter from 2010 to 2015.

chunks.title: Kelly Osbourne

chunks.title: Penske Media Corporation
chunks.text: Penske Media Corporation (PMC) is an American digital media, publishing, and information services company founded in 2003.

chunks.title: Penske Media Corporation
chunks.text: PMC publishes more than 22 digital brands, including a joint venture in India with ZEE TV for its India.com brand.

chunks.title: Penske Media Corporation
chunks.text: The company also produces more than 50 annual events and conferences as well as housing a research and emerging data business.

chunks.title: Penske Media Corporation

chunks.title: Penske Media Corporation

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records
chunks.text: Puerto Roc Records is an independent record label that was established in 2006 by founder and sole owner Jonathan "DJ Primo" Padilla.

chunks.text: The independent label is based out of Miami, Florida and has its main focus on hip hop/rap music.

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records
chunks.text: and won the 2006 Independent Rap Artist of the Year at the 16th annual L.A. Music Awards in November 2006.

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records

chunks.title: Puerto Roc Records
chunks.text: Puerto Roc Records looks forward to the release of E Grizzly's next main single titled "Audiograf", which was scheduled to be released in 2008.

chunks.text: The Young Hollywood Awards was an award presented annually which honors the year's biggest achievements in pop music, movies, sports, television, fashion and more, as voted on by teenagers aged 13–19 and young adults.

chunks.title: Young Hollywood Awards

chunks.title: Young Hollywood Awards

chunks.text: He is currently the head coach at Samford University.

chunks.title: Chris Hatcher (American football)
chunks.text: Previously, Hatcher served as the head coach at Murray State University, a position he held since the 2010 season.

chunks.title: Chris Hatcher (American football)
chunks.text: He has also served as head coach at Valdosta State University from 2000 to 2006 and Georgia Southern University from 2007 to 2009.

chunks.title: Chris Hatcher (American football)
chunks.text: Hatcher played college football as a quarterback at Valdosta State from 1991 to 1994.

chunks.text: The Choctaws are in the process of becoming full members of the Gulf South Conference.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: Jim Yarbrough (born February 8, 1964) is a distinguished college basketball head coach with a 230-177 record over 14 seasons at Valdosta State University and Southeastern Louisiana University.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: He was named Southeastern Louisiana's 11th head basketball coach on June 23, 2005, and was dismissed on March 17, 2014, after compiling a 133-135 record in nine seasons that made Yarbrough the second-winningest men's basketball coach in SLU history, with the second-highest winning percentage in school history.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: His tenure included wins over Mississippi State, Penn State and Oregon State.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: Prior to his SLU career, Yarbrough led Valdosta State to multiple seasons in the NCAA Division II postseason tournament, including two seasons in which he was named both NCAA Division II South Region Coach of the Year and Gulf South Conference Coach of the Year.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: His 2003-04 Valdosta State team finished 25-4 and ranked No. 3 in the nation at the close of the season.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: Before beginning his college head coaching career at Valdosta State, he served six years as an assistant coach and associate head coach under John Kresse in the storied College of Charleston basketball program that compiled a 153-28 record and six conference championships during Yarbrough's years as a top assistant.

chunks.title: Jim Yarbrough (basketball)
chunks.text: At SLU, Yarbrough coached the Lions to five winning seasons and a school-record five winning campaigns in the Southland Conference, along with 11 players named to all-SLC teams.

chunks.text: Kerwin Douglas Bell (born June 15, 1965) is an American college and professional football coach and former player who was a quarterback in the National Football League (NFL), World League of American Football (WLAF) and the Canadian Football League (CFL) for fourteen seasons in the 1980s, 1990s and early 2000s.

chunks.title: Kerwin Bell

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: Ehyophsta (Cheyenne for "Yellow-Haired Woman") was a Cheyenne woman.

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: She was the daughter of Stands-in-the-Timber who died in 1849, and she was the niece of Bad Faced Bull.

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: She fought in the Battle of Beecher Island in 1868, and also fought the Shoshone that same year, where she counted coup against one enemy and killed another.

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: She fought the Shoshone again in 1869.

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: She was also a member of a secret society composed exclusively of Cheyenne women.

chunks.title: Ehyophsta
chunks.text: She died in 1915.

chunks.title: Lean Bear
chunks.text: Lean Bear (Cheyenne name Awoninahku, 1813–1864), alternatively translated as Starving Bear, was a Cheyenne peace chief.

chunks.title: Lean Bear
chunks.text: He was a member of the Council of Forty-four, a tribal governance devoted to maintaining peace with encroaching United States settlers.

chunks.title: Lean Bear
chunks.text: Lean Bear's most notable peace deals include the Treaty of Fort Wise and a meeting with US President Abraham Lincoln.

chunks.title: Lean Bear
chunks.text: His work towards peace between his people and the American settlers in the Southern Plains were cut short when he was murdered by the 1st Colorado Cavalry Regiment and violent retaliations ensued.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: The Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation (Tsėhéstáno in Cheyenne, formerly named the Tongue River Indian Reservation) is home of the federally recognized Northern Cheyenne Tribe.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: Located in southeastern Montana, the reservation is approximately 444,000 acres in size and home to approximately 5,000 Cheyenne people.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: The tribal and government headquarters are in Lame Deer, which is also the home of the annual Northern Cheyenne Pow wow.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: The reservation is bounded on the east by the Tongue River and on the west by the Crow Reservation.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: There are small parcels of non-contiguous off-reservation trust lands in Meade County, South Dakota, northeast of the city of Sturgis.

chunks.title: Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation
chunks.text: Its timbered ridges that extend into northwestern South Dakota are part of Custer National Forest and it is approximately 40 mi east of the site of the 1876 Battle of the Greasy Grass (known to most Americans as the Battle of the Little Bighorn).

chunks.title: Lame Deer, Montana
chunks.text: Lame Deer (Meaveʼhoʼeno in Cheyenne) is a census-designated place (CDP) in Rosebud County, Montana.

chunks.title: Lame Deer, Montana
chunks.text: The community is named after Miniconjou Lakota chief Lame Deer, who was killed by the U.S. Army in 1877 under a flag of truce south of the town.

chunks.title: Lame Deer, Montana
chunks.text: It is the tribal and government agency headquarters of the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation.

chunks.title: Lame Deer, Montana
chunks.text: This is the location of the Chief Dull Knife College and the annual Northern Cheyenne Powwow.

chunks.title: Executive Order 13175
chunks.text: Executive Order 13175, "Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments," was issued by U.S. President Bill Clinton on November 6, 2000.

chunks.title: Executive Order 13175
chunks.text: This executive order required federal departments and agencies to consult with Indian tribal governments when considering policies that would impact tribal communities.

chunks.title: Executive Order 13175
chunks.text: Executive Order 13175 reiterated the federal government's previously acknowledged commitment to tribal self-government and limited autonomy.

chunks.title: Cheyenne
chunks.text: The Cheyenne ( ) are one of the Indigenous peoples of the Great Plains and their language is of the Algonquian language family.

chunks.title: Cheyenne
chunks.text: The Cheyenne comprise two Native American tribes, the Só'taeo'o or Só'taétaneo'o (more commonly spelled as Suhtai or Sutaio) and the Tsétsêhéstâhese (also spelled Tsitsistas).

chunks.title: Cheyenne
chunks.text: These tribes merged in the early 19th century.

chunks.title: Cheyenne
chunks.text: Today, the Cheyenne people are split into two federally recognized Nations: the Southern Cheyenne, who are enrolled in the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes in Oklahoma, and the Northern Cheyenne, who are enrolled in the Northern Cheyenne Tribe of the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation in Montana.

chunks.title: Chief Dull Knife College
chunks.text: Chief Dull Knife College (originally Dull Knife Memorial College) is a small, open-admission, Native American tribal community college and land grant institution.

chunks.title: Chief Dull Knife College
chunks.text: Located on the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation, in the city of Lame Deer, it has a current enrollment of about 141 students.

chunks.title: Chief Dull Knife College
chunks.text: On average, more than half of its graduates move on to four-year colleges.

chunks.title: Council of Forty-four
chunks.text: The Council of Forty-four was one of the two central institutions of traditional Cheyenne Indian tribal governance, the other being the military societies such as the Dog Soldiers.

chunks.title: Council of Forty-four
chunks.text: The influence of the Council of Forty-four waned in the face of internal conflict among the Cheyenne about Cheyenne policy toward encroaching white settlers on the Great Plains, and was dealt a severe blow by the Sand Creek Massacre.

chunks.title: Cheyenne military societies
chunks.text: Cheyenne military societies are one of the two central institutions of traditional Cheyenne Indian tribal governance, the other being the Council of Forty-four.

chunks.title: Cheyenne military societies
chunks.text: While council chiefs are responsible for overall governance of individual bands and the tribe as a whole, the headmen of military societies are in charge of maintaining discipline within the tribe, overseeing tribal hunts and ceremonies, and providing military leadership.

chunks.title: Cheyenne military societies
chunks.text: Historically, council chiefs selected which of the six military societies would assume these duties; after a period of time on-duty, the chiefs would select a different society to take up the duties.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: Eugene Little Coyote was the president of the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation from 2004 to 2007.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: He was elected in November 2004, defeating the incumbent president, Geri Small.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: However, after a conflict with reservation vice president Rick Wolfname that began in July 2007 escalated, the Northern Cheyenne tribal council declared that it would oust Little Coyote as the tribe's president.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: Little Coyote was forcibly removed from office and arrested for trespassing in the tribal office building on December 28, 2007.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: It is worth noting that the move by the tribal council to remove Little Coyote from office was deemed unconstitutional and void by the Northern Cheyenne Constitutional Court.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: The Constitutional Court was however overruled by Bureau of Indian Affairs' regional director Ed Parisian, and later the Assistant Secretary of Indian Affairs Carl J. Artman.

chunks.title: Eugene Little Coyote
chunks.text: Their involvement in this matter set a historical precedence of the BIA directly meddling with tribal governments.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: Alice Russell Glenny (1858–1924) was an American painter, sculptor, and graphic artist who lived and worked in Buffalo, New York.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: Glenny was a fixture of the thriving artistic scene in Buffalo in the early twentieth century.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: From 1893-1894 and 1903–1904, she served as president of the Buffalo Society of Artists.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: She studied under top teachers, such as William Merritt Chase and Gustav Boulanger, in both the United States and France, and was considered in her time to be one of the city's top artists.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: Today, Glenny is best remembered for her Art Nouveau posters and magazine illustrations.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: Her posters were featured prominently in Buffalo's Pan-American Exposition of 1901, famous for being the location of the shooting of President William McKinley.

chunks.title: Alice Russell Glenny
chunks.text: She also regularly contributed illustrations to the Buffalo-Courier Express, one of the major newspapers in Buffalo at the time.

chunks.title: Assassination of James A. Garfield
chunks.text: James A. Garfield, the 20th President of the United States, was assassinated at 9:30 am on July 2, 1881, less than four months into his term as President.

chunks.title: Assassination of James A. Garfield
chunks.text: He was shot by Charles J. Guiteau at the Baltimore and Potomac Railroad Station in Washington, D.C., and died in Elberon, New Jersey on September 19, 1881.

chunks.title: Assassination of James A. Garfield
chunks.text: Guiteau's motive was revenge against Garfield for an imagined political debt.

chunks.title: Assassination of James A. Garfield
chunks.text: Garfield was the second of four Presidents to be assassinated, following Abraham Lincoln and preceding William McKinley and John F. Kennedy.

chunks.title: Assassination of James A. Garfield
chunks.text: His Vice President, Chester A. Arthur, succeeded Garfield as President.

chunks.title: Rose C. Davison
chunks.text: Rosalie Compton Kahipuleokalaniahumanu Davison, known as Rose C. Davison, (September 22, 1868 – May 26, 1913) was a part Native Hawaiian female educator, philanthropist and governmental social worker.

chunks.title: Rose C. Davison
chunks.text: She served as assistant secretary of the Board of Education of the Territory of Hawaii and represented Hawaii in the 1901 Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: Mission furniture is a style of furniture that originated in the late 19th century.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: It traces its origins to a chair made by A.J. Forbes around 1894 for San Francisco's Swedenborgian Church.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: The term mission furniture was first popularized by Joseph P. McHugh of New York, a furniture manufacturer and retailer who copied these chairs and offered a line of stylistically related furnishings by 1898.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: The word "mission" references the Spanish missions throughout colonial California, though the design of most Mission Style furniture owed little to the original furnishings of these missions.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: The style became increasingly popular following the 1901 Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo.

chunks.title: Mission style furniture
chunks.text: The style was popularly associated with the American Arts and Crafts movement.

chunks.title: Pan-American Exposition
chunks.text: The Pan-American Exposition was a World's Fair held in Buffalo, New York, United States, from May 1 through November 2, 1901.

chunks.title: Pan-American Exposition
chunks.text: The fair occupied 350 acre of land on the western edge of what is now Delaware Park, extending from Delaware Avenue to Elmwood Avenue and northward to Great Arrow Avenue.

chunks.title: Pan-American Exposition
chunks.text: It is remembered today primarily for being the location of the assassination of President William McKinley.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: Caroline Peddle Ball (1869-1938) was an American sculptor.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: Born at Terre Haute, Indiana, she was a pupil at the Art Students' League, under Augustus Saint-Gaudens and Kenyon Cox.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: She received honorable mention at Paris Exhibition, 1900.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: She was a member of the Guild of Arts and Crafts and of Art Students' League.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: This sculptor exhibited at Paris a Bronze Clock.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: She designed for the Tiffany Glass Company the figure of the Young Virgin and that of the Christ of the Sacred Heart.

chunks.title: Caroline Peddle Ball
chunks.text: A memorial fountain at Flushing, Long Island, a medallion portrait of Miss Cox of Terre Haute, a monument to a child in the same city, a Victory in a quadriga seen on the United States Building, Paris, 1900, and also at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, 1901, are among her important works.

chunks.title: Temple of Music
chunks.text: The Temple of Music was a concert hall and auditorium built for the Pan-American Exposition which was held in Buffalo, New York in 1901.

chunks.title: Temple of Music
chunks.text: U.S. President William McKinley was assassinated inside the building on September 6, 1901.

chunks.title: Temple of Music
chunks.text: The structure, like most of the other buildings at the exposition, was demolished when the fair ended.

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: The 1901 State of the Union Address was given on Tuesday, December 3, 1901, by the 26th President of the United States, Theodore Roosevelt.

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: It was presented to both houses of the 57th United States Congress, but he was not present.

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: He stated, "The Congress assembles this year under the shadow of a great calamity.

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: On the sixth of September, President McKinley was shot by an anarchist while attending the Pan-American Exposition at Buffalo, and died in that city on the fourteenth of that month."

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: He concluded it with, "Indeed, from every quarter of the civilized world we received, at the time of the President's death, assurances of such grief and regard as to touch the hearts of our people.

chunks.title: 1901 State of the Union Address
chunks.text: In the midst of our affliction we reverently thank the Almighty that we are at peace with the nations of mankind; and we firmly intend that our policy shall be such as to continue unbroken these international relations of mutual respect and good will."

chunks.title: Put Me Off at Buffalo
chunks.text: Put Me Off at Buffalo is a song by the vaudeville team of the Dillon Brothers, with lyrics by Harry Dillon and music by John Dillon.

chunks.title: Put Me Off at Buffalo
chunks.text: It was first published in 1895, and also appeared in the play "A Trip to Chinatown".

chunks.title: Put Me Off at Buffalo
chunks.text: After an initial period of popularity, the tune was revived in 1901 in connection with the Pan-American Exposition held in Buffalo.

chunks.title: Put Me Off at Buffalo
chunks.text: The song's lyrics were planted in the lawn of Buffalo's city hall during the event.

chunks.title: Assassination of William McKinley
chunks.text: On September 6, 1901, William McKinley, the 25th President of the United States, was shot on the grounds of the Pan-American Exposition at the Temple of Music in Buffalo, New York.

chunks.title: Assassination of William McKinley
chunks.text: He was shaking hands with the public when Leon Czolgosz, an anarchist, shot him twice in the abdomen.

chunks.title: Assassination of William McKinley
chunks.text: McKinley died eight days later on September 14 of gangrene caused by the gunshot wounds.

chunks.title: Assassination of William McKinley
chunks.text: He was the third American president to have been assassinated, following Abraham Lincoln in 1865 and James A. Garfield in 1881.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: Boston United Football Club is an English football club based in Boston, Lincolnshire.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: The club participates in the National League North, the sixth tier of English football.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: The club is known as 'the Pilgrims' in reference to the Pilgrim Fathers, who left England and sailed to North America and founded Boston, Massachusetts.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: The club's crest, the pilgrim fathers' ship 'The Mayflower', is also a reference to them.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: The club's traditional colours are amber and black.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: Boston's neighbours include Lincoln City, Scunthorpe United and Grimsby Town.

chunks.title: Boston United F.C.
chunks.text: The club is one of only 12 in the country to run a Centre of Excellence, provides a Study Support Centre and is also the basis of the 'Boston United Football in the Community Scheme'.

chunks.title: National League North
chunks.text: The National League North, formerly Conference North (currently named the Vanarama National League North for sponsorship reasons), is a division of the National League in England, taking its place immediately below the top division National League.

chunks.title: National League North
chunks.text: Along with the National League South, it is at Step 2 of the National League System and the sixth overall tier of the English football league system.

chunks.title: National League North
chunks.text: It consists of teams located in Northern England, Norfolk, the English Midlands and North Wales.

chunks.title: National League North
chunks.text: From the start of the 2015–16 season, the league has been known as the National League North.

chunks.title: National League North
chunks.text: As part of a sponsorship deal with Vanarama, the National League North is now known as the Vanarama National League North.

chunks.title: Jack Truelove
chunks.text: Jack Christopher Truelove (born 27 December 1995) is an English football player who most recently played for National League North side Hednesford Town on loan from Oldham Athletic.

chunks.title: Jack Truelove
chunks.text: He is currently registered to play for National League North side Curzon Ashton.

chunks.title: Gainsborough Trinity F.C.
chunks.text: Gainsborough Trinity Football Club is a football club based in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, England.

chunks.title: Gainsborough Trinity F.C.
chunks.text: Established in 1873, the club became members of the Football League in 1893 and remained members of the Second Division until 1912, making Gainsborough one of the smallest towns in England to have had a Football League team.

chunks.title: Gainsborough Trinity F.C.
chunks.text: They are currently members of the National League North, the sixth tier of English football, and play at the Northolme.

chunks.title: Chris Williams (English footballer)
chunks.text: Christopher Jonathan "Chris" Williams (born 2 February 1985) is an English semi-professional footballer who last played for Salford City as a forward.

chunks.title: National League South
chunks.text: The National League South, formerly Conference South (billed as The Vanarama National League South for sponsorship reasons), is one of the second divisions of the National League in England, taking its place immediately below the top division National League.

chunks.title: National League South
chunks.text: Along with National League North it is at the second level of the National League System, and at the sixth tier overall of the English football league system.

chunks.title: National League (English football)
chunks.text: The National League is an association football league in England consisting of three divisions, the National League, National League North and National League South.

chunks.title: National League (English football)
chunks.text: It was called the Alliance Premier League from 1979 until 1986.

chunks.title: National League (English football)
chunks.text: Between 1986 and 2015, the league was known as the Football Conference.

chunks.title: National League (English football)
chunks.text: As part of a sponsorship deal with car leasing company Vanarama, the league is known as the Vanarama National League.

chunks.title: Curzon Ashton F.C.
chunks.text: Curzon Ashton Football Club is a semi-professional football club based in the market town of Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester, England, that competes in the National League North, the sixth-highest division overall in the English football league system, and are members of the Manchester County Football Association.

chunks.title: Curzon Ashton F.C.
chunks.text: Nicknamed "the Nash", the club was founded in 1963 and moved to its current stadium, Tameside Stadium, in 2005.

chunks.title: Salford City F.C.
chunks.text: Salford City Football Club is a professional football club in the Kersal area of Salford, Greater Manchester, England, which plays in National League North, the sixth tier of English football.

chunks.title: Spennymoor Town F.C.

chunks.title: Community High School District 117

chunks.title: Community High School District 117
chunks.text: District 117 is composed of two high schools: Antioch Community High School, which is located in the city of its namesake; and Lakes Community High School, which is, in turn, located in Lake Villa.

chunks.title: Community High School District 117
chunks.text: The district superintendent is Jim McKay,

chunks.title: Antioch Community High School
chunks.text: Antioch Community High School, Antioch, or ACHS, is a public four-year high school located in Antioch, Illinois, a far north suburb of Chicago, Illinois, in the United States.

chunks.title: Antioch Community High School
chunks.text: It is part of Community High School District 117, which also includes Lakes Community High School.

chunks.title: Franklin Community Schools

chunks.title: Franklin Community High School

chunks.title: Franklin Community High School
chunks.text: It is a part of Franklin Community Schools.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 is a school district in the southwest suburbs of Chicago.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: Created in 1951, the district serves the communities of New Lenox, Frankfort, Mokena, Manhattan, and small portions of Tinley Park and Orland Park.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: Four high schools comprise Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210: Lincoln-Way Central, Lincoln-Way East, Lincoln-Way North and Lincoln-Way West.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: Lincoln-Way Central and Lincoln-Way West are located in New Lenox; Lincoln-Way East and Lincoln-Way North are located in Frankfort.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: District 210 offices are located at Lincoln-Way Central.Effective for the 2016-2017 school year, due to financial troubles, Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 will consolidate to a three school district.

chunks.title: Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210
chunks.text: The three schools to comprise the district are Lincoln-Way Central, Lincoln-Way East, and Lincoln-Way West.

chunks.title: St. Charles Community Schools
chunks.text: St. Charles Community Schools (STCCS) is a school district headquartered in St. Charles, Michigan.

chunks.title: St. Charles Community Schools
chunks.text: It is a part of the Saginaw Intermediate School District and serves the St. Charles area, including the village of St. Charles, the northern portions of Brant and St. Charles townships, and the southern portions of Fremont and Swan Creek townships.

chunks.title: St. Charles Community Schools
chunks.text: Its schools include St. Charles Elementary School, Anna M. Thurston Middle School, and St. Charles Community High School.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School or RCHS is a public high school located on the Davenport, Florida and Haines City, Florida Line.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: RCHS was established in 2005 in Polk County.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: It currently serves 2,600 students and has 106 teachers on campus.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School is one of many schools with a separate 9th Grade campus with its own front office.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: The main campus holds students in 10th, 11th, and 12th grade with some exceptions.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School sits on 76 acre of land.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School is zoned for Davenport and Haines City.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School's rivals include Haines City High School, Lake Wales High School and others in Polk County.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: The principal of RCHS is currently Russell Donnelly who replaced Sherry Wells, the acting principal between the school's opening in 2005 and 2015 and has a few assistant principals.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: Ridge Community High School is part of the Polk County School Board.

chunks.title: Ridge Community High School
chunks.text: RCHS's mascot is the Bolt, and the school motto is Once a Bolt, always a Bolt.

chunks.title: Culver Community High School
chunks.text: Culver Community High School is a four-year comprehensive public high school in Culver, Indiana.

chunks.title: Culver Community High School
chunks.text: It is fully accredited by the Indiana Department of Education and the North Central Association Commission on Accreditation and School Improvement.

chunks.title: Culver Community High School
chunks.text: The high school is part of the Culver Community Schools Corporation, along with one middle school and one elementary school.

chunks.title: Lakes Community High School
