chunks.title: Lakes Community High School
chunks.text: It is part of Community High School District 117, which also includes Antioch Community High School.

chunks.title: East Peoria Community High School
chunks.text: East Peoria Community High School is a four-year public high school located in East Peoria, Illinois, and is the only school of East Peoria Community High School District 309.

chunks.title: East Peoria Community High School
chunks.text: It has approximately 1,200 students.

chunks.title: East Peoria Community High School
chunks.text: East Peoria Community High School has several feeder schools: Central Junior High School (East Peoria School District 86), Parkview Middle School (Creve Coeur School District 76), and Robein Elementary School (District 85).

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The Atlanta Hawks are an American professional basketball team based in Atlanta, Georgia.

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: They play in the Southeast Division of the Eastern Conference in the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The team began playing in 1946 as a member of the National Basketball League (NBL), and joined the NBA in 1949.

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The team has had five names since its inception; the Buffalo Bisons (1946), the Tri-Cities Blackhawks (1946–1951), the Milwaukee Hawks (1951–1955), the St. Louis Hawks (1955–1968), and the Atlanta Hawks (1968–present).

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The Hawks won their only NBA championship in 1958, and have not returned to the NBA Finals since 1960.

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The team has played its home games at the Philips Arena since 1999.

chunks.title: List of Atlanta Hawks head coaches
chunks.text: The Hawks are owned by Atlanta Spirit, LLC, and Danny Ferry is their general manager.

chunks.title: Atlanta Hawks, LLC
chunks.text: Atlanta Hawks, LLC (formerly known as Atlanta Spirit LLC) was an Atlanta, Georgia-based parent company formerly the holder of the franchise of the Atlanta Hawks, a professional basketball team in the NBA, and the Atlanta Thrashers, a former professional hockey team in the NHL.

chunks.title: Atlanta Hawks, LLC
chunks.text: The Atlanta Spirit LLC name was changed to Atlanta Hawks, LLC on March 14, 2014.

chunks.title: Zaza Pachulia
chunks.text: Zaza Pachulia (Georgian: ზაზა ფაჩულია ; February 10, 1984) is a Georgian professional basketball player for the Golden State Warriors of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Zaza Pachulia
chunks.text: He was born as Zaur Pachulia, but his first name was legally changed to Zaza.

chunks.title: Zaza Pachulia
chunks.text: In 2017, Pachulia won his first NBA Championship as a member of the Warriors.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: The 2004–05 NBA season was the Bucks' 37th season in the National Basketball Association.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: During the offseason, the Bucks signed free agents Mike James and second-year guard Mo Williams, while acquiring Zaza Pachulia from the expansion Charlotte Bobcats.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: Injuries hampered the Bucks from the start as second-year guard T.J. Ford was lost for the entire season due to a neck injury.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: The Bucks would get off to a sluggish start losing 16 of their first 22 games.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: At midseason, the team traded Keith Van Horn to the Dallas Mavericks, and dealt James to the Houston Rockets.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: They continued to struggle losing 15 of their final 18 games including an 8-game losing streak, finishing last place in the Central Division with a 30–52 record.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: The only bright spot came from Michael Redd, who averaged a team high of 23.0 points per game.

chunks.title: 2004–05 Milwaukee Bucks season
chunks.text: Following the season, head coach Terry Porter was fired, and Pachulia signed as a free agent with the Atlanta Hawks.

chunks.title: Marco Belinelli
chunks.text: Marco Stefano Belinelli (] ; born March 25, 1986) is an Italian professional basketball player for the Atlanta Hawks of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

chunks.title: Marco Belinelli
chunks.text: He was selected 18th overall in the 2007 NBA draft by the Golden State Warriors.

chunks.title: Marco Belinelli
chunks.text: In 2014, he won the NBA championship with the San Antonio Spurs, becoming the first Italian player to achieve such a feat.

chunks.title: Marco Belinelli
chunks.text: He also won the NBA Three-Point Shootout during the 2014 NBA All-Star Weekend.

chunks.title: Marco Belinelli
chunks.text: He also played the 2007, 2011, 2013, 2015 and 2017 editions of the FIBA EuroBasket and the 2006 FIBA World Championship with the Italian national basketball team.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: The 1957–58 NBA season was the franchise's third in St. Louis and the 12th season overall in the NBA.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: Coming off their trip to the 1957 NBA Finals, the Hawks won the Western Division by 8 games with a record of 41 wins and 31 losses.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: Bob Pettit ranked 3rd in scoring and 2nd in rebounding.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: In the Western Finals, the Hawks would beat the Detroit Pistons in 5 games.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks would face the Boston Celtics in the NBA Finals.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: After Games 1 and 2, the teams headed to St. Louis with the series tied at a game apiece.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks took Game 3, as the Celtics lost Bill Russell to an ankle injury.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: Despite playing without Russell, the Celtics were triumphant in Game 4.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks pulled out a 2-point victory in the 5th match to take control of the series.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: Needing one more win for their first NBA Championship, the Hawks beat the Celtics 110–109.

chunks.title: 1957–58 St. Louis Hawks season
chunks.text: Bob Pettit scored 50 points playing against an injured Bill Russell as the Hawks and owner Ben Kerner won their first NBA Championship.

chunks.title: Bruce Levenson
chunks.text: Bruce Levenson is an American businessman, former NBA team owner, and philanthropist.

chunks.title: Bruce Levenson
chunks.text: He was a co-owner of Atlanta Hawks, LLC (formerly Atlanta Spirit LLC), which owns and operates the Atlanta Hawks basketball team and Philips Arena.

chunks.title: Bruce Levenson
chunks.text: Levenson has also served as the Hawks' Governor on the NBA Board of Governors since 2004.

chunks.title: Skip Harlicka
chunks.text: Jules Peter "Skip" Harlicka (born October 14, 1946) is an American former NBA basketball player for the Atlanta Hawks.

chunks.title: Skip Harlicka
chunks.text: Skip went to the University of South Carolina on a basketball scholarship, but also played baseball his freshmen year.

chunks.title: Skip Harlicka
chunks.text: During his college basketball career, Skip averaged 17.5 points per game on 47.5% shooting from the field.

chunks.title: Skip Harlicka
chunks.text: Skip was drafted with the 13th pick in the 1968 NBA Draft by the Atlanta Hawks.

chunks.title: Skip Harlicka
chunks.text: He played one season for the Hawks, appearing in 26 games while averaging 4.1 points per game and 1.4 assists per game.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The 2007–08 NBA season was the Atlanta Hawks' 59th season in the National Basketball Association, and 40th season in Atlanta.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: After missing the playoffs for eight straight seasons, the Hawks selected Al Horford out of the University of Florida with the third pick in the 2007 NBA draft.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks started out the season by defeating the Dallas Mavericks 101–94 in their season opener, marking the first time they won their first game of the season since the 1999 lockout season.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: However, their struggles continued as they went on a six-game losing streak around the All-Star break.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: At midseason, the Hawks traded Tyronn Lue, Lorenzen Wright, Anthony Johnson and second-year forward Shelden Williams to the Sacramento Kings for Mike Bibby.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks finished third in the Southeast Division with a 37–45 record, and made the playoffs for the first time since 1999.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: Joe Johnson was selected for the 2008 NBA All-Star Game, and Horford made the All-First Rookie Team.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: In the first round of the playoffs, they lost to the top-seeded Boston Celtics in seven games.

chunks.title: 2007–08 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: Following the season, Josh Childress left to play overseas.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The 2005–06 NBA season was the Atlanta Hawks' 57th season in the National Basketball Association, and 38th season in Atlanta.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: After finishing the previous season with the worst record, the Hawks selected Marvin Williams with the second overall pick in the 2005 NBA draft.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: During the offseason, the team acquired Joe Johnson from the Phoenix Suns, and signed free agent Zaza Pachulia.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: However, tragedy struck as center Jason Collier suffered a heart attack during the preseason and died suddenly on October 15.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks would stumble out of the gate again losing their first nine games, on their way to an awful 2–16 start.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: However, they would play better in December winning five of their next seven games, including a win over the defending champion San Antonio Spurs, 94–84 on December 10.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks played .500 basketball in February, which included a 99–98 victory over the Detroit Pistons on February 7.

chunks.title: 2005–06 Atlanta Hawks season
chunks.text: The Hawks doubled their win total by finishing last place in the Southeast Division with a 26–56 record, tied with the second-year Charlotte Bobcats.

chunks.title: Ruth Todd
chunks.text: Ruth Todd is an award-winning Salt Lake City television news anchor.

chunks.title: Ruth Todd
chunks.text: She most recently worked in television for KTVX ABC4.

chunks.title: Ruth Todd
chunks.text: Todd joined the ABC4 news team in December 2001, but first appeared on-air April 15, 2002 as the station's lead female anchor.

chunks.title: Ruth Todd
chunks.text: Her last newscast was February 28, 2007, after her five-year contract expired.

chunks.title: Cartoon Network
chunks.text: Cartoon Network is an American basic cable and satellite television channel that is owned by The Cartoon Network, Inc., a subsidiary of Turner Broadcasting System, itself being a subsidiary of Time Warner.

chunks.title: Cartoon Network
chunks.text: It was founded by Betty Cohen and launched on October 1, 1992.

chunks.title: Color Rhapsodies
chunks.text: Color Rhapsodies was a series of usually one-shot animated cartoon shorts produced by Charles Mintz for Columbia Pictures.

chunks.title: Color Rhapsodies
chunks.text: They were launched in 1934, following the phenomenal success of Walt Disney's Technicolor "Silly Symphonies".

chunks.title: Color Rhapsodies
chunks.text: Because of Disney's exclusive rights to the full three strip Technicolor process, "Color Rhapsodies" were produced in the older two-tone Technicolor process until 1935, when Disney's exclusive contract expired.

chunks.title: Underfist: Halloween Bash
chunks.text: Underfist: Halloween Bash (otherwise known as Underfist) is an American animated spin-off special of "The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy".

chunks.title: Underfist: Halloween Bash
chunks.text: It aired on October 12, 2008.

chunks.title: Underfist: Halloween Bash
chunks.text: The special was going to be the setup for a new series spin-off of "Grim & Evil", but the contract of Maxwell Atoms with Cartoon Network expired before moving to Disney Channel for the TV series "Fish Hooks" and the special was ultimately the finale of the "Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy" franchise.

chunks.title: Igor Musa
chunks.text: Igor Musa (born 18 October 1973, Jajce, Bosnia and Herzegovina) is a former central midfielder.

chunks.title: Igor Musa
chunks.text: He went to Hajduk from Slaven Belupo in the summer of 2006 and then to AEL Limassol in July 2007.

chunks.title: Igor Musa
chunks.text: He was in Hajduk previously in 2001/2002.

chunks.title: Igor Musa
chunks.text: At end of the season his contract expired and he left.

chunks.title: Igor Musa
chunks.text: He played for some Spanish clubs before returning to Croatia.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: Temptation was an Australian game show which premiered on the Nine Network on 30 May 2005.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: Hosted by Ed Phillips and Livinia Nixon, the show was a remake of "Sale of the Century", which aired on Nine in the same timeslot for more than twenty years between 1980 and 2001.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: "Temptation" had the same general format of its predecessor, but with several new features and a de-emphasis on the "shopping" aspects of the endgame.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: The show ran until 30 November 2007, when it was placed on hiatus by the network following strong competition from game show "Deal or No Deal" on the rival Seven Network; during the hiatus, Nine filled the timeslot with episodes of the American sitcom "Two and a Half Men".

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: When Ed Phillips made an appearance on "The NRL Footy Show" he announced "maybe summer" would be the return of the show.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: This statement was accurate, as "Temptation" returned for a shortened fourth series from 1 December 2008 with unaired episodes which were recorded during 2008.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: During that time, Ed Phillips was dumped by the Nine Network after his contract expired in November, and "Temptation" never returned to the schedule.

chunks.title: Temptation (Australian game show)
chunks.text: After 23 January 2009, when the show's final episode aired, all "Temptation" websites were removed, and "Two and a Half Men" returned to Channel Nine's 7:00pm schedule.

chunks.title: Julian Kern
chunks.text: Julian Kern (born December 28, 1989) is a German former road bicycle racer.

chunks.title: Julian Kern
chunks.text: Kern previously competed for the during the 2012 season, before joining Ag2r–La Mondiale on a two-year contract from the 2013 season onwards.

chunks.title: Julian Kern
chunks.text: In November 2014, Kern retired from cycling when his contract expired and he was unable to find a new team.

chunks.title: Ocean Park Halloween Bash
chunks.text: Ocean Park Halloween Bash (海洋公園哈囉喂) is an annual Halloween event held by Ocean Park Hong Kong.

chunks.title: Ocean Park Halloween Bash
chunks.text: It contains haunted attractions and shows, the park area is decorated with Halloween decorations and full of Halloween characters that are dressed up by the officials.

chunks.title: Ocean Park Halloween Bash
chunks.text: The Halloween Bash in Ocean Park started in 2001 and it held during late September to 1 November each year.

chunks.title: Ocean Park Halloween Bash

chunks.title: Junaid Hartley

chunks.text: He moved abroad for spells with Vitória de Setúbal in the Primeira Liga and Lens in Ligue 1.

chunks.title: Junaid Hartley

chunks.title: Junaid Hartley

chunks.title: HitRadio Veronica (Sky Radio)
chunks.text: HitRadio Veronica is a Dutch radio station that broadcasts over the internet.

chunks.title: HitRadio Veronica (Sky Radio)
chunks.text: On December 27, 2006 at 12:00pm TMF Radio was officially launched.

chunks.title: HitRadio Veronica (Sky Radio)
chunks.text: TMF Radio until October 1, 2008 had a partnership between Sky Radio Group (Sienna Holding BV) and MTV Networks Benelux (TMF) and transmitted mostly hits from the cable frequency of Hitradio BV, which was acquired permanently in the spring of 2007 by Sky Radio Group and MTV Networks BV.

chunks.title: HitRadio Veronica (Sky Radio)

chunks.title: HitRadio Veronica (Sky Radio)

chunks.title: Great ape personhood
chunks.text: Great ape personhood is a movement to extend personhood and some legal protections to the non-human members of the Hominidae or great ape family: chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas, and orangutans.

chunks.title: Anne E. Russon
chunks.text: Russon is widely published in the fields of primate behavior and ecology, is executive director of the Borneo Orangutan Society of Canada, and is the author of several popular press books dealing with Great Apes including "Orangutans: Wizards of the Rainforest", "Reaching into Thought: The Minds of the Great Apes", and "The Evolution of Thought: Evolution of Great Ape Intelligence".

chunks.title: Oliver the chimpanzee
chunks.text: Oliver (c. 1958 – 2 June 2012) was a former "performing" ape once promoted as a missing link or "Humanzee" due to his (somewhat) unusually human-like appendages and a tendency to walk upright.

chunks.title: Oliver the chimpanzee
chunks.text: Despite his somewhat unusual appearance and behavior, scientists determined that Oliver was not a human-chimpanzee hybrid.

chunks.title: Great Ape Project
chunks.text: The Great Ape Project (GAP), founded in 1993, is an international organization of primatologists, anthropologists, ethicists, and others who advocate a United Nations Declaration of the Rights of Great Apes that would confer basic legal rights on non-human great apes: chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas, and orangutans.

chunks.title: Kanzi
chunks.text: Kanzi (born October 28, 1980), also known by the lexigram (from the character 太), is a male bonobo who has been featured in several studies on great ape language.

chunks.title: Kanzi
chunks.text: According to Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, a primatologist who has studied the bonobo throughout her life, Kanzi has exhibited advanced linguistic aptitude.

chunks.title: Bonobo
chunks.text: The bonobo ( or ; "Pan paniscus"), formerly called the pygmy chimpanzee and less often, the dwarf or gracile chimpanzee, is an endangered great ape and one of the two species making up the genus "Pan"; the other is "Pan troglodytes", or the common chimpanzee.

chunks.title: Bonobo
chunks.text: Although the name "chimpanzee" is sometimes used to refer to both species together, it is usually understood as referring to the common chimpanzee, whereas "Pan paniscus" is usually referred to as the bonobo.

chunks.title: Orangutan (disambiguation)
chunks.text: The orangutan is a great ape.

chunks.title: Humanzee
chunks.text: The humanzee ("Homo sapiens sapiens" × "Pan") (also known as the Chuman or Manpanzee) is a hypothetical chimpanzee/human hybrid.

chunks.title: Humanzee
chunks.text: An unsuccessful attempt to breed such a hybrid was made by Ilya Ivanovich Ivanov in the 1920s.

chunks.title: Humanzee
chunks.text: There have been occasional reports of human-chimpanzee hybridization, notably regarding a performing chimp named Oliver during the 1970s, but none of them have been confirmed.

chunks.title: Chimpanzee
chunks.text: Chimpanzees (or chimps) are the species of the great apes in the genus Pan, consisting of the common chimpanzee and the bonobo.

chunks.title: Chimpanzee
chunks.text: Together with gorillas, they are the only great apes that are currently restricted in their range to Africa.

chunks.title: Chimpanzee
chunks.text: Native to sub-Saharan Africa, both chimpanzees and bonobos are currently found in the Congo jungle.

chunks.title: Great ape research ban
chunks.text: A great ape research ban, or severe restrictions on the use of great apes in research, is currently in place in the Netherlands, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Sweden, Germany

chunks.title: Macross Ace Frontier
chunks.text: Macross Ace Frontier (マクロス エース フロンティア , makurosu ēsu furontia ) is a shooting game developed by Artdink for the PlayStation Portable.

chunks.title: Macross Ace Frontier
chunks.text: The game is based on Studio Nue's popular "Macross" series, one of which is known in the West as the first generation of "Robotech".

chunks.title: Macross Ace Frontier
chunks.text: It features original elements as well as characters, mechanics, episode plots and BGM borrowed from 1982's "The Super Dimension Fortress Macross" original TV series, the 1992 "Macross Plus" OVA series, the 1994 "Macross 7" TV series and the 2008 "Macross Frontier" TV series, as well as incorporating more elements from the 1984 "" feature film and the 2002 prequel OVA series "Macross Zero".

chunks.title: Leonard Hofstadter
chunks.text: Leonard Leakey Hofstadter, Ph.D., is a fictional character in the CBS television series "The Big Bang Theory", in which he is portrayed by actor Johnny Galecki.

chunks.title: Leonard Hofstadter
chunks.text: Leonard is an experimental physicist, who shares an apartment with colleague and best friend Dr. Sheldon Cooper (Jim Parsons).

chunks.title: Leonard Hofstadter
chunks.text: For his portrayal, Galecki was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award in 2011.

chunks.title: Steven Molaro
chunks.text: Steven Molaro, also known as Steve Molaro, is an American television producer and writer.

chunks.title: Steven Molaro
chunks.text: He has worked on such productions as "Freddie", "The Class", "Complete Savages" and the Dan Schneider-produced series "All That", "The Amanda Show", "What I Like About You", "Drake & Josh", "Zoey 101" and "iCarly".

chunks.title: Steven Molaro
chunks.text: Since 2007, he has been a producer/writer on the sitcom "The Big Bang Theory".

chunks.title: Steven Molaro
chunks.text: , Molaro also co-created it's prequel spinoff, "Young Sheldon" with Chuck Lorre.

chunks.title: Sheldon Cooper
chunks.text: Sheldon Lee Cooper, Ph.D., Sc.D.

chunks.title: Sheldon Cooper
chunks.text: , is a fictional character in the CBS television series "The Big Bang Theory" and "Young Sheldon", portrayed by actor Jim Parsons in "The Big Bang Theory" and Iain Armitage in "Young Sheldon".

chunks.title: Sheldon Cooper
chunks.text: For his portrayal, Parsons has won four Primetime Emmy Awards, a Golden Globe Award, a TCA Award, and two Critics' Choice Television Awards.

chunks.title: Sheldon Cooper
chunks.text: The childhood of the character is the focus of "Young Sheldon", the show being set in 1989, when 9-year-old Sheldon, who has skipped ahead four grades, starts high school alongside his older brother.

chunks.title: Margo Harshman
chunks.text: Margo Cathleen Harshman (born March 4, 1986) is an American actress known for her role as Tawny Dean on the Disney Channel series "Even Stevens".

chunks.title: Margo Harshman
chunks.text: She is also known for her role on "The Big Bang Theory" as Sheldon Cooper's assistant, Alex Jensen, and as Delilah Fielding on "NCIS".

chunks.title: Jim Parsons
chunks.text: James Joseph Parsons (born March 24, 1973) is an American actor.

chunks.title: Jim Parsons
chunks.text: He is known for playing Sheldon Cooper in the CBS sitcom "The Big Bang Theory".

chunks.title: Jim Parsons
chunks.text: He has received several awards for his performance, including four Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series and the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Television Series Musical or Comedy.

chunks.title: Young Sheldon
chunks.text: Young Sheldon (stylized as young Sheldon) is an American television sitcom on CBS created by Chuck Lorre and Steven Molaro.

chunks.title: Young Sheldon
chunks.text: The series is a spin-off prequel to "The Big Bang Theory" and follows the character Sheldon Cooper at the age of 9, living with his family in East Texas and going to high school.

chunks.title: Young Sheldon
chunks.text: Iain Armitage stars as young Sheldon, alongside Zoe Perry, Lance Barber, Montana Jordan, and Raegan Revord.

chunks.title: Young Sheldon
chunks.text: Jim Parsons, who portrays an adult Sheldon Cooper on "The Big Bang Theory", narrates the series and serves as an executive producer.

chunks.title: Euglossa bazinga
chunks.text: Euglossa bazinga is a euglossine bee species found in Brazil.

chunks.title: Euglossa bazinga
chunks.text: It is named after the catchphrase of the fictional character Dr. Sheldon Cooper from the television show "The Big Bang Theory".

chunks.title: Euglossa bazinga
chunks.text: It was previously misidentified as "Euglossa ignita", and is threatened with habitat loss.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: Damon Dark is an independent public access TV series and web series from Australia about a heroic and obsessive investigator of UFO incidents and other strange cases, created by Australian writer, actor and film maker Adrian Sherlock.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: Damon James Dark became a dedicated alien investigator after a close encounter during his teenage years.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: He is associated with both the secret service and friendly aliens, including a character called Vincent Kosmos (an alien time traveller) and Trans-Dimensional Control (an alien law enforcement agency).

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: The character of Damon Dark has appeared in a 5-week TV series on Community TV 31 in Melbourne Australia, a self-published novel ("Biodome") on Amazon's createspace platform and a long running web series on YouTube.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: He has also been involved in related web series "Young Damon Dark" and "Vincent Kosmos."

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: He has also been the focus of a one actor stage drama.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: The character of Damon Dark has been played by Adrian Sherlock, Bruce Hughes, Aiden Sherlock and Jack Knoll.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: Damon Dark is a loner, dresses in black, has a huge experience of aliens and their technology.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: Damon is characterized by his high intelligence, idealistic moral outlook and wry sense of humor.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: His best friend in the series is the long-suffering Gary Sutton, played by actor Robert Trott.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: Damon Dark began in 1999, with a five-part weekly series on Melbourne's Community TV 31, (although the pilot was shot in 1996 and the show had been in development since 1990) following a screening of a 65-minute version of the story "Maddox" at the 57th World Science Fiction Convention (Aussiecon Three) held in Melbourne.

chunks.title: Damon Dark
chunks.text: The series was later revived as a YouTube webseries which inspired several related webseries, including "The Young Damon Dark Adventures" in which the character is played as a teenager, and Vincent Kosmos, (created by and starring Chris Heaven, , an Italian actor and musician, about a renegade alien character who is a friend of Damon.

chunks.title: Penny (The Big Bang Theory)
chunks.text: Penny is a fictional character on the American CBS sitcom "The Big Bang Theory", portrayed by actress Kaley Cuoco.

chunks.title: Penny (The Big Bang Theory)
chunks.text: She is the primary female character in the series, befriending her across-the-hall neighbors Leonard Hofstadter (Johnny Galecki) and Sheldon Cooper (Jim Parsons), two physicists who work at the nearby California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

chunks.title: Penny (The Big Bang Theory)
chunks.text: Penny's lack of advanced education, but outgoing personality and common sense drastically contrast with the personalities of the primary male characters in the series, even though she is considered part of their group.

chunks.title: Penny (The Big Bang Theory)
chunks.text: She is the love interest of Leonard, with whom she maintains a brief romantic relationship during the third season, which is later resumed in the fifth season and culminates in an engagement at the end of the seventh season and a wedding at the start of season 9.

chunks.title: Penny (The Big Bang Theory)
chunks.text: Penny is the only main character of the show whose last name has not been revealed, although she has been occasionally referred to or addressed with the last name Hofstadter since her wedding.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The 2013–14 season of Division 1, the third tier of ice hockey in Sweden, organized by the Swedish Ice Hockey Association (SIHA), began on 11 September 2013.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The regular season concluded on 16 February 2014.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The following playoffs towards the qualifier to the second-tier league HockeyAllsvenskan began on 19 February 2014 and ended on 7 March 2014.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The qualifiers to Division 1 began on 2 March 2014 and ended on 26 March 2014.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The qualifier to HockeyAllsvenskan began on 13 March 2014 and ended on 5 April 2014.

chunks.title: 2013–14 Division 1 season (Swedish ice hockey)
chunks.text: The 2013–14 season was the last season the league was named "Division 1"; in April 2014, the league was renamed "Hockeyettan".

chunks.title: Patrick Mercer
chunks.text: Colonel Patrick John Mercer, OBE (born 26 June 1956) is an author and former British politician.

chunks.title: Patrick Mercer
chunks.text: He was Conservative shadow homeland security spokesman before being forced to resign by David Cameron in 2007 for making "unacceptable" racist remarks in an interview with "The Times".

chunks.title: Patrick Mercer
chunks.text: He was elected as a Conservative in the 2001 general election, until resigning the party's parliamentary whip in May 2013 following questions surrounding paid advocacy, and was an Independent MP representing the constituency of Newark in Parliament until his resignation at the end of April 2014 after the Standards Committee suspended him for six months for "sustained and pervasive breach of the house's rules".

chunks.title: Newark (UK Parliament constituency)
chunks.text: Newark is a constituency in Nottinghamshire, England.

chunks.title: Newark (UK Parliament constituency)
chunks.text: It is currently represented by Robert Jenrick of the Conservative Party, who won the seat in a by-election on 5 June 2014, following the resignation of Patrick Mercer in April 2014.

chunks.title: Sunday Night Football (AFL)
chunks.text: Sunday Night Football is an Australian sports broadcast series aired on the Seven Network on 28 April 1991 until 9 April 2000 and returned on 6 April 2014 until 29 June 2014 in VIC, SA, WA, TAS and on 7mate on 6 April 2014 until on 29 June 2014 in NSW & QLD.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: The 2014 season of the Indian Premier League, abbreviated as IPL 7 or Pepsi IPL 2014, was the seventh season of the IPL, established by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in 2007.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: The tournament featured eight teams, one fewer than in 2013 after the withdrawal of the Pune Warriors India, and was held from 16 April 2014 to 1 June 2014.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: The opening ceremony was held in the UAE on 15 April 2014.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: The Mumbai Indians were the defending champions, having won the 2013 season.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: Kolkata Knight Riders won the tournament, defeating Kings XI Punjab by 3 wickets with Manish Pandey declaring the man of the match in the final.

chunks.title: 2014 Indian Premier League
chunks.text: The average attendance was 31,750.

chunks.title: Newark mayoral election, 2014
chunks.text: The 2014 Newark mayoral election took place in Newark, the most populous city in New Jersey, USA, on May 13, 2014.

chunks.title: Newark mayoral election, 2014
chunks.text: The race was characterized as a contest between two candidates, Ras J. Baraka and Shavar Jeffries, both from Newark's South Ward.

chunks.title: Newark mayoral election, 2014
chunks.text: Elections for all seats on the nine member Municipal Council of Newark also took place.

chunks.title: Newark mayoral election, 2014
chunks.text: Luis A. Quintana, who had become Mayor of Newark following the resignation of Cory Booker, did not seek the seat.

chunks.title: Bishop of Bradford (diocese)
chunks.text: The Bishop of Bradford was, until 20 April 2014, the ordinary of the Diocese of Bradford, which covered the extreme west of Yorkshire and was centred in the city of Bradford where the bishop's seat ("cathedra") is located in the Cathedral Church of Saint Peter.

chunks.title: Bishop of Bradford (diocese)
chunks.text: The bishop's residence was "Bishopscroft" in Bradford.

chunks.title: Bishop of Bradford (diocese)
chunks.text: The office existed since the foundation of the see from part of the Diocese of Ripon in 1920 under George V.

chunks.title: Bishop of Bradford (diocese)
chunks.text: The last diocesan Bishop of Bradford was Nick Baines, from 21 May 2011 until 20 April 2014.

chunks.title: Bishop of Bradford (diocese)
chunks.text: Baines was on sabbatical from February 2014 until the dissolution of the diocese on Easter Day 2014, during which time retired bishop Tom Butler was acting diocesan Bishop of Bradford.

chunks.title: Ras J. Baraka
chunks.text: Ras J. Baraka (born April 9, 1970) is an American educator, author, and politician who is the 40th and current Mayor of Newark, New Jersey.

chunks.title: Ras J. Baraka
chunks.text: He was previously a member of the Municipal Council of Newark and the principal of the city's Central High School until he took an indefinite leave of absence to run for the 2014 Newark mayoral election, which he won on May 13, 2014.

chunks.title: Ras J. Baraka
chunks.text: Baraka was sworn in as the city's 40th mayor at ceremonies at the New Jersey Performing Arts Center on July 1, 2014 for a four-year term.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins (born 1957) is an American politician in Newark, New Jersey.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: on the Municipal Council of Newark.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: She had previously served from 1995 to 2006, and ran on the slate of Ras J. Baraka, a candidate in the 2014 Newark mayoral election, for the city's Central Ward.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: and faced incumbent Darrin Sharif in a run-off.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: Preliminary results released the night of the run-off election on June 10, 2014 showed that Chaneyfield-Jenkins won the seat.

chunks.title: Gayle Chaneyfield-Jenkins
chunks.text: She was sworn in on July 1, 2014.

chunks.title: Newark by-election, 2014
chunks.text: The Newark by-election was a by-election in the Newark constituency of the British House of Commons, which was held on 5 June 2014, following the resignation of Patrick Mercer.

chunks.title: Newark by-election, 2014
chunks.text: Conservative Robert Jenrick won the seat with a majority of 7,403.

chunks.title: Mitridate, re di Ponto
chunks.text: Mitridate, re di Ponto ("Mithridates, King of Pontus"), K. 87 (74a), is an early opera seria in three acts by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

chunks.title: Mitridate, re di Ponto
chunks.text: The libretto is by after Giuseppe Parini's Italian translation of Jean Racine's play "Mithridate".

chunks.title: La fille de Madame Angot
chunks.text: La fille de Madame Angot ("The Daughter of Madame Angot") is an opéra comique in three acts by Charles Lecocq.

chunks.title: La fille de Madame Angot
chunks.text: The French text was by Clairville, Paul Siraudin and Victor Koning.

chunks.title: Arsilda, regina di Ponto
chunks.text: Arsilda, regina di Ponto is a dramma per musica by Antonio Vivaldi.

chunks.title: Arsilda, regina di Ponto
chunks.text: The opera was first performed at the Teatro Sant'Angelo in Venice on 27 or 28 October 1716.

chunks.title: Anne de La Tour d'Auvergne
chunks.text: Anne de La Tour d'Auvergne (1496–1524) was sovereign Countess of Auvergne from 1501 until 1524, and Duchess of Albany by marriage to John Stewart, Duke of Albany.

chunks.title: Anne de La Tour d'Auvergne
chunks.text: In her marriage contract, she was called 'Anne de Boulogne fille de Jehan Comte de Boulogne et Auvergne.'

chunks.title: La jolie fille de Perth
chunks.text: La jolie fille de Perth "(The Fair Maid of Perth)" is an opera in four acts by Georges Bizet (1838–1875), from a libretto by Jules-Henri Vernoy de Saint-Georges and Jules Adenis, after the novel by Sir Walter Scott.

chunks.title: La jolie fille de Perth
chunks.text: Many writers have reserved severe criticism for the librettists for their stock devices and improbable events, while praising Bizet's advance on his earlier operas in construction of set pieces and his striking melodic and instrumental ideas.

chunks.title: La Fille de marbre
chunks.text: La Fille de marbre is a ballet-pantomime in 2 acts by Arthur Saint-Léon, with music by Cesare Pugni, premiered on 20 October 1847 at the Opéra de Paris.

chunks.title: Detroit (horse)
chunks.text: Detroit (24 February 1977 – 20 May 2001) was a French Thoroughbred racehorse and broodmare who won the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe in 1980.

chunks.title: Detroit (horse)
chunks.text: Unraced as a two-year-old, Detroit won her first four races in 1980 including the Prix Fille de l'Air, Prix Chloé and Prix de la Nonette.

chunks.title: Detroit (horse)
chunks.text: She was beaten when favourite for the Prix Vermeille before winning the Arc in record time.

chunks.title: Detroit (horse)
chunks.text: She remained in training as a four-year-old and won three more races including the Prix Foy.

chunks.title: Detroit (horse)
chunks.text: She was retired to stud where she produced the Arc de Triomphe winner Carnegie.

chunks.title: Teatro Regio Ducal
chunks.text: The Teatro Regio Ducal (Italian, "Royal Ducal Theatre") was the opera house in Milan from 26 December 1717 until 25 February 1776, when it was burned down following a carnival gala.

chunks.title: Teatro Regio Ducal
chunks.text: Many famous composers and their operas are associated with it, including the premieres of Mozart's "Ascanio in Alba", "Mitridate, re di Ponto", and "Lucio Silla".

chunks.title: Teatro Regio Ducal
chunks.text: The opera house also saw the premiere of Maria Teresa Agnesi Pinottini's "Ciro in Armenia" in 1753; one of the earliest successfully received operas by a female composer.

chunks.title: Teatro Regio Ducal
chunks.text: Variant forms such as "Regio-Ducal Teatro" and "Teatro Regio Ducale" are also seen.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: Louise Fitzjames was a 19th-century ballerina.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: She was born on 10 December 1809 in Paris, and danced at Paris Opera from 1832 to 1846.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: When Marie Taglioni dropped out of Meyerbeer's "Robert le diable" after a few appearances, Fitzjames took on Taglioni's role of the Abbess.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: She danced the Abbess over 230 times.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: She was criticized by poet Théophile Gautier for her emaciated appearance.

chunks.title: Louise Fitzjames
chunks.text: Other roles included those in "Le Dieu et la bayadere" and "La Jolie Fille de Gand" in 1842.

chunks.title: La dame blanche
chunks.text: La dame blanche ("The White Lady") is an opéra comique in three acts by the French composer François-Adrien Boieldieu.

chunks.title: La dame blanche
chunks.text: The libretto was written by Eugène Scribe and is based on episodes from no fewer than five works of the Scottish writer Sir Walter Scott, including his novels "The Monastery", "Guy Mannering", and "The Abbot".

chunks.title: La dame blanche
chunks.text: The opera has typical elements of the Romantic in its Gothic mode, including an exotic Scottish locale, a lost heir, a mysterious castle, a hidden fortune, and a ghost, in this case benevolent.

chunks.title: La dame blanche
chunks.text: The work was one of the first attempts to introduce the fantastic into opera and is a model for works such as Giacomo Meyerbeer's "Robert le diable" and Charles Gounod's "Faust".

chunks.title: La dame blanche
chunks.text: The opera's musical style also heavily influenced later operas like "Lucia di Lammermoor", "I puritani" and "La jolie fille de Perth".

chunks.title: Gaetano Donizetti
chunks.text: Domenico Gaetano Maria Donizetti (] ; 29 November 1797 – 8 April 1848) was an Italian composer.

chunks.title: Gaetano Donizetti
chunks.text: Along with Gioachino Rossini and Vincenzo Bellini, Donizetti was a leading composer of the "bel canto" opera style during the first half of the nineteenth century.

chunks.title: Gaetano Donizetti
chunks.text: Donizetti's close association with the bel canto style was undoubtedly an influence on other composers such as Giuseppe Verdi (1813–1901).

chunks.title: Mémoires (Berlioz)
chunks.text: The Mémoires de Hector Berlioz are an autobiography by French composer Hector Berlioz.

chunks.title: Mémoires (Berlioz)
chunks.text: First serialised in several contemporary journals including "Journal des Débats" and "Le Monde Illustré", their compilation into one book was completed on New Year's Day, 1865 and after much proof-reading, an initial printing of 1200 was carried out in July.

chunks.title: Mémoires (Berlioz)
chunks.text: After distributing some copies to certain friends, they were put aside until Berlioz died.

chunks.title: Mémoires (Berlioz)
chunks.text: After Berlioz's death in 1869, they were published in 1870.

chunks.title: Mémoires (Berlioz)
chunks.text: They provide an extremely colourful, if biased, account of Berlioz's life, and are invaluable to anyone with an interest in the artistic life of the time.

chunks.title: L'enfance du Christ
chunks.text: L'enfance du Christ (English: "The Childhood of Christ" ), Opus 25, is an oratorio by the French composer Hector Berlioz, based on the Holy Family's flight into Egypt (see Gospel of Matthew 2:13).

chunks.title: L'enfance du Christ
chunks.text: Berlioz wrote his own words for the piece.

chunks.title: L'enfance du Christ
chunks.text: Most of it was composed in 1853 and 1854, but it also incorporates an earlier work "La fuite en Egypte" (1850).

chunks.title: L'enfance du Christ
chunks.text: It was first performed at the Salle Herz, Paris on 10 December 1854, with Berlioz conducting and soloists from the Opéra-Comique: Jourdan (Récitant), Depassio (Hérode), the couple Meillet (Marie and Joseph) and Bataille (Le père de famille).

chunks.title: Hector Berlioz
chunks.text: Louis-Hector Berlioz (] (English: ); 11 December 1803 – 8 March 1869) was a French Romantic composer, best known for his compositions "Symphonie fantastique" and "Grande messe des morts" (Requiem).

chunks.title: Hector Berlioz
chunks.text: Berlioz made significant contributions to the modern orchestra with his "Treatise on Instrumentation".

chunks.title: Hector Berlioz
chunks.text: He specified huge orchestral forces for some of his works, and conducted several concerts with more than 1,000 musicians.

chunks.title: Hector Berlioz
chunks.text: He also composed around 50 songs.

chunks.title: Hector Berlioz
chunks.text: His influence was critical for the further development of Romanticism, especially in composers like Richard Wagner, Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov, Franz Liszt, Richard Strauss, and Gustav Mahler.

chunks.title: Roméo et Juliette (Berlioz)
chunks.text: Roméo et Juliette is a "symphonie dramatique," a large-scale choral symphony by French composer Hector Berlioz, which was first performed on 24 November 1839.

chunks.title: Roméo et Juliette (Berlioz)
chunks.text: The libretto was written by Émile Deschamps, and the completed work was assigned the catalogue numbers Op. 17 and H.79.

chunks.title: Roméo et Juliette (Berlioz)
chunks.text: It is based on Shakespeare's play "Romeo and Juliet"; it is regarded as one of Berlioz's finest works, and it is among the most original in form.

chunks.title: Roméo et Juliette (Berlioz)
chunks.text: The score is Berlioz's most comprehensive and detailed programmatic piece.

chunks.title: Il furioso all'isola di San Domingo
chunks.text: Il furioso all'isola di San Domingo "(The Madman on the Island of San Domingo)" is a "romantic melodramma" in two acts by the composer Gaetano Donizetti.

chunks.title: Il furioso all'isola di San Domingo
chunks.text: Jacopo Ferretti, who since 1821 had written five libretti for Donizetti and two for Rossini (including "La cenerentola"), had proposed the unusual subject and he was contracted to write the Italian libretto based on a five-act play of the same title by an unknown author in 1820, which "had been given in the same theatre [...] and which Donizetti had immediately loved".

chunks.title: Il furioso all'isola di San Domingo
chunks.text: However, as has been noted by Charles Osborne, the "ultimate derivation of both play and libretto is an episode in part 1 of "Don Quixote" by Miguel de Cervantes's published in 1605" which is the story of Cardenio and Lucinda.

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: The French composer Hector Berlioz made four attempts at winning the Prix de Rome music prize, finally succeeding in 1830.

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: As part of the competition, he had to write a cantata to a text set by the examiners.

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: Berlioz's efforts to win the prize are described at length in his "Memoirs".

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: He regarded it as the first stage in his struggle against the musical conservatism represented by the judges, who included established composers such as Luigi Cherubini, François-Adrien Boieldieu and Henri Montan Berton.

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: Berlioz's stay in Italy as a result of winning the prize also had a great influence on later works such as "Benvenuto Cellini" and "Harold en Italie".

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: The composer subsequently destroyed the scores of two cantatas ("Orphée" and "Sardanapale") almost completely and reused music from all four of them in later works.

chunks.title: Prix de Rome cantatas (Berlioz)
chunks.text: There was a revival of interest in the cantatas in the late 20th century, particularly "La mort de Cléopâtre", which has become a favourite showcase for the soprano and mezzo-soprano voice.

chunks.title: Berlioz (disambiguation)
chunks.text: Hector Berlioz (1803–1869) was a French Romantic composer.

chunks.title: American Opera Society
chunks.text: The American Opera Society (AOS) was a New York City based musical organization that presented concert and semi-staged performances of operas between 1951 and 1970.

chunks.title: American Opera Society
chunks.text: The company was highly influential in sparking and perpetuating the post World War II bel canto revival, particularly through a number of highly lauded productions of rarely heard works by Gioachino Rossini, Gaetano Donizetti, and Vincenzo Bellini.

chunks.title: American Opera Society
chunks.text: The AOS also presented many operas to the American public for the first time, including the United States premieres of Benjamin Britten's "Billy Budd", Giuseppe Verdi's "Giovanna d'Arco", George Frideric Handel's "Hercules" and Hector Berlioz's "Les troyens" to name just a few.

chunks.title: Eugenio Cavallini
chunks.text: Eugenio Cavallini (16 June 1806 — 11 April 1881) was an Italian conductor, composer, violinist, and violist.

chunks.title: Eugenio Cavallini
chunks.text: In 1833 he became first violinist of the orchestra at La Scala, a post he held through 1855.

chunks.title: Eugenio Cavallini
chunks.text: He also served as a conductor at La Scala, notably leading the world premieres of Gaetano Donizetti's "Lucrezia Borgia" (1833), Donizetti's "Gemma di Vergy" (1834), Donizetti's "Maria Stuarda" (1835), Saverio Mercadante's "Il giuramento" (1837), Mercadante's "Il bravo" (1839), Giuseppe Verdi's "Oberto" (1839), Verdi's "Un giorno di regno" (1840), Donizetti's "Maria Padilla" (1841), Verdi's "Nabucco" (1842), Verdi's "I Lombardi alla prima crociata" (1843), Verdi's "Giovanna d'Arco" (1845), Federico Ricci's "Estella di Murcia" (1846), and Domenico Ronzani's "Salvator Rosa" (1854).

chunks.title: Jay T. Wright
chunks.text: Jay T. Wright (born 1972) is an American filmmaker best known for showing in European video spaces and independent film festivals.

chunks.title: Jay T. Wright
chunks.text: His work synergizes theoretical math, science and art.

chunks.title: Jay T. Wright
chunks.text: The argument in much of his work is about the generic quality of all mechanically or digitally manufactured images and ability or lack of ability to communicate content.

chunks.title: Jay T. Wright
chunks.text: This tension acts, in many of his films, as a competing motive and sometimes in direct conflict with any idea of narrative.

chunks.title: Mother's Day (1980 film)
chunks.text: Mother's Day is a 1980 American horror film directed, co-written and produced by Charles Kaufman, brother of Troma Entertainment co-founder Lloyd Kaufman who served as an associate producer for the film.

chunks.title: Mother's Day (1980 film)
chunks.text: The plot focuses on a mentally abnormal mother and her two deranged sons capturing and torturing a trio of women camping within the woods.

chunks.title: Mother's Day (1980 film)
chunks.text: The film also contains elements of the satire and thriller genres.

chunks.title: List of Troma Team Video Titles
chunks.text: Troma Entertainment was founded out of the rubble of Lloyd Kaufman’s Armor Films in 1974 as a production company.

chunks.title: List of Troma Team Video Titles
chunks.text: In 1995, Kaufman and vice president Michael Herz formed Troma Team Video who would handle all of their distribution instead of going through a third company.

chunks.title: List of Troma Team Video Titles
chunks.text: Since 1995, they have been releasing Troma titles (including titles the company has bought since being formed and a mighty collection of older classics with The Roan Group) on DVD and virally.

chunks.title: List of Troma Team Video Titles
chunks.text: They started re-releasing their films on Blu-ray in 2010.

chunks.text: The First Turn-On!

chunks.title: The First Turn-On!
chunks.text: is a 1983 comedy film directed by Lloyd Kaufman and Michael Herz of Troma Entertainment.

chunks.title: The First Turn-On!

chunks.title: The First Turn-On!

chunks.title: The First Turn-On!
