chunks.title: Pat Swinney Kaufman
chunks.text: Patricia Swinney Kaufman (born 1950) is the executive director of the New York State Governor's Office for Motion Picture and Television Development and the deputy commissioner of Empire State Development.

chunks.title: Pat Swinney Kaufman
chunks.text: Kaufman is the former president of the Association of Film Commissioners International, where she still serves on the board of directors.

chunks.title: Pat Swinney Kaufman
chunks.text: She is the secretary for the Hamptons International Film Festival and has also acted in some films directed by her husband, Lloyd Kaufman, the co-founder of Troma Entertainment.

chunks.title: I Was a Teenage TV Terrorist
chunks.text: I Was a Teenage TV Terrorist (also known as Amateur Hour) is a 1985 comedy film directed by Stanford Singer and distributed by Troma Entertainment.

chunks.title: I Was a Teenage TV Terrorist
chunks.text: The film follows two bored teenagers, anarchic troublemaker Paul and aspiring actress Donna, as they use Paul's father's TV station to stage an elaborate bomb hoax and throw the media into a frenzy.

chunks.title: I Was a Teenage TV Terrorist
chunks.text: The film was produced by Susan Kaufman, the sister of Lloyd Kaufman, the president of Troma Entertainment.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Aiden Dillard is an American independent film director and artist.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: He is known for using surreal humor and camp (style) within the confines of low-budget film.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Aiden Dillard was born in Escondido, California, but grew up in Durham, North Carolina.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Aiden Dillard's feature films and video art often deals with contrasts between a rural and urban area, and high culture and low culture.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: While studying at Cooper Union in New York City on a full-tuition scholarship, his student film "The Battle of the Burps and Farts" was screened at TromaDance 2004 and was the only film in the history of the festival that was booed by everybody in attendance.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Upon graduation Aiden Dillard directed an outrageous psychedelic spoof of "Reefer Madness", titled "Meat Weed Madness", which featured set decoration by Joe Holtzman, the editor-in-chief of Nest (magazine), and crudely constructed props and stop-motion animation. "

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Meat Weed Madness" premièred at the Wolfsonian-FIU in December 2005 during Art Basel Miami Beach, and was released on DVD by Troma Entertainment in 2006.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: Aiden Dillard's even more outrageous sequel "Meat Weed America" was released by Troma Entertainment on DVD in the fall of 2007, and features Troma's president Lloyd Kaufman, Debbie Rochon, and Peter Stickles.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: In 2008, Aiden Dillard moved to Miami, and wrote, produced, and directed a psychedelic crime-drama about children with autism who see angels called "Special Angelz", which premiered at Borscht Film Festival.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: In 2009, Aiden Dillard wrote, produced, and directed an action-comedy spoof of "Death Wish" called "Death Print", which was set in the Miami art-world and shows an art dealer, played by Ted Vernon, who battles a Cuban Communist terrorist, with the help of musician Otto Von Schirach.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: This movie had a sold out premiere at the Colony Theatre in South Beach.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: From 2010-2012 Aiden Dillard performed in an art noise band, called Ballscarf, that incorporated video projections and Aiden Dillard's own nudity to produce an effect that was described as "nightmaris chaos".

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: In 2013, Aiden Dillard moved back to North Carolina and began to focus on visual art.

chunks.title: Aiden Dillard
chunks.text: In 2014 Troma Entertainment released Aiden Dillard's campy yet bloody slasher film "Bikini Swamp Girl Massacre" on DVD.

chunks.title: When Nature Calls
chunks.text: When Nature Calls is a 1985 spoof comedy written and directed by Charles Kaufman and starring Academy Award nominee David Strathairn in an early performance.

chunks.title: When Nature Calls
chunks.text: The film was distributed by Charles Kaufman's brother, Lloyd Kaufman, of Troma Entertainment (sister Susan Kaufman worked as an art director and their father Stanley appeared as an actor in the film).

chunks.title: Michael Herz (producer)
chunks.text: Michael Herz is an American film producer, director and screenwriter.

chunks.title: Michael Herz (producer)
chunks.text: With Lloyd Kaufman, the two are the co-founders of Troma Entertainment, the world's longest running independent film studio, known for their comedic horror films, including the cult favorite "Toxic Avenger series and "Tromeo and Juliet".

chunks.title: Lloyd Kaufman
chunks.text: Stanley Lloyd Kaufman, Jr. (born December 30, 1945) is an American film director, producer, screenwriter, and actor.

chunks.title: Lloyd Kaufman
chunks.text: With producer Michael Herz, he is the co-founder of Troma Entertainment film studio, and the director of many of their feature films, including "The Toxic Avenger" and "Tromeo and Juliet".

chunks.title: Panicum
chunks.text: Panicum (panicgrass) is a large genus of about 450 species of grasses native throughout the tropical regions of the world, with a few species extending into the northern temperate zone.

chunks.title: Panicum
chunks.text: They are often large, annual or perennial grasses, growing to 1–3 m tall.

chunks.title: Popgenie
chunks.text: Populus Genome Integrative Explorer (PopGenIE) is an integrated set of tools for exploring the genome and transcriptome of the model plant system "Populus".

chunks.title: Panicum lycopodioides
chunks.text: Panicum lycopodioides, common name false club-moss panic grass or (in French) panic faux-lycopode, is endemic to the French island of Réunion in the Indian Ocean.

chunks.title: Panicum lycopodioides
chunks.text: It is found at high altitudes on the island, at elevations over 2000 m (6700 feet).

chunks.title: Panicum lycopodioides
chunks.text: The highest point on the island is Piton des Neiges, 3069 m (10,230 feet).

chunks.title: Panicum lycopodioides
chunks.text: The plant requires full sun-light and a cold climate.

chunks.title: List of Panicum species
chunks.text: s of July 2014 the "World Checklist of Selected Plant Families" recognises about 450 accepted taxa (of species and infraspecific names) in the plant genus "Panicum".

chunks.title: Populus
chunks.text: Populus is a genus of 25–35 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.

chunks.title: Populus
chunks.text: English names variously applied to different species include poplar , aspen, and cottonwood.

chunks.title: Panicum turgidum
chunks.text: Panicum turgidum is an old world clumping desert bunchgrass of the "Panicum" genus.

chunks.title: Panicum turgidum
chunks.text: It is a plant of arid regions across Africa and Asia, and has been introduced to other parts of the world.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic virus
chunks.text: "Panicum mosaic virus" (PMV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA viral pathogen that infects plant species in the Panicoid tribe of the grass family "Poaceae".

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic virus
chunks.text: The pathogen was first identified in Kansas in 1953 and most commonly causes disease on select cultivars of turf grass, switchgrass, and millet.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic virus
chunks.text: The disease most commonly associated with the panicum mosaic virus pathogen is St. Augustine Decline Syndrome, which infects species of turf grass and causes chlorotic mottling.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic virus
chunks.text: In addition to St. Augustine Decline, panicum mosaic virus is responsible for chlorotic streaking and mild green mosaicking in select cultivars of switchgrass and millet.

chunks.title: Panicum capillare
chunks.text: Panicum capillare, known by the common name witchgrass, is a species of grass.

chunks.title: Panicum capillare
chunks.text: It is native plant to most of North America from the East Coast through all of the West Coast and California.

chunks.title: Panicum capillare
chunks.text: It can be found as an introduced species in Eurasia, and as a weed in gardens and landscaped areas.

chunks.title: Panicum capillare
chunks.text: It grows in many types of habitat.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic satellite virus
chunks.text: Panicum mosaic satellite virus (SPMV) is a plant satellite virus.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic satellite virus
chunks.text: It only infects grasses which are infected by Panicum mosaic virus.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic satellite virus
chunks.text: One study found that 72% of "Stenotaphrum secundatum" (St Augustine grass) infected with panicum mosaic virus was also infected with SPMV.

chunks.title: Panicum mosaic satellite virus
chunks.text: In addition to SPMV, many plants infected with panicum mosaic virus are also infected with satellite RNAs.

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: Echinochloa crus-galli is a type of wild grass originating from tropical Asia that was formerly classified as a type of panicum grass.

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: It is commonly known as cockspur (or cockspur grass), barnyard millet, Japanese millet, water grass, common barnyard grass, or simply "barnyard grass" (which may refer to any species of "Echinochloa" or the genus as a whole however).

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: This plant can grow to 60" (1.5 m) in height and has long, flat leaves which are often purplish at the base.

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: Most stems are upright, but some will spread out over the ground.

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: Stems are flattened at the base.

chunks.title: Echinochloa crus-galli
chunks.text: The seed heads are a distinctive feature, often purplish, with large millet-like seeds in crowded spikelets.

chunks.title: Leaps and Bounds (playplace)
chunks.text: Leaps and Bounds was a chain of indoor play-places that was started by McDonald's in 1991.

chunks.title: Leaps and Bounds (playplace)
chunks.text: It was merged with competitor Discovery Zone in 1995.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone is a park in Monroe, Connecticut, United States.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: Its mission is to provide excellence in outdoor education and to promote exploration and learning in a fun, hands-on environment as a prototype for the Federal No Child Left Inside initiative.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: The park covers 170 acre and has 3 loop trails, each with marked interpretive signs.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: There is also an outdoor classroom for schools and groups, and a scavenger hunt scorecard.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: The park provides additional educational resources for teachers, as well as programs for school groups, daycare centers, and scouts.

chunks.title: Webb Mountain Discovery Zone
chunks.text: The park is owned by the Town of Monroe and administered by the Friends of Webb Mountain.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: Herald House or Herald Publishing House is the publishing division of the Community of Christ in Independence, Missouri.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: It publishes books, periodicals and other materials at the direction of the First Presidency.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: Its history dates to the publication of a church periodical called the "True Latter Day Saints' Herald" in Cincinnati, Ohio in 1860.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: The first church-owned press was located in Plano, Illinois and a much larger facility was opened in Lamoni, Iowa in 1881.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: The publishing plant in Lamoni was destroyed by fire in 1907.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: A replacement facility was built shortly thereafter.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: When the church headquarters moved to Independence, Missouri in 1921, the Herald House was relocated to a facility that had previously been used by an artillery battalion of the Missouri National Guard.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: In 1965, a modern publishing facility was built for Herald House on Noland Road in Independence.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: That facility was closed in 1999 and printing has been outsourced since that date.

chunks.title: Herald House
chunks.text: The publishing offices were moved to The Temple and The Auditorium in Independence, Missouri.

chunks.title: Great Falls Tectonic Zone
chunks.text: The Great Falls Tectonic Zone is a major intracontinental shear zone between the Hearne craton and Wyoming craton basement rock of the Archean Eon which form part of the North American continent.

chunks.title: Great Falls Tectonic Zone
chunks.text: The zone is an area about 100 miles (150 km) wide extending from the southwestern Idaho-Montana border across Montana to the northwestern Montana-Saskatchewan-North Dakota border.

chunks.title: Great Falls Tectonic Zone
chunks.text: It is named for the Great Falls of the Missouri River, a major geologic feature of the area.

chunks.title: Great Falls Tectonic Zone
chunks.text: The central and western portions of the zone are believed to be about 1.1 to 3.3 billion years old.

chunks.title: Great Falls Tectonic Zone
chunks.text: The central part of the zone lacks Archean rock, however, leading at least one group of scientists to speculate that it was formed very late in the Paleoproterozoic Era.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: The University of North Texas Discovery Park Campus, formerly Research Park, is a satellite research facility of the University of North Texas.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: Discovery Park is located in Denton, Texas, north of the main campus, on U.S. Highway 77.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: In January 2004, the 550000 sqft facility, formerly occupied by Texas Instruments, opened to students from the UNT College of Engineering.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: In 2008, the newly formed College of Information joined the Discovery Park campus.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: The facility houses offices and labs for the Departments of Engineering Technology, Computer Science and Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical and Energy Engineering, Library and Information Science and Learning Technologies.

chunks.title: University of North Texas Discovery Park
chunks.text: The Center for Technology Development and Transfer (CTDT) began operations from Discovery Park in 2006.

chunks.title: Discovery Zone
chunks.text: Discovery Zone (DZ) was a chain of entertainment facilities featuring games and elaborate indoor mazes designed for young children, including roller slides, climbing play structures and ball pits.

chunks.title: Discovery Zone
chunks.text: It also featured arcade games.

chunks.title: Discovery Zone
chunks.text: The chain was founded by Ronald Matsch, Jim Jorgensen and Dr. David Schoenstadt in 1989.

chunks.title: Discovery Zone
chunks.text: The first location was opened in Kansas City, Missouri in October 1989.

chunks.title: Discovery Zone
chunks.text: An early investor and vocal supporter of the company was tennis player Billie Jean King.

chunks.title: Valentino's
chunks.text: Valentino's is a regional Italian restaurant chain based in Lincoln, Nebraska.

chunks.title: Valentino's
chunks.text: Valentino's was founded by Val and Zena Weiler in 1957.

chunks.title: Valentino's
chunks.text: The restaurant was purchased by two Lincoln families in 1971 and began franchising additional locations.

chunks.title: Valentino's
chunks.text: The first carry-out store opened in 1990, and many of the full-scale restaurants converted to the buffet concept in the early-2000s.

chunks.title: Valentino SpA
chunks.text: Valentino SpA is a clothing company founded in 1960 by Valentino Garavani.

chunks.title: Valentino SpA
chunks.text: It is a part of Valentino Fashion Group, which in turn is owned by the State of Qatar through Mayhoola for Investments S.P.C.

chunks.title: Valentino SpA
chunks.text: Since October 2008, the creative director is Pier Paolo Piccioli.

chunks.title: Valentino SpA
chunks.text: Alessandra Facchinetti was Valentino's creative designer from 2007 to 2008.

chunks.title: Valentino SpA
chunks.text: Valentino is headquartered in Milan,while the creative direction is in Rome.

chunks.title: Aliso Canyon Oil Field
chunks.text: The Aliso Canyon Oil Field (also Aliso Canyon Natural Gas Storage Field, Aliso Canyon Underground Storage Facility) is an oil field and natural gas storage facility in the Santa Susana Mountains in Los Angeles County, California, north of the Porter Ranch neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles.

chunks.title: Aliso Canyon Oil Field
chunks.text: Discovered in 1938 and quickly developed afterward, the field peaked as an oil producer in the 1950s, but has remained active since its discovery.

chunks.title: Aliso Canyon Oil Field
chunks.text: One of its depleted oil and gas producing formations, the Sesnon-Frew zone, was converted into a gas storage reservoir in 1973 by the Southern California Gas Company, the gas utility servicing the southern half of California.

chunks.title: Aliso Canyon Oil Field
chunks.text: This reservoir is the second-largest natural gas storage site in the western United States, with a capacity of over 86 billion cubic feet of natural gas.

chunks.title: Aliso Canyon Oil Field
chunks.text: Currently it is one of four gas storage facilities owned by Southern California Gas, the others being the La Goleta Gas Field west of Santa Barbara, Honor Rancho near Newhall, and Playa del Rey.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: The Missouri Theatre, is a concert and entertainment venue in downtown Columbia, Missouri, occupying most of a city block between 9th street between Locust and Elm Streets.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: It was designed after the Opéra Garnier by the Boller Brothers, built in 1928, and is on the National Register of Historic Places.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: It is Columbia's only surviving pre-Depression movie palace and vaudeville stage.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: In 2011, the University of Missouri began a three-year lease of the facility.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: The Missouri Theatre is the resident home of the Missouri Symphony Orchestra, and is also frequently used by University of Missouri and civic groups.

chunks.title: Missouri Theatre (Columbia, Missouri)
chunks.text: As of July 1, 2014, The University of Missouri took over ownership of the Missouri Theatre.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: This is a list of hospitals in North Carolina.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: There are 126 hospitals in 83 counties.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: Seventeen counties currently do not have a hospital.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: Duke University Hospital is currently the largest hospital, with 943 hospital beds.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: Vidant Bertie Hospital is currently the smallest, with six hospital beds.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: Charlotte has the highest concentration of hospitals, with seven.

chunks.title: List of hospitals in North Carolina
chunks.text: Four hospitals serve as university-affiliated academic medical centers: Duke University Hospital, Vidant Medical Center, UNC Health Care and Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center, while Carolinas Medical Center is unaffiliated.

chunks.title: MedStar Washington Hospital Center
chunks.text: MedStar Washington Hospital Center is the largest private hospital in Washington, D.C. A member of MedStar Health, the not-for-profit Hospital Center is licensed for 926 beds.

chunks.title: MedStar Washington Hospital Center
chunks.text: Health services in primary, secondary and tertiary care are offered to adult and neonatal patients.

chunks.title: MedStar Washington Hospital Center
chunks.text: It also serves as a teaching hospital for Georgetown University School of Medicine.

chunks.title: Banner University Medical Center Tucson
chunks.text: Banner - University Medical Center Tucson (BUMCT), formerly University Medical Center and the University of Arizona Medical Center, is a private, non-profit, 487-bed acute-care hospital located on the campus of the University of Arizona in Tucson, Arizona.

chunks.title: Banner University Medical Center Tucson
chunks.text: BUMCT is part of the University of Arizona Health Sciences (UAHS) center campus which includes the university's Colleges of Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and Public Health.

chunks.title: Banner University Medical Center Tucson
chunks.text: It is Southern Arizona's only Level I trauma center for both adult and pediatric patients.

chunks.title: Banner University Medical Center Tucson
chunks.text: BUMCT is one of two University of Arizona affiliated academic medical centers in Tucson with Banner - University Medical Center South (formerly Kino Community Hospital, University Physicians Healthcare Hospital, and University of Arizona Medical Center - South Campus) being the other such institution.

chunks.title: Banner University Medical Center Tucson
chunks.text: The area's only dedicated Children's hospital, Banner Children's at Diamond Children's Medical Center, is located within and adjacent to BUMCT.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital is one of the national capital area's oldest academic teaching hospitals.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: It is a not-for-profit, acute care teaching and research facility located in the Georgetown neighborhood of the Northwest Quadrant of Washington, D.C.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: MedStar Georgetown is co-located with the Georgetown University Medical Center and is affiliated with the Georgetown University School of Medicine.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: Its clinical services represent one of the largest, most geographically diverse, and fully integrated healthcare and delivery networks in the area.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: MedStar Georgetown is home to the internationally known Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center, as well as centers of excellence in the neurology, neurosurgery, psychiatry, gastroenterology, transplant and vascular surgery.

chunks.title: MedStar Georgetown University Hospital
chunks.text: Originally named Georgetown University Hospital, it became part of the MedStar Health network in 2000.

chunks.title: Children's National Medical Center
chunks.text: Children’s National Medical Center (formerly DC Children’s Hospital) is ranked among the top 10 children’s hospitals in the country by "U.S. News & World Report."

chunks.title: Children's National Medical Center
chunks.text: Located just north of the McMillan Reservoir and Howard University, it shares grounds with Washington Hospital Center, National Rehabilitation Hospital, and the DC Veterans Affairs Medical Center.

chunks.title: Children's National Medical Center
chunks.text: Kurt Newman, M.D., has served as the president and chief executive officer of Children’s National since 2011.

chunks.title: Children's National Medical Center
chunks.text: Children's National is a not-for-profit institution that performs more than 450,000 visits each year.

chunks.title: Children's National Medical Center
chunks.text: Featuring 303 beds and a Level IV NICU, Children's National is the regional referral center for pediatric emergency, trauma, cancer, cardiac and critical care as well as neonatology, orthopaedic surgery, neurology and neurosurgery.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center is a hospital located in Portland, Oregon, United States.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: It was founded in 1893 as Hahnemann Hospital.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: By 1947 the hospital had 100 beds, and that year it changed its name to Holladay Park Hospital with plans to expand to 200 beds.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: With a 1985 merger with Physicians & Surgeons Hospital (which had been known as Coffey Memorial Hospital until 1945), the name was changed to Holladay Park Medical Center.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: At that time both hospitals were part of Metropolitan Hospitals, Inc. that had been formed by Physicians & Surgeons Hospital and Emanuel Hospital.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: After becoming part of Legacy Health when it was formed in 1989, Legacy closed the then 171-bed hospital in 1994.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: As of 2014, the former hospital was used by Legacy as the Legacy Research Institute.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: Legacy proposed converting the building into an emergency room for psychiatric patients in 2014 after the Legacy Research Institute moved to a new building.

chunks.title: Legacy Holladay Park Medical Center
chunks.text: Legacy, Oregon Health & Science University, Adventist Health, and Kaiser Permanente agreed to operate the ER, with a planned opening in 2016.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: Providence Portland Medical Center, located at 4805 NE Glisan St. in the North Tabor neighborhood of Portland, Oregon, is a full-service medical center specializing in cancer and cardiac care.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: Opened in 1941, the hospital is licensed for 483 beds, and has over 3,000 employees.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: There are approximately 1,000 physicians on staff.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: The campus is also home to Providence Child Center, a 58-bed facility dedicated exclusively to medically fragile children.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: Providence Portland Medical Center is part of the Providence Health & Services in Oregon.

chunks.title: Providence Portland Medical Center
chunks.text: Providence Portland Medical Center is one of four nursing magnet hospitals in Oregon, the others being Providence St. Vincent Medical Center, Veterans Affairs hospital, and OHSU Hospital in Portland.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: Vassar Brother Medical Center (locally known as Vassar Hospital or VBMC) is a major medical facility located in the city of Poughkeepsie, New York that is a member of the Health Quest network, a nonprofit family of hospitals and healthcare centers in the Hudson Valley area.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: VBMC is one of two major medical centers located in Dutchess County, New York, the other being Mid-Hudson Regional Hospital of Westchester Medical Center.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: The hospital was first incorporated in 1882 under the name Vassar Brothers Hospital, following contributions made by John Guy Vassar following the death of his brother.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: The hospital opened its doors in 1887, and initially had 40 beds divided up into four wards, each containing ten beds.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: At the time the hospital opened it also contained a labor and delivery ward, a children's ward, a nursery, three private rooms, and two isolation rooms.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: Several major renovations occurred in 1983, 1991, and 2001; adding critical care areas, a new operating and delivery wing, and a cancer care center, respectively.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: In 2002 Vassar Brothers Hospital officially became Vassar Brothers Medical Center.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: In September 2016, VBMC announced a new $500 million expansion which would almost double the number of available rooms.

chunks.title: Vassar Brothers Medical Center
chunks.text: Construction on the expansion is expected to be completed in 2019.

chunks.title: Murphy Medical Center
chunks.text: Murphy Medical Center (MMC) is a hospital located in Murphy, North Carolina certified by the United States Department of Health and Human Services.

chunks.title: Murphy Medical Center
chunks.text: Murphy Medical Center is the only hospital west of Bryson City and Franklin.

chunks.title: Murphy Medical Center
chunks.text: MMC is licensed for 191 beds.

chunks.title: Murphy Medical Center
chunks.text: Of the 191 beds, 120 are nursing home beds, 57 are general beds, and 14 are alzheimers beds.

chunks.title: Brad Wenstrup
chunks.text: Brad Robert Wenstrup (born June 17, 1958) is an American politician, Army Reserve officer, and Doctor of Podiatric Medicine, who has been the U.S. Representative for Ohio 's 2 congressional district since 2013.

chunks.title: Brad Wenstrup
chunks.text: A Republican, he defeated U.S. Representative Jean Schmidt in the 2012 Republican primary election and Democrat William R. Smith in the 2012 general election.

chunks.title: Brad Wenstrup
chunks.text: Wenstrup is a colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve and an Iraq War veteran.

chunks.title: Brad Wenstrup
chunks.text: After the shooting of Congressman Steve Scalise on the morning of June 14, 2017, Wenstrup attended to the wounded congressman until he was transported to MedStar Washington Hospital Center.

chunks.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
chunks.text: Oz the Great and Powerful is a 2013 American fantasy adventure film directed by Sam Raimi and produced by Joe Roth, from a screenplay written by David Lindsay-Abaire and Mitchell Kapner.

chunks.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
chunks.text: The film stars James Franco, Michelle Williams, Rachel Weisz and Mila Kunis, with Zach Braff, Bill Cobbs, Joey King, and Tony Cox in supporting roles.

chunks.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
chunks.text: Based on L. Frank Baum's "Oz" novels and set 20 years before the events of the original novel, "Oz the Great and Powerful" is a spiritual prequel to the 1939 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer film, "The Wizard of Oz".

chunks.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
chunks.text: The film tells the story of Oscar Diggs, a deceptive magician who arrives in the Land of Oz and encounters three witches: Theodora, Evanora, and Glinda.

chunks.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
chunks.text: Oscar is then enlisted to restore order in Oz, while struggling to resolve conflicts with the witches and himself.

chunks.title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
chunks.text: The Marvelous Land of Oz: Being an Account of the Further Adventures of the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, commonly shortened to The Land of Oz, published on July 5, 1904 , is the second of L. Frank Baum's books set in the Land of Oz, and the sequel to "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz" (1900).

chunks.title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
chunks.text: This and the next 34 Oz books of the famous 40 were illustrated by John R. Neill.

chunks.title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
chunks.text: The book was made into an episode of "The Shirley Temple Show" in 1960, and into a Canada/Japan co-produced animated series of the same name in 1986.

chunks.title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
chunks.text: It was also adapted in comic book form by Marvel Comics, with the first issue being released in November 2009.

chunks.title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
chunks.text: Plot elements from "The Marvelous Land of Oz" are included in the 1985 Disney feature film "Return to Oz".

chunks.title: Compilation (The Clean album)
chunks.text: Compilation is a compilation cassette by New Zealand group The Clean.

chunks.title: Compilation (The Clean album)
chunks.text: It was released first time in 1986 by Flying Nun Records.

chunks.title: Compilation (The Clean album)
chunks.text: The album consists of early recordings, as well as songs from their 2 EPs, "Boodle Boodle Boodle" and "Great Sounds Great, Good Sounds Good, So-so Sounds So-so, Bad Sounds Bad, Rotten Sounds Rotten".

chunks.title: Compilation (The Clean album)
chunks.text: The CD version also contains 6 additional live tracks.

chunks.title: James Franco
chunks.text: James Edward Franco (born April 19, 1978) is an American actor, director, screenwriter, and producer.

chunks.title: James Franco
chunks.text: For his role in "127 Hours" (2010), Franco was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Actor.

chunks.title: James Franco
chunks.text: He is known for his roles in live-action films such as "Milk" (2008), "Pineapple Express" (2008), "Rise of the Planet of the Apes" (2011), "Spring Breakers" (2012), "Oz the Great and Powerful" (2013), "This Is the End" (2013), " The Disaster Artist" (2017), and Sam Raimi's "Spider-Man" trilogy, while also voicing characters in the animated films "The Little Prince" (2015) and "Sausage Party" (2016).

chunks.title: Deewana (1992 film)
chunks.text: Deewana (English: 'Crazy' ) is a 1992 Indian romantic drama film directed by Raj Kanwar, and produced by Guddu Dhanoa and Lalit Kapoor and featuring Shah Rukh Khan, Divya Bharti and Rishi Kapoor in the lead.

chunks.title: Deewana (1992 film)
chunks.text: This was Shah Rukh's debut release, and he appears only in the second half of the film.

chunks.title: Deewana (1992 film)
chunks.text: He replaced Armaan Kohli, who walked out of the project due to creative differences after the first schedule.

chunks.title: Deewana (1992 film)
chunks.text: The film released on June 25, 1992. "

chunks.title: Deewana (1992 film)
chunks.text: Dil Aashna Hai" was supposed to be the debut movie of Shahrukh Khan however "Deewana" was released first.

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: Toys in the Attic (Czech: Na půdě aneb Kdo má dneska narozeniny?

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: ; festival title: In the Attic: Who Has a Birthday Today?)

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: is a 2009 Czech-French-Japanese-Slovak primarily stop-motion animated fantasy comedy thriller family film directed by Jiří Barta and written by Edgar Dutka and Barta which depicts a community of toys and other objects in an attic who come to life when no human is around.

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: It is an international co-production of Czech, Japanese and Slovak companies.

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: The film was released first in the Czech Republic on 5 March 2009 and has been shown subtitled at film festivals internationally.

chunks.title: Toys in the Attic (2009 film)
chunks.text: An American dub – adapted, produced and directed by Vivian Schilling and performed by actors including Forest Whitaker, Joan Cusack, Cary Elwes and Schilling herself – has been recorded, which the film was first shown with on 3 March 2012 at the New York International Children's Film Festival and was released nationally on 24 August 2012 by Hannover House.

chunks.title: Game (2016 film)
chunks.text: Game in Kannada, Oru Melliya Kodu (English: A thin line) in Tamil, is a 2016 Indian bilingual language crime thriller film directed by A. M. R. Ramesh.

chunks.title: Game (2016 film)
chunks.text: This movie is an unofficial remake of the 2012 Spanish thriller El Cuerpo (Spanish title) also known as "The Body", and features Arjun Sarja, Shaam and Manisha Koirala in the lead roles.

chunks.title: Game (2016 film)
chunks.text: With music composed by Ilayaraaja, the film was simultaneously shot in Kannada and Tamil; the former released first on February 26, 2016 while the later released on July 1, 2016.

chunks.title: Game (2016 film)
chunks.text: The film was dubbed and released in Telugu as "Notuku Potu" in 2017.

chunks.title: Sneha (actress)
chunks.text: Suhasini Rajaram Naidu, popularly known by her stage name Sneha, is an Indian film actress, who works in the South Indian film industry.

chunks.title: Sneha (actress)
chunks.text: She debuted in the Malayalam film "Ingane Oru Nilapakshi" (2000), directed by Anil – Babu and was later signed for the Tamil film "Virumbugiren", though it was only released two years later.

chunks.title: Sneha (actress)
chunks.text: She started getting offers in Tamil and moved her focus to Kollywood, and the movie "Ennavale", where she starred opposite R. Madhavan, was released first in the same year.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: Snegithiye (English:Oh Friend! "

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: (female)" ) is a 2000 Tamil mystery thriller film directed by Priyadarshan.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: The story is loosely based on the 1999 Marathi film "Bindhaast" written by Chandrakant Kulkarni.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: The film notably features only female characters in the lead roles, played by Jyothika, Sharbani Mukherjee, Tabu and Ishita Arun.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: Music was composed by Vidyasagar.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: The film, released in 2000, proved to be an average grosser at the box office but bagged positive reviews from critics.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: Today, it is considered a cult classic that was underrated at the time of its release.

chunks.title: Snegithiye
chunks.text: Originally planned to be made as a bilingual, in Tamil and in Malayalam, the film released first in Tamil only, while the Malayalam dubbed version, "Raakilipattu", as well as the dubbed Hindi version, "Friendship", released seven years later.

chunks.title: Sacred Planet
chunks.text: Sacred Planet is a 2004 documentary directed by Jon Long and Hairul Salleh Askor.

chunks.title: Sacred Planet
chunks.text: Robert Redford provided narration for the film.

chunks.title: Sacred Planet
chunks.text: The film was released by Walt Disney Pictures on April 22, 2004, and grossed $1,108,356.

chunks.title: The Grotto (album)
chunks.text: The Grotto is the sixth solo album released by Kristin Hersh.

chunks.title: The Grotto (album)
chunks.text: It was released on 17 March 2003 on 4AD records, simultaneously with the Throwing Muses (2003) record.

chunks.title: The Grotto (album)
chunks.text: It features Howe Gelb on piano and Andrew Bird on violin.

chunks.title: The Grotto (album)
chunks.text: Kristin Hersh produced the album as well as playing all other instruments.

chunks.title: The Grotto (album)
chunks.text: The album peaked at #39 on the US's Billboard Top Independent Albums Chart.

chunks.title: In Shock
chunks.text: In Shock is the first single from Kristin Hersh's seventh solo album "Learn to Sing Like a Star".

chunks.title: In Shock
chunks.text: It was released in several versions by 4AD and Yep Roc Records.

chunks.title: In Shock
chunks.text: As well as the title track the single contains two new, previously unleashed Kristin Hersh tracks, "Windowpane" and "Blackstone" and the traditional song "Poor Wayfaring Stranger".

chunks.title: Mike Patton
chunks.text: Michael Allan "Mike" Patton (born January 27, 1968) is an American musician, singer, songwriter, actor, record producer, multi-instrumentalist and film composer, best known as the lead singer of the alternative metal band Faith No More.

chunks.title: Mike Patton
chunks.text: Patton was also the founder and lead singer of Mr. Bungle, and has played with Tomahawk, Fantômas, Lovage, The Dillinger Escape Plan, and Peeping Tom.

chunks.title: Throwing Muses
chunks.text: Throwing Muses is an alternative rock band formed in 1981 in Newport, Rhode Island, that toured and recorded extensively until 1997, when its members began concentrating more on other projects.

chunks.title: Throwing Muses
chunks.text: The group was originally fronted by two lead singers, Kristin Hersh, and Tanya Donelly, who both wrote the group's songs.

chunks.title: Throwing Muses
chunks.text: Throwing Muses are known for performing music with shifting tempos, creative chord progressions, unorthodox song structures, and surreal lyrics.

chunks.title: Throwing Muses
chunks.text: The group was set apart from other contemporary acts by Hersh's stark, candid writing style; Donelly's pop stylings and vocal harmonies; and David Narcizo's unusual drumming techniques eschewing use of cymbals.

chunks.title: Throwing Muses
chunks.text: Hersh's hallucinatory, febrile songs occasionally touched on the subject of mental illness, more often drawing portraits of characters from daily life or addressing relationships.

chunks.title: Red Heaven
chunks.text: Red Heaven is a 1992 album by the American alternative rock band Throwing Muses, released on Sire/Warner Bros.

chunks.title: Red Heaven
chunks.text: Records.

chunks.title: Red Heaven
chunks.text: Recorded at The Power Station and Fort Apache Studios following the departure of Tanya Donelly and Fred Abong, "Red Heaven" was recorded by Kristin Hersh and drummer David Narcizo with help from former bassist Leslie Langston.

chunks.title: Red Heaven
chunks.text: Former Hüsker Dü vocalist/guitarist Bob Mould took time off from his new band Sugar to record vocals for "Dio".

chunks.title: Red Heaven
chunks.text: Initial copies of the album came with the otherwise unavailable Kristin Hersh solo acoustic album "Live at Maxwell's Hoboken".

chunks.title: Strange Angels (Kristin Hersh album)
chunks.text: Strange Angels is Kristin Hersh's second studio album, produced by Kristin Hersh and co-produced by Joe Henry (except for "Like You" which was co-produced by Steve Rizzo).

chunks.title: Strange Angels (Kristin Hersh album)
chunks.text: The album peaked at #64 on the Official UK Albums Chart.

chunks.title: Strange Angels (Kristin Hersh album)
chunks.text: It also peaked at #40 on the US's Billboard Heatseekers Album Chart.

chunks.title: Strange Angels (Kristin Hersh album)
chunks.text: The album carried the dedication: "for Billy, Dylan, Ryder, Wyatt and TM (1984-97)".

chunks.title: Kristin Hersh
chunks.text: Kristin Hersh (born August 7, 1966) is an American singer, songwriter and author, known for her solo work and with her rock bands Throwing Muses and 50FootWave.

chunks.title: Kristin Hersh
chunks.text: She has released ten solo albums.

chunks.title: Kristin Hersh
chunks.text: Her guitar work and composition style ranges from jaggedly dissonant to traditional folk.

chunks.title: Kristin Hersh
chunks.text: Hersh's lyrics have a stream-of-consciousness style, reflecting her personal experiences.

chunks.title: Murder, Misery and Then Goodnight
chunks.text: Murder, Misery and Then Goodnight is Kristin Hersh's third solo album and quite a departure from her other solo recordings, in that it contains solely Appalachian folk songs about murder and death arranged by Kristin Hersh, rather than songs written by Kristin herself.

chunks.title: Murder, Misery and Then Goodnight
chunks.text: Hersh's son, Ryder James O'Connell, plays piano and sings backing vocals.

chunks.title: Sky Motel
chunks.text: Sky Motel is Kristin Hersh's fourth studio album.

chunks.title: Sky Motel
chunks.text: Vocals and most of the music are performed by Kristin Hersh.

chunks.title: Sky Motel
chunks.text: Drums on tracks 1, 5 & 7 are played by Carlo Nuccio who also provides a drum loop for track 8.

chunks.title: Sky Motel
chunks.text: Drum loops for tracks 3 & 11 are provided by David Narcizo.

chunks.title: Hips and Makers
chunks.text: Hips and Makers is the debut solo album by Kristin Hersh, best known as the primary singer and songwriter of the band Throwing Muses.

chunks.title: Hips and Makers
chunks.text: The album was released by 4AD in the UK on January 24, 1994, and by Sire Records in the US on February 1, 1994.

chunks.title: Hips and Makers
chunks.text: In contrast to Hersh's rock-oriented work with Throwing Muses, the album is primarily acoustic, with Hersh usually playing unaccompanied.

chunks.title: Hips and Makers
chunks.text: Other credited musicians include Jane Scarpantoni on cello and Michael Stipe of R.E.M., who sings backing vocals on the opening track, "Your Ghost."

chunks.title: Hips and Makers
chunks.text: In addition to Hersh's own material, the album features a cover of the traditional song "The Cuckoo".

chunks.title: Halophyte
chunks.text: A halophyte is a plant that grows in waters of high salinity, coming into contact with saline water through its roots or by salt spray, such as in saline semi-deserts, mangrove swamps, marshes and sloughs and seashores.

chunks.title: Halophyte
chunks.text: The word derives from Ancient Greek ἅλας (halas) 'salt' and φυτόν (phyton) 'plant'.

chunks.title: Halophyte
chunks.text: An example of a halophyte is the salt marsh grass "Spartina alterniflora" (smooth cordgrass).

chunks.title: Halophyte
chunks.text: Relatively few plant species are halophytes—perhaps only 2% of all plant species.

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus (LNYV) is a plant virus belonging to the virus order "Mononegavirales", family "Rhabdoviridae" and genus "Cytorhabdovirus".

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: It was first identified in Australia in the plant species "Lactuca sativa" in 1963 by Stubbs et al.

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: Since then it has been identified in many other plant species including "Datura stramonium" and "Nicotiana glutinosa".

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: The virus is transmitted by the insect vector "Hyperomyzus lactucae" the insect can become infected by feeding on an infected plant.

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: It then acts as a reservoir for the virus in which it can multiply.

chunks.title: Lettuce necrotic yellows virus
chunks.text: The virus is also transmitted congenitally to its progeny

chunks.title: Dacrydium
chunks.text: Dacrydium is a genus of conifers belonging to the podocarp family Podocarpaceae.

chunks.title: Dacrydium
chunks.text: Sixteen species of evergreen dioecious trees and shrubs are presently recognized.

chunks.title: Dacrydium
chunks.text: The genus was first described by Solander in 1786, and formerly included many more species, which were divided into sections A, B, and C by Florin in 1931.

chunks.title: Dacrydium
chunks.text: The revisions of de Laubenfels and Quinn (see references), reclassified the former section A as the new genus "Falcatifolium", divided Section C into new genera "Lepidothamnus, Lagarostrobos" and "Halocarpus", and retained Section B as genus "Dacrydium".

chunks.title: Flora of Western Australia
chunks.text: The flora of Western Australia comprises 10,252 published native vascular plant species and a further 1,245 unpublished species.

chunks.title: Flora of Western Australia
chunks.text: They occur within 1,543 genera from 211 families; there are also 1,276 naturalised alien or invasive plant species more commonly known as weeds.

chunks.title: Flora of Western Australia
chunks.text: There are an estimated 150,000 cryptogam species or nonvascular plants which include lichens, and fungi although only 1,786 species have been published, with 948 algae and 672 lichen the majority.

chunks.title: Flora of Lebanon
chunks.text: The flora of Lebanon" includes approximately 2,600 plant species.

chunks.title: Flora of Lebanon
chunks.text: Situated on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Basin", Lebanon is a reservoir of plant diversity and one of the world's Biodiversity hotspots for conservation priorities.

chunks.title: Flora of Lebanon
chunks.text: Endemic species constitute 12% of the Lebanese flora, 221 plant species are broad endemics and 90 are narrow endemics.

chunks.title: Centaurium
chunks.text: Centaurium (Centaury) is a genus of 20 species in the gentian family (Gentianaceae), tribe Chironieae, subtribe Chironiinae.

chunks.title: Centaurium
chunks.text: The genus was named after the centaur Chiron, famed in Greek mythology for his skill in medicinal herbs.

chunks.title: Centaurium
chunks.text: It is distributed across Europe and into Asia.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: The flora of India is one of the richest in the world due to the wide range of climate, topology and habitat in the country.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: There are estimated to be over 16,000 species of flowering plants in India, which constitute some 6-7 percent of the total plant species in the world.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: India is home to more than 45,000 species of plants, including a variety of endemics.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: The use of plants as a source of medicines has been an integral part of life in India from the earliest times.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: There are more than 3000 Indian plant species officially documented as possessing great medicinal potential.

chunks.title: Flora of India
chunks.text: India is divided into eight main floristic regions : Western Himalayas, Eastern Himalayas, Assam, Indus plain, Ganges plain, the Deccan, Malabar and the Andaman Islands.

chunks.title: Centaurium pulchellum
chunks.text: Centaurium pulchellum is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family known by the common name lesser centaury.

chunks.title: Centaurium pulchellum
chunks.text: It differs from "Centaurium erythraea" by lacking basal rosette of leaves and by having a developed peduncle below the flowers.

chunks.title: Centaurium pulchellum
chunks.text: It is often much smaller, less than ten centimetres.

chunks.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso
chunks.text: Burkina Faso is largely wild bush country with a mixture of grass and small trees in varying proportions.

chunks.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso
chunks.text: The savanna region is mainly grassland in the rainy season and semi desert during the harmattan period (defined as the period when stormy and dusty Sahara winds blow dry and hot).

chunks.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso
chunks.text: Fauna, one of the most diverse in West Africa, includes the elephant, hippopotamus, buffalo, monkey, lions, crocodile, giraffe, various types of antelope, and a vast variety of bird and insect life.

chunks.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso
chunks.text: The country has 147 mammal species, 330 aquatic species including 121 species of fish and 2067 different plant species.

chunks.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso
chunks.text: Of the plant species, the dominant endemic species are shea tree "(Butyrospermum parkii") and the baobab, the former plant species has immense economic value to the country.

chunks.title: Plant cover
chunks.text: The abundances of plant species are often measured by plant cover, i.e. the relative area covered by different plant species in a small plot.

chunks.title: Plant cover
chunks.text: Plant cover is not biased by the size and distributions of individuals, and is an important and often measured characteristic of the composition of plant communities.

chunks.title: Plant cover
chunks.text: Plant cover data may be used to classify the studied plant community into a vegetation type, to test different ecological hypothesis on plant abundance, and in gradient studies, where the effects of different environmental gradients on the abundance of specific plant species are investigated.

chunks.title: Black Velvet Flag
chunks.text: Black Velvet Flag was a New York City-based comedy music trio, known for their humorous, lounge-styled covers of songs by Southern California punk rock bands, and for performing while wearing tuxedos.

chunks.title: Black Velvet Flag
chunks.text: They became known in 1994, after performing on the New York music scene, which suddenly propelled them to fame in just six months.

chunks.title: Black Velvet Flag
chunks.text: Their only full-length album, "Come Recline", was released in 1995 on Go-Kart Records.

chunks.title: Black Velvet Flag
chunks.text: In 2003, an interactive documentary of the band, entitled "The Rise and Fall of Black Velvet Flag", was released; it was directed by Sheldon Schiffer.

chunks.title: Planter's Punch
chunks.text: Planter's Punch is an IBA Official Cocktail made of dark rum, several juices, grenadine syrup, sugar syrup, and Angostura bitters.

chunks.title: Velvet painting
chunks.text: A velvet painting is a type of painting distinguished by the use of velvet (usually black velvet) as the support, in place of canvas, paper, or similar materials.

chunks.title: Velvet painting
chunks.text: The velvet provides an especially dark background against which colors stand out brightly.

chunks.title: Black rose (symbolism)
chunks.text: Black roses are symbols featured in fiction with many different meanings and titles such as black velvet rose, black magic, barkarole, black beauty, Tuscany superb, black jade, and baccara.

chunks.title: Black rose (symbolism)
chunks.text: The roses commonly called black roses are technically a very dark shade of red, purple or maroon.

chunks.title: Black rose (symbolism)
chunks.text: The color of a rose may be deepened by placing a dark rose in a vase of water mixed with black ink.

chunks.title: Black rose (symbolism)
chunks.text: Other black roses may be blackened by other methods such as burning.

chunks.title: Edgar Leeteg
chunks.text: Edgar William Leeteg (April 13, 1904 East St. Louis, Illinois – February 7, 1953 Papeete, Tahiti) was an American painter often considered the father of American velvet painting.

chunks.title: Edgar Leeteg
chunks.text: He became a French citizen after immigrating to French Polynesia in 1933, where he spent the rest of his life painting the local life on black velvet.

chunks.title: Velvet Elvis
chunks.text: A Velvet Elvis is a painting of Elvis Presley on velvet.

chunks.title: Velvet Elvis
chunks.text: It typically represents a costumed torso of Elvis holding a microphone, painted on black velvet (or velvet of some other dark color, such as navy blue, red or purple).

chunks.title: Velvet Elvis
chunks.text: This iconic velvet painting is considered an archetypical example of kitsch.

chunks.title: Black Velvet (beer cocktail)
chunks.text: The Black Velvet is a beer cocktail made from stout (often Guinness) and white, sparkling wine, traditionally Champagne.

chunks.title: Bigger and Blackerer
chunks.text: Bigger and Blackerer: a 2010 album and DVD that stars American stand-up comedian David Cross.

chunks.title: Bigger and Blackerer
chunks.text: The album's title plays on Chris Rock's comedy album, "Bigger & Blacker", and the cover plays off of the popular art form of painting on black velvet, such as Velvet Elvis (and is reminiscent of the Ray Charles album "Ray Charles Greatest Hits").

chunks.title: Bigger and Blackerer
chunks.text: Cross taped and recorded the album during two shows at the Wilbur Theatre in Boston.

chunks.title: Black Velvet (magazine)
chunks.text: Black Velvet is a quarterly independent rock magazine based in the UK.

chunks.title: Black Velvet (magazine)
chunks.text: The zine originated in 1994 and is published/edited by Shari Black Velvet.

chunks.title: Black Velvet (magazine)
chunks.text: The zine includes in-depth interviews, CD, concert and zine reviews and more.

chunks.title: Black Velvet (magazine)
chunks.text: Sugarcult's Marko 72 also wrote a regular column for a while although now a different musician writes a column each issue.

chunks.title: Velvet (bus company)
chunks.text: Black Velvet Travel Limited, trading as Velvet, was an English bus company based in Eastleigh, that operated between November 2007 and January 2015.

chunks.title: Dev Hynes
chunks.text: David Joseph Michael Hynes (born December 23, 1985), better known as Devonté "Dev" Hynes or Blood Orange and formerly Lightspeed Champion, is a British singer, songwriter, composer, producer and author.

chunks.title: Dev Hynes
chunks.text: From 2004 to 2006, Hynes was a member of the band Test Icicles, playing guitar, synth, and occasionally performing vocals.

chunks.title: Dev Hynes
chunks.text: They released one full-length album in 2005.

chunks.title: Dev Hynes
chunks.text: Hynes went on to release two solo studio albums as Lightspeed Champion and subsequently three more as Blood Orange, between 2008 and 2016.

chunks.title: Dev Hynes
chunks.text: Dev has cited Prince, Hercules & The Love Affair and Gary Utteridge amongst his musical influences.

chunks.title: NLS Crew
chunks.text: NLS Crew was a short lived hip hop and thrash metal fusion group, formed as a spin-off from Test Icicles.

chunks.title: For Screening Purposes Only
chunks.text: For Screening Purposes Only is the debut album by UK dance-punk trio Test Icicles.

chunks.title: For Screening Purposes Only
chunks.text: After being released in 2005, the album was critically praised for being unique and compelling in an increasingly homogenous indie music scene.

chunks.title: For Screening Purposes Only
chunks.text: Following the group's split in February 2006, the album remains Test Icicles' only LP.

chunks.title: Test Icicles
chunks.text: Test Icicles were a short-lived dance-punk band that formed in England, primarily influenced by indie rock but containing musical elements from a variety of genres (notably hip hop, crossover thrash and punk).

chunks.title: Test Icicles
chunks.text: The band was formed in 2004 by Rory Attwell and Sam Mehran, who were later joined by Devonte Hynes.

chunks.title: Test Icicles
chunks.text: Hynes and Mehran were both 18 years old at the time of the band's inception.

chunks.title: Test Icicles
chunks.text: The group has since become notable due to the later success of its members.

chunks.title: The Ordinary Boys (album)
chunks.text: The Ordinary Boys is the self-titled fourth studio album by The Ordinary Boys released on 2 October 2015.

chunks.title: The Ordinary Boys (album)
chunks.text: The album has so far spawned the singles "Awkward" and "Four Letter Word".

chunks.title: The Ordinary Boys (album)
chunks.text: It was produced by Rory Attwell of Test Icicles and Matt Johnson of Hookworms.

chunks.title: Boa vs. Python (song)
chunks.text: "Boa vs. Python" is a song by Test Icicles which was released as the first single from their debut album "For Screening Purposes Only".

chunks.title: Boa vs. Python (song)
chunks.text: It was released on the 1 August 2005.

chunks.title: Boa vs. Python (song)
chunks.text: The song peaked at #46 in the UK Singles Chart.

chunks.title: Dig Your Own Grave
chunks.text: Dig Your Own Grave was a CD/DVD EP released on 23 April 2006 by Test Icicles.

chunks.title: Dig Your Own Grave

chunks.title: Noori

chunks.title: Noori
chunks.text: Since the inception of the band, there had been many changes in the line-up; the only consistent members being, brothers, Ali Noor and Ali Hamza.

chunks.text: During their time together they released the album "For Screening Purposes Only", and had UK Top 40 singles with "What's Your Damage" and "Circle.
