chunks.title: Connie Sachs
chunks.text: Connie Sachs is a fictional character created by John le Carré.

chunks.title: Connie Sachs
chunks.text: Sachs plays a key supporting role in le Carré's "Karla Trilogy" of spy novels including "Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy"; "The Honourable Schoolboy"; and "Smiley's People".

chunks.title: Call for the Dead
chunks.text: Call for the Dead is John le Carré's first novel, published in 1961.

chunks.title: Call for the Dead
chunks.text: It introduces George Smiley, the most famous of le Carré's recurring characters, in a story about East German spies inside Great Britain.

chunks.title: Call for the Dead
chunks.text: It also introduces a fictional version of British Intelligence, called "the Circus" because of its location in Cambridge Circus, that is apparently based on MI6 and that recurs throughout le Carré's spy novels.

chunks.title: John le Carré
chunks.text: David John Moore Cornwell (born 19 October 1931), known by the pseudonym John le Carré ( ), is a British author of espionage novels.

chunks.title: John le Carré
chunks.text: During the 1950s and the 1960s, he worked for both the Security Service and the Secret Intelligence Service, and began writing novels under his pen name.

chunks.title: John le Carré
chunks.text: His third novel, "The Spy Who Came in from the Cold" (1963), became an international best-seller and remains one of his best-known works.

chunks.title: John le Carré
chunks.text: Following the success of this novel, he left MI6 to become a full-time author.

chunks.title: Spy film
chunks.text: The spy film genre deals with the subject of fictional espionage, either in a realistic way (such as the adaptations of John le Carré) or as a basis for fantasy (such as many James Bond films).

chunks.title: Spy film
chunks.text: Many novels in the spy fiction genre have been adapted as films, including works by John Buchan, le Carré, Ian Fleming (Bond) and Len Deighton.

chunks.title: Spy film
chunks.text: It is a significant aspect of British cinema, with leading British directors such as Alfred Hitchcock and Carol Reed making notable contributions and many films set in the British Secret Service.

chunks.title: Control (fictional character)
chunks.text: Control is a fictional character created by John le Carré.

chunks.title: Control (fictional character)
chunks.text: Control is an intelligence officer who acts as the head of "the Circus", the British overseas intelligence agency.

chunks.title: Control (fictional character)
chunks.text: He is a character in the novels "The Spy Who Came in from the Cold", "The Looking Glass War", and "Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy", and is referred to in several others, usually by association with le Carré's recurring protagonist George Smiley, who has served as Control's right-hand man.

chunks.title: The Deadly Affair
chunks.text: The Deadly Affair is a 1966 British espionage–thriller film, based on John le Carré's first novel "Call for the Dead".

chunks.title: The Deadly Affair
chunks.text: The film stars James Mason, Harry Andrews, Simone Signoret and Maximilian Schell and was directed by Sidney Lumet from a script by Paul Dehn.

chunks.title: The Deadly Affair
chunks.text: In it George Smiley, the central character of the novel and many other le Carré books, is renamed Charles Dobbs as Paramount, which owned the film rights of their recently filmed "The Spy Who Came in from the Cold", had the rights to the Smiley character.

chunks.title: The Deadly Affair
chunks.text: The soundtrack was composed by Quincy Jones, and the bossa nova theme song, "Who Needs Forever", is performed by Astrud Gilberto.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: Joseph Hone (February 25, 1937 – August 15, 2016) was an Irish writer of the spy novel.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: His most famous novels featured a British spy called Peter Marlow.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: The first of the series was "The Private Sector" (1971), set in the Six Day War.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: Marlow's story continues in "The Sixth Directorate" (1975), "The Flowers of the Forest" (a.k.a. "The Oxford Gambit") (1980), and "The Valley of the Fox" (1982).

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: During his heyday, in the 1970s, Hone was favourably compared with writers such as Len Deighton, Eric Ambler and John le Carré.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: Whilst some spy novels, such as those of le Carré are often set mainly inside the offices of the spy department, and attract praise for the depth of their characterization and plotting, others (such as the James Bond series) are set in the field, and provide explosive action.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: Joseph Hone's stories by contrast, have a foot in both camps, and he has become renowned amongst aficionados of the spy genre for both the quality of his writing, and the excitement of his plots.

chunks.title: Joseph Hone
chunks.text: He released his memoir, "Wicked Little Joe" in 2009.

chunks.title: Hart Crane
chunks.text: Harold Hart Crane (July 21, 1899 – April 27, 1932) was an American poet.

chunks.title: Hart Crane
chunks.text: Finding both inspiration and provocation in the poetry of T. S. Eliot, Crane wrote modernist poetry that was difficult, highly stylized, and ambitious in its scope.

chunks.title: Hart Crane
chunks.text: In his most ambitious work, "The Bridge", Crane sought to write an epic poem, in the vein of "The Waste Land", that expressed a more optimistic view of modern, urban culture than the one that he found in Eliot's work.

chunks.title: Hart Crane
chunks.text: In the years following his suicide at the age of 32, Crane has been hailed by playwrights, poets, and literary critics alike (including Robert Lowell, Derek Walcott, Tennessee Williams, and Harold Bloom), as being one of the most influential poets of his generation.

chunks.title: John le Carré: The Biography
chunks.text: John le Carré: The Biography is a 2015 biography of John le Carré written by Adam Sisman and published by Harper.

chunks.title: Bill Haydon
chunks.text: Bill Haydon is a fictional character created by John le Carré in le Carré's "Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy".

chunks.title: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes
chunks.text: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes is a 1969 American comedy film starring Kurt Russell, Cesar Romero, Joe Flynn and William Schallert.

chunks.title: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes
chunks.text: It was produced by Walt Disney Productions and distributed by Buena Vista Distribution Company as part of "The Last Laughs of the 1960s".

chunks.title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
chunks.text: National Treasure: Book of Secrets (released on home video as National Treasure 2: Book of Secrets) is a 2007 mystery adventure film directed by Jon Turteltaub and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer.

chunks.title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
chunks.text: It is a sequel to the 2004 film "National Treasure" and is the second part of the "National Treasure" franchise.

chunks.title: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
chunks.text: The film stars Nicolas Cage, Diane Kruger, Justin Bartha, Jon Voight, Harvey Keitel, Ed Harris, Bruce Greenwood, and Helen Mirren.

chunks.title: Medfield College
chunks.text: Medfield College is a fictitious university used as the setting for several films by The Walt Disney Company.

chunks.title: Medfield College
chunks.text: Among them are the two "Professor Brainard" movies, "The Absent-Minded Professor" (1961) and "Son of Flubber" (1963); and the "Dexter Reilly" trilogy: "The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes" (1969), "Now You See Him, Now You Don't" (1972), and "The Strongest Man in the World" (1975); as well as the remake of "The Absent-Minded Professor", "Flubber" (1997).

chunks.title: Sneakers
chunks.text: Sneakers (also known as athletic shoes, tennis shoes, gym shoes, runners, takkies, or trainers) are shoes primarily designed for sports or other forms of physical exercise, but which are now also often used for everyday wear.

chunks.title: Sneakers
chunks.text: The term generally describes a type of footwear with a flexible sole made of rubber or synthetic material and an upper part made of leather or synthetic materials.

chunks.title: Sneakers
chunks.text: Examples of such shoes include athletic footwear such as: basketball shoes, tennis shoes, cross trainers and other shoes worn for specific sports.

chunks.title: PAJ animation studio
chunks.text: PAJ animation studio is a persian animation film studio based in IRAN.

chunks.title: PAJ animation studio
chunks.text: The studio produced several short films, television commercials, and one feature film.

chunks.title: PAJ animation studio
chunks.text: It was founded on 30 October 2007.

chunks.title: PAJ animation studio
chunks.text: PAJ animation studio produced a mini series called the hidden lives in 2017 .

chunks.title: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes (1995 film)
chunks.text: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes is a 1995 American made-for-television comedy science fiction film and a remake of the 1969 film of the same name produced by Walt Disney Television which premiered on February 18, 1995 as part of "The Wonderful World of Disney".

chunks.title: The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes (1995 film)
chunks.text: It is the second in a series of four remakes of classic Disney films produced for broadcast on ABC during the 1994–95 television season.

chunks.title: The Strongest Man in the World
chunks.text: The Strongest Man in the World is a 1975 Disney film starring Kurt Russell, still a student in the fictional Medfield College.

chunks.title: The Strongest Man in the World
chunks.text: It is the sequel to the 1972 film "Now You See Him, Now You Don't", itself a sequel to the 1969 film, "The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes".

chunks.title: National Treasure (film)
chunks.text: National Treasure is a 2004 American adventure heist film produced and released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: National Treasure (film)
chunks.text: It was written by Jim Kouf and the Wibberleys, produced by Jerry Bruckheimer and directed by Jon Turteltaub.

chunks.title: National Treasure (film)
chunks.text: It is the first film in the "National Treasure" franchise and stars Nicolas Cage, Harvey Keitel, Jon Voight, Diane Kruger, Sean Bean, Justin Bartha and Christopher Plummer.

chunks.title: Now You See Him, Now You Don't
chunks.text: Now You See Him, Now You Don't is a 1972 Walt Disney Productions film starring Kurt Russell as a chemistry student who accidentally discovers the secret to invisibility.

chunks.title: Now You See Him, Now You Don't
chunks.text: It is the sequel to the 1969 film "The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes" and was followed by 1975's "The Strongest Man in the World".

chunks.title: Celebration of Annihilation
chunks.text: Celebration of Annihilation was one of five singles Servotron released in 1996.

chunks.title: Celebration of Annihilation
chunks.text: It was released orange vinyl and black vinyl on Eastside Records.

chunks.title: Celebration of Annihilation
chunks.text: "The Computer Wore Tennis Shoes" is about the 1969 Disney film starring Kurt Russell, later remade for TV with Kirk Cameron.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: Flat Rock is a historic African American community in DeKalb County, Georgia.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: It is located within the city of Lithonia, as well as the Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: Flat Rock is believed to be the oldest African American settlement in DeKalb County and one of the oldest in Georgia.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: It began as an agricultural community bounded by the large South, Lyon, and Johnson farms.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: After emancipation, many former slaves stayed in the area, building schools, churches, and civic organizations.

chunks.title: Flat Rock, Georgia
chunks.text: The community remained intact through The Great Migration and is the site of Flat Rock Archives and a historic cemetery.

chunks.title: John Markowitz
chunks.text: John C. Markowitz (born 1954 in New York City) is an American physician, a Professor of Clinical Psychiatry at the Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons and a Psychiatric Researcher at the New York State Psychiatric Institute.

chunks.title: John Markowitz
chunks.text: For several decades he has conducted research on psychotherapies and medications as treatments for mood disorders (major depressive disorder and dysthymic disorder), anxiety disorders, and personality disorders.

chunks.title: John Markowitz
chunks.text: He is currently conducting an outcome study of three psychotherapies for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) thanks to a five year grant from the National Institute of Mental Health.

chunks.title: John Markowitz
chunks.text: He is most widely published in the area of interpersonal psychotherapy or IPT, a manualized form of treatment, in which he was trained by the late Gerald L. Klerman, M.D. Dr. Markowitz is a graduate of Columbia University and Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons and received his psychiatric residency training at the Payne Whitney Psychiatric Clinic of Cornell University Medical School/New York-Presbyterian Hospital.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Nellie Louise Young (June 7, 1907 - September 22, 1997) was the first African American woman licensed to practice medicine in Maryland.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Young was born in Baltimore, Maryland, to Dr. Howard E. Young, Maryland's first African American pharmacist, and Estelle Hall Young.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Her father's pharmacy served as a place of inspiration for Young as a child:"I admired the doctors...and I wanted to be able to send my prescriptions to my father's drugstore.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: "She attended the old Colored High School (now Fredrick Douglass High School) in Baltimore.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Following her graduation in 1924, Young enrolled in Howard University where she earned her bachelor of science degree in social sciences and later obtained her medical degree from the Howard University School of Medicine in 1930.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Young initially served as an intern at Freedmen’s Hospital in Washington, D.C., after she was not accepted to the Provident Hospital in Baltimore due to the lack of housing accommodations for women.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: After her internship, Young opened her own practice in offices above her father's drugstore in 1932.

chunks.title: N. Louise Young
chunks.text: Around the same time, she was appointed staff physician at the Maryland Training School for Girls, where she served from 1933-1940.

chunks.title: Museum Ovartaci
chunks.text: Museum Ovartaci in Aarhus, Denmark is a combined art and historical museum dedicated to the history of psychiatric treatment and art produced by patients at the Risskov Psychiatric Hospital.

chunks.title: Museum Ovartaci
chunks.text: It is a part of Aarhus University Hospital and resides in the same buildings as the Psychiatric Hospital in Risskov.

chunks.title: Museum Ovartaci
chunks.text: The museum also offers social programmes directed at psychiatric patients, including an open atelier, creative workshops and a café.

chunks.title: New York State Psychiatric Institute
chunks.text: The New York State Psychiatric Institute, located in the Columbia University Medical Center in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, was established in 1895 as one of the first institutions in the United States to integrate teaching, research and therapeutic approaches to the care of patients with mental illnesses.

chunks.title: New York State Psychiatric Institute
chunks.text: In 1925, the Institute affiliated with Presbyterian Hospital, now New York-Presbyterian Hospital, adding general hospital facilities to the Institute's psychiatric services and research laboratories.

chunks.title: Howard University Hospital
chunks.text: Howard University Hospital, previously known as Freedmen's Hospital, is a major hospital lcated in Washington, D.C., built on the site of the previous Griffith Stadium.

chunks.title: Howard University Hospital
chunks.text: The hospital has served the African American community in the area for over 150 years, having been established in 1862 to cater for the medical needs of the thousands of African Americans who came to Washington during the Civil War, seeking their freedom.

chunks.title: Howard University Hospital
chunks.text: The first hospital of its kind to provide medical treatment for former slaves, it later became the major hospital for the area's African-American community.

chunks.title: Howard University Hospital
chunks.text: Following the closure of D.C. General Hospital, As of 2016, the hospital has the highest rate of wrongful death lawsuits of any health facility in Washington D.C. over the previous decade.

chunks.title: Psychiatric Institute of Washington
chunks.text: The Psychiatric Institute of Washington (PIW) is an acute (104 bed) psychiatric hospital in Washington, D.C. Opened in 1967, PIW is a short-term, private hospital.

chunks.title: Psychiatric Institute of Washington
chunks.text: It offers behavioral healthcare to patients suffering from mental and addictive illnesses, including children, adolescents, adults and the elderly.

chunks.title: Psychiatric Institute of Washington
chunks.text: Services offered by PIW include inpatient, partial and intensive outpatient hospitalization, and group treatment programs for substance abuse and addiction.

chunks.title: The New Freedmen's Clinic
chunks.text: The New Freedmen's Clinic (first opened in the summer of 2009) is a free student-run health care clinic affiliated with Howard University Hospital (HUH) and Howard University College of Medicine (HUCM).

chunks.title: The New Freedmen's Clinic
chunks.text: It gets its name from HUH's original name - Freedmen's Hospital.

chunks.title: The New Freedmen's Clinic
chunks.text: It is currently located in the heart of Washington, DC, within HUH.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: University Hospital Limerick (formerly known as Limerick Regional Hospital or Mid-Western Regional Hospital, Limerick) is a hospital located in Dooradoyle, Limerick, Ireland.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: It is managed by the Irish Government's Health Service Executive and provides acute-care hospital services, including a 24-hour emergency department, for the population of Ireland's Mid West Region, encompassing; counties Limerick, Clare, North Tipperary, and South Tipperary.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: In 2008, the hospital served 120,316 out-patients, and 23,014 in-patients, with an average stay of 5.8 nights.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: 72.8% of admissions were made via the accident and emergency department or 16,720 patients.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: In total, 56,528 patients presented to the emergency department in 2008.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: The hospital saw 20,143-day cases in the same year.

chunks.title: University Hospital Limerick
chunks.text: In July 2011, it was reported that the hospital would undergo its third name change in five years to become University Hospital Limerick following the establishment of the Graduate Medical School at the University of Limerick which is affiliated to the hospital.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: Charles DeWitt Watts (September 21, 1917 – July 12, 2004) was an African American surgeon and activist for the poor.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: Watts was the first surgeon of African American ancestry in North Carolina.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: Earning his medical degree in 1943 from Howard University College, he was the first African American board certified surgeon to serve in North Carolina.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: After surgical training at Freedman's Hospital in Washington, D.C. in 1949, he moved to Durham, North Carolina in 1950 and established a clinic to provide access to medical services for the poor.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: Breaking the social customs of racial obstacles, he advocated for certification of African American medical students.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: He also became a member of many professional colleges including the National Academy of Science's Institute of Medicine and the American College of Surgeons.

chunks.title: Charles DeWitt Watts
chunks.text: He served as chief of surgery at Durham's Lincoln Hospital and was later one of the key figures in converting it to the Lincoln Community Health Center, a low-priced clinic for the poor.

chunks.title: Bruce Rowland
chunks.text: Bruce Rowland (born May 9, 1942 in Melbourne) is a well-known Australian composer.

chunks.title: Bruce Rowland
chunks.text: He composed the soundtrack for the 1982 movie "The Man from Snowy River", as well as the soundtrack for its 1988 sequel "The Man from Snowy River II" (which has the United States title of "Return to Snowy River", and the United Kingdom title of "The Untamed").

chunks.title: Bruce Rowland
chunks.text: Both films were based on Banjo Paterson's poem The Man from Snowy River.

chunks.title: Bruce Rowland
chunks.text: His other film scores include "Now and Forever" (1983), "Phar Lap" (1983), "Bushfire Moon" (1987), "Cheetah" (1989), "Weekend with Kate" (1990), "Gross Misconduct" (1993), "Andre" (1994), "Lightning Jack" (1994), "Zeus and Roxanne" (1997) and the TV movie "" (1997).

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (soundtrack)
chunks.text: "The Man from Snowy River is the original motion picture soundtrack from the 1982 film "The Man from Snowy River".

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Dangal (English: "Wrestling competition" ) is a 2016 Indian Hindi-language biographical sports drama film loosely based on the story of Mahavir Singh Phogat, an amateur wrestler, who trains his daughters Geeta Phogat and Babita Kumari to be world-class wrestlers.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: It was directed by Nitesh Tiwari.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Produced by Walt Disney Pictures, Aamir Khan Productions and UTV Motion Pictures, it stars Aamir Khan as the father.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Both daughters go on to win medals at the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Babita won a silver medal at the Games, in the 51 kg class and gold at the 2014 Glasgow Games in the 55 kg class.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: In 2012, Geeta became the first Indian female wrestler to qualify for the Olympics.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Mahavir's efforts inspired dozens of Indian women to take to wrestling.

chunks.title: Dangal (film)
chunks.text: Fatima Sana Shaikh and Sanya Malhotra play the older selves of the sisters while Sakshi Tanwar plays their mother and Aparshakti Khurana, their cousin.

chunks.title: Return to Snowy River
chunks.text: Return to Snowy River is the original motion picture soundtrack from the 1988 film "The Man from Snowy River II".

chunks.title: Return to Snowy River
chunks.text: The soundtrack album is named after the American title for the film.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: The Barry Way is a partly unsealed alpine road running from Jindabyne southwest to the Victorian border, where it becomes the Snowy River Road.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: It eventually leads to Buchan, a total distance of 170 kilometres with no services or towns.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: It is sealed for the first 27 kilometres from Jindabyne, becoming unsealed at Ingebirah Gap, remaining so as far as the Victorian border.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: The road passes through some very remote and unspoilt wilderness in the Australian Alps.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: The scenery along the road provides views of the Snowy River valley and the surrounding mountains.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: There are a number of campsites along the road, from Jacobs River southwards.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: During the summer months, the weather on the Barry Way can be extremely hot and the sun's rays powerful whilst in winter the road can be closed for considerable amounts of time due to heavy snowfalls and dangerous ice.

chunks.title: Barry Way
chunks.text: At the NSW/VIC border, the Barry Way becomes known as Snowy River Road and continues southward into the Gippsland region of Victoria.

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (poem)
chunks.text: "The Man from Snowy River" is a poem by Australian bush poet Banjo Paterson.

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (poem)
chunks.text: It was first published in "The Bulletin", an Australian news magazine, on 26 April 1890, and was published by Angus & Robertson in October 1895, with other poems by Paterson, in "The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses
chunks.text: The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses (1895) is the first collection of poems by Australian poet Banjo Paterson.

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses
chunks.text: It was released in hardback by Angus and Robertson in 1895, and features the poet's widely anthologised poems "The Man from Snowy River", "Clancy of the Overflow", "Saltbush Bill" and "The Man from Ironbark".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River and Other Verses
chunks.text: It also contains the poet's first two poems that featured in The Bulletin Debate, a famous dispute in "The Bulletin" magazine from 1892-93 between Paterson and Henry Lawson.

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River II
chunks.text: The Man from Snowy River II is a 1988 Australian drama film, the sequel to the 1982 film "The Man from Snowy River".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (TV series)
chunks.text: The Man from Snowy River is an Australian adventure drama television series based on Banjo Paterson's poem "The Man from Snowy River".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (TV series)
chunks.text: Released in Australia as "Banjo Paterson's The Man from Snowy River", the series was subsequently released in both the United States and the United Kingdom as "Snowy River: The McGregor Saga".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (1982 film)
chunks.text: The Man from Snowy River is a 1982 Australian drama film based on the Banjo Paterson poem "The Man from Snowy River".

chunks.title: The Man from Snowy River (1982 film)
chunks.text: The film had a cast including Kirk Douglas in a dual role as the brothers Harrison (a character who appeared frequently in Paterson's poems) and Spur, Jack Thompson as Clancy, Tom Burlinson as Jim Craig, Sigrid Thornton as Harrison's daughter Jessica, Terence Donovan as Jim's father Henry Craig, and Chris Haywood as Curly.

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind (album)
chunks.text: Third Eye Blind is the debut studio album by American rock band Third Eye Blind, released on April 8, 1997.

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind (album)
chunks.text: The album spawned five singles, including the top ten chart hits "Semi-Charmed Life", "Jumper", and "How's It Going to Be".

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind
chunks.text: Third Eye Blind is an American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1993.

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind
chunks.text: The songwriting duo of Stephan Jenkins and Kevin Cadogan signed the band's first major label recording contract with Elektra Records in 1996, which was later reported as the largest publishing deal ever for an unsigned artist.

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind
chunks.text: The band released their self-titled album, "Third Eye Blind", in 1997, with the band largely consisting of Jenkins (lead vocals, rhythm guitar), Cadogan (lead guitar), Arion Salazar (bass guitar), and Brad Hargreaves (drums).

chunks.title: Third Eye Blind
chunks.text: Shortly after the release of the band's second album in 1999, "Blue", with the same line-up, Cadogan was released from the band under controversial circumstances.

chunks.title: Kevin Cadogan
chunks.text: Kevin Rene Cadogan (born August 14, 1970) is an American singer/songwriter, producer and rock guitarist.

chunks.title: Kevin Cadogan
chunks.text: A founding member of the band Third Eye Blind, he performed with the band from 1993 to 2000.

chunks.title: Kevin Cadogan
chunks.text: He co-wrote some of Third Eye Blind's most notable hits, including "How's It Going to Be", "Losing a Whole Year", and "Graduate", and 10 of the 14 songs on their debut album "Third Eye Blind".

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: Sick Puppies is an Australian rock band, formed in 1997.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: Sick Puppies rose to prominence in 2006 when their song "All the Same" was uploaded along with a video to YouTube.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: The video supported the Free Hugs Campaign which was launched in Sydney, and has since received over 77 million views on the website.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: This success followed up with "Dressed Up as Life" in 2007, which entered the "Billboard" 200 at number 181.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: Their third studio album, released on 14 July 2009, is titled "Tri-Polar".

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: The band's fourth studio album "Connect" was released on 16 July 2013.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies
chunks.text: They released their fifth studio album "Fury" on 20 May 2016 with new vocalist Bryan Scott after Shimon Moore left the band on October 2014.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies EP
chunks.text: Sick Puppies EP is the fourth EP by Australia rock band Sick Puppies.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies EP
chunks.text: The EP was sold at live events and is now only available on the secondhand market.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies EP
chunks.text: The EP was released as an enhanced CD with bonus multimedia content featuring lyrics, a photo gallery, the YouTube Free Hugs video for "All the Same", and a live video trailer.

chunks.title: Sick Puppies EP
chunks.text: All the tracks were re-released on the album Dressed Up As Life.

chunks.title: Blue (Third Eye Blind album)
chunks.text: Blue is the second studio album by American rock band Third Eye Blind, released on November 23, 1999.

chunks.title: Blue (Third Eye Blind album)
chunks.text: The album's creation was difficult, namely due to power struggles and arguments between frontman Stephan Jenkins and lead guitarist Kevin Cadogan, leading to a quick but isolated recording experience between members.

chunks.title: Blue (Third Eye Blind album)
chunks.text: The album was generally well received by critics, and was certified platinum by the RIAA, but performed below the band's prior album, the multi-platinum "Third Eye Blind".

chunks.title: Blue (Third Eye Blind album)
chunks.text: While managing to stay together for the creation of the album, shortly after its release, the band fired Cadogan, touring in support of the album with replacement guitarist Tony Fredianelli.

chunks.title: Blue (Third Eye Blind album)
chunks.text: As such, the album was the last to feature Cadogan, and the last to be released without significant gaps and delays prior to release.

chunks.title: Red Star (EP)
chunks.text: Red Star is a digital-only EP by Third Eye Blind released in 2008 in anticipation of their fourth studio album "Ursa Major".

chunks.title: Red Star (EP)
chunks.text: Previews of the songs on the EP were posted to the band's myspace page on November 12, 2008, and it was released officially on November 18, 2008 through all major digital music outlets.

chunks.title: Red Star (EP)
chunks.text: Also released with the EP was a music video for "Non-Dairy Creamer" featuring Third Eye Blind's recent Japan tour.

chunks.title: The Nod
chunks.text: The Nod was an American Indie-Rock band from Madison, Wisconsin, formed in 2008 at the University of Wisconsin.

chunks.title: The Nod
chunks.text: Their debut EP, Shoddy Heart, earned the band live TV appearances on Urban Theater and WBUW TV, as well as opening appearances for national touring acts OK GO, Cage the Elephant and Third Eye Blind.

chunks.title: The Nod
chunks.text: To this date the band has released three studio albums: Shoddy Heart (2009), Easy, Maverick (2010) and Tomorrow Compadre (2011).

chunks.title: The Nod
chunks.text: Their music is distributed by independent record label Yes Please Records - a label created by singer Brett Newski to produce Nod albums.

chunks.title: Out of the Vein
chunks.text: Out of the Vein is the third studio album by American rock band Third Eye Blind.

chunks.title: Out of the Vein
chunks.text: Released on May 13, 2003, "Out of the Vein" is the band's first album with guitarist Tony Fredianelli, who replaced longtime guitarist Kevin Cadogan in 2000.

chunks.title: Out of the Vein
chunks.text: It would also be Third Eye Blind's final album with Elektra Records.

chunks.title: Stephan Jenkins
chunks.text: Stephan Douglas Jenkins (born September 27, 1964) is an American musician best known as the lead singer, songwriter, and guitarist for Third Eye Blind.

chunks.title: Stephan Jenkins
chunks.text: Under Jenkins's leadership, Third Eye Blind has sold over 12 million copies worldwide of five albums: "Third Eye Blind" (1997), "Blue" (1999), "Out of the Vein" (2003), "Ursa Major" (2009), and "Dopamine" (2015).

chunks.title: Stephan Jenkins
chunks.text: Jenkins wrote or co-wrote all of the band's most notable hits, including "Semi-Charmed Life", "Jumper", "How's It Going to Be", "Losing a Whole Year", "Graduate", "Deep Inside of You", "Never Let You Go" and "Blinded".

chunks.title: Don Sherwood (DJ)
chunks.text: Don Sherwood (September 7, 1925 – November 6, 1983) was an American radio personality.

chunks.title: Don Sherwood (DJ)
chunks.text: He was a San Francisco, California, disc jockey during the 1950s and 1960s.

chunks.title: Don Sherwood (DJ)
chunks.text: Billed as "The World's Greatest Disc Jockey," Sherwood spent most of his career hosting a 6-9 a.m. weekday program on KSFO in San Francisco (560 kHz, 5000 watts), which was then owned by the singing cowboy actor Gene Autry.

chunks.title: M. G. Kelly
chunks.text: Gary Sinclair (born 1952 in Ada, Oklahoma), known professionally as Michael Gary “M.G.” Kelly and Machine Gun Kelly, is an American actor, disc jockey and radio personality.

chunks.title: M. G. Kelly
chunks.text: In addition to hosting several radio programs over the years, Kelly has held several acting roles as a disc jockey; also, he has served as an offstage announcer on two game shows.

chunks.title: At Your Request
chunks.text: At Your Request was an Australian television daytime series which aired from 1958 to 1959.

chunks.title: At Your Request
chunks.text: The series aired on Tuesdays at 2:30PM on Melbourne station HSV-7, and was hosted by baritone Charles Skase, who was also known as a radio personality.

chunks.title: At Your Request
chunks.text: Information on this series is scarce.

chunks.title: At Your Request
chunks.text: The series presented requested songs, but it is not clear how these songs were presented (such as whether it was a disc jockey series like "TV Disc Jockey", a lip-sync series like "Hit Parade", or a live music series like "Sweet and Low").

chunks.title: At Your Request
chunks.text: The archival status of the series is also not known, although being a daytime series aired in a single city means it is unlikely (though not impossible) that kinescope recordings exist of it.

chunks.title: XY TV

chunks.title: XY TV
chunks.text: It was wholly owned by American radio personality John Garabedian.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: A radio personality (American English) or radio presenter (British English), commonly referred to as a "disc jockey" or "DJ" for short, is a person who has an on-air position in radio broadcasting.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: A radio personality that hosts a radio show is also known as a radio host, and in India and Pakistan as a radio jockey.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: Radio personalities who introduce and play individual selections of recorded music are known as disc jockeys.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: The term has evolved to also describe a person who mixes a continuous flow of recorded music in real time.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: Broadcast radio personalities may include talk radio hosts, AM/FM radio show hosts, and satellite radio program hosts.

chunks.title: Radio personality
chunks.text: Notable radio personalities include pop music radio hosts Martin Block, Alan Freed, Dick Clark, Delilah Luke, Ameen Sayani, Wolfman Jack, and Casey Kasem, shock jocks such as Don Imus and Howard Stern, as well as sports talk hosts such as Mike Francesa and political talk hosts such as Rush Limbaugh.

chunks.title: Lin Brehmer
chunks.text: Lin Brehmer (born August 19, 1954) is a disc jockey and radio personality at WXRT in Chicago, Illinois.

chunks.title: Lin Brehmer
chunks.text: Brehmer has been serving as the morning-drive slot disc jockey since 1991.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: Big Wilson (born Malcolm John Wilson, Jr.; October 3, 1924 – October 5, 1989) was an American radio personality.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: He worked as a disc jockey at WNBC AM in New York City from the early 1960s until 1974 and moved to Miami in 1975 where he worked for WIOD and WCIX-TV.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: He was one of the last two hosts of the NBC network program Monitor.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: Prior to moving to NYC, Wilson and his wife Jody lived in a riverfront home in Rocky River, Ohio.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: He commuted to Cleveland where he was the leading radio personality for some years.

chunks.title: Big Wilson
chunks.text: Tim Conway and other well-known persons visited their home.

chunks.title: Charles A. Agemian
chunks.text: Charles A. Agemian (July 22, 1909 – March 30, 1996) was an American banker who took early retirement from Chase Manhattan Bank, where he was executive vice president of operations, to become chairman and chief executive officer of the Hackensack Trust Co., which later was renamed Garden State National Bank.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: Open House Party (most of the time, shortened to OHP) is an American radio show hosted on Saturday and Sunday nights by Kannon, who also hosts the afternoon drive slot on 102.9 Now.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: The show promotes itself as "the Biggest Party on the Planet".

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: It focuses on playing contemporary hit radio (CHR) music, also known as Top 40.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: The show differentiates itself from most Top 40 because it plays a high rotation of remixes.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: Unlike most radio stations or programs, every song played on OHP is by a listener request, rather than computer systems automatically inserting songs that may not even be popular anyways.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: The show started in 1987, and was hosted by John Garabedian from September 1987 to January 2017.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: Garabedian created the show, and hosted both Saturday and Sunday nights for a long period of time.

chunks.title: Open House Party
chunks.text: Open House Party is broadcast on more than 50 stations around the world.

chunks.title: John Garabedian
chunks.text: John H. Garabedian is an American radio personality and disc jockey born on December 20, 1941 (age 75).

chunks.title: John Garabedian
chunks.text: He is best known as the creator and former long-time host of "Open House Party".

chunks.title: John Garabedian
chunks.text: He has been involved in Massachusetts radio and television stations for over fifty years.

chunks.title: John Garabedian
chunks.text: Garabedian currently owns three homes, all in New England: one in Southborough, Massachusetts, another on Cape Cod, and a cabin-like home in Cabot, Vermont.

chunks.text: Shuangmiao () is a town under the administration of Hanggin Rear Banner in southwestern Inner Mongolia, China, located about 26 km southwest of the banner seat and 44 km north-northwest of downtown Bayannur.

chunks.title: Shuangmiao, Inner Mongolia

chunks.title: Chahar Right Rear Banner
chunks.text: Chahar Right Rear Banner (Mongolian: ᠴᠠᠬᠠᠷ ᠪᠠᠷᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠲᠤ ᠬᠣᠰᠢᠭᠤ ; Цахар баруун гарын хойд хошуу; "Čaqar Baraɣun Ɣarun Qoyitu qosiɣu"; ) is a banner of Inner Mongolia, People's Republic of China, bordering Shangdu County to the northeast, Xinghe County to the southeast, Chahar Right Front Banner to the south, Zhuozi County to the southwest, Chahar Right Rear Banner to the west, Siziwang Banner to the northwest, and Xilin Gol to the north.

chunks.title: Chahar Right Rear Banner
chunks.text: It is under the administration of Ulaan Chab City, which lies to the south along the G55 Erenhot–Guangzhou Expressway.

chunks.title: Chahar Right Rear Banner
chunks.text: The most important settlement in the banner is Baiyinchagan.

chunks.title: Horqin Left Rear Banner
chunks.text: Horqin Left Rear Banner (Mongolian: ᠬᠣᠷᠴᠢᠨ ᠵᠡᠭᠦᠨ ᠭᠠᠷᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠲᠤ ᠬᠣᠰᠢᠭᠤ Қорчин Жэгүн арун Қоыиту қосиу "Qorčin Jegün Ɣarun Qoyitu qosiɣu"; Mongolian: "Qorcin jegün garun qoyidu qosigu" 'Northern banner of the Khorchin east wing'; , original Mongolian name "Büve vang qosigu") is a banner of southeastern Inner Mongolia, People's Republic of China, bordering Liaoning province to the south.

chunks.title: Horqin Left Rear Banner

chunks.title: Horqin Left Rear Banner

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Islam is historically divided into two major sects, Sunni and Shia Islam, each with its own sub-sects.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Large numbers of Shia Arab Muslims live in some Arab countries including Lebanon, Yemen, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE, and Qatar.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Shia Muslims are a numerical majority in Iraq and Bahrain.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Approximately half of the population in Yemen are Shia Muslims.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Exactly half of Muslims in Lebanon are Shia Muslims.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: There is also a very large population of Shia Muslims living in the Arab Persian Gulf countries especially in Saudi Arabia.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Approximately the whole population of East Saudi Arabia, the Eastern Province are Shia Muslims.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Although government statistics claim that roughly only 20-40% of the Muslim population are Shia Muslims, there has been dispute to the authenticity of this figure and recent reports and investigations indicate that there is in fact a much larger population of Shia Muslims present, with estimate figures over 45% or even making the majority of Muslim population.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Saudi Arabia follows a strict recently established sect of Islam, Wahhabism, there is little freedom of religion between the different sects even whilst all of the population are Muslims.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Smaller Shia groups are present in Egypt and Jordan.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Despite the heavy presence of Shia Muslims in some Arab countries, particularly among the population of the Persian Gulf Arab countries, they have been treated poorly throughout history.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: Additionally, in recent times, Shia Muslims along with Kurds have faced genocide by the pan-Arabist regime of Saddam Hussein.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: For both historical and political reasons, the Shia have fared rather poorly in much of the Arab world, and the topic of Shi‘ism and Shia groups is one of the most sensitive issues for the Sunni elite.

chunks.title: Shia Muslims in the Arab world
chunks.text: This article discusses both the history of Shī‘a Islam in the Arab world from the dawn of Islam and their current situation in the Arabic-speaking world.

chunks.title: Statistical inference

chunks.title: Statistical inference

chunks.title: Altanochir (1882–1949)

chunks.title: Altanochir (1882–1949)
chunks.text: He served as deputy head of Yeke-juu League (today Ordos City).

chunks.title: Altanochir (1882–1949)

chunks.title: Riverview, New Brunswick

chunks.title: Riverview, New Brunswick
chunks.text: Riverview is located on the south side of the Petitcodiac River, across from the larger cities of Moncton and Dieppe.

chunks.title: Riverview, New Brunswick
chunks.text: Riverview has an area of 34 km2 , and a population density of 564.6 PD/km2 .

chunks.title: Riverview, New Brunswick
chunks.text: Riverview's slogan is "A Great Place To Grow".

chunks.title: Riverview, New Brunswick
chunks.text: With a population of 19,667, Riverview is the fifth largest municipality in New Brunswick, having a larger population than the cities of Edmundston, Bathurst, Campbellton, and Miramichi, despite its designation of "town".

chunks.title: Urad Rear Banner
chunks.text: Urad Rear Banner (Mongolian: ᠤᠷᠠᠳ ᠤᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠢᠲᠤ ᠬᠣᠰᠢᠭᠤ "Urad-un Qoyitu Qosiɣu", Урадын хойд хошуу; ) or Urad Houqi is a banner of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Urad Rear Banner
chunks.text: Its seat is located in the town of Bayan Bolag (巴音宝力格镇).

chunks.title: Shanghai

chunks.title: Shanghai
chunks.text: It is a global financial centre and transport hub, with the world's busiest container port.

chunks.title: Shanghai
chunks.text: Located in the Yangtze River Delta, it sits on the south edge of the estuary of the Yangtze in the middle portion of the East China coast.

chunks.title: Shanghai
chunks.text: The municipality borders the provinces of Jiangsu and Zhejiang to the north, south and west, and is bounded to the east by the East China Sea.

chunks.title: Pashmina
chunks.text: Pashmina is a fine type of cashmere wool.

chunks.title: Pashmina
chunks.text: The textiles made from it were first woven in Kashmir, India.

chunks.title: Pashmina
chunks.text: The name comes from Persian: پشمینه‎ ‎ / "pašmina", meaning "made from wool" and literally translates to "Soft Gold" in Kashmiri.

chunks.title: Pashmina
chunks.text: Pashmina shawls are known to pass entirely through a wearable ring with diameter of about half an inch.

chunks.title: Pashmina

chunks.title: Pashmina
chunks.text: The wool comes from four distinct breeds of the Cashmere goat; namely the Changthangi or Kashmir Pashmina goat from the Changthang plateau in Kashmir region, the Malra from Kargil area in Kashmir region, the Chegu from Himachal Pradesh in northern India and Pakistan, and Chyangara or Nepalese Pashmina goat from Nepal.

chunks.title: Pashmina

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: Poleconomy is a board game invented by New Zealander Bruce E. Hatherley and first published in 1980.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: It is similar to "Monopoly" but the board is divided into companies rather than properties.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: Players compete to acquire properties and investments through stylized economic and political activity.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: The playing time is set by agreement from all players, e.g. 2 hours, and the winner is determined by the monetary sum of all player cash, companies, insurance or other assets.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: The game can also end when there are no more companies, advertisements in the bank or bonds in the treasury.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: Another objective of the game is "to teach players some of the fundamentals of economics, and the ways in which the economy and the government interact."

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: Different editions were published for several different countries.

chunks.title: Poleconomy
chunks.text: The name "Poleconomy" is a portmanteau of "politics" and "economy".

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: "Verão Vermelho" is a song by Santana which came off the album "Festival".

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: Carlos Santana pays homage to Brazilian singer, Elis Regina.

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: This song features some excellent acoustic guitar with The Waters Family backing vocalists (Julia, Oren, and Maxine Willard Waters) singing the meaningless words, ”Badadup, badadup, badadup, ba pa pa ba pa pa.”

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: It is carried along by a marching drum beat and maracas. Santana plays a flamenco guitar solo during the intro and at the conclusion.

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: This is a first for him.

chunks.title: Verão Vermelho
chunks.text: The flamenco guitar solo during the coda is accompanied by a keyboard flourish by Tom Coster.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: The Ford flathead V8 (often called simply the Ford flathead, flathead Ford, or flatty when the context is implicit, such as in hot-rodding) is a V8 engine of the valve-in-block type designed by the Ford Motor Company and built by Ford and various licensees.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: During the engine's first decade of production, when overhead-valve engines were rare, it was usually known simply as the Ford V‑8, and the first car model in which it was installed, the Model 18, was (and still is) often called simply the "Ford V‑8", after its new engine.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: Although the V8 configuration was not new when the Ford V8 was introduced in 1932, the latter was a market first in the respect that it made an 8-cylinder affordable and a V engine affordable to the emerging mass market consumer for the first time.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: It was the first independently designed and built V8 engine produced by Ford for mass production, and it ranks as one of the company's most important developments.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: A fascination with ever-more-powerful engines was perhaps the most salient aspect of the American car and truck market for a half century, from 1923 until 1973.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: The Ford flathead V8 was perfectly in tune with the cultural moment of its introduction, leading the way into a future of which the Ford company was a principal architect.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: Thus it became a phenomenal success.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: The engine design, with various changes but no major ones, was installed in Ford passenger cars and trucks until 1953, making the engine's 21-year production run for the U.S. consumer market longer than the 19-year run of the Ford Model T engine for that market.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: The engine was on Ward's list of the 10 best engines of the 20th century.

chunks.title: Ford flathead V8 engine
chunks.text: It was a staple of hot rodders in the 1950s, and it remains famous in the classic car hobbies even today, despite the huge variety of other popular V8s that followed.

chunks.title: Friendship Hall
chunks.text: Friendship Hall is a historic home located at East New Market, Dorchester County, Maryland.

chunks.title: Friendship Hall
chunks.text: It is a Georgian-style brick dwelling.

chunks.title: Friendship Hall
chunks.text: It consists of a large five-bay, two-story main block built about 1790; a two-bay one-story passage; and a 1 ⁄ -story kitchen wing.

chunks.title: Friendship Hall
chunks.text: Also on the property is a tall frame smokehouse with board-and-batten siding and a steep gable roof.

chunks.title: Friendship Hall
chunks.text: It is associated with the locally prominent Sulivane family, who first came to Maryland in 1695.

chunks.title: Vetigel
chunks.text: Veti-gel is a veterinary product, a plant-derived injectable gel that is claimed to quickly stop traumatic bleeding on external and internal wounds.

chunks.title: Vetigel
chunks.text: Its name is coined from Medi-Gel, from the video game Mass Effect.

chunks.title: Vetigel
chunks.text: It uses a plant-based haemophilic polymer made from polysaccharides that forms a mesh which seals the wound.

chunks.title: Vetigel
chunks.text: It is manufactured by Suneris Inc, an American biotechnology company, which is also exploring human products derived from its technology, slated to launch as early as 2016.

chunks.title: Vetigel
chunks.text: The company plans on releasing a product for the military and the emergency medicine market first, followed by a product for the human surgical market when FDA approval is granted.

chunks.title: Rove goat
chunks.text: The Rove is a breed of goat first domesticated in France.

chunks.title: Rove goat
chunks.text: The breed was previously considered endangered, but as of 2003, more than 5000 registered Roves are on French farms.

chunks.title: Rove goat
chunks.text: The goat was originally bred for meat, but because the current French market for goat meat is poor, farmers have begun to use the Rove for dairying, instead.

chunks.title: Chatta Bazaar
chunks.text: Chatta Bazaar (English: under roof market), is located in Hyderabad, India.

chunks.title: Chatta Bazaar
chunks.text: Chatta Bazar is one of the oldest bazaars in Hyderabad and was the first to organize shops under a roof for better storage of goods.

chunks.title: VELUX
chunks.text: VELUX is a Danish manufacturing company that specializes in roof windows and skylights.

chunks.title: VELUX
chunks.text: The first VELUX roof window was installed in a Danish school over 75 years ago by the founder of the company, Villum Kann Rasmussen.

chunks.title: VELUX
chunks.text: The company has been steadily growing since, entering the German market in 1952 in a partnership with Ernst Günter Albers and then later between the sons, Lars Kann-Rasmussen and Peter Albers

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: 34th Street was an express station on the demolished IRT Ninth Avenue Line, New York, United States.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: It was originally built on July 30, 1873 by the New York Elevated Railroad Company, and had two levels.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The lower level was built first and had two tracks and two side platforms.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The upper level was built as part of the Dual Contracts and had one track and two side platforms over the lower level local tracks.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: It closed on June 11, 1940.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The next southbound local stop was 30th Street.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The next southbound express stop was 14th Street.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The next northbound local stop was 42nd Street.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: The next northbound express stop was 66th Street.

chunks.title: 34th Street (IRT Ninth Avenue Line)
chunks.text: This station also serviced Penn Station and was west of the IRT and IND subway stations at Penn Station.

chunks.title: Abraham M. Radcliffe
chunks.text: Abraham M. Radcliffe (1827–1886) was an architect born in New York City.

chunks.title: Abraham M. Radcliffe
chunks.text: He opened a Minneapolis office in 1857 and a St. Paul office in 1858.

chunks.title: Abraham M. Radcliffe
chunks.text: He closed his Minneapolis office in 1868.

chunks.title: Abraham M. Radcliffe
chunks.text: He designed early commercial buildings in St. Paul and Minneapolis, as well as the Dakota County Courthouse in Hastings, Minnesota.

chunks.title: Abraham M. Radcliffe
chunks.text: Radcliffe inspired the architectural career of Cass Gilbert, the skyscraper pioneer who designed the Woolworth Building in New York City and the United States Supreme Court building, among many important public structures.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: The Petroleum Building (formerly known as the Hogan Building) is a highrise in downtown Midland, TX.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: The building was built in 1928 and consists of 12 floors and has a neo-gothic style architecture to it.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: The building stands at 137 ft but with its spires reaches a height of 151 ft. The Hogan building is a registered, Texas historical landmark.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: The tower is named for lawyer and oil entrepreneur Thomas Stephen Hogan.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: For information on Hogan, see article on Jacob Bunn.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: The design of the Petroleum Building, like the Woolworth Building in New York City and the Baum Building in Oklahoma City, utilizes many classic architectural devices.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: Gothic spires and Moorish arches, lavish carved surfaces and opulent marble, all intended to clothe the business house with the respectability of a cathedral.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: Thomas Stephen Hogan intended his building to be a landmark and (Fort Worth architect-engineer) Wyatt Hedrick designed a building that people would talk about.

chunks.title: Petroleum Building (Midland)
chunks.text: However, behind the ornate cast-stone façade was (sic) functional reinforced concrete, the finest equipment available, and the determination of one man to establish Midland as the headquarters of the West Texas oil fields.

chunks.title: Westchester Avenue (NYW&B station)
chunks.text: Westchester Avenue is a former railroad station located in the borough of the Bronx in New York City, partially suspended over Amtrak's busy Northeast Corridor line.

chunks.title: Westchester Avenue (NYW&B station)
chunks.text: It was built in 1908 with rich terra cotta detailing to a design by Cass Gilbert, who would later employ similar terra cotta detailing in his 1910 design for the Woolworth Building.

chunks.title: Westchester Avenue (NYW&B station)
chunks.text: Train service to the station ceased in 1937, and as of 2014 the station was a ruin in poor condition.

chunks.title: 1 New York Plaza
chunks.text: 1 New York Plaza is an office building in New York City's Financial District, built in 1969 at the intersection of South and Whitehall Streets.

chunks.title: 1 New York Plaza
chunks.text: It is the southernmost of all Manhattan skyscrapers.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: The Woolworth Building is an historic building in Watertown, New York.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: It is a contributing building in the Public Square Historic District.

chunks.title: F. W. Woolworth Building (Watertown, New York)
chunks.text: Plans for the Woolworth Building were begun in 1916 by Frank W. Woolworth, the founder of the Woolworth's chain of department stores.

chunks.title: 90 West Street
chunks.text: 90 West Street (alternatively West Street Building) is a building in Lower Manhattan, New York City.

chunks.title: 90 West Street
chunks.text: It was designed by architect Cass Gilbert and structural engineer Gunvald Aus for the West Street Improvement Corporation.

chunks.title: 90 West Street
chunks.text: When completed in 1907, the building's Gothic styling and ornamentation served to emphasize its 23-story height, and foreshadowed Gilbert's later work on the Woolworth Building.

chunks.title: 90 West Street
chunks.text: Originally built as an office building, the main tenant was the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and the top floor was occupied by Garret's Restaurant, which advertised itself as the "world's highest restaurant".

chunks.title: Transportation Building
chunks.text: The Transportation Building is a 44-story office building located at 225 Broadway on the corner of Barclay Street in the Civic Center neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City.

chunks.title: Transportation Building
chunks.text: It also carries the address 2-4 Barclay Street.

chunks.title: Transportation Building
chunks.text: It was built in 1927 and was designed by the architecture firm of York & Sawyer, in the Renaissance Revival style, using setbacks common to skyscrapers built after the adoption of the 1916 Zoning Resolution.

chunks.title: Transportation Building
chunks.text: It sits across Barclay Street from the Woolworth Building.

chunks.title: Woolworth Building
chunks.text: The Woolworth Building, at 233 Broadway, Manhattan, New York City, designed by architect Cass Gilbert and constructed between 1910 and 1912, is an early US skyscraper.

chunks.title: Woolworth Building
chunks.text: The original site for the building was purchased by F. W. Woolworth and his real estate agent Edward J. Hogan by April 15, 1910, from the Trenor Luther Park Estate and other owners for $1.65 million.

chunks.title: Woolworth Building
chunks.text: By January 18, 1911, Woolworth and Hogan had acquired the final site for the project, totaling $4.5 million.

chunks.title: Woolworth Building
chunks.text: More than a century after its construction, it remains, at 241.4 m , one of the 100 tallest buildings in the United States as well as one of the 30 tallest buildings in New York City.

chunks.title: Woolworth Building
chunks.text: It has been a National Historic Landmark since 1966, and a New York City landmark since 1983.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: Rubin Schron, who goes by Ruby, is a New York City real estate investor, landlord and the founder of Cammeby's International Group.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: He has a personal net worth of well over $10 billion, according to data company Real Capital Analytics.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: The portfolio of Cammeby's, which Schron founded in 1967, includes office buildings, market-rate and government-subsidized apartment complexes, nursing homes, the 16-building complex in Sunset Park now known as Industry City, a stake in the bottom half of Woolworth Building and industrial properties scattered across Long Island.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: In 2013, Schron made an unsolicited and unsuccessful offer to buy the Empire State Building for $2 billion, but he has not had problems closing many other deals throughout his long career.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: In 2003, an investment group led by Schron paid $600 million for a portfolio of about 6,000 outer-borough apartments from Donald Trump.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: Other buildings he owns include the Monterey, a 521-unit rental multifamily building on Manhattan's Upper East Side; over the decades, Schron has also amassed a portfolio of Mitchell-Lama apartment buildings whose values have been skyrocketing to record values, after reverting to market rates when government subsidies expired.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: In 2007, he sold nearly 4,000 units of former Mitchell-Lama properties in five complexes in Harlem and on Roosevelt Island for $940 million.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: Schron, who practices Orthodox Judaism, has eight children and 50 grandchildren.

chunks.title: Rubin Schron
chunks.text: He and his family have lived in the same single-family home in Brooklyn for many decades.

chunks.title: Lysiloma
chunks.text: Lysiloma is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family, Fabaceae.
