chunks.text: In 1861, Reichenbach recognized ten species in this subsection.

chunks.title: Epidendrum subsect. Umbellata
chunks.text: Of these, nine are recognized with the same names by Kew (page numbers refer to Reichenbach):

chunks.title: Coeloplana fishelsoni
chunks.text: Coeloplana fishelsoni is a species of benthic comb jelly from the Red Sea, that lives as an episymbiont on colonies of "Xenia umbellata" and "Paralemnalia" species.

chunks.title: Coeloplana fishelsoni
chunks.text: It can be differentiated from its cogenerate species by their host, colour, and colour pattern.

chunks.title: Elaeagnus umbellata
chunks.text: Elaeagnus umbellata is known as Japanese silverberry, umbellata oleaster, autumn olive, autumn elaeagnus, or spreading oleaster.

chunks.title: Elaeagnus umbellata
chunks.text: The species is indigenous to eastern Asia and ranges from the Himalayas eastwards to Japan.

chunks.title: Elaeagnus umbellata
chunks.text: Because it fixes atmospheric nitrogen in its roots, it often grows vigorously and competitively in infertile soils.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: Sabicu wood or sabicu is the wood of at least two species of the genus "Lysiloma". "

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: Lysiloma sabicu" (L.) Benth.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: occurs sparingly in the Bahamas, Jamaica, Haiti and the Dominican Republic, and Cuba.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: It was named by George Bentham (1800-1884) from a Cuban specimen examined in 1854.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: Bentham went on to identify a second species, "Lysiloma latisiliquum" (L.) Benth., which grows best in the Bahamas.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: The latter is commonly known as 'wild tamarind' or 'false tamarind'.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: The wood of both species is similar, being mid-brown in colour, sometimes with a reddish hue, heavy (specific gravity of 0.40-0.75) hard and durable.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: Some timber is well figured, but most relatively plain.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: The wood has been used in construction, shipbuilding and in furniture making, although its weight is a distinct drawback for the latter purpose.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: The stairs of The Crystal Palace in London, in which The Great Exhibition of 1851 was held, were made of sabicu due to its durability.

chunks.title: Sabicu wood
chunks.text: Despite the enormous traffic that passed over them, the wood at the end was found to be little affected by wear.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: Hunteria umbellata grows as either a shrub or small tree up to 22 m tall, with a trunk diameter of up to 40 cm .

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: Its flowers feature a white, creamy or pale yellow corolla.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: The fruit is yellow and smooth.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: Its habitat is forests from sea level to 600 m altitude.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: Its numerous local medicinal uses include for fever, leprosy sores, stomach and liver problems and as an anthelmintic, especially against internal worms.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: "Hunteria umbellata" has been used as arrow poison.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: The plant's hard wood is used in carving and to make small tools.

chunks.title: Hunteria umbellata
chunks.text: The species is native to west and west-central tropical Africa.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides, known commonly as water pennywort, floating pennywort, or floating marshpennywort, is an aquatic plant in the family Apiaceae.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: It is native to North and South America and parts of Africa.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: In the United Kingdom it is an invasive alien species which is currently spreading in waterways.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: It was one of five aquatic plants which were banned from sale in the UK from April 2014, and was the first prohibition of its kind there.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: Water pennywort is also a weed in Australia.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle ranunculoides
chunks.text: On the other hand, it is a threatened species in parts of its native range in the United States.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Hydrocotyle javanica, commonly known as Java pennywort, is a species of "Hydrocotyle".

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: It is a prostrate herb found in NE India and SE Asia.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Leaves are simple, circular-heart-shaped, with seven triangular shallow lobes.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Leaves are 2.5-5 x 3-5.5 cm in size, and the margin has rounded teeth.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Java pennywort is closely related to Indian pennywort.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Tiny white flowers arise in 20 flowered umbels.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Java pennywort is seen in shady, moist places at altitudes greater than 1300 m. Flowers have five greenish-white petals and five stamens.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Fruit is broadly ovoid, 1 mm, laterally compressed.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: In Manipur, the leaves are eaten as a substitute for Indian pennywort.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle javanica
chunks.text: Flowering: June-July.

chunks.title: Lysiloma latisiliquum
chunks.text: Lysiloma latisiliquum, commonly known as false tamarind or wild tamarind, is a species of tree in the pea family, Fabaceae, that is native to southern Florida in the United States, The Bahamas, the Caribbean, southern Mexico, and northern Central America.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle umbellata
chunks.text: Hydrocotyle umbellata, is an aquatic plant that thrives in wet, sandy habitat.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle umbellata
chunks.text: Its English common name is manyflower marshpennywort or dollarweed.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle umbellata
chunks.text: It is native to North America and parts of South America.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle umbellata
chunks.text: It can also be found growing as an introduced species and sometimes a noxious weed on other continents.

chunks.title: Hydrocotyle umbellata
chunks.text: It is an edible weed that can be used in salads or as a pot herb.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara Library
chunks.text: The University of California, Santa Barbara Library is the university library system of the University of California, Santa Barbara in Santa Barbara, California.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara Library
chunks.text: The Library includes four facilities: Two libraries (the Main Library and the Music Library) and two annexes (Annex I and Annex II).

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara Library
chunks.text: The library has some three million print volumes, 30,000 electronic journals, 34,450 e-books, 900,055 digitized items, five million cartographic items (including some 467,000 maps and 3.2 million satellite and aerial images), more than 3.7 million pieces of microform, 167,500 sound recordings, and 4,100 manuscripts.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara Library
chunks.text: The Library states that it holds 3.2 mi of manuscript and archival collections.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara Library
chunks.text: According to data collected by the American Library Association, as of July 2010 the UC Santa Barbara Library holds the 99th largest library collection in America, reporting 2,948,999 volumes.

chunks.title: USNS Mission Santa Barbara (T-AO-131)
chunks.text: SS "Mission Santa Barbara" was a Type T2-SE-A2 tanker built for the United States Maritime Commission during World War II.

chunks.title: USNS Mission Santa Barbara (T-AO-131)
chunks.text: After the war she was acquired by the United States Navy as USS "Mission Santa Barbara" (AO-131).

chunks.title: USNS Mission Santa Barbara (T-AO-131)
chunks.text: Later the tanker transferred to the Military Sea Transportation Service as USNS "Mission Santa Barbara" (T-AO-131).

chunks.title: USNS Mission Santa Barbara (T-AO-131)
chunks.text: She was a member of the "Mission Buenaventura"-class oiler and was named for Mission Santa Barbara in Santa Barbara, California.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara High School
chunks.text: Santa Barbara Senior High School, "Home of the Dons," is situated on a 40 acre campus in Santa Barbara, California and is part of the Santa Barbara Unified School District.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara High School
chunks.text: One of the oldest high schools in California, it was established in 1875, and moved to its current site in 1924.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara High School
chunks.text: Until the creation of two rival high schools in 1959 and 1966, it was the sole public high school serving the city of Santa Barbara.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara High School
chunks.text: In November 2005, its 18th-century Spanish influenced design was named an official California and City historic landmark.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara High School
chunks.text: Today, Santa Barbara High School has an enrollment of roughly 2,200 pupils and certified staff numbering 108.

chunks.title: Hamdard University
chunks.text: Hamdard University (Urdu: ) is a private research university with campuses in Karachi and Islamabad, Pakistan.

chunks.title: Hamdard University
chunks.text: It was founded in 1991 by the renowned philanthropist Hakim Said of the Hamdard Foundation.

chunks.title: Hamdard University
chunks.text: Hamdard is one of the first and the oldest private institutions of higher education in Pakistan.

chunks.title: Hamdard University
chunks.text: In Karachi, Hamdard University is the largest private research university with a campus area of over 350 acres.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: Erno S. Daniel M.D. Ph.D (Born December 15, 1946, Died February 21, 2015) is an internal medicine specialist and author.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: He is of Hungarian descent.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: He has practiced at the Sansum Clinic in Santa Barbara (formerly known as the Santa Barbara Medical Foundation Clinic) since 1978.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: Since that time, he has participated in teaching activities at Santa Barbara's Cottage Hospital, whose internal medicine residency training program is affiliated with University of Southern California School of Medicine.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: Because of his activities, for a period of time Dr. Daniel held an appointment as Associate Clinical Professor of Medicine at USC.

chunks.title: Erno S. Daniel
chunks.text: He also participated as a lecturer for the Introduction to Medicine course offered by the University of California at Santa Barbara.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara
chunks.text: The University of California, Santa Barbara (commonly referred to as UC Santa Barbara or UCSB) is a public research university and one of the 10 campuses of the University of California system.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara
chunks.text: The main campus is located on a 1022 acre site near Isla Vista, California, United States, 8 mi from Santa Barbara and 100 mi northwest of Los Angeles.

chunks.title: University of California, Santa Barbara
chunks.text: Tracing its roots back to 1891 as an independent teachers' college, UCSB joined the University of California system in 1944 and is the third-oldest general-education campus in the system.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: The Santa Barbara International Marathon and Half Marathon is an annual race that takes place in Goleta, California and Santa Barbara, California.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: The inaugural race was on December 6, 2009.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: For the last five years the Santa Barbara City College has been the official host for the finish line and general operations.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: Rusty and June Snow are the co-directors of the race with Dan Campbell as the technical director.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: The Snow's moved from the East Coast and wanted to bring a marathon to Santa Barbara.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: After a few years of getting the race approved and organized it was finally set to happen in 2009, Rusty Snow states, “I learned to be stubborn from running marathons.”

chunks.title: Santa Barbara International Marathon
chunks.text: The Santa Barbara International Marathon course serves as a Boston Marathon qualifier.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: KUSC (91.5 MHz FM) is a listener-supported classical music radio station broadcasting from downtown Los Angeles, California, United States.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: KUSC is owned and operated by the University of Southern California, which also operates student-run Internet station KXSC (AM) and San Francisco's classical station KDFC.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: It is the largest non-profit classical music station in the country and the only classical radio station in the Greater Los Angeles Area.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: In February 2014, public radio station KCRW of Santa Monica announced that it would buy the Santa Barbara Foundation's classical station KDB (FM) 93.7 in Santa Barbara for $1 million.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: The transaction will allow KCRW to begin using KQSC, USC's current repeater station in Santa Barbara, as a repeater for KCRW's programming, while transferring KUSC's classical programming from KQSC to KDB, thus perpetuating KDB's role as Santa Barbara's classical station.

chunks.title: KUSC
chunks.text: The legacy KDB call letters have been retained.

chunks.title: Mission Santa Barbara
chunks.text: Mission Santa Barbara, also known as Santa Barbara Mission, is a Spanish mission founded by the Franciscan order near present-day Santa Barbara, California.

chunks.title: Mission Santa Barbara
chunks.text: It was founded by Padre Fermín Lasuén on December 4, 1786, the feast day of Saint Barbara, as the tenth mission for the religious conversion of the indigenous local Chumash-Barbareño tribe of Native American people.

chunks.title: Mission Santa Barbara
chunks.text: The mission is the namesake of the city of Santa Barbara as well as of Santa Barbara County.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara City College
chunks.text: Santa Barbara City College (SBCC) is a two-year community college that opened in 1909 and is located on a 74 acre campus in the city of Santa Barbara, California, USA.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara City College
chunks.text: SBCC was named co-winner of the 2013 Aspen Institute Prize for Community College Excellence, earning it a #1 national ranking.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara City College
chunks.text: The college was recognized for its quality and focus in four areas: facilitating underrepresented and minority student success, student learning outcomes, degree completion and transfer rates, and labor market success in securing good jobs after college.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara City College
chunks.text: Santa Barbara City College was established by the Santa Barbara High School District in 1909, making it one of the oldest community colleges in California.

chunks.title: Santa Barbara City College
chunks.text: The college was discontinued shortly after World War I, and its work largely taken over by the Santa Barbara State Normal School, which became the Santa Barbara State College, and later, the University of California, Santa Barbara.

chunks.title: Béla Bartók Music High School
chunks.text: Béla Bartók Music High School (Bartók Béla Zeneművészeti Szakközépiskola) is situated in the Palace of Music (Zenepalota) in Bartók square Miskolc, Hungary.

chunks.title: Béla Bartók Music High School
chunks.text: It is a famous Music school named after the famous Hungarian composer Béla Bartók.

chunks.title: Béla Bartók Music High School
chunks.text: It was founded in 1966.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: The String Quartet No. 6, Sz.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: 114, BB 119, was the final string quartet that Béla Bartók wrote before his death.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: It was begun in August 1939 in Saanen, Switzerland, where Bartók was a guest of his patron, the conductor Paul Sacher.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: Shortly after he completed the Divertimento for String Orchestra on the 17th, he started on a commission for his friend, the violinist Zoltán Székely.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: Székely was acting as intermediary for the "New Hungarian Quartet", who had given the Budapest premiere of the String Quartet No. 5.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: With the outbreak of World War II and his mother's illness, Bartók returned to Budapest, where the quartet was finished in November.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: After his mother's death, Bartók decided to leave with his family for the United States.

chunks.title: String Quartet No. 6 (Bartók)
chunks.text: Due to the difficulties of the war, communication between Bartók and Székely was difficult, and the quartet was not premiered until 20 January 1941, when the Kolisch Quartet, to whom the work is dedicated, gave its premiere at the Town Hall in New York City.

chunks.title: List of string quartets by Béla Bartók
chunks.text: The Hungarian composer Béla Bartók wrote six string quartets, each for the usual forces of two violins, viola and cello.

chunks.title: List of string quartets by Béla Bartók
chunks.text: Notable composers who have been influenced by them include Benjamin Britten, particularly in the Sonata in C for Cello and Piano (; ), Elliott Carter, who refers in the opening of his own First String Quartet to Bartók’s Sixth Quartet , Chen Yi , Edison Denisov, whose Second Quartet is closely related to Bartók’s Fifth Quartet , Franco Donatoni, who was deeply impressed when he heard a broadcast of Bartók's Fourth Quartet , Robert Fripp, who mentions them as an influence upon King Crimson , Miloslav Ištvan , György Kurtág, whose Opp.

chunks.title: List of string quartets by Béla Bartók
chunks.text: 1 and 28 both owe a great deal to Bartók's quartets (; ), György Ligeti, whose two string quartets both owe a great deal to Bartók’s quartets (; ), Bruno Maderna , George Perle, who credits the Bartók Fourth and Fifth Quartets as precedents for his use of arrays of chords related to one another by different types of symmetry , Walter Piston (; ), Kim Dzmitrïyevich Tsesakow , Wilfried Westerlinck , Stefan Wolpe, who explained in a public lecture how he had derived ideas from Bartók’s Fourth Quartet , and Xu Yongsan .

chunks.title: Palace of Music (Miskolc)
chunks.text: The Palace of Music ("Zenepalota") is a building in Bartók square, Miskolc, Hungary.

chunks.title: Palace of Music (Miskolc)
chunks.text: It is the building of the Béla Bartók Secondary School and the Béla Bartók Music Institute (a faculty of the University of Miskolc.)

chunks.title: Palace of Music (Miskolc)
chunks.text: The Palace was designed by Gyula Waelder in Neo-baroque style and was built between 1926 and 1927.

chunks.title: Palace of Music (Miskolc)
chunks.text: The construction was financed from USA loans, just like that of the Hotel Palace in Lillafüred and the Market Hall on Búza tér.

chunks.title: List of compositions by Béla Bartók
chunks.text: This aspires to be a complete list of compositions by Béla Bartók.

chunks.title: List of compositions by Béla Bartók

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: "The Barbarian" is the opening track on the eponymous debut album of British progressive rock band Emerson, Lake & Palmer, released in 1970.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: The song is instrumental, and it is the shortest song on the album (4:27).

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: Although the composition of "The Barbarian" was attributed to the three band members, it is an arrangement for rock band of Béla Bartók’s 1911 piano piece "Allegro barbaro".

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: Although the original piece is for piano only, the band arranged the song for organ, bass, and drums too.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: The music of the song is aggressive with a hard rock influence.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: Greg Lake used a fuzz box to give his bass a fuller, guitar-like sound.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: The band members didn't give credit to Bartók, thinking that the label would arrange the matter.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: Bartók's family sued ELP for copyright infringement, but eventually, the band gave the credit to Bartók too.

chunks.title: The Barbarian (song)
chunks.text: The song was never included in a compilation album of the band until the album "The Essential Emerson, Lake & Palmer".

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: The Suite, Op. 14, Sz.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: 62, BB 70 is a piece for solo piano written by Béla Bartók.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: It was written in February 1916, published in 1918, and debuted by the composer on April 21, 1919, in Budapest.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: The Suite is one of Bartók's most significant works for piano, only comparable with his 1926 Piano Sonata.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: Though much of Bartók's work makes frequent use of Eastern European folk music, this suite is one of the few pieces without melodies of folk origin.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: However, Romanian, Arabic, and North African rhythmic influences can still be found in some movements.

chunks.title: Suite, Op. 14 (Bartók)
chunks.text: Originally intending the suite to be a five-movement work, Bartók later decided against the idea and discarded the second movement, the "Andante", which was published only posthumously in the October 1955 issue of "Új Zenei Szemle" (New Musical Review).

chunks.title: Zorian Quartet
chunks.text: The Zorian Quartet was an English all-female string quartet ensemble.

chunks.title: Zorian Quartet
chunks.text: It was founded in 1942 by and named after violinist Olive Zorian.

chunks.title: Zorian Quartet
chunks.text: It gave the premiere performances of, and made the first recordings of, several compositions for string quartet by English composers, including Benjamin Britten and Michael Tippett.

chunks.title: Zorian Quartet
chunks.text: It also gave the premiere English performances of quartets by Ernest Bloch and Béla Bartók.

chunks.title: Béla Bartók
chunks.text: Béla Viktor János Bartók ( ; ] ; 25 March 1881 – 26 September 1945) was a Hungarian composer, pianist and an ethnomusicologist.

chunks.title: Béla Bartók
chunks.text: He is considered one of the most important composers of the 20th century; he and Liszt are regarded as Hungary's greatest composers .

chunks.title: Béla Bartók
chunks.text: Through his collection and analytical study of folk music, he was one of the founders of comparative musicology, which later became ethnomusicology.

chunks.title: Benjamin Britten
chunks.text: Edward Benjamin Britten, Baron Britten {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (22 November 1913 – 4 December 1976) was an English composer, conductor and pianist.

chunks.title: Benjamin Britten
chunks.text: He was a central figure of 20th-century British classical music, with a range of works including opera, other vocal music, orchestral and chamber pieces.

chunks.title: Benjamin Britten
chunks.text: His best-known works include the opera "Peter Grimes" (1945), the "War Requiem" (1962) and the orchestral showpiece "The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra" (1945).

chunks.title: Slavery in Libya
chunks.text: Slavery in Libya has a long history and a lasting impact on the Libyan culture.

chunks.title: Slavery in Libya
chunks.text: It is closely connected with the wider context of slavery in north Africa.

chunks.title: Slavery in Libya
chunks.text: Therefore, it is better understood when this wider scope is taken into account.

chunks.title: Great Is My Country
chunks.text: Vast is my Native Land (1958), also known as "Great is my Country", (Russian: Широка страна моя родная , "Shiroka strana moya rodnaya" ), from the song of the same name, which is featured in the film, by the Russian composer Isaac Dunaevsky) was the first film shot in the Soviet wide-screen film format known as Kinopanorama.

chunks.title: Great Is My Country
chunks.text: The film was directed by Roman Karmen, known for various documentary films produced in the Soviet Union.

chunks.title: Great Is My Country
chunks.text: The music was composed by Kirill Molchanov, a noted composer of music for ballet and opera.

chunks.title: Oleg Makara
chunks.text: Oleg Makara-Kalmáry (born October 13, 1954, Czechoslovakia) is a film director, screenwriter and Slovak writer.

chunks.title: Oleg Makara
chunks.text: In 1969, he wrote his debut as a screenwriter "Pozlátené dievča" at the age of 14.

chunks.title: Oleg Makara
chunks.text: He then went on to study film directing at All States Institute (now Gerasimov Institute of Cinematography) in Moscow under Roman Karmen.

chunks.title: Oleg Makara
chunks.text: A pseudonym is after his grandfather, art carpenter, Eduard Kalmáry.

chunks.title: Oleg Makara
chunks.text: E. Kalmáry was a chief manager of water sawmill in Remetské Hámre, East Slovakia, owned by family Vanderbilts.

chunks.title: Christopher Guest
chunks.text: Christopher Haden-Guest, 5th Baron Haden-Guest (born February 5, 1948), simply known as Christopher Guest, is an English-American screenwriter, composer, musician, director, actor, and comedian who holds dual British and American citizenship.

chunks.title: Christopher Guest
chunks.text: Guest is most widely known in Hollywood for having written, directed and starred in his series of comedy films shot in mock-documentary (mockumentary) style.

chunks.title: Christopher Guest
chunks.text: Many scenes and character backgrounds in Guest's films are written and directed, although actors have no rehearsal time and the ensemble improvise scenes while filming them.

chunks.title: Christopher Guest
chunks.text: The series of films began with "This Is Spinal Tap" (directed by Rob Reiner), and continued with "Waiting for Guffman", "Best In Show", "A Mighty Wind", "For Your Consideration", and "Mascots".

chunks.title: Roman Karmen
chunks.text: Roman Lazarevich Karmen (Russian: Рома́н Ла́заревич Карме́н ; 29 November [O.S. 16 November] 1906 in Odessa – 28 April 1978 in Moscow) was a Soviet war camera-man and film director and one of the most influential figures in documentary film making.

chunks.title: Music for Dogs
chunks.text: Music for Dogs is the third studio album by American indie rock band Gardens & Villa.

chunks.title: Music for Dogs
chunks.text: Released on 21 August 2015 by independent record label Secretly Canadian.

chunks.title: Music for Dogs
chunks.text: The album was orchestrated with the help of visionary producer Jacob Portrait of Unknown Mortal Orchestra.

chunks.title: Music for Dogs
chunks.text: The band hoped ""Music for Dogs"" would maintain a wider scope than some of their other work by making it sound just as much like the futuristic music of tomorrow as it does the classic tunes of '76

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold (died 799) was an Alamannian nobleman who served the Frankish King, Charlemagne, as Margrave of the Avarian March and Prefect of Bavaria in what is now South-Eastern Germany.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold played a significant role in the integration of Bavaria into the Frankish Kingdom during Carolingian expansion in the late 8th, and early 9th centuries.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold both aided the continuity of Agilofing rule of Bavaria, as well as took steps to integrate Bavarians into the wider scope of the Frankish Kingdom.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold was related both to the Agilofing family, the ruling class of Bavaria, as well as the Carolingian family.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: The Agilofings had ruled Bavaria since Duke Garibald I in 548.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold was born into the Agilofings, and his sister Hildegard was married to Charlemagne in 771.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: From these familial connections, he was appointed Prefect of Bavaria following the deposition of Duke Tassilo III in 788.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: Gerold was heralded as a superb military commander, giving rise to his promotion to Prefect as a defender of the eastern border of the Frankish Kingdom.

chunks.title: Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria
chunks.text: In 799, Gerold is said to have fallen in battle against the Avars, shortly after the same Avars killed his ally, Erich, Duke of Friuli, through treachery.

chunks.title: Science Supercourse
chunks.text: Science Supercourse is a free online accessible educational resource currently encompassing more than 165,000 downloadable PowerPoint lectures covering four main areas of science; Public Health, Computer Engineering, Environment and Agriculture.

chunks.title: Science Supercourse
chunks.text: It represents an extension to ""Supercourse"" initiative which started out at the University of Pittsburgh by scientist Ronald LaPorte in the 80's.

chunks.title: Science Supercourse
chunks.text: It is mirrored at the Library of Alexandria, and networks over 56,000 scientists in 174 countries.

chunks.title: Science Supercourse
chunks.text: Being a useful tool for at least one million students from around the globe, Supercourse has been a well-established starting point which triggered the emergence of the new Science Supercourse in 2008 with a wider scope in terms of content and functionalities.

chunks.title: Nuremberg Trials (film)
chunks.text: The Nuremberg Trials is a 1947 Soviet-made documentary film about the trials of the Nazi leadership.

chunks.title: Nuremberg Trials (film)
chunks.text: It was produced by Roman Karmen, and was an English-language version of the Russian language film "Суд народов" (Judgment of the Peoples).

chunks.title: Women's Missionary and Service Commission
chunks.text: The Women's Missionary and Service Commission, previously known as the Women's Missionary and Service Auxiliary and abbreviated WMSC or WMSA, was a women's organization of the "old" Mennonite Church that originated out of the Mennonite Sewing Circle movement.

chunks.title: Women's Missionary and Service Commission
chunks.text: Named the WMSC in 1971, there were many precursor organizations and it has since involved into Mennonite Women USA, an organization with a much wider scope.

chunks.title: Geronimo (2014 film)
chunks.text: Geronimo is a 2014 French drama film directed by Tony Gatlif.

chunks.title: Geronimo (2014 film)
chunks.text: It premiered in the Special Screenings section at the 2014 Cannes Film Festival on 20 May.

chunks.title: Tony Gatlif
chunks.text: Tony Gatlif (born as Michel Dahmani on 10 September 1948 in Algiers) is a French film director of Romani ethnicity who also works as a screenwriter, composer, actor, and producer.

chunks.title: Korkoro
chunks.text: Korkoro ("Alone" in the Romanes) is a 2009 French drama film written and directed by Tony Gatlif, starring French actors Marc Lavoine, Marie-Josée Croze and James Thiérrée.

chunks.title: Korkoro
chunks.text: The film's cast were of many nationalities such as Albanian, Kosovar, Georgian, Serbian, French, Norwegian, and nine Romani people Gatlif recruited in Transylvania.

chunks.title: Latcho Drom
chunks.text: Latcho Drom ("safe journey") is a 1993 French documentary film directed and written by Tony Gatlif.

chunks.title: Latcho Drom
chunks.text: The movie is about the Romani people's journey from north-west India to Spain, consisting primarily of music.

chunks.title: Latcho Drom
chunks.text: The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 1993 Cannes Film Festival.

chunks.title: Exils
chunks.text: Exiles is a 2004 French film by Tony Gatlif.

chunks.title: Exils
chunks.text: The film follows two young bohemians, Zano and Naima.

chunks.title: Exils
chunks.text: After having sex, the two spontaneously decide that they will travel to Algeria, where Naima's parents come from, and where Zano's (Romain Duris) "pied-noir" parents were once exiled.

chunks.title: Exils
chunks.text: Their adventurous journey to Algiers is full of character exploration, relationship hiccups and imagery.

chunks.title: Exils
chunks.text: The film was also a homecoming for Gatlif himself, seeing him return to Algeria 43 years after he left.

chunks.title: Je suis né d'une cigogne
chunks.text: Je suis né d'une cigogne (English: Children of the Stork ) is a 1999 French road movie directed by Tony Gatlif, starring Romain Duris, Rona Hartner, Ouassini Embarek, Christine Pignet and Marc Nouyrigat.

chunks.title: Je suis né d'une cigogne
chunks.text: Following its French release, it received mixed reviews but was nominated for a "Golden Bayard" at the "International Festival of Francophone Film" in Namur, Belgium.

chunks.title: Tchavolo Schmitt
chunks.text: Tchavolo Schmitt (born 1954 in Paris) is a gypsy jazz guitarist.

chunks.title: Tchavolo Schmitt
chunks.text: Schmitt performed as a member of various ensembles in the 1970s.

chunks.title: Tchavolo Schmitt
chunks.text: Then he settled in Strasbourg and left the professional circuit for a time, releasing solo albums in 2000.

chunks.title: Tchavolo Schmitt
chunks.text: He played Miraldo in the Tony Gatlif film "Swing."

chunks.title: Rona Hartner
chunks.text: Rona Hartner (born March 9, 1973, Bucharest) is a Romanian actress, painter and singer.

chunks.title: Rona Hartner
chunks.text: She is best known for her role in Tony Gatlif's film Gadjo Dilo.

chunks.title: Rona Hartner
chunks.text: Hartner currently focuses on her music career, specializing in Gypsy music.

chunks.title: Transylvania (film)
chunks.text: Transylvania is a 2006 French drama film starring Asia Argento.

chunks.title: Transylvania (film)
chunks.text: In 2006, Director Tony Gatlif and composer Delphine Mantoulet won the "Georges Delerue Prize" at the Flanders International Film Festival for the score, and Gatlif was nominated for the "Grand Prix" award.

chunks.title: Transylvania (film)
chunks.text: "Transylvania" premiered at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival in France on May 28, and premiered in the United States on March 16, 2007 at the Cleveland International Film Festival and in the United Kingdom at the Cambridge Film Festival on July 6, 2007 (with a later theatrical release on August 10, 2007).

chunks.title: David O. Russell
chunks.text: David Owen Russell (born August 20, 1958) is an American film director, screenwriter, and producer.

chunks.title: David O. Russell
chunks.text: His early directing career includes the comedy films "Spanking the Monkey" (1994), "Flirting with Disaster" (1996), "Three Kings" (1999) and "I ♥ Huckabees" (2004).

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: Paul M. Birdsall (????

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: -May 2, 1970) was a historian and diplomat.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: Educated at St. Paul's School, he earned his doctorate at Harvard University in 1928, where he studied under the influence of Charles Howard McIlwain.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: He taught European history at Williams College as assistant and then associate professor.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: In 1936 he became Dean of Students at Williams College.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: He was also a trustee of Vassar College.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: He then entered a career in government service.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: During World War Two, he served in the Office of Strategic Services.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: In 1947, he was assistant military attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Paris.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: In 1948-1949 he worked for the Brookings Institution.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: He later served as a reserve foreign service officer in Paris and at the U.S. Embassy in Stockholm.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: According to obituaries, however, he actually worked for the Central Intelligence Agency from 1949 to 1962.

chunks.title: Paul M. Birdsall
chunks.text: Birdsall died at the age of seventy in Christiansted, United States Virgin Islands, where he had been in retirement for eight years.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: Hans Wilhelm Gatzke (1915–1987) was a historian of German foreign policy since World War I.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: Born in Dülken, Germany, he attended the University of Bonn and the University of Munich, finally graduating from Williams College in 1938.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: After serving in the United States Army during World War II as a second lieutenant, he received his M.A. (1939) and PhD.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: (1947) from Harvard University.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: He taught at Johns Hopkins University from 1947 to 1964, during which time he was awarded a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1956.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: He joined the department of history at Yale University in 1965 and remained there until his retirement in 1986.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: Gatzke anonymously funded a prize, awarded biennially by the American Historical Association, in honor of Paul M. Birdsall (who was Dean of Students at Williams when Gatzke arrived there in the late 1930s) for the best work in the field of European military or strategic history since 1870.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: His involvement was revealed upon his death in 1987.

chunks.title: Hans W. Gatzke
chunks.text: He is remembered by a named professorship in his honor (the Hans W. Gatzke '38 Professor of Modern European History) at Williams College.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: Edward Everett Wilson was an African-American lawyer born in Texas, on January 1, 1867.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: He initially attended Oberlin College, but later transferred to Williams College.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: He received his degree, with honors, from Williams College in 1892.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: Wilson was elected to the Phi Beta Kappa honorary society, one of the first African Americans to attain that honor.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: Subsequently, he obtained his Bachelor of Laws degree from Howard University in 1894.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: Moving to Chicago, he filled the post of assistant state attorney for Cook County, Illinois, from 1912 until his retirement in 1947.

chunks.title: Edward E. Wilson
chunks.text: Wilson died in France while on vacation on February 21, 1952.

chunks.title: Brian Lukacher
chunks.text: Brian Lukacher is professor of art at Vassar College where he has taught since 1986.

chunks.title: Brian Lukacher
chunks.text: Lukacher received his M.A. from Williams College, and received his PhD from the University of Delaware.

chunks.title: Brian Lukacher
chunks.text: Following his time at Williams College, Lukacher received the Chester A. Dale and Samuel H. Kress Fellowship for 1981 at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C. His research interests relate to the social history and esthetic philosophy of late eighteenth and nineteenth-century British art and architecture.

chunks.text: Robert Earl Wise (September 10, 1914 – September 14, 2005) was an American film director, producer and editor.

chunks.title: Robert Wise
chunks.text: He won Academy Awards for Best Director and Best Picture for both "West Side Story" (1961) and "The Sound of Music" (1965).

chunks.title: Robert Wise
chunks.text: He was also nominated for Best Film Editing for "Citizen Kane" (1941) and directed and produced "The Sand Pebbles" (1966), which was nominated for Best Picture.

chunks.title: Cash (1933 film)
chunks.text: Cash is a 1933 British comedy film directed by Zoltan Korda and starring Edmund Gwenn, Wendy Barrie and Robert Donat.

chunks.title: Cash (1933 film)
chunks.text: It was made by Alexander Korda's London Film Productions.

chunks.title: Suining
chunks.text: Suining (; Sichuanese Pinyin: Xunin; Sichuanese pronunciation: ; ) is a prefecture-level city of eastern Sichuan province in Southwest China.

chunks.title: Suining
chunks.text: In 2002, Suining had a population of 658,798.

chunks.title: Daying County
chunks.text: Daying County () is a county of Sichuan province, China, under the administration of Suining City and in the central part of the Sichuan Basin.

chunks.title: Daying County
chunks.text: In 2002, it had a population of 520,000 residing in an area of 703 km2 .

chunks.title: Daying County
chunks.text: Daying is remarkable for being the home of the "Chinese Dead Sea", a tourist attraction that is based on a salt lake with 9 times the salinity of the ocean and which constitutes the largest indoor water park in China.

chunks.title: Daying County
chunks.text: The G42 Shanghai–Chengdu Expressway and Dazhou–Chengdu Railway (达成铁路) traverses east–west through the entire length of the county.

chunks.title: Qionghai
chunks.text: Qionghai () is one of the seven county-level cities of Hainan province, China.

chunks.title: Qionghai
chunks.text: Although called a "city", Qionghai refers to a large land area in Hainan - an area which was once a county.

chunks.title: Qionghai
chunks.text: Within this area is the main city, Qionghai City.

chunks.title: Qionghai
chunks.text: It is located in the east of the island at the mouth of the Wanquan River, 86 km from the provincial capital of Haikou.

chunks.title: Qionghai
chunks.text: It has an area of 1692 km2 and in 2010, it had a population of 483,217.

chunks.title: Sex (I'm A...)
chunks.text: "Sex (I'm A..

chunks.title: Sex (I'm A...)
chunks.text: is a song by the American band Berlin from their second album "Pleasure Victim".

chunks.title: Sex (I'm A...)
chunks.text: The song was co-written by group members John Crawford, Terri Nunn and David Diamond and sung as a duet by Crawford and Nunn.

chunks.title: Candyland (album)
chunks.text: Candyland is the tenth studio album by Italian gothic metal band Theatres des Vampires, released through Scarlet Records on 14 October 2016.

chunks.title: Candyland (album)
chunks.text: Initially announced on 7 July 2016, it is their first studio album in 5 years since "Moonlight Waltz", and also their first release with guitarist Giorgio Ferrante, who replaced Stephan Benfante early in 2016.

chunks.title: Candyland (album)
chunks.text: It is noticeably more guitar-driven than the band's previous releases with Sonya Scarlet on vocals, and its lyrics focus less on the vampiric and occult themes the band is famous for.

chunks.title: Candyland (album)
chunks.text: A music video for the track "Morgana Effect" was uploaded to the band's official YouTube channel on 29 September 2016.

chunks.title: Sonya Scarlet
chunks.text: Sonya Scarlet (born 2 April 1980) is the singer and lyricist of the Italian extreme gothic metal band Theatres des Vampires.

chunks.title: Terri Nunn
chunks.text: Terri Kathleen Nunn (born June 26, 1961), is an American singer and actress.

chunks.title: Terri Nunn
chunks.text: She is best known as the lead vocalist of the new wave/synthpop band Berlin.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: Pleasure Victim is the second studio album by the American new wave band Berlin.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: The original album was recorded in 1982 and released that year by independent label Enigma Records.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: After considerable attention received by the second single, "Sex (I'm A..

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: ", the album was re-released worldwide by Geffen Records on January 26, 1983.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: The album marked the return of lead singer Terri Nunn to the group.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: To date, it is Berlin's best-selling album and was certified gold by the RIAA in September 1984 and platinum in February 1993.

chunks.title: Pleasure Victim
chunks.text: It is the only one of Berlin's albums to be certified platinum and the first that reached gold; two subsequent studio albums and a greatest hits compilation were also certified gold.

chunks.title: Berlin (band)
chunks.text: Berlin is an American new wave band.

chunks.title: Berlin (band)
chunks.text: The group was formed in Orange County in 1979 by John Crawford (bass guitar).

chunks.title: Berlin (band)
chunks.text: Band members included Crawford, Terri Nunn (vocals), David Diamond (keyboards), Ric Olsen (guitar), Matt Reid (keyboards) and Rod Learned (drums).

chunks.title: Berlin (band)
chunks.text: The band gained mainstream-commercial success in the early 1980s with singles including "The Metro", "Sex (I'm A..

chunks.title: Berlin (band)
chunks.text: ", "No More Words" and then in the mid 1980s with the chart-topping single "Take My Breath Away" from the 1986 film "Top Gun".

chunks.title: The Georgia Peaches
chunks.text: The Georgia Peaches (also known as Follow That Car) is a 1980 American made-for-television action-adventure comedy film produced by Roger Corman as a pilot for a proposed television series.

chunks.title: The Georgia Peaches
chunks.text: It starred Tanya Tucker, Terri Nunn and Dirk Benedict as three friends extorted into becoming undercover FBI agents for the government and was broadcast on CBS on November 8, 1980.

chunks.title: Information (Berlin album)
chunks.text: Information is the first album by Berlin, released in 1980 by Vinyl Records.

chunks.title: Information (Berlin album)
chunks.text: It was recorded during the period when Terri Nunn had temporarily left the band to pursue an acting career and Virginia Macolino performed the lead vocals.

chunks.title: Information (Berlin album)
chunks.text: Several songs were written by previous lead singer Toni Childs who went solo prior to the album's release.

chunks.title: Thank God It's Friday (film)
chunks.text: Thank God It's Friday is a 1978 American musical comedy film directed by Robert Klane and produced by Motown Productions and Casablanca FilmWorks for Columbia Pictures (whose torch-holding mascot, in a specially produced animation, dances to disco music before the opening credits).

chunks.title: Thank God It's Friday (film)
chunks.text: Produced at the height of the disco craze, the film features The Commodores performing "Too Hot ta Trot", and Donna Summer performing "Last Dance", which won the Academy Award for Best Song in 1978.

chunks.title: Thank God It's Friday (film)
chunks.text: The film features an early performance by Jeff Goldblum and the first major screen appearance by Debra Winger.

chunks.title: Thank God It's Friday (film)
chunks.text: The film also features Terri Nunn who would go on to fame in the 1980s new wave group Berlin.

chunks.title: Moment of Truth (Terri Nunn album)
chunks.text: Moment of Truth is the début and sole solo album from American singer and actress Terri Nunn, best known as lead singer of the American New Wave/Synthpop band Berlin.

chunks.title: Boeing Field
chunks.text: Boeing Field, officially King County International Airport (IATA: BFI, ICAO: KBFI, FAA LID: BFI) , is a public airport owned and operated by King County, five miles south of downtown Seattle, Washington.

chunks.title: Boeing Field
chunks.text: The airport is sometimes referred to as KCIA, but this is not the airport identifier.

chunks.title: Boeing Field
chunks.text: The airport has some passenger service, but is mostly used by general aviation and cargo.

chunks.title: Boeing Field
chunks.text: It is named after the founder of Boeing, William E. Boeing.

chunks.title: Sam Chu Lin
chunks.text: Samuel "Sam" Chu-Lin (; c. 1939 – March 5, 2006) was an American journalist.

chunks.title: Sam Chu Lin
chunks.text: Born in Greenville, Mississippi, Chu-Lin died at the age of 67 in Burbank, California.

chunks.title: Sam Chu Lin
chunks.text: He became ill at Bob Hope Airport in Burbank after flying in from Phoenix and was taken to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead, said his son, Mark.

chunks.title: Burbank–Bob Hope Airport station
chunks.text: Burbank-Bob Hope Airport is an unstaffed Amtrak and Metrolink rail station at Bob Hope Airport in the city of Burbank, California.

chunks.title: Burbank–Bob Hope Airport station
chunks.text: It is served by both Amtrak's "Pacific Surfliner" from San Luis Obispo to San Diego and Metrolink's Ventura County Line from Los Angeles Union Station to east Ventura.

chunks.title: Burbank–Bob Hope Airport station
chunks.text: The ten "Pacific Surfliner" trains that serve the station daily and 29 Metrolink trains that serve the station each weekday connect arrivals from the airport to downtown Los Angeles' Union Station in about 30 minutes.

chunks.title: Burbank–Bob Hope Airport station
chunks.text: Amtrak's "Coast Starlight" which travels between Seattle, Washington and Los Angeles also stops here.

chunks.title: Bob Hope School
chunks.text: Bob Hope School is a charter school system in Port Arthur, Texas.

chunks.title: Bob Hope School
chunks.text: It has two campuses, Bob Hope Elementary Campus and Bob Hope Middle/High School.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Patriotic Hall
chunks.text: Bob Hope Patriotic Hall is a 10-story building that was dedicated as Patriotic Hall by the Los Angeles Board of Supervisors in 1925 and was built to serve veterans of Indian Wars, Spanish–American War, World War I and to support the Grand Army of the Republic.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Patriotic Hall
chunks.text: It serves as the home of the Los Angeles County Department of Military and Veterans Affairs.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Patriotic Hall
chunks.text: Patriotic hall was rededicated to honor of Bob Hope and renamed "Bob Hope Patriotic Hall" on November 12, 2004.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Patriotic Hall
chunks.text: Ruth A. Wong became the Director of Military and Veterans Affairs on July 16, 2013.

chunks.title: Downtown Burbank station
chunks.text: Downtown Burbank is a passenger rail station near downtown Burbank, California.

chunks.title: Downtown Burbank station
chunks.text: It is served by Metrolink's Antelope Valley Line to Lancaster and Ventura County Line to East Ventura with both terminating at Los Angeles Union Station.

chunks.title: Downtown Burbank station
chunks.text: Amtrak trains do not stop at this station; rather, Amtrak trains stop at the Burbank Airport station, adjacent to Bob Hope Airport, several miles to the northwest of downtown Burbank.

chunks.title: Downtown Burbank station
chunks.text: Megabus started providing long distance motorcoach service from the station on August 15, 2013.

chunks.title: Judith Richards Hope
chunks.text: Judith Richards Hope (born November 1940) is a lawyer, law professor, and corporate director.

chunks.title: Judith Richards Hope
chunks.text: She is a visiting law professor at Georgetown University in addition to being the president and CEO of an international consulting firm, Hope & Company, P.C.

chunks.title: Judith Richards Hope
chunks.text: She is the former daughter-in-law of Bob Hope, as she was the first wife of Bob Hope's son, Tony Hope.

chunks.title: JetBlue Flight 292
chunks.text: JetBlue Flight 292 was a scheduled flight from Bob Hope Airport in Burbank, California to John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City.

chunks.title: JetBlue Flight 292
chunks.text: On September 21, 2005, Captain Scott Burke executed an emergency landing in the Airbus A320-200 at Los Angeles International Airport after the nose gear jammed in an abnormal position.

chunks.title: JetBlue Flight 292
chunks.text: No one was injured.

chunks.title: Boeing Plant 2
chunks.text: Boeing Plant 2 (also known as Air Force Plant 17) was a factory building which was built in 1936 by the Boeing Corporation in King County, Washington in the United States.

chunks.title: Boeing Plant 2
chunks.text: By the time production ceased in the building, the plant had built half of the Boeing B-17 Flying Fortresses, the Boeing 307s, the Boeing 377s, some of the Boeing B-29 Superfortresses, Boeing B-50 Superfortresses, B-47 Stratojets, B-52 Stratofortresses, and the initial Boeing 737s.

chunks.title: Boeing Plant 2
chunks.text: It was located between the Duwamish River and Boeing Field.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Airport
chunks.text: Bob Hope Airport, branded as Hollywood Burbank Airport (IATA: BUR, ICAO: KBUR, FAA LID: BUR) is a public airport 3 mi northwest of downtown Burbank, in Los Angeles County, California.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Airport
chunks.text: The airport serves the northern Greater Los Angeles area, including Glendale, Pasadena, and the San Fernando Valley.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Airport
chunks.text: It is closer to Griffith Park and Hollywood than Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), and is the only airport in the area with a direct rail connection to downtown Los Angeles.

chunks.title: Bob Hope Airport
chunks.text: Non-stop flights mostly serve cities in the western United States, while JetBlue Airways has a daily red-eye flight to New York City.

chunks.title: Botanical garden
chunks.text: A botanical garden or botanic garden is a garden dedicated to the collection, cultivation and display of a wide range of plants labelled with their botanical names.

chunks.title: Botanical garden
chunks.text: It may contain specialist plant collections such as cacti and other succulent plants, herb gardens, plants from particular parts of the world, and so on; there may be greenhouses, shadehouses, again with special collections such as tropical plants, alpine plants, or other exotic plants. Visitor services at a botanical garden might include tours, educational displays, art exhibitions, book rooms, open-air theatrical and musical performances, and other entertainment.

chunks.title: International Plant Names Index
chunks.text: The International Plant Names Index (IPNI) describes itself as "a database of the names and associated basic bibliographical details of seed plants, ferns and lycophytes." Coverage of plant names is best at the rank of species and genus.

chunks.title: International Plant Names Index
chunks.text: It includes basic bibliographical details, associated with the names, and its goals include eliminating the need for repeated reference to primary sources for basic bibliographic information about plant names.

chunks.title: Grex (horticulture)
chunks.text: The term grex (pl.

chunks.title: Grex (horticulture)
chunks.text: greges or grexes; abbreviation gx), derived from the Latin noun "grex, gregis" meaning 'flock', has been coined to expand botanical nomenclature to describe hybrids of orchids, based solely on their parentage.

chunks.title: Grex (horticulture)
chunks.text: Grex names are one of the three categories of plant names governed by the International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants; within a grex the "cultivar group" category can be used to refer to plants by their shared characteristics (rather than by their parentage), and individual orchid plants can be selected (and propagated) and named as cultivars.

chunks.title: Zygotritonia
chunks.text: Zygotritonia is a genus of herbaceous, perennial and bulbous plants in the Iris family (Iridaceae).

chunks.title: Zygotritonia
chunks.text: It contains four species distributed in Tropical Africa.

chunks.title: Zygotritonia
chunks.text: The genus name is derived from the word zygomorphic (meaning bilabiate), and the apparent resemblance to some species in the genus "Tritonia".

chunks.title: List of plants by common name
chunks.text: This is a list of plants organized by their common names. However, the common names of plants often vary from region to region, which is why most plant encyclopedias refer to plants using their scientific names, in other words using binomials or "Latin" names.

chunks.title: Phyteuma
chunks.text: Phyteuma is a genus of flowering plants in the family Campanulaceae, native to Europe and Morocco.

chunks.title: Tritoniopsis
chunks.text: Tritoniopsis is a genus of flowering plants in the family Iridaceae, first described as a genus in 1926.

chunks.title: Tritoniopsis
chunks.text: The entire genus is endemic to Cape Province in South Africa.

chunks.title: Tritoniopsis
chunks.text: The genus name refers to the African genus "Tritonia" and is combined with the Greek word "opsis", meaning "look-alike".

chunks.title: Vascular plant
chunks.text: Vascular plants (from Latin "vasculum": duct), also known as tracheophytes (from the equivalent Greek term "trachea") and also higher plants, form a large group of plants (c. 308,312 accepted known species ) that are defined as those land plants that have lignified tissues (the xylem) for conducting water and minerals throughout the plant.

chunks.title: Vascular plant
chunks.text: They also have a specialized non-lignified tissue (the phloem) to conduct products of photosynthesis.

chunks.title: Vascular plant
chunks.text: Vascular plants include the clubmosses, horsetails, ferns, gymnosperms (including conifers) and angiosperms (flowering plants).

chunks.title: Vascular plant
chunks.text: Scientific names for the group include Tracheophyta and Tracheobionta.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: Thonningia is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Balanophoraceae containing the single species Thonningia sanguinea.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: It is distributed throughout much of southern and western Africa, particularly the tropical regions.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: Common names for the plant include ground pineapple.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: A familiar plant to humans, it has an extremely long list of common names in many African languages.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: Many names are inspired by the resemblance of the plant's inflorescence to a pineapple or palm tree.

chunks.title: Thonningia
chunks.text: Some of the names can be translated as pineapple of the bush (from Anyi), duiker's kolanut (from Igala), and crown of the ground (from Yoruba).

chunks.title: Tritonia (plant)
chunks.text: Tritonia (flame freesia) is a genus of flowering plants in the iris family first described as a genus in 1802.

chunks.title: Tritonia (plant)
chunks.text: They are naturally distributed across southern Africa, with a high concentration of species in Cape Province of western South Africa.

chunks.title: Tritonia (plant)
chunks.text: The genus is closely related to the genus "Ixia".

chunks.title: Western Allied invasion of Germany
chunks.text: The Western Allied invasion of Germany was coordinated by the Western Allies during the final months of hostilities in the European theatre of World War II.

chunks.title: Western Allied invasion of Germany
chunks.text: The Allied invasion of Germany started with the Western Allies crossing the Rhine River in March 1945 before fanning out and overrunning all of western Germany from the Baltic in the north to Austria in the south before the Germans surrendered on 8 May 1945.

chunks.title: Western Allied invasion of Germany
chunks.text: This is known as the "Central Europe Campaign" in United States military histories.

chunks.title: Battle of Langemarck (1917)
chunks.text: The Battle of Langemarck from 16–18 August 1917, was the second Allied general attack of the Third Battle of Ypres, during the First World War.

chunks.title: Battle of Langemarck (1917)
chunks.text: The battle took place near Ypres in Belgian Flanders, on the Western Front against the German 4th Army.

chunks.title: Battle of Langemarck (1917)
chunks.text: The French First Army had a big success on the northern flank and the main British gain of ground occurred near Langemark, adjacent to the French.

chunks.title: Battle of Langemarck (1917)
chunks.text: The Allied attack succeeded from Langemarck to Drie Grachten (Three Canals) but early advances in the south on the Gheluvelt Plateau were forced back by powerful German counter-attacks.

chunks.title: Matthew Ridgway
chunks.text: General Matthew Bunker Ridgway (March 3, 1895 – July 26, 1993) was the 19 Chief of Staff of the United States Army.

chunks.title: Matthew Ridgway
chunks.text: He served with great distinction during World War II, where he was the Commanding General (CG) of the 82nd Airborne Division, leading it in action in Sicily, Italy and Normandy, before taking command of the newly formed XVIII Airborne Corps in August 1944, holding this post until the end of the war, commanding it in the Battle of the Bulge, Operation Varsity and the Western Allied invasion of Germany.

chunks.title: Battle of Savo Island
chunks.text: The Battle of Savo Island, also known as the First Battle of Savo Island and, in Japanese sources, as the First Battle of the Solomon Sea (第一次ソロモン海戦 , Dai-ichi-ji Soromon Kaisen ) , and colloquially among Allied Guadalcanal veterans as The Battle of the Five Sitting Ducks, was a naval battle of the Pacific Campaign of World War II between the Imperial Japanese Navy and Allied naval forces.

chunks.title: Battle of Savo Island
chunks.text: The battle took place on August 8–9, 1942 and was the first major naval engagement of the Guadalcanal campaign, and the first of several naval battles in the straits later named Ironbottom Sound, near the island of Guadalcanal.

chunks.title: Battle of the Canal du Nord
chunks.text: The Battle of Canal du Nord was part of a general Allied offensive against German positions on the Western Front during the Hundred Days Offensive of World War I.

chunks.title: Battle of the Canal du Nord
chunks.text: The battle took place in the Nord-Pas-de-Calais region of France, along an incomplete portion of the Canal du Nord and on the outskirts of Cambrai between 27 September and 1 October 1918.

chunks.title: Battle of the Canal du Nord
chunks.text: To avoid the risk of having extensive German reserves massed against a single Allied attack, the assault along the Canal du Nord was undertaken as part of a number of closely sequenced Allied attacks at separate points along the Western Front.

chunks.title: Battle of the Canal du Nord
chunks.text: It began one day after the Meuse-Argonne Offensive, one day before an offensive in the Flanders region of Belgium and two days before the Battle of St. Quentin Canal.

chunks.title: 21st Army Group
chunks.text: The 21st Army Group was a World War II British headquarters formation, in command of two field armies and other supporting units, consisting primarily of the British Second Army and the First Canadian Army.

chunks.title: 21st Army Group
chunks.text: Established in London during July 1943, under the command of Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force (SHAEF), it was assigned to Operation Overlord, the Western Allied invasion of Europe, and was an important Allied force in the European Theatre.

chunks.title: 21st Army Group
chunks.text: The 21st Army Group operated in Northern France, Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany from June 1944 until the end of the war in Europe in May 1945, after which it was redesignated the British Army of the Rhine (BAOR).

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: The Battle of Clitheroe was a battle between a force of Scots and English knights and men at arms which took place on 10 June 1138 during the period of The Anarchy.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: The battle was fought on the southern edge of the Bowland Fells, at Clitheroe, Lancashire.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: It took place in the course of an invasion of England by King David I of Scotland.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: In the summer of 1138, King David split his army into two forces.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: One of them, commanded by William fitz Duncan, Mormaer of Moray, marched into Lancashire.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: There he harried Furness and Craven.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: On 10 June, William fitz Duncan was met by a force of knights and men-at-arms.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: A pitched battle took place and the result was that the English army was routed.

chunks.title: Battle of Clitheroe
chunks.text: The battle was a prelude to the Battle of the Standard later in the summer, where the result was reversed.

chunks.title: Operation Epsom
chunks.text: Operation Epsom, also known as the First Battle of the Odon, was a British Second World War offensive that took place between 26 and 30 June 1944, during the Battle of Normandy.

chunks.title: Operation Epsom
chunks.text: The offensive was intended to outflank and seize the German-occupied city of Caen, an important Allied objective, in the early stages of Operation Overlord, the Allied invasion of north-west Europe.

chunks.title: Battle of Fredericksburg
chunks.text: The Battle of Fredericksburg was fought December 11–15, 1862, in and around Fredericksburg, Virginia, between General Robert E. Lee's Confederate Army of Northern Virginia and the Union Army of the Potomac, commanded by Major General Ambrose Burnside, as part of the American Civil War.

chunks.title: Battle of Fredericksburg
chunks.text: The Union Army's futile frontal attacks on December 13 against entrenched Confederate defenders on the heights behind the city are remembered as one of the most one-sided battles of the war, with Union casualties more than three times as heavy as those suffered by the Confederates.

chunks.title: Battle of Fredericksburg
chunks.text: A visitor to the battlefield described the battle to U.S. President Abraham Lincoln as a "butchery."

chunks.title: Allied invasion of Italy
chunks.text: The Allied invasion of Italy was the Allied amphibious landing on mainland Italy that took place on 3 September 1943 during the early stages of the Italian Campaign of World War II.

chunks.title: Allied invasion of Italy
chunks.text: The operation was undertaken by General Sir Harold Alexander's 15th Army Group (comprising General Mark W. Clark and General Bernard Montgomery's British Eighth Army) and followed the successful invasion of Sicily.

chunks.title: Allied invasion of Italy
chunks.text: The main invasion force landed around Salerno on 9 September on the western coast in Operation Avalanche, while two supporting operations took place in Calabria (Operation Baytown) and Taranto (Operation Slapstick).

chunks.title: Francis Irby Gwaltney
chunks.text: Francis Irby Gwaltney (born 9 September 1921 in Traskwood, Arkansas died 27 February 1981) was a prolific Southern American author.

chunks.title: Francis Irby Gwaltney
chunks.text: He was the most well known author to have set his books in Arkansas.

chunks.title: Tarık Buğra
chunks.text: Tarık Buğra or born Süleyman Tarık Buğra (2 September 1918 - 26 February 1994) was Turkish journalist, novelist and short story author.

chunks.title: Tarık Buğra
chunks.text: He was well known author at Republican literature in his country.

chunks.title: Tarık Buğra
chunks.text: He was honoured as State Artist in 1991.

chunks.title: Tarık Buğra
chunks.text: Buğra is father of scientist Ayşe Buğra.

chunks.title: Roger Angell
chunks.text: Roger Angell (born September 19, 1920) is an American essayist known for his writing on sports, especially baseball.

chunks.title: Roger Angell
chunks.text: He has been a regular contributor to "The New Yorker" and was its chief fiction editor for many years.

chunks.title: Roger Angell
chunks.text: He has written numerous works of fiction, non-fiction, and criticism, and for many years wrote an annual Christmas poem for "The New Yorker".

chunks.title: Season Ticket: A Baseball Companion
chunks.text: Season Ticket: A Baseball Companion is a 1988 book written by Roger Angell, whose previous works include "Five Seasons", "Late Innings", and the New York Times best-seller, "The Summer Game".

chunks.title: Season Ticket: A Baseball Companion
chunks.text: Angell is considered one of the country's premier baseball writers.

chunks.title: Harry Stephen Keeler
chunks.text: Harry Stephen Keeler (November 3, 1890 – January 22, 1967) was a prolific but little-known American author of mysteries and science fiction.

chunks.title: Gerard Mannix Flynn
chunks.text: Gerard Mannix Flynn, sometimes written only as Mannix Flynn, is an Irish politician.

chunks.title: Gerard Mannix Flynn
chunks.text: He was born in Dublin in May 1957.

chunks.title: Gerard Mannix Flynn
chunks.text: Aside from his work on the Dublin City Council he is also a well known author and playwright, having written the novel "Nothing To Say" in 1983 and the play "James X" in 2002.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper was written in the 1690s and is not a very well known work.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: John Dryden was a very well known author, however, this work is lesser known.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: England during this time was going through many changes.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: There were political changes, religious changes, and there was a lot of unrest in the everyday lives of the people.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: However, this play shows none of this unrest.

chunks.title: Mr. Limberham; or, the Kind Keeper
chunks.text: This play has people who are on the wealthy side of life and are not dealing with the real life problems of other people.

chunks.title: Sing Sing Nights (film)
chunks.text: Sing Sing Nights is a 1934 American film directed by Lewis D. Collins, based on the 1927 novel by American Author Harry Stephen Keeler (Hutchinson 1927, Dutton 1928, Ward & Lock 1929).

chunks.title: Abdelaziz al-Maghrawi
chunks.text: Abu Faris abd al-Aziz al-Maghrawi was a Moroccan poet and the first known author of a qasida written in malhun.

chunks.title: Abdelaziz al-Maghrawi
chunks.text: He was one of the poets of the court of the Saadian sultan Ahmad al-Mansur (1578–1602).

chunks.title: Abdelaziz al-Maghrawi
chunks.text: He is still well known in Morocco.

chunks.title: Abdelaziz al-Maghrawi
chunks.text: His name is preserved in the proverb "Nothing that is long is of interest except the palmtree and al-Maghrawi".

chunks.title: The Mysterious Mr. Wong
chunks.text: The Mysterious Mr. Wong is a tongue-in-cheek 1934 mystery film starring Bela Lugosi as a powerful Fu Manchu type criminal mastermind of the Chinatown underworld, and Wallace Ford as a wisecracking reporter.

chunks.title: The Mysterious Mr. Wong
chunks.text: The film is based on Harry Stephen Keeler's 1928 short story "The Strange Adventure of the Twelve Coins of Confucius" one of three stories in Keeler's book "Sing Sing Nights".

chunks.title: The Mysterious Mr. Wong
chunks.text: Despite the name of the title character and being directed by William Nigh, it has no relation to Monogram Pictures later Mr Wong film series.

chunks.title: The Mysterious Mr. Wong
chunks.text: The character of Mr. Wong does not appear in the original story.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (film)
chunks.text: Something Wicked This Way Comes is a 1983 American horror fantasy film directed by Jack Clayton and produced by Walt Disney Productions from a screenplay written by Ray Bradbury, based on his novel of the same name.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (film)
chunks.text: The novel's title was taken directly from a line in Act IV of William Shakespeare's "Macbeth": "By the pricking of my thumbs / Something wicked this way comes."

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (film)
chunks.text: The film stars Jason Robards, Jonathan Pryce, Diane Ladd, and Pam Grier.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (film)
chunks.text: It was shot in Vermont and at the Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (film)
chunks.text: The film had a troubled production – Clayton fell out with Bradbury over an uncredited script rewrite, and after test screenings of the director's cut failed to meet the studio's expectations, Disney sidelined Clayton, fired the original editor, and scrapped the original score, spending some $5 million and many months re-shooting, re-editing and re-scoring the film, before its eventual release.

chunks.title: Cheyne Coates
chunks.text: April M. Coates (born 6 September 1970) is an Australian dance music and pop singer-songwriter and producer, who performs as Cheyne Coates or Cheyne.

chunks.title: Cheyne Coates
chunks.text: Coates on lead vocals and Andrew Van Dorsselaer (a.k.a. Andy Van) on background vocals and DJ were the pop duo, Madison Avenue (1998–2003).

chunks.title: Cheyne Coates
chunks.text: Their song "Don't Call Me Baby" peaked at number two on the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Singles Chart in 1999 and at the top of the UK Singles Chart and the "Billboard" dance charts in 2000.

chunks.title: Cheyne Coates
chunks.text: Since the break-up of Madison Avenue in 2003, Cheyne recorded an album, "Something Wicked This Way Comes", and its first single "I've Got Your Number" which reached No. 26 in 2004.

chunks.title: The Wind in the Willows
chunks.text: The Wind in the Willows is a children's novel by Kenneth Grahame, first published in 1908.

chunks.title: The Wind in the Willows
chunks.text: Alternately slow moving and fast paced, it focuses on four anthropomorphised animals in a pastoral version of Edwardian England.

chunks.title: The Wind in the Willows
chunks.text: The novel is notable for its mixture of mysticism, adventure, morality and camaraderie, and celebrated for its evocation of the nature of the Thames Valley.

chunks.title: Framing Armageddon: Something Wicked Part 1
chunks.text: Framing Armageddon: Something Wicked Part 1 is the eighth studio album from Iced Earth, released on September 11, 2007.

chunks.title: Framing Armageddon: Something Wicked Part 1
chunks.text: It is part one of two concept albums based on a trilogy of songs from Iced Earth's fifth studio album, "Something Wicked This Way Comes".

chunks.title: Framing Armageddon: Something Wicked Part 1
chunks.text: The saga, aptly titled the Something Wicked Saga, tells the fictional history of mankind, from its creation to its destruction.

chunks.title: Framing Armageddon: Something Wicked Part 1
chunks.text: It is the second and final album with vocalist Tim "Ripper" Owens.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (novel)
chunks.text: Something Wicked This Way Comes is a 1962 dark fantasy novel by Ray Bradbury.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (novel)
chunks.text: It is about 13-year-old best friends, Jim Nightshade and William Halloway, and their nightmarish experience with a traveling carnival that comes to their Midwestern town one October, and how the boys learn about combatting fear.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (novel)
chunks.text: The carnival's leader is the mysterious "Mr. Dark" who seemingly wields the power to grant the citizenry's secret desires.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (novel)
chunks.text: In reality, Dark is a malevolent being who, like the carnival, live off the life force of those they enslave.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (novel)
chunks.text: Mr. Dark's presence is countered by that of Will's father, Charles Halloway, who harbors his own secret fear of growing older because he feels he is too old to be Will's dad.

chunks.title: Carnival Arcane
chunks.text: Carnival Arcane is the 14th album by dark ambient band Midnight Syndicate, released in 2011.

chunks.title: Carnival Arcane
chunks.text: The theme of the CD surrounds a fictional turn of the century traveling circus called The Lancaster Rigby Carnival.

chunks.title: Carnival Arcane
chunks.text: The CD was inspired by research into carnivals of that time period and Ray Bradbury's "Something Wicked This Way Comes".

chunks.title: Carnival Arcane
chunks.text: It features voiceovers by actor, Jason Carter.

chunks.title: Carnival Arcane
chunks.text: In 2012, the album won the Best CD category in the 2012 Rondo Hatton Classic Horror Awards.

chunks.title: Overture of the Wicked
chunks.text: Overture of the Wicked is an EP by Iced Earth, which was released on June 4, 2007 in Europe and June 5, 2007 in the US.

chunks.title: Overture of the Wicked
chunks.text: The EP features the band's new single "Ten Thousand Strong" which was recorded for the new album released later that same year "", as well as a rerecording of the original "Something Wicked" song cycle (from the album "Something Wicked This Way Comes").

chunks.title: Overture of the Wicked
chunks.text: The re-recorded tracks are also slightly rearranged, with the piano intro to "The Coming Curse" notably absent in the new version.

chunks.title: Overture of the Wicked
chunks.text: This EP was reissued as part of Iced Earth's Box of the Wicked collection.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (Cheyne album)
chunks.text: Something Wicked This Way Comes is the first solo studio album by Australian singer Cheyne Coates after leaving Madison Avenue.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (Cheyne album)
chunks.text: It produced two singles, "I've Got Your Number" and "Taste You", released in Australia.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (Ugly Betty)
chunks.text: "Something Wicked This Way Comes" is the sixth episode in season two of the dramedy series "Ugly Betty", and the 29th episode in the series, which aired on November 1, 2007.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (Ugly Betty)
chunks.text: The episode was written by Henry Alonso Myers and directed by Wendey Stanzler.

chunks.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes (Ugly Betty)
chunks.text: The episode takes its title from the phrase "something wicked this way comes", as well as the fact that this episode features the popular Broadway musical "Wicked" as a date venue.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: "Something Wicca This Way Comes" is the first episode of the television series "Charmed", which was broadcast on The WB on October 7, 1998.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: This is the second and only aired pilot for the series.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: The original pilot never made it to air and was shot in the actual manor that is shown on the show.
