chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: After Lori Rom quit "Charmed", executive producer Aaron Spelling asked Alyssa Milano, whom he knew from "Melrose Place", to be her replacement and the show moved to a sound studio.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: "Something Wicca This Way Comes" was the highest rated episode of "Charmed" in the entire series.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: It was watched by 7.7 million viewers and broke the record for the highest-rated premiere episode in The WB's three-year history.

chunks.title: Something Wicca This Way Comes
chunks.text: The name of this episode is a play on words from Shakespeare's "Macbeth": "By the pricking of my thumbs, something wicked this way comes."

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: Independence is a town in Grayson County, Virginia, United States.

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: The population was 947 at the 2010 census.

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: It is the county seat of Grayson County.

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: Independence is home to a major town celebration on July 4 every year, held in front of the 1908 courthouse.

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: It features bluegrass and old-time music and dance, food, crafts and a wild pony sale.

chunks.title: Independence, Virginia
chunks.text: The courthouse is also the location of the Mountain Foliage Festival, held in the autumn and featuring a parade, crafts, arts and music, as well as a race in which contestants use outhouses, the Grand Privy Race.

chunks.title: Frozen 2
chunks.text: Frozen 2 is an upcoming American computer-animated film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and will be released by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Frozen 2
chunks.text: It is a sequel to the 2013 film, "Frozen".

chunks.title: Preston Stutzman
chunks.text: Preston Stutzman is a film producer and actor.

chunks.title: Preston Stutzman
chunks.text: He produced the 1999 independent film "Chillicothe", which was screened at the Sundance Film Festival and the 2005 independent computer-animated film "Hoodwinked!

chunks.title: Preston Stutzman
chunks.text: ", which was one of the first computer-animated films to be completely independently funded.

chunks.title: Preston Stutzman
chunks.text: He also performed the minor role of Timmy in "Hoodwinked!"

chunks.title: Shrek (franchise)
chunks.text: The "Shrek" franchise from DreamWorks Animation, based on William Steig's picture book "Shrek!

chunks.title: Shrek (franchise)
chunks.text: ", consists of four computer-animated films including: "Shrek" (2001), "Shrek 2" (2004), "Shrek the Third" (2007), and "Shrek Forever After" (2010), with a fifth film planned for a 2019 or 2020 release.

chunks.title: Shrek (franchise)
chunks.text: A short 4-D film, "Shrek 4-D", which originally was a theme park ride, was released in 2003.

chunks.title: Pony Penning
chunks.text: Pony Penning is an annual event held in Chincoteague, Virginia on the last consecutive Wednesday and Thursday in July.

chunks.title: Pony Penning
chunks.text: The Chincoteague Volunteer Fire Department conducts the event and it consists of a Wild Pony Swim on Wednesday and a Pony Auction on Thursday.

chunks.title: Pony Penning
chunks.text: For the Wild Pony Swim, Salt Water Cowboys round up feral Chincoteague Ponies from Assateague Island and drive them across the Assateague Channel to Veteran’s Memorial Park on Chincoteague Island.

chunks.title: Pony Penning
chunks.text: The ponies swim across the channel during slack tide, when the water has minimal tidal movement.

chunks.title: Pony Penning
chunks.text: Once on Chincoteague Island, the salt water cowboys herd the ponies to pens on the Chincoteague Carnival Grounds where some of the foals are auctioned off on Thursday.

chunks.title: The Wild Pony
chunks.text: The Wild Pony is a made for pay-TV movie produced in 1983 by Kevin Sullivan ("Anne of Green Gables") and Eda Lishman.

chunks.title: The Wild Pony
chunks.text: Sullivan and Lishman also co-wrote the screenplay based on the book "The Year of the Black Pony" by American author Walt Morey.

chunks.title: The Wild Pony
chunks.text: "The Wild Pony" has the distinction of being the first example of a Canadian film produced specifically for pay-TV.

chunks.title: The Wild Pony
chunks.text: The film, directed by Kevin Sullivan and starring Canadian Actors Marilyn Lightstone, Art Hindle and Josh Byrne, was filmed in Calgary, Alberta against the backdrop of the Canadian Rockies.

chunks.title: Ride a Wild Pony
chunks.text: Ride a Wild Pony is a 1975 American-Australian family adventure film produced by Walt Disney Productions, directed by Don Chaffey and based on the novel "A Sporting Proposition" by James Aldridge.

chunks.title: Chucaro: Wild Pony of the Pampa
chunks.text: Chúcaro: Wild Pony of the Pampa (1958) is a book written by Francis Kalnay and illustrated by Julian De Miskey.

chunks.title: Chucaro: Wild Pony of the Pampa
chunks.text: It won Newbery Honor in 1959.

chunks.title: Chucaro: Wild Pony of the Pampa
chunks.text: Although a work of fiction, it contains factual information about gauchos on the pampas of South America and their way of life, including details about their work, what they wear and eat, and how they entertain themselves.

chunks.title: Bonnee Buttered Beef Steaks
chunks.text: Bonnee Buttered Beef Steaks were the flagship product of the Bonnee Frozen Products Company, which also produced frozen tamales and cubed steaks.

chunks.title: Bonnee Buttered Beef Steaks
chunks.text: Bonnee Buttered Beef Steaks consisted of “finely chopped beef, molded, frozen, sliced and buttered.”

chunks.title: Bonnee Buttered Beef Steaks
chunks.text: They were sold in packages which each contained four frozen 2-ounce beef patties and four frozen pats of 94-score butter.

chunks.title: Pony ride
chunks.text: A pony ride is an opportunity for children to ride real ponies for a short time, usually seen at fairs, guest ranches, zoos, summer camps, private children's parties and similar places.

chunks.title: Pony ride
chunks.text: Children on pony rides do not handle the pony themselves, but they need to be old enough to sit up straight and hold their head up without support.

chunks.title: Pony ride
chunks.text: Pony rides may be given on individually hand-led ponies, or in a group of ponies, usually four to six, placed on a "pony wheel," a small type of hot walker that leads all ponies in a walk on a small circle so that fewer handlers are needed.

chunks.title: Pony ride
chunks.text: Safety is a paramount concern and insurance companies consider pony rides to be a high-risk activity.

chunks.title: Pony ride
chunks.text: There are concerns about the welfare of some ponies used for pony rides.

chunks.title: Margulis lemma
chunks.text: In differential geometry, a subfield of mathematics, the Margulis lemma (named after Grigory Margulis) is a result about discrete subgroups of isometries of a non-positively curved Riemannian manifolds (e.g. the hyperbolic n-space).

chunks.title: Margulis lemma
chunks.text: Roughly, it states that within a fixed radius, usually called the Margulis constant, the structure of the orbits of such a group cannot be too complicated.

chunks.title: Margulis lemma
chunks.text: More precisely, within this radius around a point all points in its orbit are in fact in the orbit of a nilpotent subgroup (in fact a bounded finite number of such).

chunks.title: Napkin folding problem
chunks.text: The napkin folding problem is a problem in geometry and the mathematics of paper folding that explores whether folding a square or a rectangular napkin can increase its perimeter.

chunks.title: Napkin folding problem
chunks.text: The problem is known under several names, including the Margulis napkin problem, suggesting it is due to Grigory Margulis, and the Arnold's rouble problem referring to Vladimir Arnold and the folding of a Russian ruble bank note.

chunks.title: Napkin folding problem
chunks.text: Some versions of the problem were solved by Robert J. Lang, Svetlana Krat, Alexey S. Tarasov, and Ivan Yaschenko.

chunks.title: Napkin folding problem
chunks.text: One form of the problem remains open.

chunks.title: Leftover hash lemma
chunks.text: The leftover hash lemma is a lemma in cryptography first stated by Russell Impagliazzo, Leonid Levin, and Michael Luby.

chunks.title: Ratner's theorems
chunks.text: In mathematics, Ratner's theorems are a group of major theorems in ergodic theory concerning unipotent flows on homogeneous spaces proved by Marina Ratner around 1990.

chunks.title: Ratner's theorems
chunks.text: The theorems grew out of Ratner's earlier work on horocycle flows.

chunks.title: Ratner's theorems
chunks.text: The study of the dynamics of unipotent flows played a decisive role in the proof of the Oppenheim conjecture by Grigory Margulis.

chunks.title: Ratner's theorems
chunks.text: Ratner's theorems have guided key advances in the understanding of the dynamics of unipotent flows.

chunks.title: Ratner's theorems
chunks.text: Their later generalizations provide ways to both sharpen the results and extend the theory to the setting of arbitrary semisimple algebraic groups over a local field.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: Gabriel Levin (Born 1948, Paris) is a poet, translator and essayist.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: He lives in Jerusalem with his wife and children.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: Levin is one of the founding editors of Ibis Editions, a small non-profit press devoted to the publication of the literature of the Levant, and serves as its Editor-at-large.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: Levin's work has appeared in numerous literary magazines, including PN Review, The Times Literary Supplement, the Chicago Review, Raritan and Parnassus.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: "To these Dark Steps", a volume written in response to operation "Cast Lead" (2008), was set by British composer Alexander Goehr for tenor, children's choir, and ensemble and premiered September 2012 at the CBSO Centre in Birmingham.

chunks.title: Gabriel Levin
chunks.text: Levin is the son of the American novelist Meyer Levin (best known for "Compulsion", the first "non-fiction novel") and French novelist Tereska Torres.

chunks.title: Superrigidity
chunks.text: In mathematics, in the theory of discrete groups, superrigidity is a concept designed to show how a linear representation ρ of a discrete group Γ inside an algebraic group "G" can, under some circumstances, be as good as a representation of "G" itself.

chunks.title: Superrigidity
chunks.text: That this phenomenon happens for certain broadly defined classes of lattices inside semisimple groups was the discovery of Grigory Margulis, who proved some fundamental results in this direction.

chunks.title: Oseledets theorem
chunks.text: In mathematics, the multiplicative ergodic theorem, or Oseledets theorem provides the theoretical background for computation of Lyapunov exponents of a nonlinear dynamical system.

chunks.title: Oseledets theorem
chunks.text: It was proved by Valery Oseledets (also spelled "Oseledec") in 1965 and reported at the International Mathematical Congress in Moscow in 1966.

chunks.title: Oseledets theorem
chunks.text: A conceptually different proof of the multiplicative ergodic theorem was found by M. S. Raghunathan.

chunks.title: Oseledets theorem
chunks.text: The theorem has been extended to semisimple Lie groups by V. A. Kaimanovich and further generalized in the works of David Ruelle, Grigory Margulis, Anders Karlsson, and François Ledrappier.

chunks.title: The Voice (Russia season 5)
chunks.text: The fifth season of the Russian reality talent show "The Voice" premiered on 2 September 2016 on Channel One with Dima Bilan and Leonid Agutin returning as coaches alongside Polina Gagarina and Grigory Leps.

chunks.title: The Voice (Russia season 5)
chunks.text: Dmitry Nagiev returns as the show's presenter.

chunks.title: The Voice (Russia season 5)
chunks.text: Darya Antonyuk was announced the winner on 30 December 2016 marking Leonid Agutin's first win as a coach.

chunks.title: Leonid Levin
chunks.text: Leonid Anatolievich Levin ( ; Russian: Леони́д Анато́льевич Ле́вин ; Ukrainian: Леоні́д Анато́лійович Ле́він ; born November 2, 1948) is a Soviet-American computer scientist.

chunks.title: Grigory Margulis
chunks.text: Gregori Aleksandrovich Margulis (Russian: Григо́рий Алекса́ндрович Маргу́лис , first name often given as Gregory, Grigori or Grigory; born February 24, 1946) is a Russian-American mathematician known for his work on lattices in Lie groups, and the introduction of methods from ergodic theory into diophantine approximation.

chunks.title: Grigory Margulis
chunks.text: He was awarded a Fields Medal in 1978 and a Wolf Prize in Mathematics in 2005, becoming the seventh mathematician to receive both prizes.

chunks.title: Grigory Margulis
chunks.text: In 1991, he joined the faculty of Yale University, where he is currently the Erastus L. De Forest Professor of Mathematics.

chunks.title: A Company Man
chunks.text: A Company Man () is a 2012 South Korean action thriller film starring So Ji-sub, Lee Mi-yeon, Kwak Do-won and Kim Dong-jun.

chunks.title: A Company Man
chunks.text: It is about a hitman who find himself targeted by his ex-employers after he falls in love with a single mother and quits his job.

chunks.title: Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: Walden Michael Thoreau Schmidt is a fictional character in the CBS sitcom "Two and a Half Men", portrayed by Ashton Kutcher.

chunks.title: Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: The character was introduced in the season nine premiere episode, "Nice to Meet You, Walden Schmidt" to replace the character of Charlie Harper after actor Charlie Sheen was sacked from the series.

chunks.title: Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: Walden was a main character throughout the show's final four seasons (seasons 9-12).

chunks.title: Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: He is listed on Forbes' fictional list of the top 15 richest characters as number 11, with a wealth of approximately $1.3 billion.

chunks.title: Kim Dong-jun
chunks.text: Kim Dong-jun (hangul: 김동준; hanja: 金桐俊; born February 11, 1992) is a South Korean singer and actor.

chunks.title: Kim Dong-jun
chunks.text: He is a member of the South Korean boyband and its sub-group ZE:A Five and ZE:A J.

chunks.title: Nice to Meet You, Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: "Nice to Meet You, Walden Schmidt" is the ninth season premiere of the comedy series "Two and a Half Men" and the first appearance of Ashton Kutcher as Walden Schmidt, "an internet billionaire with a broken heart".

chunks.title: Nice to Meet You, Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: It is the 178th episode of the show, and the first episode without former lead Charlie Sheen as Charlie Harper.

chunks.title: Nice to Meet You, Walden Schmidt
chunks.text: The episode was watched by 28.74 million people on its original air date, making it the most watched episode of "Two and a Half Men".

chunks.title: Black (TV series)
chunks.text: Black () is an upcoming fantasy-thriller South Korean television series starring Song Seung-heon, Go Ara, Lee El and Kim Dong-jun.

chunks.title: Black (TV series)
chunks.text: It is set to air on OCN starting October 14, 2017 on Saturdays and Sundays at 22:20 (KST) time slot, replacing "Save Me".

chunks.title: That Darn Priest
chunks.text: "That Darn Priest" is the season finale of the eighth season of the American sitcom "Two and a Half Men" and the final appearance of Charlie Sheen as Charlie Harper.

chunks.title: That Darn Priest
chunks.text: The episode is the 16th and final episode of the season, though it was meant to be the ninth to last episode, but the season was cut short due to Sheen's problems related to drug and alcohol abuse.

chunks.title: That Darn Priest
chunks.text: Three weeks after the episode's original airing, Sheen was officially fired from the show.

chunks.title: That Darn Priest
chunks.text: CBS and Warner Bros. later announced that Ashton Kutcher would join the show's cast as Sheen's replacement.

chunks.title: Charlie Harper (singer)
chunks.text: Charlie Harper (born David Charles Perez, 25 May 1944, Hackney, London) is a British singer and songwriter.

chunks.title: Charlie Harper (singer)
chunks.text: He is best known as the lead singer from the punk band U.K. Subs.

chunks.title: Kim Dong-jun (footballer)
chunks.text: Kim Dong-jun (Korean: 김동준 , born 19 December 1994) is a South Korean footballer who plays as a goalkeeper for Yonsei University and South Korea national team.

chunks.title: Nangnangnangnang
chunks.text: "Nangnangnangnang" is the eleventh-season premiere of the comedy series "Two and a Half Men" and the first appearance of Amber Tamblyn as Charlie Harper's estranged daughter, Jenny.

chunks.title: Nangnangnangnang
chunks.text: The episode aired on September 26, 2013.

chunks.title: Two and a Half Men
chunks.text: Two and a Half Men is an American television sitcom that originally aired on CBS for twelve seasons from September 22, 2003 to February 19, 2015.

chunks.title: Two and a Half Men
chunks.text: Originally starring Charlie Sheen, Jon Cryer, and Angus T. Jones, the series was about a hedonistic jingle writer, Charlie Harper; his uptight brother Alan; and Alan's troublesome son Jake.

chunks.title: Two and a Half Men
chunks.text: After Alan divorces, he moves with his son to share Charlie's beachfront Malibu house and complicates Charlie's freewheeling life.

chunks.title: Patrinia
chunks.text: Patrinia is a genus of herbaceous plants in the honeysuckle family.

chunks.title: Patrinia
chunks.text: There are about 17 species native to grassy mountain habitats in China, Siberia and Japan.

chunks.title: Patrinia
chunks.text: These are unassuming clump-forming perennial plants having thin, erect stems with few leaves and bearing a terminal inflorescence with yellow or white flowers.

chunks.title: Patrinia
chunks.text: The use for this plant is to provide a flower through long hot summers.

chunks.title: Oeceoclades calcarata
chunks.text: Oeceoclades calcarata is a terrestrial orchid species in the genus "Oeceoclades" that is endemic to Madagascar.

chunks.title: Oeceoclades calcarata
chunks.text: It was first described by the British botanist Robert Allen Rolfe in 1905 as "Eulophia paniculata".

chunks.title: Oeceoclades calcarata
chunks.text: The German botanist Rudolf Schlechter later described this species as "Cymbidium calcaratum" in 1915 and then transferred his own taxon to the genus "Eulophia" (as "E. calcarata") in 1925.

chunks.title: Oeceoclades calcarata
chunks.text: When Leslie Andrew Garay and Peter Taylor revised the genus "Oeceoclades" in 1976, they transferred this species to the expanded "Oeceoclades" as "O. calcarata" because even though "Eulophia paniculata" was the older name and thus had priority, there had already been an earlier species named "Oeceoclades paniculata" (so named by John Lindley and now recognized as a species in the genus "Robiquetia") that prevented using that specific epithet.

chunks.title: Cymbidium
chunks.text: Cymbidium , or boat orchid, is a genus of 52 evergreen species in the orchid family Orchidaceae.

chunks.title: Cymbidium
chunks.text: The new Latin genus name is derived from the Latin "cymba" meaning boat.

chunks.title: Cymbidium
chunks.text: Its first known use was in 1815.

chunks.title: Thecostele
chunks.text: Thecostele is a monotypic genus of orchids (family Orchidaceae) and of subtribe Cymbidiinae.

chunks.title: Thecostele
chunks.text: The only species in the genus is Thecostele alata, first described as "Cymbidium alatum" by the Scottish botanist William Roxburgh in 1832.

chunks.title: Thecostele
chunks.text: It was transferred to the genus "Thecostele" in 1874 by the English botanist Charles Samuel Pollock Parish and the German botanist Heinrich Gustav Reichenbach.

chunks.title: Thecostele
chunks.text: It is native to tropical Asia and is found in northeastern India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines.

chunks.title: Thecostele
chunks.text: Two species formerly recognized in this genus ("T. secunda" and "T. maingayi") were transferred to the new genus "Thecopus" by the Danish botanist Gunnar Seidenfaden in 1983, a decision supported by the number of pollinia and shape of the column.

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: Cássio van den Berg (born 1971) is a Brazilian botanist.

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: He is noted for work in orchid classification and evolution, especially great changes in the generic circumscriptions of ornamental orchids in the genus "Cattleya", based on DNA studies for the subtribe Laeliinae.

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: Based on this studies, he proposed a fusion of the genera "Cattleya", "Laelia" (only Brazilian species), and "Sophronitis".

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: In Laeliinae, the studies pointed out to the separation of subtribe Ponerinae, and the transfer of "Dilomilis" and "Neocogniauxia" to Pleurothallidinae.

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: He also worked in the taxonomy of other orchid genera, such as "Acianthera", "Baptistonia", "Bulbophyllum", "Cymbidium", "Encyclia", "Galeandra", "Isabelia" and "Pleione".

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: In 2004, he described a new genus of Laeliinae, "Adamantinia" Van den Berg & C.N.Gonç.

chunks.title: Cássio van den Berg
chunks.text: Currently he is full professor and curator of the Laboratory of Plant Molecular Systematics.

chunks.title: Cymbidium suave
chunks.text: Cymbidium suave (R. Brown 1810), or the snake orchid, is an Australian orchid species that is part of the genus "Cymbidium" which consists of 52 species.

chunks.title: Cymbidium elegans
chunks.text: Cymbidium elegans, the elegant cymbidium - In China Suo Cao Lan (Chinese: 莎草蘭 or 莎草兰), is an orchid species in the genus "Cymbidium" found in South West China.

chunks.title: Chivita 100%
chunks.text: Chivita 100% is a juice brand manufactured by Chi Limited.

chunks.title: Chivita 100%
chunks.text: It was first introduced into the Nigerian market in 1996 as Chivita Premium Fruit Juice.

chunks.title: Chivita 100%
chunks.text: The brand’s name was changed in 2014 to Chivita 100% to reflect its 100% fruit juice offering.

chunks.title: Appy Fizz
chunks.text: Appy Fizz is a product by Parle Agro, introduced in India in 2005.

chunks.title: Appy Fizz
chunks.text: Appy Fizz consists of carbonated apple juice, and is used as the basis for cocktails and is a popular drink with the youth.

chunks.title: Appy Fizz
chunks.text: After the success of Appy which was clean apple juice, Parle launched its sequel product as Grappo Fizz, which is a carbonated grape juice.

chunks.title: Painkiller (cocktail)
chunks.text: A Painkiller is a rum cocktail trademarked by Pusser's Rum Ltd, their signature drink.

chunks.title: Painkiller (cocktail)
chunks.text: It is often associated with Tiki establishments.

chunks.title: Painkiller (cocktail)
chunks.text: The Painkiller is a blend of Pusser's rum with 4 parts pineapple juice, 1 part cream of coconut and 1 part orange juice, well shaken and served over the rocks with a generous amount of fresh nutmeg on top.

chunks.title: Painkiller (cocktail)
chunks.text: It may be made with either two, three or four ounces of Pusser's dark rum.

chunks.title: Doi Kham
chunks.text: The Doi Kham Company (Thai : ดอยคำ ) is a rural farm development project of King Bhumibol's started in 1969.

chunks.title: Doi Kham
chunks.text: The meaning of the words "Doi Kham" comes from two northern Thai words.

chunks.title: Doi Kham
chunks.text: The word "doi" means "mountain" or "hill" while the word "kham" is a shortened word for "thongkham" which means "gold".

chunks.title: Doi Kham
chunks.text: The company produces a variety of agricultural products including ready-to-drink fruit juice, fruit juice concentrates, dehydrated fruits, fruit jam, canned fruits, tomato paste, frozen fruit and full fat soya flour.

chunks.title: Lebedyansky (company)
chunks.text: Lebedyansky, a Russian multi-national company that manufacturers fruit juice, baby food, vegetable juice, and soft drinks, which is owned by PepsiCo, is the largest fruit juice manufacturer in Eastern Europe and the sixth largest in the world.

chunks.title: Lebedyansky (company)
chunks.text: Lebedyansky has two major production centers, both located in the Lipetsk Oblast.

chunks.title: Fizz (cocktail)
chunks.text: A "fizz" is a mixed drink variation on the older sours family of cocktail.

chunks.title: Fizz (cocktail)
chunks.text: Its defining features are an acidic juice (such as lemon or lime) and carbonated water.

chunks.title: Vampiro (cocktail)
chunks.text: The Vampiro is a cold mixed cocktail that includes fruit juice, spices, fruit soda, fresh lime juice, and tequila, a distilled alcoholic beverage that is popular in Mexico.

chunks.title: Vampiro (cocktail)
chunks.text: The Vampiro "...has a fruity, lightly carbonated, and spicy taste to it."

chunks.title: Appletiser
chunks.text: Appletiser is a sparkling fruit juice created by blending fruit juice with carbonated water.

chunks.title: Appletiser
chunks.text: French-Italian immigrant Edmond Lombardi created Appletiser in 1966 in Elgin Valley of the Western Cape, South Africa.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: Pago is a fruit juice producer operating internationally in the fruit juice sector.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: The company has been producing fruit juice for more than 100 year In the past, Pago as a member of the BRAU UNION Group, belongs to the Dutch Heineken Group.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: Heineken sold Pago to GRANINI JUICES.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: In the Netherlands Pago was distributed by Pago Nederland.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: They lost a lawsuit with VRUMONA in 2013.

chunks.title: Pago International
chunks.text: Vrumona is doing now distribution in the Netherlands.

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: Juice is a beverage made from the extraction or pressing out of the natural liquid contained in fruit and vegetables.

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: It can also refer to liquids that are flavored with these or other biological food sources such as meat and seafood (e.g., clam juice).

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: Juice is commonly consumed as a beverage or used as an ingredient or flavoring in foods or other beverages, such as smoothies. Juice emerged as a popular beverage choice after the development of pasteurization methods allowed for its preservation without using fermentation (the approach used with wine production).

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) estimated the total world production of citrus fruit juices to be 12,840,318 tonnes in 2012.

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: The largest fruit juice consumers are New Zealand (nearly a cup, or 8 ounces, each day) and Colombia (more than three quarters of a cup each day).

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: Fruit juice consumption on average increased with country income level.

chunks.title: Juice
chunks.text: To the American food industry, fruit juice is more profitable than only fruit.

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: Aspidistra is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Nolinoideae, native to eastern and southeastern Asia, particularly China and Vietnam.

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: They grow in shade under trees and shrubs.

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: Their leaves arise more or less directly from ground level, where their flowers also appear.

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: The number of species known has increased considerably from the 1980s onwards, with around 100 accepted as of July 2013 . "

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: Aspidistra elatior" is common worldwide as a foliage house plant that is very tolerant of neglect.

chunks.title: Aspidistra
chunks.text: It and other species can also be grown in shade outside, where they are generally hardy to -5 C .

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: Imazapyr is a non-selective herbicide used for the control of a broad range of weeds including terrestrial annual and perennial grasses and broadleaved herbs, woody species, and riparian and emergent aquatic species.

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: It is used to eliminate "Lithocarpus densiflorus" (Tan Oak) and "Arbutus menziesii" (Pacific Madrone).

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: Additionally, imazapyr is used to control annual and perennial grass and broadleaved weeds, brush, vines and many deciduous trees.

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: Imazapyr is absorbed by the leaves and roots, and moves rapidly through the plant.

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: It accumulates in the meristem region (active growth region) of the plant.

chunks.title: Imazapyr
chunks.text: In plants, imazapyr disrupts protein synthesis and interferes with cell growth and DNA synthesis.

chunks.title: List of power stations in Nigeria
chunks.text: There are currently two main types of power plants operating in Nigeria: (1) hydro-electric and (2) thermal or fossil fuel power plants.

chunks.title: List of power stations in Nigeria
chunks.text: With a total installed capacity of 8457.6MW (81 percent of total) in early 2014, thermal power plants (gas-fired plants) dominates the Nigerian power supply mix.

chunks.title: List of power stations in Nigeria
chunks.text: Electricity production from hydroelectric sources (% of total) in Nigeria was reported at 17.59 % in 2014, according to the World Bank collection of development indicators, compiled from officially recognized sources.

chunks.title: List of power stations in Nigeria
chunks.text: There have been two main types of fossil fuel/thermal power plants in the country: (i) coal-fired and (ii) natural gas-fired.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: Silene menziesii is a species of flowering plant in the pink family known by the common names Menzies' campion and Menzies' catchfly.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: It is native to western North America from Alaska through the western half of Canada to the southwestern United States.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: It can be found in many types of habitat and it is quite common in much of its range.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: It is variable in morphology and there are a number of varied subtaxa.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: In general, it is a perennial herb growing from a caudex, appearing matlike, decumbent, or erect, with stems a few centimeters to over half a meter long.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: It is usually hairy in texture, with upper parts bearing sticky glandular hairs.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: The leaves are lance-shaped, oppositely arranged in pairs, and a few centimeters in length, upper leaves usually smaller than lower.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: Flowers may occur in a cyme at the top of the stem, or in leaf axils, or both.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: Each is encapsulated in a hairy, veined calyx of fused sepals.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: The petals are white with two lobes at the tips.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: The plant is dioecious with male and female plants producing different flowers.

chunks.title: Silene menziesii
chunks.text: The male and female flower types look the same externally; the stamens are reduced in female plants and the stigmas are reduced in the male.

chunks.title: Trellis (architecture)
chunks.text: A trellis (treillage) is an architectural structure, usually made from an open framework or lattice of interwoven or intersecting pieces of wood, bamboo or metal that is normally made to support and display climbing plants, especially shrubs.

chunks.title: Trellis (architecture)
chunks.text: There are many types of trellis for different places and for different plants, from agricultural types, especially in viticulture, which are covered at vine training systems, to garden uses for climbers such as grapevines, clematis, ivy, and climbing roses or other support based growing plants.

chunks.title: Trellis (architecture)
chunks.text: The rose trellis is especially common in Europe and other rose-growing areas, and many climbing rose varieties require a trellis to reach their potential as garden plants.

chunks.title: Trellis (architecture)
chunks.text: Some plants will climb and wrap themselves round a trellis without much artificial help being needed while others need training by passing the growing shoots through the trellis and/or tying them to the framework.

chunks.title: Aspidistra nikolaii
chunks.text: Aspidistra nikolaii is a plant species of the genus "Aspidistra" that was one of the new 21 species of plants and animals recently discovered in the Annamite Range of central Vietnam.

chunks.title: Aspidistra nikolaii
chunks.text: It was named after a late Russian botanist named Nicolai Arnautov.

chunks.title: Aspidistra nikolaii
chunks.text: It has a dark blue flower that is almost black.

chunks.title: Self-pollination
chunks.text: Self-pollination is when pollen from the same plant arrives at the stigma of a flower (in flowering plants) or at the ovule (in Gymnosperms).

chunks.title: Self-pollination
chunks.text: There are two types of self-pollination: In autogamy, pollen is transferred to the stigma of the same flower.

chunks.title: Self-pollination
chunks.text: In geitonogamy, pollen is transferred from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on the same flowering plant, or from microsporangium to ovule within a single (monoecious) Gymnosperm.

chunks.title: Self-pollination
chunks.text: Some plants have mechanisms that ensure autogamy, such as flowers that do not open (cleistogamy), or stamens that move to come into contact with the stigma.

chunks.title: Self-pollination
chunks.text: The term selfing that is often used as a synonym, is not limited to self-pollination, but also applies to other types of self fertilization.

chunks.title: Arbutus
chunks.text: Arbutus is a genus of 11 accepted species of flowering plants in the family Ericaceae, native to warm temperate regions of the Mediterranean, western Europe, the Canary Islands (Teneriffa) and North America.

chunks.title: Arbutus
chunks.text: The name "Arbutus" was taken from Latin, where it referred to "A. unedo".

chunks.title: Thorius munificus
chunks.text: Thorius munificus is a species of salamander in the family Plethodontidae.

chunks.title: Thorius munificus
chunks.text: It is endemic to Mexico and only known from near its type locality near Las Vigas, Veracruz.

chunks.title: Thorius munificus
chunks.text: Its natural habitats are pine-oak and pine forests, woodlands, and "Arbutus" forests with abundant shrubby and ericaceous plants.

chunks.title: Thorius munificus
chunks.text: The species is threatened by habitat loss caused by logging, agriculture, and human settlement.

chunks.title: False vivipary
chunks.text: False vivipary is an abnormal condition found in many types of plants in which a plantlet is produced where the flower should appear.

chunks.title: False vivipary
chunks.text: It is not a completely understood topic, but some say it could be caused by a hormonal mistake.

chunks.title: False vivipary
chunks.text: The plantlet which appears can be rooted and grown like normal plants.

chunks.title: False vivipary
chunks.text: This abnormal behavior can occasionally be seen in many types of carnivorous plants.

chunks.title: Sanctuary (band)
chunks.text: Sanctuary is an American heavy metal band founded in Seattle in 1985.

chunks.title: Sanctuary (band)
chunks.text: They split up in 1992, but reformed 18 years later.

chunks.title: Sanctuary (band)
chunks.text: The band consists of Warrel Dane (vocals), Lenny Rutledge (guitar), Nick Cordle (guitar), George Hernandez (bass), and Dave Budbill (drums).

chunks.title: Sanctuary (band)
chunks.text: To date, they have released four studio albums and one live EP.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Dreaming Neon Black is the third full-length album released by Seattle progressive metal band Nevermore, and was released through Century Media in 1999.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Unlike its predecessor, "The Politics of Ecstasy", this album is very emotional and contains many slower, ballad-type songs.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: It is also notable that "Dreaming Neon Black" is a concept album of sorts.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: According to Nevermore's lead singer, Warrel Dane, "it's a very simple story about a man who slowly goes insane after losing a woman that he was very close to.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Progressive levels of insanity are expressed in the songs, he goes through phases of denial and self-blame, blaming God, then denouncing God.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: The ending is a little...tragic, a little depressing.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Shakesperian.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Everybody dies, it's all happy."

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: , which may be based on an event in the life of Dane.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: Supposedly, his old girlfriend left him when she joined a religious cult and was never heard from again, and he began having nightmares of her crying out to him as she drowned.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: This has been confirmed by Warrel himself in an older interview.

chunks.title: Dreaming Neon Black
chunks.text: The spoken word samples from the tracks "Ophidian" and "Forever" are from the Clive Barker movie, "Lord of Illusions".

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: Into The Mirror Live / Black Reflections is live promotional EP of the band Sanctuary recorded on May 12, 1990 at The Country Club in Reseda, California, during their "Into the Mirror Black" tour.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: Approximately 1000 CD copies of this were made and less than 500 were ever distributed to radio stations and record stores.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: Because of contractual problems with Epic Records, the full version was never released for public consumption.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: Epic Records destroyed 500+ copies of this CD.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: Warrel Dane has stated on several occasions that he has the master tapes and copyrights of the full show and intended to have it finally released.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: To date that has not happened.

chunks.title: Into the Mirror Live
chunks.text: This CD has been heavily pirated over the years as a 2-on-1 CD with the Satan's Host "Metal From Hell" album on the notorious Reborn Classics record label.

chunks.title: Nevermore (album)
chunks.text: Nevermore is the eponymous debut studio album by American heavy metal band Nevermore, released on February 14, 1995 by Century Media Records.

chunks.title: Nevermore (album)
chunks.text: It was singer Warrel Dane and bassist Jim Sheppard's first release after departing from their previous band, Sanctuary, in 1994.

chunks.title: Nevermore (album)
chunks.text: Having recruited drummer Van Williams and former Sanctuary touring guitarist Jeff Loomis, they formed the band Nevermore and began anew.

chunks.title: Nevermore
chunks.text: Nevermore is an American progressive metal band from Seattle, Washington, United States.

chunks.title: Nevermore
chunks.text: Formed in 1991, they are known to incorporate elements from various styles such as power metal, modern hard rock, classic heavy metal and technical thrash metal.

chunks.title: Nevermore
chunks.text: The band has been on hiatus since 2011, due to personal issues between the band members.

chunks.title: Nevermore
chunks.text: In April 2015, lead singer Warrel Dane confirmed that Nevermore has not disbanded, and there is a possibility for them to continue in the next two years with another album.

chunks.title: The Year of the Voyager
chunks.text: The Year Of The Voyager is a double DVD/CD released by Nevermore.

chunks.title: The Year of the Voyager
chunks.text: It was released in Europe on October 20, 2008 and in North America on November 25, 2008 via Century Media.

chunks.title: The Year of the Voyager
chunks.text: The set covers the "This Godless Endeavor" touring cycle, starting with live footage from the U.S. Gigantour 2005, the Metal Mania festival 2006 in Poland, the Wacken Open Air festival in 2006 in Germany and the main DVD show recorded at the Zeche in Bochum, Germany.

chunks.title: The Year of the Voyager
chunks.text: Bonus material includes two songs from Century Media USA 10th Anniversary Party 2001, all promo videos and an interview with singer Warrel Dane which was recorded at the Roax Film Studios in Berlin in the spring of 2008.

chunks.title: Warrel Dane
chunks.text: Warrel Dane (born March 7, 1969) is the lead singer of the American power metal band Sanctuary.

chunks.title: Warrel Dane
chunks.text: He is also known as the former lead singer of currently inactive progressive metal band Nevermore.

chunks.title: Warrel Dane
chunks.text: He is a natural baritone, though he was known for his high-pitched vocals with Serpent's Knight and on the first two Sanctuary albums.

chunks.title: Warrel Dane
chunks.text: Later in his career, Dane became more notable for his distinctively deep, dramatic voice.

chunks.title: Toshi (musician)
chunks.text: Toshimitsu Deyama (出山利三 , Deyama Toshimitsu , born October 10, 1965 in Tateyama, Chiba) , known exclusively by his stage name Toshi, is a Japanese singer and songwriter.

chunks.title: Toshi (musician)
chunks.text: He is best known as the lead vocalist and a co-founder of the heavy metal band X Japan, which disbanded in 1997.

chunks.title: Toshi (musician)
chunks.text: Toshi then went on to have an extensive solo career.

chunks.title: Toshi (musician)
chunks.text: In 2007, X Japan reunited and began an ongoing world tour in 2010.

chunks.title: Toshi (musician)
chunks.text: His distinctive, impassioned tenor vocals have been compared to those of Steve Perry.

chunks.title: Peter Wichers
chunks.text: Peter Wichers is best known as one of the founding members of Swedish melodic death metal band, Soilwork.

chunks.title: Peter Wichers
chunks.text: From 1995 until late 2005, when he announced his departure from the band, he was known as the lead guitarist and also a songwriter, especially on their "Stabbing the Drama" album., He rejoined Soilwork in 2008 and played on 2010s The Panic Broadcast and in June 2012 he quit Soilwork for the second time.

chunks.title: Peter Wichers
chunks.text: After leaving Soilwork, he filled in for Adam Dutkiewicz when he was injured on Killswitch Engage's European tour.

chunks.title: Peter Wichers
chunks.text: More recently, he has collaborated with singers from across the melodic death metal genre including Anders Fridén, former band mate Björn "Speed" Strid and John Bush (vocalist of Anthrax) to make a CD much in the same style as "Roadrunner United", entitled "Nuclear Blast All-Stars".

chunks.title: Peter Wichers
chunks.text: He also co-wrote Warrel Dane's solo record "Praises to the War Machine".

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: Praises to the War Machine is the debut and only solo release/album by heavy metal vocalist Warrel Dane from Nevermore, released on April 25, 2008.

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: The album was produced by Peter Wichers, who was tapped by Dane to work on the album while Wichers was still a member of Soilwork.

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: After leaving that band in 2007, Wichers co-wrote the album with Dane and played on eight of its tracks.

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: Soilwork drummer Dirk Verbeuren and former Himsa guitarist Matt Wicklund also played on the album.

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: Nevermore guitarist Jeff Loomis and the band's touring guitarist at the time Chris Broderick make guest appearances, along with James Murphy, who had performed on the Nevermore album "This Godless Endeavor".

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: "Praises to the War Machine" includes two cover songs, The Sisters of Mercy's "Lucretia My Reflection" and "Patterns" by Paul Simon.

chunks.title: Praises to the War Machine
chunks.text: Dane had previously covered a Simon song on Nevermore's album "Dead Heart in a Dead World".

chunks.title: Keiko Utoku
chunks.text: Keiko Utoku (宇徳敬子 , "Utoku Keiko" , born April 7, 1967 in Izumi, Kagoshima, Japan) is a Japanese singer and songwriter under UK Sweet label.Keiko made first debut with chorus part in band B.B.Queens then joined with J-pop female band Mi-Ke from 1991 to 1993, before starting a solo career.

chunks.title: Keiko Utoku
chunks.text: As a child, Utoku listened to a lot of music, including music made by Momoe Yamaguchi.

chunks.title: Keiko Utoku
chunks.text: She has written and sung many songs, such as "Wasurenagusa", and Sonic the Hedgehog fans remember her for her vocal work in the original version of the Sonic CD video game's opening and closing themes in Japan and Europe, "Sonic – You Can Do Anything" and "Cosmic Eternity – Believe In Yourself" in 1993.

chunks.title: Keiko Utoku
chunks.text: In addition, she also provided Sonic's vocals in the game.

chunks.title: Keiko Utoku
chunks.text: At recent dates, she has released 15 singles, 5 digital singles, 4 studio albums, 1 mini and 2 best albums.

chunks.title: Juliet Weber
chunks.text: Juliet Weber is a producer, director, writer, and an editor for the film industry.

chunks.title: Juliet Weber
chunks.text: She co-produced films such as Fastpitch (2000) and Unchained Memories (2003).

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: The Shame of a City is a 2006 feature-length documentary, which premiered at the Philadelphia Film Festival.

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: Filmmaker Tigre Hill chronicles the 2003 Philadelphia mayoral race between Democrat incumbent mayor John Street and Republican challenger Sam Katz.

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: Early polls showed Katz with a small lead in this predominantly Democratic city but twenty-seven days before the election, an FBI bug was found in the mayor’s office.

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: The discovery at first seemed like a death knell to the Street campaign and a near certain victory for Katz.

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: Yet this prediction was proven wrong when Street and his supporters successfully polarized the campaign by leveling accusations of instituational racial prejudice and playing on historical skepticism of the Republican-controlled federal government.

chunks.title: The Shame of a City
chunks.text: As a result, Street won re-election by a sixteen-point margin.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: Admiral of the Fleet Lord John Hay, GCB (23 August 1827 – 4 May 1916) was a Royal Navy officer and politician.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: After seeing action in 1842 during the First Opium War, he went ashore with the Naval Brigade and took part in the defence of Eupatoria in November 1854 and the Siege of Sevastopol in Spring 1855 during the Crimean War.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: He also took part in the Battle of Taku Forts in August 1860 during the Second Opium War.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: As a politician, he became Member of Parliament for Wick and later for Ripon.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: He was sent to the Mediterranean in July 1878 to take control of Cyprus and to occupy it in accordance with decisions reached at the Congress of Berlin.

chunks.title: Lord John Hay (Royal Navy officer, born 1827)
chunks.text: In a highly political appointment, he was made First Naval Lord in March 1886 when the Marquis of Ripon became First Lord of the Admiralty but had to stand down just five months later when William Gladstone's Liberal Government fell from power in August 1886.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: Admir Čavalić is the Director of Association "Multi", a non-profit organization dedicated to promoting libertarian ideals in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: "Multi" is the first non-profit organization registered in Bosnia and Herzegovina that advocates libertarian ideas.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: Čavalić is the director of OPEN Fest, biggest libertarian festival in Europe.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: Čavalić also works at Faculty of Economics University of Tuzla, as an assistant teacher.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: Čavalić with Dženan Smajić wrote "Islam and Free Market" in 2014.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: The book, that was published in Bosnian, provides arguments for Islam's connection with the ideas of economic liberalism.

chunks.title: Admir Čavalić
chunks.text: Čavalić made first bosnian documentary about economics, titled "Economy".

chunks.title: Unchained Memories
chunks.text: Unchained Memories is a 2003 documentary film about the stories of former slaves interviewed during the 1930s as part of the Federal Writers' Project and preserved in the WPA Slave Narrative Collection.

chunks.title: Unchained Memories
chunks.text: This HBO film interpretation directed by Ed Bell and Thomas Lennon is a compilation of slave narratives, narrated by actors, emulating the original conversation with the interviewer.

chunks.title: Unchained Memories
chunks.text: The slave narratives may be the most accurate in terms of the everyday activities of the enslaved, serving as personal memoirs of more than two thousand former slaves.

chunks.title: Unchained Memories
chunks.text: The documentary depicts the emotions of the slaves and what they endured.

chunks.title: Unchained Memories
chunks.text: The "Master" had the opportunity to sell, trade, or kill the enslaved, for retribution should one slave not obey.

chunks.title: List of Austrian mountain climbers
chunks.text: This is a list of Austrian mountaineers.

chunks.title: List of Austrian mountain climbers
chunks.text: On 5 of the 14 Eight-thousanders Austrians have made the first ascent, more than any other nation can claim.

chunks.title: List of Austrian mountain climbers
