chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: Secret Garden is the third mini-album by South Korean girl group Apink, released on July 5, 2013.

chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: This is their first official release as six-member group and they returned after 14 months since they last promoted their last album "Unee Anee" with "Hush" and "Bubibu" in May 2012.

chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: They made first comeback stage on Mnet’s “M!

chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: Countdown" one day before the official release.

chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: The theme of the album is healing, aim to that will soothe the listeners’ eyes and ears.

chunks.title: Secret Garden (EP)
chunks.text: The album consist of five new songs including the title track “NoNoNo” produced by Shinsadong Tiger.

chunks.title: Albert R. Ellingwood
chunks.text: Albert Russell Ellingwood (22 June 1887 – 12 May 1934) was a pioneering mountaineer and climber in the western United States during the first half of the twentieth century.

chunks.title: Albert R. Ellingwood
chunks.text: He made first ascents of many peaks and routes in the Rocky Mountains, particularly in Colorado, including Lizard Head in the San Juan Mountains, Ellingwood Ridge on La Plata Peak in the Sawatch Range, and Crestone Needle in the Sangre de Cristo Range.

chunks.title: Albert R. Ellingwood
chunks.text: Many mountain features are named for him, on peaks such as Middle Teton, on which Ellingwood made the first ascent, the Ellingwood Ridge of La Plata Peak, and the Ellingwood Arete ascent of Crestone Needle; the fourteener Ellingwood Point, near Blanca Peak in southern Colorado, is named for him as well.

chunks.title: King Electric
chunks.text: King Electric is Chris Isepp and Peter Hartwig.

chunks.title: King Electric
chunks.text: They took their first musical attempts at the end of 1980s / beginning 1990s and first met each other at the upcoming and flourishing Viennese techno scene back in '92.

chunks.title: King Electric
chunks.text: While Hartwig was touring with the well known noise-pop band the Basket Boys, Isepp made first attentions as Electro DJ & Producer.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: Urdu Digest (Urdu: ‎ ) is a monthly Urdu magazine in Pakistan.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: It is first digest in Pakistan and was first published in November 1960 in Lahore.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: Its appearance is similar to the famous American monthly, "Reader's Digest".

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: Its writings present a traditional way of religious Pakistani life and covers a large variety of topics.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: "Urdu Digest" is constantly performing the duty of character building and consciousness of Pakistanis for the last 53 years.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: The magazine also has been serving to strengthen the ideology of Pakistan and promoting national integration.

chunks.title: Urdu Digest
chunks.text: "Urdu Digest" publishes translations of international literary stories, adventure stories, hunting stories and articles on science, technology, history, animals, education, health, positive thinking and business role models.

chunks.title: Trusted Media Brands, Inc.
chunks.text: Trusted Media Brands, Inc. (TMBI), formerly known as the Reader's Digest Association, Inc. (RDA), is an American multi-platform media and publishing company that is co-headquartered in New York City and White Plains, New York.

chunks.title: Trusted Media Brands, Inc.
chunks.text: The company was founded by husband and wife DeWitt Wallace and Lila Bell Wallace in New York City in 1922 with the first publication of "Reader's Digest".

chunks.title: Football Digest
chunks.text: Football Digest was a sports magazine for fans interested in professional American football, with in-depth coverage of the National Football League (NFL).

chunks.title: Football Digest
chunks.text: The magazine modeled the "Reader's Digest" idea, to bring the best in football journalism from newspapers and magazines that the fans would have otherwise not had an opportunity to read.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest
chunks.text: Reader's Digest is an American general-interest family magazine, published ten times a year.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest
chunks.text: Formerly based in Chappaqua, New York, it is now headquartered in Midtown Manhattan.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest
chunks.text: The magazine was founded in 1920, by DeWitt Wallace and Lila Bell Wallace.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest
chunks.text: For many years, "Reader's Digest" was the best-selling consumer magazine in the United States; it lost the distinction in 2009 to "Better Homes and Gardens".

chunks.title: Reader's Digest
chunks.text: According to Mediamark Research (2006), "Reader's Digest" reaches more readers with household incomes of $100,000+ than "Fortune", "The Wall Street Journal", "Business Week", and "Inc." combined.

chunks.title: Gene Methvin
chunks.text: Eugene Hilburn "Gene" Methvin (September 19, 1934 – January 19, 2012) was an American pilot, journalist, and senior editor for the "Reader's Digest" Washington, D.C., bureau.

chunks.title: Gene Methvin
chunks.text: A self-described "shoe leather reporter," Methvin contributed more than 100 articles to "Reader's Digest" and its 48 editions, reaching more than 100 million readers worldwide.

chunks.title: Gene Methvin
chunks.text: His articles covered topics ranging from the U.S. Supreme Court, civil liberties and constitutional law, to U.S. defense posture, Kremlin politics, U.S.-Soviet relations, organized crime and international terrorist groups.

chunks.title: Gene Methvin
chunks.text: An article by Methvin in the January 1965 "Reader's Digest", "How the Reds Make a Riot," won the magazine the coveted award for public service in magazine journalism given annually by the Society for Professional Journalists.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: If on a winter's night a traveler (Italian: Se una notte d'inverno un viaggiatore ) is a 1979 novel by the Italian writer Italo Calvino.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: The postmodernist narrative, in the form of a frame story, is about the reader trying to read a book called "If on a winter's night a traveler".

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: Each chapter is divided into two sections.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: The first section of each chapter is in second person, and describes the process the reader goes through to attempt to read the next chapter of the book he is reading.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: The second half is the first part of a new book that the reader ("you") finds.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: The second half is always about something different from the previous ones and the ending is never explained.

chunks.title: If on a winter's night a traveler
chunks.text: The book was published in an English translation by William Weaver in 1981.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Condensed Books
chunks.text: The Reader's Digest Condensed Books were a series of hardcover anthology collections, published by the American general interest monthly family magazine "Reader's Digest" and distributed by direct mail.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Condensed Books
chunks.text: Most volumes contained five (although a considerable minority consisted of three, four, or six) current best-selling novels and nonfiction books which were abridged (or "condensed") specifically for "Reader's Digest".

chunks.title: Out Traveler
chunks.text: Out Traveler is a gay and lesbian travel magazine from the publishers of "Out" and "The Advocate", combining photography with coverage of LGBT travel topics.

chunks.title: Out Traveler
chunks.text: Published as a stand-alone title from 2003 to 2008, it was subsequently incorporated as a supplement to "Out" magazine and is no longer available for subscriptions as a stand-alone title.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Select Editions
chunks.text: The Reader's Digest Select Editions are a series of hardcover fiction anthology books, published bi-monthly and available by subscription, from "Reader's Digest".

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Select Editions
chunks.text: Each volume consists of four or five current bestselling novels selected by "Digest" editors and abridged (or "condensed") to shorter form to accommodate the anthology format.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Press
chunks.text: Reader's Digest Press was a United States publisher of the mid-1970s to early 1980s, owned by The Reader's Digest Association.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Press
chunks.text: It published full-length, original non-fiction books, often concerning military or political topics.

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Press
chunks.text: (It thus differed from the better-known Reader's Digest Condensed Books.)

chunks.title: Reader's Digest Press
chunks.text: Its works were sometimes distributed by Thomas Y. Crowell Co.

chunks.title: Sumoll
chunks.text: The Sumoll is a black grape variety, although there is also a white strain.

chunks.title: Sumoll
chunks.text: It is a rustic variety, native from the Penedès region in Catalonia (EU), drought resistant and with uniform development.

chunks.title: Sumoll
chunks.text: The grape is long and big.

chunks.title: Sumoll
chunks.text: It is used to produce red, white, rosé wines and cava (Catalan form of Champagne, the so-called Traditional Method).

chunks.title: Sumoll
chunks.text: Its former presence is also evident in the number of different names in Catalan dialects: sumoi, chimoi, saumoll, somoi, sumoy, ximoll, somoll, ximoy, xemoll, among others.

chunks.title: Vernaccia
chunks.text: Vernaccia is a white wine grape that is found in many Italian wines but is most commonly associated the Tuscan wine Vernaccia di San Gimignano.

chunks.title: Vernaccia
chunks.text: Ampelographers have determined that the Vernaccia vine has many clonal varieties but is unrelated to some Italian vines known as "Vernaccia" such as the Sardinian varieties used in the Sherry-like wine "Vernaccia di Oristano", the Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol red wine grape known as Vernatsch or the black grape used in the red sparkling wine of the Marche "Vernaccia di Serrapetrona".

chunks.title: Vernaccia
chunks.text: A possible reason for this is that the root of the name Vernaccia translates to "vernacular" and can apply to any local grape.

chunks.title: Balance and Composure
chunks.text: Balance and Composure is an American alternative rock band from Doylestown, Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: Balance and Composure
chunks.text: They formed in the winter of 2007, after the breakup of two local Doylestown bands.

chunks.title: Balance and Composure
chunks.text: The band's music is often suggested having similarities to Title Fight, Brand New, and Nirvana.

chunks.title: Balance and Composure
chunks.text: They've released three studio albums and five EPs since their inception.

chunks.title: Balance and Composure
chunks.text: Their second album "The Things We Think We're Missing" reached number 51 on the "Billboard" 200, number 10 on the Independent Albums, number 13 on the Modern Rock/Alternative Albums and number 16 on the Rock Albums charts.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: Morellino di Scansano DOCG is an Italian red wine made in the hilly environs of the village of Scansano, GR, in the Maremma region of coastal Tuscany, which has an ancient but obscure tradition of winemaking.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: Morellino is the local name for the Sangiovese grape variety.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: Many people think that the name "Morellino" comes from "morello" (brown), the colour of the region's horses.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: The name may also come from the morello cherry, a dark red cherry with great tartness and acidity.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: The wine, which was granted DOC status in 1978, then upgraded to DOCG status beginning with the 2007 vintage, is made from at least 85% Sangiovese, which is also the basis of the Tuscan wines Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino, and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.

chunks.title: Morellino di Scansano
chunks.text: The remaining 15% can comprise any non-aromatic black grape varieties included in a list made and periodically updated by Tuscan wine authorities.

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: Pignolo is a red Italian wine grape grown predominantly in the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region of northeast Italy.

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: Believed to have been cultivated in the hills of Rosazzo, the grape is now a prominent variety in the Colli Orientali del Friuli "Denominazione di origine controllata" (DOC).

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: In Italian the grape's name originates from "pigna" (pine cone), because the grapes are dense like pine cones.

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: The first recorded mention of the grape was in Abbot Giobatta Michieli's late 17th century book "Bacchus in Friuli" in which he described the grape making "excellent black wine".

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: Today the grape is used to make rich, deep colored, full bodied wine that does well with some time in oak.

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: Well made examples of the wine have good balance between the grape's acidity and tannins with flavor notes of plum and blackberry.

chunks.title: Pignolo (grape)
chunks.text: Most experts believe that it is not related to the Lombardy Pignola grape of the Valtellina region.

chunks.title: Black Grape
chunks.text: Black Grape are a rock band from England, featuring former members of Happy Mondays and Ruthless Rap Assassins.

chunks.title: Black Grape
chunks.text: Their musical style fuses funk and electronic rock with electronic programming and samples.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Black Spanish is now known to be a seedling of an American hybrid grape resulting from a cross of the American "Vitis aestivalis" species of grape with an unknown "Vitis vinifera" pollen donor.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: This hybridization is not known to have been purposeful, and may have occurred naturally, as was the case with many of the early American grape cultivars.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Recently, it was revealed from the microsatellite DNA (a.k.a. Simple Sequence Repeats or SSRs) analyses conducted on various 'Jacquez cultivars' by Dr Jerry Rodrigues that at least two of the European accessions (grapevine collections) which are presently curated in Europe were originally derived from the oldest known Jacquez cultivar (the Madeira Jacquez).

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: The original American hybrid grape parent had found its way to the Madeira Islands early in the 18th century (where it was called Jaquez or Jacquet) and thence to France.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Lenoir is another such seedling similar to Black Spanish which was propagated by Herbemont.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Many other historical names appeared on the scene throughout the early history of these Jacquez seedlings such as Jack, Blue French, Ohio, and El Paso, among others.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: For example, Herbemont tells us that he received Lenoir seeds from a man named Lenoir who cultivated it near Stateburg SC, in the vicinity of the Santee River sometime in the 18th Century.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Lenoir made its way to Texas early, where it even took on the names El Paso and Black Spanish.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: From its wild South Carolina parent, Lenoir (and also Black Spanish) carries natural resistance to the Phylloxera pest, as well as to the deadly Pierce's Disease, which is a common threat to "Vitis vinifera" vineyards in warm winter areas of the United States.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Lenoir was also one of the American vines which the grape breeder Thomas Volney Munson experimented with in the late 19th Century in Denison, Texas.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Prior to its use by Munson, Lenoir was grown and used in wine by Nicholas Herbemont of Columbia, South Carolina in the 1830s, though to a lesser extent than the similar, lighter-skinned variety "Warren" ("Brown French") which become known as Herbemont because of his promotion of that variety.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Lenoir was introduced to Europe in the mid-19th Century, where French vintners were intrigued by its similarity to European "Vitis vinifera" winegrapes, and gave it the names Jacquez and Jacquet.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: It became an important direct producing grape in Europe during the phylloxera crisis, and later was used to some extent as a rootstock to protect the classic vinifera grapes from phylloxera.

chunks.title: Black Spanish (grape)
chunks.text: Ulysses P. Hedrick's famous "Grapes of New York" in 1908 provides the seminal discussion of Lenoir and many of the early North American grapes.

chunks.title: Black Grape Global
chunks.text: Black Grape Global is a London-based artist and entertainment management company.

chunks.title: Black Grape Global
chunks.text: Black Grape's founder attended Kingston University and organised events there, and for other universities in the United Kingdom.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: Petit Manseng (sometimes translated: Small Manseng, rarely "Little Manseng") is a white wine grape variety that is grown primarily in South West France.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: It produces the highest quality wine of any grape in the Manseng family.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: The name is derived from its small, thick skin berries.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: Coupled with the small yields of the grapevine, most Petit Manseng farmers produce around 15 hl of wine per hectare.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: The grape is often left on the vine till December to produce a late harvest dessert wine.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: The grape is grown primarily in Gascony, Jurançon and Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh but has recently drawn interest in New World wine regions like California, North Georgia, Virginia, Ohio, and Australia.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: The reason is that it is expected to follow Viognier's path to popularity among white wine drinkers.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: It was already present in Uruguay, when Basque settlers brought "Manseng" and Tannat vines with them to their new home.

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: Despite being easily recognizable as a white grape while true Manseng is a black grape, wine that is Petit Manseng is still normally labeled as just "Manseng".

chunks.title: Petit Manseng
chunks.text: The grape is often left on the vine to produce a late harvest wine made from its nearly raisin like grapes.

chunks.title: Bez (dancer)
chunks.text: Mark Berry (born 18 April 1964), known professionally by his stage name Bez, is an English percussionist, author, dancer, media personality and comedian.

chunks.title: Bez (dancer)
chunks.text: He is a member of the rock bands Happy Mondays and Black Grape and plays the maracas.

chunks.title: Illyrian Shepherd
chunks.text: The Illyrian Shepherd was a dog breed registered with the Fédération Cynologique Internationale FCI since 1939 under Standard number 41 "Illirski Ovcar".

chunks.title: Illyrian Shepherd
chunks.text: In 1957 the FCI changed the name of the breed to "Yugoslavian Shepherd Dog Sharplanina" (Šarplaninac).

chunks.title: Illyrian Shepherd
chunks.text: Up to 16 March 1968 the Karst Shepherd (kraški ovčar) carried the same name.

chunks.title: Illyrian Shepherd
chunks.text: Since then the two breeds are independent.

chunks.title: Taigan
chunks.text: The Taigan (Kyrgyz: Тайган ) also known as Kyrgyzdyn Taighany (Kyrgyzskaya Borzaya Taigan in Russian) is a sighthound breed from Kyrgyzstan, which is not yet recognized by the FCI, but is recognized by a number of kennel clubs on national level.

chunks.title: Brazilian Dogo
chunks.text: Brazilian Dogo(Portuguese: "Dogue Brasileiro" ), also called Brazilian Dogge, is a Molosser-type working dog breed originating in Brazil.

chunks.title: Brazilian Dogo
chunks.text: It is neither recognized by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) nor the American Kennel Club (AKC).

chunks.title: Brazilian Dogo
chunks.text: However, it has the official national recognition of the Confederação Brasileira de Cinofilia(CBKC) where it belongs to the Group 11 - Breeds not recognized by the FCI ("Raça não reconhecida pela FCI").

chunks.title: Rastreador Brasileiro
chunks.text: The Rastreador Brasileiro (in English, Brazilian Tracker) is a large breed of dog from Brazil, first recognised by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 1967, but an outbreak of disease, compounded by an overdose of insecticide, wiped out the breed's entire breeding stock.

chunks.title: Rastreador Brasileiro
chunks.text: The FCI and the Brazilian Kennel Club (Confederação Brasileira de Cinofilia) then declared the breed extinct in 1973 and delisted it.

chunks.title: Rastreador Brasileiro
chunks.text: Since then, efforts have been made to re-create the breed.

chunks.title: Rastreador Brasileiro
chunks.text: The Rastreador Brasileiro is a hunting dog of the scenthound type.

chunks.title: Rastreador Brasileiro
chunks.text: The breed is also known by the names "Urrador" (for its hunting cry) or "Urrador Americano", in reference to the American (U.S.) coonhounds in its background.

chunks.title: Continental bulldog
chunks.text: The Continental Bulldog is a dog breed from Switzerland.

chunks.title: Continental bulldog
chunks.text: This bulldog breed is not officially recognized by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale, although the procedure towards recognition by the FCI was started on 24 January 2011.

chunks.title: Continental bulldog
chunks.text: The breed has been officially recognized by the Swiss kennel club SKG since 5 December 2004.

chunks.title: Barbado da Terceira
chunks.text: The Barbado da Terceira is a medium-sized dog, with a volumous and robust look.

chunks.title: Barbado da Terceira
chunks.text: The Barbado da Terceira is the most recently recognized Portuguese breed.

chunks.title: Barbado da Terceira
chunks.text: The Portuguese Kennel Club (CPC) recognized it, on a provisional basis, on November 2004; it is not yet recognized by The Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI).

chunks.title: Barbado da Terceira
chunks.text: It is a population native to the Azores Islands, in particular the Terceira Island.

chunks.title: Small Münsterländer
chunks.text: The Small Münsterländer (also SM or Kleiner Münsterländer) is a versatile hunting-pointing-retrieving dog breed that reached its current form in the area around Münster, Germany.

chunks.title: Small Münsterländer
chunks.text: The Large Münsterländer is from the same area, but was developed from different breeding stock and is not related as the names would suggest.

chunks.title: Small Münsterländer
chunks.text: Small Münsterländers bear a resemblance to both spaniels and setters but are more versatile while hunting on land and water.

chunks.title: Small Münsterländer
chunks.text: The Small Münsterländer is recognized by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale under Group 7, Section 1.2, Continental Pointing Dogs of Spaniel type, by the American Kennel Club as a Foundation Breed, and by The Kennel Club and the United Kennel Club as a gun dog.

chunks.title: Small Münsterländer
chunks.text: It is related to the Epagneul Français and the Drentsche Patrijshond.

chunks.title: Korean Jindo
chunks.text: The Korean Jindo (Hangul: 진돗개 ; Hanja: 珍島狗 ) is a breed of hunting dog that originated on Jindo Island in South Korea.

chunks.title: Korean Jindo
chunks.text: Brought to the United States with South Korean expatriates, it is celebrated in its native land for its fierce loyalty and brave nature.

chunks.title: Korean Jindo
chunks.text: The Jindo breed became recognized by the United Kennel Club on January 1, 1998 and by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 2005.

chunks.title: Guatemalan Dogo
chunks.text: Guatemalan Dogo ("Dogo Guatemalteco"), formerly known as the Guatemalan Bull Terrier ("Bullterrier Guatemalteco"), and Guatemalan Mastiff, is a Molosser-type dog breed originating in Guatemala.

chunks.title: Guatemalan Dogo
chunks.text: It is neither recognized by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) nor the American Kennel Club (AKC).

chunks.title: Guatemalan Dogo
chunks.text: However, it has the official national recognition of the Asociación Canofila Guatemalteca (ACANGUA) where it belongs to the Group 2.2.1 - Mastiffs.

chunks.title: Guatemalan Dogo
chunks.text: As the unique breed originating in Guatemala, it is also the national dog of the country.

chunks.title: Guatemalan Dogo
chunks.text: Nowadays it has spread to various other countries, such as the USA.

chunks.title: List of dog breeds recognized by the FCI
chunks.text: A list of the dog breeds recognized by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale.

chunks.title: List of dog breeds recognized by the FCI
chunks.text: The list can be organized by the FCI number, the breed group, and either the official original, English, French, German or Spanish FCI name.

chunks.title: Marx Reloaded
chunks.text: Marx Reloaded is a 2011 German documentary film written and directed by the British writer and theorist Jason Barker.

chunks.title: Marx Reloaded
chunks.text: Featuring interviews with several well-known philosophers, the film aims to examine the relevance of Karl Marx's ideas in relation to the Great Recession.

chunks.title: Marx Reloaded
chunks.text: The film's title is a wordplay on "The Matrix Reloaded", the sequel to "The Matrix," which is parodied in the documentary.

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: Leonard Marx (March 22, 1887 – October 11, 1961), known professionally as Chico Marx, was an American comedian, musician, bandleader, actor and film star.

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: He was a member of the Marx Brothers (Groucho Marx, Harpo Marx, and Zeppo Marx).

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: His persona in the act was that of a charming, dim-witted albeit crafty con artist, seemingly of rural Italian origin, who wore shabby clothes and sported a curly-haired wig and Tyrolean hat.

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: In virtually every film that includes the main trio of the Marx Brothers, Chico is seen working with Harpo Marx, usually as partners in crime.

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: Leonard was the oldest of the Marx Brothers to live past early childhood (first-born Manfred Marx had died in infancy).

chunks.title: Chico Marx
chunks.text: In addition to his work as a performer, he played an important role in the management and development of the act in its early years.

chunks.title: The Private Life of Plants
chunks.text: The Private Life of Plants is a BBC nature documentary series written and presented by David Attenborough, first shown in the United Kingdom from 11 January 1995.

chunks.title: Une double famille
chunks.text: Une double famille ("A Second Home") is a lengthy short story by Honoré de Balzac, which first appeared in 1830 under the title "La femme vertueuse" ("The Virtuous Woman").

chunks.title: Une double famille
chunks.text: It was subsequently published in 1832 by Mame et Delaunay as part of Balzac's "Scènes de la vie privée" ("Scenes from Private Life").

chunks.title: Une double famille
chunks.text: In 1835 it appeared, in an edition by Madame Béchet, in the collection "Études de mœurs" ("Studies of Manners").

chunks.title: Une double famille
chunks.text: The novel only acquired its present title in 1842, when the fifth edition appeared in Volume I of the "Scenes from Private Life", which was also the first volume of Balzac's "La Comédie humaine".

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: Groucho: A Life in Revue is a stage play written by Groucho Marx's son Arthur Marx and Robert Fisher .

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: With musical direction by Jim Grady.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: It is a look at the life and career of the famous entertainer Groucho Marx of the Marx Brothers and "You Bet Your Life" fame.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: It opened off-Broadway at the Lucille Lortel Theatre on October 8, 1986 and played 254 performances closing on May 3, 1987.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: It starred 23-year-old actor Frank Ferrante as Groucho Marx from age 15 to 85, Les Marsden as Harpo Marx and Chico Marx, Faith Prince as The Girls and Rusty Magee as The Citizen of Freedonia.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: It was directed by Arthur Marx.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: The play opened to rave reviews. "

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: The New York Times" wrote, "There is laughter in abundance" and described Ferrante's performance as "artful...his timing is digital sharp."

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: The "New York Post" dubbed it "hilarious...a brilliant revue."

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: "Groucho" was nominated for two NY Outer Critics Circle Awards - one for Best Play and one for Ferrante's performance.

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: Ferrante won a 1987 New York Theatre World Award for 'Outstanding New Talent.'

chunks.title: Groucho: A Life in Revue
chunks.text: The play was produced by Nancy and Ronnie Horowitz.

chunks.title: The Private Life of the Kingfisher
chunks.text: The Private Life of the Kingfisher (styled in its opening titles as "The private life of the KINGFISHER), made in 1966 and screened in 1967 as episode 144 of the nature series "Look", was the first BBC natural history film to be shown in colour.

chunks.title: Marx in Soho
chunks.text: Marx in Soho is a 1999 one-man play written by American historian Howard Zinn, about the life of 19th-century philosopher Karl Marx.

chunks.title: Marx in Soho
chunks.text: Zinn wrote the play to "show Marx as few people knew him, as a family man, struggling to support his wife and children."

chunks.title: Marx in Soho
chunks.text: The play is set in the New York City neighborhood of Soho, a humorous nod to the London neighborhood of the same name in which Marx spent much of his life.

chunks.title: Work–life interface
chunks.text: Work–life interface is the intersection of work and private life.

chunks.title: Work–life interface
chunks.text: There are many aspects of one's personal life that can intersect with work including family, leisure, and health.

chunks.title: Work–life interface
chunks.text: Work–life interface is bidirectional; for instance, work can interfere with private life, and private life can interfere with work.

chunks.title: Work–life interface
chunks.text: This interface can be adverse in nature (e.g., work-life conflict) or can be beneficial (e.g., work-life enrichment) in nature.

chunks.title: The Private Life of Louis XIV
chunks.text: The Private Life of Louis XIV or Liselotte of the Palatinate (German:Liselotte von der Pfalz) is a 1935 German historical film directed by Carl Froelich and starring Renate Müller, Eugen Klöpfer and Maria Krahn.

chunks.title: The Private Life of Louis XIV
chunks.text: The film's English language release title is a reference to the hit British film "The Private Life of Henry VIII" (1933).

chunks.title: The Private Life of the Gannets
chunks.text: The Private Life of the Gannets is a 1934 British short documentary film, directed by Julian Huxley, about a colony of Northern Gannet (Morus bassanus) on the small rocky island of Grassholm, off the coast of Wales.

chunks.title: The Private Life of the Gannets
chunks.text: It received a special mention at the 3rd Venice International Film Festival in 1935 and won the Best Short Subject (One-Reel) at the 10th Academy Awards in 1938.

chunks.title: The Private Life of the Gannets
chunks.text: The title was chosen by producer Alexander Korda as a reference to "The Private Life of Henry VIII" (1933), his breakthrough film of the previous year.

chunks.title: Land Ho!
chunks.text: Land Ho!

chunks.title: Land Ho!
chunks.text: is an American-Icelandic adventure comedy film co-written and co-directed by Martha Stephens and Aaron Katz.

chunks.title: Land Ho!
chunks.text: The film made its world premiere at 2014 Sundance Film Festival on January 19, 2014.

chunks.title: Land Ho!
chunks.text: It also screened at the 2014 Tribeca Film Festival, Los Angeles Film Festival, Nantucket Film Festival, Locarno International Film Festival, and BFI London Film Festival .

chunks.title: Long Prairie Municipal Airport
chunks.text: Long Prairie Municipal Airport (FAA LID: 14Y) , also known as Todd Field or Todd Field Airport, is a public use airport located four nautical miles (7 km) south of the central business district of Long Prairie, a city in Todd County, Minnesota, United States.

chunks.title: Long Prairie Municipal Airport
chunks.text: The airport is owned by Todd County and the City of Long Prairie.

chunks.title: Dance Party USA (film)
chunks.text: Dance Party USA is a 2006 film written and directed by Aaron Katz.

chunks.title: Dance Party USA (film)
chunks.text: It stars Cole Pensinger and Anna Kavan.The film and director have also been mentioned by the media as an important part of the "mumblecore" movement in independent cinema.

chunks.title: Mumblecore
chunks.text: Mumblecore is a subgenre of independent film characterized by naturalistic acting and dialogue (often improvised), low-budget film production, an emphasis on dialogue over plot, and a focus on the personal relationships of people in their 20s and 30s.

chunks.title: Mumblecore
chunks.text: Filmmakers associated with the genre include Andrew Bujalski, Lynn Shelton, Mark Duplass, Jay Duplass, Aaron Katz, Joe Swanberg, and Ry Russo-Young; in many cases, though, these directors reject the term.

chunks.title: Aaron Katz (filmmaker)
chunks.text: Aaron Katz (born October 29, 1981) is an award-winning independent American filmmaker from Portland, Oregon.

chunks.title: Diamonds (1999 film)
chunks.text: Diamonds is a 1999 American comedy film directed by John Mallory Asher and written by Allan Aaron Katz.

chunks.title: Diamonds (1999 film)
chunks.text: The film stars Kirk Douglas, Dan Aykroyd, Lauren Bacall, Jenny McCarthy, and Corbin Allred.

chunks.title: Todd Field
chunks.text: William Todd Field (born February 24, 1964) is an American actor and three-time Academy Award nominated filmmaker.

chunks.title: Gemini (2017 film)
chunks.text: Gemini is a 2017 American mystery thriller film written, directed, edited by Aaron Katz.

chunks.title: Gemini (2017 film)
chunks.text: It stars Lola Kirke, Zoë Kravitz, Greta Lee, Michelle Forbes, Nelson Franklin, Reeve Carney, Jessica Parker Kennedy, James Ransone and Ricki Lake.

chunks.title: Cold Weather
chunks.text: Cold Weather is an American mystery film written by Aaron Katz, Ben Stambler, and Brendan McFadden and directed by Katz with Stambler and McFadden producing.

chunks.title: Cold Weather
chunks.text: The film stars Cris Lankenau as a former forensic science student investigating the mysterious disappearance of his ex-girlfriend.

chunks.title: Cold Weather
chunks.text: The film was shot and set in Portland, Oregon, which was also the setting of Katz's debut feature, "Dance Party USA".

chunks.title: Quiet City (film)
chunks.text: Quiet City is a 2007 film directed by Aaron Katz that premiered at the 2007 South by Southwest Film Festival in the Emerging Visions category.

chunks.title: Quiet City (film)
chunks.text: Subsequently it played at film festivals around the world, including the Sarasota Film Festival, Maryland Film Festival, Stockholm Film Festival and Milano Film Festival, before premiering theatrically in New York in August 2007.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Golden Receiver
chunks.text: Air Bud: Golden Receiver (also known as Air Bud 2) is the 1998 sequel to "Air Bud".

chunks.title: Air Bud: Golden Receiver
chunks.text: The film was shot in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Golden Receiver
chunks.text: It is also the last of the "Air Bud" films to be released theatrically.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Golden Receiver
chunks.text: Outside the United States the film was often titled "Air Bud 2".

chunks.title: Air Bud: Golden Receiver
chunks.text: This film is dedicated in memory of the original Air Bud (Air Buddy), who died of Synovial sarcoma, a rare form of cancer that affects soft tissue near the joints of the arm, leg, or neck in 1998, just several months before the movie's release.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Seventh Inning Fetch
chunks.text: Air Bud: Seventh Inning Fetch (also known as Air Bud 4) is a 2002 made-for-video American film, and the fourth film in the "Air Bud" series.

chunks.title: Blank Check (film)
chunks.text: Blank Check is a 1994 American comedy film directed by Rupert Wainwright and starring Brian Bonsall, Karen Duffy, Miguel Ferrer, James Rebhorn, Tone Lōc, Jayne Atkinson and Michael Lerner.

chunks.title: Blank Check (film)
chunks.text: It was released on February 11, 1994 by Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Air Bud: World Pup
chunks.text: Air Bud: World Pup (also known as Air Bud 3 in most other countries) is a 2000 made-for-video American film, and the third film in the "Air Bud" series.

chunks.title: Air Bud: World Pup
chunks.text: It was the first Air Bud movie to be filmed without Buddy, the canine star of the first two films; Buddy died after production of the previous film, "".

chunks.title: Air Bud (series)
chunks.text: The Air Bud film series (also known as Air Buddies or Disney Buddies) is an American film franchise based on a sports-playing Golden Retriever named Buddy, portrayed by Air Buddy.

chunks.title: Air Bud (series)
chunks.text: The franchise began in 1997 with the theatrical release of "Air Bud", followed by the theatrical release of "" in 1998.

chunks.title: Air Bud (series)
chunks.text: The rest of the films in the series were released in direct-to-video form.

chunks.title: Air Bud (series)
chunks.text: The "Air Buddies" or "Disney Buddies" spin-off series began in 2006 with the release of "Air Buddies" and it focuses on the adventures of Buddy's talking Golden Retriever puppies.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Spikes Back
chunks.text: Air Bud: Spikes Back (also known as Air Bud 5) is the fifth and final film in the original "Air Bud series".

chunks.title: Air Bud: Spikes Back
chunks.text: The film series itself was followed by a spin-off series: the "Air Buddies" franchise.

chunks.title: Air Bud: Spikes Back
chunks.text: It was released on June 24, 2003 as a direct to video sequel.

chunks.title: Griffin Newman
chunks.text: Griffin Claude Beresford Dauphin Hunter Newman (born February 19, 1989), known professionally as Griffin Newman, is an American actor and comedian.

chunks.title: Griffin Newman
chunks.text: He currently stars as Arthur in Amazon's remake of "The Tick" TV series.

chunks.title: Griffin Newman
chunks.text: He co-hosts the podcast "Blank Check (with Griffin and David)" in which he and David Sims over-analyze filmographies of directors they deem to have earned a "blank check" in Hollywood.

chunks.title: Blank cheque
chunks.text: A blank cheque (US: blank check) or carte blanche, in the literal sense, is a cheque that has no numerical value written in, but is already signed.

chunks.title: Blank cheque
chunks.text: In the figurative sense, it is used to describe a situation in which an agreement has been made that is open-ended or vague, and therefore subject to abuse, or in which a party is willing to consider any expense in the pursuance of their goals.

chunks.title: The Magnificent Marble Machine
chunks.text: The Magnificent Marble Machine is an American television game show which featured a giant pinball machine as its centerpiece.

chunks.title: The Magnificent Marble Machine
chunks.text: The program premiered on NBC on July 7, 1975, at 12:00 pm ET, replacing the short-lived game show "Blank Check", whose time slot had been taken over by "Jackpot".

chunks.title: Air Bud
chunks.text: Air Bud is a 1997 American comedy film that sparked the franchise centered on the real-life dog, Buddy, a Golden Retriever.

chunks.title: Air Bud
chunks.text: The film was financially successful, grossing $4 million in its opening weekend and totaling $27.8 million in its run, against an estimated $3 million budget.

chunks.title: List of soft drinks by country
chunks.text: This is a list of soft drinks in order of the brand's country of origin.

chunks.title: List of soft drinks by country
chunks.text: A soft drink is a beverage that typically contains water (often, but not always, carbonated water), usually a sweetener and usually a flavoring agent.

chunks.title: List of soft drinks by country
chunks.text: The sweetener may be sugar, high-fructose corn syrup, fruit juice, sugar substitutes (in the case of diet drinks) or some combination of these.

chunks.title: List of soft drinks by country
chunks.text: Soft drinks may also contain caffeine, colorings, preservatives and other ingredients.

chunks.title: Solo (Norwegian soft drink)
chunks.text: Solo is an orange-flavoured soft drink, owned by the Norwegian companies Ringnes, Oskar Sylte, Aass, and Mack.

chunks.title: Solo (Norwegian soft drink)
chunks.text: The recipe was originally Spanish, and brought to the Tønsberg Bryggeri by Torleif Gulliksrud in 1934.

chunks.title: Solo (Norwegian soft drink)
chunks.text: Solo quickly became Norway's most popular soft drink, and until the 1960s was bigger than Coca-Cola in Norway.

chunks.title: Solo (Norwegian soft drink)
chunks.text: In 1999, Pepsi passed Solo in market share, leaving Solo as third most popular.

chunks.title: Sunkist (soft drink)
chunks.text: Sunkist is a brand of primarily orange flavored soft drinks launched in 1979.

chunks.title: Jūrokucha
chunks.text: Jūrokucha (十六茶 ) is a blended tea drink produced and distributed by Asahi Soft Drinks in Japan.

chunks.title: Jūrokucha
chunks.text: The drink was originally created and sold by Chanson Cosmetics as a dry blended green tea.

chunks.title: Jūrokucha
chunks.text: Beginning in March 1993, Chanson and Asahi Soft Drinks released Jūrokucha as a joint venture premade beverage.

chunks.title: Jūrokucha
chunks.text: In February 2007, the packaging and flavor was updated.

chunks.title: United Soft Drinks
chunks.text: United Soft Drinks is a producer of soft drinks based in Utrecht in the Netherlands.

chunks.title: United Soft Drinks
chunks.text: Their best known-brands are AA Drink, a line of sport drinks, Bar-le-Duc, a line of mineral waters, London, a line of bitter lemonades, Raak, a line of fruit syrups, and the product Kindercola.

chunks.title: United Soft Drinks
chunks.text: The company also produces a number of private label lemonades.

chunks.title: Soda fountain
chunks.text: A soda fountain is a device that dispenses carbonated soft drinks, called fountain drinks.

chunks.title: Soda fountain
chunks.text: They can be found in restaurants, concession stands and other locations such as convenience stores.

chunks.title: Soda fountain
chunks.text: The device combines flavored syrup or syrup concentrate and carbon dioxide with chilled and purified water to make soft drinks, either manually, or in a vending machine which is essentially an automated soda fountain that is operated using a soda gun.

chunks.title: Soda fountain
chunks.text: Today, the syrup often is pumped from a special container called a bag-in-box (BIB).

chunks.title: Barr Britvic Soft Drinks
chunks.text: Barr Britvic Soft Drinks plc was a proposed company to be founded by the merger between two British soft drink manufacturers, A G Barr and Britvic.

chunks.title: Barr Britvic Soft Drinks
chunks.text: Former Britvic shareholders were to own 63 per cent of the combined entity, whilst Barr shareholders would have held 37 per cent.

chunks.title: Barr Britvic Soft Drinks
chunks.text: Measured by revenue, it would have been one of the largest soft drinks companies in Europe.

chunks.title: Barr Britvic Soft Drinks
chunks.text: The company would have had annual sales of more than £1.5 billion and would have employed around 4,300 staff.

chunks.title: Geo. Hall & Sons
chunks.text: Geo.

chunks.title: Geo. Hall & Sons
chunks.text: Hall & Sons, better known as Halls was a soft drink manufacturer founded in 1849 in Marryatville, South Australia, by English immigrant George Hall (1818-1881).

chunks.title: Geo. Hall & Sons
chunks.text: During his teenage years, Hall had pursued the brewing of non alcoholic drinks as a hobby.

chunks.title: Geo. Hall & Sons
chunks.text: Halls produced a wide range of soft drinks and cordials, having established itself as a local bottler specialising in "stonie" ginger beer by 1851.

chunks.title: Geo. Hall & Sons
chunks.text: Other soft drinks included Passiona, a Cottee's product they bottled for local consumption.

chunks.title: Asahi Soft Drinks
chunks.text: Asahi Soft Drinks Co., Ltd (アサヒ飲料株式会社 , Asahi Inryō Kabushiki Kaisha ) is a soft drink company founded in 1982 and headquartered in the Azuma-bashi district of Sumida, Tokyo, Japan.

chunks.title: Asahi Soft Drinks
chunks.text: It is a subsidiary of Asahi Breweries.

chunks.title: Asahi Soft Drinks
chunks.text: The company sponsors the Asahi Soft Drinks Challengers, an American football team in the Japanese X-League, as well as a futsal team.

chunks.title: Cott
chunks.text: The Cott Corporation is a supplier of private label carbonated soft drinks distributing to the United States, Canada, Mexico, the United Kingdom, and Europe.

chunks.title: Cott
chunks.text: In addition to producing private-label beverages for retailers, Cott also has portfolio of its own brands, including Cott, RC (excluding the United States, where it is part of Dr Pepper Snapple Group), Ben Shaws, Stars & Stripes, Vintage and Vess soft drinks, ready-to-drink teas, sparkling and flavoured waters, sports and energy drinks, juice drinks and smoothies. Newer Cott brands include Orient Emporium, GL-7, Red Rain Energy and After Shock Energy.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The P2 Mk2 and P3 Mk2 are Pakistani plastic cased minimum metal anti-tank blast mines.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The P2 Mk2 has a square case with a central circular ribbed pressure plate, the P3 is circular with a central circular pressure plate.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: Both mines use anti-personnel mines as the fuse, typically the either the P4 Mk1 or P2 Mk2 anti-personnel mines.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The anti-personnel mine sits in a cavity below the pressure plate, when enough pressure is place on the pressure plate of the mine, it collapses onto the anti-personnel mine triggering it and the main charge which sits below it.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: A yellow canvas carrying strap is normally fitted to the side of the mine.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The mines have a secondary fuse well on the bottom which can be used with anti-handling devices.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: A GLM-2 electronic booby trap can be fitted to the cavity under the pressure plate.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The mine is supplied with a steel disc which makes the mine more easily detectable, although this is seldom used.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: Since 1997 only a detectable version of the mine has been produced, and to comply with the Convention on Conventional Weapons amended protocol II, Pakistani stocks of the mine are being retrofitted with steel detection discs.

chunks.title: P3 Mk2 mine
chunks.text: The mines are found in Afghanistan, Angola, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Pakistan, Somalia, and Tajikistan.

chunks.title: N.W.T. Mining Heritage Society
chunks.text: The N.W.T. Mining Heritage Society, in the Northwest Territories, Canada, was first formed in early 2000 as the Giant Mine Heritage Group to rescue items from the Giant Mine site after its owner, Royal Oak Mines Incorporated, went bankrupt.

chunks.title: Cascadero Falls
chunks.text: Cascadero Falls is a waterfall on the Finlay River in the Northern Interior of British Columbia, Canada, located just below that river's head at the outlet of Thutade Lake.

chunks.title: Cascadero Falls
chunks.text: The height of the falls is 180 ft and below it there are numerous cascades or rapids in a twisting course prior to the river's general northeastward trend from this area.

chunks.title: Cascadero Falls
chunks.text: The falls are slated for hydroelectric development in connection with the area's mines, the largest of which is the Kemess Mine owned by Northgate Minerals Inc., located just east of the foot of Thutade Lake in the valley of Kemess Creek.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: The National Mine Map Repository (NMMR) is part of the United States Department of the Interior (DOI), Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE or OSM).

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: The NMMR resides in the Pittsburgh suburb of Green Tree, Pennsylvania, and collects and maintains mine map information and images for the entire country, including data and maps of coal mines in the anthracite coal region of northeastern Pennsylvania.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: The Green Tree facility provides and stores, digitally and in microfilm (aperture cards), over 182,000 maps of abandoned mines.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: This repository contains maps of mine workings from the 1790s to the present day.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: It serves as a point of reference for mine maps and other information for both surface and underground mines throughout the United States.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: It also serves as a location to retrieve mine maps in an emergency.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: The NMMR provides services ranging from retrieving mine related data for economic analysis to assessing the potential risk associated with underground mining.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: Through analysis of mine maps and related information, the repository assists private and public sectors in industrial and commercial development, highway construction, and the preservation of public health, safety, and welfare.

chunks.title: National Mine Map Repository
chunks.text: In addition, they collect, reproduce, and maintain a national inventory of mine maps and supporting documentation for private and public interests.

chunks.title: Dondero High School
chunks.text: George A. Dondero High School (formerly Royal Oak High School) was opened in 1927 in Royal Oak, Michigan in Greater Detroit.

chunks.title: Dondero High School
chunks.text: It was named after former United States congressman and Royal Oak School Board President George A. Dondero.

chunks.title: Dondero High School
chunks.text: A part of the Royal Oak Neighborhood Schools, it was merged into the new Royal Oak High School.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: The Colomac Mine was a privately owned and operated open pit gold mine located 220 km northwest of Yellowknife in the Northwest Territories in Canada .

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: The Colomac mine operated between 1990–1992, and 1994–1997.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: It was operated by Neptune Resources Limited that had little success in making a profit during its operation.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: In 1994, the mine had reopened under Royal Oak Mines Inc.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: Both Neptune Resources and Royal Oak Mines where both owned and operated by Peggy Witte.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: Due to low gold prices and high cost of mining, Royal Oak Mines was forced into bankruptcy.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: The Federal Government of Canada became owners of the mine, along with the related environmental issues.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: A major cleanup effort is under way to prevent the mine from polluting the environment, but this might be too late at this stage.

chunks.title: Colomac Mine
chunks.text: This mine is now owned and controlled by the Indigenous and Northern Affairs department of the Federal government, while Public Works and Government services is the current contracting authority.

chunks.title: Royal Oak Neighborhood Schools
chunks.text: Royal Oak Neighborhood Schools or Royal Oak School District (ROSD) is a school district in Greater Detroit, Michigan.

chunks.title: Royal Oak Neighborhood Schools
chunks.text: The district provides public school services for the municipality of Royal Oak and the easternmost portion of Berkley.

chunks.title: Royal Oak Neighborhood Schools
chunks.text: The official name is School District of the City of Royal Oak.

chunks.title: Kemess Mine
chunks.text: The Kemess Mine was an open-pit copper and gold mine, located just northeast of the foot of Thutade Lake, at the head of the Finlay River, in the Omineca Mountains of the Northern Interior of British Columbia, Canada.

chunks.title: Kemess Mine
chunks.text: It was operated by Royal Oak Mines from 1998 to 1999, when it was bought by Northgate Minerals.

chunks.title: Kemess Mine
chunks.text: Northgate operated the mine until its closure in 2011; that year Northgate was taken over by AuRico Gold.

chunks.title: Kemess Mine
chunks.text: In 2014 AuRico Gold partitioned off its portion of kemess Mine ownership creating a new company called AuRico Metals.

chunks.title: Kemess Mine
chunks.text: AuRico Metals is actively implementing permits for a block caving mine.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: Thutade Lake is located in the Omineca Mountains of the Northern Interior of British Columbia, Canada.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: About 40 km in length, and no more than about 2 km wide, the lake is primarily significant as the ultimate source of the Mackenzie River.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: The lake is at the head of the Finlay River, which joins the Peace River via Williston Lake.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: The area is very remote, being located about 260 km north of Smithers, although several mining operations for ores containing copper, lead, zinc and silver have occurred around the lake.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: The largest of these is the Kemess Mine, an iron and copper property originally owned by Royal Oak Mines and now by Northgate Minerals, located in the valley of Kemess Creek, which is off the northeast end of Thutade Lake.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: The mine is accessed by the Omineca Resource Road and other resource routes, and is 400 km by road from Prince George.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake
chunks.text: Just downstream from the outlet of Thutade Lake, the Finlay plunges over 180 ft Cascadero Falls, and then through a series of cataracts in a twisting course until it begins its main northeastward trend.

chunks.title: Thutade Lake

chunks.title: Bullying in medicine
chunks.text: Bullying in the medical profession is common, particularly of student or trainee physicians.

chunks.title: Bullying in medicine
chunks.text: It is thought that this is at least in part an outcome of conservative traditional hierarchical structures and teaching methods in the medical profession which may result in a bullying cycle.

chunks.title: Leonty Magnitsky
chunks.text: Leonty Filippovich Magnitsky (Russian: Леонтий Филиппович Магницкий ), born Telyatin (Russian: Телятин ), (June 9, 1669, Ostashkov – October 19, 1739, Moscow) was a Russian mathematician and educator.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: A stereotype is a generalized idea or image about a particular person or thing that is often oversimplified and offensive.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: Stereotypes are victim of prejudice when negative portrayals of a group are untrue of individual members.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: Nursing has been stereotyped throughout the history of the profession.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: A common misconception is that all nurses are female; this has led to the stereotype of male nurses as effeminate.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: These generalized ideas of the nursing profession have formed a skewed image of nurses in the media.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: The image of a nurse projected by the media is typically of a young white single female being over-sexualized as well as diminished intellectually; this idea is then portrayed in get-well cards, television shows and novels.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: The over-sexualized nurse is commonly referred to as a naughty nurse and is shown as a sex symbol or nymphomaniac. Along with these common stereotypes, studies have identified several other popular images used in media such as handmaiden, angel, torturer, homosexual male, alcoholic, buffoon and woman in white.

chunks.title: Nurse stereotypes
chunks.text: Common stereotypes of nursing and portrayal of these misconceptions have fueled a discussion on the effects they have on the profession, harmful or good.

chunks.title: Leonid Khachiyan
chunks.text: Leonid Genrikhovich Khachiyan (Armenian: Լեոնիդ Գենրիխովիչ Խաչիյան ; Russian: Леонид Генрихович Хачиян ; May 3, 1952 – April 29, 2005) was a Soviet mathematician of Armenian descent who taught Computer Science at Rutgers University.

chunks.title: Leonid Khachiyan
chunks.text: He was most famous for his ellipsoid algorithm (1979) for linear programming, which was the first such algorithm known to have a polynomial running time.

chunks.title: Leonid Khachiyan
chunks.text: Even though this algorithm was shown to be impractical due to the high degree of the polynomial in its running time, it has inspired other randomized algorithms for convex programming and is considered a significant theoretical breakthrough.

chunks.title: Reading law
chunks.text: Reading law is the method by which persons in common law countries, particularly the United States, entered the legal profession before the advent of law schools.

chunks.title: Reading law
chunks.text: This usage specifically refers to a means of entering the profession (although in England it is still customary to say that a university undergraduate is "reading" a course, which may be law or any other).

chunks.title: Reading law
chunks.text: "Reading the law" consists of an extended internship or apprenticeship under the tutelage or mentoring of an experienced lawyer.

chunks.title: Reading law
chunks.text: A small number of U.S. jurisdictions still permit this practice today.

chunks.title: Mursmäcka

chunks.title: Mursmäcka
chunks.text: A mursmäcka was a female construction worker with the task to hand mortar during construction work.

chunks.title: Mursmäcka
chunks.text: The profession is recorded from at least 1691 (though it is not confirmed by name until the 1830s) and discontinued in 1922.

chunks.title: Mursmäcka
chunks.text: This was a very hard but common work for a poor uneducated women during the 19th century, particularly in Stockholm.

chunks.title: Mursmäcka
chunks.text: In July 1888, the Mursmäcka of Stockholm performed a great strike action which attracted considerable attention in contemporary Sweden.

chunks.title: Legal Profession Admission Board

chunks.title: Legal Profession Admission Board

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: A convention, in the sense of a meeting, is a gathering of individuals who meet at an arranged place and time in order to discuss or engage in some common interest.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: The most common conventions are based upon industry, profession, and fandom.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Trade conventions typically focus on a particular industry or industry segment, and feature keynote speakers, vendor displays, and other information and activities of interest to the event organizers and attendees.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Professional conventions focus on issues of concern to the profession and advancements in the profession.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Such conventions are generally organized by societies or communities dedicated to promotion of the topic of interest.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Fan conventions usually feature displays, shows, and sales based on pop culture and guest celebrities.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Science fiction conventions traditionally partake of the nature of both professional conventions and fan conventions, with the balance varying from one to another.

chunks.title: Convention (meeting)
chunks.text: Conventions also exist for various hobbies, such as gaming or model railroads.

chunks.text: He was succeeded by Metropolitan Irenaeus (Bekish).

chunks.title: Catlin Seaview Survey

chunks.title: Hot toddy
chunks.text: A hot toddy, also known as hot whiskey in Ireland, is typically a mixed drink made of liquor and water with honey (or, in some recipes, sugar), herbs (such as tea) and spices, and served hot.

chunks.title: Hot toddy
chunks.text: Hot toddy recipes vary and are traditionally drunk before retiring for the night, or in wet or cold weather.

chunks.title: Hot toddy
chunks.text: Some believe the drink relieves the symptoms of the cold and flu—in "How to Drink", Victoria Moore describes the drink as "the vitamin C for health, the honey to soothe, the alcohol to numb".

chunks.title: Nadar climber

chunks.title: Submarino (beverage)

chunks.title: Kir (cocktail)

chunks.title: Vino cotto

chunks.title: Vino cotto
chunks.text: It is a strong ruby-colored wine, usually semi-sweet, and traditionally drunk in small glasses with puddings and cheese.

chunks.title: 1912 World Hard Court Championships
chunks.text: This tournament was open to all international amateur tennis players and was part of a series of world championships being advanced by the International Lawn Tennis Federation (ILTF), the others being the World Grass Court Championships (Wimbledon) and the World Covered Court Championships held in a variety of countries.

chunks.title: 1912 World Hard Court Championships
chunks.text: The WHCC was open to all nationalities unlike the French Championships which were open only to tennis players who were licensed in France.

chunks.text: In 1904 New Zealand Lawn Tennis Association amalgamated with six Australian state tennis associations to form the Lawn Tennis Association of Australasia.

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: New Zealand Lawn Tennis Association played a significant role in the origin of the Australian Open.

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: New Zealand hosted the championship twice— Christchurch (1906) and Hastings (1912).

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: The geographical remoteness of both the countries (Australia and New Zealand) made it difficult for foreign players to enter the tournament.

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: In Christchurch in 1906, of a small field of 10 players, only two Australians attended, and the tournament was won by a New Zealander (Tony Wilding).

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: Lawn Tennis Association of Australasia was one of the twelve national associations of tennis which established the International Lawn Tennis Federation (ILTF) in a conference in Paris, France on 1 March 1913.

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: From 1905 until 1919, New Zealand and Australian tennis players participated in the International Lawn Tennis Challenge (Davis Cup) under the alias of "Team Australasia", the team claimed a title six times (1907, 1908, 1909, 1911, 1914, 1919), however, there were attempts to severance this trans-tasmanian partnership, in order to allow New Zealand players to represent their nation on international tennis events.

chunks.title: Tennis New Zealand
chunks.text: In 1922, New Zealand dropped out from this partnership and on 16 March 1923 New Zealand Lawn Tennis Association was granted affiliation to the International Lawn Tennis Association and thereby became eligible to enter the International Lawn Tennis Challenge in its own right.

chunks.text: Cars 2 is a 2011 American computer-animated action comedy spy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures.

chunks.title: Cars 2
chunks.text: It is the sequel to 2006's "Cars", and features the voices of Owen Wilson, Larry the Cable Guy, Michael Caine, Emily Mortimer, John Turturro, and Eddie Izzard.

chunks.title: Cars 2
chunks.text: In the film, race car Lightning McQueen and tow truck Mater head to Japan and Europe to compete in the World Grand Prix, but Mater becomes sidetracked with international espionage.

chunks.title: Cars 2
chunks.text: The film was directed by John Lasseter, written by Ben Queen, and produced by Denise Ream.

chunks.title: The Polar Bears
chunks.text: The Polar Bears is a 2012 3D computer animated short film presented by The Coca-Cola Company, produced by Ridley Scott, written by David Reynolds, and directed by John Stevenson.

chunks.title: The Polar Bears
chunks.text: The film features the voices of Lin-Manuel Miranda, Armie Hammer, Jonathan Adams, and Megyn Price.

chunks.title: The Polar Bears
chunks.text: The film is based on Coca-Cola's iconic polar bears and was released on the company's website and YouTube channel on December 31, 2012.

chunks.title: Moana (soundtrack)
chunks.text: Moana: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is the soundtrack to the 2016 Disney animated film "Moana".

chunks.title: Moana (soundtrack)
chunks.text: The soundtrack was released by Walt Disney Records on November 19, 2016.

chunks.title: Moana (soundtrack)
chunks.text: It features songs written by Lin-Manuel Miranda, Mark Mancina and Opetaia Foa'i, with lyrics in English, Samoan, Tokelauan, and Tuvalu.

chunks.title: Moana (soundtrack)
chunks.text: The two-disc deluxe edition includes the score, which was composed by Mancina, as well as demos, outtakes and instrumental karaoke tracks.

chunks.title: Things Ain't What They Used to Be
chunks.text: In 1941 there was a strike against the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, of which Duke Ellington was a member.

chunks.title: Things Ain't What They Used to Be
chunks.text: Because of the strike he could not air his songs on the radio.

chunks.title: Things Ain't What They Used to Be
chunks.text: Instead, he used songs written by his son Mercer and pianist Billy Strayhorn.

chunks.title: Things Ain't What They Used to Be
chunks.text: Strayhorn's compositions of this time include "Take the 'A' Train", "Chelsea Bridge" and "Day Dream", and Mercer wrote "Things Ain't What They Used to Be", "Blue Serge" and "Moon Mist".

chunks.title: Your Obedient Servant (song)
chunks.text: "Your Obedient Servant" is the twentieth song from Act 2 of the musical "Hamilton", based on the life of Alexander Hamilton, which premiered on Broadway in 2015.

chunks.title: Your Obedient Servant (song)
chunks.text: Lin-Manuel Miranda wrote both the music and lyrics to the song.

chunks.title: Your Obedient Servant (song)
chunks.text: The song is sung by the characters of Hamilton and Aaron Burr, originally performed by Miranda and Leslie Odom Jr., respectively.

chunks.title: Cabinet Battle
chunks.text: "Cabinet Battle #1", "Cabinet Battle #2", and "Cabinet Battle #3" are songs written for Act II of the musical "Hamilton", based on the life of Alexander Hamilton, which premiered on Broadway in 2015.

chunks.title: Cabinet Battle
chunks.text: Lin-Manuel Miranda wrote both the music and lyrics to the song.

chunks.title: Illmind

chunks.title: Illmind

chunks.title: Lishu District
chunks.text: Lishu District () is a district of the city of Jixi, Heilongjiang, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: Jixi () is a city in southeastern Heilongjiang Province, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: At the 2010 census, 1,862,165 people resided within its administrative area of 22488.47 km2 and 757,647 in its built-up ("or metro") area made up of 3 out of 6 urban districts (including Jiguan, Hengshan and Chengzihe).

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: Jixi is on the Muling River about 30 km from the border with Russia's Primorsky Krai and 120 km from Khanka Lake.

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: The mayor of Jixi is Zhu Deyi (朱德义 ) since July 2009.

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: The area is one of the important coal mining bases in China.

chunks.title: Jixi
chunks.text: A crater on asteroid 253 Mathilde was named after the city.

chunks.title: Didao District
chunks.text: Didao () is a district of the city of Jixi, Heilongjiang province, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Yandu District
chunks.text: Yandu District () is one of three districts of Yancheng, Jiangsu province, China.

chunks.title: Yandu District
chunks.text: (The other two are Tinghu District and Dafeng District).

chunks.title: Mashan District
chunks.text: Mashan District () is a district of the city of Jixi, Heilongjiang, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Mashan District
chunks.text: It is under the administration of the Jixi city.

chunks.title: Jiguan District
chunks.text: Jiguan District () is a district and the seat of the city of Jixi, Heilongjiang province, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Dafeng District
chunks.text: Dafeng () is a coastal district under the administration of Yancheng, Jiangsu province, China.

chunks.title: Dafeng District
chunks.text: Located on the Jiangsu North Plain with a coastline of 112 km , Dafeng was historically one of the largest salt-making areas in China and now is famed for its well preserved eco-system and numerous national conservation parks.

chunks.title: Dafeng District
chunks.text: The district has the largest national nature reserve for a rare deer species, Père David's Deer or Milu (麋鹿 ) in Chinese.

chunks.title: Dafeng District
chunks.text: It borders the prefecture-level city of Taizhou to the southwest.

chunks.title: Chengzihe District
chunks.text: Chengzihe () is a district of Jixi, Heilongjiang, People's Republic of China.

chunks.title: Tinghu District
chunks.text: Tinghu District () is one of three districts of Yancheng, Jiangsu province, China.

chunks.title: Tinghu District
chunks.text: (The other two are Yandu District and Dafeng District).

chunks.title: Tinghu District
chunks.text: Prior to 2004, Tinghu District was called the Urban District ()of Yancheng.

chunks.title: Hengshan District, Jixi
chunks.text: Hengshan District () is a district of the city of Jixi, Heilongjiang province, People's Republic of China.

Angélica Vale (born Angélica María Vale Hartman on November 11, 1975 in Mexico City, Mexico) is a Mexican actress, singer, and comedian known also as the daughter of Angélica María, "La Novia de Mexico" (Mexico's Sweetheart), and as the daughter of comedian Raúl Vale.

She has been working as an actress for almost 30 years, but achieved fame in 2006 when she became the protagonist of "La Fea Más Bella" ("The Prettiest Ugly Girl"), a Mexican telenovela, with her real-life mother.
She starred in the webnovela "No me hallo" as Luchita Guerra a young woman with a big dream of becoming a singer.
Early in 2012, Vale was a team captain on the Mexican TV Show "Parodiando", of Televisa network.
María Eugenia Llamas Andresco (19 February 1944 – 31 August 2014) was a Mexican actress best known for her roles as "La Tucita" in the Golden Age of Mexican cinema in the late 1940s and in the 1950s.
She began appearing in these films in 1948 at the age of four.
She was the winner of the Mexican equivalent of the Oscar, the Premio Ariel.
While she appeared in many movies after her childhood, she is less known for them.

However, she remained popular for her radio and television appearances, for her on-stage story telling talent, and as a live theater actress, and was the 2007 recipient of the Diploma Medalla al Mérito (Medal of Merit) award from the Spanish American Itinerate Academy of Itinerate Oral Narration.

Silvia Navarro (born as Silvia Angélica Navarro Barba on September 14, 1978 in Irapuato, Guanajuato, Mexico) is a Mexican actress of film, television, and theatre, primarily known for starring in several telenovelas.
In May 2012, People en Español magazine named her one of the "50 Most Beautiful".
Sofía Espinosa Carrasco (born September 22, 1989) is a Mexican actress, producer, writer and director.

She began her artistic preparation at the National Conservatory of Music, and followed with studies at Casazul in Mexico, Claudio Tolcachir's school in Argentina, the Stella Adler Studio in New York City, and the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London.
She received recognition for her role of Mati in the Mexican film "La Niña en la Piedra (Nadie Te Ve)" (2006), for which she was nominated for an Ariel Award for Best Actress.
She subsequently starred in the TV series "Capadocia" (2010) and "Bienvenida Realidad" (2011).
Adriana Fonseca (] ; born Adriana Fonseca Castellanos March 16, 1979) is a Mexican actress and dancer.

She is best known for her several roles in Televisa's telenovelas like "La usurpadora" as Veronica Soriano (1998), "Rosalinda" as Lucy Pérez Romero (1999), "Mariana de la Noche" as Caridad "Chachi" Montenegro (2003), "Contra viento y marea" as Sandra Serrano Rudell (2005), "Bajo las riendas del amor" as Montserrat Linares (2007) and recently for her protagonist role in Telemundo's successful telenovela "Corazón Valiente" as Angela Valdez (2012).
American Heiress is a telenovela which debuted on March 13, 2007 at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on the American television network MyNetworkTV.
This romantic melodrama tells the story of a roughneck pilot and a pampered heiress who survive a plane crash.
The show was produced by Twentieth Television, based on the 2004 TV Azteca series "La Heredera" (""The Heiress"").
La Heredera (The Heiress) is a Mexican telenovela produced by TV Azteca.
It marked the third reunion for Silvia Navarro and Sergio Basañez as protagonists.
The series was then developed into an American telenovela by the title of "American Heiress".
Rita Macedo (1925–1993) was a Mexican actress who performed during the Golden Age of Mexican cinema.
She was nominated for an Ariel Award for her 1956 performance in "Ensayo de un crimen" and in 1991 for a TVyNovelas Prize for "Alcanzar una estrella".
She won the Best Actress Ariel Award in 1972 for "Tú, yo, y nosotros".

She was married to a pioneer of Mexican radio, television and film, Luis de Llano Palmer, by whom she had two children, Julissa, an actress and musician, and Luis de Llano Macedo, renowned telenovela producer.
She also was instrumental in bringing many works of international writers to the Mexican stage.
Gabriel Porras (born Carlos Gabriel Porras Flores, February 13, 1968 in Mexico City, Mexico) is a Mexican actor.
He began his acting career working for TV Azteca in telenovelas like "Tres Veces Sofia" along with Mexican diva Lucía Méndez and "El Tio Alberto".
His acting career strengthened when he played his first protagonist role in a "El Alma Herida", a telenovela, produced by Telemundo which is owned by NBC Universal.
In "El Alma Herida" he shared credits along with Mexican actress Itatí Cantoral with whom he had a relationship in real life.
Marlene Favela (born Silvia Marlene Favela Meraz on August 5, 1976 in Santiago Papasquiaro, Durango, Mexico) is a Mexican actress.
In Mexican television, she is best known as Esmeralda in the TV show "Zorro, La Espada y la Rosa".
Roger Kitter (20 October 1949 – 3 January 2015) was an English actor best known for playing Captain Alberto Bertorelli in series 7 of the British sitcom TV series "'Allo 'Allo!
He had previously appeared weekly with Lulu throughout the 10-week run of her 1973 BBC1 series "It's Lulu".
With Kaplan Kaye he also recorded a song "Chalk Dust – the Umpire Strikes Back" using the moniker 'The Brat'.
Released on the Hansa label, it entered the UK Singles Chart on 10 July 1982; it reached a peak of number 19, and remained in the chart for 8 weeks.
The song was a Top 10 hit in the Netherlands, Belgium and South Africa, and lampooned John McEnroe complaining about line calls in tennis ("The ball's in, everyone can see that the ball's in!")
He was also an impressionist, who provided the voice of Tommy Cooper in the Lego 'Kipper' advertisement.
Grown-Ups is a 1980 British BBC television film devised and directed by Mike Leigh.
It stars Lesley Manville, Philip Davis, Brenda Blethyn, Janine Duvitski, Lindsay Duncan and Sam Kelly.
It was edited by Robin Sales and produced by Louis Marks for the BBC, and originally shown on BBC 2 on 28 November 1980.
Richard Gibson (born 1 January 1954) is an English actor, probably best known for his role as the archetypal Gestapo Officer Herr Otto Flick in the BBC hit sitcom series, "'Allo 'Allo!
Paris is a British sitcom produced by Talkback Productions for Channel 4.
It was written jointly by Irish writers Arthur Mathews and Graham Linehan, best known for their later sitcom Father Ted.
The show only lasted one series consisting of six episodes in October and November 1994.
It featured the escapades of French artist Alain Degout living in 1920s Paris, who wants to be famous, but his work gets him nowhere.
Unlike BBC sitcom 'Allo 'Allo, which was also set in France, featuring characters speaking in French accents, the characters of Paris spoke in an English accent.

Jack Haig (born John Cecil Coppin, 5 January 1913 – 4 July 1989) was an English actor who specialised in supporting roles, mainly in Television comedy, he was best known for his role on sitcom 'Allo 'Allo!
as Monsieur Roger LeClerc
The Best of 'Allo 'Allo!
was broadcast on 17 August 1994, two years after the ending of the BBC sitcom "'Allo 'Allo!
", to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the broadcast of the first series.
The actual pilot for the show had been broadcast nearly 12 years earlier, when this show was broadcast.

Following the Pilot in 1982, the series was officially launched two years later in 1984 (Series 1) and continued to Series 9 (1992); including two Christmas Special episodes in 1985 (between Series 2 and 3) and in 1991 (between Series 7 and 8).
The last series (Series 9) was followed by two retrospective episodes in 1994 ("The Best of 'Allo 'Allo!

In total, including the Pilot, the two Christmas Specials and the two post series retrospective episodes; there are 87 episodes.
Dates shown are original air dates on BBC One (except for the "The Return of 'Allo 'Allo!
" episode which was broadcast on BBC Two).
